The page is legible at 300 dpi; the words marked [?] are the ones I cannot settle letter by letter. "O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two deities of this name, who preside over night and day, hear (śrutam, listen to) these my invocations; not only my invocation, but also hear the praise being offered on all sides by the udgātṛ priests and others in the sacrificial house (sadane); and further, he who gives wealth that is heard of everywhere (śroturātiḥ), or [him who is] a good hearer (suśrotuḥ) of my invocation, Sindhu, the deity of waters, making the good fields (sukṣetrā) moist with the water of the rains — that is what must be supplied. Or else: making our fields well-fruited with water, let him hear our call; let him hear [it] that the good state of the fields may be obtained." Havā imā: in both words the ending is ā; in śrutam the luk of the vikaraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. He mitrāvaruṇā — O Mitra and Varuṇa (you two); imā — these; havā — my (praise-filled) invocations; śrutam — hear; uta — and; sadane — in the sacrificial house; viśvataḥ — (by the Udgātṛs and others) everywhere (being made); sīm — this praise too; śrutam — hear; śroturātiḥ — [Sindhu] who has well-known (famous) wealth-giving; suśrotuḥ — (our invocation) well-hearing; sindhuḥ — the deity of the waters; adbhiḥ — with water (our fields); sukṣetrā — (our) fields, to be good fields (make); naḥ — our (praise); śrotu — let him hear.

original p. 33

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Mitra and Varuṇa, hear my first invocation, which is full of praise; hear the praise that is made everywhere (by the Udgātṛs and others) in the sacrificial house; may the deity of the waters (Sindhu), well-hearing our invocation, hear it, and may he make (our fields) fruitful with water.

Printed English (as printed): Mitra and Varuna, hear these my invocations, and moreover listen to those (that are) everywhere (uttered) in the chamber of sacrifice; and may Sindhu, the renowned bestower of wealth, hear us, (fertilizing our) broad fields with water.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6. Pointing out the defect that the last pāda of this ṛk is not metrically regular, the English scholar Bloomfield has said as follows:

The entire stanza with its hysterical repetition of root śru is secondary clap-trap, its last Pada is metrically defective. It is quite probable that such a versifix [sic] borrowed his first pada from the faultless stanza VII 62. 5. [Rigveda Repititions [sic] Pt. I. P. 126]

प्र बाहवा सिसृतं जीवसे न आ नो गव्यूतिमुक्षतं घृतेन । आ नो जने श्रवयतं युवाना श्रुतं मे मित्रावरुणा हवेमा ॥

pra bāhavā sisṛtaṃ jīvase na ā no gavyūtimukṣataṃ ghṛtena | ā no jane śravayataṃ yuvānā śrutaṃ me mitrāvaruṇā havemā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-62-5, as printed; the English "VII 62. 5" above confirms it.) He is of the opinion that the last pāda of this ṛk, śrutaṃ me mitrāvaruṇā havemā, was made the first pāda here, and that this ṛk was built on it.

sīm — sīm iti parigrahārthīyo vā padapūraṇo vā (Ni. 1-7, as printed; the OCR reads it) — the Nirukta writer says that the word is used in the sense "completely" and also at the time of filling out a verse-quarter (padapūraṇa).

प्र सीमादित्यो असृजद्विधर्ता ऋतं सिन्धवो वरुणस्य यन्ति ।

pra sīmādityo asṛjadvidhartā ṛtaṃ sindhavo varuṇasya yanti |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-4 [?], as read; the reader's OCR has the letter-shaped "5-25-4".)

original p. 34

Citing this ṛk, they have shown that there the word sīm may be given the sense "everywhere" (sarvataḥ), or that the word may be taken as mere pāda-filler and not be explained. In the ṛk in hand, since the sense sarvataḥ is shown by the word viśvataḥ itself, the word sīm may be known as mere pāda-filling.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 6, noted briefly). Śrutam — the root śru śravaṇe; loṭ, 2nd dual, lat-like, thas replaced by tam; by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of the vikaraṇa; by sārvadhātukam apit the suffix is ṅit-like, so no guṇa of the root's i/u; because it is at the beginning of the verse-quarter, no nighāta; by the suffix accent the word ends in an acute. Mitrāvaruṇā — mitraś ca varuṇaś ca; by devatādvandve ca (Pā. Sū. 6-3-26) the ānaṅ substitution for the former member; in the vocative dual, by supāṃ sulug… (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the ā for the ending; āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the nighāta. Havā — the root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; in the sense of action by bhāve 'nupasargasya (Pā. Sū. 3-3-75) the suffix ap; because of the conjunction, saṃprasāraṇa and pūrvarūpa; guṇa of the root's u; av-ādeśa; the form hava; accusative plural by supāṃ sulug… (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the ā; imā likewise. Sadane — the root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) the s; "sīdanty asmin iti sadanaṃ gṛham" — the suffix lyuṭ in the locative sense; yuvor anākau (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 [?] as read; the OCR has "6-1-1") ana; liti (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the acute of the suffix's first part; locative singular. Viśvataḥ — pañcamyāḥ tasil (Pā. Sū. 5-3-7), the suffix tasil in the sense of the ablative; being lit, by liti the acute goes to the vowel before the suffix; a word with its middle acute. Śrotu — the root śru śravaṇe; loṭ, 3rd singular, the suffix tip; by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of the vikaraṇa; by eruḥ the u in place of the suffix's i; …

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स्तुषे सा वां वरुण मित्र रातिर्गवां शता पृक्षयामेषु पज्रे । श्रुतरथे प्रियरथे दधानाः सद्यः पुष्टिं निरुन्धानासो अग्मन् ॥ ७ ॥

stuṣe sā vāṃ varuṇa mitra rātirgavāṃ śatā pṛkṣayāmeṣu pajre | śrutarathe priyarathe dadhānāḥ sadyaḥ puṣṭiṃ nirundhānāso agman ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

स्तुषे । सा । वाम् । वरुण । मित्र । रातिः । गवाम् । शता । पृक्षऽयामेषु । पज्रे । श्रुतऽरथे । प्रियऽरथे । दधानाः । सद्यः । पुष्टिम् । निऽरुन्धानासः । अग्मन् ॥ ७ ॥

stuṣe | sā | vām | varuṇa | mitra | rātiḥ | gavām | śatā | pṛkṣa 'yāmeṣu | pajre | śruta 'rathe | priya 'rathe | dadhānāḥ | sadyaḥ | puṣṭim | ni 'rundhānāsaḥ | agman ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मित्र हे वरुण देव वां युवामहं स्तुषे । स्तौमि [?] । व्यत्ययेन मध्यमः [?] ॥ युवयोः सम्बन्धिनी सा प्रसिद्धा रातिर्दानं शता शतानां शतसङ्ख्यानामपरिमितानां गवां सम्बन्ध्यसङ्ख्यातगोविषया रातिः पज्रे कक्षीवति मयि पृक्षयामेषु । पृक्ष इत्यन्ननामास्ति । पृक्षाणामन्नानां नियमनं येषु स्तोत्रेषु यज्ञेषु वा तेषु निमित्तभूतेषु भवत्विति शेषः । किञ्च मित्रादयो

he mitra he varuṇa deva vāṃ yuvāmahaṃ stuṣe | staumi [?] | vyatyayena madhyamaḥ [?] ‖ yuvayoḥ sambandhinī sā prasiddhā rātirdānaṃ śatā śatānāṃ śatasaṅkhyānāmaparimitānāṃ gavāṃ sambandhyasaṅkhyātagoviṣayā rātiḥ pajre kakṣīvati mayi pṛkṣayāmeṣu | pṛkṣa ityannanāmāsti | pṛkṣāṇāmannānāṃ niyamanaṃ yeṣu stotreṣu yajñeṣu vā teṣu nimittabhūteṣu bhavatviti śeṣaḥ | kiñca mitrādayo

देवाः श्रुतरथे सर्वत्र प्रसिद्धरथोपेते प्रियरथे प्रीयमाणरथयुक्ते सर्वदा रथप्रिये पज्रे च मय्येव दधानाः प्रीतिं धारयन्तः सद्य आगमनानन्तरमेव पुष्टिं गवादिपोषं निरुन्धानासोऽरुन्धाना [?] अस्मास्वेव स्थापयन्तः । यद्वा । मयि पुष्टिं दधानाः कुर्वाणा निरुन्धानासः कृत्स्नामेव पुष्टिं मयि स्थिरां कुर्वन्तोऽग्मन्नागच्छन्तु ॥

devāḥ śrutarathe sarvatra prasiddharathopete priyarathe prīyamāṇarathayukte sarvadā rathapriye pajre ca mayyeva dadhānāḥ prītiṃ dhārayantaḥ sadya āgamanānantarameva puṣṭiṃ gavādipoṣaṃ nirundhānāso 'rundhānā [?] asmāsveva sthāpayantaḥ | yadvā | mayi puṣṭiṃ dadhānāḥ kurvāṇā nirundhānāsaḥ kṛtsnāmeva puṣṭiṃ mayi sthirāṃ kurvanto 'gmannāgacchantu ‖

The rest of the bhāṣya is the grammatical tail — rātiḥ: the root rā dāne, the suffix ktin in the sense of action, the initial acute by mantre vṛṣeṣa…; śatā: the lengthening of the preceding vowel before the ending by supāṃ sulug…; dadhānāḥ: juhotyādi, the śap → śluḥ, abhyastānām ādiḥ; agman: the root gam, Vedic luṅ, the elision of cli by mantre ghasa…, the loss of the penultimate by gamahana… — only characterised, not transcribed.

"O Mitra, O Varuṇa, I praise (stuṣe, I praise; the second-person form for the first by vyatyaya) you two. That well-known gift (rātiḥ) of yours, of hundreds (śatā) of cows, countless — a gift related to the countless cows — [may it be] for me, Kakṣīvān the Pajra, in the pṛkṣayāmeṣu: pṛkṣa is a name of food; may it become, in the praises or sacrifices in which food is regulated (niyamana) [i.e. food is provided in a fixed order], the occasion of them — that is what remains to be supplied. And further, may the gods Mitra and the rest — [who are] śrutarathe, in me, the one possessed of a famous chariot everywhere; priyarathe, one whose chariot is dear, who always loves the chariot, and a Pajra — placing their affection on me alone, quickly, immediately after coming, holding back (nirundhānāsaḥ) the nourishment (puṣṭi, the fattening of cattle and so on) and establishing it in us alone — come." Or else, "dadhānāḥ, placing nourishment in me, making [it], nirundhānāsaḥ, making all that nourishment firm in me, may they come."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. He mitra, he varuṇe — O Mitra and Varuṇa; vām — you two; stuṣe — [I] praise; sā — that well-known; śatā — innumerable; gavām — of cows; rātiḥ — the gift; pajre — in the Pajra (Kakṣīvān), me; pṛkṣayāmeṣu — in the sacrifices or praises that follow a fixed rule (about food) [may it be] (bhavatu — may it be); (kiñca — and); śrutarathe — famous (for my chariot) [in me], whose chariot is famous; priyarathe — [in me] who has a dear chariot; dadhānāḥ — placing affection; sadyaḥ — [at once] immediately; puṣṭim — the nourishment of cattle and so on; (dhadhānāḥ — having made [me] firm); nirundhānāsaḥ — [in me] having made it firm (and in us); agman — let them come.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Mitra and Varuṇa, I praise you both. Give (O gods) your well-known gift of countless cows to me, the performer of sacrifices with their rule about food and the like; and, placing your trust in me, who have famous and dear chariots (and love chariots), come to establish firmly the nourishment of cattle and so on.

Printed English (as printed): I praise you, Mitra and Varuna, for your gift of numerous cattle to the Pajra, and (from those praises) may abundant food (proceed). May (the gods), bestowiug [sic] nourishment on me, come quickly unimpeded, (each) in his famous and favourite car.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 7. pṛkṣayāmeṣu — pṛkṣaśabda is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 3-9, as read by the reader's OCR), pṛkṣāṇām annānāṃ niyamanaṃ yeṣu stotreṣu yajñeṣu vā — [in the praises or the sacrifices] in which food is regulated, or the …

original p. 37

…pṛkṣayāmeṣu (continued): "…whether for the sake of sacrifices or [of praises] — this is the sense." The scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit-English Dictionary, has pointed to this word in this same ṛk and given the meaning "Driviug [sic] swift horses" and "Probably name of a family" — "probably the name of a family", he has inferred. The epithets that follow, priyarathe śrutarathe, refer to Kakṣīvān's chariots, so this meaning, it appears, was probably given for them.

nirundhānāsaḥ — āvarundhānāḥ asmāsv eva sthāpayantaḥ | yadvā | mayi puṣṭiṃ dadhānāḥ kurvāṇāḥ nirundhānāsaḥ kṛtsnām eva puṣṭiṃ mayi sthirāṃ kurvantaḥ — "establishing in me alone the nourishment of cattle and so on" — or "making the nourishment that they have established firm [in me]".

priyarathe śrutarathe — By Svanaya, the cows and chariots given in great numbers, who were lords (svāmin) over them — it seems probable that Kakṣīvān described himself by these epithets.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 7, noted briefly). Stuṣe — the root ñiṣṭuñ stutau, adādi; by vyatyayo bahulam the laṭ 1st-person singular suffix is replaced by thās, and by thāsaḥ se the se; the śap has luk; after an atiṅanta no nighāta; the suffix accent. Rātiḥ — the root rā dāne; by striyāṃ ktin the suffix ktin in the sense of the action; though nit, by mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā… (Pā. Sū. 3-3-96 [?]) the acute on the suffix. Śatā — the word śata, the genitive plural; supāṃ sulug… (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) lengthening of the preceding vowel. Pṛkṣayāmeṣu — pṛkṣāṇāṃ yāmāḥ yeṣu te pṛkṣayāmāḥ, among them; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the accent of the first member; likewise in śrutarathe priyarathe. Dadhānāḥ — the root dhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; laṭ, the suffix śānac; juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-75) śluḥ for the vikaraṇa; ślau reduplication of the root; hrasvaḥ (shortening) and jakṣ… ; abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) the first-syllable acute.

original p. 38

Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 7). Nirundhānāsaḥ — the prefix ni; the root rudhir āvaraṇe; laṭ, the suffix śānac; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam (Pā. Sū. 3-1-78) the vikaraṇa śnam, which is mit, so it is placed after the last vowel; since it is apit, the sārvadhātuka suffix is ṅit, so there is no guṇa; śnasor alloṣaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111) the elision of the a of the vikaraṇa; the remaining n becomes anusvāra with paravarṇa; cita (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the final udātta; when jas follows, ājjaser asuk (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50) the augment asuk. Agman — the root gamḷ gatau; to show the sense of the aorist in the Chandas, chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6) luṅ; 3rd plural, jhi has ant, the elision of the i; mantre ghasahvaranaśavṛdahādvṛc… (Pā. Sū. 2-4-80) the luk of cli; since the suffix is jit/ṇit, the loss of the root's penultimate; the augment aṭ for the stem; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. ‖ 7 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अस्य स्तुषे महिमघस्य राधः सचा सनेम नहुषः सुवीराः । जनो यः पज्रेभ्यो वाजिनीवानश्वावतो रथिनो मह्यं सूरिः ॥ ८ ॥

asya stuṣe mahimaghasya rādhaḥ sacā sanema nahuṣaḥ suvīrāḥ | jano yaḥ pajrebhyo vājinīvānaśvāvato rathino mahyaṃ sūriḥ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अस्य । स्तुषे । महिऽमघस्य । राधः । सचा । सनेम । नहुषः । सुऽवीराः । जनः । यः । पज्रेभ्यः । वाजिनीवान् । अश्वऽवतः । रथिनः । मह्यम् । सूरिः ॥ ८ ॥

asya | stuṣe | mahi 'maghasya | rādhaḥ | sacā | sanema | nahuṣaḥ | su 'vīrāḥ | janaḥ | yaḥ | pajrebhyaḥ | vājinīvān | aśva 'vataḥ | rathinaḥ | mahyam | sūriḥ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

महिमघस्य । महि महत्पूज्यं मघो धनमन्नं वा यस्य देवसंघस्य स तथोक्तः । तादृशस्यास्य राधो धनं स्तुषे । स्तुवे । व्यत्ययेन मध्यमः । धनलाभाय प्रभूतधनं देवसंघं स्तौमीत्यर्थः । किञ्च नहुषः । मनुष्यनामैतत् ।

mahimaghasya | mahi mahatpūjyaṃ magho dhanamannaṃ vā yasya devasaṃghasya sa tathoktaḥ | tādṛśasyāsya rādho dhanaṃ stuṣe | stuve | vyatyayena madhyamaḥ | dhanalābhāya prabhūtadhanaṃ devasaṃghaṃ staumītyarthaḥ | kiñca nahuṣaḥ | manuṣyanāmaitat |

original p. 39

परस्परस्नेहबन्धोपेता मनुष्या वयं कक्षीवन्तः सुवीराः शोभनपुत्राद्युपेताः सन्तः सचा सह परस्परैकमत्येन सनेमु [?] । त्वद्दत्तं धनं सम्भजेमहि । लभेमहि । देवसंघो विशेष्यते । यो जनो देवजनो यष्ट [?] देवसंघः पज्रेभ्योऽङ्गिरोगोत्रोत्पन्नेभ्यः कक्षीवद्भ्यः । पज्रा वा अङ्गिरस इति श्रुतेः । तेभ्यो वाजिनीवान् । वाजोऽन्नम् । तद्वती क्रिया वाजिनी । तया तद्वान् वाजिनीवान् । यद्वा । एको मत्वर्थीयप्रत्ययश्छान्दसः । अस्मभ्यं प्रदेयेन वत्रेण वान्नेन तद्वान्वाजिनीवानित्यर्थः । यश्च देवसंघोऽश्वावतो बहुभिस्तद्दत्त्रैरश्वैस्तद्वतो रथिनो रथवतो मह्यं मे सूरिः प्रेरको भवति । अश्वानां रथानां प्रेरयितारं देवसंघं स्तुष इत्यर्थः ॥ सुवीराः । वीरवीर्ये चेत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अश्वावतः । अश्वशब्दस्य मन्त्रे सोमाश्वेत्यादिना मतुपि दीर्घत्वम् ॥

parasparasnehabandhopetā manuṣyā vayaṃ kakṣīvantaḥ suvīrāḥ śobhanaputrādyupetāḥ santaḥ sacā saha parasparaikamatyena sanemu [?] | tvaddattaṃ dhanaṃ sambhajemahi | labhemahi | devasaṃgho viśeṣyate | yo jano devajano yaṣṭa [?] devasaṃghaḥ pajrebhyo 'ṅgirogotrotpannebhyaḥ kakṣīvadbhyaḥ | pajrā vā aṅgirasa iti śruteḥ | tebhyo vājinīvān | vājo 'nnam | tadvatī kriyā vājinī | tayā tadvān vājinīvān | yadvā | eko matvarthīyapratyayaśchāndasaḥ | asmabhyaṃ pradeyena vatreṇa vānnena tadvānvājinīvānityarthaḥ | yaśca devasaṃgho 'śvāvato bahubhistaddattrairaśvaistadvato rathino rathavato mahyaṃ me sūriḥ prerako bhavati | aśvānāṃ rathānāṃ prerayitāraṃ devasaṃghaṃ stuṣa ityarthaḥ ‖ suvīrāḥ | vīravīrye cetyuttarapadādyudāttatvam | aśvāvataḥ | aśvaśabdasya mantre somāśvetyādinā matupi dīrghatvam ‖

(The last two sentences are the grammatical tail, partly legible; they are given as read.) "Of that [assembly of the gods] who have great (mahi) wealth (magha, wealth or food), I praise the gift (rādhaḥ, wealth); stuṣe — 'I praise'; the second person is used for the first by vyatyaya — that is, 'to obtain wealth I praise the assembly of the gods which has abundant wealth'. And further, nahuṣaḥ: this is a name for men: we men, joined by mutual affection and ties, the Kakṣīvats, with good sons and the like (suvīrāḥ), together, with mutual unity of mind, might gain (sanemu) [it]; might share (sambhajemahi) the wealth given by you. [Then] the assembly of the gods is qualified: the people, the divine people, the sacrificer [?], the assembly of the gods is vājinīvān for the Pajras — the descendants of Aṅgiras, the Kakṣīvats; for the śruti says pajrā vā aṅgirasaḥ ("Pajras indeed are Aṅgirases"). Vāja is food; the action connected with it is vājinī; he who has it is vājinīvān. Or else, a single possessive suffix, in the Vedic way: he who has food or the like to be given to us. And the assembly of the gods who, to me — who have horses (aśvavataḥ) given by them in great numbers and who have chariots (rathinaḥ) — is sūri, the impeller; that is: 'I praise the assembly of the gods who impel [or give] the horses and chariots'."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Yaḥ janaḥ — which assembly of the gods; pajrebhyaḥ — to the Pajras born in the Aṅgiras line (to us who are called Kakṣīvats); vājinīvān — (giving) one with food; (yaḥ janaḥ — which assembly of the gods); aśvavataḥ — one with horses (given by them); rathinaḥ — one with chariots; mahyam — to me; sūriḥ — the impeller; (tasya — of such [an assembly]); mahimaghasya — endowed with excellent wealth (food); asya — of this assembly of the gods; rādhaḥ — the wealth; stuṣe — I praise; kiñca — and; nahuṣaḥ — we men; suvīrāḥ — having excellent sons and the like; sacā — with one mind; sanema — may we gain the wealth (given by them).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. In order to obtain wealth I praise the deities who give us food, to be given by the Aṅgirases, who impel me — I who have horses and chariots given by them — and who are of excellent wealth. Grant that we, with heroic sons and with one mind, may obtain the wealth given by you.

Printed English (as printed): I laud the treasures of that opulent (assembly of the god s) : may we, men who (are blessed) with excellent descendants, partake of them together : the assembly conferring upon the Pajras abundant food, has been my benefactor, and has made me the master of horses and chariots.

original p. 40

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 8.

nahuṣaḥ — This word is recorded among the names of manuṣya ("man") (Ni. 3-7, as read by the reader's OCR). Parasparasnehabandhopetā manuṣyā vayaṃ kakṣīvantaḥ — "we, Kakṣīvān's people, bound by mutual affection and kinship": the sense indicated by the word nahuṣa has been explained [above]. [The matter of Nahuṣa has been told earlier.]

sūriḥ — The word sūri is recorded among the names of the praiser (stotṛ) (Ni. 3-19, as read by the reader's OCR); it has been used in the Saṃhitās in the senses medhāvin, krāntadarśin, tattvajña ("intelligent", "far-seeing", "knower of the truth"); here the Nirukta writers have given the meaning preraka ("impeller") for the word sūri.

जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमुखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ।

jiṣṇurvāmanyaḥ sumukhasya sūrirdivo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-4 [?], as read.) In citing this ṛk they have shown, for the word sūri in it, that the sense is erayitā, prerakaḥ ("one who sets in motion, an impeller") (Ni. 12-3, as read by the reader's OCR; my own first reading "13-2" was wrong). In the same way here too: "the assembly of the gods, the people, is for me sūri — that is: 'the impeller to carry out the sacrificial duties and the like'."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 8, noted briefly). Asya — ūḍidaṃpadādi… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171), the ending takes the acute. Stuṣe — the root ñiṣṭuñ stutau, adādi; vyatyayo bahulam — the laṭ 1st-person suffix is replaced by thās; by se ; śap has luk; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Mahimaghasya — mahi pūjyaṃ maghaṃ dhanaṃ yasya saḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the accent of the first member. Rādhaḥ — rādhnuvanti anena iti rādhaḥ dhanam; the root rādha saṃsiddhau; sarvadhātubhya asun (Uṇ. Sū. 4-628, as read by the reader's OCR) the suffix asun; since nit, the initial acute. Sacā — the root ṣacaḥ samavāye; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) sa for the initial; since it belongs to the sampadādi group, sampadādibhyaḥ kvip (Pā. Sū. 3-3-108 [?], as read) the suffix kvip in the sense of the action; instrumental singular; though a word of one syllable, by vyatyaya the root accent remains.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ 150 dpi, small type; the Devanagari is read letter by letter and the doubtful places are marked [?].

हे मित्रावरुणौ युष्माकं यो जनोऽभिध्रुक् अभितो द्रोग्धा भवति । अयष्टा भवतीत्यर्थः । यश्चाक्ष्णयाध्रुक् वक्रेण मार्गेण द्रुह्यति अन्यथाप्रकारेण द्रुह्यति । द्रोहप्रकार उच्यते । वां युवामपः सोमरसान्न सुनोति । अभिषवं न करोति । युवामतिक्रम्यान्यदेवतार्थं सुनोतीत्यभिप्रायः । अयमेवाक्ष्णयाद्रोहः । स मूढो द्विविधो [?] जनः स्वयं यक्ष्मं व्याधिं हृदये स्वचित्ते नि धत्ते । स्थापयति । अनुष्ठा[?]ं …भोगान्प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः [?] । यत् । लिङ्व्यत्ययः । य उक्तविलक्षणः पुमान् ऋतावा यज्ञवान् परिगृहीतयज्ञो होत्राभिर्वाङ्मयैः [?] स्तुतिवाग्भिरीमेनं सोमरसमाप व्याप्नोति स्तुवन् सोममभिषुणोतीति यावत् । स नरः प्रैत्स्वा [?]… वक्ष्यमाणेन सह सम्बन्धः ॥ अभिध्रुक् । द्रुहेः सत्सूद्विष… क्विप् । संहितायां भष्भावश्छान्दसः । ऋतावेत्यत्र छन्दसीवनिपावित्यनेन मत्वर्थीयो वनिप् । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वम् ॥

he mitrāvaruṇau yuṣmākaṃ yo jano 'bhidhruk abhito drogdhā bhavati | ayaṣṭā bhavatītyarthaḥ | yaścākṣṇayādhruk vakreṇa mārgeṇa druhyati anyathāprakāreṇa druhyati | drohaprakāra ucyate | vāṃ yuvāmapaḥ somarasānna sunoti | abhiṣavaṃ na karoti | yuvāmatikramyānyadevatārthaṃ sunotītyabhiprāyaḥ | ayamevākṣṇayādrohaḥ | sa mūḍho dvividho [?] janaḥ svayaṃ yakṣmaṃ vyādhiṃ hṛdaye svacitte ni dhatte | sthāpayati | anuṣṭhā[?]ṃ …bhogānprāpnotītyarthaḥ [?] | yat | liṅvyatyayaḥ | ya uktavilakṣaṇaḥ pumān ṛtāvā yajñavān parigṛhītayajño hotrābhirvāṅmayaiḥ [?] stutivāgbhirīmenaṃ somarasamāpa vyāpnoti stuvan somamabhiṣuṇotīti yāvat | sa naraḥ praitsvā [?]… vakṣyamāṇena saha sambandhaḥ ‖ abhidhruk | druheḥ satsūdviṣa… kvip | saṃhitāyāṃ bhaṣbhāvaśchāndasaḥ | ṛtāvetyatra chandasīvanipāvityanena matvarthīyo vanip | anyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvam ‖

"O Mitra and Varuṇa, whoever among your [worshippers] is abhidhruk — an abhitaḥ drogdhā, one who is hostile to you all around, that is, one who does not sacrifice; and he who is akṣṇayādhruk — hostile in a crooked way, hostile in another manner: the manner of hostility is told: he does not press (sunoti) the Soma-juice for you two (apaḥ — the waters, i.e. the Soma-juice); he does not make the pressing; the sense is that he passes you over and presses for another deity. This is akṣṇayā-droha (crooked hostility). That fool, a man of two kinds, himself places (ni dhatte) yakṣma, a disease, in his own heart (mind). … But he who, being different from what has been said, is a man ṛtāvā, possessing sacrifice, who has undertaken the sacrifice, āpa — attains (vyāpnoti) this Soma-juice (īm) through the hotrās, speech-forms, praising words; that is, praising, presses the Soma. [May he have] … — to be joined with what follows." The Devanagari of the grammar tail — abhidhruk: the root druh with kvip; bhaṣ-substitution in the Chandas; ṛtāvā: the suffix vanip in the possessive sense; lengthening in the Saṃhitā — is characterised only.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. He mitrāvaruṇau — O Mitra and Varuṇa; yaḥ janaḥ — which man; abhidhruk — hostile to you in an open way (he who does not sacrifice to you); (yaḥ — who); akṣṇayādhruk — he who is hostile in any other, crooked, way; vām — to you two; apaḥ — the Soma-juice; na sunoti — does not prepare; saḥ — that (fool); svayam — by himself; yakṣmam — the disease; hṛdaye — in his own heart; ni dhatte — makes it settle; yat — which [man]; ṛtāvā — performing the sacrifice; hotrābhiḥ — with praising words; īm — this Soma-juice; āpa — prepares [him]; [for the connection with the following ṛk].

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Mitra and Varuṇa, whoever is hostile to you in any way, and does not prepare the Soma-juice for you, those two fools themselves make the disease settle in their own hearts; but the one who performs the sacrifice and prepares the Soma-juice with praising words — [connect with the next ṛk].

Printed English (as printed): The man who does you wrong, Mitra and Varuna, who injures you in any way, who does not qresent [sic] you with oblations, contracts for himself sickness in his heart ; but he who, performing worship, (celebrates it) with praises—

original p. 43

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 9. In this ṛk a difference is shown between the experiences to come of the performer of a sacrifice and of one who has not carried out the sacrifice. One who is not a performer of sacrifice becomes a drohin ("hater").

तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ।

tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ |

(Bhagavadgītā 3-12, as printed "೩-೧೨".) As this saying has it, one who, having enjoyed the food produced by the gods' favour — rain and the like — from the rain and so on that were granted by the deities, does not practise sacrifice in thankfulness to them, commits a kind of treason against the gods. This droha is of two kinds: abhidhruk, direct hatred, and akṣṇayādhruk, acting with hostility by deceitfully going the crooked way, as a performer of sacrifice. Those who live out the life of such hatred have no kind of wealth. Seeing all the wealth the sacrificers enjoy, they feel jealousy, and this jealousy burns the heart. That disease is called yakṣma. Ordinarily yakṣma is consumption (kṣayaroga); because jealousy causes the heart to waste, it too is called yakṣma.

hotrābhiḥ — The word hotrā is recorded among the names of speech (vāṅnāmāni) (Ni. 2-23, as read by the reader's OCR) — "by praising words"; it is also recorded among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-19, as read by the reader's OCR); so it can also mean "by sacrificial acts".

समानं योनिमनु सञ्चरन्तं द्रप्सं जुहोम्यनु सप्त होत्राः ।

samānaṃ yonimanu sañcarantaṃ drapsaṃ juhomyanu sapta hotrāḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-11[?]-[?], as read.) In this ṛk, for the word hotrāḥ, whichever of these two meanings is taken it fits, as may be seen in the bhāṣya.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 9, noted briefly). Mitrāvaruṇau — mitraś ca varuṇaś ca; by devatādvandve ca the ānaṅ substitution for the first member; in the vocative by āmantritasya ca the nighāta accent. Abhidhruk — the root druha jighāṃsāyām; satsūdviṣadruhaduha… the suffix kvip; with su following, by vā druhamuha… the gh-substitution optionally, and by ekāco baśo bhaṣ… the bhaṣ substitution; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt the accent of the last member.

Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 9, noted briefly). Apaḥ — ūḍidaṃpadādi…: the ending takes the acute. Sunoti — the root ṣuñ abhiṣave; laṭ, 3rd singular, the suffix tip; svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ the vikaraṇa śnu, with guṇa as the cause is the suffix; since the word yajña [or yat] stands in connection, the nighāta does not arise; the vikaraṇa's accent remains. Dhatte — the root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; laṭ, 3rd singular; tiṅ atiṅaḥ the nighāta. Āpa — the root āpḷ vyāptau; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ the liṭ in the present sense; 3rd singular; since the word ati… is not a verb, the nighāta does not arise; since the suffix is lit, by liti the acute for the vowel before the suffix. Yat — vyatyayo bahulam: the neuter form for the masculine. Ṛtāvā — ṛtam asya asti iti ṛtavā; chandasīvanipau the suffix vanip in the possessive sense; the form ṛtavan; in the Chandas, anyeṣām api dṛśyate the lengthening before the suffix; since the suffix is pit it is unaccented; in the nominative singular the penultimate lengthening and su-elision, n-elision. ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Read from the small type of this page at 150 dpi; many letters are doubtful, and the grammar-tail part is only characterised: daṃsujūtaḥ — the word accent of the first member by tṛtīyā karmaṇi; gūrtaśravāḥ — from the root gurī udyamane; visṛṣṭarātiḥ — the niṣṭhā suffix of the root sṛj with the prefix vi, in the passive; the prefix keeps its own accent by gatir anantaraḥ; pṛtsu — pṛtanā gets the substitute pṛd by the statement "pādādiṣu māṃspṛtsnāmupasaṅkhyānam"; the ending takes the acute by sāvekācaḥ; bāḷhasṛtvā — the suffix kvanip after the root sṛ by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante.

हे मित्रावरुणौ युवां गतमन्त्रावसानोक्तलक्षणो यष्टा [?] जनो दंसुजूतः दंसनीयैरश्वैः सुशिक्षितैः प्रेरितः अत एव नरां नराणां शर्धस्तरः अतिशयेन बलवान् । अथवातिशयेन बलवान् । नराणां स्वसमानानां मध्ये गूर्तश्रवा उद्गूर्णदीप्तिः प्रख्यातान्नो वा विसृष्टरातिर्थिभ्यः [?] प्रदत्तधनः । एवं महानुभावः शूरः सन् विश्वासु पृत्सु सर्वेषु जन्येषु सङ्ग्रामेषु व्राधतः । महतामेतत् । हिंसकान्बलीयसोऽपि नहुषः । मनुष्यनामैतत् । मनुष्यान् शत्रून् प्रति बाळ्हसृत्वा भृशं सर्ता शङ्कितगमनः सन् सदमित् सद्य एव याति गच्छति ॥ दंसुजूतः । दामे… तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । गूर्तश्रवाः । गुरी उद्यमने… विसृष्टरातिः । विपूर्वात्सृजतेः कर्मणि निष्ठा । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । पृत्सु । पदादिषु मांस्पृत्स्नामुपसङ्ख्यानमिति पृतनाशब्दस्य पृदादेशः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । बाळ्हसृत्वा । सर्तेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति क्वनिप् ॥

he mitrāvaruṇau yuvāṃ gatamantrāvasānoktalakṣaṇo yaṣṭā [?] jano daṃsujūtaḥ daṃsanīyairaśvaiḥ suśikṣitaiḥ preritaḥ ata eva narāṃ narāṇāṃ śardhastaraḥ atiśayena balavān | athavātiśayena balavān | narāṇāṃ svasamānānāṃ madhye gūrtaśravā udgūrṇadīptiḥ prakhyātānno vā visṛṣṭarātirthibhyaḥ [?] pradattadhanaḥ | evaṃ mahānubhāvaḥ śūraḥ san viśvāsu pṛtsu sarveṣu janyeṣu saṅgrāmeṣu vrādhataḥ | mahatāmetat | hiṃsakānbalīyaso 'pi nahuṣaḥ | manuṣyanāmaitat | manuṣyān śatrūn prati bāḷhasṛtvā bhṛśaṃ sartā śaṅkitagamanaḥ san sadamit sadya eva yāti gacchati ‖ daṃsujūtaḥ | dāme… tṛtīyā karmaṇīti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | gūrtaśravāḥ | gurī udyamane… visṛṣṭarātiḥ | vipūrvātsṛjateḥ karmaṇi niṣṭhā | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvena sa eva śiṣyate | pṛtsu | padādiṣu māṃspṛtsnāmupasaṅkhyānamiti pṛtanāśabdasya pṛdādeśaḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | bāḷhasṛtvā | sarteranyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti kvanip ‖

"O Mitra and Varuṇa, the man of the kind described at the end of the last mantra — the sacrificer [?] — is daṃsujūta, urged on by well-trained, admirable horses; and therefore śardhastara among men, 'exceedingly strong'. Among men of his own kind he is gūrtaśravāḥ — of lofty splendour, or of famed food — visṛṣṭarāti, one who has given away wealth to the needy [?]. Being thus a great-souled hero, in all combats (pṛtsu), in all battles with men, he is vrādhata: 'mighty' [this is said of great ones]. Even against stronger violent men — nahuṣaḥ ('man'; this is a name for men) — against hostile men, he is bāḷhasṛtvā, 'one who goes violently, firmly, with undaunted going', and sadam it — he goes at once, without delay."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. He mitrāvaruṇau — O Mitra and Varuṇa; saḥ — that (man described in the previous ṛk); daṃsujūtaḥ — urged on by well-trained horses; narām — among men; śardhastaraḥ — exceedingly strong; gūrtaśravāḥ — famous (with famed food); visṛṣṭarātiḥ — a giver of gifts (to petitioners); śūraḥ — a hero; viśvāsu pṛtsu — in all battles; vrādhataḥ — (mighty) enemies [even against them]; nahuṣaḥ — against men; bāḷhasṛtvā — going fearlessly; sadamit — always; yāti — he goes.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. (The man of the characteristics of the previous ṛk,) O Mitra and Varuṇa, borne by well-trained horses, exceedingly strong, famous, a giver of gifts, and a hero, in all battles — however mighty the enemies are — always goes forward undaunted (aprativhata).

Printed English (as printed): He, borne by well-trained horses, endowed with surpassing strength renowned above men, munificent in gifts, moves a hero, ever uudaunted [sic] in all combats, (even) against mighty men.

original p. 46

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 10.

daṃsujūtaḥ — dāntair aśvaiḥ suṣṭhu preritaḥ — "well urged on by well-trained horses": that is, a man full of enthusiasm and powerful.

śardhastaraḥ — It has been explained before that the word śardha means "strength" and that it has other meanings too. Here the sense is "strength that can be compared with all [others]".

gūrtaśravāḥ — gūrta means "praiseworthy"; or, "well known". Śravas here means "food": one of excellent splendour, or one with famous food.

bāḷhasṛtvā — bāḷha means vṛddha ("strong").

असर्जि वां स्थविरा वेधसा गीर्बाळ्हे अश्विना त्रेधा क्षरन्ती ।

asarji vāṃ sthavirā vedhasā gīrbāḷhe aśvinā tredhā kṣarantī |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-139-2 [?], as read.) In this ṛk Sāyaṇa has given for the word bāḷhe the sense dhṛḍhe, sthirakarme ("firm, of steady action"). So also here: "going with firmness, free from fear, since the help of Mitra and Varuṇa is with him, [yet] against enemies of whatever kind, with a steadiness that carries [him]" — and therefore he explained it as aśaṅkitagamanaḥ ("one whose going is without fear").

vrādhataḥ nahuṣaḥ — mahannāmaitat | hiṃsakān mahato 'pi śatrūn — "(this is a name of 'great'); against violent enemies, though they be great". Ordinarily the word mahat is current in the sense "worthy of honour"; but because the epithet vrādhataḥ is used here of enemies, it comes to mean "extremely strong, powerful". This epithet is also found for gods.

इमे ये ते सु वायो बाह्वोजसोऽन्तर्नदी ते पतयन्त्युक्षणो महि व्राधन्त उक्षणः ।

ime ye te su vāyo bāhvojaso 'ntarnadī te patayantyukṣaṇo mahi vrādhanta ukṣaṇaḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-134-4 [?], as read.) In this ṛk the word vrādhantaḥ is an epithet of the horses of Vāyu: mahi vrādhantaḥ — ati prabhūtaṃ vardhamānāḥ, "growing very abundantly" — that is the sense. And:

स चेन्द्रो विप्र मर्त्यो महो व्राधन्तमो दिवि ।

sa cendro vipra martyo maho vrādhantamo divi |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-2 [?], as read.)

original p. 47

In this ṛk the epithet is of a man worthy of worship, to show greatness: vrādhantamaḥ — pravṛddhatamaḥ, "the most grown"; itaradevānām api śreṣṭhaḥ — "more excellent than even the other gods", is the sense. Thus, leaving aside one or two more ṛks, in all the other places [the word] is used in the sense of "enemy".

शत्रूयन्तो अभि ये नस्ततस्रे महि व्राधन्त ओगणास इन्द्र ।

śatrūyanto abhi ye nastatasre mahi vrādhanta ogaṇāsa indra |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-9[?]-1[?], as read.) Here vrādhantaḥ — asmān bādhamānāḥ, "those who afflict us greatly" is the sense. In just the same way, in many other places the word means an enemy that is extremely strong, not to be checked, and one who inflicts violence; likewise in the ṛk in hand, however mighty an enemy may be, the [man described] may move about not mindful of him, and without fear — that is the purport.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 10, noted briefly). Vrādhataḥ — the root vṛdhu vṛddhau, with the uṇādi suffix ati; the augment a… by that [combination]; vṛṣādīnāṃ ca — the initial acute. Daṃsujūtaḥ — the root damu upaśame; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate the suffix vic; in vic, total elision; jū is a sautra root of the sense of motion; the suffix kta in the passive by niṣṭhā; tṛtīyā karmaṇi — the first member keeps its natural accent. Narām — the word nṛ; the genitive plural; jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam — the nuṭ does not come; guṇa by vyatyaya; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ… — the ending takes the acute. Gūrtaśravāḥ — the root gurī udyamane; the suffix kta by niṣṭhā; since it is ra-… the cerebral ṇ is not [substituted]; gūrtaṃ śravaḥ yasya saḥ gūrtaśravāḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam — the accent of the first member. Visṛṣṭarātiḥ — the root sṛja visarge; with the prefix vi, the niṣṭhā suffix in the passive; vraścabhrasja… — ṣatva of the j; the suffix kta in the sense of ṣṭu; gatir anantaraḥ — the prefix keeps its own accent.

Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 10, noted briefly). Visṛṣṭarātiḥ (concluded) — visṛṣṭā rātir yena saḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam: the accent of the first member. Yāti — the root yā prāpaṇe; laṭ, 3rd singular; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Bāḷhasṛtvā — bāḍhaṃ sarati iti bāḷhasṛtvā; the root sṛ gatau; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate the suffix kvanip; since it is kit, no guṇa; since it is pit, by hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk the tuk augment for the short vowel — the word sṛtvan; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt: the accent of the last member. Pṛtsu — the word pṛtanā; when the locative plural follows, by the statement pādādiṣu māṃspṛtsnām upasaṅkhyānam the substitute pṛd; khari ca the d becomes t; because it has one syllable, sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ… the ending takes the acute. ‖ 10 ‖

अध ग्मन्ता नहुषो हवं सूरेः श्रोता राजानो अमृतस्य मन्द्राः । नभोजुवो यन्निरवस्य राधः प्रशस्तये महिना रथवते ॥ ११ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे राजानो राजमानाः सर्वस्येश्वरा वा हे मन्द्रा मादयितारो यूयममृतस्यामरणस्य सूरेः स्तोत्रादिप्रेरकस्य नहुषो मनुष्यस्य मम हवमाह्वानं श्रोत शृणुत । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । अमृतस्येत्यत्र बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । अधाथ श्रवणानन्तरं ग्मन्त । आगच्छत । गमेश्छान्दसो लङ् । मध्यमबहुवचनस्य व्यत्ययेन थः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । गमहनेत्युपधालोपः ॥ किमर्थमागमनमुच्यते । नभोजुवो नभसि व्याप्ता यूयं यद्यस्मान्निरवस्य निर्गतरक्षकस्य युष्मद्व्यतिरेकेण रक्षकान्तररहितस्य । अथवा निर्गतो मुखादुच्चरितो रवः शब्दः स्तोत्ररूपो यस्मात्तादृशस्य । रथवते रथवतो यजमानस्य । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । महिना महिम्ना माहात्म्येन ॥ मकारलोपश्छान्दसः ॥ तेन युक्तं राधः समृद्धिसाधनं हविर्लक्षणं संराधकं स्तोत्रं वा प्रशस्तये प्रशंसितुं कामयध्वे । तस्मादाह्वानं शृणुतागच्छत चेति ॥

he rājāno rājamānāḥ sarvasyeśvarā vā he mandrā mādayitāro yūyamamṛtasyāmaraṇasya sūreḥ stotrādiprerakasya nahuṣo manuṣyasya mama havamāhvānaṃ śrota śṛṇuta | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | amṛtasyetyatra bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityantodāttatvam | adhātha śravaṇānantaraṃ gmanta | āgacchata | gameśchāndaso laṅ | madhyamabahuvacanasya vyatyayena thaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | gamahanetyupadhālopaḥ ‖ kimarthamāgamanamucyate | nabhojuvo nabhasi vyāptā yūyaṃ yadyasmānniravasya nirgatarakṣakasya yuṣmadvyatirekeṇa rakṣakāntararahitasya | athavā nirgato mukhāduccarito ravaḥ śabdaḥ stotrarūpo yasmāttādṛśasya | rathavate rathavato yajamānasya | ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī | mahinā mahimnā māhātmyena ‖ makāralopaśchāndasaḥ ‖ tena yuktaṃ rādhaḥ samṛddhisādhanaṃ havirlakṣaṇaṃ saṃrādhakaṃ stotraṃ vā praśastaye praśaṃsituṃ kāmayadhve | tasmādāhvānaṃ śṛṇutāgacchata ceti ‖

Read at 150 dpi; a few words are doubtful, and the grammar tail — amṛtasya: the final acute in a bahuvrīhi by nañsubhyām; gmanta: the Vedic laṅ of the root gam, with tha for the second-person plural and the loss of the penultimate by gamahana… — is characterised only. "O kings — shining ones or lords of all — O mandrāḥ, givers of delight: you, hear (śrota) the invocation of me, a nahuṣa (man), of the undying (amṛta) praiser (sūri), the impeller of praises and so on; and then, after hearing, come (gmanta). For what purpose is the coming said? You who traverse the sky (nabhojuvaḥ), since you [are able], for the sake of [me] the niravasya — who has no other protector than you, or from whose mouth the sound of praise has been uttered — for the chariot-owner (rathavate: the dative in the sense of the genitive) — the sacrificer — mahinā, with greatness; makāra-elision in the Chandas — that with which [I] desire to praise rādhas, the wealth: the oblation that is the means of prosperity, or the praise that gives satisfaction; therefore hear the invocation and come."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Nabhojuvaḥ — (you) who traverse the sky; yat — for what reason; niravasya — who has no other protector (than you); rathavate — [of the sacrificer] who has a chariot; mahinā — excellent; rādhaḥ — the oblation that causes prosperity (the praise); praśastaye — to praise [it]; rājānaḥ — O sovereign lords of all (the shining); and mandrāḥ — O givers of delight (you); amṛtasya — the deathless; sūreḥ — the one who recites praise and so on; nahuṣasya — man's (my); havam — the invocation filled with praise; śrota — hear; adha — (after hearing the invocation) afterwards; gmanta — come (to our sacrifice).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O sovereign lords, givers of joy, you who traverse the sky (O deities), [being] the sacrificer who has chariots and has no protector other than you, I who praise you have prepared an excellent oblation, the cause of prosperity (the praise), to praise you; hear the invocation of the praising, undying man — me — and come here.

Printed English (as printed): Royal bestowers of delight, listen to the invocation of (your) undying worshipper, and then come hither, that you who traverse the sky may be … continues on p. 50

original p. 50

Printed English of Ṛk 11 (concluded, as printed): …propitiated by the greatness of the (sacrificial) wealth presented to you by the sacrificer, who acknowledges no other protector.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 11.

adha — The th of the word atha has become dh in the Vedic way. "Afterwards" is the sense.

gmantā — the final syllable of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text, for the sake of the metre.

nahuṣaḥ — since the word nahuṣaḥ is recorded among the twenty-five names of man, manuṣyāḥ, narāḥ and so on (Ni. 3-7, as read by the reader's OCR), nahuṣaḥ means "of man". Here the word nahuṣaḥ is the genitive singular of the word nahus.

sūreḥ — stotrādipreṇakasya: "of the one who impels praise and so on". Since the word sūri is recorded in the group of thirteen names of praisers beginning with rebhaḥ, jaritā (Ni. 3-19, as read by the reader's OCR), sūreḥ means "of one who makes praise and so on".

amṛtasya — the bhāṣyakāra has given for this word the ordinary meaning amaraṇasya, "of the deathless". Since this word is an epithet of nahuṣaḥ — "of man (of me)" — the doubt naturally arises how a man can be deathless. The bhāṣyakāra has not given a proper explanation of this.

mandrāḥ — mādayitāraḥ: "makers of delight".

nabhojuvaḥ — nabhasi vyāptāḥ: "pervading the sky"; those who stand in the place of the middle region.

niravasya — nirgatarakṣakasya | yuṣmadvyatirekeṇa rakṣakāntararahitasya: "of one who has no other protector besides you"; or, nirgato mukhād uccarito ravaḥ śabdaḥ stotrarūpo yasya tādṛśasya — "one from whose mouth a sound in the form of praise comes forth", that is, "one who praises".

rathavate — here the dative stands in place of the genitive: for rathavataḥ, the word rathavate; "of the sacrificer who has a chariot".

praśastaye — praśaṃsitum kāmayadhve: "you wish to praise"; therefore hear our invocation and come here — that is the sense.

rādhaḥ — samṛddhisādhanaṃ havirlakṣaṇaṃ saṃrādhakaṃ stotraṃ vā: "the oblation that is the means of prosperity, or the praise that gives satisfaction" — that is, for praising the food in the form of oblation which we have prepared for prosperity, or the praise which we offer in a special way.

original p. 51

The greater part of this ṛk, and in it the second half, is full of difficulties. The meaning does not fit properly; the word amṛtasya in the first half is opposed to the nature of man: all men must be subject to death, so how can they be deathless? In the second half too, the use of the word rathavate cannot be explained as it ought to be, as the sacrificing yajamāna who is said to be fed; and since there is no verb in this sentence, neither the main intention of the sentence nor the seer's meaning is clear.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 11, noted briefly; sūtra numbers not reproduced). Adha — when atha is said, the dh replaces the th by vyatyaya. Gmanta — the root gamḷ gatau; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ — laṅ in the sense of the imperative; by vyatyayo bahulam the suffix jhi … in the second-person plural; bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of the vikaraṇa; sārvadhātukam apit — since the suffix is ṅit-like, gamahanajana… the loss of the penultimate of the root; the suffix jhi … jhoṃtaḥ — the ant; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi — the augment aṭ is not [added]; since adha is connected as an nipāta, nipātair yad yady… the nighāta is prevented, so the suffix's first acute remains. Havam — the root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; in the sense of action by bhāve 'nupasargasya the suffix ap; saṃprasāraṇa, saṃprasāraṇācca the pūrvarūpa; taking the suffix as the cause, by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ the guṇa for the u; av-substitution; the suffix is pit, so it is unaccented, and the root accent remains; accusative singular. Śrota — the root śru śravaṇe; loṭ, 2nd plural, with the lat-like ta-substitute; by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of śap; by vyatyaya the guṇa of the root's u with the suffix as the cause; since it stands at the beginning of the verse-quarter, no nighāta; the root accent remains; dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ — in the Saṃhitā the lengthening of the i. Rājānaḥ — the root rājṛ dīptau; the uṇādi suffix kanin; nominative plural in the vocative; āmantritasya ca the nighāta.

Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 11). Amṛtasya — the root mṛṅ prāṇatyāge; the suffix kta in the sense of the action; na vidyate mṛtaṃ yasya saḥ tasya; ñño jaramarami… — the initial acute of the latter member [amṛtāḥ]. Nabhojuvaḥ — ju is a sautra root; used in the sense of motion; the suffix kvip; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt — the accent of the latter member. Praśastaye — the root śaṃsu stutau; in the sense of action by striyāṃ ktin the suffix ktin; anidita… the loss of the nasal; tādau ca niti the prefix (pra) keeps its own accent; dative singular. Mahinā — the word mahiman; in the instrumental singular by alopo 'naḥ the loss of the a of an, and in the Vedic way the loss of the kāra too. Rathavate — rathaḥ asya asti iti rathavān; the suffix matup by tad asyāsti…; mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ the m becomes v; vivakṣātaḥ kārakāṇi bhavanti — hence the dative in the sense of the genitive; the suffix is pit, so it is unaccented. ‖ 11 ‖

The rest of the page is the grammar tail: dhāma — from the root dadhāti with a luṅ…; tātiḥ — from the root tan with ktin, with ātva by vyatyaya; rāran — rā dāne, leṭ, in the Vedic way śap with śluḥ, chandasy ubhayathā… the loss of the ā of the root and of iṭ; reduplicative syllable… — only characterised.

यस्य सूरेर्हविरादिप्रेरकस्य यजमानस्य सम्बन्धिनो दशतयस्य दशेन्द्रियसंवर्धकत्वेन दशावयवस्यान्नस्य नंशे प्राप्तये वयमाहूताः स्म तस्मै यजमानायैतमिदानीं दात्रव्यत्वेन [?] वर्तमानं शर्धं परेषामभिभावकमन्नं तत्प्राप्तिहेतुं बलं वा धाम विदधाम [?] करवामेत्यवोचन् देवाः ॥ धाम । दधातेर्लुजि [?] … येषु देवेषु द्युम्नानि द्योतमानान्यन्नानि वसुताति[र्वसू]नां धनानां तातिर्विस्तारो वसून्येव वा रारन् रमन्ते भृशम् । तातिः । तनोतेः क्तिनि व्यत्ययेनात्वम् । तेषु विश्वे सर्वे देवाः प्रभृथेषु प्रकृष्टभरणेषु यागेषु वाजमन्नं सन्वन्तु ददतु । प्रयच्छन्तु ॥ षणु दाने ॥ यद्वा यस्य सूरेः स्तुतिकर्तुः दशतयस्य दश चमसेष्ववस्थितस्य सोमस्य प्राप्तये वयमाहूताः स्म तस्मादेतं शर्धं धामेत्यवोचन् …

yasya sūrerhavirādiprerakasya yajamānasya sambandhino daśatayasya daśendriyasaṃvardhakatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya naṃśe prāptaye vayamāhūtāḥ sma tasmai yajamānāyaitamidānīṃ dātravyatvena [?] vartamānaṃ śardhaṃ pareṣāmabhibhāvakamannaṃ tatprāptihetuṃ balaṃ vā dhāma vidadhāma [?] karavāmetyavocan devāḥ ‖ dhāma | dadhāterluji [?] … yeṣu deveṣu dyumnāni dyotamānānyannāni vasutāti[rvasū]nāṃ dhanānāṃ tātirvistāro vasūnyeva vā rāran ramante bhṛśam | tātiḥ | tanoteḥ ktini vyatyayenātvam | teṣu viśve sarve devāḥ prabhṛtheṣu prakṛṣṭabharaṇeṣu yāgeṣu vājamannaṃ sanvantu dadatu | prayacchantu ‖ ṣaṇu dāne ‖ yadvā yasya sūreḥ stutikartuḥ daśatayasya daśa camaseṣvavasthitasya somasya prāptaye vayamāhūtāḥ sma tasmādetaṃ śardhaṃ dhāmetyavocan …

"[The gods said:] 'We were called for the sake of obtaining (naṃśe) the daśataya — the tenfold, i.e. the food of ten parts, as it increases the ten organs — [belonging] to the sacrificer who is the impeller of oblations and the rest (sūri). For that sacrificer we, at this time, establish (vidadhāma) this śardha (the food that overcomes the others, or the strength that is the means of getting it) as what is to be given' — thus the gods said. [For] in the gods in whom dyumnāni, the shining foods, are [found], vasutātiḥ, the spreading of wealth — or rāran, they delight greatly in treasures —; may all those gods give (sanvantu, let them give, let them bestow) food at the prabhṛtheṣu, the sacrifices with excellent preparations." Or else: "of the Soma standing in the ten camasa cups, of the praiser (sūri) — we were called for obtaining it; therefore the gods said: 'this śardha we establish'."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Yasya sūreḥ — of which praising sacrificer; daśatayasya — (ten-sense-organ-increasing) of the food with ten parts; naṃśe — for obtaining (we who have been called); (tasmai — to that sacrificer); etam — this (now to be given); śardham — food that gives strength to overcome others; dhāma — we give; iti avocan — thus (the gods) said; yeṣu — in which gods; dyumnāni — shining foods and the like; vasutātiḥ — the wealth too; rāran — delighting; (te — those); viśve — all (gods); prabhṛtheṣu — in sacrifices where excellent preparations are made; vājam — food; sanvantu — let them give. [Or: yasya sūreḥ — of which sacrificer; daśatayasya — [of the Soma that stands] in the ten camasas; naṃśe — for obtaining (we are called); tasmai — for that sacrificer; etaṃ śardham — this food; dhāma — we give; ity avocan — (the gods) said (therefore).]

original p. 54

Pratipadārtha, concluded: yeṣu — in which sacrifices; vasutātiḥ — the wealth in the form of oblation, spreading (the priests); dyumnāni — excellent oblations; rāran — delighting; (teṣu — in those); prabhṛtheṣu — in sacrifices with excellent preparations; vājam — food in the form of Soma; viśve — all the gods; sanvantu — let them accept.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. (The gods say: "Accepting [the oblation], to the sacrificer who invokes us [with the ten organs' increasing offering] we give this food of ten parts, which gives strength": thus the Viśvedevas say.) May the Viśvedevas, who are endowed with shining food and the like and with wealth, accept the food and the like in these sacrifices that we have prepared. Or else, "to the sacrificer who invokes us to drink the Soma-juice prepared in the ten camasas, [we give] the strength-increasing food": thus say the Viśvedevas; may they accept the oblations in the form of Soma-juice, prepared by the priests who offer the oblation.

Printed English (as printed): The gods have declared—"We confer present vigour upon the worshipper (who invokes us) to partake of the decupled (libation)" May all (the gods) in whom splendours and riches abound, bestow (abundant) food at (solemn) sacrifices.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 12.

śardham — Among the twenty-eight names of strength beginning ojaḥ, pājaḥ, the word śardha is recorded (Ni. 2-9 [?] — as read by me; the reader's OCR gives "39", the hyphen lost, which may be 3-9 or 2-9), so śardha means strength. The bhāṣyakāra has given, in this ṛk, for the word śardha the meaning balam and, as pareṣām abhibhāvakam annam — "food that gives the capacity to overcome others (enemies)". Besides this, in other ṛks, according to the context, he has given different meanings to this word. For example:

क्रीळं वः शर्धो मारुतमनर्वाणं रथे शुभम् । कण्वा अभि प्र गायत ॥

krīḷaṃ vaḥ śardho mārutamanarvāṇaṃ rathe śubham | kaṇvā abhi pra gāyata ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-37-1, as read.) In this ṛk śardha means strength; and in

प्र शंसा गोष्वघ्न्यं क्रीळं यच्छर्धो मारुतम् । जम्भे रसस्य वावृधे ॥

pra śaṃsā goṣvaghnyaṃ krīḷaṃ yacchardho mārutam | jambhe rasasya vāvṛdhe ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-37-5 [?], as read.) śardhaḥ — prasahanaśīlaṃ tejaḥ: "a power that overpowers" — that is, an unobstructed brilliance (tejas), he says.

Special topics, Ṛk 12 (continued). śardham (continued):

इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमूतये मारुतं शर्धो अदितिं हवामहे ।

indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimūtaye mārutaṃ śardho aditiṃ havāmahe |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-106-1, as read.) In this ṛk mārutaṃ śardhaḥ means the strength of the Maruts — a strength in the form of a group-power.

स हि शर्धो न मारुतं तुविष्वणिरप्नस्वतीषूर्वरास्विष्टनिरार्तनास्विष्टनिः ।

sa hi śardho na mārutaṃ tuviṣvaṇirapnasvatīṣūrvarāsviṣṭanirārtanāsviṣṭaniḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-127-6 [?], as read.) In this ṛk mārutaṃ śardhaḥ is explained as the strength of the Maruts — or the strength in the form of the group-power of the deities, the Maruts, which ordinarily this word indicates; and in ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-71-8; 1-139-1 it is used of Agni too. Since food, or sustenance, is a strengthener of power, the bhāṣyakāra has taken the word in the ṛk in hand as food that gives strength.

daśatayasya — daśendriyasaṃvardhakatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya: "of the food of ten parts, as it increases the ten organs" — that is, food that nourishes the body that has ten organs. In the next ṛk of this same Sūkta [that is, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-13] this word occurs; there the bhāṣyakāra says daśatayasya dhāseḥ dāśendriyatṛptisādhanatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya … daśacamasagṛhītatvād annasya daśavidhatvam — he explains it as "ten kinds of food that are the means of satisfying the ten organs". [As] the food (or Soma) is held in ten camasa vessels, there are ten kinds. And in

मा मामेधो दशतयश्चितो धाक् प्र यद्वां बद्धस्त्मनि खादति ष्ठाम् ।

mā māmedho daśatayaścito dhāk pra yadvāṃ baddhastmani khādati ṣṭhām |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-158-4 [?], as read.) the bhāṣyakāra has explained the word daśatayaḥ as "daśayaḥ — dwelling [in the ten]". Hence the word daśataya has only the meaning "ten-fold" or "of ten kinds". In the context in hand it is explained, so as to fit it, as "that which is the means of satisfying the ten organs".

naṃśe — daśatayasya naṃśe — "to us, [the sacrificers] who offer food in the form of oblation and call [you], give the food that gives strength to bring about the defeat of enemies" — thus the gods speak among themselves; that is the sense.

dyumnāni — Among the twenty-eight names of wealth, mahaṃ rekṇaḥ and so on, the word dyumna is recorded (Ni. 2-10 [?] — as read by me; the reader's OCR gives "39" for the Nirukta reference here too, the hyphen lost), so dyumnāni means "riches". In this ṛk the bhāṣyakāra has explained dyotamānānnāni:

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; the hyphens, and sometimes a digit, may be lost — e.g. "4-628" is 4-6xx — so use only as a check on the readings above): 1-71-8; 1-139-1; 1-122-13

"foods that shine, that is, nourishing foods" (Ni. 5-5 [?] — as read by me; the OCR has "39" in this place). Yāska says: dyumnaṃ dyotateḥ yaśo vā annaṃ vā — "dyumna is from dyut, 'to shine': glory, or food" — and with this derivation (of "the glory that shines well, or food"), to support this meaning:

शतं ते शिप्रिन्नूतयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु । जहि वर्धर्नुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥

śataṃ te śiprinnūtayaḥ sudāse sahasraṃ śaṃsā uta rātirastu | jahi vardharnuṣo martyasyāsme dyumnamadhi ratnaṃ ca dhehi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3[?]-[?], as read.) — they have cited this ṛk as an example.

vasutātiḥ — vasūnāṃ dhanānāṃ tātir vistāraḥ: "the spread (abundance) of wealth" — wealth in abundance, abundant wealth. The word vasutāti occurs in the ṛk that follows and nowhere else. For this word the bhāṣyakāra [says] vasutātir vasūnāṃ haviḥ-lakṣaṇānāṃ dhanānāṃ vā vistārayitāra ṛtvijaḥ | vacanavyatyayaḥ — "the priests who spread the wealth in the form of oblations; the number is changed [from plural to singular]"; since the priests offer oblation-wealth, "vasutātiḥ" means the priests. Here he has said the singular is used in place of the plural by vyatyaya.

prabhṛtheṣu — prakṛṣṭabharaṇeṣu yāgeṣu: "in sacrifices which are attended with excellent preparations" — in sacrifices equipped with excellent materials.

As the main intention of the second half of this ṛk, one may say, according to the opinion of the Western scholar Wilson: "all the deities should come and accept the foods in the form of Soma, which the priests offer abundantly in the sacrifice."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 12, noted briefly; sūtra numbers not reproduced). Dhāma — the root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ — loṭ-sense in luṅ; in the 1st person plural the suffix mas; nityaṃ ṅitaḥ — the s is dropped; when cli comes, sic; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu — its luk; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi — the aṭ augment does not come; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Avocan — the root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; luṅ, 3rd plural, the suffix jhi; elision of the i; jhoṃtaḥ — the ant; when cli comes, asyativakti khyātibhyo 'ṅ — the aṅ; vaca um — …

Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 12, noted briefly). Avocan (concluded) — the augment um in the root after aṅ …; by mider guṇaḥ [as printed in part] guṇa; the augment aṭ for the stem; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Daśatayasya — daśa avayavā asya, daśatayan; saṅkhyāyā avayave tayap the suffix tayap; since it is pit, the suffix ini-like is unaccented. Vasutātiḥ — vasūnāṃ tātiḥ vasutātiḥ; the root tan vistāre; in the sense of action by striyāṃ ktin the suffix ktin; by vyatyaya the ā-substitution for the root when it follows; marutvṛdhādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṅkhyānam — the accent of the end of the first member; or by sarvadevāt tātil the suffix tātil, which was prescribed [for sarva and deva], comes by vyatyaya in its own sense after this word too; by liti the first-member acute. Rāran — the root ramu krīḍāyām; in the sense of intensity, dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ the suffix yaṅ; yaṅo 'ci ca the luk; after a yaṅluganta the Vedic present sense luṅ; 3rd plural, jhi, the ant, loss of the i; dīrgha iṇkitaḥ — the lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; the connection with the word yeṣu before it, yadvṛttānnityam — the nighāta is prevented; the first-syllable acute of the suffix; the augment aṭ is not [added] in the Vedic way. In the second explanation, the root rā dāne; leṭ, 3rd plural, jhi; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu — the loss of the i; bahulaṃ chandasi — a substitute for śap, śluḥ; taking this as the cause, doubling of the root; chandasy ubhayathā — since the vikaraṇa has the name ārdhadhātuka, sārvadhātuka-cause jit… ato lopa iṭi ca the loss of the root's ā; for that reason abhyastānām ādiḥ the first-syllable acute does not arise. Sanvantu — the root ṣaṇu dāne; loṭ, 3rd plural; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. In the second explanation, the root vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; as before the suffix jhi, the ut substitute; vyatyayo bahulam — u as the vikaraṇa for śap; the form as before. ‖ 12 ‖

Rik 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

मन्दामहे दशतयस्य धासेर्द्विर्यत्पञ्च बिभ्रतो यन्त्यन्ना । किमिष्टाश्व इष्टरश्मिरेत ईशानासस्तरुष ऋञ्जते नॄन् ॥ १३ ॥

mandāmahe daśatayasya dhāserdviryatpañca bibhrato yantyannā | kimiṣṭāśva iṣṭaraśmireta īśānāsastaruṣa ṛñjate nṝn ‖ 13 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

मन्दामहे । दशतयस्य । धासेः । द्विः । यत् । पञ्च । बिभ्रतः । यन्ति । अन्ना । किम् । इष्टाश्वः । इष्टरश्मिः । एते । ईशानासः । तरुषः । ऋञ्जते । नॄन् ॥ १३ ॥

mandāmahe | daśatayasya | dhāseḥ | dviḥ | yat | pañca | bibhrataḥ | yanti | annā | kim | iṣṭāśvaḥ | iṣṭaraśmiḥ | ete | īśānāsaḥ | taruṣaḥ | ṛñjate | nṝn ‖ 13 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

मन्दामहे । स्तुमो वयं देवान् । मदि स्तुतौ । इदित्त्वान्नुम् ॥ किमर्थम् । दशतयस्य धासेर्दशेन्द्रियतृप्तिसाधनत्वेन दशावयवस्यान्नस्य यद्यस्माद्द्विः पञ्च दशविधान्यन्नानि । दशचमसगृहीतत्वादन्नस्य दशविधत्वम् । एवंविधमन्नं बिभ्रतो धारयन्तो दश चमसाध्वर्यवो यन्ति होमाय गच्छन्त्याहवनीयं प्रति । यद्वा । आश्वमेधिकानि दशान्नानि जुहोतीत्याम्नातान्याज्यमधुप्रभृतीनि [?] दशविधान्यन्नानि विश्वेभ्यो होतुं धारयन्तो यन्ति यदा तदा मन्दामह इति । न चेष्टाश्वप्रभृतीन्यप्यनिहाय [?] कस्मादस्मान्स्तुत्यागमिष्यन्तीति वाच्यम् । तरुषः शत्रूणां तारकान् । तरतेरौणादिक उसिन् ॥ नॄन् नेतृकर्माणाम् [?] । एवं महानुभावान् वरुणादीन्विश्वांश्च देवानेतन्नामको राजा किमृञ्जते । किं प्रसाधयति । तथेष्वरश्च [?] किमृञ्जते । एते इदानीं वर्तमाना ईशानासः पृथिव्या ईश्वरा राजानश्च किं प्रसाधयन्ति । यद्वा । येषां स्तोतॄणामस्माकमेते स्तुता देवा ईशानासः स्वामिनः किल तादृशांस्तरुषः शत्रूणां तारकान् नॄन् कर्मनिर्वाहकानस्मानिष्टाश्वादयः किं साधयन्ति किमुपद्रवन्ति प्रभवन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

mandāmahe | stumo vayaṃ devān | madi stutau | idittvānnum ‖ kimartham | daśatayasya dhāserdaśendriyatṛptisādhanatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya yadyasmāddviḥ pañca daśavidhānyannāni | daśacamasagṛhītatvādannasya daśavidhatvam | evaṃvidhamannaṃ bibhrato dhārayanto daśa camasādhvaryavo yanti homāya gacchantyāhavanīyaṃ prati | yadvā | āśvamedhikāni daśānnāni juhotītyāmnātānyājyamadhuprabhṛtīni [?] daśavidhānyannāni viśvebhyo hotuṃ dhārayanto yanti yadā tadā mandāmaha iti | na ceṣṭāśvaprabhṛtīnyapyanihāya [?] kasmādasmānstutyāgamiṣyantīti vācyam | taruṣaḥ śatrūṇāṃ tārakān | taraterauṇādika usin ‖ nṝn netṛkarmāṇām [?] | evaṃ mahānubhāvān varuṇādīnviśvāṃśca devānetannāmako rājā kimṛñjate | kiṃ prasādhayati | tatheṣvaraśca [?] kimṛñjate | ete idānīṃ vartamānā īśānāsaḥ pṛthivyā īśvarā rājānaśca kiṃ prasādhayanti | yadvā | yeṣāṃ stotṝṇāmasmākamete stutā devā īśānāsaḥ svāminaḥ kila tādṛśāṃstaruṣaḥ śatrūṇāṃ tārakān nṝn karmanirvāhakānasmāniṣṭāśvādayaḥ kiṃ sādhayanti kimupadravanti prabhavantītyarthaḥ ‖

150 dpi; some words doubtful, as marked. "Mandāmahe: we praise the gods (the root madi stutau; the num augment because it has the indicatory i). For what purpose? Daśatayasya dhāseḥ — of the food (dhāsi, food) of ten parts, as it is the means of satisfying the ten organs: since there are twice five, ten kinds of food — the food has ten kinds because it is held in ten camasa vessels. Bearing food of this kind, the ten camasa-priests (adhvaryus) go to the āhavanīya fire to make the offering. Or else: ten kinds of food — ghee, honey and so on, mentioned in the Āśvamedhika text ["he offers the ten foods"] — they go carrying, to offer to all the gods; when it is so, mandāmahe, 'we praise'. It must not be said, 'why will [the gods] come to us, leaving even Iṣṭāśva and the others?' [The gods are] taruṣaḥ, 'rescuers (tāraka) of enemies' — from the root tṛ, the uṇādi suffix usin. Nṝn — 'the leaders of deeds'. 'What does the king of this name (Iṣṭāśva) ṛñjate, what does he accomplish [against] such great-souled deities Varuṇa and the rest and all the gods? And so too Iṣṭaraśmi, what do they accomplish? What do these now-existing lords (īśānāsaḥ) of the earth, the kings, accomplish?' Or else: 'to us the praisers who have praised these gods, who are indeed lords (svāmin), what can Iṣṭāśva and the others accomplish [against] such men, we the taruṣaḥ (rescuers of enemies?), the leaders who carry out the sacrificial work — what can they trouble, what power can they have?' — that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Yat — because; daśatayasya — (that increases the ten organs) of ten kinds; dhāseḥ — of food; dviḥ pañca — ten (since it is held in ten camasa vessels); annā — (in the form of oblation) the foods; bibhrataḥ — carrying (the Adhvaryus and others); yanti — go (to make the offering).

(How can they harm?)]

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. When (the Adhvaryus and others) go to offer the ten kinds of food, having taken it in the ten camasas, we praise the Viśvedevas. What satisfaction can Iṣṭāśva, Iṣṭaraśmi and other kings give, as the Viśvedevas are the rescuers of enemies and the carriers out of sacrificial works? (Having obtained the Viśvedevas as lords, how can Iṣṭāśva and the others harm us, who are rescuers of enemies and workers at the rites?)

Printed English (as printed): we rejoice that for the satisfaction of the ten (organs of sense) the (priests) bearing the twice five (ladles of) sacrificial food, proceed (to the altar). What can Ishtashwa; (what can) Ishtarashmi, (what can) those who are now lords of the earth, achieve (with respect) to the leaders of men, the conquerors of their foes?

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 13.

daśatayasya dhāseḥ — daśendriyatṛptisādhanatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya: the commentator explains it as food which is the means of satisfying the ten organs — the five organs of action and the five organs of knowledge, ten in all. Since daśatayasya means "of ten kinds", it can also mean the oblations, Soma, ghee and other materials placed in the ten camasa vessels. The word dhāsi is recorded among the twenty-eight names of food (Ni. 3-9, as read by the reader's OCR).

dviḥ pañca — that is, ten. Daśavidhānyannāni — daśacamasagṛhītatvād annasya daśavidhatvam: here the foods placed in the ten camasa vessels are called "foods of ten kinds".

bibhrataḥ yanti annā — ṛtvijaḥ, that is, the Adhvaryus and the rest, carry in their hands the foods with which the ten vessels are filled, in order to offer them to the gods, and go to the āhavanīya fire to make the oblation.

Special topics of Ṛk 13, continued. …(they go to the fire) with the intention of going near that fire in order to offer. Or else, in the Aśvamedha sacrifice, the commentator gives another meaning: they prepare ten kinds of oblation materials — ghee, honey, food and so on — and go near the fire to offer them to the Viśvedevas.

iṣṭāśvaḥ, iṣṭaraśmiḥ — The commentator has explained these words as kings of these names. Since these words occur nowhere else in the Ṛgveda except in this ṛk, nothing more can be said about them.

īśānāsaḥ — vartamānā pṛthivyā īśvarā rājānaś ca: "the present lords of the earth" — that is, kings, chiefs and so on.

The meaning of the second half of this ṛk is obscure; the seer's intention is not clearly understood.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 13, noted briefly; sūtra numbers not reproduced). Mandāmahe — the root madi stutau; idito num dhātoḥ the num augment; laṭ, 1st plural, the suffix mahiṅ; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere — e for the ṭi-part; the vikaraṇa śap; ato dīrgho yañi — lengthening of the stem's a; at the beginning of the verse-quarter no nighāta; since a lasārvadhātuka follows the a of the stem, by tāsyanudāttet… the a is unaccented, so the root accent remains. Bibhrataḥ — the root ḍubhṛñ bharaṇe; in the sense of laṭ the suffix śatṛ; the vikaraṇa śluḥ; reduplication of the root; bhṛñām it — i in the reduplicative syllable; since sārvadhātukam apit the suffix is ṅit-like, no guṇa; yaṇ substitution; nābhyastāc chatuḥ — in the nominative plural the num augment does not come; abhyastānām ādiḥ — the first-syllable acute. Yanti — the root iṇ gatau, adādi; laṭ, 3rd plural, jhi; jhoṃtaḥ — ant; iṇo yaṇ — yaṇ for the root; since yvoḥ… the nighāta does not arise; the suffix's first-syllable acute. Annā — in the neuter plural, when śi has come, śeś chandasi bahulam the śi is dropped.

Īśānāsaḥ — in the nominative plural when jas comes, ājjaser asuk the augment asuk; for the final s, ruṭ and visarga. 150 dpi; a few words doubtful. "Hiraṇyakarṇam: one whose ear has golden earrings and the like; maṇigrīvam: one whose neck has jewels and the like. These two stand for all the limbs; thus arṇaḥ — a form (araṇīyam rūpam) adorned with ornaments on all limbs, [that is] children and the like who are to be praised. Or [that] form of ours of the kind described: may all the gods (viśve devāḥ) varivasyantu — wait upon [us], bestow [it]. Aryaḥ — the company of all the deities, worthy to be approached; jagmuṣīḥ — the praises coming out of the praiser's mouth; usrāḥ — milk, ghee and other oblations (the word for the original [cow] is used for the product): may they at once — immediately after our sacrifice — desire (cākantu), 'wish': śap with śluḥ and parasmaipada in the Vedic way; or else the num is absent when the luk of yaj; or ā cākantu may be joined: 'let them wish sufficiently'. In what? Asme, in our — both the praises and the sacrificers; or, in both our results in this world and the next."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Hiraṇyakarṇam — one who has golden earrings; maṇigrīvam — one who has a jewelled necklace; arṇaḥ — one of pleasing form; tat — sons and the like; naḥ — to us; viśve devāḥ — Viśvedevas; varivasyantu — may they favour; aryaḥ — the company (of the Viśvedevas) worthy of praise; ā jagmuṣīḥ — coming from the mouth of the praiser; giraḥ — the praising words; usrāḥ — the oblations of milk and the like; asme — of us (to us); ubhayeṣu — in the two kinds of results (the benefits of this world and the next); sadyaḥ — at once; ā cākantu — may they greatly desire (may they favour strongly).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. May the Viśvedevas favour us with sons and the like, adorned with earrings and jewelled necklaces; may that venerable company [of the gods] accept the praises that issue from the mouth of the praiser, and the oblations given by the sacrificer. May they strongly desire (apekṣa, accept) both the results — of this world and of the next — of us who are theirs.

Printed English (as printed): May all the gods favour us with a person decorated with golden earrings and jewel necklace: may the venerable (company of the deities) be propitiated by the praises issuing (from the mouth of the worshipper): may our offerings be acceptable to them, and (may they be pleased) with both (our praises and offerings).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 14.

hiraṇyakarṇam, maṇigrīvam — the prayer is that the deities should bless us with children and others who wear golden ornaments such as earrings in the ears and jewelled necklaces and other ornaments on the neck. Or the prayer is: "Be gracious so that we ourselves may wear earrings and the like and jewelled necklaces on the neck."

arṇaḥ — though the word arṇa is recorded among the hundred names of water (Ni. 2-23, as read by the reader's OCR), here the bhāṣyakāra explains araṇīyaṃ rūpaṃ — "a son of pleasing form".

aryaḥ — the word arya has the meaning of master, lord; here the bhāṣyakāra says "the group of the Viśvedevas".

gira ā jagmuṣīḥ — the praising words coming forth from our mouth.

usrāḥ — usriyeti gonāma | usrāviśvo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ usreti ca (Ni. 4-19, as read by the reader's OCR) — "usriyā is a name of the cow; usrā …". Though the word usrāḥ means "cows that give milk", as the bhāṣyakāra says, vikāre prakṛtiśabdaḥ — "the name of the original is used for the product": kṣīrājyādīni haviṃṣi ca — milk, ghee and the like; by usage the word usrāḥ is employed for things made from cows, namely milk, ghee and the like. In some places usrāḥ also means "rays" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-5 and so on).

ubhayeṣu — two kinds of people, those who praise and those who sacrifice; or, in another sense, this world and the other world.

asme — this word is used in the sense of all seven cases. For example:

  1. asme te bandhuḥ | vayam ity arthaḥ — "asme ity etat padaṃ sarvavibhaktyantam | tasmād ekārtham | ekam eva hy etac chabdarūpaṃ saptasv api vibhaktyartheṣu vartate | prakaraṇādivaśāt tasya niyamo bhavati | tadyathā — prathamāyās tvat — asme te bandhuḥ | vayam ity arthaḥ" — that is, the word asme is used in the sense of the seven cases according to the context; according to the context in each place, any of the seven cases may be given to this word. For example, in the sentence asme te bandhuḥ the word asme has the sense vayam, "we"; this is an example of the meaning of the first case —

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 14, noted briefly; sūtra numbers not reproduced). Hiraṇyakarṇam — hiraṇyaṃ karṇau yasya saḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam: the accent of the first member; accusative singular. Arṇaḥ — the root ṛ gatau; arti iti arṇaḥ; udake nuṭ ca (Uṇ. Sū. 4-636, as read by the reader's OCR) the suffix asun and the augment nuṭ; guṇa of the root and ra; ñnityādir nityam — the initial acute. Varivasyantu — varivas is a nominal stem; when the sense "to do this" is intended, namovarivaścitrāṅaḥ kyac the suffix kyac; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ — it takes the name of a root; loṭ, 3rd plural, jhi, the substitute ut, ant; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Aryaḥ — the root ṛ gatau; āryaḥ svāmivaiśyayoḥ — the suffix yat by irregular formation; āryasya svāmyākhyā ceti (Phiṭ. Sū. 1[?]) the final acute.

Cākantu — the root kamu kāntau; kānti means wish; vyatyayo bahulam — in loṭ, 3rd singular, tu is the parasmaipada suffix and śap gets śluḥ; ślau the reduplication of the root; tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya the lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Asme — the word asmad; when the genitive (locative) ending follows, supāṃ sulug… the substitute śe; śeṣe lopaḥ — the loss of the portion after m; the ending takes the acute. ‖ 14 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

चत्वारः । मा । मशर्शारस्य । शिश्वः । त्रयः । राज्ञः । आयवसस्य । जिष्णोः । रथः । वाम् । मित्रावरुणा । दीर्घऽअप्साः । स्यूमऽगभस्तिः । सूरः । न । द्यौत् ॥ १५ ॥

catvāraḥ | mā | maśarśārasya | śiśvaḥ | trayaḥ | rājñaḥ | āyavasasya | jiṣṇoḥ | rathaḥ | vām | mitrāvaruṇā | dīrgha 'apsāḥ | syūma 'gabhastiḥ | sūraḥ | na | dyaut ‖ 15 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

मा मां कक्षीवन्तं मशर्शारस्य । मशकीकृत्य भृशं शृणोति शारयति वामित्रानिति मशर्शारः । एतन्नामकस्य राज्ञः शिश्वः शिशवः शिशुवदप्रबुद्धाश्चत्वारः पुत्रा बाधन्त इति शेषः ॥ शिशुशब्दस्य जसादिषु छन्दसि वावचनमिति गुणाभावः ॥ तथायवसस्य सर्वतः प्राप्तान्नस्यैतन्नाम्नो राज्ञो जिष्णोर्जयशीलस्य पुत्रास्त्रयस्त्रयोऽपि बाधन्त इति शेषः । हे मित्रावरुणैतन्नामानौ देवौ वां युवयोः सम्बन्धी रथो दीर्घाप्साः अतिविस्तृतरूपः स्यूमगभस्तिः स्यूमिति सुखनाम सुखकरदीप्तिः सन् सूरो न सूर्य इवाद्यौत् । द्योतताम् । उक्तानामस्मद्विरोधिनां पुरतः स्फुरन् भयजनको भवत्वित्यर्थः ॥ द्युतेश्छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति लुङ् । द्युद्भ्यो लुङि [?] इति परस्मैपदम् । सिचि वृद्धिः परस्मैपदेषु इति वृद्धिः । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यडभावे हल्ङ्यादिसंयोगान्तलोपौ । यद्वा । द्य अभिगमने आदादिकः । छान्दसे लुङ्यतो वृद्धिर्लुकि हलि इति वृद्धिः ॥

mā māṃ kakṣīvantaṃ maśarśārasya | maśakīkṛtya bhṛśaṃ śṛṇoti śārayati vāmitrāniti maśarśāraḥ | etannāmakasya rājñaḥ śiśvaḥ śiśavaḥ śiśuvadaprabuddhāścatvāraḥ putrā bādhanta iti śeṣaḥ ‖ śiśuśabdasya jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanamiti guṇābhāvaḥ ‖ tathāyavasasya sarvataḥ prāptānnasyaitannāmno rājño jiṣṇorjayaśīlasya putrāstrayastrayo 'pi bādhanta iti śeṣaḥ | he mitrāvaruṇaitannāmānau devau vāṃ yuvayoḥ sambandhī ratho dīrghāpsāḥ ativistṛtarūpaḥ syūmagabhastiḥ syūmiti sukhanāma sukhakaradīptiḥ san sūro na sūrya ivādyaut | dyotatām | uktānāmasmadvirodhināṃ purataḥ sphuran bhayajanako bhavatvityarthaḥ ‖ dyuteśchandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti luṅ | dyudbhyo luṅi [?] iti parasmaipadam | sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu iti vṛddhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasītyaḍabhāve halṅyādisaṃyogāntalopau | yadvā | dya abhigamane ādādikaḥ | chāndase luṅyato vṛddhirluki hali iti vṛddhiḥ ‖

Small type; the grammar tail with its sūtra references is given as read, partly abbreviated in the print. "Mā: me, Kakṣīvān. Maśarśāra: 'he who makes [enemies] into gnats and greatly crushes (śṛṇoti, śārayati) the foes' — the śiśvaḥ, the four children (sons) of the king of this name, immature as babes, trouble [me] — this must be supplied. In the word śiśu the lack of guṇa in jas etc. is by chandasi vā vacanam. Likewise the three sons of the king āyavasa — of this name, who has obtained food on all sides — the jiṣṇu, 'the victorious' — trouble [me] — this is to be supplied. O Mitra and Varuṇa, deities of these names: your chariot, dīrghāpsāḥ ('of very wide form'), syūmagabhastiḥ — syūma is a name for 'comfort'; being of a comfort-giving radiance, may it shine (adyaut) like the Sun. May it shine; that is, may it be dreadful as it flashes before the enemies spoken of, our opponents. The root dyut, by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ a luṅ; the parasmaipada by dyudbhyo luṅi; vṛddhi in sic before a parasmaipada suffix; bahulaṃ chandasi gives the absence of aṭ, and halṅyābbhyo… the loss of the final s and the conjunct final. Or else: dya abhigamane of the ādādika class; in the Vedic luṅ, ato vṛddhir luki hali — vṛddhi."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Mā — me (Kakṣīvān); maśarśārasya — of the king named Maśarśāra; śiśvaḥ — the immature; catvāraḥ — four (sons); and āyavasasya — of the one named Āyavasa (who has obtained food); jiṣṇoḥ — of the victorious; rājñaḥ — of the king; trayaḥ — three (sons); (bādhante — trouble); he mitrāvaruṇā — O Mitra and Varuṇa; vām — your; rathaḥ — chariot; dīrghāpsāḥ — of very wide form; syūmagabhastiḥ — of comforting light; sūro na — like the Sun; adyaut — may it shine (to be fearful to them).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Mitra and Varuṇa, the four immature sons of the king named Maśarśāra and the three sons of the king named Āyavasa trouble me, Kakṣīvān; may your chariot, of vast form and comforting light, shine like the Sun (to be terrifying to them).

Printed English of Ṛk 15 (as printed): The four (silly) sons of Masarsara, the three of the victorious monarch Ayavasa, (annoy) me. Let your spacious and bright-rayed chariot, Mitra and Varuna, blaze (before them) like the sun, (filling them with fear).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 15.

maśarśārasya, āyavasasya — The commentator's explanation is that these are names of two kings. Who are they? Their story is not told. Since their names are not found elsewhere in the Ṛgveda either, more details cannot be learned. A German scholar named Ludwig has held that Maśarśāra is Murmurāra, Nāpusasa; but there is no proper evidence for it.

dīrghāpsāḥ — apsas is recorded among the fifteen names of form (Ni. 3-13, as read by the reader's OCR). Dīrgha means large, extended; the chariot is "of large, extended form".

syūmagabhastiḥ — syūmam iti sukhanāma — "syūma means comfort-giving; gabhasti — a light or rays": the sense is "with comforting rays".

रथो वां मित्रावरुणा दीर्घाप्साः स्यूमगभस्तिः सूरो नाद्यौत् ।

ratho vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā dīrghāpsāḥ syūmagabhastiḥ sūro nādyaut |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-15.) Mitra and Varuṇa, [we pray], may your chariot, of very bright form, though comforting for the eyes of those who worship, be fierce and terrible, like the light of the Sun, to our enemies — thus Mitra and Varuṇa are prayed.

As to the chariot of Mitra and Varuṇa, whose form is mild to the eyes of the worshippers:

दर्शं नु विश्वदर्शतं दर्शं रथमधि क्षमि । एता जुषत मे गिरः ॥

darśaṃ nu viśvadarśataṃ darśaṃ rathamadhi kṣami | etā juṣata me giraḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3?-[?], as read.) Punaḥśepa says that the chariot of Mitra and Varuṇa is seen by all, and that he himself saw it.

हिरण्यरूपमुषसो व्युष्टावयःस्थूणमुदिता सूर्यस्य । आ रोहथो वरुण मित्र गर्तमतश्चक्षाथे अदितिं दितिं च ॥

hiraṇyarūpamuṣaso vyuṣṭāvayaḥsthūṇamuditā sūryasya | ā rohatho varuṇa mitra gartamataścakṣāthe aditiṃ ditiṃ ca ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-6[?]-[?], as read.) In ṛks such as these the matter of Mitra and Varuṇa mounting the chariot is described.

Catvāraḥ — the word catur; in the nominative plural, catur anaḍuhor āmudāttaḥ — the augment ām with the acute; since it is mit, it comes after the last vowel. Maśarśārasya — the root śṝ hiṃsāyām; after a ṇijanta, the suffix ghañ; vṛddhi of the root's ṛ, with ra; the initial acute by ñnityādir nityam; in the compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt — the accent of the final member by the accent of the original; genitive singular. Śiśvaḥ — śiśu + jas; jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam — by this statement, and jasi ca — no guṇa comes; iko yaṇaci — yaṇ substitution. Jiṣṇoḥ — the root ji jaye; glājisthaś ca gnuḥ — the suffix gnu; since it is git, kṅiti ca — guṇa is prohibited; ādeśapratyayayoḥ — the s of the suffix becomes ṣ; the final acute by the suffix accent; genitive singular. Mitrāvaruṇā — devatādvandve ca — ānaṅ for the former member; the dual ending au, and supāṃ sulug… — ā for it; āmantritasya ca — the nighāta. Syūmagabhastiḥ — syūmāḥ gabhastayaḥ yasya saḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam — the accent of the first member. Adyaut — the root dyut dīptau; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ — luṅ in the sense of loṭ; though it is ātmanepadin, dyudbhyo luṅi — it becomes parasmaipadin; 3rd singular, tip; iś ca — the loss of its i; cleḥ sic — the substitute sic; bahulaṃ chandasi — the augment aṭ does not come; sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu — vṛddhi of the root since sic follows a parasmaipada suffix; the stem is adyaut + s + t; halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt… — the loss of the suffix; saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ — the loss of the s of sic; the form adyaut. Or: the root dya abhigamane …
