Colophon of the Sūkta (Kannada): illige nūra ippatteraḍane sūkta mugidudu — "Here the hundred-and-twenty-second Sūkta ends."

Sūkta 123 — pṛthū rathaḥ (begins at the foot of printed p. 70; the contents table gives p. 71)

Heading (Kannada): nūra ippattamūraneya sūktavu — "The hundred-and-twenty-third Sūkta."

This Sūkta, like the one that follows, is addressed to Uṣas. In this first Maṇḍala the following are the only Sūktas addressed to Uṣas: 30th Sūkta, ṛks 20–22 [?]; the 48th Sūkta (15 ṛks) [?], the 49th Sūkta (4 ṛks) [?], the 92nd Sūkta (18 ṛks) [?], the 113th Sūkta (20 ṛks) [?], the 123rd Sūkta (13 ṛks) [?] and the 124th Sūkta (13 ṛks) [?] (the numerals in this passage are small and were read at 150 dpi only). Leaving aside the last two of these, the others were explained in the earlier parts; now we shall comment on the 123rd and 124th Sūktas.

About the deity Uṣas, Yāska says: uṣāḥ kasmād ucchatīti satyā rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ (Ni. 2-19, as read by the reader's OCR): that is, who is the deity Uṣas? What is her nature? What is the reason for this name? Raising such questions he says: uṣaḥ kasmāt | ucchatīti satyaḥ | ucchī vivāse | vivāsayati hīyaṃ tamāṃsi tasmād ucchatīty enam asyāḥ karttari kārake uṣā ity etad abhidhānaṃ bhavati | kā punar iyam uṣā iti | rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ sa uṣā ity ucyate — he explains that the name is formed from the root ucchī vivāse ("to shine out"), which has the sense of "to send out". What is sent out? Darkness. Because this deity dispels darkness and spreads light, she is called Uṣas. And that time is what? The last part of the night: the time that has no darkness and is full of light, just before sunrise as the night ends, is named uṣaḥkāla, "dawn-time".

"Since the dawn-time arrives after the night passes, the dawn-time is said to be born from the night" — a custom. To support this, Yāska: The verse that Yāska cites continues at the top of p. 71, where it is given in full; it is not written here to avoid reproducing a half-read line.

Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 4". Anuvāda (Kannada). Of the six Sūktas of the eighteenth Anuvāka, which begins with kad itthā, this Sūkta pṛthū rathaḥ is the third. It has thirteen ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says "pṛthuḥ saptonoṣasyaṃ tu" [as read]. The seer of this Sūkta is Kakṣīvān, the son of Dīrghatamas; the metre is Triṣṭubh; since the word tu is used in the sūtra, this Sūkta and the next are addressed to Uṣas. At the time of reciting the prātaranuvāka mantras, this Sūkta and the following one are applied for the mantras connected with the Uṣas rite (uṣasya kratu) — so it is prescribed in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, section ahoṣasyaḥ, by the sūtra pṛthū ratha iti sūkte pratyṛcam ityādi (Āś. 4-14 [as read; the OCR has "4 14", the hyphen lost]); and for the Aśvina-śastra mantras too these two Sūktas are applied, as stated by the sentence prātaranuvāka-nyāyena (Āś. 6-3).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

दक्षिणायाः प्रवृद्धायाः स्वव्यापारकुशलाया उषोदेवतायाः पृथुर्विस्तीर्णो रथोऽयोजि । अश्वैर्युक्तः सन्नद्धोऽभूत् । अत्र यद्यपि देवताविशेषो न श्रुतस्तथापि सूक्तस्योषोदेवताकत्वादुषस इति गम्यते । एनं सन्नद्धं रथममृतासोऽमरणधर्माणो देवासो देवनशीला हविर्भाजो देवा आस्थुः । आस्थितवन्तः । देवयजनं गन्तुमारूढा इत्यर्थः । अनन्तरं सोषाः कृष्णात् कृष्णवर्णाद्रात्रिरूपात्तमसः सकाशादुदस्थात् । उत्थिताभूत् । कृष्णं कृष्यतेर्निकृष्टो वर्णः (नि. २-२०) इति यास्कः । कीदृशी सा । अर्या अरणीया पूजनीया विहाया विविधगमनयुक्ता महती वा । विहाया इति महन्नाम विहायो यह्वः इति तन्नाममु पाठात् । मानुषाय क्षयाय मनुष्याणां निवासाय चिकित्सन्ती अन्धकारनिवारणरूपां चिकित्सां कुर्वती । तमो निवारयन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

dakṣiṇāyāḥ pravṛddhāyāḥ svavyāpārakuśalāyā uṣodevatāyāḥ pṛthurvistīrṇo ratho 'yoji | aśvairyuktaḥ sannaddho 'bhūt | atra yadyapi devatāviśeṣo na śrutastathāpi sūktasyoṣodevatākatvāduṣasa iti gamyate | enaṃ sannaddhaṃ rathamamṛtāso 'maraṇadharmāṇo devāso devanaśīlā havirbhājo devā āsthuḥ | āsthitavantaḥ | devayajanaṃ gantumārūḍhā ityarthaḥ | anantaraṃ soṣāḥ kṛṣṇāt kṛṣṇavarṇādrātrirūpāttamasaḥ sakāśādudasthāt | utthitābhūt | kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣyaternikṛṣṭo varṇaḥ (ni. 2-20) iti yāskaḥ | kīdṛśī sā | aryā araṇīyā pūjanīyā vihāyā vividhagamanayuktā mahatī vā | vihāyā iti mahannāma vihāyo yahvaḥ iti tannāmamu pāṭhāt | mānuṣāya kṣayāya manuṣyāṇāṃ nivāsāya cikitsantī andhakāranivāraṇarūpāṃ cikitsāṃ kurvatī | tamo nivārayantītyarthaḥ ‖

The phrase "tasmin sūkte" and the number-reference of Yāska are read as printed: Ni. 2-20, as in the OCR "2-20" on p. 76; at the end the small-type grammar reference is only characterised. "Of Dakṣiṇā — the grown (pravṛddhā), skilled in her work — the goddess Uṣas, the broad (pṛthu, wide) chariot was yoked (ayoji): it was made ready, fitted with horses. Here, though no particular deity is named, it is understood to be Uṣas, since the Sūkta is addressed to Uṣas. This ready chariot the immortal (amṛtāsaḥ, of deathless nature) gods (devāsaḥ, the shining; the gods who partake of oblations) mounted (āsthuḥ): that is, they ascended in order to go to the place of the divine sacrifice. Afterwards she, Uṣas, kṛṣṇāt, from the black — from the darkness in the form of night — rose up (udasthāt). Kṛṣṇa [is derived] from the root kṛṣ; it is a lower colour (Ni. 2-20), says Yāska. What kind is she? Āryā: worthy of approach, worthy of worship; vihāyāḥ: of various motion, or great — vihāyaḥ is a name of 'great', by its reading among the names of 'great' (yahvaḥ). Mānuṣāya kṣayāya: for the dwelling of men, cikitsantī — making the cure in the form of the removal of darkness: that is, dispelling the darkness."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Dakṣiṇāyāḥ — of the skilful (Uṣas deity); pṛthuḥ — broad; rathaḥ — the chariot; ayoji — was made ready (yoked with horses); enam — this (ready chariot); amṛtāsaḥ — immortal; devāsaḥ — gods; ā asthuḥ — mounted (afterwards); āryā — worshipful; vihāyāḥ — of manifold motion (Uṣas); mānuṣāya kṣayāya — for the dwelling of men; cikitsantī — performing the cure in the form of removing darkness; kṛṣṇāt — from black (darkness); ut asthāt — rose up.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The broad chariot of the skilful (Uṣas deity) was yoked with horses; the immortal gods mounted it. Afterwards the worshipful and many-moving (Uṣas deity), performing a cure in the form of removing darkness for the dwellings of men, rose up from the black (darkness).

Printed English (as printed): The spacious chariot of the graceful (Dawn) has been harnessed ; the immortal gods have ascended it; the noble and all-pervading Ushas has risen up from the darkness, bringing health to human habitations.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 1.

dakṣiṇāyāḥ — pravṛddhāyāḥ svavyāpārakuśalāyāḥ: "of her who is much developed and skilled in carrying out her own work, [the goddess] Uṣas" — the two senses having been given, he has joined this word as an epithet of the deity Uṣas.

Yāska in the Nirukta has given the derivation of the word dakṣiṇā in several meanings (Ni. 1-7, as read by the reader's OCR).

नूनं सा ते प्रति वरं जरित्रे दुहीयदिन्द्र दक्षिणा मघोनी । शिक्षा स्तोतृभ्यो मा ति धग्भगो नो बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥

nūnaṃ sā te prati varaṃ jaritre duhīyadindra dakṣiṇā maghonī | śikṣā stotṛbhyo mā ti dhagbhago no bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1[?]-[?], as read; the OCR is garbled.) For the word dakṣiṇā in this ṛk, the Nirukta explains in one way: dakṣiṇā dakṣateḥ samardhayati karmaṇo vṛddham samardhayatīti — "dakṣiṇā [is so called] because she completes (samardhayati) the work, brings the deficient to fullness". Here the vṛttikāra [Sāyaṇa's predecessor] says: yajñe hi yat kiñcid vigataṛddhikaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati tad iyaṃ samardhayati viśiṣṭaṃ hi yajñasya sādhanam etad iti — "in the sacrifice, whatever is made deficient in its completeness is made complete by this; hence it is a special means of the sacrifice": whatever in the sacrifice is deficient in the means of completion, this makes perfect; therefore this produces prosperity; hence, in the matter of the completion of a sacrifice this is the means — so the meaning is explained. In the second explanation of the Nirukta: api vā pradakṣiṇāgamanād diśam abhipretya digdiśasuprakṛtiḥ [as read, doubtful] — dakṣiṇa means the southern direction. Here the vṛttikāra explains that the priests go round the sacrificial altar in a clockwise (pradakṣiṇa) circuit; the cause of this going round, namely to go first facing the south — [the sense is] that dakṣiṇā in the sense of the southern direction (Ni. 1-2, as read in the OCR). In the third explanation of the Nirukta, dakṣiṇo hasto dakṣateḥ utsāhakarmaṇaḥ ("dakṣiṇa is the hand, from dakṣ in the sense of exertion"): when working, the worker uses the right hand to show his exertion; hence dakṣiṇā means "the right hand". Following this meaning also, [dakṣiṇā] is derived from the root dāś "to give" (dāśater vā syād dānakarmaṇaḥ, "or [it comes] from the root dāś, in the sense of giving"), so that the word dakṣiṇā is formed. Following the three kinds of meaning given by the Nirukta writer, Sāyaṇa explains pravṛddhāyāḥ, "of one who has reached excess" (Ni. 1-3 [?], as read).

kṛṣṇāt — nikṛṣṭavarṇāt naiśāt tamasaḥ (Ni. 1-7 [?], as read): "from the darkness of night, which is of a low (black) colour"; this is the sense. The Nirukta writer —

रुशद्वत्सा रुशती श्वेत्यागादारैगु कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः । समानबन्धू अमृते अनूची द्यावा वर्णं चरत आमिनाने ॥

ruśadvatsā ruśatī śvetyāgādāraigu kṛṣṇā sadanānyasyāḥ | samānabandhū amṛte anūcī dyāvā varṇaṃ carata āmināne ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-2, as printed on p. 71.) — citing this ṛk, [he says] kṛṣṇavarṇā rātriḥ | kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣyater nikṛṣṭo varṇaḥ (Ni. 2-20) — "kṛṣṇa is black-coloured night; [the word] kṛṣṇa is formed from the root kṛṣ; it means a low, base colour" — thus he has explained it.

āryā — araṇīyā pūjanīyā — "worthy of worship": that is, that which is worthy of worship. The word ārya is recorded among the four names of Īśvara ("lord") (Ni. 3-11, as read). The Nirukta writer cites a use of the word ārya in the sense of Īśvara; but the meaning "lord" is explained as fitting one who deserves praise. For example:

प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नामार्यः शंसामि वयुनानि विद्वान् । तं त्वा गृणामि तवसमतव्यान् क्षयन्तमस्य रजसः पराके ॥

pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭa nāmāryaḥ śaṃsāmi vayunāni vidvān | taṃ tvā gṛṇāmi tavasamatavyān kṣayantamasya rajasaḥ parāke ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-5 [?], as read; the OCR has "7-10-5".)

अर्योऽहमीश्वरः स्तोतॄणामर्यस्त्वमसीति वा ।

aryo 'hamīśvaraḥ stotṝṇāmaryastvamasīti vā |

(Ni. 5-9 [?], as read by the OCR.) Here the vṛttikāra says: yasmād aryo 'hamasmi īśvaraḥ stutīnām udīraṇe … or arya asi, ārya īśvaraḥ mad-anugrahāya samarthaḥ — "since I am a master (ārya), able to utter praises, I know well your qualities in order to praise you; therefore you, who are worthy of praise, [I am] able to praise; or, since you are able to show grace, you are (ārya) worshipful" — he explains thus. In this ṛk the word uṣas does not occur, but from the context he has given the sense pūjanīyā for the word āryā in describing the qualities of the deity Uṣas.

vihāyāḥ — vividhagamanayuktā mahatī vā: "Uṣas moves about in many ways, or is filled with greatness". The word vihāyāḥ is recorded in the group of twenty-five names of 'great', beginning with mahat, brahman [as read] (Ni. 3-13, as read by the OCR). The Nirukta writer has cited a use of the word vihāyāḥ in this same sense (Ni. 10-26, as read by the OCR). For example:

विश्वकर्मा विमना आद्विहाया धाता विधाता परमोत संदृक् । तेषामिष्टानि समिषा मदन्ति यत्रा सप्तर्षीन् पर एकमाहुः ॥

viśvakarmā vimanā ādvihāyā dhātā vidhātā paramota saṃdṛk | teṣāmiṣṭāni samiṣā madanti yatrā saptarṣīn para ekamāhuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-82-[?], as read.)

supeśasaṃ sukhaṃ rathaṃ yamadhyasthā uṣastvam | tenā suśravasaṃ janaṃ prāvādya duhitardivaḥ ‖

ratho āyoji — aśvair yuktaḥ saṃnaddho 'bhūt: "the chariot was made ready, yoked with horses". Here "horses" does not mean stallions; as Yāska says in the Nirukta, aruṇo gāva uṣasaḥ — "the red cows are Uṣas's [horses]" — the horses of Uṣas's chariot are the red-coloured cows (or rays) (Ni. 2-18 [?], as read).

enaṃ devāso amṛtāso asthuḥ — the gods, deathless, mounted Uṣas's chariot. The gods' mounting Uṣas's chariot means that at dawn the sacrificer who begins the sacrifice invokes the gods, so that those gods go to the sacrificial altar at dawn together with Uṣas who is riding in her chariot — that is the sense.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 1, noted briefly; the sūtra numbers listed by the reader's OCR for this page are given in the block at the end). Ayoji — the root yuji yoge; luṅ in the passive, 3rd singular, the suffix ta; ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ — ciṇ in place of cli, with the loss of ta by ciṇo luk (ciṇo luk, as printed); the augment aṭ; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Devāsaḥ — the root divu; since it is of the pacādi group the suffix ac; the guṇa of the light penultimate; final acute by cit; when jas follows, ājjaser asuk. Amṛtāsaḥ — the root mṛṅ prāṇatyāge; the suffix kta; with nañ in the compound, ñño jaramarami… the final acute of the latter member; when jas follows, as before the asuk. Asthuḥ — the root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; luṅ, 3rd plural, jhi; cleḥ sic, and by gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ the luk of sic; ātaḥ the substitute jus for jhi; usyapadāntāt the pararūpa; since it follows an atiṅanta the nighāta; so too asthāt in the 3rd singular. Cikitsantī — the root kita nivāse; kitaḥ… (by the sūtra kiter vyādhipratīkāre) the suffix san; taking it as the cause, reduplication of the root by sanyaṅoḥ; by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ the stem cikitsa gets the name of a root; the suffix śatṛ in the sense of the present, …

पूर्वा विश्वस्माद्भुवनादबोधि जयन्ती वाजं बृहती सनुत्री । उच्चा व्यख्ययुवतिः पुनर्भूरोषा अगन्प्रथमा पूर्वहूतौ ॥ २ ॥

pūrvā | viśvasmāt | bhuvanāt | abodhi | jayantī | vājam | bṛhatī | sanutrī | uccā | vi | akhyat | yuvatiḥ | punaḥ 'bhūḥ | ā | uṣāḥ | agan | prathamā | pūrva 'hūtau ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

विश्वस्माद्भुवनात्सर्वस्मात्सुप्ताद्भूतजातात्पूर्वा प्रथमा सेयमुषा अबोधि । बुद्धाभूत् । उषःकालमुपगम्य हि पश्चात्सर्वे प्राणिनः प्रतिबुध्यन्ते । कीदृशी सा । वाजं गमनशीलं प्रकाशं निर्वर्त्याभकारं [?] जयन्ती पराभवं कुर्वती । यद्वा । वाजशब्दोऽन्ननामसु पठितत्वादन्नं नाम । अन्नं वै वाजः (श. ब्रा. ९-३-४-१) इति श्रुतेः । यजमानार्थमन्नं सम्पादयन्ती । बृहती महती सनुत्री सर्वं जगत्सम्भजन्ती धात्री वा प्रकाशस्य । किञ्च सोषा उच्चैरुच्चैरूर्ध्वप्रदेशेषु स्थिता सती व्यख्यत् । विचष्टे । सर्वं जगत्प्रकृतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशी सा । युवतिर्मिश्रणशीला नित्ययौवना वा पुनर्भूः पुनःपुनर्भवनशीला प्रतिदिनं वर्तमानत्वात् । सोषाः पूर्वहूतौ सत्यां प्रथमा मुख्या प्रकृष्टा सत्यागन् देवयजनदेशं प्रत्यागच्छति । प्रथम इति मुख्यनाम प्रतमो भवतीति यास्कः । नि. २-२२ । इतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वमाहूता सती शीघ्रमेवागच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

viśvasmādbhuvanātsarvasmātsuptādbhūtajātātpūrvā prathamā seyamuṣā abodhi | buddhābhūt | uṣaḥkālamupagamya hi paścātsarve prāṇinaḥ pratibudhyante | kīdṛśī sā | vājaṃ gamanaśīlaṃ prakāśaṃ nirvartyābhakāraṃ [?] jayantī parābhavaṃ kurvatī | yadvā | vājaśabdo 'nnanāmasu paṭhitatvādannaṃ nāma | annaṃ vai vājaḥ (śa. brā. 9-3-4-1) iti śruteḥ | yajamānārthamannaṃ sampādayantī | bṛhatī mahatī sanutrī sarvaṃ jagatsambhajantī dhātrī vā prakāśasya | kiñca soṣā uccairuccairūrdhvapradeśeṣu sthitā satī vyakhyat | vicaṣṭe | sarvaṃ jagatprakṛtītyarthaḥ | kīdṛśī sā | yuvatirmiśraṇaśīlā nityayauvanā vā punarbhūḥ punaḥpunarbhavanaśīlā pratidinaṃ vartamānatvāt | soṣāḥ pūrvahūtau satyāṃ prathamā mukhyā prakṛṣṭā satyāgan devayajanadeśaṃ pratyāgacchati | prathama iti mukhyanāma pratamo bhavatīti yāskaḥ | ni. 2-22 | itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvamāhūtā satī śīghramevāgacchatītyarthaḥ ‖

Small type at 150 dpi; the Śatapatha reference and the Nirukta number are partly doubtful, as marked. "From all beings (viśvasmād bhuvanāt) — from all creatures that were asleep — she is first (pūrvā): this Uṣas awoke (abodhi). For after Dawn's arrival all living beings wake. What is she like? Jayantī vājam — overcoming (jayantī) the vāja, the moving light — that is, defeating the darkness [or: vāja is among the names of food: 'food is vāja' (Śa. Brā. 9-3-4-1, as printed "೯-೩-೪-೧"; the OCR reads it clearly) — providing food for the sacrificer]. Bṛhatī: great; sanutrī: she who shares out everything to the world, or the supporter of light. And further, she, Uṣas, standing in lofty regions, vyakhyat: looks at, sees all the world. What is she like? Yuvatiḥ — ever young, or mingling; punarbhūḥ — becoming again and again, as she comes each day. She, Uṣas, the first at the first invocation (pūrvahūtau), chief, excellent, comes (agan) to the place of the divine sacrifice. Prathama is a name of 'chief': 'it becomes pratama', says Yāska (Ni. 2-22, as read by the reader's OCR). The sense: being invoked before the other gods, she comes at once."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Vājam — the moving (the darkness that moves away) or [alternatively] food; jayantī — she who has conquered (and brings [it] to the sacrificer); viśvasmāt — all; bhuvanāt — from creatures (those asleep, born beings); pūrvā — first; bṛhatī — great; sanutrī — giving light (to the world) [she]; uṣāḥ — the deity Uṣas; abodhi — awoke (appeared); (kiñca — and); yuvatiḥ — ever young; punarbhūḥ — she who again and again appears (that [Uṣas]); uccā — from the lofty (regions); vi akhyat — looks at all the world (gives light); (sā — she); pūrvahūtau — at the first prayer (of the day); prathamā — before all, as excellent; ā agan — comes (to the sacrificial region).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Casting off the transient (shadowy) darkness and giving light (to the whole world), the great Uṣas awoke first among all the world (showed herself). Ever young and rising day after day; from a lofty region she looks at the whole world (gives light); at the sacrifice she comes first of all (before all the deities) at the first invocation.

Printed English (as printed): First of all the world is she awake, triumphing over transitory (darkness): the mighty, the giver (of light) from on high, she beholds (all things): ever youthful, ever reviving, she comes first to the invocation.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.

viśvasmāt bhuvanāt pūrvā abodhi — suptāt bhūtajātāt iyam uṣāḥ prathamā abodhi: "from the sleeping creatures, this Uṣas awoke first". For after the dawn-time comes, all living beings awaken afterwards. The sense is: she wakes before all the creatures that sleep; that is, Uṣas rises. Then all awake — this is the sense. Here Sāyaṇa explains the word pūrvā as prathamā.

vājaṃ jayantī — gamanaśīlaṃ prakāśaṃ nirvartya andhakāraṃ parābhavaṃ kurvatī: "the deity Uṣas, removing the darkness connected with the night, makes light so that beings may move about" — this is one sense. Here Sāyaṇa has explained the word vāja as darkness. Then he says yadvā vājaśabdo 'nnanāmasu paṭhitatvād annanāma — "or the word vāja is recorded among names of food": the word vāja is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9), among the names of battle (Ni. 5-9), and as the name of a king (Ni. 1-17); and "oblations" or "water" (Ni. 11-27) (all as read by the reader's OCR, with hyphens partly lost) — he thus gives these meanings, because the Nirukta writer gives them; and since the word is used in the Śruti passages in the sense of food — annaṃ vai vājaḥ (Śa. Brā. 9-3-4-1, Tai. Brā. 1-3-6-2, as read by the reader's OCR) — he also gives the meaning "food". Thereby yajamānārthaṃ annaṃ saṃpādayantī, "she provides food for the sake of the sacrificer" — another meaning. Thus he has given two meanings.

bṛhatī sanutrī — mahatī sarvaṃ jagat sambhajantī dātrī vā prakāśasya: "great, sharing everything with the world, or giver of light". He explains that Uṣas stirs all the creatures in the world to go about their tasks, or that she is endowed with a greatness by which she makes light for the benefit of the whole world: two meanings. The Nirukta writer says that the word bṛhatī denotes "filled with greatness".

रमध्वं मे वचसे सोम्याय ऋतावरीरुप मुहूर्तमेवैः । प्र सिन्धुमच्छा बृहती मनीषावस्युरहवे कुशिकस्य सूनुः ॥

ramadhvaṃ me vacase somyāya ṛtāvarīrupa muhūrtamevaiḥ | pra sindhumacchā bṛhatī manīṣāvasyurahave kuśikasya sūnuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33-5, as read.) For the word bṛhatī in this ṛk he has given the meaning mahatyā, "great".

आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ । दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥

punarbhūḥ — punaḥ punar bhavanaśīlā pratidinaṃ vartamānatvāt: "she who becomes again and again, since she is present every day": because Uṣas rises every day, it means she has a nature that stays differently on each day. That is, she is born again and again. Therefore in many ṛks it is said that this deity Uṣas is ever young:

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-10 [?], as read.) In ṛks such as these Uṣas is described as rising again and again.

pūrvahūtau satyām uṣāḥ prathamā — mukhyā — that Uṣas, at the sacrifice, when she is invoked before the other deities for the acceptance of the oblation, comes to the place where the sacrifice is going on, in front of all the deities: that is the sense. Itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvam āhūtā satī śīghram evāgacchatīty arthaḥ — this is Sāyaṇa's explanation.

Yāska gives for the word prathama the meaning "chief":

देवानां माने प्रथमा अतिष्ठन् कृन्तत्रादेषामुपरा उदायन् । त्रयस्तपन्ति पृथिवीमनूपा द्वा बर्बूकं वहतः पुरीषम् ॥

devānāṃ māne prathamā atiṣṭhan kṛntatrādeṣāmuparā udāyan | trayastapanti pṛthivīmanūpā dvā barbūkaṃ vahataḥ purīṣam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-27-23, as read by the reader's OCR.) In this ṛk, prathama iti mukhyanāma pratamo bhavati (Ni. 2-22, as read by the reader's OCR): for the word prathama he gives the sense "chief". In this ṛk the vṛttikāra explains prathamāḥ as prakṛṣṭatamāḥ — "most excellent" — i.e. "chief".

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सुजाते शोभनजनने देवि देवनशीले हे उषः उषःकालाभिमानिदेवते मर्त्यत्रा मनुष्याणां पालयित्री त्वमद्यास्मिन्काले नृभ्यो मनुष्येभ्यो यदद्य भागं भजनीयं स्वकीयप्रकाशस्यांशं विभजासि विभज्य ददासि । यद्वा । मर्त्येषु मध्ये नृभ्यो यजमानेभ्यो देवानां भागं विभज्य ददासि । उषसि प्रवृत्तायां हविषो दीयमानत्वादुषसो वाऽतृत्वमुपचर्यते । अत्रास्मिन्भागविषये दमूना यजमानेभ्योऽभिमतफलदानमनाः । दमूना दममना वा दानमना वा दान्तमना वेति निरुक्तवचनं (नि. ४-४) तादृशः सविता प्रेरको देवोऽस्मान् अनागसो वोचति । अपापान् याग-योग्यान्स्वेतु । अनुग्रहाया… इत्यर्थः । किमर्थम् । सूर्यायास्माद्यागदेशं प्रति सूर्यस्यागमनार्थम् ॥

sujāte śobhanajanane devi devanaśīle he uṣaḥ uṣaḥkālābhimānidevate martyatrā manuṣyāṇāṃ pālayitrī tvamadyāsminkāle nṛbhyo manuṣyebhyo yadadya bhāgaṃ bhajanīyaṃ svakīyaprakāśasyāṃśaṃ vibhajāsi vibhajya dadāsi | yadvā | martyeṣu madhye nṛbhyo yajamānebhyo devānāṃ bhāgaṃ vibhajya dadāsi | uṣasi pravṛttāyāṃ haviṣo dīyamānatvāduṣaso vā 'tṛtvamupacaryate | atrāsminbhāgaviṣaye damūnā yajamānebhyo 'bhimataphaladānamanāḥ | damūnā damamanā vā dānamanā vā dāntamanā veti niruktavacanaṃ (ni. 4-4) tādṛśaḥ savitā prerako devo 'smān anāgaso vocati | apāpān yāga-yogyānsvetu | anugrahāyā… ityarthaḥ | kimartham | sūryāyāsmādyāgadeśaṃ prati sūryasyāgamanārtham ‖

Small type; I could not settle some letters at the end of the passage; the sense as given in the Kannada follows. "O well-born, divine Uṣas, deity presiding over the dawn-time, protectress of mortals (martyatrā): whatever share (bhāga) to be enjoyed, a part of your own light, you apportion (vibhajāsi) to men today — or: among mortals, you divide and give the gods' portion to the sacrificers, since the oblation is given once Uṣas has begun, [and hence] the giving is figuratively attributed to Uṣas. In this matter of the share, may the god Savitṛ, the impeller, damūnāḥ — whose mind is bent on giving the desired fruit to the sacrificers [damūnā is dama-manāḥ, 'of subdued mind', or dāna-manāḥ, 'of giving mind', or dānta-manāḥ, 'of restrained mind' — Nirukta (Ni. 4-4, as read by the reader's OCR)] — declare us (vocati) sinless (anāgasaḥ), fit for the sacrifice: out of grace. For what purpose? For the sake of the Sun's coming (sūryāya) to the sacrificial place."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Sujāte — O well-born one; devi — O one of shining nature; he uṣaḥ — O deity Uṣas; martyatrā — protectress of men (you); adya — now; nṛbhyaḥ — for men (for the sacrificers); yat — whatever; bhāgam — (your) share of light (and the share of oblation); vibhajāsi — you apportion (to the gods); atra — in this matter of the share; damūnāḥ — (disposed to give the desired [fruit] to the sacrificers) or in giving, of good mind; devaḥ savitā — the god Savitṛ; naḥ — us; anāgasaḥ — free from sin (fit for the sacrifice); sūryāya — for the Sun (to come to our sacrificial hall); vocati — may he tell.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O well-born, divine Uṣas, you who protect men! Whatever portion of your light you now apportion to men — to men who perform sacrifices, the portion of the oblation to the several gods — in that matter may the god Savitṛ, disposed to give what is desired to the sacrificers, declare us sinless and fit for the sacrifice, so that the Sun may come to our sacrificial hall.

original p. 85

Printed English (as printed): Well-born and divine Ushas, you are the protectress of mortals; whatever share (of light) you apportion to-day to men, may the radiant Savitri be disposed (to confirm) the gift, and declare us free from sin; so that (he) the sun (may come to our sacrificial hall).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.

martyatrā bhāgaṃ vibhajāsi nṛbhyaḥ — manuṣyāṇāṃ pālayitrī tvaṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ svakīyaprakāśasyāṃśaṃ vibhajya dadāsi | yadvā martyeṣu madhye yajamānebhyo devānāṃ bhāgaṃ vibhajya dadāsi: "Uṣas, the protectress of men, gives men separately a part of her light for their benefit — that is one sense." "To the sacrificers, who deserve protection among men, Uṣas gets the gods' respective shares of the oblation distributed separately" — that is another sense. Both meanings are explained by Sāyaṇa in the bhāṣya. In the first meaning the word martyatrā is used in the sense "protectress of men"; in the second meaning the word nṛbhyaḥ, though a general word for men, indicates a speciality of those who perform sacrifices.

It is Agni himself who apportions the oblation shares to the gods. But since, when the dawn-time has come, the oblation is at once offered in the fire, the character of "giver of the oblation shares" is attributed to Uṣas figuratively (aupacārika). He has stated this clearly: uṣasi pravṛttāyāṃ haviṣo dīyamānatvāt uṣaso dātṛtvam upacaryate.

damūnāḥ — yajamānebhyo 'bhimataphaladānamanāḥ: "one with a mind to grant the desired fruit to the sacrificers". In the Nirukta the word damūnāḥ (Ni. 4-4, as read by the reader's OCR) is explained damanamanāḥ — one with a cruel/restrained mind [as printed]; or dānamanāḥ, one willing to give; or dāntamanāḥ, one whose mind is calmed by the restraints (yama, niyama); or "…

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 4-4

original p. 86

Special topics of Ṛk 3, concluded. …[damūnāḥ] — having explained four kinds of meaning, he applies the epithet damūnāḥ gṛhapatir agniḥ ("the household lord Agni, damūnāḥ") to Agni. Here the epithet damūnāḥ devaḥ savitā, in the phrase "the god Savitṛ", is applied to Savitṛ; this indicates the identity of Agni (or the Sun) with Savitṛ; or it suggests that, like Agni, the god Savitṛ too has a greatness of the kind that makes him a damūnas.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 3; sūtra numbers as read by the reader's OCR). Vibhajāsi — the root bhaja sevāyām; leṭ, 2nd singular, the suffix sip; leṭo 'ḍāṭau (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) the augment aḍ; since there is a connection with yat the nighāta does not arise; since sip and śap are pit they are unaccented, so the root accent remains. Martyatrā — in the sense of the seventh case (among men) by devamanuṣyapuruṣamartyebhyo dvitīyāsaptamībhyāṃ… (Pā. Sū. 5-4-56) the suffix trā; the final acute by the suffix accent. Sujāte — śobhanaṃ jātaṃ jananaṃ yasyāḥ sā sujātā; the vocative singular form; by āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the nighāta. Anāgasaḥ — na vidyate āgo yeṣāṃ te anāgasaḥ; nalopo nañaḥ — the loss of the n of nañ; tasmān nuḍ aci — the augment nuṭ before a vowel; in the indeclinable-prefixed compound the first member's accent; accusative plural. Vocati — the root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; leṭ, 3rd singular, tip; adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ the luk of śap; leṭo 'ḍāṭau — the augment aḍ for the stem, by vyatyaya; vaca um (Pā. Sū. 7-4-20) the augment um; since it is mit it comes after the last vowel; guṇa; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Sūryāya — the root sṛ gatau; sarati iti sūryaḥ — rājasūyasūrya… (Pā. Sū. 3-1-114) formed with the suffix kyap by irregular formation; since it is pit it is unaccented, so the root accent remains; dative singular. ‖ 3 ‖

अहना । उषोनामैतत् । अहना द्योतनेति तन्नाममु पाठात् । सा देवी दिने दिने प्रत्यहं दिवे दिव इत्यहर्नाममु पाठात् । गृहं गृहं तत्तद्यज्ञ-गृहमच्छाभिमुख्येन याति । गच्छति । कीदृशी । अध्यधिकं नाम नमनं प्रह्वत्वमुद्योगं प्रतिगृहमुद्योगं प्रकाशनरूपं दधाना धारयन्ती । यद्वा । अधि दधानाधिकं धारयन्ती । किञ्च सिषासन्ती सम्भक्तुमिच्छन्ती द्योतना कृत्स्नं जगद्द्योतनशीला शश्वत् प्रतिदिनमागात् । आगच्छति । पूर्वं यातीत्युक्तत्वात्पुनरागादिति वचनमावश्यकत्वद्योतनार्थम् । आगत्य च वसूनां धनानां हविर्लक्षणानामग्रमग्रमित् तत्तच्छ्रेष्ठभागं भजते सेवते स्वीकरोतीत्यर्थः ॥

Small type; the passage marked [?] is a doubtful stretch; the Kannada commentary below confirms the sense. "Ahanā: this is a name of Uṣas, by its reading among the names ahanā, dyotanā. She, the goddess, comes day by day (dive dive — read among the names of 'day'). She goes (yāti) to house after house — to each sacrificial house — facing it (accha). What is she like? Adhi nāma dadhānā: bearing an excess of nāma, 'bending', that is 'eagerness', 'effort' — bearing for every house an effort in the form of light; or adhi dadhānā — bearing more. And, desiring to confer (siṣāsantī), illuminating the whole world (dyotanā), she has come (āgāt), always, every day. Having come, she takes (bhajate, serves, accepts) the foremost, the choicest portion (agram agram), of the riches — of the wealth in the form of oblations."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Ahanā — the deity Uṣas; dive dive — every day; adhi — in excess; nāma — the effort (the bending) of the form of light; dadhānā — bearing; gṛhaṃ gṛham — to every sacrificial house; accha yāti — she goes facing; (kiñca — and); siṣāsantī — wishing to bestow favour; dyotanā — illuminating the world; śaśvat — always (every day); āgāt — she comes (having come); vasūnām — of the oblations and the like; agram agram it — the choicest portions only; bhajate — she accepts.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Uṣas, assuming each day the effort (udyoga) in the form of light, goes to every house of sacrifice; wishing to favour (the sacrificers), illuminating the world, she comes always, every day; having come she accepts only the choicest part of the oblations offered.

original p. 88

Printed English (as printed): Ahana, charged with downward-bending (light), goes daily from house to house; she comes, perpetually diffusing light, and desirous of bestowing (benefits), and accepts the choicest portions of (the sacrificial) treasures.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 4.

ahanā — "the deity Uṣas": that is the sense. Among the sixteen names of Uṣas beginning vibhāvarī, sūnarī, bhāsvatī (Ni. 2-19) the word ahanā too is declared (see the introduction of this Sūkta).

dive dive — since this word is declared (Ni. 2-21) among the twelve names of "day" beginning vasoḥ, dyauḥ, bhānuḥ, it means "every day".

accha — acchābhi-rāptam iti śākapūṇiḥ (Ni. 5-15, as read by the reader's OCR): "the word accha is used in the sense of abhi and in the sense of āptam — so the opinion of the teacher Śākapūṇi". Sāyaṇa here gives for the word accha the sense ābhimukhyena, "facing". Gṛhaṃ gṛham accha yāti — the sense is "the deity Uṣas enters the sacrificial houses with favour".

adhi nāma dadhānā — in this sentence Sāyaṇa explains adhikaṃ namanaṃ prahvatvam udyogaṃ prakāśanarūpaṃ pratigṛhaṃ dadhānā: "Uṣas bears in every house her extraordinary light-effort" — that is one explanation; or adhi dadhānā adhikaṃ dadhānā: "bearing exceedingly light" — another: thus two explanations.

gṛhaṃgṛham ahanā yāti — "Uṣas shines in every house"; and by saying again śaśvat āgāt ("she comes every day"), the necessity of the coming of Uṣas is shown.

vasūnām agram agram it bhajate — dhanānāṃ havirlakṣaṇānāṃ tattacchreṣṭhabhāgaṃ svīkarotīty arthaḥ: "the deity Uṣas accepts the several choice portions of the oblations offered by the sacrificers" — that is the sense. The word vasu conveys many meanings. This word is declared among the names of rays (Ni. 2-15, as read by the reader's OCR) and among the names of wealth, maghaṃ rekṇaḥ and the rest (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR; the OCR gives "3, 3-9").

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

भगस्य स्वसा वरुणस्य जामिरुषः सूनृते प्रथमा जरस्व । पश्चा स दध्या यो अघस्य धाता जयेमं तं दक्षिणया रथेन ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सूनृते सुष्ठु मनुष्याणां नेत्र्यृतो हे उषो देवते भगस्य सर्वैर्भजनीयस्यादित्यस्य स्वसासि । स्वसृस्थानीयासि । तेन सहोत्पद्यमानत्वात्प्रसूतत्वाद्वेत्यर्थः । तथा वरुणस्य तमोनिवारकस्य सवितुर्देवस्य जामिरसि । भगिनीस्थानीयासि । एकस्मिन्नेव स्थाने उत्पद्यमानत्वात् । जनयन्त्यपत्यान्यस्यामपत्कमन्य इति जामिः [?] । यद्वा । जमति गच्छति स्वोत्पत्तिस्थानादन्यत्रेति । उक्तनिर्वचनद्वयमभिप्रेत्य यास्क आह । न जामयेभगिन्यै [?] जामिरन्यस्यां जनयन्ति जामिपत्कं जमतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मणो निर्गमनप्राया भवति (नि. ३-६ [?]) इति । तादृशी त्वं प्रथमेतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वोत्कृष्टा वा सती जरस्व । स्तुता भव । जरतिः स्तुतिकर्मा (नि. १०-८) इति यास्कः । पश्चा पश्चात्त्वत्स्तुतेरनन्तरं योऽघस्य दुःखस्य कस्मिंश्चिद्दुःखस्य कारणस्य वा पापस्य धाता धारयिता [?] अस्ति स सः पापी दध्याः । गच्छतु । वचनव्यत्ययः । दध्य दभ्नोतीति गत्यर्थेषु पाठात् । यदि स पापी बलीयान् तं दक्षिणया प्रवृद्धया सहायभूतया त्वया रथेनास्मदीयरथादिसाधनेन च जयेम ॥

sūnṛte suṣṭhu manuṣyāṇāṃ netryṛto he uṣo devate bhagasya sarvairbhajanīyasyādityasya svasāsi | svasṛsthānīyāsi | tena sahotpadyamānatvātprasūtatvādvetyarthaḥ | tathā varuṇasya tamonivārakasya saviturdevasya jāmirasi | bhaginīsthānīyāsi | ekasminneva sthāne utpadyamānatvāt | janayantyapatyānyasyāmapatkamanya iti jāmiḥ [?] | yadvā | jamati gacchati svotpattisthānādanyatreti | uktanirvacanadvayamabhipretya yāska āha | na jāmayebhaginyai [?] jāmiranyasyāṃ janayanti jāmipatkaṃ jamatervā syādgatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyā bhavati (ni. 3-6 [?]) iti | tādṛśī tvaṃ prathametaradevebhyaḥ pūrvotkṛṣṭā vā satī jarasva | stutā bhava | jaratiḥ stutikarmā (ni. 10-8) iti yāskaḥ | paścā paścāttvatstuteranantaraṃ yo 'ghasya duḥkhasya kasmiṃścidduḥkhasya kāraṇasya vā pāpasya dhātā dhārayitā [?] asti sa saḥ pāpī dadhyāḥ | gacchatu | vacanavyatyayaḥ | dadhya dabhnotīti gatyartheṣu pāṭhāt | yadi sa pāpī balīyān taṃ dakṣiṇayā pravṛddhayā sahāyabhūtayā tvayā rathenāsmadīyarathādisādhanena ca jayema ‖

Small type; a few words doubtful, the sūtra-like references to the Nirukta as read by me: Ni. 3-6 [?] for jāmi, Ni. 10-8 [?] for jarati. "O Sūnṛtā — leader of men in a good way — O deity Uṣas, you are the sister (svasā) of Bhaga — of the Āditya, who is to be served by all: that is, you stand in the place of a sister, since you were produced together with him. And so, you are the jāmi of Varuṇa — of the god Savitṛ, the remover of darkness: you stand in the place of a sister, since you arise in one place. Jāmi — [from] janayanti apatyāni... or from jam, 'to go': 'she goes elsewhere from the place of her birth'. Intending both derivations, Yāska says: na jāmaye 'bhinai jāmir anyasyāṃ janayanti jāmipatkam jamater vā syād gatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyā bhavati (Ni. 3-6 [?]). Such as you are, first (prathamā), or excelling the other gods, jarasva — be praised (jaratiḥ stutikarmā: 'to praise', Ni. 10-8 [?], says Yāska). Paścā — afterwards, after your praise: he who is the bearer (dhātā) of sin (agha) — of some sorrow or of the cause of sorrow — sa dadhyāḥ: let that sinner go (the number is changed; the root dadh, 'to go'); if that sinner is stronger, we shall conquer him with you, the grown (dakṣiṇayā), the helper — with our chariot and other means."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Sūnṛte — O one who leads men to the good path; uṣaḥ — O deity Uṣas (you); bhagasya — of Āditya, who is to be served by all; svasā — the sister; (tathā — likewise); varuṇasya — of Savitṛ, the remover of darkness; jāmiḥ — the sister (you); prathamā — first, before the other deities, best; jarasva — be praised (by us); paścā — afterwards (when we have been pleased by praising); yaḥ — who; aghasya — of sin, the cause of sorrow; dhātā — the supporter; saḥ — he; dadhyāḥ — let him go away (from here); tam — him; dakṣiṇayā — with the helping you; rathena — with our chariot; jayema — we conquer.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Uṣas, leader of men on the good path, you are the sister of Āditya, who is to be served by all, and the sister of Savitṛ, the dispeller of darkness; first and best among all the gods, you are to be praised by us; so we praise you; let the one who is the cause of sorrow (the sin) go away from here; with your help we conquer him with our chariots.

original p. 92

Printed English of Ṛk 5 (as printed): Ushas, endowed with truth, you are the sister of Bhaga, the sister of Varuna, you are hymned first (of the gods): then let the worker of iniquity depart, for we shall overcome him with our chariot, through your assistance.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 5.

bhagasya svasā — sarvaiḥ bhajanīyasya ādityasya svasā svasṛsthānīyā asi: "you are the sister of Āditya, who is to be worshipped by all" — Uṣas the deity is worshipped by all as the sister of the Sun. By the connection of being born together with the Āditya, she is, like the Āditya, worthy of worship by reason of greatness: that is the sense. The word bhaga has many meanings.

The word bhaga is recorded (Ni. 1-7, as read by the reader's OCR) and, in the ṛk "nūnaṃ sā te" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-21, as read by the OCR), it is a word for "wealth", and in (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR; "39") the meaning "wealth" is also given.

वामंवामं त आदुरे देवो ददात्वर्यमा । वामं पूषा वामं भगो वामं देवः करूळती ॥

vāmaṃvāmaṃ ta ādure devo dadātvaryamā | vāmaṃ pūṣā vāmaṃ bhago vāmaṃ devaḥ karūḷatī ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-4[?]-[?], as read; the OCR is garbled.) In this ṛk the word bhaga refers to a god, one among the Ādityas;

श्रद्धयाग्निः समिध्यते श्रद्धया हूयते हविः । श्रद्धां भगस्य मूर्धनि वचसा वेदयामसि ॥

śraddhayāgniḥ samidhyate śraddhayā hūyate haviḥ | śraddhāṃ bhagasya mūrdhani vacasā vedayāmasi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-151-1, as printed.) Here the vṛttikāra explains bhagasya bhāgadheyasya dharmasya — "of Bhaga, of the bhāgadheya [one's allotted portion], of dharma": he gives the word bhaga the sense dharma;

प्रातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम वयं पुत्रमदितेर्यो विधर्ता । आध्रश्चिद्यं मन्यमानस्तुरश्चिद्राजा चिद्यं भगं भक्षीत्याह ॥

prātarjitaṃ bhagamugraṃ huvema vayaṃ putramaditeryo vidhartā | ādhraścidyaṃ manyamānasturaścidrājā cidyaṃ bhagaṃ bhakṣītyāha ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-41-2, as read.) — in ṛks such as this bhaga is used also as a name of the Sun.

varuṇasya jāmiḥ — tamo vārakasya savitur devasya bhaginīsthānīyā asi — "you stand in the place of a sister to the god Savitṛ, who restrains darkness": janayanty apatyāny asyām apatkam anye iti jāmiḥ … (the Kannada explains that Uṣas and Savitṛ, the Sun, have one origin; that is why Sāyaṇa says "they are born in one place"; since the root jam means 'to go', the word jāmi is formed from the root jan: in a woman, offspring are born; this woman is called jāmi because, since she is born here, the family goes to another house — the second sense.) Both these meanings are stated by Yāska.

न जामये भगिन्यै जामिरन्यस्यां जनयन्ति जामिपत्यं जमतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मणो निर्गमनप्रायो भवति ॥

na jāmaye bhaginyai jāmiranyasyāṃ janayanti jāmipatyaṃ jamatervā syādgatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyo bhavati ‖

(Ni. 3-6, as printed "೩-೬"; the Sanskrit as read letter by letter from the large type; I read the first words as na jāmaye bhaginyai and the fourth as jāmipatyam.) Daughters are not entitled to the funeral oblations (? — pāyasa-bhāga) [[?] the first sentence of the Kannada gloss: "women are not fit for a share in the inheritance"]. They are not fit for a share in their brother's estate, since they, having nourished children, are given away to a husband. The word jāmi is well known in the sense "sister"; or the word jāmi formed from the root jam meaning 'to go' conveys the sense 'one who joins, from the family where she was born, another family' — such are the two meanings given by Sāyaṇa, in accord with the intention of the Nirukta writer.

prathamā jarasva — itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvā utkṛṣṭā vā satī stutā bhava: "Uṣas is praised first in the sacrifice; or, being chief above all other deities, is praised" — he gives these two meanings.

Yāska explains jarā stutiḥ jaratiḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 10-8, as read by the OCR) — "jarā means praise: from the root jṝ, 'to praise'"; since the word jarate is recorded among the verbs of praising (Ni. 3-6 [?]), the verb jarati is explained by Sāyaṇa in the sense of praise.

yaḥ aghasya dhātā saḥ dadhyāḥ — yaḥ kaścid duḥkhasya tadutpādakapāpasya vā dhārayitā saḥ gacchatu: "he who holds sorrow — he who has sin that causes sorrow — let him go from here (by your grace) and be conquered by us" — this is the prayer that is explained.

dadhyāḥ — Yāska classes dadhyati, dabhnoti (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR on p. 93) among the verbs meaning 'to go'; hence here he explains the word dadhyāḥ as gacchatu.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 5; sūtra numbers as read by the reader's OCR for p. 94). Jāmiḥ — the root jani prādurbhāve; the suffix iñ of the uṇādi class by bahulagrahaṇa; vyatyaya gives m for the n; janayanty asyām apatyam anye iti jāmiḥ — or jamati gacchati svotpattisthānād anyatra iti jāmiḥ; thus in the second sense, taking the root jam adane, with the suffix iñ as before; since roots have many meanings, it is used in the sense of going. Sūnṛte — the root ūna parihāṇe; sutarāṃ ūnayati apriyam iti sūnā; vāk of the pleasant and true; sūnṛtā — in the vocative sūnṛte; āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the nighāta. Jarasva — the root jṝṣ vayohānau; here used in the sense of praise; loṭ, 2nd singular; by vyatyaya no yak-type augment in the passive-like middle; savābhyāṃ vāmau (…) the am; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Paścā — paścāt (Pā. Sū. 5-3-33) the substitution paśca for the word apara, and in the sense of the fifth case [astāti], the suffix āti, by irregular formation; in the Vedic way the final t drops; the first-syllable acute of the suffix. Dadhyāḥ — dadhyati dabhnoti (Ni. 3-9 and OCR "14-61" [?]) says the Nirukta, reading it among the verbs of going; hence here it is used in that sense; liṅ, 2nd singular; by vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85) the tip-like singular ending; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Dhātā — the root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; in the sense of the agent the suffix tṛc; since it is cit, the final acute; nominative singular. Jayema — the root ji jaye; āśīrliṅ [as printed vidhiliṅ], 1st plural, the form jayema; since yat is connected with the word yaḥ before it, yadvṛttānnityam (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) prevents the nighāta; since the suffix is lasārvadhātuka, tāsyanudāttet (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the root accent remains. Dakṣiṇayā — the root dakṣa vṛddhau; druhakṣibhyām inan (Uṇ. Sū. 2-1[?]-[?], as read) the suffix inan; in the feminine, since it ends in a, ṭāp; since the suffix is nit, ñnityādir nityam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) the first-syllable acute; instrumental singular. ‖ 5 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उदीरतां सूनृता उत्पुरंधीरुदग्नयः शुशुचानासो अस्थुः । स्पार्हा वसूनि तमसापगूळ्हाविष्कृण्वन्त्युषसो विभातीः ॥ ६ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सूनृताः प्रियसत्यात्मिका वाच उदीरताम् । उद्गच्छन्तु । हे ऋत्विज उत्कृष्टं यथा भवति तथा स्तोत्रं प्रवर्तयध्वम् । तथा पुरन्धीः पुरन्धयः । पुरं शरीरं यासु धीयते याभिर्वा ताः पुरन्धयः प्रज्ञाः प्रयोगविषयाः । ता उत्तिष्ठन्तु । प्रज्ञोपलक्षितानि कर्माणि प्रवर्तन्तामित्यर्थः । यद्यपि प्राणवायुना शरीरं धार्यते तथापि यो वै प्राणः सा प्रज्ञा या वा प्रज्ञा स प्राण इति श्रुतेः प्राणप्रज्ञयोरेकात्मत्वात्प्रज्ञायाः शरीरधारणमविरुद्धम् । तथाग्नय आहवनीयाद्याः शुशुचानासोऽत्यन्तं दीप्यमाना उदस्थुः । उत्तिष्ठन्तु । प्रज्वलयन्त्वित्यर्थः । किमर्थमेवमिति तदुच्यते । यतो विभातीर्विविधं भासमाना उषस उषो-देवताः तमसापगूळ्हान्धकारेणात्यन्तं गोपितानि स्पार्हा स्पृहणीयानि वसूनि वासयोग्यानि यज्ञसाधनभूतहविरादीन्याविष्कृण्वन्ति यथावस्तु प्रकटीकुर्वन्ति । तस्मात्स्तोत्रादिकं कुर्वन्त्वित्यर्थः ॥

sūnṛtāḥ priyasatyātmikā vāca udīratām | udgacchantu | he ṛtvija utkṛṣṭaṃ yathā bhavati tathā stotraṃ pravartayadhvam | tathā purandhīḥ purandhayaḥ | puraṃ śarīraṃ yāsu dhīyate yābhirvā tāḥ purandhayaḥ prajñāḥ prayogaviṣayāḥ | tā uttiṣṭhantu | prajñopalakṣitāni karmāṇi pravartantāmityarthaḥ | yadyapi prāṇavāyunā śarīraṃ dhāryate tathāpi yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā yā vā prajñā sa prāṇa iti śruteḥ prāṇaprajñayorekātmatvātprajñāyāḥ śarīradhāraṇamaviruddham | tathāgnaya āhavanīyādyāḥ śuśucānāso 'tyantaṃ dīpyamānā udasthuḥ | uttiṣṭhantu | prajvalayantvityarthaḥ | kimarthamevamiti taducyate | yato vibhātīrvividhaṃ bhāsamānā uṣasa uṣo-devatāḥ tamasāpagūḷhāndhakāreṇātyantaṃ gopitāni spārhā spṛhaṇīyāni vasūni vāsayogyāni yajñasādhanabhūtahavirādīnyāviṣkṛṇvanti yathāvastu prakaṭīkurvanti | tasmātstotrādikaṃ kurvantvityarthaḥ ‖

Read at 150 dpi; letters that were unclear are marked [?] or taken as the Kannada's plain sense. "May the pleasant and true words (sūnṛtāḥ) rise up (udīratām): let them go up. O priests, so recite the praise that it be excellent. Likewise purandhīḥ — purandhayaḥ: 'those in which the body (pura) is placed, or by which it is placed' — the powers of intelligence (prajñā), that are the field of operation: let them rise; that is, let acts marked by intelligence go forward. Although the body is held by the vital air, still, by the Śruti yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā, yā vā prajñā sa prāṇaḥ (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 3-3, as read by the reader's OCR), since prāṇa and prajñā are one in nature, the holding of the body by prajñā is not inconsistent. Likewise the fires — Āhavanīya and the others — śuśucānāsaḥ, shining intensely, udasthuḥ: may they rise, may they blaze. Why so? It is said: because the Uṣases (the Uṣas deities), who shine (vibhātīḥ) in various ways, reveal (āviṣkṛṇvanti) in their true form the desirable riches (spārhā vasūni), the oblations and other means of sacrifice, suitable for dwelling, that were hidden by darkness; therefore they should do their praise and the rest."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Vibhātīḥ — shining in various forms; uṣasaḥ — the Uṣas deities; tamasā — by darkness; apagūḷhā — well hidden; spārhā — desirable; vasūni — dwelling-suitable houses (the oblations and the like); āviḥ kṛṇvanti — make manifest; (therefore); sūnṛtāḥ — the pleasant and true (praise-) words; ut īratām — let them rise; …

original p. 96

Pratipadārtha, concluded: …ut īratām — let them rise; purandhīḥ — (connected with action) the powers of knowledge, the actions marked by knowledge; ut [asthuḥ] — let them begin (and); agnayaḥ — the fires (Āhavanīya and the others); śuśucānāsaḥ — blazing; ut asthuḥ — let them blaze up.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. When the deities Uṣas arise in diverse forms, the houses — or the oblation materials — that are much desired and had been well hidden by the darkness (so that they were not seen with the eye) become manifest; therefore, O priests, at that time (ut) chant in a loud voice good praise-words; begin (acts that are the fruits of sacrificial knowledge); and let the fires (Āhavanīya and others) be kindled so that they shine brightly.

Printed English (as printed): Let words of truth be spoken : let works of wisdom (be performed) : let the blazing fires rise up, so that the many radiant Ushas may make manifest the desirable treasures hidden by the darkness.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6.

sūnṛtāḥ — priyasatyātmikāḥ vācaḥ: Yāska records the word sūnṛtā among the names of speech (Ni. 2-19, as read by the OCR) and among the names of food (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR). Sāyaṇa, however, explains that for it the meaning "speech that is beneficial and true" is used in another sense. The idea is: "may the priests recite hymns that are most agreeable, which will give delight to the deities".

purandhīḥ ut tiṣṭhantu — puraṃ śarīraṃ yāsu dhīyate yābhir vā tāḥ purandhayaḥ prajñāḥ prayogaviṣayāḥ | prajñopalakṣitāni karmāṇi pravartantām ity arthaḥ: the word pura conveys "body"; purandhi means prajñā ("wisdom") that holds the body properly in place. The sense is "let [acts] done with pure knowledge, or performed with conduct, begin".

In the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad it is said: yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā, yā vā prajñā sa prāṇaḥ (Kau. Upa. 3-3, as read by the OCR). By this sentence the identity of prāṇa and prajñā is declared: prāṇa (vital air) itself holds the body in place; yet "that prajñā holds the body" appears to be a contradiction; but it is removed by the identity between prāṇa and prajñā.

In the bhāṣya, by saying yadyapi prāṇavāyunā śarīraṃ dhāryate tathāpi prāṇaprajñayor ekatvāt prajñāyāḥ śarīradhāraṇam aviruddham, Sāyaṇa has described the manner of removing the contradiction, and given for the word purandhi the meaning prajñā ("[the powers of] knowledge, the acts joined with knowledge").

Yāska reads the two words purandhi and purandhī, and has shown the difference of their meanings. The word purandhī means "Earth and Heaven" [as read: vyāvāpṛthivīvācaka] (Ni. 3-22, as read by the OCR).

ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमाः सधस्थं विश्वे अभि सन्ति देवाः । ताँ अध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टी भगं नासत्या पुरन्धिम् ॥

te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmāḥ sadhasthaṃ viśve abhi santi devāḥ | tā~ adhvara uśato yakṣyagne śruṣṭī bhagaṃ nāsatyā purandhim ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-3[?]-[?], as read.)

पुरन्धिर्बहुधीस्तत्र कर्मा [?] । पुरन्धिर्भगः पुरस्तात्स्यान्यादेश इत्येकम् । इन्द्र इत्यपरं स बहुकर्मतमः पुरां च दारयितृतमः । वरुण इत्यपरम् ॥

purandhirbahudhīstatra karmā [?] | purandhirbhagaḥ purastātsyānyādeśa ityekam | indra ityaparaṃ sa bahukarmatamaḥ purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ | varuṇa ityaparam ‖

(Ni. 6-1[?]-[?], as read.) Thus Yāska has said. According to one opinion [of the vṛttikāra Durgācārya], the word purandhi means the deity named Bhaga; according to another opinion, since dhī means "action", he who does many bold deeds is Indra — [this is] the meaning; and still others say that, since purandhi is he who destroys clouds and enemy cities, the word expresses the sense "Indra". Others [say] "Varuṇa":

इमामू नु कवितमस्य मायां महीं देवस्य नकिरा दधर्ष । एकं यदुद्ना न पृणन्त्येनीरासिञ्चन्तीरवनयः समुद्रम् ॥

imāmū nu kavitamasya māyāṃ mahīṃ devasya nakirā dadharṣa | ekaṃ yadudnā na pṛṇantyenīrāsiñcantīravanayaḥ samudram ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-4[?]-[?], as read.) In this ṛk the seer of the mantra praises Varuṇa. Dhīr iti prajñānāma sā yasya pūrvī bahvī sa purandhiḥ | varuṇaś ca prajñayā stūyate kasmāt varuṇaḥ purandhiḥ — the vṛttikāra explains thus: dhī is a word for prajñā; since Varuṇa is praised with much prajñā, the doer of many things, he says the word purandhi has the sense "Varuṇa". That is one opinion.

[the first line of this ṛk is in small type and I could not settle it letter by letter; not transcribed] अत्रा पुरन्धिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥

atrā purandhirajahādarātīrmade somasya mūrā amūraḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-2[?]-[?], as read; the first line has been read doubtfully and is not transcribed as Sanskrit.) In this ṛk they explain the word purandhi as bahuno dhanasya dātā, "the giver of much wealth".

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

इदानीमहोरात्रस्तुतिद्वारोषाः स्तूयते । विषुरूपे वक्ष्यमाणप्रकारेण नानारूपे अहनी अहश्च रात्रिश्चोभे सं चरेते । समित्येकीभावे । सहैवाव्यवधानेन चरतः । अत्राहः साहचर्यात्तत्प्रतियोगित्वाच्च रात्रिरप्यहरित्युच्यते । उत्तरत्र मन्त्रान्तरेऽयमेवार्थः स्पष्ट आम्नातः । अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः (ऋ. ६-९-१) इति । तयोर्मध्येऽन्यद्रात्रिरूपमहरपैति । अपगच्छति । प्रतिलोमं गच्छति वा । अपेत्येतस्य प्रातिलोम्यम् (नि. १-३) इति यास्कः । अन्यच्च दिवसाख्यमहरभ्येति । अभिमुखेन गच्छति । अभीत्याभिमुख्यम् (नि. १-३) इति यास्कः । रात्र्यां प्रतिनिवृत्तायामहराभिमुखमागच्छतीत्यर्थः । विषुरूपे सं चरेते इति यदुक्तं तदेव स्पष्टीक्रियते । परिक्षितोः पर्यायेण निवसतोः परिक्षपयितोर्वा । प्राणिनामायुः क्षयात्प्रक्षपणं प्रसिद्धं तयोर्मध्येऽन्या रात्रिस्तमस्तमोरूपा गुहा पदार्थानां गूहनमकः करोति । अन्या हरेकदेशभूतोषाः शोशुचता भृशं दीप्येन रथेनाद्यौत् । द्योतते । प्रकाशते प्रकाशयति वा सर्वम् । रात्रिस्तमोरूपत्वात्सर्वं जगदावृणोति । उषास्तु सर्वान्प्राकाश्य-यतीत्युषसः स्तुतिः ॥

idānīmahorātrastutidvāroṣāḥ stūyate | viṣurūpe vakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa nānārūpe ahanī ahaśca rātriścobhe saṃ carete | samityekībhāve | sahaivāvyavadhānena carataḥ | atrāhaḥ sāhacaryāttatpratiyogitvācca rātrirapyaharityucyate | uttaratra mantrāntare 'yamevārthaḥ spaṣṭa āmnātaḥ | ahaśca kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ (ṛ. 6-9-1) iti | tayormadhye 'nyadrātrirūpamaharapaiti | apagacchati | pratilomaṃ gacchati vā | apetyetasya prātilomyam (ni. 1-3) iti yāskaḥ | anyacca divasākhyamaharabhyeti | abhimukhena gacchati | abhītyābhimukhyam (ni. 1-3) iti yāskaḥ | rātryāṃ pratinivṛttāyāmaharābhimukhamāgacchatītyarthaḥ | viṣurūpe saṃ carete iti yaduktaṃ tadeva spaṣṭīkriyate | parikṣitoḥ paryāyeṇa nivasatoḥ parikṣapayitorvā | prāṇināmāyuḥ kṣayātprakṣapaṇaṃ prasiddhaṃ tayormadhye 'nyā rātristamastamorūpā guhā padārthānāṃ gūhanamakaḥ karoti | anyā harekadeśabhūtoṣāḥ śośucatā bhṛśaṃ dīpyena rathenādyaut | dyotate | prakāśate prakāśayati vā sarvam | rātristamorūpatvātsarvaṃ jagadāvṛṇoti | uṣāstu sarvānprākāśya-yatītyuṣasaḥ stutiḥ ‖

Read from 150 dpi; the letters of a few words are marked or approximate, e.g. the compound prakāśayati near the end. "Now, through the praise of Day and Night, Uṣas is praised. Viṣurūpe — two of various forms (in the manner to be told), Day and Night, both saṃ carete (sam means 'together': they move together, without interval). Here, because of its companionship with day and because it is its counterpart, night too is called ahar ('day'). In another mantra later the same sense is clearly handed down: ahaś ca kṛṣṇam ahar arjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1, as printed "೬-೯-೧"). Of the two, one — the night form of the 'day' — apaiti: goes away, or goes backward (pratilomam): apety etasya prātilomyam (Ni. 1-3, as read by the OCR), says Yāska. The other, called day, abhyeti: goes facing; abhīty ābhimukhyam (Ni. 1-3), says Yāska — when the night has gone back, the day comes facing. What is said — viṣurūpe saṃ carete — is now made clear. Parikṣitoḥ: of the two that dwell in turn, or that make [life] wane — the waning of the lives of creatures is well known; between them, the other, Night, which has the form of darkness, makes guhā — a hiding — of things. The other, the day-portion, Uṣas, brilliantly shining (śośucatā) with her chariot, adyaut: shines, or illuminates everything. Night, being of the form of darkness, covers the whole world; Uṣas, however, makes everything visible: thus the praise of Uṣas."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Viṣurūpe — (in the manner told further on) of various forms; ahanī — the two, Day and Night; saṃ carete — move together; anyat — of the two, one (Night); apa eti — goes backward (passes); anyat — the other (Day); abhi eti — goes forward; parikṣitoḥ — of the two that dwell in turn (that cause the lives of beings to wane, as they come and go); anyā — one (Night); tamaḥ — in the form of darkness; guhā — (things) concealing; akaḥ — does; anyā — the other; uṣāḥ — Uṣas, the portion of the day; śośucatā — brilliantly shining; rathena — with her chariot; adyaut — illuminates all.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The Day and the Night, of various forms, move together; of the two, one (Night) goes backward, the other (Day) goes forward; Night, which destroys the lives of beings, makes things hidden in the form of darkness; the other, the day-portion Uṣas, shines with her radiant chariot and illuminates the whole world, which was covered by darkness.

Printed English (as printed): The twofold day proceeds unseparated; one (part going) forward, one backward; one of these two alternating (periods) effects the concealment (of things); the Dawn illumines them with her radiant chariot.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 7. In this ṛk Uṣas is praised through the praise of Day and Night. The Day and Night, the two, move one after the other in many forms.

viṣurūpe — vakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa nānārūpe | ahaś ca rātriś cobhe sahaiva avyavadhānena carataḥ — Sāyaṇa explains: "Day and Night both move together without interval". Atrāhnaḥ sāhacaryāt tatpratiyogitvāc ca rātrir apy ahar ity ucyate — "here, from association with day and from being its counterpart, night too is called ahar":

अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः । वैश्वानरो जायमानो न राजावातिरज्ज्योतिषाग्निस्तमांसि ॥

ahaśca kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ | vaiśvānaro jāyamāno na rājāvātirajjyotiṣāgnistamāṃsi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1, as printed.) Citing this ṛk, he describes that from association with day and from being contrary to it, night too is called "day". In the compound word [the Kannada explains], although the word "day" itself has two forms in common usage — as a day consisting of "day and night" — in the name ahas the "night" aspect — it is [another of] the many forms; in the day-forms, the night is covered with darkness and conceals all things from the sight of everyone; while it [the day] moves the opposite way … This same idea is explained by Yāska in tayor madhye 'nyā rātrirūpam aharapaiti prātilomaṃ gacchati vā [as printed].

original p. 102

apa + eti — in this the prefix apa is used in the sense of "contrary" (prātilomya). Yāska explains: vyapetyaitasya prātilomyam (Ni. 1-3, as read by the OCR).

In the same way anyac ca divasākhyam ahar abhi eti abhimukhena gacchati — "the other, the 'day' called divasa, goes forth facing; the day is [so] named; since Uṣas, in contrast to night, exists in the form of a luminous source, she comes facing [the night] — that is, goes to meet it, after the night has passed."

abhi + eti — the prefix abhi is used in the sense of "facing": abhītyābhimukhyam (Ni. 1-3, as read by the OCR) is Yāska's description. The sense: after the night has gone, Uṣas comes facing [the world].

parikṣitoḥ — paryāyeṇa nivasatoḥ parikṣapayitor vā — "of the two that dwell by turns, or that make [life] wane": the day and the night come one after another; and they reduce (kṣapayanti) the lives of beings by their going and coming — that is the sense.

uṣāḥ śośucatā rathena adyaut — dyotate prakāśate prakāśayati vā sarvam: "Night covers the whole world with darkness; Uṣas, with her radiance, illuminates the whole world, and shines herself with her own light": thus Uṣas is praised here.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अद्यास्मिन्नहनि सदृशीरित् परस्परं सदृश्य एव । तथा श्व इत् परस्मिन्नहनि सदृशीः परस्परं सदृश्य एव । उशब्दोऽपिकारार्थः । इच्छब्द एवार्थः । अद्यतन्योऽपि श्वस्तनीभिः सदृश्यः श्वस्तन्यश्चाद्यतनीभिः । एवमहरन्तरेण सादृश्यम् । कथं सादृश्यमिति तदुपपाद्यते । यदा नक्षत्राणि न दृश्यन्ते सूर्यश्च नोदेति उषःकालः । स चैकविंशतिघटिकाभिः षड्विंशतिपराभिः [?] सम्मितः । सूर्यो हि प्रतिदिनमेकोनषष्ट्यधिकपञ्चसहस्रयोजनानि [?] मेरुं प्रादक्षिण्येन परिभ्रमति । तथा सति यत्र यत्र लङ्कादिभूप्रदेशे सूर्यो गच्छति तस्य तस्य पुरस्त्रिंशद्योजनमुषा अपि गच्छति । सूर्यो यस्मिन्देशे गच्छति तत्र त्रिंशद्योजनं पुरस्ताद्देशस्थितानामुषो दृश्यते । एवं सर्वप्रदेशेष्वपि । तथोषा अपि यत्र गच्छति ततः पुरस्त्रिंशद्योजनभूभागवर्तिनामुदिता दृश्यते । एवं लङ्कादिसर्वप्रदेशस्थानामुषस उदयो गन्तव्यः । एवं च सत्येकस्मिन्भूभागे यावत्कालं यथोषाः प्रकाशयति तथा भूभागान्तरेऽपि तावन्तं कालं प्रकाशयति । एवमुक्तरीत्यैकस्मिन्नेवाहनि सर्वप्रदेशवर्तिनामुषसः सदृश्यः । प्रदेशबाहुल्यमपेक्ष्योषसां बहुत्वाद्बहुवचनम् । एवमेकरूपा उषसोऽनवद्याः शुद्धाः । तासामुदयात्सर्वे भावा अनवद्या भविष्यन्ति किमु वक्तव्यं तासामनवद्यत्वम् । दीर्घमुक्तरीत्यात्यन्तमायतं वरुणस्य तमोनिवारकस्य सूर्यस्य धाम स्थानं मेरुवलयं सचन्ते । प्रतिदिनं सेवन्ते । कियद्दूरमिति तदुच्यते । त्रिंशतं योजनानि त्रिंशद्योजनानि पुरतः । सूर्यो यत्र यत्रोदेति ततस्त्रिंशद्योजनं पुरस्तादुद्यन्तीत्यर्थः । किञ्चासां मध्य एकैकोषा लङ्कादिकैकभूभागवर्तिनां क्रतुं गमनागमनादिरूपं कर्म तद्विषयां प्रज्ञां वा । तथा च निरुक्तम् । क्रतुं प्रधिकर्म वा प्रज्ञां वा (नि. २-२८ [?]) इति । सद्यस्तदानीमेव हि स्वोदयकाल एव परि यन्ति । परितो गच्छन्ति । निर्वहन्तीत्यर्थः । तत्तद्भूभागविशेषेण सूर्यस्योदयो ज्योतिश्शास्त्रे प्रदर्शितः । उदयो यो

लङ्कायां सोऽस्तमयः सवितुरेव सिद्धपुरे । मध्याह्नो यवकोट्यां रोमकविषयेऽर्धरात्रः स्यात् । (आर्य. ४-१३) इति ॥

laṅkāyāṃ so 'stamayaḥ savitureva siddhapure | madhyāhno yavakoṭyāṃ romakaviṣaye 'rdharātraḥ syāt | (ārya. 4-13) iti ‖

"Today, on this day, the Uṣases (dawns) are all alike with one another; likewise tomorrow they are all alike with one another. The word u has the sense of api ('also'); it has the sense of eva. Today's are like tomorrow's, and tomorrow's like today's. In this way there is likeness from day to day. How is the likeness established? When the stars are not seen and the Sun has not yet risen, that is the dawn-time; it is measured by twenty-one ghaṭikās or twenty-six [?] beyond them. The Sun goes round Meru each day in a clockwise way [for 5,059 [?] yojanas]; and so in whatever place on the earth, Laṅkā and so on, the Sun goes, the dawn goes thirty yojanas in front of him. In whatever region the Sun goes, to those who are stationed thirty yojanas in front, the dawn is seen. So in all regions. And likewise wherever the dawn goes, she is seen to have risen to those in the part of the earth thirty yojanas ahead. In this way the rising of Uṣas is to be understood for those in all regions, Laṅkā and the rest. And so, as long as Uṣas lights one part of the earth, so long she lights another part. In this way, in one and the same day, the dawns are alike for those in all regions; the plural is used out of regard to the many regions. Thus the dawns are of one form, anavadyāḥ — pure: from their rising all things will be blameless — what then need be said of their own blamelessness? Dīrgham: in the manner told, very extended: they follow (sacante) the region (dhāma) of Varuṇa — of the Sun, the remover of darkness — the ring of Meru; day by day they serve it. How far? Thirty yojanas ahead (puratas): wherever the Sun rises, thirty yojanas ahead of that they rise — that is the sense. And among them each Uṣas, for each region of the earth, such as Laṅkā, kratum — 'action in the form of going and coming', or the intelligence concerning it; thus the Nirukta (kratuṃ pradhikarma vā prajñāṃ vā, Ni. 2-28, as read by the OCR) — sadyas — just then, at their own rising, pari yanti: go round, accomplish. The Sun's rising in each part of the earth is shown in the science of the heavens: 'the rising at Laṅkā is the setting at Siddhapura, at Yavakoṭi it is midday, in the country of Romaka it is midnight' (Āryabhaṭīya 4-13)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Uṣasaḥ — the dawns; adya — now; sadṛśīḥ it — (one to another) alike; śvaḥ — tomorrow also; sadṛśīḥ u — alike (thus of one form); anavadyāḥ — pure ones (they); dīrgham — very long (extended); varuṇasya — of the remover of darkness (the Sun); dhāma — the region (path); triṃśatam yojanāni — thirty yojanas distance (rising ahead of the Sun); sacante — they follow (they go round); ekaikā — each (dawn); kratum — the action (of going and coming, as applicable to each part of the earth); sadyaḥ — at once (at the time of her rising); pari yanti — they accomplish.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The dawns of today and of tomorrow are alike; they are pure; they go round the very extended region (the path) of the Sun, the remover of darkness, rising thirty yojanas ahead of the Sun; and every dawn at its time of rising performs its action, applying it to the region concerned.

Printed English (as printed): The same to-day, the same tomorrow, the irreproachable (Dawns) precede the distant course of Varuna (Sun) by thirty yojanas, and each in succession revolves in its (appointed) office.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 8.

sadṛśīr adya sadṛśīr idu śvaḥ — asminn ahani parasparaṃ sadṛśyaḥ | parasminn ahani api parasparaṃ sadṛśya eva | adyatanyo 'pi śvastanībhiḥ sadṛśyaḥ śvastanyaś cādyatanībhiḥ | evam ahar-antareṇa sādṛśyam — here the likeness of days to one another is described: "today's day is alike to tomorrow's day; tomorrow's day is alike to today's; yesterday's day is alike to today's; tomorrow's is alike to today's" — a mutual likeness is set out. "On the ground of the equal quality — the same kind of character — produced by the Sun's special motion, it may be said that the likeness holds for the other days too" — that is the sense. This kind of likeness Sāyaṇa has explained.

original p. 106

Special topics of Ṛk 8, continued; from here the Kannada text was read from the page image and cross-checked word by word against the reader's OCR, which for the Kannada prose is good. …"…when the stars are not seen and the Sun has not yet risen" — people reckon the time from twenty-one ghaṭikās to twenty-six ghaṭikās [before sunrise] as the dawn-time (uṣaḥkāla), which comes in the last part of the night. The Sun goes round Mount Meru each day in a clockwise circuit of five thousand and fifty-nine [[?] "ಐದು ಸಾವಿರದ ಐವತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತು"] yojanas. Before the Sun rises (in the regions where he rises, Laṅkā and the rest), by the time the Sun comes there, the dawn has already arrived thirty yojanas ahead of him. Hence in the region ahead of where the Sun is, at a distance of thirty yojanas, the rising of the Sun is seen as the dawn. This arrangement holds in all regions.

In the same way the dawn, too, rises in the region thirty yojanas ahead of the region where she herself is. For all who live in all regions, from Laṅkā onward, it is to be understood that the rising of Uṣas is perceived in one and the same manner.

Thus, as the light of Uṣas is seen in one region, so at the same time in all the other regions the same equal light of Uṣas is perceived by all. Therefore, because the days are reckoned as different days beginning from the dawn-time, and because the regions are different, it is to be understood that the one Uṣas is many Uṣases, and the mutual likeness (sādṛśya, comparison) of these is here described.

When the regions are not taken into account, Uṣas, rising of her own nature perfectly pure, and since in Uṣas there is a supreme purity that makes all things pure, there is no need to explain at length about Uṣas's purity.

varuṇasya dīrghaṃ dhāma sacante — atyantam āyataṃ tamonivārakasya sūryasya meruvalayaṃ pratidinaṃ sevante: "they serve every day the very extended ring of Meru of the Sun, the remover of darkness". Though the Sun's light is far from the region where he is, it destroys darkness, and the pervasion of the Sun's light is perceived. It is described that, just as the Sun goes round Meru in a clockwise circuit, so does Uṣas every day.

"When the Sun rises at the city of Laṅkā, it is sunset at Siddhapura, midday at Yavakoṭi, and midnight in the country of Romaka" — thus Sāyaṇa here describes a doctrine of astronomy (jyotiḥśāstra) that teaches the order of risings and settings caused by the Sun's particular motion.

Sū. 6-1-64) the initial s; laṭ, 3rd plural; after an atiṅanta the nighāta. Anavadyāḥ — na vidyate avadyaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ anavadyāḥ; nañsubhyām (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) the accent of the end of the latter member. Ekaikā — kriyāsamabhihāre sarvanāmno dve bhavataḥ [as printed]: when repetition of action is shown, doubling; tasya parām āmreḍitam (Pā. Sū. 8-1-2) the second member gets the name āmreḍita; anudāttaṃ ca (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3) it is unaccented.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

jānatī | ahnaḥ | prathamasya | nāma | śukrā | kṛṣṇāt | ajaniṣṭa | śvitīcī | ṛtasya | yoṣā | na | mināti | dhāma | ahaḥ 'ahaḥ | niḥ 'kṛtam | ā 'carantī ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

उषाः प्रथमस्य मुख्यस्य प्रथमानस्य वाह्नो दिवसस्य नाम नमनमागमनं जानत्यवगच्छन्ती । प्राणिनां प्रज्ञापयन्तीत्यर्थः । सोषाः शुक्रा स्वतो दीप्ता अत एव श्वितीची श्वैत्यं गच्छन्ती प्रकाशं प्राप्नुवती कृष्णात् कृष्णवर्णात्तमसः सकाशादजनिष्ट । प्रादुर्भवति । यद्यपि तमसः सकाशान्नोत्पद्यते तथापि तदनन्तरभावित्वात्तत उत्पद्यत इत्युपचर्यते । उत्पन्ना सा ऋतस्य सत्यभूतस्यादित्यस्य धाम तेजोयुक्तं स्थानं योषा मिश्रयन्ती न मिनाति । न हिनस्ति । न तेनेयं तेजो न पराभवति । अपि त्वहरहः सर्वेष्वहःसु निष्कृतमाचरन्ती । अलङ्कारशोभां कुर्वती । यद्वा । ऋतस्य सत्यभूतस्य यज्ञस्य धाम देवयजनाख्यं स्थानं योषा मिश्रणशीला सती न मिनाति । न हिनस्ति । किन्त्वहरहः सर्वेषु यागदिवसेषु निष्कृतं हविरादीनां प्रकाशनरूपमलङ्कारमाचरन्ती कुर्वन्ती । तादृश्युषा अजनिष्टेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥

uṣāḥ prathamasya mukhyasya prathamānasya vāhno divasasya nāma namanamāgamanaṃ jānatyavagacchantī | prāṇināṃ prajñāpayantītyarthaḥ | soṣāḥ śukrā svato dīptā ata eva śvitīcī śvaityaṃ gacchantī prakāśaṃ prāpnuvatī kṛṣṇāt kṛṣṇavarṇāttamasaḥ sakāśādajaniṣṭa | prādurbhavati | yadyapi tamasaḥ sakāśānnotpadyate tathāpi tadanantarabhāvitvāttata utpadyata ityupacaryate | utpannā sā ṛtasya satyabhūtasyādityasya dhāma tejoyuktaṃ sthānaṃ yoṣā miśrayantī na mināti | na hinasti | na teneyaṃ tejo na parābhavati | api tvaharahaḥ sarveṣvahaḥsu niṣkṛtamācarantī | alaṅkāraśobhāṃ kurvatī | yadvā | ṛtasya satyabhūtasya yajñasya dhāma devayajanākhyaṃ sthānaṃ yoṣā miśraṇaśīlā satī na mināti | na hinasti | kintvaharahaḥ sarveṣu yāgadivaseṣu niṣkṛtaṃ havirādīnāṃ prakāśanarūpamalaṅkāramācarantī kurvantī | tādṛśyuṣā ajaniṣṭeti pūrvatrānvayaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the first half is clear; "nahinasti"/"tejo" in the middle is read as printed. "Uṣas knows (jānatī, understands) the nāma — the 'bowing', the coming — of the first (prathama), the chief, the beginning day (ahnaḥ); that is, she causes living beings to know it. She, Uṣas, śukrā (self-shining, of herself bright) and therefore śvitīcī (reaching whiteness, getting light), was born (ajaniṣṭa) from kṛṣṇāt — from the black darkness; that is, she appears. Although she is not born from the darkness, still, because she comes after it, it is said figuratively that she is born from it. Born, she, yoṣā, mingling with the dhāma (the brilliant place) of the true Āditya (ṛtasya), does not harm (na mināti) it — [her brightness] does not defeat his brilliance; rather, aharahaḥ, day by day on all days, niṣkṛtam ācarantī: she makes an ornament, a beauty. Or else: she, mingling with the place of the sacrifice of the true one (ṛtasya = of the true sacrifice), the place called the sacrificial ground (devayajana), does not harm it; on the contrary, day by day on all days of sacrifice she brings about the ornament in the form of the manifestation of the oblations and the like; may such an Uṣas [be born] — this is connected with what precedes."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Ṛtasya — of the true Āditya (of the sacrifice); dhāma — the brilliant place (the region); yoṣā — having joined (Uṣas); na mināti — does not defeat (the Āditya's brilliance); (api tu — but); aharahaḥ — every day; niṣkṛtam ācarantī — giving the beauty that is an ornament (making the ornament of manifest oblations and the like); (uṣāḥ — the deity Uṣas); ahnaḥ — of the day; prathamasya — of the first part; nāma — the coming; jānatī — knowing (making the world know); śukrā — self-shining (and therefore); śvitīcī — possessed of whiteness; kṛṣṇāt — from black darkness; ajaniṣṭa — came into being.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Uṣas, though she joins the place of Āditya (and enters the sacrificial hall), does not diminish his radiance (nor does she cause the sacrifice delay); every day she gives Āditya (and the sacrificial hall) the beauty that is an ornament (an ornament in the form of the manifestation of oblations and the like), makes the world know the first part of the day, and being of herself shining, white, she is born from the black (from the darkness).

Printed English (as printed): The self-illumined Dawn, announcing the declination of the first (portion) of the day, is born white-shining out of the gloom : cleansing (with the radiance) of the sun, she impairs not his splendour, but daily adds embellishment (to his lustre).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 9.

jānatī — avagacchantī prāṇināṃ prajñāpayantī: "Uṣas knows the beginning of the day and makes all beings know it" — that is the sense.

kṛṣṇāt ajaniṣṭa — nikṛṣṭāt tamasaḥ sakāśāt prādurbhavati: "Uṣas appears from base darkness, since the darkness of the night gives difficulty to others; after it has diminished, she is born from the darkness of a lower nature"; because the darkness in the night pervades widely, and because Uṣas rises in the last part of the night, the birth of Uṣas is described as from the darkness; and since she comes up after the darkness has gone, this expression is figurative (aupacārika). (See the introduction to this Sūkta.)

ṛtasya dhāma yoṣā na mināti — Sāyaṇa has given two meanings for this sentence. The first meaning: the word ṛta means the Āditya, who is truth; the place of his brilliance is joined by Uṣas with her own brilliance, but she does not disparage that brilliance.

The word ṛta is recorded among the synonyms of water (Ni. 2-14, as read by the OCR on p. 110); it is also recorded among the synonyms of udaka (water) — thus stated (as printed on p. 111: "ಋತಶಬ್ದವು ಉದಕ(ಸೂರ್ಯಯ)ನಾಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ (ನಿ. ೨-೧೪) ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿದೆ"). In the Nirukta (4-19, as read by the OCR) he explains satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā — "truth or sacrifice" — so, following the meaning "truth", the first meaning has been explained.

The second meaning: taking the meaning of the word ṛta as the sacrificial place in which oblations are offered to the deities — devayajanākhyaṃ sthānaṃ yoṣā miśraṇaśīlā satī na mināti na hinasti: Uṣas, mingling with the sacrificial ground, does not harm it; rather aharahaḥ sarveṣu yāgadivaseṣu niṣkṛtaṃ havirādīnāṃ prakāśanarūpam alaṅkāram ācarantī kurvatī ajaniṣṭa: on every day of sacrifice she makes the ornament consisting of the manifestation of the oblations and the like, and is born. That is: Uṣas, shedding her light in the sacrificial times of the various sacrifice-days that go on day after day, and making the various oblations manifest, brings the sacrifice to completion — thus the rising of Uṣas is described here.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers as read by the OCR where the page image is not clear). Words treated: jānatī — from the root jñā avabodhane (Kryādi class); śatṛ in the sense of laṭ; kryādibhyaḥ śnā (Pā. 3-1-81) gives the śnā augment; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ (Pā. 6-4-112) elides the ā; jñā janor jā (Pā. 7-3-79) gives the substitute jā; in the feminine, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp; the śatṛ without num — śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173) — gives the acute accent on the ending. kṛṣṇāt — root kṛṣ vilekhane; kṛṣer varṇe [?] (Uṇ. 3-284 as read by the OCR) gives the suffix nak; as it has the indicatory k there is no guṇa; the suffix n becomes ṇ after the ṣ; the suffix-accent makes the word final-acute (ablative singular form). ajaniṣṭa — root janī prādurbhāve; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6 [?] — the OCR reads "3-3-6", the print is not clear) gives the present sense in the Veda, with luṅ; the third person singular ta; siC substitute; the iṭ augment by the rule on ārdhadhātuka; ṣṭutva of the t of the ending after the ṣ; the augment aṭ to the stem; since it follows a verb-ending that is not at the head, the nighāta accent. śvitīcī — root añcu gatipūjanayoḥ; the word śvitam añcati iti śvitīcī; ṛtvik dadhṛk… (Pā. 3-2-59 [?]; OCR "3-2-51") gives kvin when the subanta śviti stands as the upapada; by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti the nasal of the root is elided; in the feminine, because of the ug-marker, ṅīp; by ac … (aco [?] Pā. 6-4-138, as read by the OCR) the stem having the bha designation loses the ā of the root…

…ca (Pā. 6-3-138, as read by the OCR): the nasal being elided, since the root añc with its ā follows, the preceding i is lengthened; and taking as its cause the unaccented ṅīp, the accent on the root — whose a is elided — anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (Pā. 6-1-161) gives the acute accent on the remainder (the ṅīp).

mināti — root mīñ hiṃsāyām (Kryādi); laṭ third person singular tip; kryādibhyaḥ śnā (Pā. 3-1-81) gives śnā; mīnāter nigame [?] (Pā. 7-3-81, as read by the OCR) shortens the root when śnā follows, and the form mināti results; since it stands after a non-verb word, the nighāta accent.

aharaha — in the sense of constancy, nityavīpsayoḥ (Pā. 8-1-4) gives the doubling; since the latter has the designation āmreḍita, anudāttaṃ ca (Pā. 8-1-3) makes it wholly unaccented.

niṣkṛtam — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; in the passive, niṣṭhā, the suffix kta; gatir anantaraḥ — when the prefix would have its natural accent, pravṛddhādīnāṃ ca (Pā. 6-2-147, as read by the OCR) as an exception gives the accent of the latter member's own acute.

ācarantī — root cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; śap augment; in the feminine, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp; śapśyanor nityam [?] (Pā. 7-1-81, as read by the OCR) gives the num augment; since the sārvadhātuka is unaccented by tāsyanudāttet (Pā. 6-1-186) the accent of the root remains; in the gati-compound the accent of the latter member [kṛdutarapada-prakṛtisvara] arises. ‖ 9 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

कन्येव तन्वा शाशदाना एषि देवि देवमियक्षमाणम् । संस्मयमाना युवतिः पुरस्तादाविर्वक्षांसि कृणुषे विभाती ॥ १० ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

कन्याऽइव । तन्वा । शाशदाना । एषि । देवि । देवम् । इयक्षमाणम् । संस्मयमाना । युवतिः । पुरस्तात् । आविः । वक्षांसि । कृणुषे । विभाती ॥ १० ॥

kanyā 'iva | tanvā | śāśadānā | eṣi | devi | devam | iyakṣamāṇam | saṃsmayamānā | yuvatiḥ | purastāt | āviḥ | vakṣāṃsi | kṛṇuṣe | vibhātī ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

तन्वा शरीरेण शाशदाना शाशद्यमाना स्पष्टतां प्राप्नुवती । शाशदानः शाशद्यमानः । नि. ६-१६ । इति यास्कः । कन्येव कमनीया कन्येव । कन्या कमनीया भवति कैनेयं नेतव्येति वा । नि. ४-१५ । इति यास्कः । सा यथा जनान्तिके विवसना संचरति तथा हे उषः त्वं कन्या कमनीयाप्रगल्भा सती तन्वा शरीरेण शाशदाना स्पष्टतां गच्छन्ती दृश्यसे । पश्चात्प्रगल्भा सती हे देवि देवनशीले इयक्षमाणं यष्टुमिच्छन्तमभिमतं दातुमिच्छन्तं वा देवं द्योतनस्वभावं सूर्यरूपं प्रियमेषि गच्छसि । ततः पश्चात् युवतिर्यौवनोपेता सती पुरस्तात्प्रत्युत सूर्यस्य पुरतः संस्मयमाना समीपदंशं [?] हास्यं कुर्वती विभाती अत्यन्तं भासमाना वक्षांसि वक्षसोऽलक्षितानि नानावर्णान्याविष्कृणुषे । प्रकटीकरोषि । यद्वा । युवतिरिति लुप्तोपमा । यथा लोके प्रगल्भा योषित् पुरस्तात् प्रियतमस्य पुरतः संस्मयमाना दन्तप्रदर्शनाय ईषदसनं कुर्वती वक्षांसि वक्षसोपलक्षितानि गोस्थानि बाहुमूलस्तनादीन्याविष्करोति तथा त्वमित्यर्थः । यद्वा । पुरस्तात् पूर्वस्यां दिशि संस्मयमाना स्मितोषमप्रकाशं कुर्वती युवतिः सर्वेषु भावेषु मिश्रणशीला वक्षांसि । वक्ष इति रूपनाम । वन्त्स्थानीयानि नीलपीतादीनि रूपाण्याविष्करोषि ॥
