Read from the image and checked against the OCR; the small-type words in the middle — "samīpadaṃśaṃ", "vakṣaso 'lakṣitāni", "gosthāni", "vantsthānīyāni" — are doubtful in the print and are given as read; the OCR text there is badly garbled. "Tanvā — with the body; śāśadānā — becoming visible, attaining clarity. 'Śāśadānaḥ means śāśadyamānaḥ' (Ni. 6-16, as read by the OCR), says Yāska. Kanyeva — like a lovely maiden. 'Kanyā is lovely; or [it is said] "by whom is she to be led?"' (Ni. 4-15, as read by the OCR), says Yāska. As such a maiden goes about near people in scanty dress, so, O Uṣas, you, a lovely maiden not yet bold, are seen becoming clear with your body. Afterwards, grown bold, O goddess (devi, of the shining nature), you go to the god (devam, of the shining nature, of the form of the Sun) who is dear to you, who wishes to sacrifice, or who wishes to give you what is desired. Thereafter, a young woman (yuvatiḥ) endowed with youth, in front of the Sun, smiling (saṃsmayamānā) a little, shining (vibhātī) exceedingly, you make manifest (āviḥ kṛṇuṣe) the breasts, the many-coloured [forms] [?] seen on the bosom. Or else: yuvatiḥ is a simile with the particle omitted. As in the world a bold woman, in front of her beloved, smiling, lightly laughing to show her teeth, reveals the parts of the bosom — the hollow of the arm, the breasts and the like — so you: that is the sense. Or else: purastāt — in the eastern quarter, smiling and making a light like a gentle smile, a young woman mingling in all existences, you reveal the vakṣāṃsi — 'vakṣa' is a name for form — the forms such as blue and yellow, that take the place of [the parts of the body] [?]."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Devi — O goddess; kanyā iva — like a maiden; tanvā — with the body; śāśadānā — having attained clarity; iyakṣamāṇam — wishing to give (what is desired); devam — the shining (the Sun, who is dear); eṣi — you approach; (tataḥ — afterwards); yuvatiḥ — endowed with youth (you); purastāt — in front of the beloved; saṃsmayamānā — with a slight smile; vibhātī — of special brilliance; vakṣāṃsi — the chest and all the other limbs; ā kṛṇuṣe — you make manifest. Purastāt — in the eastern quarter; saṃsmayamānā — spreading a brilliance like a gentle smile; yuvatiḥ — showing many colours; vibhātī — of special light; vakṣāṃsi — the forms (blue, yellow and the like); āviḥ kṛṇuṣe — you make manifest.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Like a maiden, having a clearly visible body, O goddess, you approach the resplendent (Sun, who is your dear one) and who is minded to give what is desired; then, like a young woman, in the presence of your husband you spread a gentle smile, and being of special radiance you make manifest all your limbs, beginning with the bosom; (or) in the eastern quarter, spreading a brilliance like a gentle smile, of special light, you make manifest many forms — blue, yellow and the like.

Printed English (as printed): Goddess, manifest in person like a maiden, you go to the resplendent and munificent (sun); and, like a youthful bride (before her husband), you uncover, smiling, your bosom in his presence.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 10.

In this ṛk Uṣas is compared to a woman who first has the state of a maiden (kanyā) and afterwards the state of a grown (prauḍha) woman.

kanyeva tanvā śāśadānā — kamanīyā kanyeva | sā yathā janāntike vivasanā saṃcarati | tathā uṣaḥ tvaṃ kamanīyā apragalbhā satī kanyā tanvā śarīreṇa śāśadānā spaṣṭatāṃ gacchantī dṛśyase | śāśadānā śāśadyamānā spaṣṭatāṃ prāpnuvatī. The Kannada comment: Uṣas is like a beautiful girl, like a small child knowing nothing, who goes about unclothed near people; that is, as soon as the time of dawn arises it is described as a beautiful girl.

Yāska — kanyā kamanīyā bhavati | kaineyaṃ netavyeti vā | kamanenānīyata iti vā kanater vā syāt kāntikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 4-15, as printed "೪-೧೫"; the OCR agrees): the word kanyā is used with beauty as its cause. Iyam — this girl; either "kai netavyā": where is she to be led, [i.e. to join]; or kamanena — by the quality that attracts others she is led — she is taken along; or, from the root kan with the sense of "beautiful, shining", the word kanyā is derived. Following this, Sāyaṇa explains kamanīyā as "lovely with the beauty of the body".

śāśadānaḥ — śāśadyamānaḥ (Ni. 6-16, as printed "೬-೧೬"): since Yāska has so explained it, the sense is "possessing the manner of being perceived by everyone".

devi iyakṣamāṇaṃ devam eṣi — by this sentence it is described that Uṣas, whose nature is to spread light, goes to the Sun, the giver of light who fulfils the wishes of the sacrificer who wishes to sacrifice — like a girl choosing her husband, who obtains him as her husband.

saṃsmayamānā yuvatiḥ vakṣāṃsi āvir kṛṇuṣe — Sāyaṇa explains two meanings by this sentence. In the first meaning he explains the word yuvatiḥ as yuvatir iva, a case of the dropped simile-particle (lupta-upamā): thus, a mature woman, that is one with an age and bodily strength fit to enjoy pleasure, a beautiful woman, in front of her beloved displays the desire for enjoyment she has, shows a gentle smile and her own grace; so Uṣas acts in front of the Sun — this is the purport.

In the second meaning, in the eastern quarter, spreading her own light that is like a gentle smile, and making her light and the objects in the world visible to all, Uṣas acts so that the beauty of the world becomes visible to all — this is the purport.

उपो अदर्शि शुन्ध्युवो न वक्षो नोधा इवाविरकृत प्रियाणि । अद्मसन्न ससतो बोधयन्ती शश्वत्तमागात्पुनरेयुषीणाम् ॥

upo adarśi śundhyuvo na vakṣo nodhā ivāvirakṛta priyāṇi | admasanna sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamāgātpunareyuṣīṇām ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-124-4 [?] — as printed; the last numeral is doubtful in my reading, and the OCR shape "n-nge-V" gives only the first two groups.) Verse read letter by letter from the image; the OCR agrees except for "puna-reyuṣīṇām". Gloss: "[She] has been seen, like the bosom of a (self-)cleansing woman; as a Nodhas-like [poet] she has made her dear [forms] manifest; waking the sleepers who lie down for food, she has come, the most continual of those who return" — editorial and tentative.

In this ṛk the word vakṣaḥ is explained as rūpāṇi ("forms"). Sāyaṇa: vakṣāṃsi — vakṣa iti rūpanāma | vantsthānīyāni nīlapītādīni rūpāṇi: the word vakṣaḥ conveys the meaning "form". As a young woman makes manifest the parts of her body, her bosom and so on, so Uṣas makes manifest the forms of the objects — blue, yellow and so on; thus the meaning is explained.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar pages pp. 115–117; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). tanvā — instrumental singular, the ending ṭā; the yaṇ substitution in the place of the acute; since the ending follows that, udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya (Pā. 8-2-4) gives the ending the svarita. śāśadānā — root śada śātane; dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ (Pā. 3-1-22) gives yaṅ in the sense of intensity; śānac after it in the sense of laṭ; chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117) gives it ārdhadhātuka designation, hence ato lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-48) elides the preceding a and yasya halaḥ (Pā. 6-4-49) the y; dīrgho 'kitaḥ (Pā. 6-4-83) lengthens the reduplication; since the preceding sūtra also gives the sārvadhātuka designation, abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the accent on the first syllable (so the word is not final-acute); in the feminine, ajādyataṣṭāp gives ṭāp; aco 'prāgṛhya- [the rule on nasalised ā] makes the ā nasalised.

eṣi — root iṅ (i gatau); second person singular sip; śap with luk; guṇa of the root-vowel on account of sip; since it stands at the head of a pāda there is no nighāta accent; since sip is pit it is unaccented, so the root's accent remains; ādeśapratyayayoḥ gives ṣatva of the ending.

iyakṣamāṇam — root yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; in the sense of wish, dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā (Pā. 3-1-7) gives san; san-yaṅoḥ (the reduplication of the root); for the reduplicative syllable the initial consonant remains, and in the Veda saṃprasāraṇa occurs; pūrvarūpa; cojaḥ kuḥ gives ku (guttural) for the j of the root; khari ca gives ca[r]; ādeśapratyayayoḥ gives ṣa for the s of san; āne muk (Pā. 7-2-82) gives the augment muk to the stem; ṇatva of the n of śānac on account of the ṣ; abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189) gives acute on the first syllable; accusative singular.

saṃsmayamānā — root ṣmiṅ īṣadhasane; śānac in that sense, śap augment; guṇa and ayādeśa with that; āne muk gives muk to the stem ending in a; since the ending follows the upadeśa the sārvadhātuka occurs, so by tāsyanudāttet (Pā. 6-1-186) it is unaccented and the root-accent remains; in the compound gatikārakopapadāt kṛt gives the accent of the final member; in the feminine, because it ends in a, ṭāp.

yuvatiḥ — the word yuvan; when the feminine is intended, yūnas tiḥ (Pā. 4-1-77) gives the suffix ti; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya gives the loss of the n; by the accent of the suffix it is final-acute.

purastāt — pūrvādharāvarāṇāṃ purdhavaś caiṣām (Pā. 5-3-39) gives the suffix astāti; for pūrva, pur is substituted; the suffix has the acute on its first syllable.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सुसंकाशा मातृमृष्टेव योषाविस्तन्वं कृणुषे दृशे कम् । भद्रा त्वमुषो वितरं व्युच्छ न तत्ते अन्या उषसो नशन्त ॥ ११ ॥

susaṃkāśā mātṛmṛṣṭeva yoṣāvistanvaṃ kṛṇuṣe dṛśe kam | bhadrā tvamuṣo vitaraṃ vyuccha na tatte anyā uṣaso naśanta ‖ 11 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

सुऽसंकाशा । मातृमृष्टाऽइव । योषा । आविः । तन्वम् । कृणुषे । दृशे । कम् । भद्रा । त्वम् । उषः । वितरम् । वि । उच्छ । न । तत् । ते । अन्याः । उषसः । नशन्त ॥ ११ ॥

su 'saṃkāśā | mātṛmṛṣṭā 'iva | yoṣā | āviḥ | tanvam | kṛṇuṣe | dṛśe | kam | bhadrā | tvam | uṣaḥ | vitaram | vi | uccha | na | tat | te | anyāḥ | uṣasaḥ | naśanta ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे उषोदेवि मातृमृष्टा मातृभिर्जननीभिः शुद्धीकृता योषेव सुसंकाशात्यर्थं प्रकाशमाना त्वं तन्वं स्वकीयां तनुं दृशे सर्वेषां दर्शनायाविः कृणुषे । प्रकटयसि । यथा लोके मात्रादिना स्वलंकृतात्यन्तं शोभना सती स्वकीयं लावण्योपेतं सर्वशरीरं दर्शनायाविष्करोति तद्वत्त्वमित्यर्थः । अत्र कमिति पादपूरणोऽत्र विशेषस्याभावात् शिशिरं जीवनाय कमिवत् । तथा च यास्काचार्यः । मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिदु इति । नि. १-९ । इति । यद्वा । कमिति सुखवचनः । सुखं यथा भवति तथाविष्कृणुष इत्यर्थः । हे उषः यत एवं करोषि अतो भद्रा कल्याणशीला स्तुत्या त्वं वितरं व्युच्छ । आवरकमन्धकारं विप्रकृष्टं यथा भवति तथा विवासय । अत्र यद्यपि विशेषो न श्रुतस्तथापि प्रकाशनिवर्त्यत्वात्परिहरणीयत्वाच्च विवासनीयं तम एवेति गम्यते । किंच ते तव तद्विवसनमन्या उषसोऽतीता आगामिन्यश्च न नशन्त । न व्याप्नुवन्ति । तथा व्युच्छेति भावः । नशतिर्व्याप्तिकर्मा । इन्नति नक्षतीति व्याप्तिकर्मसु पाठात् ॥

he uṣodevi mātṛmṛṣṭā mātṛbhirjananībhiḥ śuddhīkṛtā yoṣeva susaṃkāśātyarthaṃ prakāśamānā tvaṃ tanvaṃ svakīyāṃ tanuṃ dṛśe sarveṣāṃ darśanāyāviḥ kṛṇuṣe | prakaṭayasi | yathā loke mātrādinā svalaṃkṛtātyantaṃ śobhanā satī svakīyaṃ lāvaṇyopetaṃ sarvaśarīraṃ darśanāyāviṣkaroti tadvattvamityarthaḥ | atra kamiti pādapūraṇo 'tra viśeṣasyābhāvāt śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kamivat | tathā ca yāskācāryaḥ | mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidu iti | ni. 1-9 | iti | yadvā | kamiti sukhavacanaḥ | sukhaṃ yathā bhavati tathāviṣkṛṇuṣa ityarthaḥ | he uṣaḥ yata evaṃ karoṣi ato bhadrā kalyāṇaśīlā stutyā tvaṃ vitaraṃ vyuccha | āvarakamandhakāraṃ viprakṛṣṭaṃ yathā bhavati tathā vivāsaya | atra yadyapi viśeṣo na śrutastathāpi prakāśanivartyatvātpariharaṇīyatvācca vivāsanīyaṃ tama eveti gamyate | kiṃca te tava tadvivasanamanyā uṣaso 'tītā āgāminyaśca na naśanta | na vyāpnuvanti | tathā vyuccheti bhāvaḥ | naśatirvyāptikarmā | innati nakṣatīti vyāptikarmasu pāṭhāt ‖

Read from the image and compared with the OCR; the OCR's Devanagari is badly garbled in the middle ("tanvaṃ", "śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kamivat" are read from the image). A few words in the middle of the passage are small and doubtful, e.g. "mitākṣareṣv anarthakāḥ kam īm id u", and the numeral of the Nirukta reference, which I read as "1-9" ("೧-೯"; the OCR "१-९"). "O goddess Uṣas, mātṛmṛṣṭā — purified by her mothers, the mothers who bore her — like a young woman (yoṣā iva), susaṃkāśā — shining exceedingly: you make your own body (tanvam) manifest for all to see (dṛśe). As in the world a woman well adorned by her mother and others, being exceedingly beautiful, reveals her whole body, full of loveliness, to be seen — so you: that is the sense. Here the word kam is merely a pāda-filler, since no special meaning is found — like kam in śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kam. And Yāska says: 'In the metres of limited syllables, [the particles] kam, īm, id, u are without meaning' (Ni. 1-9). Or else kam means 'happiness': you make [your body] manifest so that there is happiness. O Uṣas, since you do thus, therefore, auspicious and praiseworthy, vitaraṃ vi uccha — dispel (vivāsaya) the darkness that covers, so that it goes far. Although it is not stated here what is to be dispelled, it is understood to be darkness itself, since it is removed by light and must be got rid of. Moreover, this dispelling of yours — other dawns, past and future, na naśanta — do not reach it (do not pervade it); so vi uccha: that is the sense. The root naś has the sense of pervading, since it is read among the verbs of pervading: innati, nakṣati."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Uṣaḥ — O goddess Uṣas; mātṛmṛṣṭā — adorned by her mother (made pure); yoṣā iva — like a woman; susaṃkāśā — exceedingly radiant; tvam — you; tanvam — (your) own body; dṛśe — for (everyone's) seeing; kam — so that it be pleasant; āviḥ kṛṇuṣe — you make manifest; (ataḥ — therefore); bhadrā — auspicious (therefore praiseworthy); (tvam — you); vitaram — the covering darkness; vi uccha — drive away; te — your; tat — that (work of dispelling the darkness); anyāḥ atītāḥ ca anāgatāḥ ca uṣasaḥ — other dawns, past and future; na naśanta — do not attain.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O goddess Uṣas, like a woman adorned by her mother, being of special radiance, you make your body to be seen (by all). Therefore, being auspicious (and praiseworthy), dispel the darkness that covers the world, in a manner that none of the dawns, past or future, can imitate.

Printed English (as printed): Radiant as a bride decorated by her mother, you willingly display your person to the view. Do you, auspicious Ushas, remove the investing (gloom), for other dawns than you do not disperse it.

Special topics, Ṛk 11.

mātṛmṛṣṭā yoṣā iva susaṃkāśā — mātṛbhiḥ jananībhiḥ śuddhīkṛtā yoṣā iva atyantaṃ prakāśamānā. yathā loke mātrādinā svalaṅkṛtā atyantaṃ śobhanā satī svakīyaṃ lāvaṇyopetaṃ sarvaśarīraṃ darśanāyāviṣkaroti tadvat tvam ity arthaḥ. A woman who has been prepared (or adorned) by her mother and other intimate women, a loving woman, being very beautiful, shows to others her body, full of loveliness, so that it comes within the sight of her beloved; so Uṣas too shows her form in front of the Sun — thus it is described.

Yāska explains the word yoṣā: it is derived from the root yu miśraṇe, "yoṣā yauteḥ" (Ni. 3-15, as read by the OCR; the print "೩-೧೫"). The commentator (vṛttikāra) explains: sā hi miśrayaty ātmānaṃ puruṣeṇa sākam — a woman unites with a man in order to have union of bodies with him.

dṛśe kam — atra kam iti pādapūraṇaḥ viśeṣasyābhāvāt śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kam iti vat | yadvā kam iti sukhavacanaḥ sukhaṃ yathā bhavati tathā āviṣkṛṇuṣe. Here, because the word kam is an indeclinable, for want of any other special meaning it is, in one way, a mere pāda-filler; Sāyaṇa has explained it so. And Yāska:

अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छन्ति पदेपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्धितेति

atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu grantheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchanti padepūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmiddhiteti

(Ni. 1-9, as printed "೧-೯", the shape in the image; read letter by letter, the last words doubtful.) Particles (indeclinables) used in sentences serve to fill out words. Since verses are bound by metres of measured syllables, the indeclinables kam, īm, it, u in them convey no meaning — so they are without meaning (anarthaka).

निष्टक्राः [?] भूरितोका वृकादिव । बिभ्यस्यन्तो वनाशिरे । शिशिरं जीवनाय कम् ॥

niṣṭakrāḥ [?] bhūritokā vṛkādiva | bibhyasyanto vanāśire | śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kam ‖

(Ni. 1-[?]; the numerals "೧-೧೮" or similar are not clear.) In this quotation the word kam is, though it is absent, used without any purpose as if for the completion of the sense — thus an example is given.

Moreover both words kam and īm are recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]4, numerals unclear), and kam is also recorded among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-[?]9, unclear). Following this explanation of Yāska, Sāyaṇa explains the word kam in the sense of happiness: Uṣas displays her own body to all in a manner that gives happiness — this is the second meaning.

bhadrā tvaṃ vyuccha — kalyāṇaśīlā stutyā āvarakam andhakāraṃ viprakṛṣṭaṃ yathā bhavati tathā vivāsaya. Since Uṣas is praised, she is prayed to destroy the dense darkness. Uṣas is described as the bringer of auspiciousness. Since Uṣas is always engaged in the act of bringing light, in the matter of the work of Uṣas there is no particular thing to be prayed for. Hence the addition (upasaṃhāra) is stated: of those past and future dawns pervading and destroying the covering darkness...

naśanta — innati, nakṣati — among these ten verbs of pervading, 'naśat' is read (Ni. 3-10, as read by the OCR); so naśanta means 'they pervade'.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page; noted briefly, numbers as read). susaṃkāśā — root kāśṛ dīptau; since it belongs to the pacādi class, the suffix aṭ; ṭāp in the feminine; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 as read by the OCR) gives the accent of the final member of the kṛt-compound; nominative singular. mātṛmṛṣṭā — mātṛbhiḥ mṛṣṭā; root mṛjū śuddhau; in the passive, niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102) gives kta; vraśca-bhrasja-…-ṣaḥ (Pā. 8-2-36) gives ṣa for the root's j; ṣṭutva of the t of the ending following that; tṛtīyā karmaṇi (Pā. 6-2-48) gives the accent of the first member; then ṭāp in the feminine as before. tanvam — the word tanu; the accusative am following, tanvādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam gives yaṇ; the yaṇ stands at the place of the acute; since the ending follows it, udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya (Pā. 8-2-4) gives the ending the svarita. dṛśe — root dṛśir prekṣaṇe; dṛśe vikhye ca (Pā. 3-4-11) records it as a tumarthe form in the Veda; since it ends in e and is a kṛdanta, kṛnmejantaḥ (Pā. 1-1-39) gives it the indeclinable designation. bhadrā — root bhadi kalyāṇe sukhe ca; the Uṇādi suffix rak (bhadrā nominative singular); final-acute by the accent of the suffix. vitaram — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; pacādi aṭ; guṇa and raparatva with that; in the compound gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the final member; the final member is final-acute by the suffix-accent. uccha — root uchī vivāse; loṭ second singular, sip with hi substituted; ato heḥ (Pā. 6-4-105) elides hi; the verb-accent nighāta after a non-verb.

naśanta — root naś adarśane; here used in the sense of motion ('going'); recorded as innati nakṣati among the verbs of pervading. By vyatyayo bahulam the ātmanepada ending (Chāndasa) …

Read from the image; the OCR is garbled in this passage, e.g. "aśvāvaratsava". The words "asmākam" near the end are doubtful. "Aśvāvatīḥ — possessed of horses, possessing many horses; likewise gomatīḥ — possessed of many cows. Viśvavārāḥ — those whose times (vārāḥ) are choiceworthy for all, i.e. who belong to all times; or else those among whom all are choosers, i.e. choiceworthy by all. Sūryasya raśmibhir yatamānāḥ — striving together with the rays of the Sun to dispel darkness. Although the Sun's rays alone are able to illumine the world, still, since the dispelling of darkness is needed before sunrise, their effort too is not inconsistent: the deities of the rays too are illuminators, that is the sense. Moreover bhadrā nāma vahamānāḥ — bearing a name that is auspicious, praiseworthy, a bowing (namanam) favourable to all people — the Uṣases, the Uṣas deities, parā ca yanti — go away, and punar ā ca yanti — come back again; the word ca is in both places in view of each other. Those that have gone in past days are the very ones that come again to us on later days — so day by day they go and come for the maintenance of the world: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 12). Aśvāvatīḥ — possessed of horses; gomatīḥ — possessed of cows; viśvavārāḥ — belonging to all times (desired by all); sūryasya — of the Sun; raśmibhiḥ — with the rays; yatamānāḥ — striving (to dispel the darkness); bhadrā — auspicious; nāma — favour (to all people); vahamānāḥ — bringing about; (the) uṣāsaḥ — Uṣas deities; parā yanti — depart; punaḥ ca ā yanti — and come again.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Possessed of horses and cows, at all times striving at the work of dispelling darkness together (in concert) with the rays of the Sun, and bringing auspiciousness to all, the Uṣas deities keep going and keep coming.

Printed English (as printed): Possessed of horses, possessed of cows, existing through all time, vying with the rays of the sun (in dissipating darkness) auspicious Dawns, sending down benefits (on mankind), pass away and again return.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 12.

viśvavārāḥ — viśve vārāḥ varaṇīyāḥ kālā yāsāṃ tāḥ | sārvakālīnāḥ | yadvā viśve varitāro yāsu tāḥ | viśvair varaṇīyāḥ. The word vāra is derived from the root vṝ (vṛñ varaṇe) which conveys "choose, desire", so it means "desired"; thus the word viśvavārāḥ, used as an epithet of the word uṣāsaḥ, is explained in one way as "for them all the times of dawn are desired", and Sāyaṇa explains it in another way as "all desire the times of dawn" (viśvaiḥ varaṇīyāḥ). By both these meanings the beauty of the times of dawn, and its being a benefit to all, becomes evident.

sūryasya raśmibhir yatamānāḥ — sūryaraśmibhiḥ sākaṃ tamonivāraṇāya prayatnaṃ kurvāṇāḥ. The sense: the dawns, joining with the rays of the Sun, strive to remove the darkness. The darkness is removed by the Sun's rays themselves; but before the Sun rises, in order to destroy darkness by making the Sun's rays manifest, Uṣas spreads her own light and is a helper — this is the sense.

"O Uṣas, following (anuyacchamānā) the ray (raśmim — the rays) of the true Āditya (ṛtasya) — acting in accord with them — place (dhehi, establish) in us each auspicious kratu, that is, each auspicious and praiseworthy action, worldly or Vedic, or the wisdom concerned with it. O Uṣas, well invoked for us (suhavā), vi uccha — dispel the darkness; make light: that is the sense. For what? That is said: maghavatsu — magha is a name for wealth: in us the sacrificers possessed of wealth in the form of oblations, may rāyaḥ (riches) — of many kinds — arise; the word ca has the sense of conjunction with the kratu mentioned before."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. He uṣaḥ — O goddess Uṣas; ṛtasya — of the true (Āditya); raśmim — the rays; anuyacchamānā — acting in accord with all (you); bhadraṃ bhadraṃ kratum — each auspicious action (and the knowledge of it); asmāsu — in us; dhehi — establish; (uṣaḥ — O goddess Uṣas;) suhavā — well (with praise) invoked (by us); naḥ — for us; vi uccha — dispel the darkness; maghavatsu — those possessed of wealth in the form of oblations; asmāsu — (among us) the sacrificers; adya — now; rāyaḥ ca syuḥ — may many kinds of wealth arise.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O goddess Uṣas, directing the rays of Āditya to suit us, make each of (our) auspicious [works] firm; well praised (by us) dispel the darkness for us; grant many kinds of prosperity to the sacrificers who are possessed of oblations and the like.

Printed English (as printed): Co-operating with the rays of the true (sun), confirm in us every propitious act : earnestly invoked by us to-day, disperse, Ushas, (the darkness), that wealth may devolve upon us, (already) affluent (in sacrificial treasures).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 13.

ṛtasya — satyabhūtādityasya — The word ṛta is used in the senses udaka (water) (Ni. 2-24, as printed, the OCR agrees), muhūrta (a particular division of time) (Ni. 2-25), satya or yajña (Ni. 4-19)…

…thus the word ṛta has many meanings; here it is an epithet of the word Āditya. It is described that Uṣas follows the ray of the true Āditya and spreads light.

bhadraṃ bhadraṃ kratuṃ dehi [as printed; the bhāṣya reads dhehi] — tattat kalyāṇaṃ stutyaṃ vā laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ karma tadviṣayāṃ prajñāṃ vā sthāpaya. In the world, skill in carrying out acts related to conduct that is praiseworthy and auspicious in various ways, or proficiency in doing the actions prescribed in the Veda — this Uṣas is prayed to bring about for us.

Yāska records the word kratu among the names of karma (Ni. 3-2) and among the names of prajñā (Ni. 3-13):

उतस्य वाजी क्षिपणिं तुरण्यति ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपिकक्ष आसनि । क्रतुं दधिक्रा अनु संतवीत्वत्पथामङ्कांस्यन्वापनीफणत् ॥

utasya vājī kṣipaṇiṃ turaṇyati grīvāyāṃ baddho apikakṣa āsani | kratuṃ dadhikrā anu saṃtavītvatpathāmaṅkāṃsyanvāpanīphaṇat ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-40-4, as printed "೪-೪೦-೪".) — citing this ṛk he has stated for kratu the meaning "action or wisdom". Sāyaṇa too has explained the word kratu in both these ways.

suhavā — suṣṭhu āhūtā: the sense is that Uṣas is invoked in the sacrifices, in the order prescribed by the Veda, in the proper way.

vyuccha — tamo vivāsaya, prakāśaṃ kuru. The root uchī conveys "removal" (vivāsana, meaning "destroy"), with the prefix vi; so Uṣas is prayed to root out the darkness and spread the light exceedingly.

asmāsu rāyaḥ maghavatsu ca syuḥ — by this sentence Uṣas is prayed that to us who perform the sacrifice there may be wealth in the form of oblations, to offer to the various deities, and that the various rites may be completed.

The word rāyaḥ and the word magha in maghavatsu also convey the meaning "wealth", being recorded among the twenty-eight names of wealth (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR): "magham, reknaḥ" and so on.

परिषद्यं हिरण्यस्य रेक्णो नित्यस्य रायः पतयः स्याम । न शेषो अग्ने अन्यजातमस्त्यचेतानस्य मा पथो वि दुक्षः ॥

pariṣadyaṃ hiraṇyasya rekṇo nityasya rāyaḥ patayaḥ syāma | na śeṣo agne anyajātamastyacetānasya mā patho vi dukṣaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-4-2 [?], as read from the print "೭-೪-೨"; the OCR "2-4-2" is letter-shaped; hiraṇyasya as read — the print may be hairaṇyasya [?].) In this ṛk, having explained for the word rāyaḥ the sense "of wealth, [rāyaḥ = dhanasya]",

…by saṃprasāraṇa and pūrvarūpa of the root, taking which as its cause sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives the guṇa of the root's u, and the av-substitution; as the ap-suffix has the marker p it is unaccented, so the root accent remains; in the compound the accent of the final member's own nature arises.

rāyaḥ — the word rai; its nominative plural with jas following; echo 'yavāyāvaḥ gives āy [as printed "ಏಚೋಽಯವಾಯಾವಃ"]. syuḥ — root as bhuvi; liṅ third person plural, the suffix jhi; for it the substitute us; the augment yāsuṭ; since it has the marker p [pit? as read], śnasor allopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-111) elides the a of the root; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. ‖ 13 ‖

Sūkta 124 — uṣā ucchantī (begins at the foot of printed p. 128)

ನೂರ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra ippattanālkaneya sūktavu (the one hundred and twenty-fourth Sūkta).

॥ भूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, from the Sāyaṇa text):

उषा उच्छन्तीति त्रयोदशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसः कक्षीवत आर्षं त्रैष्टुभमुषस्यम् । उषा उच्छन्तीत्यनुक्रान्तम् । विनियोगस्तु पूर्वसूक्त एवोक्तः ॥

uṣā ucchantīti trayodaśarcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasaḥ kakṣīvata ārṣaṃ traiṣṭubhamuṣasyam | uṣā ucchantītyanukrāntam | viniyogastu pūrvasūkta evoktaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the last word, "evoktaḥ", is given as read. "The fourth sūkta, of thirteen ṛks, beginning uṣā ucchantī, of Kakṣīvat Dairghatamasa, in the Triṣṭubh metre, addressed to Uṣas. It is listed in the Anukramaṇī as uṣā ucchantī; its application (viniyoga) has been stated in the preceding sūkta itself."

Anuvāda (Kannada). This Sūkta, beginning uṣā ucchantī, is the fourth Sūkta in the eighteenth Anuvāka. It has thirteen ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa; the deity is Uṣas; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as uṣā ucchantī; its viniyoga has been stated before.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उषा उच्छन्ती समिधाने अग्ना उद्यन्त्सूर्य उर्विया ज्योतिरश्रेत् । देवो नो अत्र सविता न्वर्थं प्रासावीद्द्विपत्प्र चतुष्पदित्यै ॥ १ ॥

uṣā ucchantī samidhāne agnā udyantsūrya urviyā jyotiraśret | devo no atra savitā nvarthaṃ prāsāvīddvipatpra catuṣpadityai ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उषाः । उच्छन्ती । सम्ऽइधाने । अग्नौ । उत्ऽयन् । सूर्यः । उर्विया । ज्योतिः । अश्रेत् । देवः । नः । अत्र । सविता । नु । अर्थम् । प्र । असावीत् । द्विऽपत् । प्र । चतुःऽपत् । इत्यै ॥ १ ॥

uṣāḥ | ucchantī | sam 'idhāne | agnau | ut 'yan | sūryaḥ | urviyā | jyotiḥ | aśret | devaḥ | naḥ | atra | savitā | nu | artham | pra | asāvīt | dvi 'pat | pra | catuḥ 'pat | ityai ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ The bhāṣya begins on this page and continues at the top of p. 130. Read from the image; the first sentence — "eṣoṣāḥ …" and the phrase "karmārthe kartṛprayogaḥ" — is doubtful in the print and given as read. Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 124".

eṣoṣāḥ samidhāne 'gnau | agniṣu sāmānyaikavacanam | agniṣu samidhyamāneṣu satsu | karmārthe kartṛprayogaḥ [?] | uṣaḥkāle hyāhavanīyādayaḥ prajvālyante | ucchantī tamo vivāsayantī urviyā uru bahulaṃ jyotiḥ prakāśamaśret | sevate | prakāśate prakāśayati vā sarvam | kimiva udyansūryaḥ | upamāpradhānanirdeśaḥ ‖

उदितः सूर्य इव सूर्यो यथा प्रकाशयति तथेत्यर्थः । अत्र त्वदुदयानन्तरमस्मिन्कर्मणि वा सविता देवः सर्वस्य प्रेरकः सूर्यो नोऽस्मदर्थं नु क्षिप्रमर्थमपेक्षितम् । अर्थशब्दोऽत्र विशेषणवाची नपुंसकलिङ्गः । अयन्नर्थानि कृण्वन्नांसीत्यादौ (ऋ. ७-६३-४ [?]) तथादृष्टत्वात् ॥ अरणीयं [?] द्विपत् पादद्वयोपेतं मनुष्यादिरूपं धनं प्रासावीत् । अनुजानातु ददात्वित्यर्थः । तथा चतुष्पत् पादचतुष्टयोपेतं गवादिरूपं धनं प्रासावीत् । किमर्थम् । इत्यै । द्विपदां चतुष्पदां च गमनाय । यद्वा । न इत्यै इति संबन्धः । अस्मद्गमनागमनादिव्यापाराये[त्यर्थः] ॥

uditaḥ sūrya iva sūryo yathā prakāśayati tathetyarthaḥ | atra tvadudayānantaramasminkarmaṇi vā savitā devaḥ sarvasya prerakaḥ sūryo no 'smadarthaṃ nu kṣipramarthamapekṣitam | arthaśabdo 'tra viśeṣaṇavācī napuṃsakaliṅgaḥ | ayannarthāni kṛṇvannāṃsītyādau (ṛ. 7-63-4 [?]) tathādṛṣṭatvāt ‖ araṇīyaṃ [?] dvipat pādadvayopetaṃ manuṣyādirūpaṃ dhanaṃ prāsāvīt | anujānātu dadātvityarthaḥ | tathā catuṣpat pādacatuṣṭayopetaṃ gavādirūpaṃ dhanaṃ prāsāvīt | kimartham | ityai | dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ ca gamanāya | yadvā | na ityai iti saṃbandhaḥ | asmadgamanāgamanādivyāpārāye[tyarthaḥ] ‖

Read from the image; the first half of the passage is doubtful in the print — "atra tvad-udayānantaram asminkarmaṇi vā" and "araṇīyam [?]" are my readings; the OCR garbles them. The Ṛg reference "7-63-4" is read from the image "೭-೬೩-೪" (the OCR agrees on the shape). Sense: "This Uṣas, when the fires (the Āhavanīya and the others) are being kindled — for the Āhavanīya and the other fires are kindled at the time of Uṣas — ucchantī, driving away the darkness, urviyā — abundantly — has resorted to (aśret, 'serves', 'shines' or 'illumines') the light (jyotiḥ, brightness), like the rising Sun (udyan sūryaḥ), that is, as the Sun illuminates when risen. Here, after your rising, the god Savitṛ, the impeller of all, the Sun, for us — nu, quickly — artham (the desired): the word artha here, as an epithet, is a neuter noun, as seen in such places as ayann arthāni kṛṇvann ajāsīt … Let him bestow (prāsāvīt, let him permit, let him give) wealth in the form of men and the like, 'two-footed' (dvipat, possessed of two feet); and likewise wealth in the form of cattle and the like, 'four-footed' (catuṣpat). For what? Ityai — for the going of the two-footed and the four-footed. Or else, the connection is: na ityai — for our activity of going and coming and the like."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Agnau — when the fire (the fires); samidhāne — are kindled; uṣāḥ — the goddess Uṣas; udyan sūryaḥ — like the rising Sun; ucchantī — driving away (the darkness); urviyā — abundantly; jyotiḥ — light; aśret — attains (she illumines everything); atra — after this (in this rite); savitā devaḥ — the god Savitṛ (the impeller of all); naḥ — for us; nu — quickly; artham — the desired; dvipat — beings with two feet (wealth in the form of men and the like); ityai — for (our) going and coming; pra asāvīt — may he grant; catuṣpat — beings with four feet (wealth in the form of cattle and the like); — may he grant.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. While the Āhavanīya and other fires are kindled, the goddess Uṣas, driving away the darkness with her (own) boundless brilliance, like the Sun, shines; after her rising, may the god Savitṛ, the Sun, for the sake of our going and coming and other works, quickly favour us with two-footed and four-footed beings.

Printed English (as printed): When the (sacred) fire is kindled, Ushas sheds abundant light, dispersing (the darkness) like the rising sun; may the divine Savitri bestow upon us for our use, wealth of both bipeds and quadrupeds.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 1.

ucchantī — For this word one may give, by way of the root uchī ("driving away"), the meaning "destroying", or, in another way, "shining with brilliance". The derivation of the word uṣāḥ is also from ucchati: uṣāḥ kasmād ucchatīti satyā rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ…

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 763-4 Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7.

original p. 131

— with this sentence the author of the Nirukta states this etymology (Ni. 2-18, as printed "೨-೧೮"; the OCR agrees). But by the sentence uṣā vaṣṭeḥ kāntikarmaṇa ucchater itarā mādhyamikā (Ni. 12-7, as read by the OCR; the print "೧೨-೭") the word ucchati may be derived either from the root vaś kāntau or from the root uchī vivāse. Ucchantī uṣāḥ means "Uṣas who, driving away the darkness, appears outside", or "Uṣas who shines".

nu — nu ity eṣo 'nekakarmā | idaṃ nu kariṣyatīti hetvapadeśe | kathaṃ nu kariṣyatīty anupraśne (Ni. 1-4, as printed "೧-೪"). The indeclinable nu has many meanings. When one says idaṃ nu kariṣyati the nu means "therefore", "because of this" (the sense of a reason); when one says kathaṃ nu kariṣyati the nu is an inquiry, "how?". Likewise athāpy upamārthe bhavati: even in indicating a comparison the word nu is used. For example —

अक्षो न चक्र्योः शूर बृहन्ते महना रिरिचे रोदस्योः । वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यूतयो रुरुहुरिन्द्र पूर्वीः ॥

akṣo na cakryoḥ śūra bṛhante mahanā ririce rodasyoḥ | vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayā vyūtayo ruruhurindra pūrvīḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-24-? — numerals "೬-೨೪-೯" as read from the print; doubtful [?].) — citing this ṛk, the author of the Nirukta (1-4) gives vṛkṣasyeva te puruhūta śākhāḥ — "like a tree, or like the branches of a tree" — for the word nu, with the sense of comparison. Likewise it also has the sense "quickly", "in a hurry".

नू मर्तो दयते सनिष्यन्यो विष्णव उरुगायाय दाशत् । प्र यः सत्राचा मनसा यजात एतावन्तं नर्यमाविवासात् ॥

nū marto dayate saniṣyanyo viṣṇava urugāyāya dāśat | pra yaḥ satrācā manasā yajāta etāvantaṃ naryamāvivāsāt ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-1, as read from the print "೭-೧೦೦-೧"; the OCR "2-100-1" is letter-shaped.) — in such ṛks nu has the sense "quickly" (kṣipram).

नू इन्द्र शूर स्तवमान ऊती ब्रह्मजूतस्तन्वा वावृधस्व । उप नो वाजान्मिमीह्युप स्त्रीन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

nū indra śūra stavamāna ūtī brahmajūtastanvā vāvṛdhasva | upa no vājānmimīhyupa strīnyūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-98-11 [?], as read from the print.) Read letter by letter; "upa stīn / strīn" — the print shows "ಉಪ ಸ್ತ್ರೀನ್ಯೂಯಂ", given as "upa strīn yūyam" without completing it from memory. In these and other places adya, that is, "now", "at once" is the meaning; likewise, as the author of the Nirukta says, nu ity eṣo 'nekakarmā (Ni. 1-4) — "this nu has many meanings" — in the present ṛk it means "quickly, soon".

ityai — this word means "going": "for going and coming", that is, for moving about. Here one connection is dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ ca gamanāya — "for the going of the two-footed and the four-footed"…

In the earlier part Prajāpati, resolving to give his daughter Sūryā to Soma for marriage, all the gods came wishing to choose her. Then Prajāpati laid down a condition that the thousand mantras known as the Āśvina-śastra be recited, and that it should not fall short of that. As a cart-wheel, once it is smeared with oil, turns smoothly, so after drinking ghee (kṛtapāna) the mantras can be recited smoothly; therefore one must first drink ghee and afterwards recite. And just as a bird, ready to fly, makes its body light, so the suitor of her must have that quality [of lightness].

The words marked [?], "mamehāstviti" and "apyākurutām", are doubtful in the print and are given as read; they match the sense of the Kannada paraphrase that follows. All the deities, running together in this race, and Agni, the foremost, came in front of all. Then the two Aśvins approached Agni and asked: "Give us the way; help us to win in this race." Agni agreed, and asked that he too be given a share in the victory; therefore in the Āśvina-śastra there is a portion for him too. Afterwards the two Aśvins followed Uṣas: "Give us the way; help us to win in this race." Then the goddess Uṣas agreed, and laid down the condition that she too have a share in their victory; they consented, and the Āśvina-śastra therefore contains the recitation of the Sūkta addressed to Uṣas. In the same way the Aśvins asked Indra as well, and made him a sharer in this.

In this context, since the mantras addressed to Agni, to Indra, and to Uṣas have to be recited, the objection comes up how it came to be named "Āśvina-śastra"; the answer is that, since it is chiefly recited for the victory of the Aśvin deities, this name belongs to all these mantras. The connection that exists between the present Sūktas 1-123 and 1-124 and the Āśvina-śastra is as stated above.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अमिनती दैव्यानि व्रतानि प्रमिनती मनुष्या युगानि । ईयुषीणामुपमा शश्वतीनामायतीनां प्रथमोषा व्यद्यौत् ॥ २ ॥

aminatī daivyāni vratāni praminatī manuṣyā yugāni | īyuṣīṇāmupamā śaśvatīnāmāyatīnāṃ prathamoṣā vyadyaut ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अमिनती । दैव्यानि । व्रतानि । प्रऽमिनती । मनुष्या । युगानि । ईयुषीणाम् । उपऽमा । शश्वतीनाम् । आऽयतीनाम् । प्रथमा । उषाः । वि । अद्यौत् ॥ २ ॥

aminatī | daivyāni | vratāni | pra 'minatī | manuṣyā | yugāni | īyuṣīṇām | upa 'mā | śaśvatīnām | ā 'yatīnām | prathamā | uṣāḥ | vi | adyaut ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

दैव्यानि व्रतानि देवसंबन्धीन्यग्निहोत्रादीनि कर्माणि । व्रतमिति कर्मनाम । व्रतं कर्वरमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तानि कर्माण्यमिनती अहिंसन्ती भानप्रदानेनानुकूलं कुर्वती । तथा मनुष्या मनुष्याणां युगानि युगोपलक्षितान्निमेषादिकालावयवान्प्रमिनती प्रकर्षेण हिंसन्ती । आयुः क्षपयन्तीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । युगानि युगानि परस्परसंयोगं प्रमिनती हिंसन्ती । वियोगं कुर्वतीत्यर्थः ।

daivyāni vratāni devasaṃbandhīnyagnihotrādīni karmāṇi | vratamiti karmanāma | vrataṃ karvaramiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tāni karmāṇyaminatī ahiṃsantī bhānapradānenānukūlaṃ kurvatī | tathā manuṣyā manuṣyāṇāṃ yugāni yugopalakṣitānnimeṣādikālāvayavānpraminatī prakarṣeṇa hiṃsantī | āyuḥ kṣapayantītyarthaḥ | yadvā | yugāni yugāni parasparasaṃyogaṃ praminatī hiṃsantī | viyogaṃ kurvatītyarthaḥ |

Read from the image; checked against the OCR. "Daivyāni vratāni — the rites that belong to the gods, the Agnihotra and the rest. Vrata is a name for 'rite' (karman), since vrataṃ karvaram is read among the names of rites. Those rites aminatī — not harming, doing what is favourable by the giving of light. And manuṣyā — of men — yugāni — the divisions of time, beginning with the twinkling of an eye, marked by the yuga — prāminatī: she wears down exceedingly; that is, she exhausts life. Or else: yugāni yugāni — the pairs: prāminatī — she harms their mutual union; that is, she causes separation."

उषःकाले सर्वे यथायथं स्वस्वव्यापाराय गच्छन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । किंच ईयुषीणां गच्छन्तीनामतीतानां शश्वतीनां नित्यानामुषसामुपमा । ताभिः सदृशीत्यर्थः । सादृश्यं च सदृशीरद्य सदृशीरिदु श्व इत्युक्तम् । ऋ. १-१२३-८ । तथायतीनां प्रथमागामिनीनामुषसां प्रथमभाविनी सती व्यद्यौत् । विशेषेण प्रकाशते । यद्वा । ईयुषीणां गमनशीलानां पश्वादीनां शश्वतीनां संततिप्रवाहरूपेण नित्यानामुपमा । तत्सन्निभेत्यर्थः । तथायतीनां रात्र्यवसानसमय उत्पद्यमानानां प्रज्ञावागादीनां प्रथमा प्रथमभाविनी । उषस्यागतायां वाचो बुद्धयश्च स्फुरन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । तादृशी देवी व्यद्यौत् । प्राणिनामनुग्रहाय द्योतते ॥

Read from the image; the reference "ऋ. १-१२३-८" is as printed and agrees with the OCR; "sadṛśīr adya sadṛśīr idu śvaḥ" is read as printed. "At the time of Uṣas it is well known that all go, each as is fitting, to his own business. Moreover she is the upamā — the likeness — of the past Uṣases, īyuṣīṇām — those that have gone — śaśvatīnām — the everlasting: that is, she is like them. The likeness has been stated in 'such dawns today, such dawns tomorrow' (Ṛ. 1-123-8). Likewise, being first (prathamā) among the Uṣases that are to come (āyatīnām, the first-coming), she shines (vi adyaut) — she shines specially. Or else: she is like īyuṣīṇām — the beasts and the like that move about — śaśvatīnām — everlasting by their continuous flow of progeny; that is, she resembles them. And āyatīnām — of the knowledge, speech and the rest that arise at the end of the night — she is the first, the first to appear; for it is well known that when Uṣas has come, speech and intellect stir to life. Such a goddess has shone; she shines for the favour of living beings."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Daivyāni — belonging to the gods; vratāni — the rites, Agnihotra and the like; aminatī — not harming (since she is a giver of light, favourable); manuṣyā — of men; yugāni — the divisions of time beginning with the twinkling of the eye, or the pairs (couples); prāminatī — [she] who wears down exceedingly (causes decay), or who separates each from each; īyuṣīṇām — of those that have gone, or that are of a moving nature (and); śaśvatīnām — to the everlasting (Uṣases), or to living beings (everlasting by the continuity of progeny); upamā — like; tathā — and likewise āyatīnām — of the Uṣases that are to come, or of (wisdom and speech) that arise at the time of Uṣas; prathamā — the first, or the one standing at the beginning; uṣāḥ — goddess Uṣas; vi adyaut — shone well (shone for the favour of beings).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The goddess Uṣas does not obstruct the rites of the gods, the Agnihotra and the rest; but she wears away the lives of men. She, like those Uṣases who went before and who are everlasting (like those that are continuous in the flow of progeny), shone well as the first of the Uṣases to come (the first at the time of dawn for the wisdom and speech of waking beings, for their favour).

Printed English (as printed): Unimpeding divine rites, although wearing away the ages of mankind, the Dawn shines the similitude of the (mornings) that have passed, or that are to be for ever, the first of those that are to come.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.

An English critic named Bloomfield describes the poetic idea and the style of composition of this ṛk as follows [printed in English]:

There can be no question that I. 124.2. is the source of the repeated padas in I. 92. 11 and 12. The antithesis between अमिनती and प्रमिनती and ईयुषीणां and आयतीनां cannot but be intentional and primary. Note also the parallelism between अमिनती and आयतीनां; and प्रमिनती and ईयुषीणां. On the other hand, we ought to allow full weight to the really senseless non-sequitur of the second distich in I. 92. 11. reducing the ages of men, the woman shines by the light of her paramour (the sun). 'For the meaning of Yuga 'age' i. e. 'period of time' see Bal Gangadhar Tilak. The Arctic Home in the Vedas.

**There can be no question that I. 124.2. is the source of the repeated padas in I. 92. 11 and 12. The antithesis between* aminatī and praminatī and īyuṣīṇāṃ and āyatīnāṃ cannot but be intentional and primary. Note also the parallelism between aminatī and āyatīnāṃ; and praminatī and īyuṣīṇāṃ. *On the other hand, we ought to allow full weight to the really senseless non-sequitur of the second distich in I. 92. 11. reducing the ages of men, the woman shines by the light of her paramour (the sun). 'For the meaning of Yuga 'age ' i. e. 'period of time ' see Bal Gangadhar Tilak. The Arctic Home in the Vedas.**

Stanza I. 124.2 is the high-water mark of Vedic composition. The two antitheses अमिनती…………प्रमिनती and ईयुषीणां…………आयतीनां mark as later imitations all repetitions that disturb this balance. The relation of the two pairs of antithetical words may be expressed in the proportion: अमिनतीः आयतीनां :: प्रमिनती ईयुषीणां. That is to say: the dawns preserve the laws of the Gods (अमिनती) by their regular appearance (आयतीनां); the ages of men waste away (प्रमिनती) as the dawns fade day by day.

**Stanza I. 124.2 is the high-water mark of Vedic composition. The two antitheses* aminatī…………praminatī and īyuṣīṇāṃ…………āyatīnāṃ mark as later imitations all repetitions that disturb this balance. The relation of the two pairs of antithetical words may be expressed in the proportion: aminatīḥ āyatīnāṃ :: praminatī īyuṣīṇāṃ. That is to say: the dawns preserve the laws of the Gods (aminatī) by their regular appearance (āyatīnāṃ); the ages of men waste away (praminatī*) as the dawns fade day by day.**

(Rig-Veda Repetitions, Vol. I, p. 108.) Reproduced as printed; the Devanagari words inside the quotation are printed in the Kannada script in the source, in the hand of the printer, and are given here in Devanagari. The printed punctuation, "pădas", "Yuga ' age'" and the stray quotation mark, are kept. Thus, in the Kannada, the idea of the two ṛks 1-92-11 and 1-92-12 is combined in this single ṛk, and the construction of the antithesis in the excellent poetic style and the expression of feeling are greatly praised.

daivyāni vratāni aminatī — daivasaṃbandhīni agnihotrādikarmāṇi ahiṃsantī | bhānapradānena anukūlaṃ kurvatī: by giving light and by furnishing what is favourable to the sacrificer, she does not obstruct, "does not harm", the rites of sacrifice belonging to the gods — this is the sense.

yugāni prāminatī — Sāyaṇa states two kinds of meaning here. The first: yugopalakṣitān nimeṣādikālāvayavān prakarṣeṇa hiṃsantī. The word yuga indicates the span of men's lives. Uṣas, by the divisions called moment, day, month and the like, wears down all the period of human life — this is the sense. In this context the Maruts protect the sacrificer at all times; here also, and likewise in other places, the expression mānuṣā yugā ("the ages of men") is used.

īyuṣīṇām upamā; āyatīnāṃ prathamā — atītānāṃ nityānām uṣasāṃ (tābhiḥ) sadṛśī; āgāminīnām uṣasāṃ prathamabhāvinī: the meaning is that she has one and the same form for all the appearances of the Uṣases — those who have gone before and those who will come ever-lasting.

In this ṛk a kind of sadness is mixed with the joy. By describing the beauty and loveliness of Uṣas, who gives consciousness and light to the whole world and fills living beings with life, the delight is expressed; and along with that, before this Uṣas, who continues ever in the state of youth, a certain agitation of mind shows itself, in the thought that humans and all other beings grow old in a short time and die. In this idea the experience of truth and the vision of beauty are joined. The vision of the truth that Uṣas wears away all the life of men is generally expressed whenever Uṣas is described. For example —

ईयुष्टे ये पूर्वतरामपश्यन्व्युच्छन्तीमुषसं मर्त्यासः । अस्माभिरू नु प्रतिचक्ष्याभूदो ते यन्ति ये अपरीषु पश्यान् ॥

īyuṣṭe ye pūrvatarāmapaśyanvyucchantīmuṣasaṃ martyāsaḥ | asmābhirū nu praticakṣyābhūdo te yanti ye aparīṣu paśyān ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-11, as printed "೧-೧೧೩-೧೧".) — in many such places those who earlier saw this everlasting beauty of Uṣas and were delighted are all gone; and the same is the fate of those who come after; but Uṣas alone is ever young and eternal: with this thought the picture of man's brief life is reflected.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2, pp. 139–140; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). aminatī — root mīñ hiṃsāyām (Kryādi); śatṛ in the laṭ sense; kryādibhyaḥ śnā (Pā. 3-1-81) gives śnā; svādīnām hrasvaḥ [as printed; the OCR "Pā. 7-3-80"] shortens the root; since the suffix has the marker p [sic: ś], śnābhyastayor ātaḥ (Pā. 6-4-112) elides the ā of śnā; in the feminine ṅīp because it is ugit; the negative naña-tatpuruṣa compound; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… [OCR "Pā. 6-2-2"] gives the natural accent of the first member (an indeclinable).

daivyāni — devasya imāni daivyāni; in the sense of relationship, devād yajñau [print: "ದೇವಾದ್ಯಜ್ಞೌ", Pā. 4-1-85, as read by the OCR] gives the suffix yañ; yasyeti ca (Pā. 6-4-148) elides the a; since the suffix has the marker ñ, ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute; accusative plural. prāminatī — with the prefix pra; the process as before. śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173) gives the acute accent to the ṅīp… [as printed: śatur anumaḥ]; in the compound the accent of the final member. manuṣyā — manor jātāv ñyat tuk ca (Pā. 4-1-161) [as read] gives the suffix yat; with it the augment tuk; tit svaritam (Pā. 6-1-185) gives the suffix the svarita; when the genitive plural [sic, nominative plural] follows, supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39) gives ā for it.

īyuṣīṇām — root iṇ gatau; when liṭ has come, kvasuś ca (Pā. 3-2-107) gives kvasu; taking it as cause the root is doubled; when the feminine is intended, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp; since it has the bha designation, vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam (Pā. 6-4-131) gives saṃprasāraṇa with pūrvarūpa; since the suffix beginning with a vowel follows, iṇo yaṇ (Pā. 6-4-81) gives yaṇ to the i of the root; dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti (Pā. 7-4-69) lengthens the reduplicative syllable; śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (Pā. 8-3-60) gives ṣatva to the s of vasu; genitive plural. As the ṅīp and sup are unaccented the accent of vasu remains.

śaśvatīnām — ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp in the feminine; genitive plural. āyatīnām — prefix ā; root iṇ gatau; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; iṇo yaṇ (Pā. 6-4-81) gives yaṇ; ṅīp in the feminine; jyāc chandasi bahulam [as printed "ಜ್ಯಾತ್ಸಂದಸಿ ಬಹುಲಮ್" (Pā. 6-1-178)] gives the acute accent to the case-ending nām in the genitive plural.

adyaut — root dyut dīptau; luṅ, third person singular tip, with loss of the i; dyudbhyo luṅi (Pā. 1-3-91) gives parasmaipada; by vyatyaya the luk of siC; where guṇa would be expected, vṛddhi occurs in the Veda; or else from the root dyu abhigamane; in luṅ, ucyato vṛddhir luki hali [print: "ಉತೋ ವೃದ್ಧಿರ್ಲುಕಿ ಹಲಿ" (Pā. 7-3-89)] gives vṛddhi; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. ‖ 2 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

एषा दिवो दुहिता प्रत्यदर्शि ज्योतिर्वसाना समना पुरस्तात् । ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेति साधु प्रजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ॥ ३ ॥

eṣā divo duhitā pratyadarśi jyotirvasānā samanā purastāt | ṛtasya panthāmanveti sādhu prajānatīva na diśo mināti ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

एषा । दिवः । दुहिता । प्रति । अदर्शि । ज्योतिः । वसाना । समना । पुरस्तात् । ऋतस्य । पन्थाम् । अनु । एति । साधु । प्रजानतीऽइव । न । दिशः । मिनाति ॥ ३ ॥

eṣā | divaḥ | duhitā | prati | adarśi | jyotiḥ | vasānā | samanā | purastāt | ṛtasya | panthām | anu | eti | sādhu | prajānatī 'iva | na | diśaḥ | mināti ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

एषोषा दिवो द्योतमानात्मकस्य द्युलोकस्य दुहिता दुहितृस्थानीया । तत उत्पद्यमानत्वाद्दुहितेत्युपचर्यते । पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिशि प्रति प्रत्येकमदर्शि । दृश्यते । सर्वेषामपि प्राणिनामाभिमुख्येन प्रकाशत इत्यर्थः । कीदृशी सा । ज्योतिर्वसाना तेजोरूपं वस्त्रमाच्छादयन्ती तेजसा प्रकाशयन्ती समना सम्यगानयित्री चेष्टयित्री । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थोऽयम् । यद्वा । सह युगपदेव मन्यतेऽवबुध्यते प्राणिभिरिति समना । व्युत्पत्त्यन्तरावधारणादनवग्रहः । सा तादृशी ऋतस्यादित्यस्य पन्थां पन्थानं मेरोः प्रान्तप्रदेशमनुक्रमेण साधु सम्यगेति । गच्छति । सूर्यो यत्र यत्र गच्छति तत्र तत्र पुरस्तादुषा अपि गच्छतीत्यर्थः । सैव विशेष्यते । प्रजानतीव प्रियभूतस्य सूर्यस्य मार्गो मयापि गन्तव्य इति चेतयन्तीव । यथा लोके प्रियस्यानुरागायुक्ता काचिद्भर्तारं सर्वास्ववस्थासु न विमुञ्चति तथेयमपीत्यर्थः । किंच दिशः प्राच्यादिका न मिनाति । न हिनस्ति । किंतूषा यत्र गच्छति सा प्राचीत्येवं प्राच्यादिव्यवहारं करोतीत्यर्थः ॥

Read from the image; checked against the OCR, whose Devanagari is garbled in the second half. A few small words — "meroḥ prāntapradeśam", "anavagrahaḥ" — are given as read. "This Uṣas is the duhitā — in the position of a daughter — of divaḥ — the shining heaven; since she arises from it she is figuratively called 'daughter'. Purastāt — in the eastern quarter — she is pratyadarśi, 'seen each one by one'; that is, she shines before the face of all living beings. What is she like? Jyotir vasānā — clothing herself in a garment of radiance, making things shine with brightness; samanā — she who well leads, who makes [beings] active (the verb ana here has the causative sense included); or else samanā — she whom living beings know, apprehend together, simultaneously; this is a derivation for which no break (avagraha) is given. Such a one follows well (sādhu) the path (panthām) of ṛta, i.e. of the Āditya — the border regions of Meru — in order; wherever the Sun goes, there Uṣas also goes in front: that is the sense. She is further described: prajānatīva — as if reflecting 'the path of the beloved Sun must be gone along by me too'. As in the world a woman full of love does not leave her husband in any condition, so this one: that is the sense. And na dišo mināti — she does not injure the quarters, east and the others; but where Uṣas goes, that is 'east' — thus she gives rise to the usage 'east' and so on."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Eṣā — this; divaḥ — of the world of the atmosphere (heaven); duhitā — in the position of a daughter, the goddess Uṣas; jyotirvasānā — wearing a garment of light; samanā — [she who] makes beings well engaged in their various occupations (or [she who] shows herself to all beings at one time); purastāt — in the eastern quarter; prati adarśi — is seen one by one; (sā — she); ṛtasya — of the Āditya; panthām — the path (the way); prajānatī iva — like a woman who has understood that she must follow in all circumstances the way of her beloved; sādhu — well; eti — goes (follows); (kiṃca — and); diśaḥ — the quarters, east and others; na mināti — does not harm (does not destroy).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The goddess Uṣas, in the form of the daughter of heaven, wearing a garment of light, showing herself at one time (to all beings), rises in the eastern quarter; as a woman who knows that she must follow the path of her beloved, she follows well the path of Āditya; (when she thus follows) she does not obstruct the (affairs of living beings) of the quarters.

Printed English (as printed): She, the daughter of heaven, is beheld in the east, gracious and arrayed in light : she travels steadily along the path of the sun, as if cognizant (of his pleasure), and damages not the quarters (of the horizon).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.

In this ṛk it is described how Uṣas, the daughter of heaven, follows the path of ṛta and moves in a fixed course. One must consider what the "path of ṛta" is. Here the word ṛta is explained as "Āditya". Therefore scholars hold that "the path of ṛta" may be the zodiac (rāśicakra). [The following English is printed as such:]

"When, in the Rig-veda, the fixed Path of Rita unerringly followed by the Devas (originally the shining ones or the luminaries) is spoken of in the Rig-veda it should, in my opinion, naturally mean Zodiac or the imaginary belt or Zone in the heavens, within which the apparent motions of the Sun, moon and the Principal Planet or Devas are confined."

(A. B. O. R. I.) as printed, with the source abbreviation. That there is some truth in this explanation is helped by the description in the ṛk which is cited below.

original p. 143

द्वादशारं नहि तज्जराय वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य । आ पुत्रा अग्ने मिथुनासो अत्र सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च तस्थुः ॥

dvādaśāraṃ nahi tajjarāya varvarti cakraṃ pari dyāmṛtasya | ā putrā agne mithunāso atra sapta śatāni viṃśatiśca tasthuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-11, as printed "೧-೧೬೪-೧೧".) The wheel of ṛta has twelve spokes; that wheel revolves around the sky; and on this wheel's path seven hundred and twenty sons stand in pairs — this is the purport of this ṛk. Probably in this description the twelve months and the three hundred and sixty days and nights are indicated.

वेद मासो धृतव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावतः । वेदा य उपजायते ॥

veda māso dhṛtavrato dvādaśa prajāvataḥ | vedā ya upajāyate ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-8, as read from the print "೧-೨೫-೮".) — as is said in this ṛk, it may also be said that the 360 days and nights are the offspring of these twelve months.

The ṛks cited below, which describe the goddess Uṣas and her path of movement, make us acquainted with the path of ṛta.

ता आ चरन्ति समना पुरस्तात्समानतः समना पप्रथानाः । ऋतस्य देवीः सदसो बुधाना गवां न सर्गा उषसो जरन्ते ॥

tā ā caranti samanā purastātsamānataḥ samanā paprathānāḥ | ṛtasya devīḥ sadaso budhānā gavāṃ na sargā uṣaso jarante ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-51-9, as read from the print "೪-೫೧-೯".) From a certain regulated place of this ṛta, the goddess Uṣas, like other luminous bodies, begins her movement visible to us. If she follows this path of ṛta without leaving it even a little, then her straight path does not fail.

जानत्यह्नः प्रथमस्य नाम शुक्रा कृष्णादजनिष्ट श्वितीची । ऋतस्य योषा न मिनाति धामाहरहर्निष्कृतमाचरन्ती ॥

jānatyahnaḥ prathamasya nāma śukrā kṛṣṇādajaniṣṭa śvitīcī | ṛtasya yoṣā na mināti dhāmāharaharniṣkṛtamācarantī ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-9.)

एषा स्या वेनी [?] भवति द्विबर्हा आविष्कृण्वाना तन्वं पुरस्तात् । ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेति साधु प्रजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ॥

eṣā syā venī [?] bhavati dvibarhā āviṣkṛṇvānā tanvaṃ purastāt | ṛtasya panthāmanveti sādhu prajānatīva na diśo mināti ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-80-4 [?], as read from the print; the word "vainī"/"venī" is doubtful in my reading.) — the daughter of heaven, wearing a garment in the form of splendour, follows the path of ṛta in a straight line: thus it is described in many contexts. But what is this path of ṛta?

अग्निं विश ईळते मानुषीर्या अग्निं मनुषो नहुषो वि जाताः । अग्निर्गान्धर्वीं पथ्यामृतस्याग्नेर्गव्यूतिर्घृत आ निषत्ता ॥

agniṃ viśa īḷate mānuṣīryā agniṃ manuṣo nahuṣo vi jātāḥ | agnirgāndharvīṃ pathyāmṛtasyāgnergavyūtirghṛta ā niṣattā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-6, as read from the print.)

original p. 144

Since the path of this ṛta is the path on which the Gandharvas move, it must be in a very high place in the atmosphere. This is the path of the Āditya, and —

उदु त्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरा एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धम् । ऋतस्य शुचि दर्शतमनीकं रुक्मो न दिव उदिता व्यद्यौत् ॥

udu tyaccakṣurmahi mitrayorā eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdham | ṛtasya śuci darśatamanīkaṃ rukmo na diva uditā vyadyaut ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-51-1, as printed.)

इदमु त्यन्महि महामनीकं यदुस्रिया सचत पूर्व्यं गौः । ऋतस्य पदे अधि दीद्यानं गुहा रघुष्यद्रघुयद्विवेद ॥

idamu tyanmahi mahāmanīkaṃ yadusriyā sacata pūrvyaṃ gauḥ | ṛtasya pade adhi dīdyānaṃ guhā raghuṣyadraghuyadviveda ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-5-5 [?], as read; the print's middle numeral is doubtful.) Read letter by letter; the last two pāda words are doubtful. — in these ṛks the rising of the Āditya, who is of the nature of ṛta, and his charming form are described —

कविर्नृचक्षा अभि षीमचष्ट ऋतस्य योना विघृते मदन्ती । नाना चक्राते सदनं यथा वेः समानेन क्रतुना संविदाने ॥

kavirnṛcakṣā abhi ṣīmacaṣṭa ṛtasya yonā vighṛte madantī | nānā cakrāte sadanaṃ yathā veḥ samānena kratunā saṃvidāne ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-6 [?], as read from the print.) — in this ṛk it is described that the Sun, rejoicing in the womb (yoni) of ṛta, is watching heaven and earth. In the same way, in many other ṛks the summit and the root of ṛta are described —

ऋतस्य बुध्न उषसामिषण्यन्वृषा मही रोदसी आ विवेश । मही मित्रस्य वरुणस्य माया चन्द्रेव भानुं वि दधे पुरुत्रा ॥

ṛtasya budhna uṣasāmiṣaṇyanvṛṣā mahī rodasī ā viveśa | mahī mitrasya varuṇasya māyā candreva bhānuṃ vi dadhe purutrā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-7 [?], as read from the print.) — here the root-region of ṛta, the light of heaven and earth in that region, and the entrance of the Āditya between them, are stated. In many such contexts the Western scholars have not explained the word ṛta in a physical sense but everywhere only in a moral sense. But in the present ṛk (1-124-3) all this description is included, and a path of a physical orb of light which Uṣas follows is indicated.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3, pp. 144–145; noted briefly, sūtra numbers as read by the OCR). divaḥ — genitive singular; ūḍidaṃpadādyappumrainyuvidbhyaḥ (Pā. 6-1-171) gives the acute accent to the case-ending. adarśi — root dṛśir prekṣaṇe; in the Veda, in the present sense, in the passive, luṅ; third person singular, the ending ta; ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ (Pā. 3-1-66) gives ciṇ for ci; ciṇo luk (Pā. 6-4-104) elides the ta; with ciṇ as cause there is guṇa of the ṛ of the root; the augment aṭ to the stem; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent.

original p. 145

vasānā — root vasa ācchādane; śānac in the laṭ sense; by vyatyaya the luk of śap does not occur; since the sārvadhātuka follows the upadeśa, tāsyanudāttet (Pā. 6-1-186) makes it unaccented and the root-accent remains. samanā — prefix sam, root ana prāṇane; as it shows a causative sense the root is of included-causative sense; ac in the agent sense; ṭāp in the feminine; citaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the final-acute. Or else from the root man avabodhane: saha yugapad eva manyate avabudhyate prāṇibhir iti samanā; since this derivation was not considered, no avagraha is shown in the pada text. purastāt — the word pūrva; pūrvādharāvarāṇāṃ purdhavaś caiṣām (Pā. 5-3-39) gives the suffix astāti and the substitution pur for the base; the suffix is acute on its first syllable. panthām — the word pathin; with the accusative singular following, vyatyayo bahulam and pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt (Pā. 7-1-85) give ā; tho nthaḥ changes th to nth; because the word pathin is formed with a suffix [Uṇ. 4-?, as printed "೪-೪೫೨" — doubtful [?]] it would be final-acute, but pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne (Pā. 6-1-199) gives it the first-syllable acute. eti — root iṇ gatau; Adādi; laṭ third person singular; since it follows a non-verb word the nighāta accent. prajānatī — root jñā avabodhane; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; kryādibhyaḥ śnā (Pā. 3-1-81); jñājanor jā (Pā. 7-3-79) gives the substitute jā; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ (Pā. 6-4-112) elides the ā of the verb-suffix; ugitaś ca gives ṅīp in the feminine; śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173) gives the acute on the ṅīp, since it follows a śatṛ without num; in the compound the accent of the final member. mināti — root mīñ hiṃsāyām (Kryādi); laṭ third person singular tip; śnā; svādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ (as printed; the OCR "Pā. 7-3-80") shortens the root; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. ‖ 3 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उपो अदर्शि शुन्ध्युवो न वक्षो नोधा इवाविरकृत प्रियाणि । अद्मसन्न ससतो बोधयन्ती शश्वत्तमागात्पुनरेयुषीणाम् ॥ ४ ॥

upo adarśi śundhyuvo na vakṣo nodhā ivāvirakṛta priyāṇi | admasanna sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamāgātpunareyuṣīṇām ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ This is the ṛk that was cited by number on p. 115 above, there given as "1-124-4 [?]": the number is thereby confirmed.

उपो इति । अदर्शि । शुन्ध्युवः । न । वक्षः । नोधाःऽइव । आविः । अकृत । प्रियाणि । अद्मसत् । न । ससतः । बोधयन्ती । शश्वत्ऽतमा । आ । अगात् । पुनः । आऽईयुषीणाम् ॥ ४ ॥

upo iti | adarśi | śundhyuvaḥ | na | vakṣaḥ | nodhāḥ 'iva | āviḥ | akṛta | priyāṇi | admasat | na | sasataḥ | bodhayantī | śaśvat 'tamā | ā | agāt | punaḥ | ā 'īyuṣīṇām ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

एषोषाः । उपो इति निपातद्वयसमुदायात्मक एको निपातः । सर्वैः समीप एवादर्शि । दृश्यते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । शुन्ध्युवो न वक्षः । अत्र नकार उपमार्थीय उपरिष्टादुपयुज्यमानत्वात् । यत्र तु प्रतिषेधो विवक्षितस्तत्र पुरस्तान्नकारः प्रयुज्यते । तथा च यास्कः । पुरस्तादुपाचारस्य यत्प्रतिषेधतीति । तस्योदाहरणं नेन्द्रं देवममंसतेति । उपरिष्टादपाचारस्य येनोपमिमीते इति । तस्योदाहरणं दुर्मदासो न सुरायामिति । नि. १-४ । ऋ. १०-८६-१ । ऋ. ८-२-१२ । शुन्ध्युरादित्यः सर्वेषां शोधकत्वात् । तस्य च वक्षःस्थानीयो रश्मिसमूहः । स यथा प्रकाशमानो दृश्यते तद्वदित्यर्थः । यद्वा शुन्ध्युरिति जलचरः श्वेतवर्णः पक्षिविशेषः । स यथा स्वकीयं वक्षः प्रकाशयन्दृश्यते तद्वदित्यर्थः । किंच नोधा इव प्रियाण्याविरकृत । नवनं स्तोत्रं धारयतीति नोधाः । एतन्नामा महर्षिर्देवताः स्तुतिव्याजेन नानाविधैर्मन्त्रैः प्रियाणि स्वमनीषितान्याविष्कृतवान् । तद्वदेषापि स्वकीयानि सर्वलोकस्य प्रियाणि तेजांस्याविरकरोत् । किंचाद्मसन्न । अत्राप्युपमार्थीयो नकारः । अद्यते इत्यद्मानम् । तस्य पाकाय गृहे सीदतीत्यद्मसत् । पाचिका योषित् ससतो बोधयन्ती । सा यथा स्वपतः पुत्रादीन्भोजनाय …

eṣoṣāḥ | upo iti nipātadvayasamudāyātmaka eko nipātaḥ | sarvaiḥ samīpa evādarśi | dṛśyate | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | śundhyuvo na vakṣaḥ | atra nakāra upamārthīya upariṣṭādupayujyamānatvāt | yatra tu pratiṣedho vivakṣitastatra purastānnakāraḥ prayujyate | tathā ca yāskaḥ | purastādupācārasya yatpratiṣedhatīti | tasyodāharaṇaṃ nendraṃ devamamaṃsateti | upariṣṭādapācārasya yenopamimīte iti | tasyodāharaṇaṃ durmadāso na surāyāmiti | ni. 1-4 | ṛ. 10-86-1 | ṛ. 8-2-12 | śundhyurādityaḥ sarveṣāṃ śodhakatvāt | tasya ca vakṣaḥsthānīyo raśmisamūhaḥ | sa yathā prakāśamāno dṛśyate tadvadityarthaḥ | yadvā śundhyuriti jalacaraḥ śvetavarṇaḥ pakṣiviśeṣaḥ | sa yathā svakīyaṃ vakṣaḥ prakāśayandṛśyate tadvadityarthaḥ | kiṃca nodhā iva priyāṇyāvirakṛta | navanaṃ stotraṃ dhārayatīti nodhāḥ | etannāmā maharṣirdevatāḥ stutivyājena nānāvidhairmantraiḥ priyāṇi svamanīṣitānyāviṣkṛtavān | tadvadeṣāpi svakīyāni sarvalokasya priyāṇi tejāṃsyāvirakarot | kiṃcādmasanna | atrāpyupamārthīyo nakāraḥ | adyate ityadmānam | tasya pākāya gṛhe sīdatītyadmasat | pācikā yoṣit sasato bodhayantī | sā yathā svapataḥ putrādīnbhojanāya …

Read from the image; checked against the OCR. The Ṛg references after Ni. 1-4 — "10-86-1" and "8-2-12" — follow the OCR where the print is small; "10-86-1" is doubtful [?]. The passage continues on p. 147. "Upo — one particle made up of the two particles upa and u: she is seen quite near, by all. A comparison there: śundhyuvo na vakṣaḥ. Here the na has the sense of comparison, since it is used after [the word compared]. Where a negation is intended, the na is used before: and so Yāska says: 'purastād upacārasya yat pratiṣedhati' ('when it negates what is said before'), the example of which is nendraṃ devam amaṃsata; and 'upariṣṭād apacārasya yenopamimīte' ('when it is used after, for what it compares'), the example of which is durmadāso na surāyām" (Ni. 1-4; Ṛ. 10-86-1 [?]; Ṛ. 8-2-12). "Śundhyu is Āditya, since he purifies all; his bosom is the mass of rays. As it appears shining, so she: that is the sense. Or else śundhyu is a water-bird, a kind of white bird; as it is seen displaying its own breast, so she. Moreover, nodhā iva priyāṇy āvir akṛta — navanaṃ stotraṃ dhārayatīti nodhāḥ: the great seer of this name, with various mantras in the guise of praise of the deities, made manifest his own desired, dear things; just so this Uṣas made manifest her own radiances, dear to the whole world. And admasan na — here too the na is of the sense of comparison. Admānam is 'what is eaten'; she who sits in the house for its cooking is admasat; the woman who cooks, awakening those who sleep; as she, for the meals of her sleeping husband, sons and others, …"

…bhojanāya bodhayati tadvat | yadvā | admeti gṛhanāma varūthamadmeti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra sīdatītyadmasajjananī | sā yathā svapataḥ putrādīnuṣaḥkāle prabodhayati tathā bhuvanākhye gṛhe sīdanti tatratyānprāṇinaḥ prabodhayatīyamuṣāḥ | īyuṣīṇāmāgamanaśīlānāṃ strīṇāṃ madhye śaśvattamā punaḥpunarāgacchati | prātarniyatamāgacchantīnāṃ vārayoṣitāṃ madhye svayamekā satī niyatamāgacchatītyabhiprāyaḥ | atra niruktam | upādarśi śundhyuvaḥ śundhyurādityo bhavati śodhanāttasyaiva vakṣo bhāso 'dhyūḍhamidamapītaradvakṣa etasmādevādhyūḍhaṃ kāyai [?] | śakunirapi śundhyurucyate śodhanādevodakacaro bhavati | āpo 'pi śundhyava ucyante śodhanādeva | nodhā ṛṣirbhavati navanaṃ dadhāti | sa yathā stutyā kāmānāviṣkuruta evamuṣā rūpāṇyāviṣkurute | admasadadmānaṃ bhavatyasādinīti vānnasāninīti vā | sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamāgātpunareyuṣīṇāṃ svapato bodhayantī śāśvatikatamāgātpunarāgāminīnām | ni. 4-16 | iti ‖

Read from the image and checked against the OCR; the words "kāyai [?]" and "adhyūḍham" in the Nirukta passage are doubtful in the print. "…[so she] awakens for meals: likewise [the Uṣas]. Or else admā is a name for 'house' (it is read among the names varūtham, admā); one who sits there is admasat, the housewife. As she wakes her sleeping husband, sons and others at the time of dawn, so this Uṣas wakes the beings who dwell in the house called the world. Among the women, īyuṣīṇām — who go [early] — she, śaśvattamā, comes again and again; among the courtesans who regularly come in the morning, she alone is regular: that is the intention. Here the Nirukta: 'upādarśi śundhyuvaḥ: śundhyu is Āditya, because of purifying; his bosom is bhāsā — what is raised by light … Also the bird śakuni is called śundhyu, because it purifies, it being a water-dweller; also the waters are called śundhyavaḥ because of purifying. Nodhā is a seer; he holds newness. As he, by praise, makes manifest his desires, so does Uṣas make forms manifest. Admasat — one who sits at food: admānaṃ bhavati, 'asādinī', or annasāninī. Sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamā āgāt punar eyuṣīṇām — waking the sleeping, the most continual, she has come again of those who are to come back.' (Ni. 4-16)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Eṣā — this goddess Uṣas; śundhyuvaḥ — of the purifying Sun (or of the water-dwelling white bird); vakṣaḥ na — like the rays which are in the position of a bosom (as when one shows the bosom); upo — near; adarśi — is seen (by all); nodhāḥ iva — as the seer called Nodhas (in the guise of praise manifested all the things dear to him); priyāṇi — the dear special forms (of radiant form); āviḥ akṛta — made manifest; admasat — the woman who cooks food and the like; sasataḥ bodhayantī na — like [her] waking the sleeping children for food (waking the sleeping beings, the goddess Uṣas); ā īyuṣīṇām — among the women who rise and come at dawn; śaśvattamā — the most unfailing (regularly); punaḥ ā agāt — comes again and again.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The goddess Uṣas is seen, like the rays of the Sun, quite nearby (by all); like the seer Nodhas she takes on many forms dear to people; like a mother who, having cooked food and the like in the house, wakes her children, she wakes the sleeping beings; she rises again and again more regularly than all the women who rise early (by habit).

Printed English (as printed): She is beheld nigh at hand, (radiant) as the breast of the illuminator (the sun); and, like Nodhas, has made manifest many pleasing

original p. 148

(objects) : like a matron she awakens (her) sleeping (children), and of all (females who are) stirring betimes, she, the most unvarying, repeatedly appears.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 4.

For this ṛk the author of the Nirukta has made the following explanation (as above):

उपादर्शि शुन्ध्युवः शुन्ध्युरादित्यो भवति शोधनात्तस्यैव वक्षो भासाध्यूढमिदमपीतरद्वक्ष एतस्मादेवाध्यूढं कायै [?] । शकुनिरपि शुन्ध्युरुच्यते शोधनादेवोदकचरो भवत्यापोऽपि शुन्ध्यव उच्यन्ते शोधनादेव । नोधा ऋषिर्भवति नवनं दधाति स यथा स्तुत्या कामानाविष्कुरुत एवमुषा रूपाण्याविष्कुरुते सदनं भवत्यसादिनीति वान्नसानिनीति वा । ससतो बोधयन्ती शश्वत्तमागात्पुनरेयुषीणां । स्वपतो बोधयन्ती शाश्वतिकतमागात्पुनरागामिनीनाम् ।

upādarśi śundhyuvaḥ śundhyurādityo bhavati śodhanāttasyaiva vakṣo bhāsādhyūḍhamidamapītaradvakṣa etasmādevādhyūḍhaṃ kāyai [?] | śakunirapi śundhyurucyate śodhanādevodakacaro bhavatyāpo 'pi śundhyava ucyante śodhanādeva | nodhā ṛṣirbhavati navanaṃ dadhāti sa yathā stutyā kāmānāviṣkuruta evamuṣā rūpāṇyāviṣkurute sadanaṃ bhavatyasādinīti vānnasāninīti vā | sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamāgātpunareyuṣīṇāṃ | svapato bodhayantī śāśvatikatamāgātpunarāgāminīnām |

(Ni. 4-16, as printed "೪-೧೬".) Read letter by letter from the image; the pieces marked [?] are not clear in the print. And, explaining thus, he states the meanings of the word śundhyu: śundhyur ādityo bhavati śodhanāt — "the Āditya has this name because of purifying" — the first meaning; śakunir api śundhyur ucyate śodhanād evodakacaro bhavati — the bird that moves in water is also called by this name because it purifies by removing the dirt there; āpo 'pi śundhyava ucyante śodhanād eva — the water too is called by this name because it purifies: thus the various meanings of the word are shown; in all contexts the root is of one and the same sense. In the Ṛk Saṃhitā —

प्र शुन्ध्युवं वरुणाय प्रेष्ठां मतिं वसिष्ठ मीळ्हुषे भरस्व । य ईमर्वाञ्चं करते यजत्रं सहस्रामघं वृषणं बृहन्तम् ॥

pra śundhyuvaṃ varuṇāya preṣṭhāṃ matiṃ vasiṣṭha mīḷhuṣe bharasva | ya īmarvāñcaṃ karate yajatraṃ sahasrāmaghaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ bṛhantam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-88-1 [?], as read from the print.) — in this ṛk śundhyu is an epithet of the praise, "that which purifies, or that which is pure of itself", "to be made pure, or to be pure by itself".

युवं रथेन विमदाय शुन्ध्युवं न्यूहथुः पुरुमित्रस्य योषणाम् । युवं ह वं वध्रिमत्या अगच्छतं युवं सुषुतिं चक्रथुः पुरंधये ॥

yuvaṃ rathena vimadāya śundhyuvaṃ nyūhathuḥ purumitrasya yoṣaṇām | yuvaṃ ha vaṃ vadhrimatyā agacchataṃ yuvaṃ suṣutiṃ cakrathuḥ puraṃdhaye ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-20, as read from the print.) — in this ṛk śundhyu means "a pure woman". In the present ṛk the appearance of Uṣas is described; it is compared to the bosom-like mass of rays of the purifier, the Sun, or to the breast of the white water-bird.

original p. 149

nodhā iva — for this word the author of the Nirukta says: nodhā ṛṣir bhavati | navanaṃ dadhāti | sa yathā stutyā kāmān āviṣkurute. As the seer called Nodhas makes visible, by his new praises that take the form of poetry, the wishes lying in his heart, so Uṣas too manifests her sleeping brilliance — thus it is compared.

Nodhas (Gautama) is well known as the seer of the seven sūktas in the first maṇḍala of the Ṛk-saṃhitā from the 58th to the 64th [numerals as read; the OCR gives "12 to 64"], and of the 88th sūkta of the eighth maṇḍala and the 93rd of the ninth. His story is told in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā itself —

तं त्वा वयं पतिमग्ने रयीणां प्र शंसामो मतिभिर्गोतमासः । आशुं न वाजंभरं मर्जयन्तः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥

taṃ tvā vayaṃ patimagne rayīṇāṃ pra śaṃsāmo matibhirgotamāsaḥ | āśuṃ na vājaṃbharaṃ marjayantaḥ prātarmakṣū dhiyāvasurjagamyāt ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-60-5, as read from the print.)

— in such ṛks, [they are] said to be "sons of Gotama" praising Agni, the lord of wealth.

एना ते हार्योजना सुवृक्ती इन्द्र ब्रह्माणि गोतमासो अक्रन् । ऐषु विश्वपेशसं धियं धाः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥

enā te hāryojanā suvṛktī indra brahmāṇi gotamāso akran | aiṣu viśvapeśasaṃ dhiyaṃ dhāḥ prātarmakṣū dhiyāvasurjagamyāt ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-16 [?], as read from the print.) — here it is said that the Gautama sons composed praises addressed to Indra. In the present ṛk it is described that the appearance of Uṣas was shining like the wishes revealed by praises composed by Nodhas Gautama.

admasat — admasad admānaṃ bhavaty asādinīti vā annasāninīti vā (Ni. 4-16, as printed): The word admā has the name "food"; it is admasat either because she sits before the food in order to eat it, or because she possesses food: thus the author of the Nirukta states the explanation of this word. Sāyaṇa:

अद्मसन्न । अत्राप्युपमार्थीयो नकारः । अद्यत इत्यद्मान्नम् । तस्य पाकाय गृहे सीदतीत्यद्मसत् । पाचिका योषित् । यद्वा अद्मेति गृहनाम । वरूथमद्मेति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र सीदतीत्यद्मसज्जननी ॥

admasanna | atrāpyupamārthīyo nakāraḥ | adyata ityadmānnam | tasya pākāya gṛhe sīdatītyadmasat | pācikā yoṣit | yadvā admeti gṛhanāma | varūthamadmeti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra sīdatītyadmasajjananī ‖

Read from the image. "Admasan na — here too the na has the sense of comparison. What is eaten is admā, 'food'; she who sits in the house for its cooking is admasat, the woman who cooks. Or else admā is a name for 'house' — since varūtham, admā are read among its names; one who sits there is admasat, the housewife (jananī)." — Because food is to be eaten, admā means food; admasat means a woman who stays in the house in order to cook it; or, since the word admā is recorded among the names of the house, she who stays in the house, the mother (jananī): he states the meaning of this word in two ways. As the na is of the sense of comparison,

सा जननी यथा स्वपतः पुत्रादीनुषःकाले प्रबोधयति तथा भुवनाख्ये गृहे सीदन्ति तत्रत्यान्प्राणिनः प्रबोधयतीयमुषाः ।

sā jananī yathā svapataḥ putrādīnuṣaḥkāle prabodhayati tathā bhuvanākhye gṛhe sīdanti tatratyānprāṇinaḥ prabodhayatīyamuṣāḥ |

— as the mother wakes her children at the time of dawn, so Uṣas, the mother of the world, wakes all the beings in the world: that is the sense.

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-9-? [?], as read — the print's last numeral is not clear.) — in this ṛk Uṣas is entreated to wake the Aśvins, as the hotṛ of the sacrifice wakes the Aśvin deities.

वद्मा हि सूनो अस्यद्मसद्वा चक्रे अग्निर्जनुषाज्मान्नम् । स त्वं न ऊर्जसन ऊर्जं धा राजेव जेरवृके क्षेष्यन्तः ॥

vadmā hi sūno asyadmasadvā cakre agnirjanuṣājmānnam | sa tvaṃ na ūrjasana ūrjaṃ dhā rājeva jeravṛke kṣeṣyantaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-4-4 [?], as read.) — in this too, and likewise in the ṛks 8-44-29 [?] and 8-43-19 [?] and others, it may be said that the word means hotṛ.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, Ṛk 4; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). śundhyuvaḥ — root śundha śuddhau; yaji-mani-śundhi-dasi-janibhyo yuc [print: "ಯಜಿಮನಿಶುಂಧಿದಸಿಜನಿಭ್ಯೋ ಯುಚ್"] (Uṇ. 3-300 as read) gives the suffix yu; with the genitive singular following, tanvādīnāṃ chandasi bahulam upasaṃkhyānam (Pā. 6-4-77, vārttika) gives uvaṅ; the accent of the suffix. nodhāḥ — navanaṃ dadhāti iti nodhāḥ; "nodhā ṛṣir bhavati navanaṃ dadhāti" (Ni. 4-16) says Yāska; root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; with navana as the upapada, the suffix asun, and no for the upapada; the accent of the final member. akṛta — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; luṅ, third person singular, the ending ta; mantre ghasa-hvara-… (Pā. 2-4-80, as read) gives luk to the cli; since the suffix has the marker ṅit, no guṇa; the augment aṭ; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent.

admasat — adyate iti admā, annam; tadarthaṃ sīdatīti admasat; sadiṣu [sic; sadiṣvañjaḥ?] (Pā. 3-2-61 as read) gives kvip to the root ṣad when a subanta stands as upapada; ṣatva… of the initial of the root; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the final member. sasataḥ — root ṣasa svapne; Adādi; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; ṣatva of the initial; accusative plural; since the case-ending follows a śatṛ without num, śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173) gives it the acute accent. bodhayantī — root budha avagamane; in the causative sense, hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26) gives ṇic; with it as cause the guṇa of the root's short penultimate vowel; after ṇijanta, śatṛ in the laṭ sense; śap; guṇa of ṇic and the ay substitute; in the feminine num by ugit; the ṇic-accent remains. śaśvattamā — suffix tamap in the sense of excess; since upottamaṃ śaśvattamau sarvatra (Pā. 6-1-160 as read) is read in the ūḍādi group, tamap though pit is final-acute. agāt — root iṇ gatau; Adādi; luṅ, third person singular tip; itaś ca elides the i; e g(ā) luṅi (Pā. 2-4-45) gives gā; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 2-4-77) elides the siC; the augment aṭ; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. ‖ 4 ‖
