॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अप्त्यस्य व्यापनशीलस्य विस्तृतस्य रजसो रञ्जकस्यान्तरिक्षलोकस्य । रजश्शब्दोऽन्तरिक्षलोकवाची लोका रजांस्युच्यन्त इति यास्कोक्तत्वात् । नि. ४-१९ । तस्य पूर्वेऽर्धे पूर्वस्मिन्भागे जनित्र्युत्पन्ना सती गवां दिशां रश्मीनां वा केतुं प्रज्ञानं प्राकृत । प्रकर्षेण करोति । यद्वा । रजसो रञ्जकस्याह्नः । रजश्शब्दोऽहर्वाची । अस्मिन्नहनि रजसी उच्येते इति यास्कोक्तत्वात् । नि. ४-१९ । तस्य पूर्वेऽर्धे पूर्वस्मिन्भागे उषःकाले गवां वाचां जनित्री जनयित्र्युत्पादयित्री । उषःकाले सर्वेषां प्राणिनां वाचः स्फुरन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । यद्वा । अप्त्यस्य कर्मसु स्थितस्य जन्तोः केतुं गमनागमनादिरूपं कर्म । केतुरिति कर्मनाम केतः केतुरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । प्राकृत । प्रकर्षेण करोति । किंच पित्रोः पालयित्र्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योरुपस्थे उत्सङ्गेऽन्तरालप्रदेशे स्थिता सती उभा उभे द्यावापृथिव्यौ पृणन्ती स्वतेजसा पूरयन्ती । यद्वा । उभोभयोः पित्रोरिति संबन्धः । वितरं विशिष्टतरं वरीय उरुतरमतिविस्तीर्णं यथा भवति तथा वि प्रथते । विशेषेणैव प्रख्याता भवति । प्रकाशत इत्यर्थः । उशब्दोऽवधारणार्थः पादपूरणो वा मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्धितीति यास्कोक्तत्वात् ॥

"Of aptya — the pervading, the extended — rajas, the colouring [world], the world of the atmosphere (the word rajas denotes the world of the atmosphere, since Yāska says 'lokā rajāṃsy ucyante', Ni. 4-19); in its eastern half (pūrve ardhe), in the front part, being born (janitrī), she makes (prākṛta, 'makes excellently') a ketu, a knowledge (perception), of the gavām — of the quarters or of the rays. Or else of the rajas, the day which colours (the word rajas denotes the day, since Yāska says 'in this day the two worlds (rajasī) are spoken of', Ni. 4-19); in its eastern half, in the former part, at the time of Uṣas, she is the janitrī — the begetter, the producer — of gavām — voices (speeches); for it is well known that at the time of Uṣas the speech of all living beings comes to life. Or else, of the creature engaged in works (aptya), she makes the ketu — activity in the form of going and coming and so on (ketu is a name for 'action', since ketaḥ, ketuḥ are read among its names). Moreover, standing in the lap, the intermediate region, of pitroḥ — the two protecting parents, heaven and earth — ubhā — filling both heaven and earth with her own brilliance; or the construction is ubhayoḥ pitroḥ; she spreads out (vi prathate) more widely (vitaram), variyaḥ — most extensively, in the widest degree; she becomes known specially; that is, she shines. The word u is for emphasis, or a pāda-filler, as Yāska says 'among the measured syllables, kam, īm, id, u are meaningless' (Ni. 1-9)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Aptyasya — of the pervading; rajasaḥ — of the world of the atmosphere; pūrve ardhe — in the front part, at the time of Uṣas; janitrī — being born; gavām — of the quarters (the rays); ketum — the knowledge; pra akṛta — [Uṣas] makes abundantly (or): aptyasya — of the creature engaged in works; rajasaḥ — of the day; pūrve ardhe — in the first half; gavām — of voices; janitrī — as the mother; ketum — the knowledge of actions (going and coming and so on); pra akṛta — (the goddess Uṣas) makes well; (kiṃca — and); pitroḥ — of the two protecting parents, earth and sky; upasthā — in the lap region (being); ubhā — heaven and earth both; ā pṛṇantī — filling with her radiance; vitaram — more; variyaḥ — widely; vi prathate — becomes well known (shines).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Uṣas, being born in the front part of the pervading atmosphere (in the front part of the day), makes known the quarters (by her light). (Being born in the front part of the day, she gives the creature engaged in works the knowledge of its works, going and coming and so on;) and, shining between earth and sky — lighting up the two regions — she becomes still more widely known (shines). The printed English translation of this ṛk begins at the foot of this page: "Born in the eastern" — see p. 153 below.

original p. 153

Printed English (Ṛk 5, as printed): Born in the eastern quarter of the spacious firmament, she displays a banner of rays of light. Placed on the lap of both parents (heaven and earth), filling them (with radiance), she enjoys vast and wide-spread renown.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 5.

For the first half of this ṛk two kinds of meaning are stated. First: aptyasya rajasaḥ pūrve ardhe janitrī gavāṃ ketuṃ pra akṛta — in the front part (the first part) of the atmosphere, which is widely pervading, Uṣas is born and produces the knowledge of the ten quarters; second: aptyasya — for the creature engaged in works — rajasaḥ — of the day — pūrve ardhe — in the first half — gavām — of voices — janitrī — as the mother — ketum — the knowledge of actions — pra akṛta — she produces well. Therefore for the words aptyasya and the others both meanings must be given.

aptyasya — vyāpanaśīlasya vistṛtasya — "very widely spread out": as an epithet of the atmosphere; or else, since the word apas is recorded among the names of karman, aptyasya means karmasu sthitasya jantoḥ — "of the creature engaged in the doing of work".

rajasaḥ — rajaśabdo 'ntarikṣalokavācī | lokā rajāṃsy ucyanta iti yāskoktatvāt (Ni. 4-19, as printed "೪-೧೯") tasya pūrve 'rdhe. According to Yāska's opinion the word rajas means "atmosphere"; Sāyaṇa, giving this as the first meaning of the word, says "in the front part of such an atmosphere"; and second, rajasaḥ rañjakasyāhnaḥ | rajaśabdo 'havācī | asyāhanī rajasī iti yāskoktatvāt (4-19) tasya pūrve 'rdhe — since it is of the nature of colouring (rañjana), the day is named rajas; quoting Yāska's own sentence he has explained "of such rajas, i.e. of the day, in the first part". Thus the meanings are not only "atmosphere" and "day"; in some ṛks the word rajas is even explained as "water" —

क्व स्विदस्य रजसो महस्परं क्वावरं मरुतो यस्मिन्नायय । यच्च्यावयथ विथुरेव संहितं व्यद्रिणा पतथ त्वेषमर्णवम् ॥

kva svidasya rajaso mahasparaṃ kvāvaraṃ maruto yasminnāyaya | yaccyāvayatha vithureva saṃhitaṃ vyadriṇā patatha tveṣamarṇavam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-6, as read from the print; vy adriṇā as printed.)

gavām — diśāṃ raśmīnāṃ vā: of the quarters, or of the rays — one meaning; or gavāṃ vācāṃ janitrī — "the mother of voices" — another meaning is stated. The word go is recorded in the Nirukta among words of many meanings. This is explained elsewhere.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). janitrī — root janī prādurbhāve; the suffix tṛc [the print: tṛn] in the agent sense; ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ gives the augment iṭ; when the feminine is intended, ṛnnebhyo ṅīp gives ṅīp; yaṇ substitution; ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute. akṛta — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6) gives luṅ in the present sense; as explained in the previous mantra, luk of cli; nighāta accent. prathate — root prathaḥ prakhyāne; laṭ third person singular; the nighāta accent. vitaram — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; pacādi aṭ [ac]; guṇa with raparatva; final-acute by the suffix; in the compound the accent of the final member's own nature. variyaḥ — atiśayena uru variyaḥ; the suffix īyasun in the sense of excess; with it following, priyasthirasphirorubahulagavyaprthucchandārasāṃ… [print: priyasthira-…-ror…] (Pā. 6-4-157) gives var in place of uru; since the suffix is nit [as printed], ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute. ubhā — supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39) gives ā to the case-ending (nominative dual, or genitive dual); likewise ā for the locative in upasthā. pṛṇantī — root pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ; Kryādi; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; kryādibhyaḥ śnā; since it belongs to the prādi group, svādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ shortens the root (Pā. 7-3-80); śnābhyastayor ātaḥ (Pā. 6-4-112) elides the ā of śnā; ugitaś ca gives ṅīp and num in the feminine; since a ṛ-vowel precedes, the n of the suffix becomes ṇ; the first-syllable acute of the śatṛ suffix. ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

एषोषा एवेत् । इच्छब्द एवकारार्थः । एवमेवेदानींभासमानप्रकारेणैव पुरुतमा विपुलतमात्यन्तविस्तृता सत्यजामिं [?] विजातीयं मनुष्यादिजातिं न परि वृणक्ति । परितः सर्वतो न वर्जयति । तथा जामिं सजातीयं देवजातिं न परि वृणक्ति । न परिवर्जयति । मनुष्यादिकं देवादिकं च तदुपलक्षितं लोकद्वयं वा कात्स्न्र्येन प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः । किमर्थमिति तदुच्यते । दृशे कं सुखेन सर्वेषां दर्शनाय । सुखं यथा भवति तथा सर्वान्दर्शयितुं वा । किंचारेपसापापया निर्मलया तन्वा शरीरेण शाशदाना शाशद्यमाना । शाशदानः शाशद्यमान इति यास्कः । नि. ६-१६ । स्पष्टतां गच्छन्तीत्यर्थः । विभाती विशेषेण प्रकाशयन्ती सार्भादल्पादपि वस्तुनः कस्मादपि सकाशान्नेषते । न गच्छति । तमसि प्रकाशयति । तथा महो महतो मेर्वादेः सकाशान्नेषते । न गच्छति । तमसि प्रकाशयति । पूर्वं लोकद्वयं प्रकाशत इत्युक्तम् । इदानीमस्मिँल्लोके परमाण्वादि पर्वतपर्यन्तं कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः ॥

Read from the image; checked against the OCR. The word "satyajāmiṃ" [?] near the beginning is as printed and doubtful, and several words in the second half are small in the print. "Eṣā uṣāḥ eva it — here it has the sense of eva. In just this way, as she now appears, purutamā — greatly extensive, spread out very widely — she does not exclude (na pari vṛṇakti, does not avoid on all sides) the ajāmi, the creatures of a different kind, men and the rest; likewise, the jāmi, those of her own kind, the race of the gods, she does not exclude; that is, she illumines entirely, men and the others and the gods and the others, or the two worlds characterized by them. What for? That is said: dṛśe kam — to be seen by all easily; or, so that all are seen, so that it is pleasant. Moreover with a faultless body (arepasā, free of sin, pure), śāśadānā — becoming visible ('śāśadānaḥ means śāśadyamānaḥ', says Yāska, Ni. 6-16), that is, going toward clarity. Shining specially (vibhātī), she does not go away from even a small thing (arbhāt), but lights it in the dark; and likewise from the great (mahaḥ), from Meru and the like, she does not go away: she lights it in the dark. It was said before that she shines on the two worlds; now, in this world, she lights up the whole, from an atom to a mountain: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Eṣā — this Uṣas; eva it — in this very way; purutamā — most extensively spread out; ajāmim — those of a different kind, men and the rest (the world of men); kaṃ dṛśe — for easy seeing; na pari vṛṇakti — does not leave out; jāmim — those of her own kind, the gods; (the world of the gods); na (pari vṛṇakti) — does not leave out; arepasā — free of sin (pure); tanvā — with the body; śāśadānā — becoming visible; vibhātī — specially bright (Uṣas); arbhāt — from what is extremely small; na īṣate — does not go away; mahaḥ — from the very great; na (īṣate) — does not go away.

original p. 156

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. In this manner, spreading out extremely (widely), the Uṣas, leaving out neither the world of men (those of a different kind) nor the world of the gods (those of her own kind), becoming visible with a pure body, and having more light, illumines all objects, with no distinction of the small and the great.

Printed English (as printed): Verily she, the wide-expanded Ushas, neglects not (to give) the joy of sight to those of her own or of a different nature : visible in her faultless person, and brightly shining, she passes not by the little or the great.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6.

jāmiṃ ajāmim — for the word jāmi the meaning "gods of the same kind", and for ajāmi the meaning "humans and others of a different kind", is given. For the word jāmi the author of the Nirukta says: jāmir anyasyāṃ janayanti jāmy apatyam | jamater vā syād gatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyā bhavati (Ni. 3-6, as printed "೩-೬"). One derivation of jāmi is from the root jan, which gives the meaning "to be born", expressing the intention that "another helps her to produce children"; another derivation is from the root jam, meaning "to go", expressing that "she is one who goes to the house of her husband". By these two explanations it is known from the Nirukta explanation that the word jāmi means "sister". In support of this meaning —

न जामये तान्वो रिक्थमारैक्चकार गर्भं सनितुर्निधानम् । यदी मातरो जनयन्त वह्निमन्यः कर्ता सुकृतोरन्य ऋन्धन् ॥

na jāmaye tānvo rikthamāraikcakāra garbhaṃ saniturnidhānam | yadī mātaro janayanta vahnimanyaḥ kartā sukṛtoranya ṛndhan ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-2, as read from the print "೩-೩೧-೨".) Read letter by letter; "rikthamāraik" is as printed and doubtful. — citing this ṛk, the word jāmi is explained as "sister". Likewise, as explained in the preceding sūkta in this section,

भगस्य स्वसा वरुणस्य जामिरुषः सूनृते प्रथमा जरस्व । पश्चा स दध्या यो अघस्य धाता जयेम तं दक्षिणया रथेन ॥

bhagasya svasā varuṇasya jāmiruṣaḥ sūnṛte prathamā jarasva | paścā sa dadhyā yo aghasya dhātā jayema taṃ dakṣiṇayā rathena ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-5, as printed "೧-೧೨೩-೫".) — in this and other ṛks too the meaning "sister" is the sense of the word jāmi.

But in the present ṛk the meaning of this word comes out in a wider extent, as "kinsmen". Jāmiṃ ajāmim — the gods who are kinsmen, and men and the rest who are not kinsmen: that is the meaning. In the same way the extended sense "kinsmen":

जामिः सिन्धूनां भ्रातेव स्वस्रामिभ्यान्न राजा वनान्यत्ति । यद्वातजूतो वना व्यस्थादग्निर्ह दाति रोमा पृथिव्याः ॥

jāmiḥ sindhūnāṃ bhrāteva svasrāmibhyānna rājā vanānyatti | yadvātajūto vanā vyasthādagnirha dāti romā pṛthivyāḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-65-4, as read from the print.)

कस्ते जामिर्जनानामग्ने को दाश्वध्वरः । को ह कस्मिन्नसि श्रितः ॥

kaste jāmirjanānāmagne ko dāśvadhvaraḥ | ko ha kasminnasi śritaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-75-3, as read from the print.) — in these and other ṛks the meaning "kinsmen" is given just as in this ṛk.

na parivṛṇakti — na parivarjayati | manuṣyādikaṃ devādikaṃ ca tadupalakṣitaṃ lokadvayaṃ vā kārtsnyena prakāśayatīty arthaḥ: she illumines the two worlds that are filled with gods, men and others, without making a distinction — that is the meaning.

arepasā — apāpayā nirmalayā tanvā: "with a body free of sin", that is, with a pure body. The author of the Nirukta, citing

इदेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा नामभिः स्वैः । जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ॥

ideha jātā samavāvaśītāmarepasā tanvā nāmabhiḥ svaiḥ | jiṣṇurvāmanyaḥ sumakhasya sūrirdivo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-4 [?], as read from the print.) — as the words arepasā tanvā in it are explained as "with a body not touched by sin", so it is to be said here too.

ajāmim — na jāmiḥ ajāmiḥ tam; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2) gives the natural accent of the first member, the negative nañ; accusative singular. vṛṇakti — root vṛjī varjane; Rudhādi; laṭ third person singular tip; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam (Pā. 3-1-78) gives śnam; midaco 'ntyāt paraḥ places it after the last vowel; coḥ kuḥ gives the guttural for the j of the root, and car; since a ṛ precedes, the n becomes ṇ; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. arepasā — na vidyate repaḥ yasyāḥ sā arepāḥ tayā arepasā; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the final-acute of the latter member. tanvā — with the instrumental singular following, tanvādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam gives yaṇ; the yaṇ stands in the place of the acute; the case-ending follows it; udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ (Pā. 8-2-4) gives the svarita. śāśadānā — explained in Ṛk 10 of 1-123; only the nasalisation (anunāsikatva) does not occur here. īṣate — root īṣa gatihiṃsādarśaneṣu; Bhvādi; laṭ third person singular īṣate; since the sārvadhātuka follows the upadeśa, tāsyanudāttet (Pā. 6-1-186) makes it unaccented, and since śap is pit the root-accent remains. mahaḥ — mahataḥ, with the loss of the t in the Veda; or else the root maha pūjāyām, with kvip (kvip ca); ablative singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168) gives the acute to the case-ending. vibhātī — root bhā dīptau; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp in the feminine; since ṅīp follows a śatṛ without num, śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173) gives it the acute accent; in the compound the accent of the final member. ‖ 6 ‖

Read from the image; the OCR is garbled here and the small type of the last lines is doubtful. "Abhrāteva — like one who has no brother: she goes (eti) toward the father and the rest, pratīcī — facing back from her own place. As in the world a woman without a brother goes to the father's home for the getting of fitting garments, ornaments and the rest — if she had a brother, he would satisfy her duly with fitting gifts and the like — so she gets what such a one gets. Or else: when there is a brother, he performs for the father the piṇḍa-offering and other filial duties; in his absence she herself goes to do that for father and others. Likewise this Uṣas, for the getting of her own fitting radiance and so on, or for the giving of her own light, goes in front of the Sun, who has become her father. This is one simile. Another simile: dhanānāṃ sanaye gartārugiva — garta is a name for the house, since kṛdaro garta are read among its names (…); here it is said to be a place presided over by the king's men, the deciders of justice; one who mounts it is gartārukh. As in the world a woman whose husband has gone [or is dead] goes to the garta to win (sanaye) the property that is her own; the assessors there, having considered the matter, if she is entitled to the property, give her his wealth; so this Uṣas too goes up to the garta, the sky, the dwelling of the Sun, for winning (sanaye) the rays of wealth that bring joy, dhanānām. This simile is made with regard to the custom of a particular country. Moreover: patye uśatī kāmayamānā suvāsā jāyeva — this is the simile for Uṣas. As in the world a wife, beautifully dressed in silk and the like, adorned, who earlier at the time of her monthly period wore soiled clothes, after her bath, shining with fine clothes and ornaments, desiring her husband with special desire for enjoyment, plays with him; so Uṣas, though in dirty clothing because enveloped in the great darkness of night, at dawn, wrapped in her own light, being well-clothed, playing with the Sun, who is in the place of a husband, hasreva — laughing, as it were, apsaḥ — the forms in the place of teeth, blue, yellow and the rest, ni riṇīte. Or else the sense is: she makes all objects that are seen go forth, makes them manifest. As in the world a lovely woman reveals her teeth under pretence of a smile, so this Uṣas makes all forms manifest. This mantra is clearly explained in the Nirukta (3-5)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Uṣāḥ — the goddess Uṣas; abhrātā — a woman without a brother; puṃsaḥ iva — (for the sake of getting ornaments and the like) as one who goes to her father and the others (or as one who does the rites that are the brother's duty for the fathers); (and) dhanānām — of riches and the like (the light that causes joy); sanaye — for the gaining; gartārukh iva — like a woman (childless and husbandless) who goes up to the place of justice; pratīcī — facing the west (to receive light from the Sun, or to give her own light); eti — goes; (kiṃ ca — and); patye — for her husband; uśatī — desiring (waiting for the Sun); suvāsāḥ — in white garments (clothed in her own light); jāyā iva — like a wife who goes (facing her husband) with desire for enjoyment; (uṣāḥ — Uṣas); hasrā iva — like one laughing; apsaḥ — the forms, blue, yellow and others (things illumined by her); ni riṇīte — makes well visible.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. As a woman without a brother, for the getting of ornaments and the like, comes to the father and the others, and as a (childless and husbandless) woman goes to the seat of justice for the getting of wealth, Uṣas goes facing the Sun; and as a woman desirous of her husband goes (to his presence) in white garments, Uṣas (like one with a smile revealing teeth and the rest) makes manifest special forms, blue, yellow and the rest.

Printed English (as printed): She goes to the west, as (a woman who has) no brother (repairs) to her male (relatives); and like one ascending the hall (of justice) for the recovery of property, (she mounts in the sky to claim her lustre): and like a wife desirous to please her husband, Ushas puts on becoming attire, and smiling as it were, displays her charms.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 7.

For this ṛk the Nirukta is as follows —

अभ्रातृकेव पुंसः पित्र्यं नेत्यभिमुखी सन्तानकर्मणे पिण्डदानाय न पतिं गर्तारोहिणीव धनलाभाय दाक्षिणात्या [?] ।

abhrātṛkeva puṃsaḥ pitryaṃ netyabhimukhī santānakarmaṇe piṇḍadānāya na patiṃ gartārohiṇīva dhanalābhāya dākṣiṇātyā [?] |

(Ni. 3-5, as printed "೩-೫".) Read letter by letter; the last word "dākṣiṇātyā" / "dākṣiṇājā" is doubtful. "A woman without a brother goes, facing toward her father's house, for the rites of progeny, for the piṇḍa-offering, not [to her] husband; the woman of the south, [like] one mounting the garta for the gain of wealth." — These two explanations are compared to the appearance of Uṣas. In this ṛk there are four similes together, namely —

अभ्रातेव पुंस इत्येका ; गर्तारोहिणीवेति द्वितीया ; जायेव पत्या इति तृतीया ; हस्रेवेति चतुर्थी ;

abhrāteva puṃsa ityekā ; gartārohiṇīveti dvitīyā ; jāyeva patyā iti tṛtīyā ; hasreveti caturthī ;

The enumeration is as printed; "jāyeva patyā" is the print's reading, as against "patye" in the ṛk. "Here, by the first simile, abhrāteva puṃsaḥ, the unsupported state (anirvāha) of a woman without a brother is indicated. As a woman without a brother turns toward the father-line, not toward the husband, so Uṣas turns toward Āditya. So the girl without a brother makes shine and increases the very family in which she was born; not the husband's family."

First, the conduct of Uṣas is compared to that of a woman who has no brother. As she leaves her husband's house and illumines (builds up) her father's house and increases that family, so Uṣas too joins her father, Āditya, and makes his orb shine all the more.

Second, gartārohiṇīva: another comparison is that, like a woman who goes up to a garta for the gain of wealth, Uṣas too travels westward-facing to obtain light from the Sun. What garta is, the author of the Nirukta explains.

original p. 162

गर्तः सभास्थाणुर्गृणातेः । सत्यसंगरो भवति । तं तत्र या पुत्रा या पतिका सारोहति तां तत्राभ्रैरभ्रश्नन्ति [?] सा रिक्थं लभते । (नि. ३-५)

gartaḥ sabhāsthāṇurgṛṇāteḥ | satyasaṃgaro bhavati | taṃ tatra yā putrā yā patikā sārohati tāṃ tatrābhrairabhraśnanti [?] sā rikthaṃ labhate | (ni. 3-5)

The word garta is derived from the root gṝ, which gives the meaning "to call for, to ask", and it indicates a "pillar of an assembly hall". All business done at that pillar is in the nature of truth (satya-saṃgara). A woman without a son and without a husband mounts that pillar-place; then those concerned there strike her with [...], and wealth falls to her — thus, having explained the purport of the words gartārukh, in accordance with this context, he then states other meanings of the word garta:

श्मशानसंचयोऽपि गर्त उच्यते गुरतेरपर्णो भवति ।

śmaśānasaṃcayo 'pi garta ucyate gurateraparṇo bhavati |

[The word garta is also well known in the sense of a heap of the cremation ground, derived from the root gur, which gives the meaning "to raise"; this is stated.] Citing the śruti text

[?]ोपरस्यावि[?]ष्णुर्याद्यदुपरस्यावि[?]ष्णुर्याद्गर्तेष्ठाः स्यात्प्रमायुक्तो यजमानः ।

[?]oparasyāvi[?]ṣṇuryādyaduparasyāvi[?]ṣṇuryādgarteṣṭhāḥ syātpramāyukto yajamānaḥ |

Read letter by letter; the text is small and doubtful. — as the Kannada paraphrases it, the lower part of the sacrificial post must not be shown or uncovered; if through carelessness one does so, such a sacrificer lies down in the cremation ground (the OCR reads the words differently, "noparasyāniṣṭhurādya…"; my transliteration of the Sanskrit is therefore uncertain) — this explains the meaning of the word garta. Next:

रथोऽपि गर्त उच्यते गृणातेः स्तुतिकर्मणः । स्तुततमं यानम् ।

ratho 'pi garta ucyate gṛṇāteḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ | stutatamaṃ yānam |

The word garta derived from the root gṝ, meaning "to praise", is also well known in the sense of "chariot". Having stated this explanation, citing the ṛk

हिरण्यरूपमुषसो व्युष्टावयःस्थूणमुदिता सूर्यस्य । आ रोहथो वरुण मित्र गर्तमतश्च चक्षाथे अदितिं दितिं च ॥

hiraṇyarūpamuṣaso vyuṣṭāvayaḥsthūṇamuditā sūryasya | ā rohatho varuṇa mitra gartamataśca cakṣāthe aditiṃ ditiṃ ca ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-62-8, as read from the print "೫-೬೨-೮"; "ayaḥsthūṇam" as read.) he shows that here the word garta is used in the sense of "chariot".

Then he explains the third simile, jāyeva patye kāmayamānā suvāsā ṛtukāleṣu: as a wife adorned with clothes and ornaments, at the proper times of her season, looks for the arrival of her husband with longing, so Uṣas, shining with her splendour, looks at Āditya. Lastly, hasreva ni riṇīte apsaḥ | hasaneva dantān nivṛṇute rūpāṇi: the four similes — as a woman with a gentle smile reveals her white teeth, Uṣas spreads her radiance — are explained. (Ni. 3-5)

apsaḥ — the word apsas is recorded among the names of form (Ni. 3-13, as printed "೩-೧೩").

अप्स इति रूपनामाप्नोतेरप्सानीयं भवत्यादर्शनीयं व्यापनीयं वा स्पष्टं दर्शनायेति शाकपूणिः । यदप्स इत्यभक्षस्य । अप्सो नामेति व्यापिनः ।

apsa iti rūpanāmāpnoterapsānīyaṃ bhavatyādarśanīyaṃ vyāpanīyaṃ vā spaṣṭaṃ darśanāyeti śākapūṇiḥ | yadapsa ityabhakṣasya | apso nāmeti vyāpinaḥ |

(Ni. 5-13 [?], as printed in the form "೫-೧೩"; doubtful.) The word apsas from the root psā, "to eat", with negation, yields the meaning "not to be eaten"; it is not to be eaten, it is only fit to be seen, says Śākapūṇi; or, from the root āp "to pervade", the name apsas is "pervading everywhere": thus the author of the Nirukta states two views on the etymology of this word (tad dhā bhavati rūpavatī apsarāḥ [?] — "she who has form is apsarā"). In the present ṛk, for the word apsas Sāyaṇa says: apso dantasthānīyāni rūpāṇi nīlapītādīni — as a woman with a gentle smile shows the forms of her white teeth, so Uṣas, with her radiance joined to the forms of blue, yellow and the rest, spreads out.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7, pp. 163–164; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). abhrātā — na vidyate bhrātā yasya sa abhrātā; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the final-acute of the latter member. puṃsaḥ — root pūñ pavane; pūño ḍuṃsun gives the suffix ḍuṃsun; because of the marker ḍ there is elision; the form puṃs; accusative plural; since it has a single syllable, sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ gives the acute to the ending. pratīcī — prefix prati, root añcu gatipūjanayoḥ; ṛtvik-dadhṛk… (Pā. 3-2-59) gives kvin; aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti elides the nasal; añcater upasaṃkhyānam gives ṅīp; since it has the bha designation, aco 'ñcaḥ (Pā. 6-4-138) elides the a of the root; since the root añc with the lost nasal and a follows, the preceding word is lengthened (ca, Pā. 6-3-138); anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (Pā. 6-1-161) gives the acute to the ṅīp. gartārukh — gartam ārohati iti gartārukh; prefix ā, root ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca; kvip; kutva of the h of the root by vyatyaya; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the final member; nominative singular.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

एकस्मादेवान्तरिक्षादुत्पन्नत्वात्परस्परं स्वसृभावः । तथा ह्युषसः प्राथम्यात्तेजस्वित्वाच्च ज्यायस्त्वम् । स्वयमेव सरतीति वा स्वसा । रात्रिः स्वस्रे ज्यायस्यै उक्तरीत्या ज्येष्ठायै उषसे योनिमुत्पत्तिस्थानमपररात्ररूपमारैक् । आरिचत् । प्रादात् । प्ररेचयतीत्यर्थः । तथा च पूर्वत्रामात् । रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् । ऋ. १-११३-१ । इति । दत्त्वा चास्या उत्पन्नाया उषसः प्रतिचक्ष्येव ज्ञापयित्वेव स्वयमपैत्येव गच्छति । ज्यायस्यागतायां तस्यै स्वस्थानं दत्त्वा स्वयं तत्र स्थातुमनुचितमिति विज्ञायैवापगच्छतीति भावः । एवमुत्पन्नैषा सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्व्युच्छन्ती तमो विवासयन्त्यञ्जि व्यञ्जकं तेजः । यद्वा । अञ्जि व्यक्तं जगत् । अङ्क्ते । अनक्ति । प्रकाशयति । किमिव । समनगा इव । सम्यगननहेतवो [?] आपः समनाः । ता गच्छन्तीति समनगा विद्युतः । व्रा व्रातः । विद्युत्संघा इव । यद्वा । सम्यग्गमनाय गच्छन्तीति समनगाः सूर्यरश्मयः । ते इव व्राः व्रातः संघीभूताः । ते यथाञ्जते जगत्प्रकाशयन्ति तथेत्यर्थः । व्राता इत्यत्र तकारलोपश्छान्दसः ॥

ekasmādevāntarikṣādutpannatvātparasparaṃ svasṛbhāvaḥ | tathā hyuṣasaḥ prāthamyāttejasvitvācca jyāyastvam | svayameva saratīti vā svasā | rātriḥ svasre jyāyasyai uktarītyā jyeṣṭhāyai uṣase yonimutpattisthānamapararātrarūpamāraik | āricat | prādāt | prarecayatītyarthaḥ | tathā ca pūrvatrāmāt | rātryuṣase yonimāraik | ṛ. 1-113-1 | iti | dattvā cāsyā utpannāyā uṣasaḥ praticakṣyeva jñāpayitveva svayamapaityeva gacchati | jyāyasyāgatāyāṃ tasyai svasthānaṃ dattvā svayaṃ tatra sthātumanucitamiti vijñāyaivāpagacchatīti bhāvaḥ | evamutpannaiṣā sūryasya raśmibhirvyucchantī tamo vivāsayantyañji vyañjakaṃ tejaḥ | yadvā | añji vyaktaṃ jagat | aṅkte | anakti | prakāśayati | kimiva | samanagā iva | samyagananahetavo [?] āpaḥ samanāḥ | tā gacchantīti samanagā vidyutaḥ | vrā vrātaḥ | vidyutsaṃghā iva | yadvā | samyaggamanāya gacchantīti samanagāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ | te iva vrāḥ vrātaḥ saṃghībhūtāḥ | te yathāñjate jagatprakāśayanti tathetyarthaḥ | vrātā ityatra takāralopaśchāndasaḥ ‖

Read from the image and checked against the OCR; "samyag-anana-hetavo" is doubtful in the print. "Because they are born from one and the same atmosphere, they are mutually sisters (svasṛ); and since Uṣas is first and more brilliant, she is the elder (jyāyasī). Or else svasā means 'she who goes of herself'. The Night, svasre jyāyasyai — in the way said, for the elder sister Uṣas — yonim — the place of origin in the form of the last watch of the night — āraik — has given (āricat, 'she has made [it] over, she has given'). Thus it has been said before, 'rātry uṣase yonim āraik' (Ṛ. 1-113-1). And having given it, praticakṣyeva — as if informing the newly born Uṣas, she herself apa eti — goes away: the sense is that, understanding it would be improper for her to stay there when the elder has come, after giving her own place, she departs. Thus born, Uṣas, dispelling the darkness with the rays of the Sun, añji — the revealing radiance; or añji — the manifest world; aṅkte — anoints, illumines. Like what? Samanagā iva — the waters that are the cause of right going are samanāḥ; those that go (gacchanti) are samanagā, the lightnings; vrā are vrātāḥ, hosts; as hosts of lightning. Or else, those who go for right going are samanagāḥ, the rays of the Sun; as they, gathered into a host, illumine the world, so she: that is the sense. In vrātāḥ the loss of t is Vedic."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Svasā — the sister (the Night, who is in the position of one's own); jyāyasyai svasre — for her elder sister (Uṣas); yonim — the place of origin (the last part of the night); āraik — has made over (has given); asyāḥ — to this (the newly born) Uṣas; praticakṣyā iva — like one who informs (having left her place, as one who understands that her being there is improper); apa eti — goes away; (thus the born goddess Uṣas) sūryasya raśmibhiḥ — by the rays of the Sun (with help); vi ucchantī — driving away (the darkness); samanagāḥ vrāḥ iva — like a host of lightnings (like a mass of the Sun's rays) (as lightning or the rays of the Sun light up the world); añji — the world-revealing radiance (the manifest world); aṅkte — makes manifest.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The younger sister, Night, makes the last part of the night the place of origin for her elder sister, the goddess Uṣas; (afterwards) the Night goes away; the Uṣas thus born, driving away (the darkness) with the help of the Sun's rays, spreads like a host of lightnings (like a mass of the Sun's rays) the radiance that reveals the world.

Printed English (as printed): The sister (Night) has prepared a birth-place for her elder sister (Day), and having made it known to her, departs. Ushas, dispersing the darkness with the rays of the sun, illumines the world, like congregated lightnings.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 8.

svasā svasre yonim āraik — Uṣas is called the elder sister of Night. As soon as Uṣas rises, the Night, of herself becoming invisible, makes a place for her sister. The word yonim is explained as "the place of birth". The author of the Nirukta, citing

इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिराग‍ाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा । यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवायँ एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥

idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā | yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya~ evā rātryuṣase yonimāraik ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-1, as printed "೧-೧೧೩-೧".) Read letter by letter; "āgāc citraḥ" is as printed and the ligature marks are doubtful. explains, evaṃ rātry uṣase yonim aricat sthānam [?] — "thus Night has given place to Uṣas" — and the yoni … (the print gives the rest as yonir abhiyuta enāṃ garbhaḥ [?], which I cannot make sure of). Durgācārya has commented on this thus (Ni. 2-19, as printed "೨-೧೯"):

रात्रिः उषसः जन्मार्थं "योनिं" "स्थानं" अवकाशं आरिचत् आरेचयति ददातीत्यर्थः । यथोषा आदित्यस्य जन्मनो हेतुस्तदनन्तरजन्मत्वात् एवं रात्रिः उषसो जन्मनो हेतुः ॥

rātriḥ uṣasaḥ janmārthaṃ "yoniṃ" "sthānaṃ" avakāśaṃ āricat ārecayati dadātītyarthaḥ | yathoṣā ādityasya janmano hetustadanantarajanmatvāt evaṃ rātriḥ uṣaso janmano hetuḥ ‖

"For the birth of Uṣas the Night gave the yoni — place, room — āricat, makes to give: that is the sense. As Uṣas is the cause of the birth of Āditya, because his birth follows hers, so Night is the cause of the birth of Uṣas." — As Uṣas is the cause of the birth of Āditya, so Night is the cause of the birth of Uṣas; and the idea is that, being the cause of her rising, Night herself becomes invisible as soon as Uṣas appears.

अरुषस्य दुहितरा विरूपे स्तृभिरन्या पिपिशे सूरो अन्या । मिथस्तुरा विचरन्ती पावके मन्म श्रुतं नक्षत ऋच्यमाने ॥

aruṣasya duhitarā virūpe stṛbhiranyā pipiśe sūro anyā | mithasturā vicarantī pāvake manma śrutaṃ nakṣata ṛcyamāne ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-186-? [?] — the numerals of the print are not clear.) — in these and many other ṛks the sisterly relationship of Night and Uṣas is described, and how both of them, by their ceaseless and regular movement, are the cause of the course of the world.

praticakṣyā iva — jñāpayitveva: like one who informs her rightly of her duty — that is the meaning. The root cakṣ with the prefix prati gives the meaning of a clear, discriminating knowledge that is neither confused nor doubtful. For example —

रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव तदस्य रूपं प्रतिचक्षणाय । इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥

rūpaṃrūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva tadasya rūpaṃ praticakṣaṇāya | indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā daśa ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-18, as read from the print.) — in this ṛk praticakṣaṇāya means pratiniyatadarśanāya — "for definite sight"; the Nirukta says ayam agnir ayaṃ viṣṇur ayaṃ rudra ity evam asaṃkīrṇadarśanāya — "for unconfused sight: this is Agni, this is Viṣṇu, this is Rudra". As the meaning is unconfused and distinct knowledge, so here too the sense is that Night has made known to Uṣas the duty, definite and distinct according to the circumstances.

samanagāḥ vrā iva — here two kinds of meaning are given. First, samyag-anana-hetava āpaḥ samanāḥ; tā gacchantīti samanagā vidyutaḥ; vrā vrātāḥ saṃghāḥ; vidyutsaṃgha ity arthaḥ: the waters, being easily moving, are named samanā; the lightnings, being in contact with the waters, are called samanagā; samanagā vrā thus means the host of lightnings. Second, samyaggamanāya gacchanti samanagāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ: since the Sun's rays move freely, they are named samanagā; samanagā vrā means the host of the Sun's rays.

The author of the Nirukta has included the word samanā among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9 [?], as read by the OCR). He then cites

बह्वीनां पिता बहुरस्य पुत्रश्चिश्चा कृणोति समनावगत्य । इषुधिः सङ्काः पृतनाश्च सर्वाः पृष्ठे निनद्धो जयति प्रसूतः ॥

bahvīnāṃ pitā bahurasya putraściścā kṛṇoti samanāvagatya | iṣudhiḥ saṅkāḥ pṛtanāśca sarvāḥ pṛṣṭhe ninaddho jayati prasūtaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-5, as read from the print.) Read letter by letter; "ciścā" is as printed and doubtful.

वह्निवेदा [?] गनीगन्ति कर्णं प्रियं सखायं परिषस्वजाना । योषेव शिङ्क्ते वितताधि धन्वञ्ज्या इयं समने पारयन्ती ॥

vahnivedā [?] ganīganti karṇaṃ priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ pariṣasvajānā | yoṣeva śiṅkte vitatādhi dhanvañjyā iyaṃ samane pārayantī ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-3 [?], as read from the print.) — citing these two ṛks he explains the word samana as "battle".

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8, pp. 167–168; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). jyāyasyai — when īyasun comes in the sense of excess, jya ca (Pā. 5-3-61) gives the substitute jya for praśasya; when jya + īyasun stand, jyādādīyasaḥ (Pā. 6-4-160) gives ā in place of the ī of īyasun; ādeḥ parasya — the initial [ī] is replaced by a [sic, ā of the print]; the form jyāyas; in the feminine, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp: jyāyasī; dative singular; since it ends in a suffix, ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute.

āraik — root ricir virecane; luṅ third person singular tip; itaś ca elides the i; bahulaṃ chandasi elides cli; puganta-laghūpadhasya ca (Pā. 7-3-86) gives guṇa of the root's short penultimate; hal-ṅyābbhyo [as printed "ಹಲ್ಜ್ಯಾಭ್ಯೋ"] elides the apṛkta suffix; by a letter-change e becomes ai; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. praticakṣyā — root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; samāse 'nañpūrve ktvo lyap (Pā. 7-1-37) gives lyap in the place of ktvā; since it is pit it is unaccented; the root-accent remains; in the compound the accent of the final member. vyucchantī — root uchī vivāse, prefix vi; when śatṛ comes in the laṭ sense, ugitaś ca gives ṅīp in the feminine; the śa-suffix accent remains. añji — root añjū vyaktimrakṣaṇakāntigatiṣu; khanikaṣyañji… (Uṇ. 4-139 as read) gives the suffix i; final-acute by the accent of the suffix. aṅkte — the root as before; laṭ third person singular; añkte; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. samanagāḥ — samanāḥ gacchanti, or samyag-ananāya gacchanti iti samanagāḥ; root gam gatau; janasanakhanakramagamo vic (Pā. 3-2-67) gives viṭ; with it following, vidvanoranunāsikasyātā (Pā. 6-4-41) gives ā to the nasal of the root; complete loss of the suffix; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the final member. vrāḥ — the form is vrātāḥ; in the Veda the t is lost. ‖ 8 ‖

āsām | pūrvāsām | aha 'su [?] | svasṛ 'ṇām | aparā | pūrvām | abhi | eti | paścāt | tāḥ | pratna 'vat | navyasīḥ | nūnam | asme iti | revat | ucchantu | su 'dināḥ | uṣasaḥ ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

स्वसृणां परस्परं स्वसृभावमापन्नानां स्वयं सरन्तीनां वा पूर्वासां पुरातनीनामासामुषसां मध्येऽहन्यहनि प्रतिदिनमपराद्यतन्युषा पूर्वामतीतदिवससंबन्धिनीमुषसं पश्चादनुसृत्याभ्येति । अभिमुखं गच्छति । अव्यवधानेन गच्छतीत्यर्थः । सर्वेष्वहःस्वेवमेवाभ्येति । नव्यसीर्नवीयस्यो नवतरा आगामिन्यस्ता उषास उषसोऽपि नूनं निश्चयेन प्रत्नवत्पुरातन्य इव सुदिनाः शोभनकर्मानुष्ठानसाधनदिवसाः शोभनदिनमुखा वा सत्योऽस्मे अस्माकं रेवद्बहुधनविशिष्टं यथा भवति तथोच्छन्तु । प्रकाशयन्तु । पूर्वतन्यो यथोच्छन् तथागमिन्योऽप्युच्छन्त्वित्यर्थः ॥

svasṛṇāṃ parasparaṃ svasṛbhāvamāpannānāṃ svayaṃ sarantīnāṃ vā pūrvāsāṃ purātanīnāmāsāmuṣasāṃ madhye 'hanyahani pratidinamaparādyatanyuṣā pūrvāmatītadivasasaṃbandhinīmuṣasaṃ paścādanusṛtyābhyeti | abhimukhaṃ gacchati | avyavadhānena gacchatītyarthaḥ | sarveṣvahaḥsvevamevābhyeti | navyasīrnavīyasyo navatarā āgāminyastā uṣāsa uṣaso 'pi nūnaṃ niścayena pratnavatpurātanya iva sudināḥ śobhanakarmānuṣṭhānasādhanadivasāḥ śobhanadinamukhā vā satyo 'sme asmākaṃ revadbahudhanaviśiṣṭaṃ yathā bhavati tathocchantu | prakāśayantu | pūrvatanyo yathocchan tathāgaminyo 'pyucchantvityarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the first sentence is clear in the print; the OCR gives "ahasu" for "ahani ahani". "Among the Uṣases of the past, svasṛṇām — who have become mutually sisters, or who move of themselves — āsām pūrvāsām — these ancient ones — day after day (ahan ahani) the later one, today's Uṣas, follows after the earlier one, the one connected with the day gone by, and goes toward her (abhi eti), face to face; that is, without any break. On all days she goes in just this way. Navyasīḥ — newer, newer still, coming; those Uṣases also, surely (nūnam), like the old ones (pratnavat), sudināḥ — days that are the means of performing auspicious rites, or having auspicious days at their head — being such, asme — for us — revat — as bringing abundant wealth — may they shine (ucchantu); as the former ones shone, so may those that are to come also shine: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Svasṛṇām — those who are sisters to each other (mutually); pūrvāsām āsām — among these Uṣases that have gone before; aparā — this Uṣas, the other; pūrvām — the earlier one; paścāt — following after; ahani ahani abhi eti — daily goes, without break; navyasīḥ — coming later (new); tāḥ uṣāsaḥ — those Uṣases too; nūnam — surely; pratnavat — like those that have gone before; sudināḥ — (for our rites) auspicious days (those that begin auspicious days); asme — for us; revat — so as to bring the gain of wealth and the like; ucchantu — may they shine.

original p. 170

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Among the departed Uṣases, who are as sisters, each follows the earlier one (without a break); may the Uṣases that are to come also, like those that have gone, shine for us as auspicious days for our rites, bringing us gain.

Printed English (as printed): Of all these sisters who have gone before, a successor daily follows the one that has preceded. So may new dawns, like the old, bringing fortunate days, shine upon us blessed with affluence.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 9.

svasṛṇām … pūrvām abhyeti paścāt — svasṛṇāṃ parasparaṃ svasṛbhāvam āpannānāṃ svayaṃ sarantīnāṃ vā pūrvāsāṃ purātanīnām āsām uṣasāṃ madhye 'han ahani pratidinam aparādyatanī uṣā pūrvām atītadivasasaṃbandhinīm uṣasaṃ paścād anusṛtya abhyeti. Since the Uṣases show themselves separately each day, the Uṣas of the next day, keeping up the sisterly relationship with the Uṣas of the previous day, follows her. Therefore the sense is that all the past Uṣases have been sisters to the Uṣas of the present day.

pratnavat — this word is recorded among the names of "old" (Ni. 3-20, as read). The author of the Nirukta, citing

पवित्रवन्तः परि वाचमासते पितैषां प्रत्नो अभि रक्षति व्रतम् । महः समुद्रं वरुणस्तिरो दधे धीरा इच्छेकुर्धरुणेष्वारभम् ॥

pavitravantaḥ pari vācamāsate pitaiṣāṃ pratno abhi rakṣati vratam | mahaḥ samudraṃ varuṇastiro dadhe dhīrā icchekurdharuṇeṣvārabham ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-73-3, as read from the print.) states for this word the meaning pratnaḥ purāṇaḥ. Pratnavat means "like the Uṣases that have gone on, since eternity, so may the Uṣas of the present day be sudināḥ — auspicious days for our rites" — thus she is prayed to.

asme — asmākam; "to us, the sacrificers and the rest", the meaning; "make for us all gain of wealth". It is stated that the word asme, though of one form, is used in all case-meanings (Ni. 6-7, as read by the OCR). (It was stated before that the word asmākam too is used in all cases.)

asme te bandhuḥ — vayam ity arthaḥ — commenting on this, Durgācārya says: asme ity etat padaṃ sarvavibhaktyantam | tasmād anekārtham | ekam eva hy etac chabdarūpam …

original p. 171

…(Durga's comment, continued from p. 170): "asme is a word that stands in all the seven cases; its sense is fixed according to the context. That is, asme te bandhuḥ — 'we [are] your kinsmen' — is the example for the nominative." Thus he states that this word asme, which can be used in all seven case-endings, must be explained in each instance according to the context; and of these asme te bandhuḥ is the example for the first case. And again —

आ श्येनस्य जवसा नूतनेनास्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । हवे हि वामश्विना रातहव्यः शश्वत्तमायाँ उषसो व्युष्टौ ॥

ā śyenasya javasā nūtanenāsme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | have hi vāmaśvinā rātahavyaḥ śaśvattamāyā~ uṣaso vyuṣṭau ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-11, as read from the print.) — citing this ṛk, "asme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ — asmān, 'to us'", he states that asme is used in the sense of the second case;

भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । भूरीणि हि कृणवामा शविष्ठेन्द्र क्रत्वा मरुतो यद्वशाम ॥

bhūri cakartha yujyebhirasme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭhendra kratvā maruto yadvaśāma ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-63-2 [?], as read from the print.) — citing this ṛk, that there it means "by us" (asmābhiḥ), in the third case;

अस्मे प्र यन्धि मघवन्नृजीषिन्निन्द्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः । अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीराञ्छश्वत इन्द्र शिप्रिन् ॥

asme pra yandhi maghavannṛjīṣinnindra rāyo viśvavārasya bhūreḥ | asme śataṃ śarado jīvase dhā asme vīrāñchaśvata indra śiprin ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-22-? [?]; the numerals are not clear.) — citing this ṛk, that it means "for us" (asmabhyam) in the fourth case;

तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम । स सुत्रामा स्ववाँ इन्द्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ॥

tasya vayaṃ sumatau yajñiyasyāpi bhadre saumanase syāma | sa sutrāmā svavā~ indro asme ārācciddveṣaḥ sanutaryuyotu ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-12, as read from the print.) — in this ṛk, asmat — "from us" — in the fifth case;

आ नो भर भगमिन्द्र द्युमन्तं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि प्ररेके । ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनाम् ॥

ā no bhara bhagamindra dyumantaṃ ni te deṣṇasya dhīmahi prareke | ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme tamā pṛṇa vasupate vasūnām ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-13 [?], as read from the print; deṣṇasya as read.) — in this, asmākam — "our" — in the sixth case; and likewise —

अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो । अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥

agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho | asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-79-4, as read from the print.) — in this one the seventh case, "in us"; thus he has shown that the examples for all the case-endings occur in one and the same form (Ni. 6-7, as read by the OCR; the numerals in the print are "೬-೭").

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). āsām — root āsa upaveśane; kvip ca gives kvip; genitive plural; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168) gives the acute accent to the case-ending. ahasu — the form of the word is ahaḥsu; the final of the word is lost in the Veda; locative plural. eti — root iṇ gatau; Adādi; laṭ third person singular; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. paścāt — paścāc (Pā. 5-3-32) gives paścā for apara and the suffix āti in the sphere of astāti; by the suffix accent the ā is acute. pratnavat — pratna iva pratnavat; pratnapūrvaviśvemāt thāl chandasi [print: "ಪ್ರತ್ನ ಪುರಾಣೇ ಪ್ರಾತ್"] gives the suffix tnap to pra in the sense of purāṇa; tatra tasyeva (Pā. 5-1-116) gives the suffix vati; final-acute by the suffix accent. navyasīḥ — atiśayena navaḥ navīyān; īyasun in the sense of excess; ugitaś ca gives ṅīp in the feminine; in the Veda the ī of īyasun is lost; since the suffix has the marker n, the first-syllable acute; with jas following, supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39) gives the lengthening by the preceding savarṇa. asme — the word asmad; with the locative [as printed "ಷಷ್ಠೀ"] plural following, supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39) gives śe; śeṣe lopaḥ elides the initial. revat — rayiḥ asya asti iti revat; rayer matau bahulam gives saṃprasāraṇa to rayi when matup follows; na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam forbids it, so the saṃprasāraṇa is of the y; saṃprasāraṇāc ca (Pā. 6-1-108) gives pūrvarūpa; guṇa; chandasīra (Pā. 8-2-15) gives va for the m of matup; re śabdāc ca matupa udāttatvaṃ vaktavyam [print: "ರೇ ಶಬ್ದಾಚ್ಚ ಮತುಪ ಉದಾತ್ತತ್ವಂ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಮ್"] gives the acute to matup though it has the marker p. ucchantu — root uchī vivāse; loṭ third person plural; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

प्र बोधयोषः पृणतो मघोन्यबुध्यमानाः पणयः ससन्तु । रेवदुच्छ मघवद्भ्यो मघोनि रेवत्स्तोत्रे सूनृते जारयन्ती ॥ १० ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

प्र । बोधय । उषः । पृणतः । मघोनि । अबुध्यमानाः । पणयः । ससन्तु । रेवत् । उच्छ । मघवत्ऽभ्यः । मघोनि । रेवत् । स्तोत्रे । सूनृते । जारयन्ती ॥ १० ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मघोनि मघवति अस्मभ्यं दातव्यैर्बहुभिर्धनैर्युक्ते हे उषोदेवि पृणतो हविःप्रदानेन यजमानान्प्र बोधय । प्रज्ञापय । प्रतिबुद्धान्कुरु । किंच पणयो व्यवहारासहिष्णवो वणिजः । पणिर्वणिग्भवतीति यास्कः । नि. २-१७ [?] । पणय इति लुब्धकाः [?] अबुध्यमाना यागादीन्कुर्वाणा अदानशीला अस्मच्छत्रवः ससन्तु । स्वपन्तु । दीर्घनिद्रा भवन्तु । म्रियन्तामित्यर्थः । तथा च मन्त्रान्तरम् । ससन्तु त्या अरातयो बोधन्तु शूर रातयः । ऋ. १-२९-४ । इति । किंच हे मघोनि मघवति हविर्भिस्त्वद्वति हे उषः मघवद्भ्यो हविर्लक्षणान्नवद्भ्यो यजमानेभ्यस्तेषामर्थं रेवद्धनवत्समृद्धिमदुच्छ । विभाहि । किंच हे सूनृते सुष्ठु मनुष्याणां नेत्रि देवि जारयन्ती सर्वप्राणिनः क्षपयन्ती त्वं स्तोत्रे स्तुतिकर्त्रे यजमानाय तदर्थं रेवद्धनवत्समृद्ध्यर्थमुच्छेति शेषः ॥

he maghoni maghavati asmabhyaṃ dātavyairbahubhirdhanairyukte he uṣodevi pṛṇato haviḥpradānena yajamānānpra bodhaya | prajñāpaya | pratibuddhānkuru | kiṃca paṇayo vyavahārāsahiṣṇavo vaṇijaḥ | paṇirvaṇigbhavatīti yāskaḥ | ni. 2-17 [?] | paṇaya iti lubdhakāḥ [?] abudhyamānā yāgādīnkurvāṇā adānaśīlā asmacchatravaḥ sasantu | svapantu | dīrghanidrā bhavantu | mriyantāmityarthaḥ | tathā ca mantrāntaram | sasantu tyā arātayo bodhantu śūra rātayaḥ | ṛ. 1-29-4 | iti | kiṃca he maghoni maghavati havirbhistvadvati he uṣaḥ maghavadbhyo havirlakṣaṇānnavadbhyo yajamānebhyasteṣāmarthaṃ revaddhanavatsamṛddhimaduccha | vibhāhi | kiṃca he sūnṛte suṣṭhu manuṣyāṇāṃ netri devi jārayantī sarvaprāṇinaḥ kṣapayantī tvaṃ stotre stutikartre yajamānāya tadarthaṃ revaddhanavatsamṛddhyarthamuccheti śeṣaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the OCR is garbled in places. The Nirukta number "2-17" is as the OCR gives it and the print's numerals are unclear; "lubdhakāḥ" is doubtful. "O maghoni — O Uṣas, rich, possessed of many riches to be given to us — wake the sacrificers, pṛṇataḥ, those who give oblations; make them know; make them awake. Moreover, paṇayaḥ — traders who cannot bear the exchange [of giving]: 'a paṇi is a trader', says Yāska (Ni. [?]). Let the paṇis — the niggardly (?), who do not wake, who do not perform sacrifices and the like, the non-givers, our enemies — sasantu, sleep; may they sleep long; may they die: that is the sense. And likewise another mantra: 'sasantu tyā arātayo bodhantu śūra rātayaḥ' (Ṛ. 1-29-4). Moreover, O maghoni, rich in oblations, O Uṣas, for the sacrificers maghavadbhyaḥ — who have food in the form of oblations — for their sake shine (uccha) wealth-bringing, abundantly. Further, O sūnṛte, good leader of men, O goddess, jārayantī, wearing out all living beings, for the praiser, the sacrificer, shine for him, with abundance of wealth: so is the sentence to be completed."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Maghoni — (O Uṣas) possessed of wealth in the form of oblations (to be given to us); (he) uṣaḥ — O goddess Uṣas; pṛṇataḥ — of those giving oblations (the sacrificers); pra bodhaya — awaken well; paṇayaḥ — the merchant-like (niggards); abudhyamānāḥ — not performing the sacrifice and the rest (our enemies who are not givers); sasantu — let them sleep (let them perish); (kiṃ ca — and); (he) maghoni — O Uṣas, possessed of oblations; maghavadbhyaḥ — to the sacrificers who have food in the form of oblations; revat — so that they get wealth and the like; uccha — shine; sūnṛte — O best leader of men; jārayantī — [you who] make [all beings] old (cause decay); stotre — to the praising sacrificer; revat — so that he gets wealth; uccha — shine.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O goddess Uṣas, possessed of wealth in the form of oblations (to be given to us), awaken the sacrificers who give oblations; make those who perform no sacrifices and the like, the niggards, sleep on (the long sleep); (O you who make all grow old) shine so that those who have oblations and the like may obtain wealth.

Printed English (as printed): Awaken, wealth-abounding Ushas, those who delight (in holy offerings) : let the (niggard) traders, reluctant to wake (for such a purpose), sleep on. Arise, opulent Ushas, bearing wealth to the liberal (worshipper) : speaker of truth, who are the waster away (of living creatures), arise, bearing wealth to him who praises you.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 10.

pṛṇataḥ — havipradānasya yajamānān: "us who give oblations, the sacrificers" is the meaning. The word pṛṇāti is recorded in the Nirukta among the names of the acts of giving (Ni. 3-19, as read by the OCR; print "೩-೧೯"). And, citing

अध्वर्यवो यो दिव्यस्य वस्वो यः पार्थिवस्य क्षम्यस्य राजा । तमूर्दरं न पृणता यवेनेन्द्रं सोमेभिस्तदपो वो अस्तु ॥

adhvaryavo yo divyasya vasvo yaḥ pārthivasya kṣamyasya rājā | tamūrdaraṃ na pṛṇatā yavenendraṃ somebhistadapo vo astu ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-11, as read from the print.) — the author of the Nirukta explains in it the word pṛṇata as pūrayata, "fill"; here too the purport is the act of giving.

original p. 175

paṇayaḥ — vyavahārāsahiṣṇavo vaṇijaḥ: "traders (merchants) who cannot bear the spending" — thus Sāyaṇa explains it, and then cites the opinion of Yāska, paṇir vaṇig bhavatīti yāskaḥ. Paṇiḥ paṇanāt | vaṇik paṇyaṃ nenekti: the trader gets the name paṇi from his trading (paṇana), and because he always keeps his goods clean (pure) so that they may be fit for trade; and, citing

कदू महीरधृष्टा अस्य तविषीः कदु वृत्रघ्नो अस्तृतमस्ति । इन्द्रो विश्वान्बेकनाटाँ अहर्दृश उत क्रत्वा पणीरभि ॥

kadū mahīradhṛṣṭā asya taviṣīḥ kadu vṛtraghno astṛtamasti | indro viśvānbekanāṭā~ ahardṛśa uta kratvā paṇīrabhi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-66-10, as read from the print.) he explains the meaning of the word paṇi in (Ni. 6-26, as read) as paṇīṃś ca vaṇijaḥ [as printed]. In the present ṛk, Sāyaṇa explains: paṇaya iti lubdhakā abudhyamānā yāgādīn akurvāṇā adānaśīlā asmacchatravaḥ — "the paṇis are the niggardly, who are unaware, who do not perform sacrifices and the like, who do not give, our enemies". (The matter of the group of Asuras called the Paṇis was explained earlier.)

sūnṛte — suṣṭhu manuṣyāṇāṃ netrī: Uṣas is addressed as "the best leader of mankind". Sūnṛtā, sūnṛtāvatī, sūnṛtāvarī and the like are all epithets of Uṣas or synonyms (Ni. 3-19 [?]; as read by the OCR "३-१९"): sūnṛteti vāṅnāma | netrī ud-vādayitrī | uṣasaḥ svābhāvānantaraṃ hi paśupakṣimṛgādayaḥ sarve śabdaṃ kurvanti | ata eva tāsāṃ vācāṃ pravartayiteti ucyate. That is, the word sūnṛtā applies to all the usage of speech; because after the rising of Uṣas the speech-activities of all animals, birds and the rest begin, Uṣas is the originator of all of them. The Ṛṣis Kutsa and Vasiṣṭha use this epithet specially in their works. For example —

भास्वती नेत्री सूनृतानामचेति चित्रा वि दुरो न आवः । प्रार्प्या [?] जगद्व्यु नो रायो अख्यदुषा अजीगर्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥

bhāsvatī netrī sūnṛtānāmaceti citrā vi duro na āvaḥ | prārpyā [?] jagadvyu no rāyo akhyaduṣā ajīgarbhuvanāni viśvā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-14 [?], as read from the print.)

एषा नेत्री राधसः सूनृतानामुषा उच्छन्ती रिभ्यते वसिष्ठैः । दीर्घश्रुतं रयिमस्मे दधाना यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

eṣā netrī rādhasaḥ sūnṛtānāmuṣā ucchantī ribhyate vasiṣṭhaiḥ | dīrghaśrutaṃ rayimasme dadhānā yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-77-6 [?], as read from the print.) — in these and other ṛks Sāyaṇa has explained the word sūnṛtānām as stutīnāṃ netrī, "the leader of praises".

jārayantī — sarvaprāṇinaḥ kṣapayantī: "making all beings pass away (grow old)"; it is an epithet of Uṣas, in the sense of making all beings sleep.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). bodhaya — root budha avagamane; hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26) gives ṇic; loṭ second person singular after ṇijanta; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. uṣaḥ — vocative singular; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19) gives the nighāta [unaccented]. pṛṇataḥ — root pṛṇa prīṇane; Tudādi; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; accusative plural; since the case-ending follows a śatṛ without num, śatur anumo nadyajādī gives it the acute. maghoni — maghaṃ vanati saṃbhajate iti maghavān; śvanyuvamaghonām [print: "ಶ್ವನ್ನುಕ್ಷನ್", vanisanyoh?] (Uṇ. 1-157 as read) gives kanin to maghavan; when the feminine is intended, since it ends in n, ṅīp by ṛnnebhyo ṅīp; since it has the bha designation, śvayuvamaghonām atddhite gives saṃprasāraṇa, and saṃprasāraṇāc ca gives the pūrvarūpa; guṇa; in the vocative, ambārthanadyor hrasvaḥ, the shortening; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19) gives the nighāta. abudhyamānāḥ — na budhyamānāḥ abudhyamānāḥ; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2) gives the natural accent of the first member (the nañ). sasantu — root ṣasa svapne; Adādi; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ gives s; loṭ third person plural; nighāta after a non-verb word. revat — explained in the previous ṛk. uccha — root uchī vivāse; loṭ second person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. stotre — root ṣṭuñ stutau; tṛc in the agent sense; guṇa of the root-vowel; dative singular; udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt gives the acute accent to the case-ending. jārayantī — root jṛṣ vayohānau; since it shows the causative sense, hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26) gives ṇic; janīj̣ṛṣkṣnasuraṃjo 'mantāś ca [print: "ಜನೀಜೃಷ್ಕ್ನಸುರಂಜೋಮಂತಾಶ್ಚ"] …

Continuing the grammar of jārayantī, Ṛk 10: …since it has the marker mit, mitāṃ hrasvaḥ (Pā. 6-4-92, as read by the OCR) gives shortening to the vṛddhi that came by reason of ṇic; after the ṇijanta, śatṛ in the laṭ sense, śap; taking it as cause, guṇa and ay-substitution of ṇic; in the feminine, because of ugit, ṅīp; since the sārvadhātuka follows the upadeśa, it is unaccented, and the accent of the ṇic remains. ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

इयमुषा युवतिर्यौवनोपेतयोषित्स्थानीया । यद्वा । सर्वेषु भावेषु मिश्रयन्ती पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिश्यव अश्वैत् । अत्यर्थमागच्छति वर्धते वा । अत्रावशब्दो विनिग्रहार्थीयो न्येति विनिग्रहार्थीय इति यास्कोक्तत्वात् । नि. १-३ । तत्कथमवगम्यत इति तत्राह । इयमरुणानामरुणवर्णानां गवां प्रसिद्धानामेतन्नामकानामश्वानां वानीकं समूहं युङ्क्ते । रथे योजयति । अरुणो गाव उषसां श्यावाः सवितुः । नि. १-१५ [?] । इति । यथा लोके वाहनसंनाहं दृष्ट्वा प्रयाणमनुमीयते तथात्राप्यरुणरश्मीनामश्वानां दर्शनादुषा आगच्छतीत्यवसीयते । यद्वा । अरुणानां रश्मीनां समूहं युङ्क्ते । तथा नूनं निश्चयमेषा व्युच्छात् । तमो विवर्जयिष्यति । यत इयं गा युनक्ति अत एव कारणाद्यथा लोके ऽश्वसंनाहं दृष्ट्वा वीरो ऽनुमीयते तथात्रापीत्यर्थः । तादृशी सा सत्यसत्प्राये [?] नीरूपेऽन्तरिक्षे तिरोधायकत्वादशोभने तमसि वा केतुः [?]

Read from the image; the lines run on to p. 178. The OCR is garbled; doubtful readings are marked [?]. "This Uṣas is yuvatiḥ — in the position of a woman endowed with youth; or else, mingling in all existences, in the east she ava aśvait — comes exceedingly, or grows. Here the word ava has the sense of vinigraha (restraint — 'without hindrance'): 'ni, ava — [prefixes] of the sense of vinigraha', says Yāska (Ni. 1-3). 'How is this known?' — to that he says: she yokes the anīkam — the host — of the gavām — the red-coloured, well-known [cows], or of the horses of this name, to her chariot: 'the red ones, the cows of the Uṣases; the dark-coloured, of Savitṛ' (Ni. 1-15, as read by the OCR). As in the world, seeing the preparation of a vehicle, one infers that a journey is about to begin, so here, seeing the red rays — the horses — one concludes that Uṣas is coming. Or else she yokes a host of red rays. And thus, surely she will shine forth, will dispel the darkness; for since she harnesses the cows, for that very reason, as in the world one infers a hero from seeing the equipment of his horses, so here too — such a one, in the formless atmosphere that hides things, or in the unlovely darkness, is ketuḥ…"

…केतुस्थानीया ज्ञापयित्री प्रकर्षेण विविधं भासत इति शेषः । उपसर्गवशाद्योगक्रियाध्याहारः । यद्वा । असति तमोरूपेऽन्धकारे प्र केतुः प्रकर्षेण ज्ञापयित्री सती नूनं व्युच्छादिति पूर्वान्वयः । तस्मिन्काले आहवनीयादिरूपोऽग्निर्गृहं गृहं सर्वयजमानगृहमग्निहोत्राद्यर्थमुप तिष्ठाते । उपतिष्ठते । दीप्यत इत्यर्थः ॥

…ketusthānīyā jñāpayitrī prakarṣeṇa vividhaṃ bhāsata iti śeṣaḥ | upasargavaśādyogakriyādhyāhāraḥ | yadvā | asati tamorūpe 'ndhakāre pra ketuḥ prakarṣeṇa jñāpayitrī satī nūnaṃ vyucchāditi pūrvānvayaḥ | tasminkāle āhavanīyādirūpo 'gnirgṛhaṃ gṛhaṃ sarvayajamānagṛhamagnihotrādyarthamupa tiṣṭhāte | upatiṣṭhate | dīpyata ityarthaḥ ‖

"…[as] the banner (ketu), the informer: she shines forth in many ways; this is the remainder of the sentence. By the force of the prefix a verb of yoking is to be supplied. Or else: in the darkness that is not (asati), as the ketu — as the one who makes known — she will surely shine forth: this is joined with the preceding. At that time Agni, in the form of the Āhavanīya and the others, in every house (gṛhaṃ gṛham), in the house of every sacrificer, for the Agnihotra and the rest, upa tiṣṭhāte — is kindled: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Iyam — this Uṣas; yuvatiḥ — endowed with youth; purastāt — in the eastern quarter; ava aśvait — comes (grows); (iyam — she); aruṇānām gavām — of the red cows (the red rays); anīkam — the host; yuṅkte — yokes (to her chariot); nūnam — surely; asati — (because it makes objects invisible) in the unreal [the darkness], or in the formless atmosphere; pra ketuḥ — (as one who makes objects) known; vi ucchāt — (will) well dispel the darkness; (then) agniḥ — the fire (the Āhavanīya and the others); gṛhaṃ gṛham — in each and every house; upa tiṣṭhāte — is established.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. This Uṣas, like a young woman, rises in the east; (she) yokes to her chariot the horses called red cows (before the time of dawn the red rays become visible); dispelling the darkness she makes the objects that were covered by gloom to be seen; (at the time of Uṣas) in every house the Āhavanīya and other fires are kindled.

Printed English (as printed): This youthful (Ushas) approaches from the east: she harnesses her team of purple cows. Assuredly she will disperse the darkness, a manifest sign (of day) in the firmament: the (sacred) fire is kindled in every dwelling.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 11.

yuvatiḥ — yauvanopetayoṣit-sthānīyā; yadvā sarveṣu bhāveṣu miśrayantī: she is described as "a woman endowed with youth", or "one who mingles in all existences". As described in such ṛks as punaḥ punar jāyamānā purāṇī (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-10), Uṣas is "at one and the same time without beginning and eternal, and by the time of the creation of the world ever young" — this description is here also.

original p. 179

As described in statements such as divo duhitā bhānum aśret (1-92-5), in the same way as the rays of the Sun, uniting with Uṣas, spread everywhere and have contact with all the worlds, so Uṣas, with the Sun's rays, has contact with the world — this supports the second explanation.

ava aśvait — śvayatir gatyarthaḥ | atyartham āgacchati vardhate vā | atrāvaśabdo vinigrahārthīyaḥ | nyeti vinigrahārthīya iti yāskoktatvāt (Ni. 1-3, as printed). Here the prefix ava is joined to the root śvi ("to go; to grow"). Yāska says that the prefixes ni, ava are of the sense of vinigraha ("without restraint"). Looking at it broadly, in the usage ava aśvait / ny aśvait, a particular fixed motion or extension seems to be meant; but Sāyaṇa, in accordance with the context, explains ava aśvait as atyartham āgacchati — "she comes exceedingly", "she moves freely or has unobstructed growth", on the authority of the Nirukta. In this ṛk too, as in

पशून्न चित्रा सुभगा प्रथाना सिन्धुर्न क्षोद उर्विया व्यश्वैत् । अमिनती दैव्यानि व्रतानि सूर्यस्य चेति रश्मिभिर्दृशाना ॥

paśūnna citrā subhagā prathānā sindhurna kṣoda urviyā vyaśvait | aminatī daivyāni vratāni sūryasya ceti raśmibhirdṛśānā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-12, as printed.) — the sense stated before is that vi aśvait means sarvaṃ jagad vyāpnot, "she pervaded the whole world".

aruṇānāṃ gavām — prasiddhānām etannāmakānām aśvānāṃ vā (anīkam): "aruṇo gāva uṣasām" (Ni. 2-28 [?], as printed) — the vehicles of the Uṣases are red cows; for the Uṣases they are vehicles equivalent to horses; the meaning is that she joins a host of these to her chariot.

asati — asatprāye nirūpe 'ntarikṣe tirodhāyakatvāt aśobhane tamasi vā: "in the atmosphere that is as if non-existent, devoid of form, since it conceals, or in the unlovely darkness": the sense is either "in the atmosphere, which is without form and therefore not of the nature of being", or "in the darkness, which is of the nature of the unlovely".

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11, pp. 179–180; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). aśvait — root ṭuośvi gativṛddhyoḥ; in luṅ, because aṅ and caṅ are optional, śvayater (Pā. 3-1-…) [print: "ಶ್ಲೇಸಿಚ್"?] gives siC; since āgamānuśāsanam anityam, the augment iṭ does not occur; sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 7-2-1) gives vṛddhi to the root vowel; since iḍādi siC does not follow, hmyantakṣaṇa… (Pā. 7-2-5) the prohibition of vṛddhi does not apply; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 7-3-97) …

…gives that the īṭ augment does not occur for the ending; saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ [as printed "ಸ್ಕೋ ಸಂಯೋ"] elides the s; the augment aṭ to the stem; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. yuvatiḥ — the word yuvan; when the feminine is intended, yūnas tiḥ (Pā. 4-1-77, as printed "೪-೧-೭೭") gives ti; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya elides the n; final-acute by the suffix accent. purastāt — pūrvādharāvarāṇāṃ purdhavaś caiṣām (Pā. 5-3-39) gives astāti and pur for the base; first-syllable acute of the suffix. yuṅkte — root yujir yoge, with included causative sense; laṭ third person singular ta; e for ṭi; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam (Pā. 3-1-78) gives śnam; mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ; coḥ kuḥ gives the guttural k, and car; since it stands at the head of a pāda, no nighāta; final-acute by the suffix accent. anīkam — root ana prāṇane; anihṛṣibhyāṃ kic ca [print: "ಆನಿಹೃಷಿಭ್ಯಾಂ ಕಿಚ್ಚ", Uṇ. 4-?] gives īkan; ñnityādir nityam gives the first-syllable acute. ucchāt — root uchī vivāse; leṭ third person singular tip; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 3-4-97) elides the i; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94) gives aṭ; tiṅ-accent nighāta. asati — na sat asat tasmin asati; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2) gives the accent of the first member; locative singular. gṛhaṃgṛham — nityavīpsayoḥ (Pā. 8-1-4) gives doubling in the sense of repetition; since the latter has the designation āmreḍita, anudāttaṃ ca (Pā. 8-1-3) makes it entirely unaccented. upa tiṣṭhāte — root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; since the prefix upa is attached, upād devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇamitrakaraṇapathiṣu (Pā. 1-3-25) [as printed] gives ātmanepada; leṭ third person singular ta; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e gives e; leṭo 'ṭāṭau gives aṭ; nighāta accent. ‖ 11 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उत्ते वयश्चिद्वसतेरपप्तन्नरश्च ये पितुभाजो व्युष्टौ । अमा सते वहसि भूरि वाममुषो देवि दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥ १२ ॥

utte vayaścidvasaterapaptannaraśca ye pitubhājo vyuṣṭau | amā sate vahasi bhūri vāmamuṣo devi dāśuṣe martyāya ‖ 12 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उत् । ते । वयः । चित् । वसतेः । अपप्तन् । नरः । च । ये । पितुऽभाजः । विऽउष्टौ । अमा । सते । वहसि । भूरि । वामम् । उषः । देवि । दाशुषे । मर्त्याय ॥ १२ ॥

ut | te | vayaḥ | cit | vasateḥ | apaptan | naraḥ | ca | ye | pitu 'bhājaḥ | vi 'uṣṭau | amā | sate | vahasi | bhūri | vāmam | uṣaḥ | devi | dāśuṣe | martyāya ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

ते तव व्युष्टौ सत्यां वयश्चिद्वयांस्यपि पक्षिणोऽपि । चिदित्यपिशब्दार्थः निपातानामनेकार्थत्वात् । उच्चावचेष्वर्थेषु निपतन्तीति । नि. १-४ । इति यास्कोक्तत्वात् । वसतेर्निवासस्थानाद्वृक्षादेरूर्ध्वमपप्तन् । उत्पतन्ति । पूर्ववाक्ये गृहं गृहमुप तिष्ठाते इत्युक्तत्वात्तदपेक्षयाप्यपिशब्दः । किंच नरश्च मनुष्याश्च ये पितुभाजोऽन्नवन्तोऽन्नार्थिनः कृषिवाणिज्यादिकर्तारः स्वस्वव्यापारार्थमुन्मुखा अपप्तन् । गच्छन्ति । तथा मन्त्रान्तरम् । पद्वद्भिर्वयो पत [?] उत्पातयति पक्षिणः । ऋ. १-४८-५ [?] । इति । एवं सत्यां हे देवि देवनशीले उषोदेवते ऽमा गृहे देवयजनाख्ये सते तिष्ठते यजमानाय तदर्थम् । अमेति गृहनाम अमा दम इति तन्नामसु पठितत्वात् । यद्वा । अमा सह हूयमानेनाग्निना सह निवसते यजमानाय । अमा वसेताम् इत्यादौ सहार्थे प्रयोगात् । मर्त्याय मनुष्याय दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय भूरि वामं बहु शोभनं धनं वहसि । प्रापयसि ॥

te tava vyuṣṭau satyāṃ vayaścidvayāṃsyapi pakṣiṇo 'pi | cidityapiśabdārthaḥ nipātānāmanekārthatvāt | uccāvaceṣvartheṣu nipatantīti | ni. 1-4 | iti yāskoktatvāt | vasaternivāsasthānādvṛkṣāderūrdhvamapaptan | utpatanti | pūrvavākye gṛhaṃ gṛhamupa tiṣṭhāte ityuktatvāttadapekṣayāpyapiśabdaḥ | kiṃca naraśca manuṣyāśca ye pitubhājo 'nnavanto 'nnārthinaḥ kṛṣivāṇijyādikartāraḥ svasvavyāpārārthamunmukhā apaptan | gacchanti | tathā mantrāntaram | padvadbhirvayo pata [?] utpātayati pakṣiṇaḥ | ṛ. 1-48-5 [?] | iti | evaṃ satyāṃ he devi devanaśīle uṣodevate 'mā gṛhe devayajanākhye sate tiṣṭhate yajamānāya tadartham | ameti gṛhanāma amā dama iti tannāmasu paṭhitatvāt | yadvā | amā saha hūyamānenāgninā saha nivasate yajamānāya | amā vasetām ityādau sahārthe prayogāt | martyāya manuṣyāya dāśuṣe havirdattavate yajamānāya bhūri vāmaṃ bahu śobhanaṃ dhanaṃ vahasi | prāpayasi ‖

Read from the image; the quotation of "another mantra" in the middle is small in the print and its words and number are doubtful. "Te vyuṣṭau — when you have dawned, the birds (vayaś cit, even the birds; cit has the sense of api, since particles have many senses: 'they fall in high and low senses', Ni. 1-4) ut apaptan — fly up from their dwelling-places, the trees and so on. Since it was said in the previous sentence gṛhaṃ gṛham upa tiṣṭhāte, the word api is used with reference to it. And moreover naraś ca — men, who are pitubhājaḥ — seeking food, doing farming, trade and the like — rise eagerly each for his own business; they go. As another mantra [says]: '… he makes the birds fly up' (Ṛ. 1-48-5 [?]). Such being so, O goddess, shining Uṣas, to the sacrificer who sits amā — in the house called the sacrificial ground — for that purpose (amā is a name for 'house': amā, dama are read among its names); or else amā — together with the fire that is being offered to, who dwells with the fire (as amā vasetām and the like, where the word is used in the sense of 'together') — to the mortal dāśuṣe — the sacrificer who has given oblations — you bring bhūri vāmam — much beautiful wealth."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Uṣaḥ — O goddess Uṣas; te — your; vyuṣṭau — at the dawning; ye vayaḥ cit — even all the birds; vasateḥ — from their dwelling-place, the nests; ut apaptan — fly up; naraḥ ca — and men; pitubhājaḥ — seeking food (they go out of their houses); devi — O goddess (you); amā sate — who is in the sacrificial hall (with the fire); dāśuṣe — who is minded to give oblations; martyāya — to the sacrificer; bhūri vāmam — abundant and auspicious wealth; vahasi — you bring.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O goddess Uṣas, as soon as you have risen, birds and men go out from their dwellings, seeking food (each for his own needs); and (you) bring abundant wealth to the sacrificer who wishes to give oblations, who is with the (kindled) fire in the sacrificial hall.

Printed English (as printed): At your dawning, (Ushas), the various birds rise up from their nests, and men who have to earn their bread (quit their homes). you bring, divine (Ushas), much wealth to the liberal mortal who is present in the chamber (of sacrifice).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 12.

vayaś cit — "even the birds": cit here is said to have the sense of api. The author of the Nirukta records the word vayaḥ only among the names of food (Ni. 3-9 [?], as printed "೩-೯"); but this word has still other meanings:

प्र सीमादित्यो असृजद्विधर्ता ऋतं सिन्धवो वरुणस्य यन्ति । न श्राम्यन्ति न वि मुचन्त्येते वयो न पप्तू रघुया परिज्मन् ॥

pra sīmādityo asṛjadvidhartā ṛtaṃ sindhavo varuṇasya yanti | na śrāmyanti na vi mucantyete vayo na paptū raghuyā parijman ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-4, as read from the print.) — in this and other ṛks, because of rapid movement, the word vayaḥ is used as a synonym of "bird";

तदिन्द्र प्रेव वीर्यं चकर्थ यत्स्नसन्तं [?] वज्रेणाबोधयोऽहिम् । अनु त्वा पत्नीर्हृषितं वयश्च विश्वे देवासो अमदन्ननु त्वा ॥

tadindra preva vīryaṃ cakartha yatsnasantaṃ [?] vajreṇābodhayo 'him | anu tvā patnīrhṛṣitaṃ vayaśca viśve devāso amadannanu tvā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-103-2, as read from the print; "snasantaṃ" doubtful.) — in this ṛk, "gantṛtvāt pakṣisādṛśyād vā maruto 'tra vaya ucyante" (the Maruts are here called vayaḥ because of their going or because of their likeness to birds) — the word vayaḥ is used as a synonym of "Maruts", because of the likeness to birds. Likewise meanings such as "strength" and "life" are current; and —

योनिष्ट इन्द्र निषदे अकारि तमा नि षीद स्वानो नार्वा । विमुच्या वयोऽवसायाश्वान्दोषा वस्तोर्वसतीयसः प्रपित्वे ॥

yoniṣṭa indra niṣade akāri tamā ni ṣīda svāno nārvā | vimucyā vayo 'vasāyāśvāndoṣā vastorvasatīyasaḥ prapitve ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-104-1, as read from the print.) — here vayaḥ means "the reins for tying the horses (aśvabandhanārthān raśmīn)". In the present ṛk, as in the common usage, it means "birds".

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अस्तोढ्वं स्तोम्या ब्रह्मणा मे अवीवृधध्वमुशतीरुषासः । युष्माकं देवीरवसा सनेम सहस्रिणं च शतिनं च वाजम् ॥ १३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

एवं सूक्तद्वयोक्तरीत्या बहुधा स्तुत्वा तां च स्तुतिमनया निवेद्य स्वाभीष्टं प्रार्थयते । हे स्तोम्याः । स्तोमः स्तोत्रं तदर्हन्तीति स्तोम्याः स्तुत्यर्हा उषसः । यतो यूयं तादृश्यः अतो मे मत्संबन्धिभूतेन ब्रह्मणा सूक्तद्वयगतमन्त्ररूपेण स्तोत्रेणास्तोढ्वम् । स्तुता भवत । किंच हे उषासः उषसः उशतीः स्तोतॄन्मां अस्मत्समृद्धिं वा कामयमाना यूयमवीवृधध्वम् । अस्मान्वर्धयत । किंच हे देवीर्देव्यो देवनशीलाः युष्माकमवसा युष्मत्संबन्धिना रक्षणेन वयं सहस्रिणं सहस्रसंख्याकमभीष्टं धनं सनेम । लभेमहि । तथा शतिनं च वाजं शतसंख्याकमपरिमितं धनं सनेम । युष्मद्रक्षणेन शतसहस्रपरिमितधनादिरूपरक्षणेन वयमपि अर्थिभ्यः शतसहस्रपरिमितस्य धनस्य सनितारो भवेमेत्यर्थः ॥

evaṃ sūktadvayoktarītyā bahudhā stutvā tāṃ ca stutimanayā nivedya svābhīṣṭaṃ prārthayate | he stomyāḥ | stomaḥ stotraṃ tadarhantīti stomyāḥ stutyarhā uṣasaḥ | yato yūyaṃ tādṛśyaḥ ato me matsaṃbandhibhūtena brahmaṇā sūktadvayagatamantrarūpeṇa stotreṇāstoḍhvam | stutā bhavata | kiṃca he uṣāsaḥ uṣasaḥ uśatīḥ stotṝnmāṃ asmatsamṛddhiṃ vā kāmayamānā yūyamavīvṛdhadhvam | asmānvardhayata | kiṃca he devīrdevyo devanaśīlāḥ yuṣmākamavasā yuṣmatsaṃbandhinā rakṣaṇena vayaṃ sahasriṇaṃ sahasrasaṃkhyākamabhīṣṭaṃ dhanaṃ sanema | labhemahi | tathā śatinaṃ ca vājaṃ śatasaṃkhyākamaparimitaṃ dhanaṃ sanema | yuṣmadrakṣaṇena śatasahasraparimitadhanādirūparakṣaṇena vayamapi arthibhyaḥ śatasahasraparimitasya dhanasya sanitāro bhavemetyarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the last sentence is small in the print, and the OCR is garbled there. "Having thus praised in many ways in the manner stated in the two sūktas, and having offered that praise, he now prays for his own desire with this [ṛk]. O stomyāḥ — stoma is praise; those who deserve it are stomyāḥ, worthy of praise, Uṣases; since you are such, therefore be praised (astoḍhvam) by my brahman — the praise in the form of the mantras contained in the two sūktas. Moreover, O Uṣases, desiring me, the praisers (uśatīḥ), or our prosperity, you have made us grow (avīvṛdhadhvam). And, O goddesses, with your protection, we would win (sanema) a thousandfold (sahasriṇam) wealth that we desire — we would obtain it; likewise a hundredfold (śatinam) wealth, measureless: may we, through your protection that takes the form of hundred-thousand-measured wealth and the like, become winners of a hundred-thousand measure of wealth for those who ask: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (He) stomyāḥ — O praiseworthy goddess Uṣases; me — my; brahmaṇā — by the mantra (in the two sūktas); astoḍhvam — be praised; (he) uṣāsaḥ — O goddess Uṣases; uśatīḥ — desiring (our prosperity, or us, your praisers); avīvṛdhadhvam — make [us] grow; he devīḥ — O goddesses; yuṣmākam — your; avasā — with protection (being so endowed, we); śatinaṃ ca sahasriṇaṃ ca — hundred-fold and thousand-fold; vājam — wealth; sanema — may we obtain.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O praised goddess Uṣases, praised by our mantras (the two sūktas), desiring only our growth, make us grow; protected by you may we obtain immeasurable wealth (by your favour).

Printed English (as printed): Praiseworthy Ushasas, be glorified by this (my) hymn ; graciously disposed towards us, augment (our prosperity); and may we obtain, goddesses, through your favour, wealth, a hundred and a thousand fold.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 13.

brahmaṇā — sūktadvayagatamantrarūpeṇa stotreṇa: "by praise in the form of mantras contained in the two sūktas": the sūkta before this (1-123) and the present one are both included, and are in the form of mantras: "by praise" is the meaning given.

The word brahma has many meanings. This word is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 3-9, as printed) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 [?], as printed "೨-೧೦"?); besides these it has also been used as a synonym of stotra (praise) and karma (rite).

ब्रह्मा कृणोति वरुणो गातुविदं तमीमहे । व्यूर्णोति हृदा मतिं नव्यो जायतामृतं विश्वं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥

brahmā kṛṇoti varuṇo gātuvidaṃ tamīmahe | vyūrṇoti hṛdā matiṃ navyo jāyatāmṛtaṃ viśvaṃ me asya rodasī ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-15 [?], as read from the print.) — in this ṛk brahma is explained as "an act in the form of protection" (karma), thus: "a rite". The author of the Nirukta too, citing

यामथर्वा मनुष्पिता दध्यङ्धियमत्नत । तस्मिन्ब्रह्माणि पूर्वथेन्द्र उक्था समग्मतार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम् ॥

yāmatharvā manuṣpitā dadhyaṅdhiyamatnata | tasminbrahmāṇi pūrvathendra ukthā samagmatārcannanu svarājyam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-16, as read from the print.) explains brahmāṇi as "rites" (karmāṇi). And —

अन्यं दिवो मातरिश्वा जभारामथ्नादन्यं परि श्येनो अद्रेः । अग्नीषोमा ब्रह्मणा वावृधानोरुं यज्ञाय चक्रथुरु लोकम् ॥

anyaṃ divo mātariśvā jabhārāmathnādanyaṃ pari śyeno adreḥ | agnīṣomā brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānoruṃ yajñāya cakrathuru lokam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-93-6, as read from the print.) — here it is explained as mantrarūpeṇa stotreṇa haviḥ-lakṣaṇenānnena vā — "by praise in the form of a mantra, or by food in the form of oblation". In the present ṛk it is evident that the meaning is "by praise in the form of mantras".

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 13, pp. 186–187; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). astoḍhvam — root ṣṭuñ stutau; luṅ in the passive, second person plural, the ending dhvam; with it as cause, guṇa of the root-vowel; the augment aṭ; iṇaḥ ṣīdhvaṃluṅliṭāṃ dho 'ṅgāt (Pā. 8-3-78) gives the cerebral ḍha for the dh; since it stands at the head of a pāda, no nighāta; since the augment is acute, the first syllable is acute. stomyāḥ — stomam arhanti iti stomyāḥ; yat in the sense of "worthy"; in the vocative, āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19) gives the nighāta. avīvṛdhadhvam — root vṛdhu vṛddhau; the causative sense gives ṇic by hetumati ca; luṅ in the sense of loṭ in the Veda after ṇyanta; second person plural, dhvam; ṇiśrisrukubhyaḥ kartari caṅ gives caṅ for cli; caṅi gives doubling of the root; here, since ṛd-ṛt … (Pā. 7-4-7) prescribes just ṛ for the penultimate ṛ, guṇa does not arise though it is internal; when doubling has occurred, the initial consonant remains; sanvallaghuni (Pā. 7-4-93) gives sanvadbhāva, and sanyataḥ (Pā. 7-4-79) gives i to the reduplicative syllable; dīrgho laghoḥ (Pā. 7-4-94) lengthens it; ṇeraniṭi elides the ṇic; the augment aṭ; no nighāta because it stands at the head of a pāda; first-syllable acute from the acute augment.

uśatīḥ — root vaś kāntau; when āṭ ("vaś" with the augment) comes, vaś is replaced by uś [as printed "ವಶ್ ... ಉಶ್"]; ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ gives luk of śap; sārvadhātukam apit: since the śatṛ suffix is [treated as] cit, grahijyāvayi… (Pā. 6-1-16) gives saṃprasāraṇa with pūrvarūpa; ugitaś ca gives ṅīp; since ṅīp follows a śatṛ without num, śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173) gives it the acute; accusative plural. uṣāsaḥ — with jas following, a long vowel in the Saṃhitā in the Veda. devīḥ — the word devī; in the vocative plural, supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39) gives lengthening by the preceding savarṇa; āmantritasya ca gives the nighāta. avasā — root ava rakṣaṇe; asun by sarvadhātubhya asun; since it has the marker n, first-syllable acute; instrumental singular. sanema — root ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ gives s for the initial; vidhiliṅ first person plural; since it follows a non-verb word, the nighāta accent. sahasriṇam, śatinam — the suffix ini in the sense of possession; the first-syllable acute of the suffix; accusative singular. ‖ 13 ‖
