॥ भूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, from the Sāyaṇa text):

प्रातारत्नमिति सप्तर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तं काक्षीवतम् । दानस्य स्तूयमानत्वाद्दानदेवत्यं यातेनोच्यते [?] सा देवता । अनु. २-५ [?] । इति परिभाषितत्वात् । त्रैष्टुभम् । उपेत्यादिके द्वे जगत्यौ । प्रातारत्नं सप्त सैनयस्य दानस्तुतिस्त्रिष्टुप्जगत्यावित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥

prātāratnamiti saptarcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktaṃ kākṣīvatam | dānasya stūyamānatvāddānadevatyaṃ yātenocyate [?] sā devatā | anu. 2-5 [?] | iti paribhāṣitatvāt | traiṣṭubham | upetyādike dve jagatyau | prātāratnaṃ sapta sainayasya dānastutistriṣṭupjagatyāvityanukramaṇikā ‖

Read from the image; "yā tenocyate sā devatā" is the Anukramaṇī's rule, with the reference "Anu. 2-5" as read by the OCR; the print's numerals are not clear. "Prātā ratnam — the fifth sūkta, of seven ṛks, of Kākṣīvata (Kakṣīvat). Since gift (dāna) is what is praised, the deity is dāna (the gift): 'that which is said by it, that is the deity' (Anukramaṇī rule). Triṣṭubh; the two beginning with upa are Jagatī. Prātā ratnam — seven; the praise of the gift of Sainya; Triṣṭubh and Jagatī — thus the Anukramaṇī." The Kannada Anuvāda and the Ṛṣi–Devatā–Chandas table of Sūkta 125 are on p. 188.

original p. 188

Anuvāda (Kannada). This Sūkta, beginning prātā ratnam, is the fifth Sūkta in the eighteenth Anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija. Since this Sūkta contains praise of a gift, its deity is said to be dānastuti, "praise of the gift": for the Anukramaṇī says yā tenocyate sā devatā (Anu. 2-5 as read by the OCR; print "೨-೫"), that is, "whatever subject is spoken of in the ṛks, that is the deity of that sūkta". The metre is Triṣṭubh; the two ṛks beginning upa (4–5) are of Jagatī metre; the remaining ṛks are Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said "prātā ratnaṃ sapta svanayasya dānastutis triṣṭup jagatyau."

सूक्त—१२५ — Sūkta 125

मण्डल—१ ‖ अनुवाक—१८ ‖ सूक्त—१२५ ‖ अष्टक—२ ‖ अध्याय—१ ‖ वर्ग—१० ‖ (Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 18; Sūkta 125; Aṣṭaka 2; Adhyāya 1; Varga 10.)

Number of ṛks in this Sūkta — 7. Ṛṣi — Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija. Devatā — Svanaya's dānastuti ("praise of the gift of Svanaya"). Chandas — Triṣṭubh; 4–5 Jagatī.

The first part of the bhāṣya, down to the list of gifts, is given as read; the list of gifts and the remaining ten lines of this long itihāsa passage are in very small type and not clear, so I do not transcribe them letter by letter here; their sense is given by the Kannada Anuvāda on pp. 191–192 and by the Bṛhaddevatā verses quoted on p. 193, which are clear. This is flagged as an open item. "Here they tell an itihāsa. The seer named Kakṣīvān, the son of Dīrghatamas, having lived long in the guru's house for the study of the Veda, having thoroughly learned the Vedas and performed the vows, and with his leave about to set out again for his own home, rested on the way at night. In the morning Svanaya, the son of Bhāvayavya, a king, sporting with his attendants, suddenly came near Kakṣīvat. He, waking quickly, rose at once. The king took him by the hand, seated him on his own seat, and seeing his beauty, with a mind to give him a maiden, asked: 'Sir, whose son are you, and what is your name?' Questioned, he told of his mother and father and his own story. The king, understanding that he was a worthy person, glad at heart, taking him to his house, honoured him with the madhuparka, with clothes, garlands and the like, and gave him ten maidens, … a hundred niṣkas, a hundred horses, a hundred bulls, … and eleven chariots. And he, receiving all this in order, came to Dīrghatamas and showed it to him."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Prātaḥ itvā — (the king called Svanaya) having come in the morning (to his own presence); ratnam — jewels and the like; prātaḥ — at the time of daybreak; dadhāti — places (in the presence of Kakṣīvat); tam — all that (offered); cikitvān — knowing it to be unfaulty; pratigṛhya — having accepted; ni dhatte — places it (in the presence of his father); (then) tena — by that (gift of the father); prajām — offspring (sons, servants and the like); vardhayamānaḥ — nourishing; āyuḥ — (of long) life; suvīraḥ — with excellent heroic sons; rāyaḥ poṣeṇa — with the growth of wealth; sacate — (he himself) is united.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The jewels and the like offered in the morning (by King Svanaya), (Kakṣīvat) understanding them to be faultless, accepts, offers them to his father; (then) nourishing sons, servants and the like with the wealth (given by the father), he is long-lived, with good offspring, and endowed with wealth.

Printed English (as printed): Having come in the early morning, (Swanaya) presents precious (wealth), knowing it (to be worthy of acceptance); and having, (therefore) accepted it, (Kashivat) brings it (to his father); wherewith the parent of excellent sons, maintaining his progeny, passes his life in the enjoyment of affluence.

…the name of the king; they are in praise of the gifts that he gave in abundance to Kakṣīvat. In this context Sāyaṇa tells the itihāsa of this in the manner given above (dairghatamasaḥ kakṣīvān nāma … dānam iti prasiddham, the itihāsa of p. 189).

The ṛṣi-youth named Kakṣīvat, the son of Dīrghatamas, after completing his study of the Veda in the guru's house in the life of a brahmacārin, and performing all the vows there, and receiving the leave of his guru, as he was returning to his own home, rested in the middle of the road, slept at night; in the morning, Svanaya, the son of Bhāvayavya, sporting with his attendants, suddenly came near Kakṣīvat. Waking, he quickly rose. Then the king took his hand, seated him on his own seat, and, understanding that he was a youth full of beauty, wishing to give him his daughter, honoured him, and asked who he was and whose son. Kakṣīvat told the whole of his story at length. Then Svanaya, taking him to his house, prepared the madhuparka, honoured him with clothes, garlands and the like, and gave him chariots, a hundred gold ornaments, a hundred horses, a hundred bulls, a thousand and sixty cows, and eleven chariots (as the Kannada reads it), and gave him his ten daughters in marriage. Then Kakṣīvat received all this in order, went to his father Dīrghatamas, and showed the king's gifts to him.

Here a difficulty arises. Kakṣyā means "the rope that ties a horse": kakṣyā rajjū raśvasya [as read, "kakṣyā rajjur aśvasya"] (Ni. 2-2 as read by the OCR). Because he has such a rope, Kakṣīvat gets the name kakṣīvān or kakṣyāvān. Horses, and the ropes that tie horses, are things useful to kings; so these belong to kings. There is no reason for them to be with a Brahmin. Since these ropes were with Kakṣīvat, he must have been a Kṣatriya. For a Kṣatriya, acceptance of gifts (pratigraha) is not a duty — as said in

याजनाध्यापने चैव विशुद्धाच्च प्रतिग्रहः ।

yājanādhyāpane caiva viśuddhācca pratigrahaḥ |

(Manu 10-76, as read by the OCR.) that is, of the six duties of a Brahmin — study, teaching, sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, giving, and receiving gifts — a Kṣatriya or Vaiśya has authority only in three: sacrificing, studying, and giving. In the other three — officiating as priest for others, teaching the Veda to others, and receiving what is given — he has no authority.

Therefore how is Kakṣīvat, being a Kṣatriya, qualified to accept the gift given by Svanaya? Is this not improper? To answer this, Sāyaṇa narrates the birth of Kakṣīvat.

The king named Kaliṅga had no children; he was old and unable to beget a son. Then the ṛṣi named Dīrghatamas, the son of Ucathya, came into the presence of the king, and the king, having no children, begged him to beget a son on the queen. In former times there was a custom by which, for various reasons, the childless obtained children for the increase of the line from a suitable Brahmin; this matter is clearly described in the Purāṇas and in the Mahābhārata. The ṛṣi accepted the king's request, and the king told his chief queen to go to the ṛṣi. The queen, being old and ugly, was ashamed to cohabit with the ṛṣi, and in her place she sent to the ṛṣi her own maid, a woman named Uśik, beautifully adorned with her own clothes and ornaments. The ṛṣi, understanding that the woman who had come to him, Uśik, was not the queen but her maid, sprinkled her with mantra-purified water, made her a ṛṣi's wife, purified her, and consorted with her. The son born to the ṛṣi by that woman Uśik is the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān. Although this son was born of a Kṣatriya woman, he is counted a Brahmin through the connection with the Brahmin. Thus although Kakṣīvat has connection with Kṣatriyas, because he was born of a Brahmin there is no obstacle to his being qualified to accept gifts. The story of the birth of this Kakṣīvat will be explained in the commentary on the Ṛk Saṃhitā 1-116th Sūkta [as read; the numerals are small — "೧-೧೧೬ನೆಯ"], earlier.

In this Sūkta and in the next Sūkta the praise of Svanaya's gift is stated. But since the Anukramaṇī says that Kakṣīvat, delighted with the gift, praised Bhāvayavya (Svanaya's father), it is natural for the doubt to arise whether two different persons are praised. That in the first ṛk of the next Sūkta it is clearly said adhi kṣiyato bhāvyasya strengthens this doubt still more. But calling the son by the father's name is often customary: in the Veda itself, when speaking of the Maruts, who are Rudra's sons, the name of the father is used, rudrāsaḥ; and in that very Sūkta, in the third ṛk, svanayena dattāḥ is also said. Therefore, although the names of father and son are used here, these two Sūktas are to be understood as the praise of the gift of one and the same person.

Read letter by letter from the clear Latin-spaced print; the third and fourth lines of the sixth verse and the first word of the penultimate verse are doubtful and I do not complete them. "Having acquired learning from his guru, Kakṣīvat, going to his own home, tired on the road, slept in a forest region. King Svanaya, the son of Bhāvayavya, going about for sport with his followers, with his wife and his priest, saw him. Seeing him endowed with beauty, like a son of the gods, he decided to give him a maiden, there being no obstacle of class or lineage. Addressing him, he asked about his class and lineage. 'O king, I am of the Aṅgirases,' replied the youth. 'I am the son of the seer Dīrghatamas, son of Ucathya, O king.' Then he gave him ten maidens decked with ornaments, and as many four-yoked chariots and horses …, wealth, base metal, goats and sheep for the maidens' conveyance, a hundred niṣkas, a hundred bulls: this is stated by the next sūkta in 'a hundred' (śatam) and so on: a hundred horses, a hundred niṣkas, ten chariots with the brides, and a thousand and sixty cows, four-yoked. Kakṣīvat, receiving [all this] from Svanaya, the son of Bhāvayavya, praised [him] and told it in the morning to his father."

Sāyaṇa has told this very story as his source, so its translation need not be given again.

prātar itvā — prātar eva ātmanaḥ sakāśam āgataḥ san: "having come at daybreak to his own presence", at the time of sunrise, to his presence.

rāyas-poṣeṇa — dhanānāṃ punaḥ punar vardhanena: "by the repeated increase of riches": since the wealth formerly held increases more and more.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सुगुरसत्सुहिरण्यः स्वश्वो बृहदस्मे वय इन्द्रो दधाति । यस्त्वायन्तं वसुना प्रातरित्वो मुक्षीजयेव पदिमुत्सिनाति ॥ २ ॥

सुऽगुः । असत् । सुऽहिरण्यः । सुऽअश्वः । बृहत् । अस्मै । वयः । इन्द्रः । दधाति । यः । त्वा । आऽयन्तम् । वसुना । प्रातःऽइत्वः । मुक्षीजयाऽइव । पदिम् । उत्ऽसिनाति ॥ २ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अत्र कक्षीवतः पित्रानीतेन धनेन संतुष्टो राजानं बहुप्रकारेणाशास्ते । असौ स्वनयो राजा सुगुरसत् । शोभनैर्बहुभिर्गोभिस्तद्वान्भवतु । तथा सुहिरण्यः सुष्ठु हितरमणीयैर्हिरण्यैस्तद्वान्भवतु । तथा स्वश्वः शोभनैरश्वैस्तद्वान्सन् अस्मै राज्ञे प्रदात्रे बृहत्प्रभूतं वयोऽन्नमिन्द्रः परमेश्वरो धर्मदेवता दधाति । दधातु । ददातु । यतोऽयं राजा गोहिरण्याश्वान्नानि बहुसंख्याकानि दत्तवान् अतस्तेषामभिवृद्धिप्रार्थनोचितैव । कस्यैवमाशीरिति तदुच्यते । यः यो राजा प्रातरित्वः प्रातरागामिन्यतिथौ पुत्रे [?] आयन्तं गुरुकुलादागतं पदिं पथिकं यदृच्छयागन्तारं त्वा त्वां वसुना अन्नसाधनेन गवादिधनेनोत्सिनाति । गमनत उत्क्षिप्तं बध्नाति । गतिं निरुणद्धीत्यर्थः । प्रतिबन्धे दृष्टान्त उच्यते । मुक्षीजयेव पदिम् । मुच्यमानासती बन्धनं जनयतीति मुक्षीजा मृगपक्ष्यादिबन्धनी रज्जुः । तया पाशको यथा पदिं गन्तारं मृगपक्ष्यादिकमुत्सिनाति बध्नाति तथा मयानुज्ञातमपि त्वां गमनतः प्रतिबध्य गवादिप्रदानादिना यो राजा तोषयति स एवं भवतीति । पदिरिति पदव्याचक्षाणेन यास्केन तदुदाहरणमयं मन्त्रो व्याख्यातः । सुगुर्भवति तेनाह्वेति [?] । नि. ५-१९ ॥

Read from the image; the last sentence — the Nirukta citation — is small and doubtful, and the OCR is garbled. The Nirukta number is as printed "५-१९"/"೫-೧೯" and as the OCR reads it. "Here Kakṣīvat's father, pleased with the wealth brought, blesses the king in many ways. May this King Svanaya be suguḥ — rich in many beautiful cows; likewise suhiraṇyaḥ — rich in lovely, beneficial gold; likewise svaśvaḥ — rich in good horses; and being so, may Indra — the supreme lord, the deity of dharma — dadhāti, 'bestow' (let him bestow, let him give) upon this king, the giver, bṛhat — abundant — vayaḥ, food. Since this king has given a great number of cows, gold, horses and food, a prayer for their increase is proper. Whose is such a blessing? That is said: yaḥ — the king who, to you, prātaritvaḥ — who came at daybreak as a guest, āyantam — arriving from the guru's house, padim — a traveller, one who came by chance — tvā — you — with vasunā, wealth in the form of cows and so on that serve as food, utsināti — fastens up, ties, stops; that is, he arrests the going. The illustration of the arresting is given: mukṣījayeva padim — mukṣījā is the snare, the rope for binding animals and birds, that, when loosed, creates the binding; as the fowler with it binds the animal or bird that goes, the padi, so he who, though permitted by me, stops you from going and pleases you with gifts of cows and the like, is such a king. Yāska has explained this mantra as the example, explaining the word padi (Ni. 5-19)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Prātaritvaḥ — (O son, Kakṣīvat) who came in the early morning; āyantam — arriving (from the guru's house); padim — a traveller; tvā — you; vasunā — with wealth such as cows (which is the means of food); mukṣījā iva padim — as one binds a living creature with a snare that binds; yaḥ — which king; utsināti — stops (hinders from going further); (saḥ — that king); suguḥ — one with excellent cows; suhiraṇyaḥ — with auspicious gold; svaśvaḥ — with fine horses; asat — may he be; asmai — (the giver) to this king; indraḥ — Indra; bṛhat — much; vayaḥ — food; dadhāti — may he bestow.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O son, the king who has stopped you, who were coming in the morning from the guru's house, with gifts of cows and the like — as one binds a living creature with a snare — may that king be endowed with excellent cows, horses and gold; may Indra bestow abundant food on him.

Printed English (as printed): May he (the Raja) be rich in cows, in gold, in horses : may Indra grant abundant food to him who delays thee, returning home in the early morning, by costly gifts, as (a hunter arrests the) wandering (animals) by his snares.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.

अथ कक्षीवतः पिता आनीतेन धनेन संतुष्टः राजानं बहुप्रकारेण आशास्ते ।

atha kakṣīvataḥ pitā ānītena dhanena saṃtuṣṭaḥ rājānaṃ bahuprakāreṇa āśāste |

"Then Kakṣīvat's father, pleased at the wealth brought by him, blesses the king in many ways." Seeing the riches given by Svanaya, Kakṣīvat's father is greatly pleased and blesses Svanaya in many ways. In this ṛk the order of the blessing is shown. For this ṛk the author of the Nirukta gives this explanation:

सुगुर्भवति सुहिरण्यः स्वश्वो महच्चास्मै वय इन्द्रो दधाति यस्त्वा यन्तमन्नेन प्रातरागामिनमतिथे । मुक्षीजयेव पदिमुत्सिनाति कुमारः । मुक्षीजा मोचनाच्च स्यनाच्च ततनाच्च ॥

"As a boy with a snare-like means arrests the going of a bird, so the king who has stopped you, who came at daybreak as a guest, by wealth such as gold and the like, as a means, and made you his own — to such a king may Indra give still more, possessions of cattle, gold and the like": that is the idea.

suguḥ asat — śobhanair bahubhir gobhis tadvān bhavatu: "may he be possessed of many fine cows"; the meaning is that he may obtain still more excellent cows.

prātaritva — prātar āgāmin atithe putra: "O son, who came as a guest in the morning, returning from the guru's house": the son, Kakṣīvat, is addressed. From the root i, which means "to go", the word itvan is formed, "he who goes" or "he who comes"; prātaritvan means "one who is to come in the morning, who is to go forward". In this ṛk and in the preceding ṛk the word prātaritvan is an epithet of both Kakṣīvat and Svanaya: Svanaya came in the morning to Kakṣīvat, and Kakṣīvat arrived as a guest in the morning.

padim — padiḥ padagantur bhavati yat padyate (Ni. 5-19 [?], as printed): since he goes (travels), the one who moves is called padi.

mukṣījayā iva — mucyamānā satī bandhanaṃ janayatīti mukṣījā mṛgapakṣyādibandhanī rajjuḥ: a net that, when thrown down, binds animals, birds and the like. Mukṣījā mocanāc ca syanāc ca tatanāc ca (the Nirukta, as printed): the net gets the name mukṣījā from being thrown down, or from being cast on the ground, or from being spread out on the ground.

utsināti — uddhṛtya sināti | badhnāti: "he binds"; on the road he stopped the journey by attracting him with riches such as gold; therefore he bound him: that is the purport. Wealth such as gold is compared to the snare, and Kakṣīvat to birds and the like.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). suguḥ — śobhanāḥ gāvaḥ yasya saḥ; gostriyor upasarjanasya (Pā. 1-2-48) gives the shortening; eca ig hrasvādeśe gives the u for the shortened vowel; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the final-acute of the latter member. asat — root as bhuvi; leṭ third person singular tip; itaś ca lopaḥ (Pā. 3-4-97) elides the final i; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94) gives aṭ; luk of śap; tiṅ-nighāta.

suhiraṇyaḥ — śobhanaṃ hiraṇyaṃ yasya saḥ; as before, nañsubhyām gives the final-acute of the latter member. dadhāti — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; leṭ third person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. āyantam — prefix ā, root iṇ gatau; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; iṇo yaṇ (Pā. 6-4-81) gives yaṇ for the i; first-syllable acute of the suffix; accusative singular; the accent of the final member in the compound. prātaritvaḥ — explained in the previous mantra; vocative, āmantritasya ca gives the nighāta. utsināti — root ṣiñ bandhane; Kryādi; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ gives s for the initial; laṭ third person singular tip; kryādibhyaḥ śnā; since yaḥ [the relative] is connected, there is no nighāta; the accent of the verb-suffix remains. ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

प्रातः पूर्वेद्युः प्रभातकालेऽयं धनं दत्तवान् तस्मिन्नेव काले सुकृतं शोभनस्य कर्तारं त्वामिच्छन् प्राप्तुमिच्छन् कदा द्रक्ष्यामीति कामयमानोऽहं मद्यात्मिन्नि [?] इदानीमायम् । प्राप्तोऽस्मि । अत्र यद्यपि केवलं प्रातरित्येव श्रुतं न पूर्वेद्युरिति तथाप्यद्येत्यायमित्युक्तत्वादर्थात्पूर्वेद्युः प्रातरिति गम्यते । कीदृशं । इष्टेरिष्टस्येष्टसाधनस्य यागस्य वा पुत्रं पुरु त्रातारं । पुत्रः पुरु त्रायते । नि. २-११ । इति यास्कः । कर्तारमित्यर्थः । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । वसुमता रथेन समृद्धधनवता रथेन साधनेन । यद्वा तेन सहेति सहार्थे तृतीया । किंच मदानीतेन समृद्धेन धनेनांशोर्वल्लीरूपस्य मत्सरस्य मादनसाधनस्य सोमस्य । मत्सरः सोमो मन्दतेः स्तृप्तिकर्मण इति निरुक्तम् । ३-१३ [?] । तस्मै सुतमभिषुतं रसं पायय । आत्मानं पायय । इष्टसाधनं सोमयागं कुर्वित्यर्थः । कृत्वा च क्षयद्वीरं क्षियन्तो निवसन्तो वीराः पुत्रभृत्यादयो यस्य तं तादृशं त्वदिष्टसाधनबहुधनप्रदातारं सूनृताभिः प्रियसत्यात्मिकाभिर्वाग्भिर्वर्धय । समृद्धं कुरु । पुत्रभृत्यादिवीर्यथा प्रवृद्धो भवति तथा कामयेत्यर्थः ॥

Read from the image; the small type is doubtful in places — "madyātminni" [?] and the Nirukta numbers "2-11" and "3-13" [?] are given as printed/read by the OCR, as the OCR gives "२-११" for the first. "Yesterday morning, at the time of daybreak, he gave this wealth; at that very time I, desiring you, the doer of good (sukṛtam), wishing to obtain you, longing 'when shall I see him?', have now come (āyam) — I have arrived. Although here only prātaḥ ('in the morning') is heard and not 'on the former day', still since adya āyam has been said, it is understood by implication to be 'the morning of the former day'. What sort? The son (putram) of iṣṭi — of the desired, of the sacrifice that is the means of the desired — the protector of many: 'putraḥ puru trāyate' (Ni. 2-11), says Yāska; that is, the doer. By what means? Vasumatā rathena — by a chariot with abundant wealth; or else the instrumental has the sense 'together with that'. And moreover with the abundant wealth brought by me, make the suta, the pressed juice, of the aṃśu, of the vine-like Soma, matsara, the means of intoxication, drunk (pāyaya): 'matsaraḥ somo mandateḥ stṛptikarmaṇaḥ' (the Nirukta, 3-13 [?]); make yourself drink; that is: perform the Soma sacrifice, the means of the desired. Having done so, kṣayadvīram — he whose heroes, the sons, servants and so on, dwell in his house — such a giver of abundant wealth, the means of what you desire, make him prosper (vardhaya) with sūnṛtābhiḥ — pleasant and true words; make him prosperous; wish so that he flourishes with sons, servants and other heroes."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Prātaḥ — in the morning (of yesterday); sukṛtam — [you] who have done good; vasumatā — wealthy; rathena — by a chariot, as the means; iṣṭeḥ — the desired (the sacrifice that is the means of the desired); putram — well protected (you); icchan — desiring (to see you), I; adya — now (today); āyam — have come; (kiṃ ca — and); aṃśoḥ — in the form of the vine; matsarasya — of the intoxicating Soma plant; sutam — the pressed (juice); pāyaya — make yourself drink (perform the Soma sacrifice, the means of the desired); kṣayadvīram — he whose sons, servants and the like are alive (the giver); sūnṛtābhiḥ — with pleasant and true speech; vardhaya — make prosperous (bless him with prosperity).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. (Yesterday) in the morning you did good deeds and protected the sacrifice in a chariot full of wealth; I, desiring to see you, Kakṣīvat, have now come. (Now, with the wealth I have brought, perform the Soma sacrifice;) drinking the intoxicating juice of the Soma plant, bless with true and pleasant words the giver, together with his sons, servants and the like, that he may prosper.

Printed English (Ṛk 3, as printed): Desirous (of again beholding thee), I have this day obtained thee, who hast done in the morning a good deed; the performer of a sacrifice, with a wealth-laden car, refresh thyself with the effused juice of the exhilarating (Soma) creeper, and augment with sincere prayers (the prosperity) of the chief of a flourishing race.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.

rathena — raṃhaṇaśīlena athavā ramaṇīyena… [as printed, the Nirukta etymology:] rathaḥ raṃhater gatikarmaṇaḥ sthiratervā syād viparītasya | ramater vā | rasater vā (Ni. 9-11, as read by the OCR; the print's numerals are small) — the author of the Nirukta shows the derivation of this word either from the root raṃh, meaning motion or speed, or, with a change of letters, from sthira (steady); or from the root ram, which gives the meaning "to sit and enjoy"; or from ras, meaning "to make a sound": it is to be a thing that yields these. वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः । गोभिः संनद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्थाता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ॥

vanaspate vīḍvaṅgo hi bhūyā asmatsakhā prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ | gobhiḥ saṃnaddho asi vīḷayasvāsthātā te jayatu jetvāni ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-26, as read from the print.)

kṣayadvīram — atibalinaṃ yasmin sarve vīrāḥ kṣīyante [as printed; the sense is: "he in whose [power] all heroes dwell"]: the word kṣi means "dwelling", and kṣayadvīra is he who makes heroes dwell: kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ vīrāṇāṃ nivāsayitā kṣayadvīraḥ | pūṣā hy astaṃ gacchan sarvavīrān sve sve sthāne nivāsayati | tenāsau kṣayadvīra ity ucyate — as Skandasvāmin has explained, the word kṣi means "dwelling-place"; Pūṣan, at the time of setting, settles all the heroes each in his own dwelling-place, and hence has the name kṣayadvīra; this was explained before (Ṛ. 1-106-4). In the present ṛk, Sāyaṇa explains: kṣiyanto nivasanto vīrāḥ putrabhṛtyādayo yasya taṃ tādṛśam — "him whose sons, servants and others dwell with him, such a one". And in

स्तोमं वो अद्य रुद्राय शिक्वसे क्षयद्वीराय नमसा दिदिष्टन । येभिः शिवः स्ववाँ एवयावभिर्दिवः सिषक्ति स्वयशा निकामभिः ॥

stomaṃ vo adya rudrāya śikvase kṣayadvīrāya namasā didiṣṭana | yebhiḥ śivaḥ svavā~ evayāvabhirdivaḥ siṣakti svayaśā nikāmabhiḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-1, as read from the print.)

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 9-11; 1-106

original p. 201

— in this and other ṛks (1-114-1; 1-114-3) kṣayadvīrāya rudrāya means kṣitaśatrave rudrāya, "to Rudra who has destroyed his enemies"; in the present ṛk the purport is "as one who dwells together with sons and the rest".

aṃśoḥ — in general aṃśu means a ray. But since the parts of the Soma plant, being shining and fine, spread like rays in many directions, these parts are called aṃśu. In the present ṛk Sāyaṇa explains aṃśoḥ as vallīrūpasya (somasya), "of Soma in the form of the vine" — the vine of the Soma plant, full of juice. The author of the Nirukta, giving the derivation of this word, says aṃśuḥ kam aśnuta iva [?] bhavati | ananāya śaṃ bhavatīti vā (Ni. 2-5, as read by the OCR): as soon as it enters the body it is wholesome, or it gives well-being to life; therefore it has the name; and he cites

ते सोमादो हरी इन्द्रस्य निंसतेंऽशुं दुहन्तो अध्यासते गवि । तेभिर्दुग्धं पपिवान्सोम्यं मध्विन्द्रो वर्धते प्रथते वृषायते ॥

te somādo harī indrasya niṃsateṃ 'śuṃ duhanto adhyāsate gavi | tebhirdugdhaṃ papivānsomyaṃ madhvindro vardhate prathate vṛṣāyate ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-? [?], as read from the print; the middle numeral is small and doubtful.) Read letter by letter; "somādo" and "niṃsate" are as printed and doubtful. But here aṃśu means Soma juice. Likewise in

आसाव्यंशुर्मदायाप्सु दक्षो गिरिष्ठाः । श्येनो न योनिमासदत् ॥

āsāvyaṃśurmadāyāpsu dakṣo giriṣṭhāḥ | śyeno na yonimāsadat ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-?-? [?], as read — numerals unclear.) — in ṛks like this too the meaning is Soma juice. When the word aṃśu comes as an epithet of the word soma, it means a piece of the Soma vine.

प्र यत्सिन्धवः प्रसवं यथायन्नापः समुद्रं रथ्येव जग्मुः । अतश्चिदिन्द्रः सदसो वरीयान्यदीं सोमः पृणति दुग्धो अंशुः ॥

pra yatsindhavaḥ prasavaṃ yathāyannāpaḥ samudraṃ rathyeva jagmuḥ | ataścidindraḥ sadaso varīyānyadīṃ somaḥ pṛṇati dugdho aṃśuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-36-6, as read from the print.)

समुद्रेण सिन्धवो यादमाना इन्द्राय सोमं सुषुतं भरन्तः । अंशुं दुहन्ति हस्तिनो भरित्रैर्मध्वः पुनन्ति धारया पवित्रैः ॥

samudreṇa sindhavo yādamānā indrāya somaṃ suṣutaṃ bharantaḥ | aṃśuṃ duhanti hastino bharitrairmadhvaḥ punanti dhārayā pavitraiḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-?-2 [?], as read.) — since in such ṛks it is an epithet of the word soma, latākhaṇḍarūpaḥ alpaḥ somaḥ, the Soma in the form of a piece of the vine and small, is stated; the small quantity of the Soma is stated.

original p. 202

Yet alpataro 'ṃśubhūtaḥ somaḥ varīyāṃsam indraṃ prīṇayati: even though Indra has a great body, the small Soma satisfies him. In the present sūkta Indra, being satisfied, is prayed to increase the prosperity of Svanaya.

matsarasya — mādanasādhanasya somasya; "the cause of joy". The author of the Nirukta gives two meanings for this word: matsaraḥ somo mandater [mandateḥ] stṛptikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 2-25, as read) — formed from the root mand meaning "to satisfy", it is a synonym of Soma juice; or matsara iti lobhanāma — since it is something that shows eagerness (atyāśā) or emulation, it is called matsara: so he gives the derivation. This word is used in both senses. For example —

सुषुमा यातमद्रिभिर्गोश्रीता मत्सरा इमे । सोमासो मत्सरा इमे ॥

suṣumā yātamadribhirgośrītā matsarā ime | somāso matsarā ime ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-137-1, as read from the print.) — here the word matsara is used to show that the present Soma juices are excellent in rivalry with the Soma juices of other sacrifices.

मत्सि सोमं वरुणं मत्सि मित्रं मत्सीन्द्रमिन्दो पवमान विष्णुम् । मत्सि शर्धो मारुतं मत्सि देवान्मत्सि महामिन्द्रमिन्दो मदाय ॥

matsi somaṃ varuṇaṃ matsi mitraṃ matsīndramindo pavamāna viṣṇum | matsi śardho mārutaṃ matsi devānmatsi mahāmindramindo madāya ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-80-2, as read from the print.) — in ṛks like this the meaning "satisfying" is understood. In the present ṛk it is "the juice that is the means of satisfaction, giving joy".

putram — putraḥ puru trāyate (Ni. 2-11, as read): the name "son" is because he protects exceedingly; here it means "the performer of the sacrifice". Sāyaṇa too, citing Yāska's etymology, shows that kartāram ity arthaḥ, "the doer", means the performer of the sacrifice.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3, pp. 202–203; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). āyam — root iṇ gatau; laṅ first person singular, mip; tasthasthamipāṃ tāmtamtāmaḥ (Pā. 3-4-101) gives am in place of the mip; āḍ ajādīnām (Pā. 6-4-72) gives the augment āṭ to the stem; āṭaś ca (Pā. 6-1-90) gives vṛddhi; eco 'yavāyāvaḥ gives āy; since it stands at the head of a pāda, no nighāta; since the augment is acute, the first syllable is acute.

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 2-11; 3-4-101; 6-4-72; 6-1-90

original p. 203

sukṛtam — śobhanaṃ karoti iti sukṛt; root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; kvip; hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk (Pā. 6-1-71) gives tuk; in the prādi-compound the accent of the final member; accusative singular. icchan — root iṣu icchāyām; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; śa-augment; iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ (Pā. 7-3-77) gives cha to the root; the accent of the verb-suffix remains. iṣṭeḥ — the root as before; mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanaviduśrībhūvārtta… (Pā. 3-3-96) gives ktin acute. putram — root pūñ pavane; puvo hrasvaś ca (Uṇ. 4-165 as read) gives the suffix tra; as it is kit there is no guṇa. pāyaya — root pā pāne; since it shows the causative sense, hetumati ca gives ṇic; with it following, śācchāsāhvāvyāvepāṃ yuk (Pā. 7-3-37) gives the augment yuk; loṭ second person singular after the ṇijanta; nighāta accent. kṣayadvīram — root kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ; śatṛ in the laṭ sense; by vyatyaya guṇa; ayādeśa; kṣayantaḥ vīrāḥ yasya saḥ tam; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1) gives the natural accent of the first member. vardhaya — root vṛdhu vṛddhau; as before, loṭ second person singular after the ṇijanta; nighāta. ‖ 3 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उप क्षरन्ति सिन्धवो मयोभुव ईजानं च यक्ष्यमाणं च धेनवः । पृणन्तं च पपुरिं च श्रवस्यवो घृतस्य धारा उप यन्ति विश्वतः ॥ ४ ॥

upa kṣaranti sindhavo mayobhuva ījānaṃ ca yakṣyamāṇaṃ ca dhenavaḥ | pṛṇantaṃ ca papuriṃ ca śravasyavo ghṛtasya dhārā upa yanti viśvataḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उप । क्षरन्ति । सिन्धवः । मयःऽभुवः । ईजानम् । च । यक्ष्यमाणम् । च । धेनवः । पृणन्तम् । च । पपुरिम् । च । श्रवस्यवः । घृतस्य । धाराः । उप । यन्ति । विश्वतः ॥ ४ ॥

upa | kṣaranti | sindhavaḥ | mayaḥ 'bhuvaḥ | ījānam | ca | yakṣyamāṇam | ca | dhenavaḥ | pṛṇantam | ca | papurim | ca | śravasyavaḥ | ghṛtasya | dhārāḥ | upa | yanti | viśvataḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

पूर्वस्यामृच्यानीतेन धनेन सोमयागं कुर्वित्युक्तम् । तमेव सोमयागं फलप्रदर्शनेन स्तौति । सिन्धवः स्यन्दनशीलाः प्रस्रुतपयोधराः । सिन्धुः स्यन्दनादिति यास्कः । नि. ९-२६ [?] । मयोभुवः सुखभावयित्र्यः । मय इति सुखनाम मयः शर्म सुखमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । धेनवः प्रीणयित्र्यो गाव ईजानं सोमयागमनुतिष्ठन्तं तथा यक्ष्यमाणं यक्ष्य इति प्रणतिं कुर्वन्तं च । न केवलमीजानमपि तु यक्ष्य इत्यध्यवसितवन्तमुप समीपमेत्य क्षरन्ति । स्रवन्ति । प्रीणयन्तीत्यर्थः । न च पूर्वस्यामृचि सोमं पिबेत्युक्तत्वात्सर्वेषां सोमयागानामग्निष्टोमात्मकज्योतिष्टोमस्य प्रकृतस्य ज्योतिष्टोमेन स्वर्गकामो यजेतेति स्वर्ग एव फलत्वेन श्रुतेः न गवादिकमिति वाच्यम् । स्वर्गवद्गवादिकामनयापि सोमयागस्य कर्तुं शक्यत्वात् । न केवलं सोमयागमनुतिष्ठतामेव महत्फलं अपि तु सुकृतसाधनानि कर्मान्तराण्यनुतिष्ठतामपि महत्फलमस्त्येवेति दर्शयति । पृणन्तं पितॄन्प्रीणयन्तं [?] पपुरिं प्रीणनशीलमिष्टदातारं प्राणिनः सर्वदा प्रीणयन्तं च पुरुषं श्रवस्यवोऽन्नमिच्छन्तोऽन्नसमृद्धिहेतवो घृतस्य धाराः । यद्वा । घृतकुल्याः । विश्वतः सर्वत उप उपेत्य यन्ति । प्राप्नुवन्ति । प्रीणयन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

pūrvasyāmṛcyānītena dhanena somayāgaṃ kurvityuktam | tameva somayāgaṃ phalapradarśanena stauti | sindhavaḥ syandanaśīlāḥ prasrutapayodharāḥ | sindhuḥ syandanāditi yāskaḥ | ni. 9-26 [?] | mayobhuvaḥ sukhabhāvayitryaḥ | maya iti sukhanāma mayaḥ śarma sukhamiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | dhenavaḥ prīṇayitryo gāva ījānaṃ somayāgamanutiṣṭhantaṃ tathā yakṣyamāṇaṃ yakṣya iti praṇatiṃ kurvantaṃ ca | na kevalamījānamapi tu yakṣya ityadhyavasitavantamupa samīpametya kṣaranti | sravanti | prīṇayantītyarthaḥ | na ca pūrvasyāmṛci somaṃ pibetyuktatvātsarveṣāṃ somayāgānāmagniṣṭomātmakajyotiṣṭomasya prakṛtasya jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajeteti svarga eva phalatvena śruteḥ na gavādikamiti vācyam | svargavadgavādikāmanayāpi somayāgasya kartuṃ śakyatvāt | na kevalaṃ somayāgamanutiṣṭhatāmeva mahatphalaṃ api tu sukṛtasādhanāni karmāntarāṇyanutiṣṭhatāmapi mahatphalamastyeveti darśayati | pṛṇantaṃ pitṝnprīṇayantaṃ [?] papuriṃ prīṇanaśīlamiṣṭadātāraṃ prāṇinaḥ sarvadā prīṇayantaṃ ca puruṣaṃ śravasyavo 'nnamicchanto 'nnasamṛddhihetavo ghṛtasya dhārāḥ | yadvā | ghṛtakulyāḥ | viśvataḥ sarvata upa upetya yanti | prāpnuvanti | prīṇayantītyarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the small type of the middle sentences is doubtful in places, and the Nirukta number "9-26" is as the OCR reads it ["೯-೨೬"]. The words "pitṝn prīṇayantam" are the reading of a small phrase. "In the previous ṛk it was said 'perform the Soma sacrifice with the wealth brought'. Now he praises that very Soma sacrifice by showing its fruit. Sindhavaḥ — flowing, with streaming udders; 'sindhuḥ syandanāt' says Yāska (Ni. 9-26 [?]). Mayobhuvaḥ — causers of happiness; maya is a name for 'happiness', since mayaḥ śarma sukham are read among its names. Dhenavaḥ — the cows that give delight; ījānam — to him who performs the Soma sacrifice; and yakṣyamāṇam — to him who makes the resolve 'I will sacrifice'; not only the performer but also him who has decided 'I will sacrifice' — coming near, they kṣaranti — flow, satisfy. It should not be said that, since the previous ṛk says 'drink Soma', and the Jyotiṣṭoma is the prescribed Agniṣṭoma-type of all Soma sacrifices, and the text 'one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma' gives only heaven as the fruit, cows and the like are not meant; for the Soma sacrifice can be performed also with a desire for cows and the like, as for heaven. And not only for those who perform the Soma sacrifice is the fruit great; for those who perform other rites that are means of good deeds also there is a great fruit: this he shows. Pṛṇantam — him who satisfies the ancestors [?], papurim — the one who is given to satisfying, the giver of what is desired, the person who constantly gratifies living beings: to him, śravasyavaḥ — desiring food, the causes of the abundance of food, ghṛtasya dhārāḥ — streams of ghee; or else ghṛtakulyāḥ, rivers of ghee; from every side upa yanti — come near, reach, satisfy."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Sindhavaḥ — [cows] yielding milk in streams; mayobhuvaḥ — (and) the means of happiness; dhenavaḥ — the cows; ījānam ca — him who performs the (Soma) sacrifice; yakṣyamāṇam ca — and him who has taken the vow, 'I will perform the (Soma) sacrifice'; upa — nearby; kṣaranti — yield (milk); pṛṇantam ca — him who satisfies (the ancestors); papurim ca — and who delights (living beings); śravasyavaḥ — causes of abundance of food; ghṛtasya dhārāḥ — streams of ghee; viśvataḥ — from all sides; upa yanti — come near (satisfy).

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 9-26

original p. 205

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The cows, which pour forth milk in streams and are the means of happiness, satisfy by giving milk to him who performs the Soma sacrifice and to him who has taken the vow "I will perform it"; (not to them alone) to the one who pleases the ancestors and all living beings, the ghee flows in streams (becomes the cause of satisfaction).

Printed English (as printed): The copiously yielding and joy-conferring cows, distil (their milk) for the celebration of the (Soma) sacrifice, and for him who has undertaken its celebration : the nutritious streams of butter converge from every quarter towards him, who both propitiates (his progenitors), and benefits (mankind).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 4.

sindhavaḥ — avanayaḥ, yahvyaḥ and the like — this word is recorded among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24, as printed). The author of the Nirukta, citing

सुदेवो असि वरुण यस्य ते सप्त सिन्धवः । अनुक्षरन्ति काकुदं सूर्म्यं सुषिरामिव ॥

sudevo asi varuṇa yasya te sapta sindhavaḥ | anukṣaranti kākudaṃ sūrmyaṃ suṣirāmiva ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-41-2, as read from the print.) shows the derivation of this word there: sindhuḥ sravaṇāt (sindhuḥ syandanāt, Ni. 9-26) — "because of flowing, the Gaṅgā and the other rivers are called sindhus". This word is used not only as a synonym of river; it is also used as an epithet for things that flow, like milk.

श्रुधी हवमिन्द्र मा रिषण्यः स्याम ते दावने वसूनाम् । इमा हि त्वामूर्जो वर्धयन्ति वसूयवः सिन्धवो न क्षरन्तः ॥

śrudhī havamindra mā riṣaṇyaḥ syāma te dāvane vasūnām | imā hi tvāmūrjo vardhayanti vasūyavaḥ sindhavo na kṣarantaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-41-1, as read from the print.) — in these and other ṛks, in the sense of ājya (ghee) and milk, so in the present ṛk the word is used as a synonym of the milk of the cows.

mayobhuvaḥ — the word mayas is recorded among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-13). Mayobhuvaḥ means "causers of happiness". This word is generally used as an epithet of the gods…

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 2-24; 9-26; 3-13

original p. 206

Special topics, Ṛk 4, continued — mayobhuvaḥ: …it is used; but in some places it shows the nature of the sacrifice and the sacrificial materials that give happiness. In the present ṛk it is an epithet of the cows that give milk.

papurim — piparti papurir iti pṛṇāti nigamau vā [print: "ಪಿಪರ್ತಿ ಪಪುರಿರಿತಿ ಪೃಣಾತಿ ನಿಗಮೌ ವಾ"] prīṇāti nigamau vā (Ni. 5-24 [?], as printed "೩-೨೪" or similar — doubtful): the words piparti and papuri are used in the senses "fills" or "satisfies"; so the author of the Nirukta explains, and, citing

हविषा जारो आसां पिपर्ति पपुरिर्नरा । पिता कुटस्य चर्षणिः ॥

haviṣā jāro āsāṃ piparti papurirnarā | pitā kuṭasya carṣaṇiḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-46-4, as read from the print.) he has explained there the word papuri as above. Likewise in

कथा शृणोति हूयमानमिन्द्रः कथा शृण्वन्नवसामस्य वेद । का अस्य पूर्वीरुपमातयो ह कथैनमाहुः पपुरिं जरित्रे ॥

kathā śṛṇoti hūyamānamindraḥ kathā śṛṇvannavasāmasya veda | kā asya pūrvīrupamātayo ha kathainamāhuḥ papuriṃ jaritre ‖

Saṃ. 4-23-2 [?], as read; the numerals are small.) — here too jaritre stotuḥ saṃbandhināṃ kāmānāṃ papuriṃ pūrayitāram enam indram — "Indra, the one who fills the desires of the praiser" — thus the meaning of papuri is shown. As the meaning is "to fill" or "to satisfy", in the present ṛk the construction is "the sacrificer who satisfies the gods with oblations and gifts".

pṛṇantam — this word is recorded among the names of acts of giving (Ni. 3-19, as printed). In this ṛk Sāyaṇa explains it as pitṝn prīṇayantam — "him who satisfies the ancestors".

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

नाकस्य पृष्ठे अधि तिष्ठति श्रितो यः पृणाति स ह देवेषु गच्छति । तस्मा आपो घृतमर्षन्ति सिन्धवस्तस्मा इयं दक्षिणा पिन्वते सदा ॥ ५ ॥

nākasya pṛṣṭhe adhi tiṣṭhati śrito yaḥ pṛṇāti sa ha deveṣu gacchati | tasmā āpo ghṛtamarṣanti sindhavastasmā iyaṃ dakṣiṇā pinvate sadā ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

नाकस्य । पृष्ठे । अधि । तिष्ठति । श्रितः । यः । पृणाति । सः । ह । देवेषु । गच्छति । तस्मै । आपः । घृतम् । अर्षन्ति । सिन्धवः । तस्मै । इयम् । दक्षिणा । पिन्वते । सदा ॥ ५ ॥

nākasya | pṛṣṭhe | adhi | tiṣṭhati | śritaḥ | yaḥ | pṛṇāti | saḥ | ha | deveṣu | gacchati | tasmai | āpaḥ | ghṛtam | arṣanti | sindhavaḥ | tasmai | iyam | dakṣiṇā | pinvate | sadā ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सोमयागप्रशंसाप्रसङ्गेन सामान्यतो दानमेतदादिभिस्तिसृभिः प्रशंसति । यद्वा । सोमस्यैव स्तुतत्वाद्दक्षिणाशब्दस्य योग एव प्रसिद्धत्वाच्च सूक्तपरिसमाप्तेः सोमयाग एव प्रस्तूयते । यः यो मर्त्यः पृणाति हविरादिदानेन देवादीन्प्रीणाति स नाकस्य । कमिति सुखनाम । तद्विरुद्धमकम् । न विद्यते कं दुःखं तत्साधनं पापं वेति नाको द्युलोकः । तथा श्रूयते । न वा अमुं लोकं जग्मुषे किं च नाकमिति [?] । नि. २-१४ [?] । तस्य पृष्ठे उन्नते उपरिदेशे श्रितः सन्नध्यधिकमाकल्पान्तं तिष्ठति । यद्वा । अधि तिष्ठति । अधिष्ठाय प्रमुखो भूत्वा तिष्ठति । न केवलं स्वर्गाश्रयणं किंतु देवेषु मध्ये ह इति प्रसिद्धौ । तस्मै प्रीणयित्रे पुरुषाय सिन्धवः स्यन्दनशीला आपो घृतं तेजोवत्सारमर्षन्ति । गच्छन्ति । रसवत्यो भवन्तीत्यर्थः । किंचेयं भूमिरपि दक्षिणा सस्यादिफलसंपादनेन सती सदा सर्वकालं पिन्वते । सेचयति । तोषयतीत्यर्थः । दातुर्जीवनसाधकान्नोदकानि रुचिराणि समृद्धानि भवन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

somayāgapraśaṃsāprasaṅgena sāmānyato dānametadādibhistisṛbhiḥ praśaṃsati | yadvā | somasyaiva stutatvāddakṣiṇāśabdasya yoga eva prasiddhatvācca sūktaparisamāpteḥ somayāga eva prastūyate | yaḥ yo martyaḥ pṛṇāti havirādidānena devādīnprīṇāti sa nākasya | kamiti sukhanāma | tadviruddhamakam | na vidyate kaṃ duḥkhaṃ tatsādhanaṃ pāpaṃ veti nāko dyulokaḥ | tathā śrūyate | na vā amuṃ lokaṃ jagmuṣe kiṃ ca nākamiti [?] | ni. 2-14 [?] | tasya pṛṣṭhe unnate uparideśe śritaḥ sannadhyadhikamākalpāntaṃ tiṣṭhati | yadvā | adhi tiṣṭhati | adhiṣṭhāya pramukho bhūtvā tiṣṭhati | na kevalaṃ svargāśrayaṇaṃ kiṃtu deveṣu madhye ha iti prasiddhau | tasmai prīṇayitre puruṣāya sindhavaḥ syandanaśīlā āpo ghṛtaṃ tejovatsāramarṣanti | gacchanti | rasavatyo bhavantītyarthaḥ | kiṃceyaṃ bhūmirapi dakṣiṇā sasyādiphalasaṃpādanena satī sadā sarvakālaṃ pinvate | secayati | toṣayatītyarthaḥ | dāturjīvanasādhakānnodakāni rucirāṇi samṛddhāni bhavantītyarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the OCR is garbled in places. The Nirukta citation "2-14" and the Veda quotation "na vā amuṃ lokaṃ jagmuṣe kiṃ ca nākam" are small and I give them as read. "By way of praise of the Soma sacrifice, in these three [ṛks] beginning with this, he praises giving in general. Or else, since only the Soma sacrifice has been praised, and since the word dakṣiṇā ('fee') is well known only in connection with it, and the sūkta is to be completed, it is the Soma sacrifice itself that is being described. Yaḥ — the mortal who pṛṇāti — satisfies the gods and others by gifts of oblations and the like, nākasya — kam is a name of happiness; the opposite is akam; nāka is the heaven in which there is no kam — no sorrow, or no sin that is its means: thus it is heard: 'to the one who has gone to yonder world there is nothing that is not nāka' (Ni. 2-14 [?]) — on its back (pṛṣṭhe), the high upper region, resting (śritaḥ), adhi tiṣṭhati — dwells till the end of the age; or adhi tiṣṭhati — presides, standing as the foremost. Not only does he gain heaven, but ha — it is well known — he goes (gacchati) among the gods, that is, himself becomes a god. For that satisfier of the gods, the sindhavaḥ — flowing waters — ghṛtam — with radiant essence — arṣanti — flow, they become full of juice. And, moreover, this earth too, being dakṣiṇā ('fee', 'fertile'), by yielding grain and the like, sadā — always — pinvate — drenches, satisfies: that is, for the giver, the food and waters that support life become lovely and abundant."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Yaḥ — which man; pṛṇāti — satisfies (the gods and others) with oblations and the like; saḥ — that man; nākasya pṛṣṭhe — on the high region of the world of heaven; śritaḥ — dwelling there; adhi tiṣṭhati — resides, [having obtained] pre-eminence for ever; deveṣu — among the gods; gacchati — goes (joins); ha — (this) is well known; tasmai — to him (who has satisfied the gods); sindhavaḥ — flowing (the nature of flowing); āpaḥ — the waters; ghṛtam — as juice (with radiant quality); arṣanti — go (and become); tasmai — to such a one; iyam — this earth; dakṣiṇā — fertile (in producing grain and the like); sadā — always; pinvate — gives satisfaction.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. If one satisfies the gods with oblations and the like, that man is honoured in the heaven-world; (not only that) he becomes one among the gods; for such a one the flowing waters become full of essence (radiant); and the earth, by giving grain and other fruits, always gives satisfaction.

Printed English (as printed): He who propitiates (the gods), gives to the gods, and sits at ease upon the summit of heaven : to him the flowing waters bear their essence ; to him this fertile (earth) every yields abundance. sic: "every" for "ever"

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 5.

nākasya — the author of the Nirukta includes the word nāka among six "common" (sādhāraṇa) names and explains its meaning as common: sādhāraṇāny uttarāṇi ṣaṭ divaś cādityasya ca (Ni. 2-13, as printed "೨-೧೩") — the later six are synonyms common to heaven and to the Āditya. Then, showing the derivation of this word: nāka ādityo bhavati | netā rasānāṃ | netā bhāsāṃ jyotiṣāṃ praṇayaḥ (Ni. 2-14, as printed) — "the Āditya is nāka, the carrier of the juices, the carrier of the lights" — he points out that the word is a synonym of Āditya, the carrier of juices and of light. Then: atha dyauḥ | kam iti sukhanāma | tatra pratiṣiddhaṃ pratiṣidhyeta [?] — "kam is a name for happiness; the negation of it is akam, that is, absence of happiness; the nāka is that which is free of sorrow", and, citing the text

न वा अमुं लोकं जग्मुषे किं च नाकम् ।

na vā amuṃ lokaṃ jagmuṣe kiṃ ca nākam |

(Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 21-2 [?], as read.) he explains: na vā amuṃ lokaṃ gatavate kiṃ ca nāsukham; puṇyakṛto hy eva tatra gacchanti — "to those who have gone to that world there is nothing that is not happiness; only doers of good deeds go there".

Thus the meaning of the word nāka is stated. In the Ṛk Saṃhitā this word is used in some places as a synonym of Āditya, in some places as a synonym of heaven.

त्रिश्चिन्नो अद्य सिन्धुभिः सप्तमातृभिस्त्र आहावास्त्रेधा हविष्कृतम् [?] । तिस्रः पृथिवीरुपरि प्रवा दिवो नाकं रक्षेथे द्युभिरक्तुभिर्हितम् ॥

triścinno adya sindhubhiḥ saptamātṛbhistra āhāvāstredhā haviṣkṛtam [?] | tisraḥ pṛthivīrupari pravā divo nākaṃ rakṣethe dyubhiraktubhirhitam ‖

ये नाकस्याधि रोचने दिवि देवास आसते । मरुद्भिरग्न आ गहि ॥

ye nākasyādhi rocane divi devāsa āsate | marudbhiragna ā gahi ‖

te avardhanta svatavaso mahitvanā nākaṃ tasthururu cakrire sadaḥ | viṣṇuryaddhāvadvṛṣaṇaṃ madacyutaṃ vayo na sīdannadhi barhiṣi priye ‖

यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवास्तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् । ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचन्त यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः सन्ति देवाः ॥

yajñena yajñamayajanta devāstāni dharmāṇi prathamānyāsan | te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacanta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-50, as read from the print.) — in these it is a synonym of heaven.

वृषैव कपिलो भूत्वा यन्नाकमधिरोहति ।

vṛṣaiva kapilo bhūtvā yannākamadhirohati |

(Bṛ. De. 3-86 [?], as read.) — in this Bṛhaddevatā sentence "atmosphere" (antarikṣa) is clear.

इतोऽसावादित्यो द्वाविंशेन परमादित्याज्जयति तन्नाकं तद्विशोकम् ॥

ito 'sāvādityo dvāviṃśena paramādityājjayati tannākaṃ tadviśokam ‖

(Chā. U. 3-10-3, as read from the print "೩-೧೦-೩".) — in this sentence of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad the heaven-world, free from sorrow, is said to be beyond the world of the Āditya. [In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and the Taittirīya Upaniṣad the name nāka is well known for the son of Mudgala, a knower of Brahman; there it means "free of sorrow".]

In the present ṛk Sāyaṇa explains na vidyate akaṃ duḥkhaṃ tatsādhanaṃ pāpaṃ veti nāko dyuloka — "the heaven-world in which there is neither sorrow nor the sin that is its cause". Such a nākasya pṛṣṭhe unnate upariprade…

arṣanti — this word, from the root meaning "to go", means "go, reach, join"; in the present ṛk it means "they obtain the state of ripening".

pinvate — secayati toṣayatīty arthaḥ: the purport is that, pouring out abundantly the waters that are the means of life of the giver, there is satisfaction for him.

dakṣiṇā 'vatām | it | imāni | citrā | dakṣiṇā 'vatām | divi | sūryāsaḥ | dakṣiṇā 'vantaḥ | amṛtam | bhajante | dakṣiṇā 'vantaḥ | pra | tirante | āyuḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

दक्षिणावतां बहुविधगोहिरण्यादिरूपदक्षिणाप्रदात्‍ऋणाम् । इच्छब्द एवकारार्थः । तेषामेवार्थ इमानि भूमौ दृश्यमानानि चित्राणि चायनीयानि स्यन्दनमणिमुक्तादिरूपाणि [?] समृद्धानि भवन्तीति शेषः । किंच दक्षिणावतामेव दिवि द्युलोके सूर्यासः सूर्यसंबन्धिनो लोकास्तदनुगृहीता भोगा वा समृद्धा भवन्ति । किंच दक्षिणावन्त एवामृतं जरामरणरहितं स्थानं भजन्ते । सेवन्ते । यद्वा । दानेनापहतपाप्मान आत्मानं विदित्वामृतमनश्नानं मोक्षं भजन्ते । प्राप्नुवन्ति । यज्ञेनैव दानेनेति श्रुतेः । किंच दक्षिणावन्त एवायुः प्र तिरन्ते । अतिदीर्घमेवमायुष्यं लभन्ते । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः । इतीति सर्वत्र संबध्यते ॥

dakṣiṇāvatāṃ bahuvidhagohiraṇyādirūpadakṣiṇāpradātṛṇām | icchabda evakārārthaḥ | teṣāmevārtha imāni bhūmau dṛśyamānāni citrāṇi cāyanīyāni syandanamaṇimuktādirūpāṇi [?] samṛddhāni bhavantīti śeṣaḥ | kiṃca dakṣiṇāvatāmeva divi dyuloke sūryāsaḥ sūryasaṃbandhino lokāstadanugṛhītā bhogā vā samṛddhā bhavanti | kiṃca dakṣiṇāvanta evāmṛtaṃ jarāmaraṇarahitaṃ sthānaṃ bhajante | sevante | yadvā | dānenāpahatapāpmāna ātmānaṃ viditvāmṛtamanaśnānaṃ mokṣaṃ bhajante | prāpnuvanti | yajñenaiva dāneneti śruteḥ | kiṃca dakṣiṇāvanta evāyuḥ pra tirante | atidīrghamevamāyuṣyaṃ labhante | prapūrvastiratirvardhanārthaḥ | itīti sarvatra saṃbadhyate ‖

Read from the image and checked against the OCR; a few small words — "syandanamaṇimuktādi" and the quotation "yajñenaiva dānena" — are given as read. "Dakṣiṇāvatām — of those who give fees (dakṣiṇā) of many kinds, in the form of cows, gold and the like. The word it has the sense of eva: for them alone these imāni — the things seen on earth, wonderful and desirable, in the form of chariots, jewels, pearls and the like — become abundant; this is the remainder of the sentence. Moreover for the givers of fees alone, divi — in the heaven-world — sūryāsaḥ — the worlds belonging to the Sun, or the enjoyments favoured by him — become abundant. Moreover only the givers of fees attain (bhajante, resort to) amṛtam — a state free of old age and death; or else, with their sin removed by giving, knowing the Self, they attain amṛta, the state of release, the not-eating: [as in] the text 'by sacrifice, by giving'. Moreover only the givers of fees prātirante — greatly lengthen their life, āyuḥ; they obtain very long life; the verb tir with the prefix pra has the sense of increase. The word iti is connected throughout."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Dakṣiṇāvatām it — only to those who give fees (in the form of cows and gold); citrā — desirable; imāni — these (the things such as chariots obtainable on this earth); dakṣiṇāvatām — to those who give fees; divi — in the atmosphere; sūryāsaḥ — the worlds connected with the Sun (enjoyments obtained by the Sun's favour); dakṣiṇāvantaḥ — the givers of fees alone; amṛtam — the state free of old age and death; bhajante — obtain; dakṣiṇāvantaḥ — the givers of fees; āyuḥ — long life; pra tirante — gain and increase.

original p. 213

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. To those who give fees of cows, gold and the like (having performed the Soma sacrifices and others) come the desirable things on this earth, such as chariots; to them the worlds of the Sun and others in the atmosphere (enjoyments obtained by the Sun's favour); and they themselves obtain the worlds free of old age and death, and (in this world) long life.

Printed English (as printed): These wonderful (rewards) verily are for those who give (pious) donations : for the donors of (pious) gifts the suns shine in heven : the givers of (pious) donations attain immortality : the givers of (pious) gifts prolong their (wordly) existence. sic: "heven", "wordly"

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6.

In this ṛk the excellent place that the givers of fees obtain is praised. For the word dakṣiṇā the author of the Nirukta shows four derivations (Ni. 1-7, as printed "೧-೭"; the OCR reads "१-७"):

दक्षिणा दक्षतेः समर्धयतीति कर्मणो वृद्धं समर्धयतीति ।

dakṣiṇā dakṣateḥ samardhayatīti karmaṇo vṛddhaṃ samardhayatīti |

"Dakṣiṇā from dakṣ — she increases; the work that has grown she makes still more complete": derived from the root dakṣ with the meaning "to make grow". As it is said in this very ṛk, dakṣiṇāvantaḥ āyuḥ pratirante — those who give fees lengthen their life — the substance given as a fee makes increase in another form; hence the name dakṣiṇā.

Second: api vā pradakṣiṇāgamanāt — at the places of sacrifice the priest goes round in circumambulation (pradakṣiṇā), and afterwards carries out his work; the circumambulation of this kind gets the name dakṣiṇā.

Third: diśam abhipretya digdhastaprakṛtiḥ dakṣiṇo ha dakṣater utsāhakarmaṇaḥ [as printed] — because the right hand has the strength to work with effort, the right hand is naturally called dakṣiṇa.

Last: dāśater vā syād dānakarmaṇaḥ — from the root dāś, meaning "to give": since the right hand is used when giving, the gift has the name dakṣiṇā. Thus he has explained in four ways; in the present ṛk all the meanings are suggested as included.

pratirante — pratiratiḥ vṛddhikarmā: "they obtain increase": this is the purport. The glory of giving in the form of the fee is praised in many places in this way.

अयमात्मा दक्षिणान्नं वनुते यो न आत्मेति हृष्यैष दक्षिणाभ्युक्तम् [?] ।

ayamātmā dakṣiṇānnaṃ vanute yo na ātmeti hṛṣyaiṣa dakṣiṇābhyuktam [?] |

(Śa. Brā. 10-1-1-10 [?], as read; the print is small.) — that giving the fee produces food; and

य एष तपति तदेवैतद्दादित्यो यशो यज्ञो हैव तद्यशस्तद्यज्ञस्तद्दक्षिणा हैव तद्यशस्तस्माद्यामस्मै दक्षिणामानयेयुर्न तां इत्वा मोऽन्यस्मा अतिदिशेत् ॥

ya eṣa tapati tadevaitaddādityo yaśo yajño haiva tadyaśastadyajñastaddakṣiṇā haiva tadyaśastasmādyāmasmai dakṣiṇāmānayeyurna tāṃ itvā mo 'nyasmā atidiśet ‖

(Śa. Brā. 4-1-1-33 as read — the Sanskrit of this quotation is read from small print and is doubtful in many syllables.) — since the fee itself is glory (yaśas) and welfare, one should not despise it; and, as Sāyaṇa has cited,

ब्राह्मणा विविदिषन्ति यज्ञेन दानेन ।

brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena |

(Bṛ. U. 4-4-22, as read.) — "Brahmins seek to know by sacrifice, by giving"; thus in other ways too there is praise of the fee.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). dakṣiṇāvatām — dakṣiṇā yeṣām asti iti dakṣiṇāvantaḥ; tad asyāsty asminn iti matup (Pā. 5-2-94) gives matup; mādupadhāyāś ca… (Pā. 8-2-9) gives va for the m; since the suffix has the marker p it is unaccented; genitive plural. citrā — root ciñ cayane; ami-ci-mi-di… (Uṇ. 4-163 as read) gives the suffix tra; since it is kit there is no guṇa; in the neuter śi arises; śeś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70) elides the śi. divi — ūḍidaṃpadādi… (Pā. 6-1-171) gives the acute to the locative ending. sūryāsaḥ — root sṛ gatau; rājasūyasūrya… (Pā. 3-1-114) records it as ending in kyap; with jas following, ājjaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50) gives the augment asuk.

mā | pṛṇantaḥ | duḥ 'itam | enaḥ | ā | aran | mā | jāriṣuḥ | sūrayaḥ | su 'vratāsaḥ | anyaḥ | teṣām | pari 'dhiḥ | astu | kaḥ | cit | apṛṇantam | abhi | sam | yantu | śokāḥ ‖ 7 ‖

अन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां दानं प्रशंसितुमाह । पृणन्तो देवादीन्हविरादिना प्रीणयन्तः सन्तो दुरितं दुष्टं यथा भवति तथा प्राप्तं दुःखमेनस्तत्साधनं पापं च मारन् । मा प्राप्नुवन् । न केवलं दातार एव अपि तु सूरयो देवानां स्तोतारो विद्वांसो मा जारिषुः । जरया न जीर्णा भवेयुः । तथा सुव्रतासः

शोभनकृच्छ्रचान्द्रायणादिनियमवन्तोऽपि मा जारिषुः । तेषामन्यः कश्चन [?] । यः कश्चन तेषां दातॄणां स्तोतॄणां वा अन्यो ऽपि पुरुषः परिधिः पापस्य परितो धारकोऽस्तु । यद्वा । अन्यो यः कश्चित्पापदेवस्तेषां परिधिस्थानीयो व्यवधायकोऽस्तु । यथाग्नेः परिधिः स्वयं रक्षःप्रकृतिभिर्बाध्यमानः स्वान्तर्हितमग्निं रक्षति तद्वत् । अथवा । अन्यो धर्मविशेषस्तेषां परिधिः परिधानमस्तु । कवचस्थानीयोऽस्तु । तर्हि किं प्राप्नुयुरिति उच्यते । अपृणन्तं देवादीनप्रीणयन्तमदातारं शोकाः क्लेशाः पीडकास्तत्साधनाः पाप्मानोऽभ्यभिमुखं सं यन्तु । सम्यक् प्राप्नुवन्तु । वयं सुखिनो भवेमेत्यर्थः ॥

śobhanakṛcchracāndrāyaṇādiniyamavanto 'pi mā jāriṣuḥ | teṣāmanyaḥ kaścana [?] | yaḥ kaścana teṣāṃ dātṝṇāṃ stotṝṇāṃ vā anyo 'pi puruṣaḥ paridhiḥ pāpasya parito dhārako 'stu | yadvā | anyo yaḥ kaścitpāpadevasteṣāṃ paridhisthānīyo vyavadhāyako 'stu | yathāgneḥ paridhiḥ svayaṃ rakṣaḥprakṛtibhirbādhyamānaḥ svāntarhitamagniṃ rakṣati tadvat | athavā | anyo dharmaviśeṣasteṣāṃ paridhiḥ paridhānamastu | kavacasthānīyo 'stu | tarhi kiṃ prāpnuyuriti ucyate | apṛṇantaṃ devādīnaprīṇayantamadātāraṃ śokāḥ kleśāḥ pīḍakāstatsādhanāḥ pāpmāno 'bhyabhimukhaṃ saṃ yantu | samyak prāpnuvantu | vayaṃ sukhino bhavemetyarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the words marked [?] near the beginning — "teṣām anyaḥ kaścana" — are small and doubtful. "To praise giving by the method of agreement and difference, he says: those who satisfy (pṛṇantaḥ) the gods and others with oblations and the like — let them not incur (mā āran) evil that has come about — duritam (sorrow, evil) and enaḥ (sin that is its cause). Not only the givers, but also sūrayaḥ — the wise praisers of the gods — let them not mā jāriṣuḥ — not be worn out by old age; and likewise suvratāsaḥ — those who keep the vows such as kṛcchra and cāndrāyaṇa — let them not be worn out. For them, some other person, anyaḥ kaścid, who is another person of the givers or praisers, let him be a paridhi — a surrounding protector against sin; or let some other deity of sin be as a paridhi — a barrier — for them: as the paridhi of the fire, itself beaten by the Rākṣasas and the like, protects the fire hidden within it, so; or let some special dharma be their paridhāna, as it were a coat of mail. If so, what will befall? That is said: apṛṇantam — him who does not satisfy the gods and others, the non-giver — śokāḥ — troubles, tormentors, the sins that are their cause — abhi saṃ yantu — let them come upon him; let them reach him thoroughly: that we may be happy."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Pṛṇantaḥ — those who have satisfied (the gods with oblations and the like); duritam — sorrow; enaḥ — sin (the cause of sorrow); mā ā aran — let them not incur; sūrayaḥ — the praisers; (and) suvratāsaḥ — those who perform good vows; mā jāriṣuḥ — let them not be worn out by old age; teṣām — (for the givers and praisers); anyaḥ kaścit — some other person; paridhiḥ — the guard (the one who keeps off sin) or (the barrier that holds off sin); astu — let him be; apṛṇantam — him who does not satisfy the gods and others (the non-giver); śokāḥ — afflictions (sins, or the sinful); abhi — against; saṃ yantu — let them come.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. For those who satisfy the gods with oblations and the like there is no sorrow or sin; for the praisers and those who perform other vows (kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa and the like) there is no old age; let some other protect them from sin; let afflictions come upon him who does not satisfy the gods.

Printed English (as printed): May those who propitiate (the gods), never commit degrading sin : may those who praise the gods and observe holy vows, never experience decay : may some (honorable) individual ever be their defence ; and may afflictions fall upon him who does not propitiate (the gods).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 7.

sūrayaḥ — since this word is recorded among the names of praisers, rebha, jaritā, kāru and the like (Ni. 3-19, as printed; the OCR reads "३-१९"), sūrayaḥ means "praisers, devotees who make praise". The word sūri has been used in many places in senses such as "wise", "discriminating", "intelligent".

When it is used of ṛṣis who have the supernatural power of vision, visual and mental, by which they grasp the essential nature of the deities and the secret truths of the universe, this epithet gives a special sense.

तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं सदा पश्यन्ति सूरयः । दिवीव चक्षुराततम् ॥

tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ | divīva cakṣurātatam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-20, as read from the print.) — in such contexts it indicates not only "those who praise" but the extraordinary power of vision of the ṛṣis. And it is used as an epithet not only of ṛṣis but also of Indra and other deities.

अस्मा इदु त्यमुपमं स्वर्षां भराम्याङ्गूषमास्येन । मंहिष्ठमच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं वावृधध्यै ॥

asmā idu tyamupamaṃ svarṣāṃ bharāmyāṅgūṣamāsyena | maṃhiṣṭhamacchoktibhirmatīnāṃ suvṛktibhiḥ sūriṃ vāvṛdhadhyai ‖

No reference is printed; read letter by letter, with "āṅgūṣam" as printed. — in ṛks such as this vipaścitam indram ("the wise Indra") shows the wisdom of Indra and other deities. Besides, the word sūri is also used to suggest the sense "lord, impeller, guide on the good path".

अस्य स्तुषे महिमघस्य राधः सचा सनेम नहुषः सुवीराः । जनो यः पज्रेभ्यो वाजिनीवानश्वावतो रथिनो मह्यं सूरिः ॥

asya stuṣe mahimaghasya rādhaḥ sacā sanema nahuṣaḥ suvīrāḥ | jano yaḥ pajrebhyo vājinīvānaśvāvato rathino mahyaṃ sūriḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-8, as printed.)

एवेदिन्द्रः सुते अस्तावि सोमे भरद्वाजेषु क्षयदिन्मघोनः । असद्यथा जरित्र उत सूरिरिन्द्रो रायो विश्ववारस्य दाता ॥

evedindraḥ sute astāvi some bharadvājeṣu kṣayadinmaghonaḥ | asadyathā jaritra uta sūririndro rāyo viśvavārasya dātā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-33-? [?], as read.)

विश्वकर्मन्हविषा वावृधानः स्वयं यजस्व पृथिवीमुत द्याम् । मुह्यन्त्वन्ये अभितो जनास इहास्माकं मघवा सूरिरस्तु ॥

viśvakarmanhaviṣā vāvṛdhānaḥ svayaṃ yajasva pṛthivīmuta dyām | muhyantvanye abhito janāsa ihāsmākaṃ maghavā sūrirastu ‖

paridhiḥ — pāpasya paritaḥ dhārakaḥ: "the one who has the power to stop sin on all sides and make it stand"; or yathā agniḥ paridhiḥ svayaṃ rakṣaḥprakṛtibhir bādhyamānaḥ svāntarhitam agniṃ rakṣati tadvat: as the paridhi of the fire, though itself struck by Rākṣasas and the like, protects the fire that is within it, so the excellent lord (sūri), himself checking sin, protects those within his protection: that is the purport.

So the Anukramaṇī says: 'Amandān — Kakṣīvān, pleased with the gift, praised Bhāvayavya in five; the last two, Anuṣṭubh, a dialogue between the married pair Bhāvayavya and Romaśā.' Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 3-3-92; 6-4-64; 6-2-139; 6-2-2; 3-5; 2-5 Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 126".

original p. 220

Anuvāda (Kannada). This Sūkta, beginning amandān, is the sixth Sūkta in the eighteenth Anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. In this Sūkta the ṛṣi of the first five ṛks is Kakṣīvān; of the sixth ṛk, Bhāvayavya; of the seventh, a brahmavādinī named Romaśā. Since the first five ṛks contain praise of Bhāvayavya, by the rule of the Anukramaṇī sa eva devatā yā tenocyate (Anu. 2-5) that praise is the deity; and since the sixth and seventh ṛks contain a conversation between Bhāvayavya and Romaśā, the deities of the sixth ṛk are Romaśā and of the seventh Bhāvayavya. But since in the third ṛk of the previous Sūkta it is said svanayena dattāḥ, a doubt arises that the praise may be of Svanaya; yet, as in the custom where the Maruts, sons of Rudra, are addressed by the name of their father rudrāsaḥ, so here too it is natural to use for the son the name of the father, Bhāvayavya, though Svanaya is the name of the son. Besides, since in the first ṛk the name Bhāvayavya is clearly stated, it must be understood that in this sūkta the ṛṣi praises Bhāvayavya. Thus the mutual contradiction is removed; this was said earlier in the preceding sūkta. The first five ṛks of this Sūkta are in Triṣṭubh metre, and the last two in Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: amandāniti kakṣīvān dānatuṣṭaḥ pañcabhir bhāvayavyaṃ tuṣṭāvānuṣṭubhau bhāvayavyaromaśayor dampatyoḥ saṃvāda. The viniyoga was stated before.

"Sindhau — in the Sindhu country, or, by implication, on the bank of the Sindhu, on the sea-shore; adhi kṣiyataḥ — of bhāvyasya, Bhāvayavya, dwelling there; that is, of his son Svanaya. For him I pra bhare — bring forth well, compose — amandān stomān — not small praises, songs of praise, proclamations of his many gifts and the like — manīṣā, with the mind, with a mind exceedingly fond. Who is the particular one? To that he says: atūrtaḥ — unharmed by anyone — yaḥ rājā — the king who for my sake sahasram savān — a thousand Soma sacrifices (savāḥ are the Soma sacrifices, since 'these Soma are pressed') — amimīta — built, by the bestowal of full wealth. Wishing what? Śravaḥ — fame that is heard of by all, desiring it for himself. Since he gave much wealth for fame alone, without the pretext of priestly service, therefore I praise him: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Atūrtaḥ — unharmed; yaḥ rājā — the king (called Svanaya); me — for me; sahasram — a thousand; savān — (Soma) sacrifices; śravaḥ — (only) fame; icchamānaḥ — wishing; amimīta — (by giving wealth) has made; tasya — that [king]; sindhau — on the bank of the Sindhu (sea); adhi kṣiyataḥ — dwelling; bhāvyasya — of Bhāvayavya's son Svanaya; amandān — endless; stomān — praises; manīṣā — with a mind; pra bhare — I make (I praise).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. (Having given wealth for the performance of a thousand Soma sacrifices, he made [the sacrifices] favourable to me, out of desire for fame alone;) I praise with my mind that king called Svanaya, son of Bhāvayavya, who dwells on the sea-shore.

original p. 222

Printed English (as printed): I repeat with a (willing) mind, the unreluctant praises of Bhavya, dwelling on the banks of the Sindhu : a prince of unequalled (might), desirous of renown, who has enabled me to celebrate a thousand sacrifices.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 1.

amandān stomān — analpān kīrtanāni: "not small, many praises". It is stated that "I resolve to compose praises in the form of Soma, which are not small and are of many kinds". In the present ṛk, though stoma means "praise", we shall consider carefully the descriptions of the various stomas as they apply.

Among the stomas there are nine main divisions: the trivṛt stoma, the pañcadaśa stoma, the saptadaśa stoma, the ekaviṃśa stoma, the triṇava stoma, the trayastriṃśa stoma, the caturviṃśa stoma, the catuścatvāriṃśa stoma, and the aṣṭācatvāriṃśa stoma; and the numbers of ṛks are in accordance with the name of each stoma. This number is to be understood as applying to each viṣṭuti of the stoma. Their descriptions are given at length in the 2nd part of the Ṛk Saṃhitā, pp. 139 to 19[?] [as printed; the second numeral is not clear].

Of these stomas, the trivṛt stoma is recited at the morning pressing, the pañcadaśa at the midday pressing, and the saptadaśa at the third pressing. In sacrifices such as the abhiplava ṣaḍaha, after the singing of the stomas — trivṛt and the like — which must be sung in the rites such as the morning pressing, there are other stomas, said in some contexts to be uttara-stomas, whose singing is called stomavṛddhi ("increase of the stoma"). For the singing of these increases of the stoma, ṛks of a larger number are to be recited, in order to equal the increase, by the maitrāvaruṇa, brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and acchāvāka priests of the hotṛ group.

Thus the nine divisions stated above can also be increased by āvāpa (insertion) to thirteen, fourteen, sixteen and so on. For example —

वसवस्त्रयोदशाक्षरेण त्रयोदशं स्तोममुदजयन्रुद्राश्चतुर्दशाक्षरेण चतुर्दशग्ं स्तोममुदजयन्नादित्याः पञ्चदशाक्षरेण पञ्चदशग्ं स्तोममुदजयन्नदितिः षोडशाक्षरेण षोडशग्ं स्तोममुदजयत्प्रजापतिः सप्तदशाक्षरेण सप्तदशग्ं स्तोममुदजयत् ॥

vasavastrayodaśākṣareṇa trayodaśaṃ stomamudajayanrudrāścaturdaśākṣareṇa caturdaśagṃ stomamudajayannādityāḥ pañcadaśākṣareṇa pañcadaśagṃ stomamudajayannaditiḥ ṣoḍaśākṣareṇa ṣoḍaśagṃ stomamudajayatprajāpatiḥ saptadaśākṣareṇa saptadaśagṃ stomamudajayat ‖

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-11-? [?], as read — the numerals "೧-೨-೧೧-೪೪" are small and doubtful.) Read letter by letter; the ग्ं notation is as printed. "The Vasus, with a thirteen-syllable [formula], won the thirteenfold stoma; the Rudras, with a fourteen-syllable, won the fourteenfold stoma; the Ādityas with a fifteen-syllable won the fifteenfold stoma; Aditi with a sixteen-syllable won the sixteenfold stoma; Prajāpati with a seventeen-syllable won the seventeenfold stoma" — by these Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentences the order in which the Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas, Aditi and Prajāpati won the thirteen-, fourteen-, fifteen-, sixteen-, and seventeen-fold stomas is

stated. The power of the stomas is exceedingly great; and that by reciting them all desired ends may be won is also stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā itself.

"In the morning pressing, with the gāyatra metre, he goes bringing light for the trivṛt stoma, with the trivṛt [which is] brahmavarcasa; he goes bringing light for the fifteenfold, with the fifteenfold [which is] vigour, heroism; for the seventeenfold, with the seventeenfold [which is] of Prajāpati, procreation; for the twenty-one-fold, … the stoma indeed, he leads the stoma to the stoma. As many as are the stomas, so many are the desires, so many the worlds, so many the lights: so many stomas, so many desires, so many worlds, so many lights he wins." In these sentences the power of four kinds of stoma is stated. The sacrificer, at the morning pressing, sets the trivṛt stoma, with the gāyatra metre, in a place of eminence; likewise with the trivṛt he makes the pañcadaśa stoma shine like a light; and the fifteenfold [he makes] full of heroism; and, with the seventeenfold, which has connection with Prajāpati and is the means of procreation, he makes the twenty-one-fold full of splendour. Thus one kind of stoma gives power and brilliance to another. As many as the stomas there are, so many worlds, so many brilliances, so many desired ends; and one who recites the stomas wins so many: thus the power of the stomas is explained, and then the loss that follows from non-recitation of the stomas. (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-3-8 to 10 [?], as read from the OCR "६-१-३-८ रिंद १०"; the print "೬-೧-೩-೮" is small.) The scholars of the śāstra have laid down that one who sacrifices with the Agniṣṭoma must sacrifice with all stomas. In this rule, if the trivṛt stoma is left out, his vital breaths are lost, so the sacrificer sacrifices with the thought "let this sacrifice be contained in my vital breaths"; likewise if the pañcadaśa is left out, heroic strength is lost; if the saptadaśa is left out, he goes without progeny; if the ekaviṃśa is left out, his support (pratiṣṭhā) is lost; if the triṇava is left out, … the seasons and the stars (as helpers) are lost to him; if the trayastriṃśa is left out, the chief deities are lost: so the sacrificer performs the rite by pañcadaśa for the sake of heroic strength, by saptadaśa for the gain of progeny, by ekaviṃśa for the support of life, by triṇava for the benefit of the seasons and constellations, by trayastriṃśa for the gain of the deities. He who knows the greatness of the trivṛt stoma, which has the first place among all stomas, wins the first place among sacrificers.

Thus describing the glory of the trivṛt and other stomas —

त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमो भवति तेज एवावरुन्धे पञ्चदशो भवतीन्द्रियमेवावरुन्धे सप्तदशो भवत्यन्नाद्यमवरुन्धे । अथो एकविंशो भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै । अथो रुचमेवात्मन्धत्ते त्रिणवो भवति विजित्यै त्रयस्त्रिंशो भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

नाधमानस्य स्वीकर्तव्यमित्युच्चैर्याचमानस्यासुरस्य धनानां निरसितुर्दानशीलस्य राज्ञः स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानस्य सैनयस्य निष्कानाभरणविशेषान् इयत्ताविशेषविशिष्टानि वा सुवर्णानि शतसंख्याकानि । शतं सहस्रमित्यपरिमितवचनः । अपरिमितान् । सद्यः प्रार्थनानन्तरमेव कक्षीवानहमादम् । आत्तवानस्मि । स्वीकृतवानस्मीत्यर्थः । तथा प्रयतान् शुद्धान्लक्षणोपेतानाशुगमनसमर्थान्हयानश्वान्शतम् । आदम् । तथा गोनां पुंगवानां बलीवर्दानामित्यर्थः । उत्तरमन्त्रे स्त्रीगवीनामभिधानात् । तेषां शतमादम् । एवं प्रदाता राजा दिवि द्युलोके श्रवः कीर्तिमजरमजीर्णं शाश्वतीमा ततान । विस्तारितवान् । गवादिप्रतिग्रहीताहं स्वर्गे कीर्तिमकरवमित्यर्थः ॥

Read from the image; a few words are small — "iyattāviśeṣa-viśiṣṭāni" and "balīvardānām" — and given as read. "Of the king who, begged with nādhamānasya — 'let it be accepted' — loudly urging, of the asura — the one who casts off riches, one who is given to giving, shining by his own splendour, Sainya — niṣkān — particular ornaments, or gold pieces of a definite number, a hundred in number. (Śatam, 'a hundred', is also a word for 'a thousand', not limiting: immeasurable.) Sadyaḥ — immediately after the asking — I, Kakṣīvat, ādam — took, accepted. Likewise prayatān — pure, with good marks, able to go swiftly, horses, aśvān, a hundred; I took. Likewise gonām — of bulls, oxen (since the next mantra speaks of cows); of them, a hundred I took. Thus the king who gave divi — in the heaven-world — śravaḥ, imperishable (ajaram), eternal fame, spread it out (ā tatāna): the sense is that I, the receiver of the gift of cows and the like, made his fame in heaven."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Kakṣīvān — Kakṣīvat (I); nādhamānasya — [who] urgently begs, "let it be accepted"; asurasya — who gives wealth; rājñaḥ — (of the king called Svanaya); śatam — countless; niṣkān — niṣkas; prayatān — pure, of good marks; śatam — a hundred; aśvān — horses (and); gonām — of bulls; śatam — a hundred; sadyaḥ — at once (immediately after his asking); ādam — I took (the king, by giving); divi — in the world of heaven; ajaram — eternal; śravaḥ — (his) fame; ā tatāna — made to spread.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. As soon as King Svanaya asked [me] to accept, I accepted the countless niṣkas he gave, a hundred pure horses, a hundred bulls; (having given gifts to me in this way) the king made his fame spread eternally in heaven (I, receiving the gifts, made his fame eternal in heaven).

original p. 228

Printed English (as printed): From which generous prince, soliciting (my acceptance), I Kakshivat, unhesitatingly accepted a hundred nishkas, a hundred vigorous steeds, and a hundred bulls, whereby he has spread his imperishable fame through heaven.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.

nādhamānasya — for the word nādhamānāḥ the author of the Nirukta gives the meaning yācamānāḥ, "those who beg" (Ni. 4-3 [?], as printed). In the present ṛk, svīkartavyam ity uccair yācamānasya — "of the one who urgently begs 'it must be accepted'" — is an epithet of the word rājñaḥ, "of the king".

asurasya — that many meanings are possible for the word asura has been shown in the special topics on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-108-6 (Ṛk Saṃhitā, part 8, p. 59[?] — as printed "ಪೇ. ೫೯೭"? the numerals are unclear) and on ṛks 1-123-1 and 1-151-4. Among them there is the chief meaning "one who is given to giving". In the present ṛk, dhanānāṃ nirasituḥ dānaśīlasya — "one who casts off [gives] riches, given to giving" — it is an epithet of the word rājñaḥ (that is, of Svanaya).

gonām — puṃgavānāṃ balīvardānām ity arthaḥ: "of bulls, of oxen".

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). nādhamānasya — root nāthṛ yācñā…; Bhvādi; śānac in the laṭ sense, śap; āne muk (Pā. 7-2-82) gives muk; since the sārvadhātuka follows the upadeśa, it is unaccented and the root-accent remains; genitive singular. niṣkān — root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; nau sader ḍiḥ [print: "ನೌ ಸದೇರ್ಡಿಃ"] (Uṇ. 3-?) gives ka when ni is the upapada; by the marker ḍ the ṭi of the root is elided; final-acute by the suffix accent. prayatān — root yam uparame; kta; anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām… (Pā. 6-4-37) elides the nasal m of the root; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49) gives the natural accent of the gati (pra); accusative plural. ādam — root ḍudāñ dāne; Juhotyādi; with ā as the upapada, ādo 'nāsyavihasane [print: "ಆಜೋ ದೋನಾಸ್ಯವಿಹರಣೇ" Pā. 1-3-20] would give ātmanepada, which does not occur here in the Veda; leṭ first person singular mip; bahulaṃ chandasi gives luk of the śap-substitute; itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 3-4-97) elides the i of the ending; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94) gives aṭ to it,

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

Read from the image; the first clause continues the sentence begun at the foot of p. 229: "…having accepted all that, this Kakṣīvat …". The Nirukta number is printed "೩-೩೦" in the Special Topics and "೩-೨೦" in the bhāṣya; the OCR gives "३-२०" for the bhāṣya, "३-३०" for the topics — I leave both, doubtful. "…Kakṣīvat, in the day abhipitve — the near, present day, among the days (ahnām), sanat — [the one who] gives to his own father the chariots and the like accepted, or accepts them himself. The word abhipitva denotes near time, like the word prapitva; and that has the sense 'near', since Yāska says 'prapitve abhīke means āsannasya' (Ni. 3-20 [?]): the sense is not different though the prefix differs."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Svanayena dattāḥ — given by Svanaya; śyāvāḥ — dark-coloured (drawn by dark-coloured horses); vadhūmantaḥ — with my wives (accompanied by wives); daśa — ten; rathāsaḥ — chariots; mā — to me; upa asthuḥ — came near; ṣaṣṭiḥ sahasram — a thousand and sixty; gavyam — a herd of cows; anu ā agāt — followed; kakṣīvān — I, Kakṣīvat; ahnām — of the days; abhipitve — on the present (near) day; sanat — gave (to my father) (accepted).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. King Svanaya gave me ten chariots drawn by dark horses and with my wives, and a thousand and sixty cows; (all of these) I offered (accepted) today [for you, that is, for the father].

Printed English (as printed): Ten chariots drawn by bay steeds, and carrying my wives, stood near me, given me by Swanaya; and a thousand and sixty cows followed: these, after a short interval of time, did Kakshivat deliver (to his father).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.

अभिपित्वशब्दः आसन्नकालवाची प्रपित्वशब्द इतिवत् । स च प्रपित्वेऽभीक इत्यासन्नस्य ।

abhipitvaśabdaḥ āsannakālavācī prapitvaśabda itivat | sa ca prapitve 'bhīka ityāsannasya |

(Ni. 3-30 [?], as printed.) abhipitva and prapitva — both words give the meaning "near, arrived". Since the author of the Nirukta has given for the word prapitve the meaning abhīke ("near"), and the word abhipitve has the same meaning, here abhipitve means "near". Ahnām abhipitve means "in the middle of many days" — the sense: "when the day arrives on which Kakṣīvat presented to his father the generous gifts given by Svanaya"; but, by the words ahnām abhipitve, the explanation "the end of the day, that is, in the evening he gave to his father" must not be taken; so some [scholars] explain…
