original p. 231

Special topics, Ṛk 3, continued from p. 230: …[some explain] that the gifts given by Svanaya in the morning, "prātā ratnaṃ prātaritvā dadhāti" (Ṛk 125-1), were offered [to the father] in the evening, and that this is in order; if one asks what the authority for this is, Sāyaṇa has given this meaning for the word abhipitve:

आ वाजा यातोप न ऋभुक्षा महो नरो द्रविणसो गृणानाः । आ वः पीतयोऽभिपित्वे अह्नामिमा अस्तं नवस्व इव ग्मन् ॥

ā vājā yātopa na ṛbhukṣā maho naro draviṇaso gṛṇānāḥ | ā vaḥ pītayo 'bhipitve ahnāmimā astaṃ navasva iva gman ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-34-5, as read from the print "೪-೩೪-೫".) Read letter by letter; "ā vājā yātopa na ṛbhukṣā" and the last pāda "astaṃ navasva iva gman" are as printed and in the OCR's garbled reading I cannot confirm them. In this ṛk he has explained abhipitve as abhipatane samāpte ("at the end of the day's coming-down") tṛtīye savane — "at the third pressing", that is, at the time of the third pressing, in the evening hour. Some hold that in the same way the present ṛk too may be so explained. The author of the Nirukta too, citing

कुह स्विद्दोषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतः कुहोषतुः । को वां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ ॥

kuha sviddoṣā kuha vastoraśvinā kuhābhipitvaṃ karataḥ kuhoṣatuḥ | ko vāṃ śayutrā vidhaveva devaraṃ maryaṃ na yoṣā kṛṇute sadhastha ā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-40-2, as read from the print.) shows that there abhipitvam means abhiprāptim — "arriving, drawing near, coming" (Ni. 3-15 [?], as printed). Therefore the arrival may be the arrival in the morning, or the arrival in the evening.

There is still another doubt about this. About the words abhipitva and prapitva there is also discussion as to whether the root is pat or āp. Monier-Williams' Dictionary derives it from abhi + pat, giving one meaning "approaching" and another "close or departure of the day". According to the Nirukta the derivation must be abhi + āp; since Sāyaṇa gives meanings for this word in two ways, it seems that it may be formed from both roots pat and āp.

As Sāyaṇa says (1-126-3), some hold that identity of the two words abhipitva and prapitva cannot be maintained, and it is also the opinion of critics that they have not stated one fixed meaning for abhipitva. In this connection the criticism made by the scholar Bloomfield is worth noting. His examination runs thus:

The first explanation of अभिपित्व occurs at Nir. III. 15; it is अभिप्राप्ति 'arrival', and so the word is explained by Sayana at R. V. I. 189-7;

The first explanation of* abhipitva occurs at Nir. III. 15; it is abhiprāpti * 'arrival ', and so the word is explained by Sayana at R. V. I. 189-7;

The summary of this opinion is that Sāyaṇa is somewhat confused in explaining the words abhipitva and prapitva. For example, in the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-34-5 (cited above) he explains this word as "evening", and the same Sāyaṇa, in

न संस्कृतं प्र मिमीतो गमिष्ठान्ति नूनमश्विनोपस्तुतेह । दिवाभिपित्वेऽवसागमिष्ठा प्रत्यवर्तिं दाशुषे शम्भविष्ठा ॥

na saṃskṛtaṃ pra mimīto gamiṣṭhānti nūnamaśvinopastuteha | divābhipitve 'vasāgamiṣṭhā pratyavartiṃ dāśuṣe śambhaviṣṭhā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-76-3, as read from the print "೫-೭೬-೩".) — has explained the corresponding word as "forenoon" (prātaḥkāla): that is this critic's remark.

In the same way there are also the words apapitva and sapitva; with the word pitva are joined prefixes, and the formation of these four words and their meanings according to the contexts will be explained later.

"Of Dakṣaratha-… — daśarathasya: of him who has ten chariots, sahasrasya — of Kakṣīvat who is attended by a thousand followers, or [who has] a thousand herds of cows — agre — in front, śoṇāḥ — forty horses of red colour: since each chariot has four, the ten chariots together have forty horses; they too, taking a row (śreṇi), lead — bring the chariots to the desired place. Or else they make the chariots, yoked with horses, go in a line: four horses, in the form of a row, draw each chariot: that is the sense. Then those [horses], the kakṣīvantaḥ — those having kakṣyā, the girth-ropes (kakṣyā is a rope: 'kakṣyā rajjū rasvasya', says Yāska, Ni. 2-2) — or else all the sons of Aṅgiras are kakṣīvantaḥ; or, by the maxim of the servant, all of Kakṣīvat's followers are kakṣīvantaḥ; pajrāḥ — [fed with] food and the like — the madacyutaḥ — those that let their rut-fluid flow, high-spirited, the ones that make the pride of enemies fall; kṛśanāvataḥ — furnished with various golden ornaments (kṛśana is a name for gold: kṛśanaṃ lohaṃ are read among its names); the atyān — horses that go constantly — ut amṛkṣanta — they rub down excellently, to remove the sweat caused by the toil of the road."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Daśarathasya — of him who is endowed with ten chariots; sahasrasya — of him who has a thousand followers (or: of him who has a thousand cows) (that is, of Kakṣīvat); agre — in front; śoṇāḥ — red; catvāriṃśat — forty (horses); śreṇim — in a row; nayanti — draw (the chariots); (atha — then); kakṣīvantaḥ — Kakṣīvat's followers; pajrāḥ — endowed with food; (kakṣīvantaḥ — those with girth-ropes); madacyutaḥ — [horses] dripping rut-fluid; kṛśanāvataḥ — endowed with golden ornaments; atyān — constantly moving (horses); ut amṛkṣanta — rub down well (limb by limb).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. In front of Kakṣīvat, who has a thousand followers (and cows) and ten chariots, forty red horses draw the chariots in a row; then, provided with food such as grass, his followers rub down well the horses that are adorned with golden ornaments, constantly moving and dripping rut-fluid, tying them with ropes.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 4.

In this ṛk the number of horses and the number of chariots are stated, as it is described in

शतमश्वाञ्छतं निष्कान्रथान्दश वधूमतः । चतुर्युजो गवां चैव सहस्रं षष्ट्यधिकम् ॥

śatamaśvāñchataṃ niṣkānrathāndaśa vadhūmataḥ | caturyujo gavāṃ caiva sahasraṃ ṣaṣṭyadhikam ‖

(Bṛ. De. 3-148 [?], as read.) — that ten chariots, a hundred horses and a thousand and sixty cows were displayed in front of Kakṣīvat.

pajrāḥ — the meaning of this word is explained in the next ṛk.

kakṣīvantaḥ — two kinds of meaning are stated for this word. First: kakṣyā rajjū rasvasya (Ni. 2-2): following the derivation of the author of the Nirukta, that the rope of a horse (the girth) has the name kakṣyā, the meaning is "followers of Kakṣīvat, who hold the horses". Second: because all the sons of the seer Aṅgiras are called by this name, it means "sons of Aṅgiras"; and it is for this reason that Dīrghatamas' son is also known by this name — [that is,] one possessed of the horse's rope, [that is,] one who is aśvayuktaḥ; and

त्यं चिदश्वं न [?] वाजिनं [?] । [?] । कक्षीवन्तं यदी पुना रथं न कृणुथो नवम् ॥

tyaṃ cidaśvaṃ na [?] vājinaṃ [?] | [?] | kakṣīvantaṃ yadī punā rathaṃ na kṛṇutho navam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-143-1, as read from the print; the first line is garbled in my reading and it is not completed. Kakṣīvantam yadī punā ratham na kṛṇutho navam is clear.) — commenting on this ṛk Sāyaṇa states: here for the word kakṣīvantam he explains: kakṣyā rajjū rasvasya tadvantam | dīrghatamasaḥ putraṃ uśijaḥ sutam ṛṣim — "the one who has the rope of the horse: the son of Dīrghatamas, the seer, son of Uśij". In the present ṛk the meaning "followers of Kakṣīvat" is appropriate.

kṛśanāvataḥ — the word kṛśana is recorded among the names of gold (Ni. 1-10 [?], as printed "೧-೧೦") and among the names of form (Ni. 3-13). Therefore it may be explained as "endowed with golden ornaments" or "possessing lovely forms". Yet its use in the sense "furnished with golden ornaments" is the more frequent.

atyān — satatagamanaśīlān aśvān — "horses whose nature is constant going", ones that go without interruption.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

इदानीमानीतं धनं बन्धुभ्यो निवेदयन्नाह । हे सुबन्धवः पूर्वां प्रयतिं पूर्वप्रदानमनु तमनुसृत्य वक्ष्यमाणानि रथादीनि वो युष्मदर्थमा ददे । स्वीकृतवानस्मि । यद्वा । पूर्वां प्रयतिं प्रदेयं रथादिकमनु दानक्रमेणैवा ददे । प्रतिगृहीतवानस्मि । कानि तानीति । त्रीनष्टौ च युक्तान् चतुर्भिश्चतुर्भिरश्वैर्धनैर्वा युक्तान् रथानिति शेषः । अत्र संख्यापृथग्निर्देशो न विवक्षितः । तथारिधायसो रिभिरीश्वरैर्धारणीया बहुमूल्या असंख्याता गाश्चादे । अत्र वक्ष्यमाणं पूर्वं प्रतिगृहीतावधिकानीति युक्तम् । पूर्वमेव पित्रे निवेदितानां पुनर्बन्धुभ्यो निवेदनासंभवात् । वधूमन्तो दश रथासो अस्थुरिति दशानां रथानामुक्तत्वादत्र त्रीनष्टौ चेत्येकादशानां वक्ष्यमाणत्वान्नवानां रथानामन्येभ्यो दातुमुचितत्वाच्चान्यानीति युक्तम् । उक्तानामेवानुवदनपक्षे दश वधूमन्तो रथा एको धनपूर्ण इति विवेकः । उक्तानामेव रथादीनां पुनर्विधानं प्रकृष्टत्वज्ञापनार्थं सर्वे ब्राह्मणा आगता वसिष्ठश्चागत इतिवत् । इदानीं परोक्षेणाह । सुबन्धवः शोभना विद्या योनिसंबन्धिनो येषां ते तथोक्ताः । यद्वा । शोभनबान्धवोपेताः परस्परमनुरागयुक्ता इत्यर्थः । विशः प्रजाः । तत्र भवा विश्याः । व्रियन्त इति वा व्रातः । तकारलोपश्छान्दसः । विशां व्राता यथा परस्परमनुरागवन्तस्तद्वत्सन्त इत्यर्थः । पज्रा अन्नवन्तोऽङ्गिरसः संतानप्रभवा ये सन्ति ते सर्वे सुबन्धवोऽनस्वन्तः शकटवन्तो हविर्धानशकटोपलक्षितसोमयागवन्तः सन्तः श्रवः सर्वत्र श्रूयमाणां कीर्तिमैषन्त । इच्छन्ति इच्छन्तु वा तदर्थमा ददे इति शेषः ॥

The bhāṣya of this ṛk is long, in small type; I give it as read, with the doubtful clause "ayam eva yuktam / vadhūmanto … anyānīti" as printed — "[?]" marks are not needed where the print was clear, but the middle (from "atra vakṣyamāṇaṃ" to "anyānīti yuktam") is only partly legible and may contain slips. "Now, announcing to his kinsmen the wealth brought: O subandhavaḥ — O good kinsmen — pūrvām prayatim anu — following the earlier gift — the chariots and the rest that are going to be named, vaḥ — for you — ā dade: I have accepted. Or else: following the gift to be given — the chariots and the rest — in the order of giving, I have taken it, accepted. What are they? Trīn aṣṭau ca yuktān — eleven chariots yoked with four horses each or with wealth. Here the separate statement of the number is not intended. Likewise, aridhāyasaḥ — to be held by ari, by lords: valuable, countless — and cows I took. … [The text then argues that these eleven chariots are in addition to the ten already mentioned, since what was presented earlier to the father cannot be presented again to the kinsmen; 'ten chariots with wives' were stated, here 'three and eight', eleven, are to be stated; so the others are for giving to others.] If the sense is only a repetition of what was said, then there are ten chariots with wives, and one full of wealth: that is the distinction. The re-statement of the chariots already stated is to show their excellence, as in 'all the Brahmins have come, and Vasiṣṭha has come'. Now he speaks indirectly: subandhavaḥ — those whose kinship by birth (or by knowledge) is good; or those having good kinsmen, that is, bound by mutual affection. Viśaḥ are subjects; those who belong to them are viśyāḥ. Vrāḥ is vrātāḥ (or: those that are chosen); the loss of t is Vedic. As troops of subjects are attached to each other, so [you] are: that is the sense. Pajrāḥ — those Aṅgirases, endowed with food, who are the offspring [of the line], all subandhavaḥ, anasvantaḥ — possessing carts, performing the Soma sacrifice, marked by the carts for the havirdhāna — may they desire (aiṣanta) śravaḥ — fame heard of everywhere; for that [purpose] I have accepted it: this is the remainder."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. He subandhavaḥ — O good kinsmen; pūrvām — said before; prayatim anu — following the gift (following the order of gifts); trīn aṣṭau [ca] — eleven; yuktān — yoked (with horses or with wealth) (chariots); aridhāyasaḥ — fit to be held by lords (countless and priceless); gāḥ ca — and cows; vaḥ — for you; ā dade — I have accepted; ye pajrāḥ — those Aṅgirases (endowed with food); subandhavaḥ — those of good kinship; vrāḥ — (those of one troop), like viśyāḥ iva — like subjects (full of mutual love); subandhavaḥ — those my kinsmen all; anasvantaḥ — possessing carts (suited to the Soma sacrifice, those having carts to carry green food); śravaḥ — fame (heard of everywhere); aiṣanta — desire (let them desire).

original p. 238

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O kinsmen, for you I have accepted cows fit for kings, eleven chariots endowed with wealth, of the kind of the gift mentioned before; (accepting these things) may all my kinsmen, bound together in mutual love, perform Soma sacrifices and gain fame.

Printed English (as printed): I have accepted a prior grant, (kinsmen), for you : three and eight harnessed chariots and cattle of incalculable value : may the kindred Pajras, like well-disposed relations, be desirous of acqiring renown by their abundant offerings. sic: "acqiring"

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 5.

aridhāyasaḥ — aribhir īśvarair dharaṇīyāḥ bahumūlyā asaṃkhyātāḥ: "to be held by lords (īśvara), that is, by wealthy persons; of great price; countless" — an epithet of cows. How the sense "lord" came to the word ari is explained by the author of the Nirukta thus: arir amitram ṛcchateḥ | īśvaro 'ris tasmād eva (Ni. 5-7 [?], as printed "೫-೭"): from the root ṛ meaning "to hurt", the word ari with the sense "enemy", as also, for the lord who has authority over servants, the name ari — and citing

puru tvā dāśvānvoce 'riragne tava svidā | todasyeva śaraṇa ā mahasya ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-150-1, as printed "೧-೧೫೦-೧"; "tvā dāśvān" as read.) as he says that the word ari means "lord", so in the present sūkta also the same meaning arises. That is: "a rich man fit to possess priceless cows".

pajrāḥ — the word pajra gives the same meaning in the previous ṛk and in this ṛk. Though here pajrāḥ is meant for Aṅgirases, the word is used in the sense of "those who have abundant food". In the previous ṛk Sāyaṇa explained it as ghāsādyannavantaḥ santaḥ — "being provided with food such as grass"; in the same way, in this sūkta too, annavanto 'ṅgirasaḥ — "Aṅgirases who have abundant food". The author of the Nirukta, citing

य इन्द्राग्नी सुतेषु वां स्तवत्तेष्वृतावृधा । जोषवाकं वदतः पज्रहोषिणा न देवा भसथश्चन ॥

ya indrāgnī suteṣu vāṃ stavatteṣvṛtāvṛdhā | joṣavākaṃ vadataḥ pajrahoṣiṇā na devā bhasathaścana ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-59-4, as read from the print "೬-೫೯-೪".) explains there pajrahoṣiṇā as prārjitahoṣiṇaḥ; of this Durgācārya says prabhūtayāgau — "[the two] of abundant sacrifice". By pajra the lineage of the Aṅgirases is also meant; the purport is "those who have abundant wealth". The pajra lineage is a famous name in the Ṛk Saṃhitā.

एतानि वां श्रवस्या सुदानू ब्रह्माङ्गूषं सदनं रोदस्योः । यद्वां पज्रासो अश्विना हवन्ते यातमिषा च विदुषे च वाजम् ॥

etāni vāṃ śravasyā sudānū brahmāṅgūṣaṃ sadanaṃ rodasyoḥ | yadvāṃ pajrāso aśvinā havante yātamiṣā ca viduṣe ca vājam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-10, as read from the print.) — in these and other ṛks the name of the pajra lineage is praised. Since Kakṣīvat was born in this lineage, he too has the name pajriya.

प्र या घोषे भृगवाणे न शोभे ययां वाचा यजति पज्रियो वाम् । प्रैषयुर्न विद्वान् ॥

सुषुप्सा वां वरुण मित्र रातिर्गवां शता पृक्षयामेषु पज्रे । श्रुतरथे प्रियरथे दधानाः सद्यः पुष्टिं निरुन्धानासो अग्मन् ॥

suṣupsā vāṃ varuṇa mitra rātirgavāṃ śatā pṛkṣayāmeṣu pajre | śrutarathe priyarathe dadhānāḥ sadyaḥ puṣṭiṃ nirundhānāso agman ‖

In the same way, in the present ṛk Sāyaṇa has explained pajrā as annavantaḥ aṅgirasaḥ.

Read from the image; the OCR is partly garbled. The words "agdhitā [?]" in the first sentence — the print has "bhojyā bhogayogyāgdhitā", which I read as "…āgadhitā" — and "yādanāma [?]" are doubtful. "Having been asked for union, Bhāvayavya, realising that his own wife Romaśā is not mature, says it, laughing. Bhojyā — fit for enjoyment, āgadhitā — taken on all sides, accepted; likewise parigadhitā — taken all round; the repetition is for the sake of great regard: 'gadhyaṃ gṛhṇāteḥ', says Yāska (Ni. 5-15). Or else āgadhitā — one who approaches from all sides … with the inner [that is, secret] speech by procreation, by arms and the rest: 'gadyatir mitho-bhāvakarmā', says Yāska (Ni. 5-15). In the first view the man is the principal one; in the latter, the woman: that is the difference. What is she like? She who jaṅgahe — grips exceedingly, never lets go. A simile of the strong grasp: kaśīkā iva — kaśīkā is the weasel with young; as she plays long with her mate and never lets him go, so she. Moreover this enjoyable one is yādurī: yādurī — she who gives much water in the form of semen, i.e. rich in semen. Such a one yāśūnām — of acts of union: yaśa is a name for procreation; the acts connected with it, yaśūni, are enjoyments; hundreds, countless, of these she gives to me."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Bhojyā — fit for enjoyment; yā — which (Romaśā); āgadhitā — accepted (and); parigadhitā — embraced; kaśīkā iva — like a female weasel; jaṅgahe — [she] who tightly clasps; (sā — she); yādurī — one richly provided with the water of semen; yāśūnām śatā — hundreds (countless) of acts of enjoyment; mahyam — to me; dadāti — gives.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Romaśā, fit for enjoyment, accepted, clasps tightly like a female weasel; and, being rich in semen, gives me endless pleasures of union.

Printed English (as printed): She, who, when her desires are assented to, clings as tenaciously as a female weasel, and who is ripe for enjoyment, yields me infinite delight.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6.

This ṛk and the next are the conversation between Bhāvayavya and his wife Romaśā. This Romaśā is the daughter of Bṛhaspati; at one time, with a desire for union, she went to her husband Bhāvayavya and asked that her desire be satisfied; in reply to that, Bhāvayavya spoke this ṛk. In reply to Bhāvayavya's words, Romaśā speaks the next ṛk. In these two ṛks, as in a dialogue of union, there is no matter such as the praise of a deity, which is common to sūktas and ṛks. Since the talk of union in these ṛks is not connected with the subject of this sūkta, some express doubt as to how it came to be included here. Moreover, of the seven ṛks of this sūkta, the first five are of Triṣṭubh metre and only these two ṛks are of Anuṣṭubh metre; so they are not a part of this sūkta. Somehow, for some other reason, they have been included here. It is indeed a wonder that matters of private life, unconnected with the subject, have been inserted into ṛks and included here.

The main idea of this ṛk and of the next may be stated thus: Bhāvayavya and his wife Romaśā speak teasingly to each other; Bhāvayavya, speaking indirectly, says in this way —

original p. 243

Special topics, Ṛk 6, continued — the dialogue: Bhāvayavya (teasing his wife Romaśā): "O, this Romaśā, like a female weasel that never lets go of her beloved male weasel, once she has clasped him (for enjoyment), wishes to embrace me a hundred times. Her body is full (or: wet) with semen."

Romaśā: "O husband, do not laugh at me as being young in age and not fit for union. Come to my side (for union), and embrace me well, clasping my limbs. Do not suppose that my limbs are not yet well grown and thus not fit for union. For my womb and other parts are thickly covered with well-grown hair, like the body of a ewe of the Gandhāra country."

The main subject here is this: when Romaśā, with desire, begged her husband, Bhāvayavya laughed at his wife as being young in age and not fit for union. In answer to that, Romaśā says that she is not a girl but a grown woman fit for union, and, to make this firm, gives an example. In the state of manhood, the hair on the hands and feet and the other limbs is naturally thick, and it indicates that they have passed boyhood and have come into youth; but for women, when they are in youth, hair on hands and feet is unusual — one may say impossible; but on the head, and chiefly in the region of the womb, thickly grown hair indicates the state of youth. Therefore, to support the point that she is in youth and fit for union, Romaśā tells the example that her womb region, like a ewe of the Gandhāra country or like the womb of a pregnant woman, is full of hair. The country of Gandhāra must be the country near Kandahar (the print has "Kandahar" in Latin letters); since that is a cold country, the sheep and other animals have much hair; so that example is told here.

āgadhitā, parigadhitā — in giving the derivation of these words, Yāska takes this very ṛk as the example, saying:

गध्यतिर्भावकर्मा । आगधिता परिगधिता इत्यपि निगमो भवति ।

gadhyatirbhāvakarmā | āgadhitā parigadhitā ityapi nigamo bhavati |

(Ni. 5-15 [?], as printed "೫-೧೫".) The word gadhyati means "mixing, uniting". Therefore in the present ṛk the "mixing of the limbs of husband and wife" means that the limbs of both are in contact with each other, one embracing the other;

original p. 244

this is the idea that the bhāṣyakāra indicates. Therefore the idea is that the two words āgadhitā and parigadhitā have the same sense, with a slight difference of more or less. In this matter Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, has given this explanation for the ṛk:

आगधितेति भावयव्यस्यार्षम् । आगधिता आगृहीता अभिमिश्रिता च । परिगधिता च परिमिश्रिता बाहुभ्यां मया परिष्वक्तेत्यर्थः । या कशीकेव प्रतिकशं कशीकेव स हि नकुलजातिः काञ्चिद्दीने कशामिति श्रूयतेऽश्वमेधे । सा यथा मदकाले प्रतिकशमतितरां परिष्वजति स हि तस्याः परिष्वजनस्वभावः । एवं या मा आजंगहे परिगृह्णाति बाहुभ्याम् । परिगृह्य च ददाति । यादुरीया आदरवती । अथवा यादः रेतःसेकेन तदस्यास्तीति । यादः इत्युदकनामसु पठितम् । आह किं ददाति मह्यम् ? इति । उच्यते — याशूनां मैथुनाख्यानां शता शतानि बहुश इत्यर्थः । या एवंप्रकारा सा मम भोज्या पत्नीत्यभिप्रायः । एवमत्र मैथुनसंबन्धात्शब्दसारूप्याच्च गध्यतिर्मिश्रीभावकर्मेत्युपपद्यते ॥

āgadhiteti bhāvayavyasyārṣam | āgadhitā āgṛhītā abhimiśritā ca | parigadhitā ca parimiśritā bāhubhyāṃ mayā pariṣvaktetyarthaḥ | yā kaśīkeva pratikaśaṃ kaśīkeva sa hi nakulajātiḥ kāñciddīne kaśāmiti śrūyate 'śvamedhe | sā yathā madakāle pratikaśamatitarāṃ pariṣvajati sa hi tasyāḥ pariṣvajanasvabhāvaḥ | evaṃ yā mā ājaṃgahe parigṛhṇāti bāhubhyām | parigṛhya ca dadāti | yādurīyā ādaravatī | athavā yādaḥ retaḥsekena tadasyāstīti | yādaḥ ityudakanāmasu paṭhitam | āha kiṃ dadāti mahyam ? iti | ucyate — yāśūnāṃ maithunākhyānāṃ śatā śatāni bahuśa ityarthaḥ | yā evaṃprakārā sā mama bhojyā patnītyabhiprāyaḥ | evamatra maithunasaṃbandhātśabdasārūpyācca gadhyatirmiśrībhāvakarmetyupapadyate ‖

(Ni. 5-15 [?]; as printed "೩-೧೫"; the OCR reads "३-१५".) Read letter by letter; the Sanskrit of this long Durga passage is partly in small type, and the words I am least sure of are "kāñcid dīne kaśām" and "svabhāvaḥ"; I mark them as read, without completing. "'Āgadhitā' is a word of Bhāvayavya's [verse]. Āgadhitā — accepted, mixed, parigadhitā — mixed all round, embraced by me with the arms: this is the sense. Kaśīkā iva — the kaśīkā, namely a weasel-kind; … as she at the time of rut embraces him closely [the male], for embracing is her nature; so she who, taking hold of me, grips with the arms, and having gripped, gives. Yādurī — [one] with abundance; or, from yādaḥ, water, [she] has it by the sprinkling of semen (yādaḥ is read among the names of water). What does she give me? It is said: of yāśūnām — [acts] called union — hundreds, many times: that is the sense. Such a one is my enjoyable wife: this is the intention. Thus here, by the connection with union and by similarity of the word, 'gadhyatir miśrībhāvakarma' (gadhyati means the act of mixing) is established."

The chief meaning of this we have already explained, so there is no need to repeat it.

kaśīkā — kaśīkā nāma sūtavatsā nakulī: a female weasel who has just given birth. Sāyaṇa explains the fitness of the simile thus: sā yathā patyā saha cirakālaṃ krīḍati na kadācid api vimuñcati tadvadeṣāpi — after giving birth, the female weasel, wishing union with her mate, does not leave him, and remains with him, fully satisfying the mate's desire. Here Bhāvayavya's wife Romaśā, like the female weasel, does not leave the husband but embraces him; so the example is given. And "jaṅgahe", the verb, is a repetition (a form of intensity) and denotes the nature of the embrace.

yādurī — the word yādurī (yādus) is recorded among the names of water; here it means "water in the form of semen".

yāśūnām — yaśa iti prajananānāma | tatsaṃbandhīni karmāṇi yāśūni bhogāḥ: yaśa is a name of procreation; the acts connected with it are yāśūni, "enjoyments": the meaning is "pleasures of union and the like that are the means of begetting offspring".

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). āgadhitā — the root gadh is used in the sense of "taking". 'gadhyaṃ gṛhṇāteḥ' (Ni. 5-15), says Yāska. In the passive, the suffix kta; the augment iṭ; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

रोमशा नाम बृहस्पतेः पुत्री ब्रह्मवादिनी परिहसन्तं स्वपतिं प्रत्याह । भो पते मे माम् । द्वितीयार्थे चतुर्थी । उपोप । द्वितीय उपशब्दः पादपूरणः । उपेत्य परा मृश । सम्यक् स्पृश । भोगयोग्यामवगत्येत्यर्थः । यद्वा । मे मम गोपनीयमङ्गं मुपोप परामृश । अत्यन्तं नान्तरं स्वकीयं परामर्शभावशङ्कां निवारयति । मे मदङ्गानि रोमाणि दभ्राणि मा मन्यथाः । अल्पानि मा बुद्ध्यस्व । दभ्रमर्भकमित्यल्पस्येति दभ्रं दभ्नोतेरिति यास्कः । नि. ३-२० । अदभ्रत्वमेव विशदयति । अहं रोमशा बहुरोमयुक्तास्मि । यतोऽहमीदृश्यतः सर्वा संपूर्णावयवास्मि । रोमशत्वे दृष्टान्तः । गन्धारीणामविकेव । गन्धारा केशां संबन्धिन्यो विजातिरिव [?] । तद्देशस्था आनवो मेषा यथा रोमशाः कथाहमस्मि । देशः । यद्वा । गन्धारीणां गर्भधारिणीनां स्त्रीणामविकार्थं तर्पयन्ती योनिरिव । तासामा प्रसवं रोमादिविकर्तनस्य शास्त्रे निषिद्धत्वाद्योनिः रोमशा भवति । अतः सोपमियते । यतोऽयं सर्वादृशीतो मामुपैहीं माम् [?] । मावबुध्यस्वेत्यर्थः ॥

romaśā nāma bṛhaspateḥ putrī brahmavādinī parihasantaṃ svapatiṃ pratyāha | bho pate me mām | dvitīyārthe caturthī | upopa | dvitīya upaśabdaḥ pādapūraṇaḥ | upetya parā mṛśa | samyak spṛśa | bhogayogyāmavagatyetyarthaḥ | yadvā | me mama gopanīyamaṅgaṃ mupopa parāmṛśa | atyantaṃ nāntaraṃ svakīyaṃ parāmarśabhāvaśaṅkāṃ nivārayati | me madaṅgāni romāṇi dabhrāṇi mā manyathāḥ | alpāni mā buddhyasva | dabhramarbhakamityalpasyeti dabhraṃ dabhnoteriti yāskaḥ | ni. 3-20 | adabhratvameva viśadayati | ahaṃ romaśā bahuromayuktāsmi | yato 'hamīdṛśyataḥ sarvā saṃpūrṇāvayavāsmi | romaśatve dṛṣṭāntaḥ | gandhārīṇāmavikeva | gandhārā keśāṃ saṃbandhinyo vijātiriva [?] | taddeśasthā ānavo meṣā yathā romaśāḥ kathāhamasmi | deśaḥ | yadvā | gandhārīṇāṃ garbhadhāriṇīnāṃ strīṇāmavikārthaṃ tarpayantī yoniriva | tāsāmā prasavaṃ romādivikartanasya śāstre niṣiddhatvādyoniḥ romaśā bhavati | ataḥ sopamiyate | yato 'yaṃ sarvādṛśīto māmupaihīṃ mām [?] | māvabudhyasvetyarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the middle of this bhāṣya — from "nāntaraṃ svakīyaṃ" to "mām" — is small and I have transcribed only what is legible; the words marked [?] are doubtful and the OCR here is badly garbled. The sense is secure from the Kannada pratipadārtha and the p. 247 comment. "Romaśā, the daughter of Bṛhaspati, a brahmavādinī, says to her husband who is teasing: O husband, me — to me (the dative has the sense of the accusative); upopa — the second upa is a pāda-filler; coming near, parā mṛśa — touch properly, understanding that I am fit for enjoyment. Or else: touch my part that is to be hidden; she dispels the doubt about the touch. Me dabhrāṇi mā manyathāḥ — do not think my limbs, my hairs, dabhrāṇi — small, few: 'dabhram arbhakam alpasya', 'dabhraṃ dabhnoteḥ', says Yāska (Ni. 3-20). She makes clear the not-smallness: I, Romaśā, am with abundant hair; therefore I am sarvā — complete in all limbs. As an example for the hairiness: gandhārīṇām avikā iva — as the ewes of Gandhāra, of that country, are woolly, so am I; the country [is to be thought of]. Or else: like the womb of pregnant women, which, since it is forbidden by the śāstra to cut the hair [of that part] until delivery, is hairy — hence this comparison. Since this is so, therefore come to me; do not think of me [as immature]: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Bho pate — O husband; me — me; upa upa — [come] near well; parā mṛśa — touch well; me — my (limbs); dabhrāṇi — small (few) things; mā manyathāḥ — do not think; aham — I; gandhārīṇām avikā iva — like a ewe of the Gandhāra country (or like the womb of the pregnant woman); romaśā — hairy; (ataḥ — therefore); sarvā — with developed limbs; asmi — I am.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O husband, come to me and touch (my limbs); I am hairy like the ewe of the Gandhāra country (or like the wombs of pregnant women); therefore I am of mature limbs; so do not think me immature.

dabhrāṇi — the word dabhra is recorded among the names of "small" (Ni. 3-13 [?]; as printed "೩-೧೩"). Dabhram arbhakam ity alpasya | dabhraṃ dabhnoteḥ sudambhaṃ bhavati (Ni. 3-20): from the root dambh, meaning "to destroy", the word dabhra gives the meaning "small", "little": that is, "easily destroyed". In the present ṛk Bhāvayavya's wife says that she is not such a tender one, but a grown woman fit for enjoyment. For the explanation of this word the author of the Nirukta has cited this very ṛk (Ni. 3-20).

gandhārīṇām avikā iva romaśā — gives two meanings. First: "a ewe of the Gandhāra country, one with exceedingly abundant hair". Second: "one with hair like the womb of a pregnant woman".

Since the main idea of this ṛk and the particulars connected with it have been included in the special topics of the preceding ṛk and translated there, I give here only the commentary of Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta:

उपोप मे परामृश .... । भावयव्यस्येयमार्षम् । अनुष्टुप् । भावयव्यमेव सा भर्तारं तेनानुपेयमाना ब्रवीति । हे राजन् उपगम्य उपस्पृश्य च मे मम परामृश यः प्रदेशः पुरुषेण प्रियया परामृष्टव्यः । किंच मा मे दभ्राणि मन्यथाः अल्पकानि लोमानि मा मन्यथाः । जानेऽहमेतत् । यथा अलोमिकाया उपगमः प्रतिषिद्धः स्मृतौ — "नाजातलोम्नीमुपहासमिच्छेत्" इति । यते वेदयामि सर्वाहमस्मि रोमशा सर्वेष्वङ्गेषु मदीयान्युत्पन्नानि रोमाणि येषु कामो [?] मुत्सृजन्ते [?] । कथं च पुनरहमस्मि रोमशा ? गन्धारीणामिवाविका गन्धारदेशजातानामविकानां मध्ये या सुष्ठु रोमशा भवेत् तथाहमस्मि रोमशा, निःशङ्को मामुपगच्छेत्यभिप्रायः ॥

upopa me parāmṛśa .... | bhāvayavyasyeyamārṣam | anuṣṭup | bhāvayavyameva sā bhartāraṃ tenānupeyamānā bravīti | he rājan upagamya upaspṛśya ca me mama parāmṛśa yaḥ pradeśaḥ puruṣeṇa priyayā parāmṛṣṭavyaḥ | kiṃca mā me dabhrāṇi manyathāḥ alpakāni lomāni mā manyathāḥ | jāne 'hametat | yathā alomikāyā upagamaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ smṛtau — "nājātalomnīmupahāsamicchet" iti | yate vedayāmi sarvāhamasmi romaśā sarveṣvaṅgeṣu madīyānyutpannāni romāṇi yeṣu kāmo [?] mutsṛjante [?] | kathaṃ ca punarahamasmi romaśā ? gandhārīṇāmivāvikā gandhāradeśajātānāmavikānāṃ madhye yā suṣṭhu romaśā bhavet tathāhamasmi romaśā, niḥśaṅko māmupagacchetyabhiprāyaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the Nirukta commentary is in small type, the words marked [?] are doubtful, and the quotation from the Smṛti "nājātalomnīm upahāsam iccheta" is as printed — I do not complete the Smṛti words. "'Upopa me parāmṛśa': this is Bhāvayavya's [verse]; Anuṣṭubh. She, the wife, urged by her husband Bhāvayavya … says: 'O king, coming near and touching me, parāmṛśa — the region which a man should touch with the beloved … And do not think dabhrāṇi — small hairs; I know this: just as in the Smṛti the approach to a woman without hair is forbidden, "one should not seek sport with her whose hair has not grown"; therefore I tell you: sarvāham asmi romaśā — I am hairy in all limbs, my hairs have grown in those [places] … And how am I hairy? Gandhārīṇām ivāvikā — as, among the ewes born in the Gandhāra country, the one that is well covered with wool, so I am hairy; come to me without fear': this is the intention."

The subject of this ṛk has been introduced in the explanation of the preceding ṛk: in order to establish that she is not a girl but a young woman fit for union, Romaśā says that the hair that indicates youth has grown on her limbs, and gives the example of the ewe of Gandhāra.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). me — by the statement "vivakṣataḥ kārakāṇi bhavanti" the dative is used in the sense of the accusative. mṛśa — root mṛśa āmarśane; Tudādi (āmarśana = touching); loṭ second person singular; tiṅ-nighāta after a non-verb word. dabhrāṇi — root dambhu dambhane; sthāyitañcivañci… [print: "ಸ್ಥಾಯಿತಂಚಿವಂಚಿ", Uṇ. 2-?] gives rak; since kit, anidito hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti elides the nasal of the penultimate; final-acute by the suffix; accusative plural. manyathāḥ — root manu avabodhane; Divādi; laṅ second person singular; since mā is connected, na māṅyoge (Pā. 6-4-74) gives no augment aṭ; tiṅ-nighāta. asmi — root as bhuvi; laṭ first person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. romaśā — romāṇi asyāḥ santi iti romaśā; because it belongs to the lomādi group, lomādipāmādipicchādibhyaḥ śanelacaḥ (Pā. 5-2-100) gives the suffix śa; final-acute by the suffix accent; in the feminine ṭāp. avikā — avir eva avikā; suffix ka in the sense of itself; final-acute by the suffix accent. ‖ 7 ‖

Sūkta 127 — agniṃ hotāram (begins at the head of printed p. 249; the Anuvāka 19 opens here)

original p. 249

ನೂರ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra ippattēḷaneya sūktavu (the one hundred and twenty-seventh Sūkta). This Sūkta opens with a long Kannada introduction on the ṛṣi Paruccheṣa, on the style of his ṛks and on their use in the śastra; the Sanskrit introduction (bhūmikā) of Sāyaṇa and the table follow later. I give the Kannada in translation.

With this Sūkta the nineteenth Anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala begins. In this Anuvāka there are 7 Sūktas, 127 to 133. In the next Anuvāka, the twentieth, there are 6 Sūktas, 134 to 139. The ṛṣi of all the 13 Sūktas of these two Anuvākas is Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi, that is, the son of Divodāsa, named Paruccheṣa. We have already explained about Divodāsa: Divodāsa or Divodāsa Atithigva is a king of very ancient times (the Vedic age). He was the son of Vadhryaśva and the father of Sudās [as read: "ವದ್ಧ್ರ್ಯಶ್ವ … ಸುವಾಸ" — the names are small and I give them as I read]. His name occurs in many places in the Ṛgveda. The chief enemy of this Divodāsa was Śambara, or Dāsa, the leader of the forest people who lived in hills and mountains; this is said there. The sūktas seen by Divodāsa himself are not found anywhere in the Ṛgveda. Therefore modern scholars differ in opinion whether his son, the ṛṣi Paruccheṣa, is the seer of these sūktas. Be that as it may, according to the Anukramaṇī — agnimīḷādaśa paruccheṣo daivodāsirāgneyaṃ tu pārucchepaṃ sarvam atyaṣṭaṃ tatrādyātiśakvarī … [as read; the last word, "ṣaṣṭhīti", is doubtful] — it is established that the ṛṣi of all 13 Sūktas (127–139) is Paruccheṣa. Yāska says in his Nirukta —

परुच्छेप ऋषिः । पर्ववच्छेपः परुषिपरुषि शेपोऽस्येति वा ।

parucchepa ṛṣiḥ | parvavacchepaḥ paruṣiparuṣi śepo 'syeti vā |

(Ni. 10-42, as printed "೧೦-೪೨"; the OCR reads "१०-४३".) That is, because he grew up in great comfort, [he had] a śepa in every joint, i.e., one endowed with good development in all the limbs and joints: such is the main idea. The literal sense of the word paruccheṣa here is not so important. The story of this ṛṣi is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Adhyāya 22, Khaṇḍa 5–6) and in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa (13-4-5). In these 13 Sūktas seen by Paruccheṣa there are in all 100 ṛks. [A statement about the son of Paruccheṣa, Ānānata Pāruccheṣi, follows:] Ānānataḥ Pāruccheṣi is the seer of the ṛks 1–[?] of the 1[?]th Sūkta of the ninth maṇḍala [as printed; numerals small]. All these ṛks have a special feature of their own. They are in the metres Atyaṣṭi, Atiśakvarī and Atidhṛti, the plural count of which is… The 127th sūkta is of the metre Atiśakvarī; the rest of the sūktas (except some ṛks) are composed in Atyaṣṭi. Such metres have 8 pādas and in all 6[?]… syllables, with an addition or deficiency of one or two syllables in some contexts. We have described the characteristics of these metres with examples in Ṛk Saṃhitā, part 1, pp. 221–231. Another peculiarity of the ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa — Yāska says —

अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते यथाहो दर्शनीयाहो दर्शनीयेति । तत्परुच्छेपस्य शीलम् ॥

abhyāse bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyante yathāho darśanīyāho darśanīyeti | tatparucchepasya śīlam ‖

(Ni. 10-43 [?], as printed "೧೦-೪೩".) That is, in the ṛks seen by this ṛṣi abhyāsa, that is, repetition, is seen specially. Ordinarily in ṛks of metres such as Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh and Jagatī there are only two parts, a first half and a second half. But in ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa, of Atyaṣṭi and other metres, there are three halves. At the end of the first and third of these three halves one or two words recur like a refrain (pallavi). For example —

अग्निं होतारं मन्ये दास्वन्तं वसुं सूनुं सहसो जातवेदसं विप्रं न जातवेदसम् ।

agniṃ hotāraṃ manye dāsvantaṃ vasuṃ sūnuṃ sahaso jātavedasaṃ vipraṃ na jātavedasam |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-127-1, the first ṛk of this very Sūkta, as printed; the OCR agrees.) In this ṛk the word jātavedasam is repeated; between this repetition stand the words vipraṃ na. This repeating word is always at the end of a sentence.

निष्षहमाणो यमते नायते धन्वासहा नायते ।

niṣṣahamāṇo yamate nāyate dhanvāsahā nāyate |

Read letter by letter; the sense is "he who overpowers restrains, does not move away; he who surpasses in the bow does not move away" — I give no gloss for the unclear words. In this ṛk the words na āyate are repeated, and between them stands the word dhanvāsahā. Yāska states this subject of repetition: abhyāse bhūyāṃsam arthaṃ manyante yathāho darśanīyāho darśanīyeti, and explains its meaning. The commentator on this sentence of the Nirukta (Durga) —

अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते । शब्दाभ्यासे यत्रान्यो विशेषो नास्ति शिष्टं विशेषमाचार्या मन्त्रार्थचिन्तका मन्यन्ते — यदुतार्थभूयस्त्वमिति । न ह्येकस्मात्स एव शब्दः पुनरभ्यस्यते । लोकेऽपि चैतद्दृष्टम् — शब्दाभ्यासेऽर्थभूयस्त्वमिति । यथा — अहो दर्शनीयः ! अहो दर्शनीयः ! इति । गुणातिशये हि स्त्रियाः शब्दाभ्यासः । तस्मान्मन्त्रेष्वपि तद्वदेवेति न्यायम् ॥

abhyāse bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyante | śabdābhyāse yatrānyo viśeṣo nāsti śiṣṭaṃ viśeṣamācāryā mantrārthacintakā manyante — yadutārthabhūyastvamiti | na hyekasmātsa eva śabdaḥ punarabhyasyate | loke 'pi caitaddṛṣṭam — śabdābhyāse 'rthabhūyastvamiti | yathā — aho darśanīyaḥ ! aho darśanīyaḥ ! iti | guṇātiśaye hi striyāḥ śabdābhyāsaḥ | tasmānmantreṣvapi tadvadeveti nyāyam ‖

Read letter by letter from the print; "mantrārthacintakāḥ" and "stṛiyāḥ" [?] are doubtful. That is, when a word is uttered twice in a sentence, in the case where the word has no two different senses, the repetition of the word indicates excess of meaning; that is, it is used in order to give prominence to the matter said, or to say it so that it is well fixed in the mind. For example, when describing the beauty of women, the repeated "aho darśanīyā, aho darśanīyā" — "what a lovely one! what a lovely one!" — Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12.

original p. 251

— there is a custom in the world of speaking so, to make clear the idea of surpassing beauty; as there, so it must be thought here too, he has said. But Sāyaṇa has in general explained the repeated words in these ṛks by giving them different meanings.

This kind of repetition has another purpose. Many ṛks of the Ṛgveda have been composed so as to be fit for singing. It is well known to all in the world that when a composition set to a rāga and the like is sung, the pallavi and the anupallavi are sung again and again. Therefore these ṛks, and many other ṛks, must have been composed with the purpose of being sung so as to be pleasing to hear. For this very reason, it is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that these Pārucchepa mantras are laid down for the recitation of the śastra; and for this very reason the greater part of the Sāmaveda consists of Ṛgveda ṛks.

When the Vedic mantras are understood with their meaning and recited or sung with devotion and faith, with the accents, there arises, for those who recite and for the audience who hear such Vedic chanting, an indescribable joy; this has come into the experience of many. Some modern scholars, such as Westerners, look at the Vedic mantras only from the point of view of meaning, and therefore have no chance of understanding fully the musical nature of the Vedic mantras; so they do not take pains for it. Some say that, though these ṛks are metrical, there are many dropped syllables (lopa) and violations of grammar in them, and that they are not suited to mature poetry. But their opinion is not tenable. For at that time there was no written language; everything had to be learnt by heart; therefore it is natural that attention should be given to pronunciation more than to meaning. And, there being no written language and no grammar, it is natural that words and the style of language current at that time were used. It must not be forgotten that grammatical treatises such as Pāṇini's were composed on the basis of Vedic words. Grammar comes out of language, not language out of grammar; language is the root; grammar is made to follow it. Therefore, it is not appropriate to apply grammatical rules strictly to the forms of words and so on that are seen in the Vedic mantras.

As was said before, many ṛks may have been composed from the point of view of singing. For that reason, in many contexts short syllables are used as long ones and long ones as short; this is seen here and there. For example, words such as ādha, ghā, sma and others are long in the Saṃhitā text. In the same way ṛtavṛdhā is pronounced as ṛtāvṛdhā.

original p. 252

…and so on. In many contexts one or two syllables of words are dropped; for example, tmanā in place of ātmanā, and bhāvyasya in place of bhāvayavyasya. Such defects of dropping are not new in the modern languages either. For example, singers, when they sing compositions, sing Kṛṣṇā mūruti in place of Kṛṣṇamūrti, and kīruti for kīrti. Such drops are many. Since the Vedic mantras have come down handed on by pronunciation alone through tradition, such small drops (which are not drops at all) are natural.

There is no doubt that the sūktas seen by Paruccheṣa belong to very ancient mantras. Because the meaning of some words and sentences in these ṛks is very difficult and unclear, the meaning does not fit well in many contexts. A large part of these mantras has been included in the śastra mantras. Their explanation is in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows:

देवासुरा वा एषु लोकेषु समयतन्त ते वै देवाः षष्ठेनैवाह्ना [?] लोकेभ्योऽसुरान्प्राणुदन्त तेषां यान्यन्तर्हस्तीनानि [?] वसून्यासंस्तान्यादाय समुद्रं प्रौहन् [?] ते वा एतेनैव छन्दसानुहायान्तर्हस्तीनानि [?] वसून्यादत्त तद्यदेतत्पदं पुनःपदं स एनान्कुत आसञ्जनाय [?] । आ द्विषतो वसु दत्ते निरेनमेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो लोकेभ्यो नुदते य एवं वेद ॥

devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samayatanta te vai devāḥ ṣaṣṭhenaivāhnā [?] lokebhyo 'surānprāṇudanta teṣāṃ yānyantarhastīnāni [?] vasūnyāsaṃstānyādāya samudraṃ prauhan [?] te vā etenaiva chandasānuhāyāntarhastīnāni [?] vasūnyādatta tadyadetatpadaṃ punaḥpadaṃ sa enānkuta āsañjanāya [?] | ā dviṣato vasu datte nirenamebhyaḥ sarvebhyo lokebhyo nudate ya evaṃ veda ‖

(Ai. Br. 22-6, as printed "ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೨೨-೬".) Read letter by letter; this long passage is in small type and I have marked the words I could not make out reliably. The words antarhastīnāni, prauhan and kuta āsañjanāya are the doubtful ones. The gods and the Asuras once fought a great battle in this world. Then the gods, performing the rites on the sixth day (of the dvādaśāha sacrifice) and conquering the Asuras, drove them out of this world. Then the Asuras, being defeated, took the wealth — gold and the like — that had come into their hands, and went away from the battlefield and threw it into the sea. Afterwards the gods, pursuing the Asuras, recovered, by the power of reciting the ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa, the riches the Asuras had thrown into the sea. In this recovery, the repeated seventh pāda of the Paruccheṣa ṛks (the pāda like sumṛḷīko na ā gahi — "be gracious, come to us") helped them. In the world it is natural that people draw out with a hook (hook in the print, in Latin letters) a thing that has fallen into a depth, with a rod joined to it. In the same way, the repeated seventh pāda of ṛks seen by this ṛṣi has the intent that, drawing the wealth lying in the midst of the sea so as to make it return to the gods, one … Understanding this matter well, and reciting the mantra accordingly and performing the rite, a man conquers enemies and drives them out of this world, and himself gets their wealth.

In the morning pressing and the midday pressing (savana means the act of pressing and extracting the Soma from the creeper) of the sixth day of the dvādaśāha or daśarātra sacrifice, the seven priests belonging to the hotṛ group recite the prasthita-yājyā mantras. That is, one must first recite the Pārucchepa ṛks one by one, and then recite the prasthita-yājyā mantras one by one. Which Pārucchepa mantras are to be recited in this context? —

The ṛks from vṛṣaṃ indra vṛṣapāṇāsa indavaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-139-6, as printed) up to the last ṛk of this [139th] sūkta (1-139-11), and from pibā somam indra suvānam adribhiḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-2) up to the last ṛk of that sūkta (1-130-[?]) — these ṛks are to be recited one by one. The ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa are called "rohita" ("ascending"), because by reciting these ṛks Indra once mounted the seventh heaven. Here the "seven heavens" are the seven divisions of heaven, differing in excellence and inferiority; whoever recites these mantras thus and performs the sacrifice, he too ascends the seven heavens.

Here there is a special matter. It is the custom that on the fifth day of this sacrifice, at the times of pressing, ṛks of five pādas (Paṅkti metre) are recited; and on the sixth day, ṛks of six pādas. Yet why are the seven-pāda Pārucchepa ṛks recited on that day? — They say: on all six days one goes beyond the six heavens by the six pādas of the ṛk, and mounts the seventh heaven by the seventh pāda. Because the seventh pāda is a repetition, in the ṛk there are counted only six pādas; the seventh pāda is [also] praised, and by reciting it one obtains…

One must praise with the trayastriṃśa stoma; one must sing with the Sāman called Raivata; one must recite ṛks of the atichandas metres (as śastra mantras). These are the special rites of this sixth day.

The metre-names and the sūtra reference "Piṅ. 4-1" [?] are as read; "ṣaṣṭhīti" at the end of the Anukramaṇī quotation I cannot confirm. "In the nineteenth Anuvāka there are seven sūktas. Of them, the first, beginning agniṃ hotāram, of eleven ṛks, is of Paruccheṣa son of Divodāsa, addressed to Agni, in Aṣṭi [as printed ātyaṣṭi] metre. Sa hi śardhaḥ is of seventy-six syllables, Atidhṛti. Among the metres Utkṛti, Abhikṛti, Saṃkṛti, Vikṛti, Ākṛti, Prakṛti, Kṛti, Atikṛti, [Dhṛti, Atidhṛti, Aṣṭi, Atyaṣṭi], beginning at one hundred and four syllables and dropping four each time, each metre comes about; thus Atidhṛti would have the stated count. All this is stated in the metre-treatise in the sūtras beginning catuḥśataṃ utkṛtiḥ (Piṅgala 4-1 [?]). And so the Anukramaṇī says: 'Agni — eleven; Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi; Āgneya; Pārucchepa; all Atyaṣṭi; in it the first Atidhṛti; the sixth …'. The special application of the sūkta is by liṅga: in the sixth day of the Daśarātra, in the morning pressing, one should sacrifice with other ṛks first before the prasthita-yājyās, together with the prākṛta ones. Of these, the first, addressed to Agni, is this one; it is laid down in the section 'of the sixth day, in the morning pressing' [Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra]: 'agniṃ hotāraṃ manye dāsvantaṃ dadharṣajña ha me januṣaṃ pūrvo aṅgirāḥ' (Āś. 8-1 [?])."

Anuvāda (Kannada). With this Sūkta the nineteenth Anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala begins. In this Anuvāka there are seven Sūktas. Of these seven Sūktas, the Sūkta beginning agniṃ hotāram is the first; it has eleven ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Paruccheṣa, the son of Divodāsa; the deity is Agni; the metre is Atyaṣṭi. The ṛk sa hi śardhaḥ is of the metre Atidhṛti, of 76 syllables. In the metres Utkṛti, Abhikṛti, Saṃkṛti, Vikṛti, Ākṛti, Prakṛti, Kṛti, Atidhṛti [as printed: "ಅತಿಧೃತಿ"], Dhṛti, Atyaṣṭi, Aṣṭi, the syllable-count of each ṛk goes down by four syllables from 104, and the last, the Aṣṭi, has 64 syllables. That is, from Utkṛti to Aṣṭi the counts are 104, 100, 96, 92, 88, 84, 80, 76, 72, 68, 64 (as printed: "೧೦೪, ೧೦೦, ೯೬, ೯೨, ೮೮, ೮೪, ೮೦, ೭೬, ೭೨, ೬೮, ೬೪" — I give the series as consistent with the printed pattern; the printed digits are small). Therefore the metres Atyaṣṭi and Atidhṛti are of 68 and 76 syllables. All this has been established in the metre-treatise by the sūtras beginning catuḥśatam utkṛtiḥ (Piṅ. 4-1 [?]). In the Anukramaṇī: agnim ekādaśa paruccheṣo daivodāsir āgneyaṃ tu pārucchepaṃ sarvam atyaṣṭaṃ tatrātidhṛtiḥ ṣaṣṭhīti. The special application of the sūkta is liṅga-based: on the sixth day of the Daśarātra sacrifice, in the morning pressing, in the rite of the prasthita-yājyā mantras, it is the custom to recite a ṛk before each yājyā mantra; of these the first, agniṃ hotāram, is to be recited by the Agni-priest. This matter is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavane, in the sūtra agniṃ hotāraṃ manye dāsvantaṃ dadharṣajña ha me januṣaṃ pūrvo aṅgirāḥ (Āś. 8-1).

"[I think of] Agni — the leader of all the divine armies, or, in sacrifices, the one led first — the hotṛ, who calls the gods to this sacrifice; or else, the hotṛ, the performer of the oblation: 'juhoter hotety aurṇavābhaḥ', says Yāska (Ni. 7-15). By the text 'he chose Agni today as hotṛ' [TB, as read], and agnim agna āvaha ('Agni, bring [the gods]'), the calling of the gods by Agni is well known. Agniṃ hotāraṃ manye — thus, manye ('I think') is connected with each epithet. Or else, since the performance of the sacrifice alone is desired, this alone is the predicate-epithet; the other epithets that follow are for praise. Dāsvantam — most generous; vasum — the cause of everyone's dwelling; sahasaḥ sūnum — the son of strength: at the time of the kindling by friction he is born, being churned with force; hence 'son' is figuratively said. Jātavedasam — the knower of what is born, one whose knowledge or strength is born; the word jātavedas has been explained in many ways by Yāska (Ni. 7-19). An illustration of jātavedas-ness: vipraṃ na jātavedasam — like a Brahmin, learned, intelligent, whom people hold in high esteem; so I too hold you: I praise [you]. The god endowed with the qualities stated — svadhvaraḥ, having a good sacrifice, well conducting the sacrifice — with ūrdhvayā — lofty, excellent — devāc'yā, that goes to the gods or worships the gods, kṛpā — with compassion, characterised by capacity: 'to the gods, one's own compassion' says Yāska (Ni. 6-8 [?]); endowed with the intent of carrying the oblation to them, ājuhvānasya — of the ghee being offered all round, sarpiṣaḥ — flowing, ghṛtasya — of the ghee that is melted and shining, vibhrāṣṭim anu — following specially its glow, he himself vaṣṭi — desires, accepts, the ghee with his flame."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Yaḥ devaḥ — which god Agni; svadhvaraḥ — endowed with a sacrifice beautified by him (one who conducts the sacrifice well); ūrdhvayā — excellent; devāc'yā — worshipping the gods; kṛpā — with compassion (being endowed with the power of carrying the oblation); ājuhvānasya — of (the sacrificer) who is invoking; sarpiṣaḥ — liquid; ghṛtasya — of the ghee; vibhrāṣṭim anu — following the flame; śociṣā — with (his own) flame; vaṣṭi — accepts; (taṃ — that); agnim — Agni (the leader of all the gods); hotāram — the one who calls the gods to our sacrifice (and the priest who performs the oblation); dāsvantam — the generous; vasum — the cause of dwelling (for all); sahasaḥ sūnum — the son of strength (necessarily produced in the kindling); jātavedasam — the intelligent; vipraṃ na — like a Brahmin; jātavedasam — one who knows everything that has been born; manye — I know (I praise).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Agni, who adorns (our) sacrifice, with excellent power that worships the gods (in the form of carrying the oblations), accepts, with his flames, the liquefied ghee offered by the sacrificer who invokes [the gods]; I know (I praise) such an Agni as the hotṛ who calls the gods to our sacrifice, as generous, as the cause of dwelling for all, and as omniscient like a wise Brahmin.

Printed English (as printed): I venerate Agni, the invoker (of the gods), the munificent, the giver of dwellings, the son of strength : he who knows all that exists, like a sage who is endowed with knowledge : who, the divine regenerator of sacrifices, through his lofty and reverential devotion, covets for the gods the blaze of the liquefied butter which is offered in oblation with his flames. Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 1.

agniṃ — sarvāsāṃ devasenānām agraṇyaṃ yajñeṣv agraṃ nīyamānaṃ vā: The word agni is used in two senses. In the first sense, "one who is the foremost of the divine armies, the army of the gods"; in the second, "the one who is led first, in sacrifices, before all, being invoked". On this Yāska says —

अग्निः पृथिवीस्थानस्तं प्रथमं व्याख्यास्यामः । अग्रणीर्भवति । अग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणीयते । अङ्गं नयति सन्नममानः ॥

agniḥ pṛthivīsthānastaṃ prathamaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | agraṇīrbhavati | agraṃ yajñeṣu praṇīyate | aṅgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ ‖

(Ni. 7-14 [?], as printed "೭-೧೪".) Agni has three places. Agni's work is spread through the three places — atmosphere, heaven and earth. Among these, since he pervades most the place of the earth, beginning with the terrestrial Agni he first explains, and gives three derivations of the form of the word agni. For the first, agraṇīr bhavati, Durgācārya says: sarveṣv artheṣu asāv ātmānam agraṃ nayati, sarvatra tathopakaroti yathā agraṃ sampadyate [?] — "in all matters he leads himself in front; he helps everywhere in such a way that the foremost place is attained", [or:] he is the chief (principal) one in Vedic rites and in worldly acts. Therefore agraṇīḥ, or — since it is said agnir vai devānāṃ senānīḥ, "Agni is the general of the gods' army" — because Agni himself, going first, is first for leading the gods to the sacrifices and so on, he is agraṇīḥ; and because he makes eminence for those who serve him he is also agraṇīḥ: thus the meaning is explained by the derivation agraṃ nayati iti agraṇīḥ.

Second: among the duties that must necessarily be done first in sacrifices, since no rite is done before the carrying forward (praṇayana) of Agni, [it is said] yajñeṣu agraṃ praṇīyate ("in sacrifices he is first led forward").

original p. 261

Special topics, Ṛk 1, continued — agniṃ: The second explanation [is that he is] the one who, among sacrifices, is made ready first; agraṃ praṇayanāt — since he is first made ready (or: brought forward) and carried: so the word agni is appropriately [explained as] "one who is called by the word agni".

The third derivation of the word agni is aṅgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ [as printed; read in the Nirukta as aṅgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ]. This god, in all rites, worldly or Vedic, is himself the chief; he makes everything else (that is inferior to himself) subordinate to himself; or, when he takes up a blade of grass or a piece of firewood, he makes it subordinate to himself and keeps it so; therefore he is called agni.

Agraṃ nayatīty agniḥ, agraṃ nīyata ity agniḥ, aṅgaṃ nayatīty agniḥ — thus Yāska has described the derivation of the word agni in three ways. The teacher Sthaulāṣṭhīvi [as printed "ಸ್ಥೌಲಾಷ್ಠೀವಿ"; the OCR "राज्यपि"] describes the nature of Agni as "one who makes whatever he receives ugly (burns it black)"; and the teacher Śākapūṇi —

त्रिभ्य आख्यातेभ्यो जायते । इताद्अक्ताद्दग्धाद्वा नीतात् । स खल्वेतेरकारमादत्ते गकारमनक्तेर्वा दहतेर्वा नीः परः ॥

tribhya ākhyātebhyo jāyate | itādaktāddagdhādvā nītāt | sa khalveterakāramādatte gakāramanaktervā dahatervā nīḥ paraḥ ‖

(Ni. 7-14 [?], as printed "೭-೧೪"; the OCR reads "२-१४".) Read letter by letter; "itād aktād dagdhād vā nītāt" and the second half are small and doubtful. — gives the derivation of the word agni: [it is formed] from three verbs — from i ("goes"), from añj ("anoints") or dah ("burns"), and from nī ("leads"); he takes the a from eti (he goes), the g from anakti or dahati, and nī after it. Durgācārya describes Agni's nature by his actions: eti ca nayati ca havīṃṣi dahati ca — or eti, vyanakti: he comes (eti), he carries oblations (nayati), he burns (dahati), he transforms (vyanakti). Sāyaṇa, explaining the word agni as one who is in front of the divine army, or one who is chief in the sacrifices, gives only two meanings.

hotāram — asmadyāgaṃ prati devānām āhvātāraṃ yadvā homaniṣpādakaṃ hotāram: "the one who calls the gods to our sacrifice, or the hotṛ who performs the oblation (and recites the mantra)": thus he explains two senses. The derivation of the word hotṛ is from the root hu dānādanayoḥ. The śruti "agnim adya hotāram avṛṇīta" (Tai. Brā. 2-6-15-1) shows that Agni is to be chosen as the hotṛ in the sacrifice; and the śruti "agnim agna āvaha" (Tai. Brā. 3-5-[?]) shows that one should first invoke Agni to call the gods. Hence both senses are possible. Therefore here too [Sāyaṇa] has said agniṃ hotāraṃ manye, and explained hotāram as the predicate-epithet of the word agni, the second-case words as the epithets of the word agni.

— the one sense. Yadvā yāganiṣpatter evāpekṣitatvād etad eva vidheyaviśeṣaṇam, itarāṇi tu vakṣyamāṇaviśeṣaṇāni stutiparāṇi: since the sacrifice must necessarily be completed, the word hotāram is the predicate-epithet and the other epithets are for praising Agni: this is the second explanation. By this the meaning arises that Agni himself is meant by the word hotṛ. Yāska, in the Nirukta, citing

अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजम् । होतारं रत्नधातमम् ॥

agnimīḷe purohitaṃ yajñasya devamṛtvijam | hotāraṃ ratnadhātamam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1, as printed.) says hotāraṃ hvātāraṃ juhoter hotā ity aurṇavābhaḥ (Ni. 7-15): the view of Aurṇavābha, that hotā derived from the root hu is "one who calls the gods to the sacrifice".

dāsvantam — atiśayena dānavantam: "the one who gives to the sacrificers in great quantity wealth and the like".

vasum — sarveṣāṃ nivāsahetum: "the cause of dwelling at ease for all". The word vasu is recorded among the names of rays (Ni. 1-[?]5, as printed "೨-೧೫" [?]) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). And in

सुगुरसत्सुहिरण्यः स्वश्वो बृहदस्मे वय इन्द्रो दधाति । यस्त्वायन्तं वसुना प्रातरित्वो मुक्षीजयेव पदिमुत्सिनाति ॥

sugurasatsuhiraṇyaḥ svaśvo bṛhadasme vaya indro dadhāti | yastvāyantaṃ vasunā prātaritvo mukṣījayeva padimutsināti ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-125-2, as printed.) vasunā is explained as annena, so the meaning "food" too arises.

देवी जोष्ट्री वसुधिती ययोरन्या ... [?] द्वेषांसि युयवदन्याव [?] ... । वार्याणि यजमानाय सुन्वते वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥

devī joṣṭrī vasudhitī yayoranyā ... [?] dveṣāṃsi yuyavadanyāva [?] ... | vāryāṇi yajamānāya sunvate vasuvane vasudheyasya vītāṃ yaja ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?], as printed "೨-೫-೧"? — doubtful; the middle of the first line I cannot read.) Here the word vasu is explained with the sense "wealth".

जम्या अत्र वसवो रन्त देवा उरावन्तरिक्षे मर्जयन्त शुभ्राः । अर्वाक्पथ उरुज्रयः कृणुध्वं श्रोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो नो अस्य ॥

jamyā atra vasavo ranta devā urāvantarikṣe marjayanta śubhrāḥ | arvākpatha urujrayaḥ kṛṇudhvaṃ śrotā dūtasya jagmuṣo no asya ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-62-5 [?], as printed "೬-೬೨-೬"? — numerals small.) Read letter by letter; jamyā / jmayā — the first word is doubtful in the print. Here the word vasavaḥ is explained as "gods". But Sāyaṇa explains the word vasu as "cause of dwelling".

sahasaḥ sūnum — balasya putram: "the son of strength": at the sacrifice, men churn in the araṇi with strength and thereby produce Agni; since Agni is born by strength, the figurative usage "son of strength" is here.

The word sahas is recorded among the one hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-[?]4, as printed "೨-೩೪" [?]) and among the twenty-eight names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]).

एता विश्वा सवना तूतुमा कृषे स्वयं सूनो सहसो यानि दधिषे । वराय ते पात्रं धर्मणे तना यज्ञो मन्त्रो ब्रह्मोद्यतं वचः ॥

etā viśvā savanā tūtumā kṛṣe svayaṃ sūno sahaso yāni dadhiṣe | varāya te pātraṃ dharmaṇe tanā yajño mantro brahmodyataṃ vacaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-6 [?], as printed "೧೦-೮೦-೬"? — numerals small.) Read letter by letter; the second half is as printed and I do not claim it. In this ṛk, sahasaḥ sūno "O son of strength" is said to be addressed to Agni, and Durgācārya has described [it as] "some say (sutam) his son".

jātavedasam — jātānāṃ veditāraṃ jātaprajñaṃ jātabalaṃ vā: "the knower of all that is born; or one whose knowledge is born; or one whose strength is born": Sāyaṇa explains the word jātaveda, which teaches the nature of Agni, in three ways: he who knows all that has come into being; he who has the power of intelligence by which everything natural can be known; he who has abundant power. Yāska in the Nirukta says —

जातानि वेद । जातानि वैनं विदुः । जाते जाते विद्यत इति वा । जातवित्तो वा जातधनः । जातविद्यो वा जातप्रज्ञानः ॥

jātāni veda | jātāni vainaṃ viduḥ | jāte jāte vidyata iti vā | jātavitto vā jātadhanaḥ | jātavidyo vā jātaprajñānaḥ ‖

(Ni. 7-19, as printed "೭-೧೯"; the OCR reads "२-१०".) Nothing in this world that is born is unknown to him; hence Agni is omniscient; all beings that are born know Agni; hence he is fit to be known by all.

यत्र ज्ञातः पशूनविन्देति तद्ज्ञातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वमिति ब्राह्मणं तस्मात्सर्वान्पशवोऽग्निमभि सर्पन्तीति च ॥

yatra jñātaḥ paśūnavindeti tadjñātavedaso jātavedastvamiti brāhmaṇaṃ tasmātsarvānpaśavo 'gnimabhi sarpantīti ca ‖

The Brāhmaṇa passage is small and the OCR garbles it; I give it as read and mark it uncertain. — this śruti sentence clearly says that Agni pervades everything that is born.

Describing the nature of Agni as one who has wealth and who by nature has wisdom, [Yāska cites]

जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोममरातीयतो नि दहाति वेदः । स नः पर्षदति दुर्गाणि विश्वा नावेव सिन्धुं दुरितात्यग्निः ॥

jātavedase sunavāma somamarātīyato ni dahāti vedaḥ | sa naḥ parṣadati durgāṇi viśvā nāveva sindhuṃ duritātyagniḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-99-1, as printed "೧-೯೯-೧".)

and

प्र नूनं जातवेदसमश्वं हिनोत वाजिनम् । इदं नो बर्हिरासदे ॥

pra nūnaṃ jātavedasamaśvaṃ hinota vājinam | idaṃ no barhirāsade ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-188-1, as printed "೧೦-೧೮೮-೧".) — in these ṛks he explains the praise of Agni called jātavedas. And:

तदेतदेकमेव जातवेदस्यं गायत्रं तृचं दशतयीषु विद्यते । यत्तु किंचिदाग्नेयं तज्जातवेदसानां स्थाने युज्यते ॥

tadetadekameva jātavedasyaṃ gāyatraṃ tṛcaṃ daśatayīṣu vidyate | yattu kiṃcidāgneyaṃ tajjātavedasānāṃ sthāne yujyate ‖

(Ni. 7-20 [?], as printed "೭-೨०"?; the OCR reads "८-२०".) Read letter by letter; "daśatayīṣu vidyate" and the second sentence are in small type and doubtful. "The Pra nūnam is the one gāyatra tṛca connected with Jātavedas that is found in the ten books; whatever else is Āgneya is employed in the place of the Jātavedas [hymns]"; thus there is no other Gāyatrī-verse connected with Jātavedas that is used in ritual; Agni himself is indicated by the word jātavedāḥ. Therefore —

स न मर्त्यायैवाग्निरित्येशे उत्तरे ज्योतिषी जातवेदसी उच्येते ततो नु मध्यमः । अभि प्रवन्त समनेव योषा इति तत्पुरस्ताद्व्याख्यातम् । अथासावादित्य उदुत्यं जातवेदसमिति तदुपरिष्टाद्व्याख्यास्यामः ॥

sa na martyāyaivāgnirityeśe uttare jyotiṣī jātavedasī ucyete tato nu madhyamaḥ | abhi pravanta samaneva yoṣā iti tatpurastādvyākhyātam | athāsāvāditya udutyaṃ jātavedasamiti tadupariṣṭādvyākhyāsyāmaḥ ‖

(Ni. 7-[?], as printed.) Read letter by letter; the first words, "sa na martyāyaivāgnir iti" [?], are doubtful. Though the nature of Agni is described also by the mantra abhi pravanta samaneva yoṣā, when one discusses the sense of the word jātavedas, the word agni [in that mantra] is an epithet of the sense of jātavedas; and by the mantra ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam it is understood that the Sun too is denoted by the word jātavedas. Durgācārya —

जातवेदसं सूर्यमुद्वहन्तीति तु विशेषणविशेष्यसामानाधिकरण्यैकवाक्यप्रसिद्धाभिः स्वनिगमसिद्धमस्मिन्मन्त्रे जातवेदाः सूर्य इति ॥

jātavedasaṃ sūryamudvahantīti tu viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasāmānādhikaraṇyaikavākyaprasiddhābhiḥ svanigamasiddhamasminmantre jātavedāḥ sūrya iti ‖

Read letter by letter; the Durga passage is small type and doubtful. — in the mantra ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam, in order to show the identity of the Sun and the Agni called Jātavedas, he accepts a single sentence through the relation of qualifier and qualified, and explains that the Sun is also Jātavedas. And —

यस्तु सूक्तं भजते यस्मै हविर्निरुप्यते [?] अयमेव सोऽग्निर्जातवेदा निपातमेवैते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी इत्येन नामधेयेन भजेते ॥

yastu sūktaṃ bhajate yasmai havirnirupyate [?] ayameva so 'gnirjātavedā nipātamevaite uttare jyotiṣī ityena nāmadheyena bhajete ‖

(Ni. 7-?? [?], as printed.) — the Agni of terrestrial form, indicated by the word jātavedas, is invoked in sacrifices by various sūktas and mantras and accepts the oblations; Vaidyuta Agni (lightning), Vaiśvānara Agni and the Sun are varieties of Agni; but the word jātavedas, though it can denote them too, by its established usage denotes the terrestrial Agni: so he has explained.

original p. 265

vipraṃ na jātavedasam — jātavidyaṃ medhāvinaṃ brāhmaṇam iva: "like a Brāhmaṇa of wisdom born, intelligent". Yāska —

नेति प्रतिषेधार्थीयो भाषायाम् । उभयमन्वध्यायम् ॥

neti pratiṣedhārthīyo bhāṣāyām | ubhayamanvadhyāyam ‖

(Ni. 1-4, as printed "೧-೪".) The word na is known in the sense of negation in the language; in the Veda it is used in both senses, negation and upamā (comparison): he has explained; in the phrase vipraṃ na, since the word na is used in the sense of comparison, Sāyaṇa says "like a Brāhmaṇa". The sense: the seer, the seer of the mantra, as one respectfully honours a learned Brāhmaṇa, so with respect and regard I praise Agni too.

ūrdhvayā devāc'yā kṛpā — utpannayā utkṛṣṭayā devān pūjayantyā devān pratyaktayā vā kṛpayā sāmarthyalakṣaṇayā: the word ūrdhva conveys by usage the meaning "high"; here, as an epithet of the word kṛpā, it means "excellent" or "exceeding". The kṛpā that Agni has toward the gods is [his power of] sending the oblations offered in the sacrifice to each god, and of honouring the gods.

Yāska, in the Nirukta, devo devāc'yā kṛpā (Ni. 6-8) — devo devān pratyakṣayā [as printed "ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ತಯಾ"] kṛpā kṛpater vā kalpater vā — explains thus. Durgācārya, citing the same ṛk agniṃ hotāraṃ manye (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-12-1 [?], as printed), says that because the word kṛpā is formed from the root kṛp (kṛpū sāmarthye) or from the root kalp, it means: by power Agni has a mind directed towards the gods.

śociṣā vaṣṭi — jvālayā kāmayate svīkarotīty arthaḥ: "with the flame he desires, accepts": it is described that Agni, following the spreading of the ghee that is offered all round and abundantly flows about him, himself shining, accepts with his flames the burning ghee. The words śocati, śociḥ are recorded among the names of burning, among the names of the burning (Ni. 1-[?]8, as printed "೨-೨೮" [?]); the sense is "flames".

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). hotāram — root hu dānādanayoḥ; tṛn in the agent sense; guṇa of the root vowel; since it has the marker n, first-syllable acute; accusative singular. manye — root manu avabodhane; laṭ first person singular; tiṅ-nighāta.

dāsvantam — root ḍudāñ dāne; sarvadhātubhya asun gives asun, the form dāś; dāḥ dānaṃ yasya saḥ dāsvān; tad asyāsty gives matup; mādupadhāyāś ca… gives va for m; tasau matvarthe (Pā. 1-4-19) gives bha-designation to the ending in s, so no rutva; since matup is unaccented, the first-syllable acute remains. jātavedasam — root vida jñāne; with jāta as upapada, gatikārakopapadayoḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca (Uṇ. 4-?, as printed "೪-೬೬೦" [?]) gives the suffix asi; the accent of the first member as an exception to the natural accent of the final member; guṇa of the short penultimate of the root; accusative singular. svadhvaraḥ — śobhanaḥ adhvaraḥ yasya saḥ svadhvaraḥ; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the final-acute of the latter member. devāc'yā kṛpā — supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39) gives luk to the instrumental ending. vibhrāṣṭim — root bhrāja dīptau; striyāṃ ktin (Pā. 3-3-94) gives ktin; vraśca… gives ṣa for the j; taking it as cause, ṣṭutva; tādau ca niti kṛty ati (Pā. 6-2-50) gives the natural accent of the gati (vi). vaṣṭi — root vaś kāntau (to desire); laṭ third person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. śociṣā — root śuca śoke; arciśuciḥ (Uṇ. 2-?, as printed "೨-೨೬೫") gives isi; guṇa of the short penultimate; first-syllable acute of the suffix. ājuhvānasya — root hu dānādanayoḥ; in the passive, śānac in the laṭ sense; in the Veda no yak; śluḥ [print: śluvikaraṇa]; doubling of the root; abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the first-syllable acute; in the prādi-compound the accent of the final member; genitive singular. sarpiṣaḥ — root sṛp gatau; arciśuciḥ gives isi; guṇa of the short penultimate; genitive singular. ‖ 1 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यजिष्ठं त्वा यजमाना हुवेम ज्येष्ठमङ्गिरसां विप्र मन्मभिर्विप्रेभिः शुक्र मन्मभिः । परिज्मानमिव द्यां होतारं चर्षणीनाम् । शोचिष्केशं वृषणं यमिमा विशः प्रावन्तु जूतये विशः ॥ २ ॥

yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā yajamānā huvema jyeṣṭhamaṅgirasāṃ vipra manmabhirviprebhiḥ śukra manmabhiḥ | parijmānamiva dyāṃ hotāraṃ carṣaṇīnām | śociṣkeśaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ yamimā viśaḥ prāvantu jūtaye viśaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यजिष्ठम् । त्वा । यजमानाः । हुवेम । ज्येष्ठम् । अङ्गिरसाम् । विप्र । मन्मऽभिः । विप्रेभिः । शुक्र । मन्मऽभिः । परिज्मानम्ऽइव । द्याम् । होतारम् । चर्षणीनाम् । शोचिःऽकेशम् । वृषणम् । यम् । इमाः । विशः । प्र । अवन्तु । जूतये । विशः ॥ २ ॥

yajiṣṭham | tvā | yajamānāḥ | huvema | jyeṣṭham | aṅgirasām | vipra | manma 'bhiḥ | viprebhiḥ | śukra | manma 'bhiḥ | parijmānam 'iva | dyām | hotāram | carṣaṇīnām | śociḥ 'keśam | vṛṣaṇam | yam | imāḥ | viśaḥ | pra | avantu | jūtaye | viśaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे विप्र मेधाविन् शुक्र दीप्तज्वालाग्ने यजिष्ठमतिशयेन यष्टृतमं त्वा त्वां यजमाना वयं यष्टारो हुवेम । आह्वयामः । यतो वयं यजमानाः यतश्च त्वं यजिष्ठः अतो हुवेमेत्यभिप्रायः । कीदृशं त्वाम् । अङ्गिरसामङ्गिरोगोत्रोत्पन्नानां मध्ये ज्येष्ठं । यद्वा । अङ्गाराणां मध्ये ज्येष्ठं ज्वालायुक्तत्वात् । अङ्गिरा अङ्गारा इति यास्कः । नि. ३-१७ । ये अङ्गारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गिरसोऽभवन्निति श्रुतेः । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । मन्मभिर्मननसाधनैर्विप्रेभिर्विशेषेण प्रीणयितृभिर्मन्मभिर्मन्त्रैः । यद्वा । विप्रेभिर्मेधाविभिर्ऋत्विग्भिर्मन्मभिर्मन्त्रैश्च सहिता वयमिति संबन्धः । त्वदाह्वानानन्तरं परिज्मानं परितो गच्छन्तं द्यामिव सूर्यमिव होतारं देवानामाह्वातारम् । केषामर्थम् । चर्षणीनां मनुष्यनामैतत् । मनुष्याणां यजमानानामर्थे । यद्वा । चर्षणीनां पूर्वं मनुष्याणामेव सतां पश्चाद्यागादिसाधनेन देवत्वमापन्नानां देवानामाह्वातारम् । तथा शोचिष्केशं केशवदत्यन्तायतातेजोज्वालोपेतं वृषणं वर्षितारमेवं रूपं यं त्वां विशः त्वामेव निविशमाना इमा विशो यजमानरूपाः प्रजा जूतये स्वर्गाद्यभिमतफलप्राप्तये प्रावन्तु । प्रकर्षेण प्रीणयन्तु । तादृशं त्वां हुवेमेति संबन्धः ॥

he vipra medhāvin śukra dīptajvālāgne yajiṣṭhamatiśayena yaṣṭṛtamaṃ tvā tvāṃ yajamānā vayaṃ yaṣṭāro huvema | āhvayāmaḥ | yato vayaṃ yajamānāḥ yataśca tvaṃ yajiṣṭhaḥ ato huvemetyabhiprāyaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | aṅgirasāmaṅgirogotrotpannānāṃ madhye jyeṣṭhaṃ | yadvā | aṅgārāṇāṃ madhye jyeṣṭhaṃ jvālāyuktatvāt | aṅgirā aṅgārā iti yāskaḥ | ni. 3-17 | ye aṅgārā āsaṃste 'ṅgiraso 'bhavanniti śruteḥ | kena sādhaneneti taducyate | manmabhirmananasādhanairviprebhirviśeṣeṇa prīṇayitṛbhirmanmabhirmantraiḥ | yadvā | viprebhirmedhāvibhirṛtvigbhirmanmabhirmantraiśca sahitā vayamiti saṃbandhaḥ | tvadāhvānānantaraṃ parijmānaṃ parito gacchantaṃ dyāmiva sūryamiva hotāraṃ devānāmāhvātāram | keṣāmartham | carṣaṇīnāṃ manuṣyanāmaitat | manuṣyāṇāṃ yajamānānāmarthe | yadvā | carṣaṇīnāṃ pūrvaṃ manuṣyāṇāmeva satāṃ paścādyāgādisādhanena devatvamāpannānāṃ devānāmāhvātāram | tathā śociṣkeśaṃ keśavadatyantāyatātejojvālopetaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ varṣitāramevaṃ rūpaṃ yaṃ tvāṃ viśaḥ tvāmeva niviśamānā imā viśo yajamānarūpāḥ prajā jūtaye svargādyabhimataphalaprāptaye prāvantu | prakarṣeṇa prīṇayantu | tādṛśaṃ tvāṃ huvemeti saṃbandhaḥ ‖

Read from the image; checked against the OCR, which is garbled in places. The words "tvadāhvānānantaram" and "ātivāyatā-" are small and doubtful. "O vipra, wise, O śukra, O Agni of shining flames, you yajiṣṭha — the most worthy of sacrifice — we the sacrificers huvema — call. Since we are sacrificers and you are most sacrificed-to, therefore we call: that is the intention. What sort are you? Jyeṣṭham aṅgirasām — the eldest among those born in the Aṅgiras lineage; or the eldest among the aṅgāras (embers), since he has flame: 'aṅgirā aṅgārāḥ' says Yāska (Ni. 3-17); 'ye aṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan' — by the śruti [Ai. Br.]. By what means? That is said: manmabhiḥ — with means of thought, viprebhiḥ — with the specially pleasing, manmabhiḥ — mantras. Or else: we, together with viprebhiḥ — wise priests — and manmabhiḥ — mantras. Parijmānam iva dyām — like the Sun going all round the sky, hotāram — the caller of the gods; for whose sake? Carṣaṇīnām — this is a name for men: for men, the sacrificers; or, for those who were first merely men and afterwards, by the means of sacrifice, attained godhood — the caller of the gods. Likewise śociṣkeśam — having hair, that is, extremely long flames of radiance, vṛṣaṇam — the showerer; whom, being such, imā viśaḥ — these people, in the form of sacrificers, resting in you alone, jūtaye — for the attainment of the desired fruit, such as heaven, pra avantu — may they greatly please. Such a you we call: so it is connected."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (He) vipra — O wise Agni; parijmānam iva dyām — like the Sun that moves around the sky; carṣaṇīnām — for the sacrificers; hotāram — the one who calls the gods; [carṣaṇīnām — for those who were first men and afterwards attained godhood, the gods; hotāram — the one who calls them]; śociṣkeśam — one with hair of shining flame (flames spread out like hair); vṛṣaṇam — the showerer of desires; yam — whom (you); viśaḥ — people; imāḥ viśaḥ — these (sacrificer) people; jūtaye — for the attainment of the fruit desired, such as heaven; pra avantu — may they please well; he śukra — O blazing Agni; taṃ — such; yajiṣṭham — most worthy of worship; aṅgirasām — among the Aṅgirases (among the embers); jyeṣṭham — the eldest (the eldest by his flame); tvā — you; manmabhiḥ — with the means of thought (and); viprebhiḥ — with special pleasing; manmabhiḥ — mantras; [manmabhiḥ — with praising; viprebhiḥ — priests; manmabhiḥ — with mantras]; yajamānāḥ — we the sacrificers; huvema — call.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O wise and blazing Agni, you call the gods, like the Sun that goes all round the sky, for the sake of men, the sacrificers; the people approach you, most worthy of worship, with hair-like flames, the giver of desired ends, for the attainment of the fruits such as heaven; to you, who are the eldest of all the Aṅgirases, we the sacrificers call, together with priests (the praisers) and mantras (the means of praise).

Printed English (as printed): We, the institutors of the ceremony, invoke you Agni, who are most deserving of worship, and are the eldest of the Angirasas, with

original p. 269

(acceptable) prayers; and with prayers (recited) by the priests, (we adore) you, who, like the traverser of the sky, (the sun), are the invoker (of the gods on behalf) of men, and whom, the bright-haired showerer (of blessings), many people approaching propitiate for the attainment of felicity.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.

śukra — dīptajvālāgne — the word śukra is recorded among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-[?]4 [as printed "೨-೩೪"; doubtful]).

आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ । दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥

ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau | divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142-7, as printed "೧-೧೪೨-೭".) Read letter by letter; "suṣvayantī" and "śukrapiśaṃ" as printed. In this ṛk, the word śukra is explained: "śukrapeśasaṃ śriyaṃ, śukraṃ śocateḥ jvalatikarmaṇaḥ" (Ni. 8-11 [?] as printed "೮-೧೧"), the word śukra, derived from śuc (burning), meaning "shining", is made an epithet of Agni, and Agni is addressed as "one with bright flames".

vipra — medhāvin — the word vipra is explained as "wise, intelligent"; as it is used as an epithet of Agni, Agni is addressed as "wise one".

yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā yajamānā huvema — atiśayena yaṣṭṛtamaṃ tvāṃ vayaṃ yaṣṭāraḥ āhvayāmaḥ: In this sentence the sacrificer is called both yajamāna and yaṣṭṛ; Agni, being necessarily required by the sacrificers (as the chief), is addressed as the most worthy of sacrifice, and the sacrificers invoke Agni for the purpose of the sacrifice, it is explained.

aṅgirasāṃ jyeṣṭham — aṅgirogotrotpannānāṃ madhye jyeṣṭhaṃ yadvā aṅgārāṇāṃ madhye jyaiṣṭhaṃ jvālāyuktatvāt aṅgirā aṅgārāḥ (Ni. 3-17), says Yāska: ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan (Ai. Br. 3-34, as printed "ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೩-೩೪"), by the śruti. The meaning is that Agni is the first of all those born in the lineage of the seer Aṅgiras; or that, by the connection with flames, he is the chief among the embers.

त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर्देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा ।

tvamagne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣirdevo devānāmabhavaḥ śivaḥ sakhā |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-1, as printed.)

त्वमग्ने प्रथमोऽङ्गिरस्तमः कविर्देवानां परिभूषसि व्रतम् ॥

tvamagne prathamo 'ṅgirastamaḥ kavirdevānāṃ paribhūṣasi vratam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-2, as printed.)

In these ṛks it is described that Agni, first of all the Aṅgirases, was born under the name of the ṛṣi Aṅgiras and was the best among those ṛṣis. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, "ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan" (Ai. Br. 3-34): the embers (aṅgāra) that arose when Agni burned became the name of the ṛṣis Aṅgiras: thus the derivation of the word aṅgiras is also given.

प्रियमेधवदत्रिवज्जातवेदो विरूपवत् । अङ्गिरस्वन्महिव्रत प्रस्कण्वस्य श्रुधी हवम् ॥

priyamedhavadatrivajjātavedo virūpavat | aṅgirasvanmahivrata praskaṇvasya śrudhī havam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-45-3, as printed "೧-೪೫-೩".) Citing this ṛk, Yāska (Ni. 3-17), "arciṣi bhṛguḥ saṃbabhūva bhṛgur bhrajyamāno na dehe | aṅgāreṣv aṅgirā aṅgārā añcanāḥ aṅkanāḥ": has explained. Durgācārya, explaining its meaning —

भृगुर्भ्रज्यमानो न देहे प्रजापतिना किल शुक्रमाक्षीयमादाय अग्नौ हुतम् । ततः अर्चिषि ज्वालायां भृगुर्नाम महर्षिः संबभूव । व्यपगते अर्चिषि यः अङ्गारेषु संबभूव सः अङ्गिराः नाम अभवत् । अङ्गाराः अङ्कनाः । ते हि यत्र निधीयन्ते तदङ्कितं भवति ॥

bhṛgurbhrajyamāno na dehe prajāpatinā kila śukramākṣīyamādāya agnau hutam | tataḥ arciṣi jvālāyāṃ bhṛgurnāma maharṣiḥ saṃbabhūva | vyapagate arciṣi yaḥ aṅgāreṣu saṃbabhūva saḥ aṅgirāḥ nāma abhavat | aṅgārāḥ aṅkanāḥ | te hi yatra nidhīyante tadaṅkitaṃ bhavati ‖

Read letter by letter; "śukram ākṣīyam ādāya" [?] is small and doubtful. "[It is said that] Bhṛgu, as if being fried in a body, [arose] when Prajāpati offered his seed in the fire; thence in the flame (arciṣi) the great seer called Bhṛgu came into being; when the flame had gone, he who came into being among the embers was called Aṅgirā. Aṅgārāḥ are aṅkanāḥ — marking: for where they are laid down, that place is marked." When Brahmā (Prajāpati) offered his seed in the fire, flames arose; from them the seer Bhṛgu was born; when all the flames had subsided, the embers remained; he who was born from these became the seer called Aṅgiras; since those that are touched are marked (aṅkana), these were named aṅgāras: so the meaning is explained. From this Sāyaṇa has described Agni, being endowed with flame, as the best among embers.

manmabhir viprebhir manmabhiḥ — mananasādhanaiḥ viśeṣeṇa prīṇayitṛbhiḥ mantraiḥ | yadvā viprair medhāvibhir ṛtvigbhiḥ manmabhir mantraiś ca sahitā vayam iti saṃbandhaḥ. The word manma is repeated here twice; by this two kinds of meanings are described. The first meaning is "means of thought", as an epithet of the word mantra. In the second, the word manma [means mantra]. For the word vipra too two meanings are explained: first, vi = special, pra = pleasing (prīṇayitā, "the satisfier"); the second meaning of the word vipra is "wise priest" (ṛtvij).
