original p. 271

The meaning is that, in sum, wise priests who are accompanied by mantras that please Agni, and we the sacrificers, invoke [Agni]. Sāyaṇa has explained this in two ways. Through the different meanings stated for vipra, a variation of sense is described here. The meaning of the word manma has been explained in the ṛk 1-[?] [as printed "೧-೧೪೪-೨"?; doubtful].

hotāraṃ carṣaṇīnām — yajamānānām arthe devānām āhvātāraṃ yadvā pūrvaṃ manuṣyāṇām eva satāṃ paścād yāgādisādhanena devatvam āpannānāṃ devānām āhvātāram: In explaining the meaning of the word hotṛ, derived from the root hve, it was described before that Agni himself is the hotṛ, and that he calls the gods to receive the oblations offered in the sacrifice to the various gods, by reciting their mantras. By this two kinds of meaning are explained here too. In the first, it is said that Agni calls all the gods for the sacrifice. In the second, to explain the word carṣaṇī — Yāska in the Nirukta cites manuṣyāḥ, naraḥ [and so on], among the twenty-five names of men (Ni. 3-8 [?], as printed "೩-೮"). And —

विश्वानरस्य वस्पतिमनानतस्य शवसः । एवैश्च चर्षणीनामूती हुवे रथानाम् ॥

viśvānarasya vaspatimanānatasya śavasaḥ | evaiśca carṣaṇīnāmūtī huve rathānām ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-? [?], as printed "೮-೬-೪"? — numerals small.) Read letter by letter; I do not complete the words from memory; "vaspatim" is doubtful. In this ṛk, carṣaṇīnām is explained as manuṣyāṇām (Ni. 12-22 [?] as read by the OCR). Following this, Sāyaṇa explains the word carṣaṇī, since it is recorded among the names of men, as yajamānānām arthe — "for the sacrificers" — in the first explanation; and in the second, those who were first mere men and, by performing sacrifice, attained the state of gods, are called carṣaṇī; Agni calls them to the sacrifice, he said.

parijmānam iva dyām — sūryam iva parito gacchantam: explaining dyām as "the sun", Sāyaṇa says that Agni, like the Sun, moves about everywhere (pervades). But Yāska —

न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतम् । अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं वि नश्यति ॥

na nūnamasti no śvaḥ kastadveda yadadbhutam | anyasya cittamabhi saṃcareṇyamutādhītaṃ vi naśyati ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-120-3 [?], as printed "೧-೧೨೦-೩".) citing this ṛk, [says] na nūnam asty adyatanaṃ, adyāsmin daivi dyur ity ahno nāmadheyaṃ dyotata iti sataḥ (Ni. 4-[?]; as read) — he explains the word dyu as ahas, "day". Durgācārya, since the ṛk says "not now … tomorrow does not exist", explains it by supplying the word adyatanam ("of today") to Yāska's statement.

Since the day (ahas) arises from a particular motion of the Sun, and is a particular time, [Sāyaṇa seems to] explain that "he who gives light to the day, who moves about like the Sun that is ever moving" — the general meaning "shining" belongs to both day and Sun.

śociṣkeśam — keśavad atyantāyatatejojvālopetam: the word śocis is recorded among the eleven names of burning beginning with jvalat (Ni. 1-[?]8 [as printed "೨-೨೮"; doubtful]); jvalataḥ means flames. As the hairs on the bodies of men are long, so are the flames of Agni long. One having such flames is Agni: that is the sense.

imāḥ viśaḥ viśaḥ jūtaye prāvantu — in this sentence the word viśaḥ is used twice. The author of the Nirukta says that the word viśaḥ is recorded among the twenty-five names of men, beginning with manuṣyāḥ, naraḥ (Ni. 3-8). And —

जराबोध तद्विविड्ढि विशेविशे यज्ञियाय । स्तोमं रुद्राय दृशीकम् ॥

jarābodha tadviviḍḍhi viśeviśe yajñiyāya | stomaṃ rudrāya dṛśīkam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-4, as printed "೧-೧೧೪-೪" [?].) Read letter by letter. In this ṛk, viśe viśe is explained as manuṣyasya manuṣyasya, "for each and every man". Sāyaṇa says of the two words viśaḥ … viśaḥ: for the one, "those who rest in you alone, taking Agni alone as their support"; for the second viśaḥ, "people in the form of sacrificers"; and since Agni, the god, is the fulfiller of what is desired, may the people who serve him, in the form of sacrificers, be satisfied by offering oblations for their respective desired ends, such as heaven: thus he prays. And — such an Agni we call and give oblations to: this is what is said.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR). yajiṣṭham — root yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; tṛc in the agent sense; when the sense "most worshipping" is intended, tuśchandasi (Pā. 5-3-59) gives iṣṭhan; with it following, turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu (Pā. 6-4-154) elides the tṛc; ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute; accusative singular.

Grammar of Ṛk 2, continued; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and the page. yajamānāḥ — the root as before; śānac in the laṭ sense, śap; āne muk (Pā. 7-2-82) gives muk to the stem in a; since the sārvadhātuka follows the upadeśa, tāsyanudāttet makes it unaccented, so the root-accent remains. huvema — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; liṅ first person plural, mas; nityaṃ ṅitaḥ elides its s; śap; the augment yāsuṭ …; iyaṅ-substitution; loponyoḥ [print: "ಲೋಪೋವೋರ್ವ್ಯೋಃ"] elides the y; guṇa; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 1-1-34 [?]) gives saṃprasāraṇa; by vyatyaya the uvaṅ substitution; tiṅ-nighāta. jyeṣṭham — atiśayena praśasyaḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ; when iṣṭhan comes in the sense of excess, jya ca (Pā. 5-3-61) gives jya for praśasya; since prakṛtyaikāc gives prakṛtibhāva, the ā-elision does not occur; guṇa; since the suffix has the marker n, first-syllable acute; accusative singular. manmabhiḥ — root mana jñāne; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. 3-2-75) gives manin; since n-marked, first-syllable acute; instrumental plural. viprebhiḥ — vipra + bhis; since bahulaṃ chandasi applies, bhis does not become ais; by the jhal rule, e in the plural. parijmānam — pari jāyate iti parijmā; recorded as formed with kanin (Uṇ. 1-[?]), accusative singular. carṣaṇīnām — final-acute by the prātipadika accent; nāmany atarasyām [print: nāmanyatarasyām] (Pā. 6-1-177) gives the acute to the case-ending (genitive plural). avantu — root ava rakṣaṇe; loṭ third person plural; tiṅ-nighāta. jūtaye — ūtijūtisātihetiḥ… (Pā. 3-3-97) records the form formed with ktin as acute; dative singular. ‖ 2 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स हि पुरू चिदोजसा विरुक्मता दीद्यानो भवति द्रुहन्तरः । परशुर्न द्रुहन्तरः । वीळु चिद्यस्य समृतौ श्रुवद्वनेव यत्स्थिरम् । निःषहमाणो यमते नायते धन्वासहा नायते ॥ ३ ॥

sa hi purū cidojasā virukmatā dīdyāno bhavati druhantaraḥ | paraśurna druhantaraḥ | vīḷu cidyasya samṛtau śruvadvaneva yatsthiram | niḥṣahamāṇo yamate nāyate dhanvāsahā nāyate ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

सः । हि । पुरु । चित् । ओजसा । विरुक्मता । दीद्यानः । भवति । द्रुहःऽतरः । परशुः । न । द्रुहःऽतरः । वीळु । चित् । यस्य । सम्ऽऋतौ । श्रुवत् । वना ऽइव । यत् । स्थिरम् । निःऽसहमानः । यमते । न । आयते । धन्वऽसहा । न । आयते ॥ ३ ॥

saḥ | hi | puru | cit | ojasā | virukmatā | dīdyānaḥ | bhavati | druhaḥ 'taraḥ | paraśuḥ | na | druhaḥ 'taraḥ | vīḷu | cit | yasya | sam 'ṛtau | śruvat | vanā 'iva | yat | sthiram | niḥ 'sahamānaḥ | yamate | na | āyate | dhanva 'sahā | na | āyate ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

स हि स एव पूर्वं स्तुत एवाग्निर्विरुक्मता विशेषेण रोचनवता ओजसा ज्वालारूपेण बलेन पुरु चित् अत्यधिकमेव दीद्यानो दीप्यमानो द्रुहन्तरो द्रोग्ध्ऋणां तरिता निवारयिता भवति । अस्मासु द्रोहं कुर्वतां शत्रूणां हिंसको भवतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । द्रुहन्तरः द्रुमाणां छेदनाय प्रयुक्तः परशुर्न परशुरिव । स यथा द्रुमं हिनस्ति तथायमपि । किंच यस्याग्नेः समृतौ संगतौ संयोगे वीळु चित् दृढमपि पाषाणादिकं श्रुवत् गच्छेत् क्षीयेत । तथा यत्स्थिरं पर्वतादि स्थिरमचलितं तदपि श्रुवत् । वीळिति दृढनाम वीळु च्छौतमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वनेव उदकमिव । उदकं यथाग्निसंयोगे शुष्यति तथेत्यर्थः । अत्यन्तदृढं स्थिरमपि हिनस्ति । अस्मद्द्रोग्धॄणामग्न्यादिरूपं शत्रुं हिंसतीति किमुतवक्तव्यमित्यभिप्रायः । किंचायमग्निर्निःषहमाणः शत्रून्नितरामभिभवन् यमते । उपरमते । शत्रुषु मध्ये क्रीडति । तानेव नाशयति । कथं कुर्वन्नायते । न गच्छति । शत्रोः सकाशात्पलायते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । धन्वसहा न । धनुषा शत्रूनभिभवतीति धान्वष्कः । सहतेरसुन् छान्दसोऽन्त्यलोपः । स यथा शत्रुमभिमुखं विध्यति न पलायते तद्वदित्यर्थः । यद्वा । दृढधनुर्वहनक्षमो धन्वसहः । अस्मिन्पक्षे पचाद्यच् । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । दृढधन्वा सन्नायते न चलति ॥

sa hi sa eva pūrvaṃ stuta evāgnirvirukmatā viśeṣeṇa rocanavatā ojasā jvālārūpeṇa balena puru cit atyadhikameva dīdyāno dīpyamāno druhantaro drogdhṛṇāṃ taritā nivārayitā bhavati | asmāsu drohaṃ kurvatāṃ śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsako bhavatītyarthaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | druhantaraḥ drumāṇāṃ chedanāya prayuktaḥ paraśurna paraśuriva | sa yathā drumaṃ hinasti tathāyamapi | kiṃca yasyāgneḥ samṛtau saṃgatau saṃyoge vīḷu cit dṛḍhamapi pāṣāṇādikaṃ śruvat gacchet kṣīyeta | tathā yatsthiraṃ parvatādi sthiramacalitaṃ tadapi śruvat | vīḷiti dṛḍhanāma vīḷu cchautamiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vaneva udakamiva | udakaṃ yathāgnisaṃyoge śuṣyati tathetyarthaḥ | atyantadṛḍhaṃ sthiramapi hinasti | asmaddrogdhṝṇāmagnyādirūpaṃ śatruṃ hiṃsatīti kimutavaktavyamityabhiprāyaḥ | kiṃcāyamagnirniḥṣahamāṇaḥ śatrūnnitarāmabhibhavan yamate | uparamate | śatruṣu madhye krīḍati | tāneva nāśayati | kathaṃ kurvannāyate | na gacchati | śatroḥ sakāśātpalāyate | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | dhanvasahā na | dhanuṣā śatrūnabhibhavatīti dhānvaṣkaḥ | sahaterasun chāndaso 'ntyalopaḥ | sa yathā śatrumabhimukhaṃ vidhyati na palāyate tadvadityarthaḥ | yadvā | dṛḍhadhanurvahanakṣamo dhanvasahaḥ | asminpakṣe pacādyac | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | dṛḍhadhanvā sannāyate na calati ‖

Read from the image; checked against the OCR. The Nirukta citation "vīḷu cautam" is as printed and doubtful. "Sa hi — that same Agni praised before, with virukmatā — specially shining — ojasā, might in the form of flame, puru cit — most abundantly, dīdyānaḥ — blazing — druhantaraḥ — he becomes the one who crosses over, who wards off, those who injure (drogdhṛṇām): the destroyer of enemies who do harm to us. An illustration: paraśur na druhantaraḥ — like an axe used for cutting trees; as it destroys the tree, so he too. Moreover, yasya samṛtau — at whose contact, vīḷu cit — even the hard stone and the like śruvat — goes, wastes away; and likewise whatever is firm, a mountain and the like, immovable, also [wastes away]. (Vīḷu is a word for 'hard': 'vīḷu cautam' is read among those names.) An illustration: vaneva — like water; as water dries up on contact with fire, so [they waste]. He destroys even the very hard and firm; what then need be said of enemies, in the form of fire and the rest, of those who harm us? That is the intention. Moreover, this Agni, niḥṣahamāṇaḥ — overpowering enemies, yamate — stays [amid them], sports among enemies; he destroys them. How does he act? Nāyate — he does not go; he does not flee from the enemy. An illustration: dhanvasahā na — as the one who overcomes enemies with the bow, an archer; sahas… the suffix asun, the last letter dropped in the Veda; as he, facing the foe, shoots and does not flee, so [Agni]. Or else dhanvasaha is one capable of bearing a strong bow; here the suffix ac in the pacādi sense; the augment ā by supāṃ sulug. Being one with a strong bow he does not go, does not waver."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Yasya — of which Agni; saṃṛtau — at the contact; vīḷu cit — even the very hard (mountains and the like); yat sthiram (tat ca) — whatever is firm (other things, whatever they are); vaneva — like water (as water is dried up by contact with fire); śruvat — go to destruction; sa hi — that Agni, praised before; virukmatā — specially shining; ojasā — with the strength in the form of flame; puru cit — most abundantly; dīdyānaḥ — blazing; druhantaraḥ — used for the destruction of enemies; paraśuḥ na — like an axe; druhantaraḥ — the destroyer of (our) enemies; bhavati — becomes; (kiṃ ca — moreover; ayam agniḥ — this Agni); niḥsahamānaḥ — wholly defeating the enemies; yamate — plays [among them] (destroys them); yathā — as; dhanvasahā — a hero who overcomes enemies as the bearer of a bow; na āyate — does not flee from enemies; (tathā — so); na āyate — does not run away (stays firm).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. In contact with Agni even the very hard and immovable mountains and the like, like water [dried by fire], perish; the same Agni, like an axe used to cut the enemies, shining especially with his flames, destroys our enemies; defeating them completely, he plays among them; like a hero bearing a bow, he does not flee, but stands firm.

Printed English (as printed): Verily, that Agni, far shining with brilliant vigour, is the destroyer of foes, like a hatchet that cuts down trees : whatever is most solid and stable dissolves like water at his contact : unsparing, he sports (amidst enemies), nor desists (from their destruction), like an archer who retreats not (from battle).

original p. 276

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.

In this ṛk there are three sentences: (1) sa dīdyānaḥ druhantaraḥ paraśur na druhantaraḥ; (2) yasya saṃṛtau vīḷu cid yat sthiraṃ vaneva śruvat; (3) niṣṣahamāṇaḥ yamate dhanvasahā na nāyate nāyate.

In the first sentence the word druhantaraḥ is used twice. For this word the meaning "one who destroys" is explained. By this it is said that Agni, shining abundantly, destroys even those who do harm to sacrificers, or enemies, or makes them submerged. In this matter, by the second druhantaraḥ an illustration is cited: as the axe that is used for cutting down trees destroys them, so Agni too, it is compared, destroys like the axe.

puru — this word is recorded among the twelve names of "many" (Ni. 3-13 [?]); it gives the meaning "much".

cit — the author of the Nirukta records this word among the particles, explaining cid iti ... anekakarmā [as printed "ಚಿದಿತ್ಯೇಷೋऽನೇಕಕರ್ಮಾ", Ni. 1-4]: (the indeclinable cit conveys many meanings); ācāryaḥ cid idaṃ brūyāt iti pūjāyām — in the sentence "the teacher may say this" cit means respect; and in caturdaśadamānāt (Ni. 3-[?]) [as printed] cit is a word of comparison.

चिदिति निपातोऽनुदात्तः । अथापि पशुनामेह भवत्युदात्तः ॥

ciditi nipāto 'nudāttaḥ | athāpi paśunāmeha bhavatyudāttaḥ ‖

(Ni. 5-[?] as printed.) Read letter by letter; the second half is doubtful. The indeclinable cit is used with an unaccented tone and is a sign of an unaccented sense; but when accented it conveys an animal [name, cit ... ]. In sadyaś cid yaḥ śavasā pañca kṛṣṭīḥ cit is a sign of the unaccented tone; in cid asi manāsi dhīr asi it is a sign of the accented tone; thus they say.

In the second sentence it is explained that even the hard stones and the like, merely through contact with Agni, dissolve [or: waste away]; the mountain that is exceedingly strong and the like are made soft; as water is dried by contact with Agni: so he gives the example. By this illustration it is said that Agni is a wonder of capacity in destroying the enemies or the injurers of those who have performed the sacrifice, who cause difficulty to the firm mountain and (rock).

vīḷu — the meaning is "hard"; the word vīḷu is recorded in the twenty-eight names of strength: vīḷu cautam (Ni. 2-[?]).

original p. 277

vaneva — Sāyaṇa explains this as "like water". Yāska has recorded the word vana also among the names of rays (Ni. 1-[?]5 [as printed "೧-೧೫"? doubtful]) —

नियश्वश्नक्षि श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि कुष्ठस्य चिद्वनिनो रोरुवद्वना ॥

niyaśvaśnakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani kuṣṭhasya cidvanino roruvadvanā ‖

Read letter by letter; the first words are small and I cannot confirm them: I give the pāda as printed in the Kannada, "niyaśvaśnakṣi …", unverified. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as printed "೧-೫೪-೫"?) — in this ṛk the word vanā is explained as vanāni udakāni, "waters".

मेद्यन्तु ते वह्नयो येभिरीयसेऽरिषण्यन्वनस्पते । आयूया धृष्णो अभिगूर्या त्वं नेष्ट्रात्सोमं द्रविणोदः पिब ऋतुभिः ॥

medyantu te vahnayo yebhirīyase 'riṣaṇyanvanaspate | āyūyā dhṛṣṇo abhigūryā tvaṃ neṣṭrātsomaṃ draviṇodaḥ piba ṛtubhiḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-3 [?], as printed "೨-೩೭-೩"; the first words are doubtful in my reading.) Citing this ṛk, in explaining the word vanaspate — vanaspatir ity eṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā vanaṃ vanoteḥ — he explains that the word vana, derived from the root van meaning "to ask", conveys the meaning "forest".

In the third sentence it is described: nāyate — Agni does not flee, does not run in fear from enemies when they come against him; niṣṣahamāṇaḥ yamate — he, overcoming the enemies greatly and sporting in their midst, destroys them.

And here, in this matter, the illustrative sentence dhanvāsahā nāyate nāyate is cited. The word dhanvasaha is used here. For dhanvasaha the meaning is dhanuṣā śatrūn abhibhavati iti dhānuṣkaḥ — "since he overcomes enemies by the bow, a bearer of a bow as weapon"; or, in the second explanation, "one who is able to bear a strong bow". By this Agni is compared to a hero who, bearing a bow or bearing a strong bow and fighting, does not move away from enemies but stays firm, facing them, or who, bending the bow firmly, fights without moving.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and page). puru — nipātasya ca (Pā. 6-3-136) lengthens the final vowel in the Saṃhitā. virukmatā — viśiṣṭā ruk virukmā, tadvān virukmān; when matup comes, since ayasmayādīni (Pā. 1-4-20) read it as having pada status, there is no kutva, and since it is bha there is no jaś-saṃdhi; instrumental singular. dīdyānaḥ — root dīdī dīptidevanayoḥ; this is a sautra root; by vyatyaya śānac; since it follows the upadeśa it is unaccented, so the root-accent remains.

Read from the image; "annānnāni" is doubtful in the print. "To this Agni dṛḷhā cid — even the hard, [i.e.] sappy oblations, in order, with each mantra, duḥ — they give; the sacrificers give. [Duḥ is the aorist of dā, with the loss of siC by gātisthā… and jus for jhi.] An illustration in giving: yathā vide — as the generous give excellent riches to the knower, the one who sees the highest truth; or else, as this Agni vide — gets (vindate) oblations over and above his own to give to the gods, accepts them: so they give. Moreover that Agni, by the tejiṣṭhābhiḥ — extremely radiant — araṇibhiḥ — [forms or ways] such as sacrifice, dāṣṭi — being honoured, gives heaven and the like. For what? Avase — for the protection of them. Or else: by araṇibhiḥ — with goings, most radiant — the oblation given by the sacrificer with reference to other gods, for their acceptance, he gives; this Agni gives, leads. Moreover, agnaye — to Agni, even at the time of giving to other deities, the sacrificer gives first, for his satisfaction: for what? avase — for protection; for if he were unsatisfied, he himself would take even what is given to the others; therefore he gives to Agni in the form of the prayājas and the like: that is the sense. Further, yaḥ — he who puruṇi pra gāhate — enters many things, [the property of the sacrificer], and entering, with flame in the form of an adze and the like takṣat — thins them, destroys. An illustration: vaneva — as forests, masses of trees and the like, are entered, cut, burnt. Moreover this Agni, sthirā anna — firm foods (rice, grain and the like) ojasā — with flame that is brightness — ni riṇāti — goes thoroughly, cooks them. (Rī — Kryādi class, 'to go', 'to hurt'; prādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ [shortening].) And with his own brightness sthirāṇi — unavoidable sins or enemies — ni riṇāti — goes through completely, destroys."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Yaḥ — which Agni; puruṇi — many (oblations and the like); pra gāhate — pervades; śociṣā — with the flame; vaneva — as a forest; takṣat — destroys (reduces); sthirā cit — even hard; annā — grains and the like; ojasā — with the bright flame; ni riṇāti — cooks well; (tathā — likewise); ojasā — with his own power; sthirāṇi cit — even the unavoidable (sins or enemies); (ni riṇāti — destroys); asmai — to such Agni; dṛḷhā cit — even the sappy [oblations]; vide yathā — as to the wise (the givers give); anu — in order (with each mantra); duḥ — they give; (kiṃ ca — and, Agni); athavā — or; tejiṣṭhābhiḥ — most radiant; araṇibhiḥ — (with sacrifice and other) ways [mārga]; (being honoured) avase — for the protection (of us the doers); dāṣṭi — gives (heaven and the like); [athavā — or; tejiṣṭhābhiḥ — most radiant; araṇibhiḥ — (with his) goings; avase — for the protection of the sacrifice; dāṣṭi — gives (the oblations to other deities); (and the sacrificer, when making the oblations to other deities,) agnaye — to Agni; avase — for the protection of the sacrifice; dāṣṭi — gives (oblation and the like)].

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Agni, entering the many things (given by the sacrificer), burns them like a forest (quickly); however hard the grains (given by the sacrificer) may be, he cooks them with his flame; and he destroys, by his power, the unavoidable (sins or enemies). To this Agni the sacrificers, as the givers to a knower, offer sappy oblations with each mantra; Agni too, with his flames most radiant, being honoured by the sacrificer, gives heaven and the like; and the sacrificer, even when offering to other gods, gives the oblation first to Agni, for the protection of the sacrifice.

original p. 281

Printed English (as printed): They have presented substantial offerings to him, as (they give riches) to a sage, and by resplendent means he grants us (grace) for our preservation : (the worshipper) presents (gifts) to Agni for preservation : he who pervades the (many offerings made to him) consumes them (as rapidly) as (he consumes) forests : he matures the standing corn by his potency ; he destroys whatever (things) are stationary by his potency.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 4.

asmai dṛḷhā cid anu duryathā vide — agnaye sāravanti havīṃṣi anukrameṇa pratimantraṃ dadati yajamānāḥ | viduṣe paramārthadarśine utkṛṣṭāni dhanāni vitaranti dānaśīlāḥ | yadvā ayam agnir yathā vide vindate svātiriktaṃ havir devebhyo dātuṃ labhate svīkaroti tathā duḥ dadati. The sacrificers who perform the sacrifice offer to Agni the substantial oblations in order, with the various mantras. As, in the world, generous persons give the best things and wealth to a wise, learned man, so the comparison is made in the matter of offering oblations to Agni; this is one meaning that Sāyaṇa gives for the sentence.

In the second way of explaining the meaning, though the meaning of the illustrating sentence is the same, it is described that, as Agni receives his own share of the oblation and also separately receives the oblations to be offered to the other gods, the sacrificers offer the oblations.

That the particle cit is used in the sense dhārtha [as printed; the sense given there is that of emphasis] has been explained in the special topics of the previous ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-127-3).

tejiṣṭhābhir araṇibhir dāṣṭy avase agnaye dāṣṭy avase — in this sentence the word dāṣṭy avase is repeated twice. In the first meaning it is explained that Agni, honoured by the performance of sacrifices and the like that are full of splendour, bestows heaven and the like for the protection of those who perform the sacrifice.

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 2-127-3

original p. 282

In the second meaning it is described that Agni, with the goings that shine by his own radiance, protects the oblations offered by the sacrificers with reference to other gods, so that the respective gods may accept them, and carries them to each of them.

By the second sentence agnaye dāṣṭy avase: when the sacrificer offers oblations for other gods, he first offers the oblation to Agni, in order that Agni be pleased. If Agni is not satisfied, there is no protection for the sacrificer in his offering also the oblations of the other gods to him; therefore, for Agni's satisfaction, he describes that the sacrificer first performs the prayājas and the like.

araṇibhiḥ — yajñādirūpaiḥ mārgaiḥ gamanaiḥ: two kinds of meaning are given for araṇi: "the ways that exist in forms such as the sacrifice", and "goings, courses". Yāska —

अग्निं नरो दीधितिभिररण्योर्हस्तच्युती जनयन्त प्रशस्तम् । दूरेदृशं गृहपतिमथर्युम् ॥

agniṃ naro dīdhitibhiraraṇyorhastacyutī janayanta praśastam | dūredṛśaṃ gṛhapatimatharyum ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-1-1, as printed "೭-೧-೧".) — citing this ṛk, he explains araṇī — agniḥ samaraṇāj jāyata iti vā; and he gives for the word araṇi the meaning "a particular wood".

puruṇi pra gāhate takṣat vaneva — bahūni | sāmarthyāt yajamānadhanādīni praviśati praviśya ca vāśyādirūpayā jvālayā tanūkaroti nāśayatīty arthaḥ | vṛkṣādisamūhāni vanāni yathā praviśya takṣati dahati tathā: this Agni, as one enters and burns the forests that are masses of trees, enters with his flames the things of the sacrificers and destroys them; so it is described.

sthirā annā ojasā ni riṇāti sthirāṇi ni cid ojasā — in this sentence the verb ni riṇāti is stated twice. In this sentence the word sthirā is explained as "hard", and made an epithet of the word annā, annāni vrīhyādīni ("grains such as rice"): Agni cooks with his flames, that are of the nature of heat, the hard rice and the like. The meaning is as such.

For the other word sthirāṇi, [Sāyaṇa] explains aparihāraṇīyāni pāpāni amitrāṇi vā, "unavoidable sins or enemies", and says that Agni destroys these by his flames, which are of the nature of radiance.

original p. 283

annā — annāni vrīhyādīni — Sāyaṇa so explains. The word anna is stated among the one hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-[?]4, as printed "೨-೨೪" [?]); annaṃ kasmād ānatam bhūtebhyo 'rtvā [as printed "ಅರ್ತ್ವಾ"?] (Ni. 3-[?]) — "because it is bent [to] beings, [it is] food", because it is food for creatures.

आद्यते चात्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यते ॥

ādyate cātti ca bhūtāni | tasmādannaṃ taducyate ‖

(Tai. U. 2-2 [?], as printed "ತೈ. ಉ. ೨-೨".) This is stated in the śruti: the word anna is derived from the root ad (to eat); it is that which is eaten by living creatures, or that which eats living creatures; thus it is described.

ojasā — tejorūpayā jvālayā, svakīyena tejasā: Sāyaṇa explains the word ojas here as the flames, which are of the nature of brightness, or as "radiance belonging to Agni". The word ojas is recorded among the twenty-eight names of strength, beginning ojaḥ pājaḥ (Ni. 2-[?]; as printed "೨-೯"); the meaning is "strength".

श्रायन्त इव सूर्यं विश्वेदिन्द्रस्य भक्षत । वसूनि जाते जनमान ओजसा प्रति भागं न दीधिम ॥

śrāyanta iva sūryaṃ viśvedindrasya bhakṣata | vasūni jāte janamāna ojasā prati bhāgaṃ na dīdhima ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as printed "೧-೫೫-೫"? — numerals unclear.) Citing this ṛk in the Nirukta (Ni. 6-8 [?]), he explains ojasā as balena, "with strength"; and says that the form ojas is from the root oj or from the root ubj.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and the page). dṛḷhā — root dṛha dṛhi vṛddhau; dṛḍhaḥ sthūlabalayoḥ (Pā. 7-2-20) records it as formed with kta; in the neuter plural dṛḷhāni; śeś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70) elides śi. duḥ — root ḍudāñ dāne; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6) gives luṅ in the present sense; for cli, siC; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 2-4-77) gives luk of it; since the root ends in ā, ātaḥ (Pā. 3-4-110) gives jus for the following jhi; usyapadāntāt (Pā. 6-1-96) gives pararūpa; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75) gives no augment; tiṅ-nighāta. vide — root vida jñāne; kvip by kvasuś ca [print: "ಕ್ವಿಸ್ ಚ"]; dative singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168) gives the acute to the ending. In the second explanation, from vidḷ lābhe; bahulaṃ chandasi gives luk of śyan; laṭ third person singular ta; ṭi becomes e; lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (Pā. 7-1-41) elides the t; since yathā precedes, no nighāta; final-acute by the suffix accent.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तमस्य पृक्षमुपरासु धीमहि नक्तं यः सुदर्शतरो दिवातरादप्रायुषे दिवातरात् । आदस्यायुर्ग्रभणवद्वीळु शर्म न सूनवे । भक्तमभक्तमवो व्यन्तो अजरा अग्नयो व्यन्तो अजराः ॥ ५ ॥

अस्यास्मै पृक्षं हविर्लक्षणमन्नमुपरासु । उपरमन्तेऽस्मिन्हवींष्युपरा वेदिसमीपभूमयः । तासु धीमहि । धारयामः । अस्येत्युक्तं कस्येत्यत आह । यो ऽग्निर्नक्तं रात्रौ दिवातरात् अहोऽपि सुदर्शतरः अत्यर्थं सर्वैर्दर्शनीयो भवति । यतोऽयं रात्रौ सर्वेषु भावेषु तमसावृतत्वाददृश्यमानेष्वपि स्वयमत्यर्थं प्रकाशते । अतोऽस्मै धीमहि । पुनः कीदृशायेति । दिवातरादह्नः सकाशादेवाप्रायुषे । प्रगतमायुर्यस्यासौ प्रायुः । न प्रायुरप्रायुः । तस्मै । असौ योऽस्तमेति स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायास्तमेतीति श्रुतेः । रात्रौ सर्वे भावा निद्रयावृतत्वात्प्रायुष इव भवन्ति । अयमग्निस्तु सर्वप्राणिप्राणापहर्तुः सूर्यस्य रात्रौ स्वस्मिन्नेव प्रवेशात्प्रकृष्टायुर्भवति । अतोऽपि धीमहि । किंचात एव कारणाद्यतोऽयं सुदर्शतरो यतश्चाप्रायुः । अतः कारणादस्मै तदर्थमायुर्हविर्लक्षणमन्नं ग्रभणवत् ग्रहणयुक्तमभूत् [?]

asyāsmai pṛkṣaṃ havirlakṣaṇamannamuparāsu | uparamante 'sminhavīṃṣyuparā vedisamīpabhūmayaḥ | tāsu dhīmahi | dhārayāmaḥ | asyetyuktaṃ kasyetyata āha | yo 'gnirnaktaṃ rātrau divātarāt aho 'pi sudarśataraḥ atyarthaṃ sarvairdarśanīyo bhavati | yato 'yaṃ rātrau sarveṣu bhāveṣu tamasāvṛtatvādadṛśyamāneṣvapi svayamatyarthaṃ prakāśate | ato 'smai dhīmahi | punaḥ kīdṛśāyeti | divātarādahnaḥ sakāśādevāprāyuṣe | pragatamāyuryasyāsau prāyuḥ | na prāyuraprāyuḥ | tasmai | asau yo 'stameti sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇānādāyāstametīti śruteḥ | rātrau sarve bhāvā nidrayāvṛtatvātprāyuṣa iva bhavanti | ayamagnistu sarvaprāṇiprāṇāpahartuḥ sūryasya rātrau svasminneva praveśātprakṛṣṭāyurbhavati | ato 'pi dhīmahi | kiṃcāta eva kāraṇādyato 'yaṃ sudarśataro yataścāprāyuḥ | ataḥ kāraṇādasmai tadarthamāyurhavirlakṣaṇamannaṃ grabhaṇavat grahaṇayuktamabhūt [?]

ग्रहणे दृष्टान्तः । सूनवे पुत्राय पितॄणां वीळु शर्म दृढं सुखसाधनं गृहं यथा ग्रहणवद्भवति तथेत्यर्थः । शर्मेति गृहनाम शर्म वर्मेति तन्नामसु पाठात् । इदानीमाहवनीयादिरूपेणाग्नेर्बहुत्वमपेक्ष्याह । एतेऽग्नयो भक्तं सेवमानमभक्तमसेवमानं च व्यन्तः एते प्राणिनोऽनुग्राह्या इति बुध्यमानाः अवः रक्षन्ति । यद्यपि विशेषेण प्राणिनो दाहपाकादिद्वारा रक्षन्ति तथाप्यस्मिन्यजमानेऽत्यन्तं कृतवन्त इत्याह । व्यन्तस्तस्मै प्रत्तं हविरश्नन्तो ऽजरा भवन्ति । स्वयं हविषाजराः सन्तो यजमानानप्यजरान्कुर्वन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

grahaṇe dṛṣṭāntaḥ | sūnave putrāya pitṝṇāṃ vīḷu śarma dṛḍhaṃ sukhasādhanaṃ gṛhaṃ yathā grahaṇavadbhavati tathetyarthaḥ | śarmeti gṛhanāma śarma varmeti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | idānīmāhavanīyādirūpeṇāgnerbahutvamapekṣyāha | ete 'gnayo bhaktaṃ sevamānamabhaktamasevamānaṃ ca vyantaḥ ete prāṇino 'nugrāhyā iti budhyamānāḥ avaḥ rakṣanti | yadyapi viśeṣeṇa prāṇino dāhapākādidvārā rakṣanti tathāpyasminyajamāne 'tyantaṃ kṛtavanta ityāha | vyantastasmai prattaṃ haviraśnanto 'jarā bhavanti | svayaṃ haviṣājarāḥ santo yajamānānapyajarānkurvantītyarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image. "[He is] one whom asya [asmai] — for him — pṛkṣam — food in the form of oblation — uparāsu — (uparāḥ are the lands near the vedi where the oblations are laid down) — in those dhīmahi — we place. Of whom? He says: the Agni who naktam — by night — is divātarāt — even more than by day — sudarśataraḥ — to be seen by all exceedingly, since in the night when all things are covered with darkness and invisible, he shines exceedingly himself. Therefore we place [the food] for him. And what is he like? Divātarāt — from the day alone — aprāyuṣe — [for him] 'whose life is not advanced': prāyuḥ is 'one whose life has advanced'; aprāyuḥ is its negative: 'The one who sets takes the breaths of all beings and sets,' says the śruti; at night all things are, as it were, prāyuṣaḥ [near-dead] because overcome by sleep. But Agni, because at night the Sun, who takes the breaths of all beings, enters into him alone, has a long life. Therefore we also place [the food] for him. Moreover for this very reason, since he is sudarśatara and aprāyu, for that reason for him, therefore, āyuḥ — food in the form of oblation — grabhaṇavat — became [fit for] seizure — [as in the simile:] sūnave — for a son, from the fathers, vīḷu — firm, śarma — house, the means of happiness, as it becomes fit for taking, so [the oblation]. (Śarma is a name for 'house'; śarma varma are read among its names.) Now, with regard to the plurality of Agni in the forms of Āhavanīya and the others, he says: ete agnayaḥ — these fires — bhaktam — the one who serves — abhaktam — and the one who does not serve — vyantaḥ — [knowing] these beings are to be favoured — avaḥ — protect. Though they specially protect beings through burning, cooking and the like, they have done this especially for this sacrificer: so he says. Vyantaḥ — eating the oblation offered to them, they become ajarāḥ — free from old age; themselves ageless by the oblation, they make even the sacrificers ageless: this is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Yaḥ — which Agni; naktam — in the night; divātarāt — more than by day; sudarśataraḥ — most worth seeing; divātarāt — from the day itself; aprāyuṣe — (in the night, since the Sun has entered into the fire) not [easily] destroyed; asya — for such Agni; tam pṛkṣam — that food in the form of oblation; uparāsu — in the places near the vedi; dhīmahi — we place; āt — for that reason itself; asya — his; āyuḥ — (in the form of oblation) food; sūnave — for a son; vīḷu — (given by the father) house; śarma na — as a means of happiness; grabhaṇavat — is fit for seizure; agnayaḥ — the fires, Āhavanīya and the others; bhaktam — [those] who serve them; abhaktam — [those] who do not serve; vyantaḥ — knowing (that all are to be favoured); avaḥ — protect; (and) vyantaḥ — those who eat the oblation offered by him; ajarāḥ — become ageless (making the sacrificers ageless too).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. We place the oblations in the places near the vedi for that Agni who shines more at night than by day and, because at night the Sun enters into him, is not, like other beings, exhausted of life. (Since he is of this nature) the oblations offered by us are fit for his acceptance, like a house given by a father to a son. The fires — the Āhavanīya and others — protect all, whether they serve [the fire] or not, thinking "all are to be favoured"; they themselves eat the oblation and become ageless (and make the sacrificers ageless).

Printed English (as printed): We place near the altar the (sacrificial) food of him who is more conspicuous by night than by day : (we offer it) to him who is scarcely alive by day : hence his (sacrificial) food finds prompt acceptance, like Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 14.

original p. 287

a dwelling (given by a father) to a son : these undecaying fires, (although) discriminating between the devout and the undevout, grant (both) protection, and accepting (the offerings of the pious), they are exempt from decay.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 5.

pṛkṣam — havirlakṣaṇam annam — the word pṛkṣa is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). Sāyaṇa explains: "food in the form of oblation".

uparāsu — uparamante 'smin havīṃṣity uparāḥ vedisamīpabhūmayaḥ: the places near the sacrificial altar, where the oblations to be offered are got ready and placed. The word upara is recorded among the eight names of the quarters, āśāḥ (Ni. 2-16, as printed "೨-೧೬"); hence Yāska explains it as "quarter". The word upara is also stated among the names of clouds. It is described that for Agni, in the regions near the sacrificial altar, food in the form of oblation is prepared.

naktam — rātrau: "in the night": the word nakta is recorded among the twenty-three names of night (Ni. 1-[?]8 [as printed "೨-೧೮"]).

divātarāt sudarśatarah — ahno 'pi atyarthaṃ sarvaiḥ darśanīyo bhavati: even when, in the night, all things are covered with darkness and are not properly visible, Agni, by his own light, shines more than he shines in the day (than the light of the day): this is the meaning.

divātarāt aprāyuṣe — ahnaḥ sakāśād eva aprāyuṣe | pragatam āyur yasyāsau prāyuḥ | na prāyuḥ aprāyuḥ: one who has no [long] life is called prāyu; aprāyu conveys "one endowed with life"; hence the sense: Agni has long life through the day.

असौ योऽस्तमेति स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायास्तमेति ॥

asau yo 'stameti sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇānādāyāstameti ‖

(Tai. Ā. 1-14 [?], as printed "ತೈ. ಆ. ೧-೧೪".) It is said in the Taittirīya śruti that when the Sun sets, he takes the breaths of all beings and makes them as if inactive, and sets. By this, all beings (in sleep) are as if without life. Sāyaṇa explains this same idea with the sentence rātrau sarve bhāvā nidrayāvṛtatvāt prāyuṣa iva bhavanti.

Ayam agnis tu sarvaprāṇiprāṇāpahartuḥ sūryasya rātrau svasminn eva praveśāt prakṛṣṭāyur bhavati — only Agni, in whom the Sun, the taker of the breaths of all, enters at night, has a long life. It is stated in the Taittirīya śruti "the Sun enters Agni" (as in agnir vāyum ādityaḥ …, as printed); thus it is stated. We meditate on Agni, whose glory is of this kind.

āyuḥ — havirlakṣaṇam annam — "food that exists in the form of oblation". Yāska has recorded the word āyuḥ among the twenty-eight names of food (Ni. 3-9).

मा नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिन्द्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतः परि ख्यन् । यद्वाजिनो देवजातस्य सप्तेः प्रवक्ष्यामो विदथे वीर्याणि ॥

mā no mitro varuṇo aryamāyurindra ṛbhukṣā marutaḥ pari khyan | yadvājino devajātasya sapteḥ pravakṣyāmo vidathe vīryāṇi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-1, as printed "೧-೧೬೨-೧".) Here āyuḥ is vāyuḥ with loss of the v: āyanāt etīti hy asau viśvam, says Durgācārya, explaining the sentence vāyur ayanaḥ, and explains the word āyus as "wind".

वात आ वातु भेषजं शंभु मयोभु नो हृदे । प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषत् ॥

vāta ā vātu bheṣajaṃ śaṃbhu mayobhu no hṛde | pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-186-1, as printed "೧೦-೧೮೬-೧".) Here the word āyus is explained with the sense "time of life".

असुनीते मनो अस्मासु धारय जीवातवे सु प्र तिरा न आयुः ।

asunīte mano asmāsu dhāraya jīvātave su pra tirā na āyuḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-59-5 [?], as printed "೧೦-೫೯-೫"; the second line in the print is garbled in my reading.)

भागं देवेभ्यो वि दधात्यायन्प्र चन्द्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः ॥

bhāgaṃ devebhyo vi dadhātyāyanpra candramāstirate dīrghamāyuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-19 [?], as printed "೧೦-೮೫-೧೯".) In these ṛks the word āyus is explained as "time of life". Here the food in the form of oblation, which is conveyed by the word āyuḥ, has been taken for offering to Agni (that is, prepared).

sūnave vīḷu śarma na grabhaṇavat — pitroḥ putrāya dṛḍhaṃ sukhasādhanaṃ gṛhaṃ yathā grahaṇavad bhavati tathā: the comparison is that, as a house giving happiness, given by the father to the son, is fit to be accepted by the son, so the oblation that we prepare is fit to be accepted by Agni.

vīḷu — this word is recorded among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9). The word śarma is recorded among the twenty-two names of house, gayaḥ, kṛdaraḥ and the like (Ni. 3-4 [?], as printed "೩-೧೩").

स्योना पृथिवि भवानृक्षरा निवेशनी । यच्छा नः शर्म सप्रथः ॥

syonā pṛthivi bhavānṛkṣarā niveśanī | yacchā naḥ śarma saprathaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-15, as printed "೧-೨೨-೧೫".)

Here śarma is explained as "happiness".

agnayaḥ vyantaḥ ajarāḥ — taiḥ prattaṃ havir aśnantaḥ ajarāḥ bhavanti | svayaṃ haviṣā ajarāḥ santo yajamānān api ajarān kurvanti: here the plural "agnayaḥ" is used. The plurality of Agni, by the divisions Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇāgni, is appropriate. It is described that these fires, enkindled by the oblations offered by the sacrificers, make the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice endowed with brilliance.

And, repeating the word vyantaḥ in this mantra, these fires protect beings by the acts of burning and cooking [for them], by making their radiance grow so as to be favourable to them, and by cooking their food; and, explaining that a result surpassing the protection of other beings comes to the sacrificer from the fires, he also describes the purpose of the repetition of the words vyantaḥ ajarāḥ.

agnayaḥ bhaktaṃ sevamānam abhaktam asevamānaṃ ca vyantaḥ ete prāṇino 'nugrāhyā iti buddhyamānāḥ avaḥ rakṣanti — the fires, knowing that some serve what is cooked and some serve what is uncooked (i.e. do not serve the fire) and that they are to be favoured, protect them: this describes the compassion Agni has in the matter of protecting beings. But by the sentence vyantaḥ ajarā bhavanti, it also shows the distinction, from the protection of other beings, [of the sacrificer], who, increased by the offering of the oblation, receives in addition the best brilliance.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and the page). dhīmahi — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; liṅ first person plural, mahiṅ; liṅaḥ sīyuṭ (Pā. 3-4-102) gives sīyuṭ; chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117) gives the sārvadhātuka designation; liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya (Pā. 7-2-79) elides the s of sīyuṭ; śap; lopo vyor vali elides the y; ātaś lopa iṭi ca (Pā. 6-4-64) elides the ā of the root; tiṅ-nighāta. sudarśataraḥ, divātarāt — in both places tarap in the sense of itself. aprāyuṣe — pragatam āyur yasya asau prāyuḥ, na prāyuḥ aprāyuḥ; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2) gives the natural accent of the first member, the indeclinable.

स हि स एव स्तुत्यतया प्रसिद्ध एवाग्निस्तुविष्वणिः । तुवीति बहुनाम तुरु तुवीति तन्नामसु पाठात् । बहुस्वनिः प्रभूतध्वनिर्युक्तो वर्तते । अत्यन्तज्वलितेऽग्नौ वायुसंपर्कात् भुगुभुगिति ध्वनिरुद्यते । ज्वलतीत्यर्थः । ध्वनने दृष्टान्तः । मारुतं शर्धो न मरुत्संबन्धि बलमिव मरुतां समूहो यथा ध्वनयति तथेत्यर्थः । कुत्रेति तदुच्यते । अप्नस्वतीषु खननप्रोक्षणादिकर्मोपेतासु । अप्न इति कर्मनाम अप्नो दंस इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । उर्वरासूरुवरणयुक्तासु श्रेष्ठासु वेदिभूमिषु । कीदृशोऽयम् । इष्टनिर्यष्टव्यः । तथा आर्तनासु । आर्तान्करोतीत्यार्तयिता [?] । आर्तयन्तीत्यार्तनाः पृतनाः । तासां जयाय इष्टनिः यष्टव्यो वा । संकटे कुर्वन्ति [?] । किंचैवं स्तुतोऽग्निः हव्यान्याज्यपुरोडाशादीन्यादत् । अत्ति । भक्षयति । छान्दसो लुङ् । यद्वा । आज्पूर्वाद्ददातेराजो ऽनाशास्यविहरणादीत्यादिना [?] व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदाभावः । गातिस्थेति सिचो लुक् । छान्दसो ह्रस्वः । केवलादेव वा छन्दस्यपि दृश्यत इत्यनाजादेरप्याडागमः । आत एवानवग्रहः । स एव शिष्यते । आददिः सर्वत्र हविरादानशीलः । तथा यज्ञस्य केतुः प्रज्ञापकः केतुस्थानीयो वा । अर्हणा पूजनीयः । सुपां सुलुगिति सोराकारः । प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वं छान्दसम् । किंच हर्षतो हविर्भक्षणादत्यन्तहर्षयुक्तस्य यद्वाभिमतफलदानेन यजमानान्हर्षयतो हृषीवत आज्यादिस्वीकारेण हर्षयुक्तस्याग्नेः पन्थां पन्थानं मार्गं विश्वे सर्वे मनुष्या जुषन्त । प्रीणयन्ति । असेवन्त वा । किमर्थम् । शुभे शुभाय शोभनाय सुखप्राप्तये । पन्थानं सर्वैर्गन्तव्यं निर्भयं प्रौढमार्गमिव [?] । तथा लोके नरो मनुष्याः शुभे शोभनाय सुखप्राप्तये पन्थानं सर्वैर्गन्तव्यं निर्भयं प्रौढमार्गमिव । सेवन्ते [?] । तथा विश्वे नरोऽग्निमेव प्रीणयन्ति साधयन्ति ॥ [?]

sa hi sa eva stutyatayā prasiddha evāgnistuviṣvaṇiḥ | tuvīti bahunāma turu tuvīti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | bahusvaniḥ prabhūtadhvaniryukto vartate | atyantajvalite 'gnau vāyusaṃparkāt bhugubhugiti dhvanirudyate | jvalatītyarthaḥ | dhvanane dṛṣṭāntaḥ | mārutaṃ śardho na marutsaṃbandhi balamiva marutāṃ samūho yathā dhvanayati tathetyarthaḥ | kutreti taducyate | apnasvatīṣu khananaprokṣaṇādikarmopetāsu | apna iti karmanāma apno daṃsa iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | urvarāsūruvaraṇayuktāsu śreṣṭhāsu vedibhūmiṣu | kīdṛśo 'yam | iṣṭaniryaṣṭavyaḥ | tathā ārtanāsu | ārtānkarotītyārtayitā [?] | ārtayantītyārtanāḥ pṛtanāḥ | tāsāṃ jayāya iṣṭaniḥ yaṣṭavyo vā | saṃkaṭe kurvanti [?] | kiṃcaivaṃ stuto 'gniḥ havyānyājyapuroḍāśādīnyādat | atti | bhakṣayati | chāndaso luṅ | yadvā | ājpūrvāddadāterājo 'nāśāsyaviharaṇādītyādinā [?] vyatyayenātmanepadābhāvaḥ | gātistheti sico luk | chāndaso hrasvaḥ | kevalādeva vā chandasyapi dṛśyata ityanājāderapyāḍāgamaḥ | āta evānavagrahaḥ | sa eva śiṣyate | ādadiḥ sarvatra havirādānaśīlaḥ | tathā yajñasya ketuḥ prajñāpakaḥ ketusthānīyo vā | arhaṇā pūjanīyaḥ | supāṃ sulugiti sorākāraḥ | pratyayādyudāttatvaṃ chāndasam | kiṃca harṣato havirbhakṣaṇādatyantaharṣayuktasya yadvābhimataphaladānena yajamānānharṣayato hṛṣīvata ājyādisvīkāreṇa harṣayuktasyāgneḥ panthāṃ panthānaṃ mārgaṃ viśve sarve manuṣyā juṣanta | prīṇayanti | asevanta vā | kimartham | śubhe śubhāya śobhanāya sukhaprāptaye | panthānaṃ sarvairgantavyaṃ nirbhayaṃ prauḍhamārgamiva [?] | tathā loke naro manuṣyāḥ śubhe śobhanāya sukhaprāptaye panthānaṃ sarvairgantavyaṃ nirbhayaṃ prauḍhamārgamiva | sevante [?] | tathā viśve naro 'gnimeva prīṇayanti sādhayanti ‖ [?]

"Sa hi — that very Agni, well known as the one to be praised, tuviṣvaṇiḥ — tuvi is a name for 'much' (turu, tuvi are read among its names); one who has a loud sound, who is endowed with abundant noise: when the fire is brightly burning, by contact with the wind the sound 'bhugubhugu' arises: that is, he blazes. An illustration of the sounding: mārutaṃ śardho na — as the host of the Maruts makes the force of the Maruts roar, so. Where? Apnasvatīṣu — in the [places] with works such as digging and sprinkling (apnaḥ is a name for 'work': apno daṃsaḥ are read among its names); urvarāsu — in the excellent places of the sacrificial altar, spread out. What is he like? Iṣṭaniḥ — to be worshipped; likewise ārtanāsu iṣṭaniḥ — in [those] battles that cause distress (ārtanāḥ are armies, pṛtanāḥ), he is to be worshipped for victory over them. Moreover Agni, thus praised, havyāni ādat — eats, consumes the oblations of ghee, cakes and the like; ādat is a Vedic aorist; or [the form arises] from the root dā with the prefix ā, with the absence of ātmanepada by vyatyaya; loss of siC by gātisthā…; Vedic shortening; the augment aṭ also appears in the Veda even for a stem not beginning with a vowel; for this very reason there is no avagraha [in the Pada]: that alone remains. Ādadiḥ — always one whose nature is to take the oblation; likewise yajñasya ketuḥ — the one who makes it known, or the banner (ketu) of the sacrifice; arhaṇā — worthy of worship (su → ā by supāṃ sulug; the accent on the first syllable of the suffix is Vedic). Moreover, harṣataḥ — of Agni, who is full of delight through eating the oblation, or who gladdens the sacrificers by giving the desired fruit, hṛṣīvataḥ — who is joyful on accepting ghee and the like, panthām — the path — viśve — all men — juṣanta — love, serve. For what? Śubhe — for the good, for the attainment of happiness: as in the world men go by a path that all must go, free of fear, like a broad road; so all men serve Agni alone, and attain their end through him."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Apnasvatīṣu — endowed with works (digging and the like); urvarāsu — in the excellent altars; mārutam — connected with the Maruts; śardhaḥ na — like the force; tuviṣvaṇiḥ — of great sound; iṣṭaniḥ — (in sacrifices) worthy of worship; ārtanāsu — in battles, for gaining victory; iṣṭaniḥ — to be worshipped (desired); ādadiḥ — of the nature of taking up the oblations and the like; yajñasya ketuḥ — the one who makes the sacrifice known (the banner of the sacrifice); arhaṇā — worthy of worship; sa hi — that very Agni; havyāni — oblations such as ghee, cakes and the like; ādat — eats; atha — therefore; harṣataḥ — made joyful (by eating the oblation) or (by giving the desired gifts) gladdening the sacrificers; hṛṣīvataḥ — joyful (with the acceptance of ghee and the like); asya — of this Agni; panthām — the path; śubhe — for the attainment of happiness; naraḥ — men; (śubhe — for happiness); panthām na — as an excellent path (they follow); viśve — all men; juṣanta sma — serve.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Agni, roaring like the wind that blows strongly, shining in the altars that are furnished with rites (digging, sprinkling and the like), to be worshipped for the destruction of enemies, the one who makes the sacrifice known (the banner of the sacrifice), and worthy of worship, accepts the ghee, cakes and the like; (satisfied by the oblations) he is gladdened and, by giving the desired gifts, gladdens the sacrificers; all men, wishing happiness, follow his very path, as men in the world follow the road to happiness.

Printed English (as printed): He roars aloud, like the roaring of the winds, amidst the sanctified and selected (rites of sacred) solemnities ; he who is to be worshipped, who is to be adored (for victory) over hosts (of enemies) ; he, the receiver (of oblations), the manifester of the sacrifice ; he, who is deserving of veneration, devours the oblations : hence, all men for their good pursue the path of Agni, who gives pleasure (to his worshippers), being pleased (himself), in like manner as men follow a path (that leads) to happiness.

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6.

sa hi tuviṣvaṇiḥ mārutaṃ śardho na — sa eva stutyatayā prasiddha evāgniḥ prabhūtadhvaniyukto vartate | atyantajvalite 'gnau vāyusaṃparkāt bhugubhugiti dhvanir udyate jvalatīty arthaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ marutsaṃbandhi balam iva marutāṃ samūho yathā dhvanayati tathā: it is a well-known fact that when a fire blazes brightly, from contact with the wind a sound is produced; just as the host of the Maruts, the force of the strong wind, causes a sound, so does this Agni.

śardho na — the word śardha is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 2-[?]; as printed "೩-೯"). By this it is explained that the word śardha means "strength".

apnasvatīṣu urvarāsu iṣṭaniḥ — since the word apnaḥ is recorded among the twenty-six names of works, apno daṃsaḥ (Ni. 2-1 [?], as printed "೨-೧"), the word apnas conveys the meaning "work". It is described that Agni is to be honoured in the excellent sacrificial altar, which is endowed with many good qualities, and, for purification of the sacrificial ground, with rites such as khanana (digging) and prokṣaṇa (sprinkling with water).

ārtanāsu iṣṭaniḥ — ārtān karotīty ārtayati | ārtayantīty ārtanāḥ pṛtanāḥ | tāsāṃ jayāya iṣṭavyaḥ yaṣṭavyo vā: armies that put into distress, or that make others distressed, are indicated by the word ārtanā. Agni is to be worshipped for the conquest of these armies, he explains.

yajñasya ketuḥ — prajñāpakaḥ ketusthānīyo vā: Sāyaṇa explains that Agni is the one who gives knowledge or who indicates victory. The author of the Nirukta records ketu, keta, among the eleven names of prajñā (Ni. 3-13), which gives the meaning "wisdom".

नवोनवो भवति जायमानोऽह्नां केतुरुषसामेत्यग्रम् । भागं देवेभ्यो वि दधात्यायन्प्र चन्द्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः ॥

navonavo bhavati jāyamāno 'hnāṃ keturuṣasāmetyagram | bhāgaṃ devebhyo vi dadhātyāyanpra candramāstirate dīrghamāyuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-19, as printed "೧೦-೮೫-೧೯".) There, Durgācārya, [explaining] ahnāṃ ketuḥ: lakṣaṇaṃ tatkālopacayāpacayābhyāṃ ahāni lakṣyante — "the days are known by the waxing and waning of the moon"; or ahnāṃ ketuḥ kartā svagativiśeṣaiḥ — "the maker of days by its particular motions": the moon, by his particular motions, causes the waxing and waning of time, and is thus the sign of the day;

or, "he makes the day by his own special motions": thus he explains it, and gives the two senses prajñāpakaḥ, kartā.

महो अर्णः सरस्वती प्र चेतयति केतुना । धियो विश्वा वि राजति ॥

maho arṇaḥ sarasvatī pra cetayati ketunā | dhiyo viśvā vi rājati ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-12, as printed "೧-೩-೧೨".) Here ketu is explained as karmaṇā prajñayā vā, "by work or by wisdom"; the two senses of "work" or "wisdom" result.

एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते । निष्कृण्वाना आयुधानीव धृष्णवः प्रति गावोऽरुषीर्यन्ति मातरः ॥

etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumañjate | niṣkṛṇvānā āyudhānīva dhṛṣṇavaḥ prati gāvo 'ruṣīryanti mātaraḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1, as printed "೧-೯೨-೧".) Here the word ketu is explained as prajñāna, "wisdom".

उदु त्यं जातवेदसं देवं वहन्ति केतवः । दृशे विश्वाय सूर्यम् ॥

udu tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahanti ketavaḥ | dṛśe viśvāya sūryam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-1, as printed "೧-೫೦-೧".) Here ketu is explained as "ray". Sāyaṇa has explained for the many-meaning word ketu here the sense "the one who makes known (indicator)".

harṣataḥ — havirbhakṣaṇād atyantaharṣayuktasya yadvā abhimataphaladānena yajamānān harṣayataḥ: the sense is: "one who is exceedingly delighted by eating oblations, or who gladdens the sacrificers by giving them desired things".

hṛṣīvataḥ panthāṃ viśve juṣanta śubhe — by this sentence it is stated that all worship Agni, or satisfy him, and follow the path that leads to fulfilment in this world and the next; and the comparison śubhe na panthāṃ naraḥ is given: as in the world men, for the sake of happiness, follow a path that all must go, free from fear — [that is,] a broad road: the sense is that, by performing in the world acts that must be done for happiness, they take to the path that brings the fruit by that practice.

naraḥ — manuṣyāḥ — the word naraḥ is recorded among the twenty-five names of men, manuṣyāḥ naraḥ (Ni. 3-8). Narā manuṣyā nṛtyanti karmasu (Ni. 5-1 [?], as printed "೫-೧"?) — the author of the Nirukta, giving the formation of the word narā, explains the meaning: "since men, when their various works demand it, move the limbs of their body here and there while doing the various works, they are nṛtyanti, 'dance', hence narāḥ".

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

यद्यं द्विता द्वित्वमापन्नं द्विप्रकारं श्रौतस्मार्तभेदेन द्वित्वमापन्नम् । यद्वा । उपलक्षणमेतत् । आहवनीयादिरूपेण नानाविधम् । यद्वा । द्विता द्विविधाय ऐहिकामुष्मिकफलायोभयाय । विभक्तेराजादेशः । ईमिममग्निं कीस्तासः कीर्तनं कुर्वन्तः स्तोतारः । पचाद्यचि छान्दसं सत्वम् । अभिद्यवः अभितो द्योतमानाः नमस्यन्तो नमस्कारोपलक्षितमुपस्थानं कुर्वन्तः भृगवः भृगुगोत्रोत्पन्ना महर्षय उपवोचन्त । उपेत्य ब्रुवन्ति । किं कुर्वन्तः । दाशा दानेन निमित्तभूतेन हविर्दानार्थं मथ्नन्तः अरण्योरग्निं मन्थनं कुर्वन्तः तथा भृगवो भ्रष्टारो हविषा पापानां वा । किंच यो ऽग्निः शुचिर्दीप्तो धर्णिर्धारणकुशलो ऽयमग्निरेषां दीयमानानां वसूनां हविर्लक्षणानामीशे ईष्टे । समर्थो भवति । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः । यद्वा । एषां दृश्यमानानां मणिमुक्तादीनां वसूनामीशे ईष्टे । समर्थो भवति प्रदातुमिति शेषः । किंचायमग्निर्मेधिरः । मेधो यज्ञः । तद्वान् स्वयं यष्टव्यत्वेन प्रधानभूतः सन् प्रियान् स्वप्रीतिहेतून्याज्यादीनपिधीन् पर्याप्तिपर्यन्तं [?] दत्तान्वनिषीष्ट । संभजताम् । संभजतां वा । तथा मेधिरो मेधावान् असौ अन्यदेवताकेष्वपि यज्ञेषु स्वयमाज्यभागप्रयाजादिरूपं हविः संभजते ॥

yadyaṃ dvitā dvitvamāpannaṃ dviprakāraṃ śrautasmārtabhedena dvitvamāpannam | yadvā | upalakṣaṇametat | āhavanīyādirūpeṇa nānāvidham | yadvā | dvitā dvividhāya aihikāmuṣmikaphalāyobhayāya | vibhakterājādeśaḥ | īmimamagniṃ kīstāsaḥ kīrtanaṃ kurvantaḥ stotāraḥ | pacādyaci chāndasaṃ satvam | abhidyavaḥ abhito dyotamānāḥ namasyanto namaskāropalakṣitamupasthānaṃ kurvantaḥ bhṛgavaḥ bhṛgugotrotpannā maharṣaya upavocanta | upetya bruvanti | kiṃ kurvantaḥ | dāśā dānena nimittabhūtena havirdānārthaṃ mathnantaḥ araṇyoragniṃ manthanaṃ kurvantaḥ tathā bhṛgavo bhraṣṭāro haviṣā pāpānāṃ vā | kiṃca yo 'gniḥ śucirdīpto dharṇirdhāraṇakuśalo 'yamagnireṣāṃ dīyamānānāṃ vasūnāṃ havirlakṣaṇānāmīśe īṣṭe | samartho bhavati | lopasta ātmanepadeṣviti talopaḥ | yadvā | eṣāṃ dṛśyamānānāṃ maṇimuktādīnāṃ vasūnāmīśe īṣṭe | samartho bhavati pradātumiti śeṣaḥ | kiṃcāyamagnirmedhiraḥ | medho yajñaḥ | tadvān svayaṃ yaṣṭavyatvena pradhānabhūtaḥ san priyān svaprītihetūnyājyādīnapidhīn paryāptiparyantaṃ [?] dattānvaniṣīṣṭa | saṃbhajatām | saṃbhajatāṃ vā | tathā medhiro medhāvān asau anyadevatākeṣvapi yajñeṣu svayamājyabhāgaprayājādirūpaṃ haviḥ saṃbhajate ‖

Read from the image; the OCR is garbled in the middle. "paryāptiparyantam" and the reading of the last clause are small and doubtful. "Yat ayam dvitā — this [Agni] having become twofold, twofold by the division into śrauta and smārta; or this is only an indication: of many kinds, by the forms Āhavanīya and so on; or dvitā — for the twofold fruit, this-worldly and the next-worldly, both; the ending ā by substitution of the case-ending. Īm — this Agni — kīstāsaḥ — those who sing the praise, the praisers (the Vedic sat-form from the suffix ac in the pacādi class); abhidyavaḥ — shining all round; namasyantaḥ — doing homage, offering attendance marked by salutation; bhṛgavaḥ — the great seers born in the lineage of Bhṛgu upavocanta — come near and speak. What are they doing? Dāśā — for the giving of oblations, with the giving as the cause; mathnantaḥ — churning the fire out of the two araṇis; and bhṛgavaḥ, the burners — the destroyers of sins by the oblation. Moreover, the Agni who is śuciḥ — bright, dharṇiḥ — skilled in bearing, this Agni īśe — has power over eṣām vasūnām — these oblations in the form of what is given; he is capable. Or else, of these visible jewels, pearls and the like, treasures, he is able to give. Moreover this Agni is medhiraḥ — medha is the sacrifice; he, endowed with it, being chief as himself to be worshipped, priyān — dear to himself, ghee and the like, apidhīn — as much as are given to satisfaction — vaniṣīṣṭa — may he partake; or may he partake of [them]. Likewise medhiraḥ — the intelligent, in sacrifices addressed to other deities also, he himself partakes of the oblation in the form of the ājya-bhāga, the prayājas and the like."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Dvitā — (in the forms śrauta and smārta) of two kinds, or of many forms such as the Āhavanīya and the others, or for the twofold fruit of this world and the next; yat — which; īm — Agni; kīstāsaḥ — those who praise; abhidyavaḥ — those who make [him] famous; namasyantaḥ — [those who] make homage (in the form of attendance); bhṛgavaḥ — the sages born of the Bhṛgu lineage; bhṛgavaḥ — those who burn up sins, or those who give oblations; dāśā — for giving oblations; mathnantaḥ — churning (in the araṇis); upavocanta — come near and praise; yaḥ agniḥ — which Agni; śuciḥ — shining; eṣām vasūnām — of these oblations (of treasures such as jewels); dharṇiḥ — the protector; īśe — is able to give (them); (saḥ — that Agni); medhiraḥ — chief in the sacrifice; apidhīn — to the satisfied ones; priyān — dear (ghee and the like; and satisfaction); vaniṣīṣṭa — may he partake; medhiraḥ — intelligent Agni; ā vaniṣīṣṭa — (in sacrifices for other deities also) may he partake of the share of the oblation.

original p. 298

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The sages of the Bhṛgu lineage, who in every place make known this Agni who is of the śrauta and smārta forms or of many forms such as the Āhavanīya (for the sake of attaining the twofold fruit of this world and the next), and who do him homage (in the form of attendance), come near and praise him while churning him for the oblation; the radiant Agni, being the support of the oblations that are given (and of jewels, pearls and the like), is able to give them; and, being chief in the sacrifice, may he accept the dear oblations of those who are satisfied; and, being intelligent, may he accept his share of the oblations (in sacrifices to other deities too).

Printed English (as printed): The descendants of Bhrigu, celebrating him (Agni) in both his forms, glorifying him, and paying him homage, proclaim his praises ; the descendants of Bhrigu, rubbing (the sticks to kindle flame) for the oblation. For the radiant Agni, who is the guardian of all these treasures, has power (to distribute them). May he, the receiver of sacrifices, partake of the agreeable (offerings) given to satiety ; may he, the receiver of sacrifices, partake (of the oblations).

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 7.

dvitā īṃ kīstāsaḥ — dvitvam āpannaṃ dviprakāraṃ śrautasmārtabhedena dvitvam āpannam | yadvā dvividhāya aihikāmuṣmikaphalāya ubhayāya imam agniṃ kīrtanaṃ kurvantaḥ stotāraḥ. For the word dvitā, first, they serve Agni both by the order of the observances stated in the śrauta-sūtra and by the order of the smārta rites stated in the gṛhya-sūtras; second, for the fruit that is to be enjoyed in this world and the benefit of the world beyond, in the worlds of virtue, they worship Agni too: this is the meaning he has given.

original p. 299

bhṛgavo mathnanto dāśā bhṛgavaḥ — bhṛgugotrotpannā maharṣayaḥ havirdānārthaṃ araṇyām agnimathanaṃ kurvantaḥ | tathā bhṛgavaḥ bhrastāro haviṣā pāpānāṃ vā: the word bhṛgavaḥ is said twice. For the first, the great seers born in the Bhṛgu lineage; for the second, "burners of sins" — the great seers of the Bhṛgu lineage who give oblations to Agni so that sins are washed away; they churn Agni in the araṇis and produce him. The author of the Nirukta, explaining the word bhṛgu, says —

भृगुरर्चिषि संबभूव भृगुर्भ्रज्यमानो न देहे ॥

bhṛgurarciṣi saṃbabhūva bhṛgurbhrajyamāno na dehe ‖

(Ni. 3-17, as printed "೩-೧೭".) — and describes "the seer Bhṛgu was born from the flame of Agni".

In the sentences of the vākya texts, the indeclinables occur as fillers (padapūraka) to complete the sentence; in verse-bound usage the indeclinables kam, īm, it, u have no meaning, and so they are said to be fillers (padapūraṇa) — thus Yāska has explained (Ni. 1-9).

एमेनं सृजता सुते मन्दिमिन्द्राय मन्दिने । चक्रिं विश्वानि चक्रये ॥

emenaṃ sṛjatā sute mandimindrāya mandine | cakriṃ viśvāni cakraye ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-[?]-[?], as printed "೮-೧-೨"? — I have read it so; the first numeral is doubtful.) Read letter by letter; "emenaṃ" for "enam" as printed. Here īm is cited as a filler word; and "pari īm sīm iti vyākhyātāḥ" is said in the Nirukta (Ni. 5-28 [?], as printed "೫-೨೮").

agniḥ śuciḥ dharṇiḥ eṣāṃ vasūnām īśe — dīptaḥ dhāraṇakuśalaḥ ayam agniḥ dīyamānānāṃ havirlakṣaṇānām īṣṭe samartho bhavati | yadvā eṣāṃ dṛśyamānānāṃ maṇimuktādīnāṃ vasūnāṃ pradātuṃ samartho bhavati: Agni is shining, endowed with the power to bear (to support); he is capable in the matter of the oblations that are given, which are of the nature of food; or he is capable of giving the visible treasures, such as jewels and pearls. The author of the Nirukta —

त्वमग्ने द्युभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिस्त्वमद्भ्यस्त्वमश्मनस्परि । त्वं वनेभ्यस्त्वमोषधीभ्यस्त्वं नृणां नृपते जायसे शुचिः ॥

tvamagne dyubhistvamāśuśukṣaṇistvamadbhyastvamaśmanaspari | tvaṃ vanebhyastvamoṣadhībhyastvaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛpate jāyase śuciḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-1, as printed "೨-೧-೧".) citing this ṛk, śuciḥ śocater jvalatikarmaṇaḥ ayam apīta(ra)ḥ śuciḥ etasmād eva jvalati — the word śuci is formed from the root śuc meaning "to burn", and so he explains that the word śuci means Agni;

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 3-17; 1-9-2; 5-28

original p. 300

and also, stating another view, that this Agni is the worldly fire, he describes the greatness of this Agni, that sins are removed by this Agni.

The word vasu, though it has many meanings, is here used in the sense of "wealth" and "food in the form of oblation".

medhiraḥ — medho yajñaḥ tadvān svayaṃ yaṣṭavyatvena pradhānabhūtaḥ: the word medha is used in the sense of "sacrifice"; Agni himself is the principal deity for those who perform the sacrifice: thus it is described.

medhira āvaniṣīṣṭa — medhāvān asau anyadevatākeṣv api yajñeṣu svayam ājyabhāgaprayājādirūpaṃ haviḥ saṃbhajate: here the word medhira is explained as "intelligent"; the intelligent Agni, even in sacrifices that are performed with reference to other deities, takes for himself the portions of the oblation, separately, and especially: thus he describes it.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and the page). dvitā — the suffix dhā in the sense of manner; in the Veda, ta is substituted; in the second explanation supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39) gives ā to the case-ending; since cit, final-acute. kīstāsaḥ — root kṛta saṃśabdane; upadhāyāś ca (Pā. 7-1-101) gives i for the penultimate ṛ; raparatva; upadhāyāṃ ca (Pā. 8-2-78) lengthens it; since it belongs to the pacādi, nandigrahapacādibhyaḥ (Pā. 3-1-134) gives the suffix ac; in the Veda s occurs for the r; with jas following, ājjaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50) gives asuk. abhidyavaḥ — abhigatā dyauḥ yaiḥ te abhidyavaḥ; the word abhi has the final-acute by the prātipadika accent; in the bahuvrīhi the accent of the first member. namasyantaḥ — namovarivaścitraṅaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-19) gives kyac in the sense of worship; after the kyac-ending, śatṛ in the laṭ sense; nominative plural; the accent of kyac remains. upavocanta — root brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; in the Veda luṅ in the present sense; third person plural, anta in place of jhi; when ci comes, bruvo vaciḥ (Pā. 2-4-53) gives vac; asyativaktikhyātibhyo 'ṅ (Pā. 3-1-52) gives aṅ for cli; vaca um (Pā. 7-4-20) gives um to the root; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi gives no augment aṭ; since yat is connected [in the Saṃhitā; as printed], no nighāta; since the word has an acute, the gati (upa) gets the nighāta accent by tiṅ ca udāttavati (Pā. 8-1-71).

"…by the force of the prefix a suitable verb is to be supplied: [āgacchanti, 'they come']. Why? Vayaḥ — aiming at food in the form of oblation, since it is given to the others from Agni's mouth. Moreover, the priests who conduct [the sacrifice] too, among the gods who are being worshipped, give oblations (havyā) to Agni."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. Viśvāsām — all; viśām — the performers of sacrifice; patim — the protector; sarvāsām — all the people; samānam — the one who is of one form; daṃpatim — the guardian of the house (in the form of Gārhapatya and the like); satyagirvāhasam — [the one] who is the refuge of praises that yield the true fruit (of the priests who are bearers of true-fruited words); tvā — you; bhuje — for enjoyment (of the oblations and the like); havāmahe — we call; mānuṣāṇām — for men; atithim — [him] worthy of worship like a guest (Agni); bhuje — to accept (the oblation and so on); havāmahe — we call; yasya — whose Agni; āsayā — in the neighbourhood; pituḥ na — like [sons dwelling] near the father; amṛtāsaḥ — those known to be eaters of oblations; amī viśve ca — and all these gods; vayaḥ — to the food in the form of oblation (aiming at it); ā — (they come) (to that Agni); vayaḥ — (of the sacrifice) the priests, who conduct it; deveṣu — among the (other) gods; havyā — the oblations; ā — (give).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. We call Agni — the protector of all performers of sacrifice (as giver of what is desired), of one form for all people (as the aid to burning, cooking and the like), the guardian of the house (in forms such as Āhavanīya), the support of the praises that give the true fruit (of the priests who recite them), and, to men, worthy of worship like a guest — for the eating of the oblations and the like. As sons attend upon the father, so all these gods, known as the eaters of the shares of the oblation, come to the neighbourhood of Agni, aiming at the oblation; the priests, at the time of giving the oblation, give an oblation to Agni among the other gods too.

Printed English (as printed): We invoke you, the protector of all people, the same alike to all, the preserver of the house, to enjoy (the oblation); you who are the wafter of our infallible prayer, to enjoy (the oblation); we invoke you, who are the guest of men, to whom all these immortals apply for their sustenance, as (a son) to a father; you, to whom the priests offer oblations amongst the gods.

original p. 304

Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 8.

In this ṛk, viśvāsāṃ viśāṃ patiṃ samānaṃ havāmahe: it is described that Agni is the protector of all the people, and of the sacrificers, since he grants to each what each desires; and that he is the same to all in rendering service.

daṃpatim — gārhapatyādirūpeṇa gṛhasya pālakam: under the name Gārhapatya, Agni protects the sacrificer's house. The author of the Nirukta reads the word dame among the twenty-two names of "house", gayaḥ kṛtiḥ [as printed, probably kṛdaraḥ] and so on (Ni. 3-13); by this dame is "in the house". And in explaining the word damūnāḥ he says damūnā iti gṛhanāma tanmanāḥ syāt (Ni. 4-4 [?]); Durgācārya: damūnā ity etad gṛhanāma etad vā yasya manasi mameti saḥ damūnāḥ gṛhapatir agniḥ — "the word damūnas, [derived from] dama 'house', for one who thinks 'it is mine' in the mind of the house; the master of the house is Agni". Since the explanation is that Agni is thus gṛhapati, "lord of the house, conscious of it as his own", the name Gārhapatya arises for Agni.

satyagirvāhasam — yathārthabhūtānām avisaṃvādiphalānāṃ stutirūpāṇāṃ girāṃ voḍhāram | yadvā giraḥ mantrarūpāḥ vahantīti girvāhasaḥ ṛtvijaḥ | satyāḥ avisaṃvādiphalā girvāhaso yasya taṃ: when praising Agni, since the sense of the words of praise that show his qualities and greatness is fixed in Agni, the meaning is that Agni has the greatness described by those words: that is one explanation; Sāyaṇa also gives another. In this meaning, giraḥ means mantras; the priests who practise these mantras are girvāhasaḥ; Agni has priests whose mantras are true, with fruit that does not fail, since they apply them in his service.

atithiṃ mānuṣāṇām — manuṣyāṇām atithivat pūjyaṃ darśādi-tithim apekṣya āgantāraṃ vā: like a guest who has come to the house, he is worthy of worship by the sacrificer; or [he comes] following the tithi, new moon and other dates, the sacrifices of the new and full moon: one comes at the wish of the sacrificer. The author of the Nirukta, citing

जुष्टो दमूना अतिथिर्दुरोण इमं नो यज्ञमुप याहि विद्वान् । विश्वा अग्ने अभियुजो विहत्य शत्रूयतामा भरा भोजनानि ॥

juṣṭo damūnā atithirduroṇa imaṃ no yajñamupa yāhi vidvān | viśvā agne abhiyujo vihatya śatrūyatāmā bharā bhojanāni ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-1-[?] [?], as printed "೭-೪-೧"? — numerals small.) explains: atithir abhyatito gṛhān bhavati | abhyeti tithiṣu parakulānīti vā paragṛhānīti vā ayam apītaro 'tithir etasmād eva.

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 3-13

original p. 305

Durgācārya: gṛhān abhi abhimukhena āsa atitho bhavati — "since he comes seeking houses, he is a guest"; or, on the tithi-days beginning with the full moon, he goes to the houses of the sacrificers: abhyeti tithiṣu parakulāni paurṇamāsyādiṣu yajamānakulāny abhyāgacchati iti atithiḥ; "ayam apītaro 'tithir etasmād eva": because he behaves like a guest, he too is a guest: so they explain in two ways. Sāyaṇa also states two kinds of meaning.

āsayā — samīpe: "near". The word āsā, āmbaram is recorded among the eleven names of "near" (Ni. 3-[?], as printed "೩-೯"?). All the gods who accept the portions of the oblation — because the portions are to be offered to them by the sacrificer through Agni — come near this Agni: so it is described.

vayaḥ pitur na — havirlakṣaṇānnam uddiśya agnimukhād eva itarebhyo dīyamānatvāt | pitur antike putrādayo yathā annādyartham sevante tadvat: in the world, sons and the like attend on their fathers for their food and so on; so all the gods, since their respective shares of oblations offered by the sacrificer are all offered to Agni, come near Agni to receive them: thus the father-and-son comparison is explained. The word vayaḥ is recorded among the twenty-eight names of food, annaṃ vājaḥ and so on (Ni. 3-9). And —

युवोः श्रियं परि योषावृणीत सूरो दुहिता परितक्म्यायाम् । यद्देवयन्तमवथः शचीभिः परि घ्रंसमोमना वां वयो गात् ॥

yuvoḥ śriyaṃ pari yoṣāvṛṇīta sūro duhitā paritakmyāyām | yaddevayantamavathaḥ śacībhiḥ pari ghraṃsamomanā vāṃ vayo gāt ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-17 [?], as printed "೧-೧೧೬-೧೭"? — numerals small and doubtful.) Read letter by letter, and not claimed; I only record that the Kannada comment says Durgācārya explains vayaḥ here as annaṃ havirlakṣaṇam.

vayaḥ deveṣu havyā ā — netāraḥ ṛtvijo 'pi itareṣu ijyamāneṣu madhye havīṃṣi dadati agnaye: in this mantra the word vayaḥ is read twice. For the first vayaḥ the meaning "food in the form of oblation" is given. The second vayaḥ is used in the sense of "priests, who perform the works of the sacrifice rightly": the priests, when making oblations to other deities, offer to Agni too the portions of the oblation.

Since prefixes have many meanings, the prefix ā here is explained as dadati, "they give"; likewise ā in āgacchanti, "they come": so he explains the meaning,

— by the force of the prefix, supplying a verb suitable to it.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and the page). viśām — genitive plural; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168) gives the acute to the case-ending. havāmahe — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ first person plural; tiṅ-nighāta. daṃpatim — jāyā ca patiś ca daṃpatī; dama is a name for 'house'; the loss of the end of the first member; patyāv aiśvarye (Pā. 6-2-18) gives the natural accent of the first member; accusative singular. bhuje — root bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ; kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76) gives kvip; dative singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ gives the acute to the ending. satyagirvāhasam — giraḥ vahanti iti girvāhasaḥ; root vaha prāpaṇe; vahihāhādhāñbhyaś chandasi [print: "ವಹಿಹಾಧಾಙ್ಭ್ಯ", Uṇ. 4-?] gives asun; since the preceding sūtra continues with ṇit, ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116) gives vṛddhi to the penultimate; the form girvāhas; satyāḥ girvāhasaḥ yasya saḥ satyagirvāhāḥ, tam; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam gives the natural accent of the first member. mānuṣāṇām — manor jātāv ñyat tuk ca (Pā. 4-1-161) gives the suffix añ to manu [print: "ಅಞ್"]; with it the augment suk [print]; taddhiteṣv acāmādeḥ (Pā. 7-2-117) gives vṛddhi to the initial; since the suffix has the marker ñ, ñnityādir nityam gives the first-syllable acute; genitive plural. amṛtāsaḥ — na mṛtāḥ amṛtāḥ; in the nañ-bahuvrīhi, as an exception to the accent of the nañ, nañ jarāmarapriyamṛtāḥ (Pā. 6-2-116) gives the first-syllable acute of the latter member; with jas following, ājjaser asuk gives the augment asuk. vayā [as read; the form is vayaḥ] — root vī gatyādiṣu; Adādi; the Uṇādi suffix ḍi [print "ಡಿ"]; by the force of ḍit the ṭi of the root is elided; the form viḥ; when jas follows, jasi ca gives guṇa; āyādeśa; by the suffix accent first-syllable acute.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

त्वमग्ने सहसा सहन्तमः शुष्मिन्तमो जायसे देवतातये । रयिर्न देवतातये । शुष्मिन्तमो हि ते मदो द्युम्निन्तम उत क्रतुः । अध स्मा ते परि चरन्त्यजर श्रुष्टीवानो नाजर ॥ ९ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अग्ने त्वं सहसा बलेन सहन्तमो ऽतिशयेन शत्रूणामभिभविता तथा शुष्मिन्तमो ऽतिशयेन तेजस्वी जायसे । सहेर्लौकिकादिकः [?] कनिन् । नाद्यस्येति नुट् । किमर्थम् । देवतातये देवानां विस्तारयुक्ताय यागाय तदर्थं यज्ञानामृत्विग्भिरुत्पद्यसे [?] । यद्वा । उक्तगुणविशिष्टः सन् जायसे । अरण्योरुत्पद्यसे । यज्ञार्थत्वे दृष्टान्तः । रयिर्न देवतातये । धनं यथा यज्ञार्थमुच्यते । तथा चोक्तं यज्ञार्थं द्रव्यमुत्पन्नमिति । किंच ते तव मद आज्यस्वीकारजनितो हर्षः शुष्मिन्तमो ऽतिशयेन बलवान् । हिशब्दः प्रसिद्धौ । आज्येनाग्नेर्मदो भवतीति प्रसिद्धम् । अपि च ते क्रतुः कर्मविशेषो द्युम्निन्तमो यशोयुक्तो ऽन्नयुक्तो वा खलु । द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वेति यास्कः । नि. ५-५ । अधातः कारणात् अजर हे जरारहिताग्ने ते त्वां परि चरन्ति यजमानाः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । श्रुष्टीवानो न दूता इव । ते यथा वार्ताविशेषप्रदानेन राजानं सेवन्ते तद्वत् । छन्दसीवनिपाविति वनिप् । छान्दसं प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अजर भक्तानामजरयितः । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्पचाद्यच् । यद्वा । अजरास्रोतः । जरा स्तुतिः । असौ कस्याप्यस्तोता भवति किंतु सर्वैः स्वयं स्तूयते । तादृशं त्वां परि चरन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

he agne tvaṃ sahasā balena sahantamo 'tiśayena śatrūṇāmabhibhavitā tathā śuṣmintamo 'tiśayena tejasvī jāyase | saherlaukikādikaḥ [?] kanin | nādyasyeti nuṭ | kimartham | devatātaye devānāṃ vistārayuktāya yāgāya tadarthaṃ yajñānāmṛtvigbhirutpadyase [?] | yadvā | uktaguṇaviśiṣṭaḥ san jāyase | araṇyorutpadyase | yajñārthatve dṛṣṭāntaḥ | rayirna devatātaye | dhanaṃ yathā yajñārthamucyate | tathā coktaṃ yajñārthaṃ dravyamutpannamiti | kiṃca te tava mada ājyasvīkārajanito harṣaḥ śuṣmintamo 'tiśayena balavān | hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau | ājyenāgnermado bhavatīti prasiddham | api ca te kratuḥ karmaviśeṣo dyumnintamo yaśoyukto 'nnayukto vā khalu | dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vānnaṃ veti yāskaḥ | ni. 5-5 | adhātaḥ kāraṇāt ajara he jarārahitāgne te tvāṃ pari caranti yajamānāḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | śruṣṭīvāno na dūtā iva | te yathā vārtāviśeṣapradānena rājānaṃ sevante tadvat | chandasīvanipāviti vanip | chāndasaṃ pratyayādyudāttatvam | ajara bhaktānāmajarayitaḥ | antarbhāvitaṇyarthātpacādyac | yadvā | ajarāsrotaḥ | jarā stutiḥ | asau kasyāpyastotā bhavati kiṃtu sarvaiḥ svayaṃ stūyate | tādṛśaṃ tvāṃ pari carantītyarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the OCR is garbled in places. The readings marked [?] — "sahe laukikādikaḥ", "ṛtvigbhir utpadyase" — are small and doubtful. The Nirukta number is as printed "೫-೫" and as the OCR reads it. "O Agni, you by sahasā — strength — are sahantamaḥ — the greatest subduer of enemies, and śuṣmintamaḥ — extremely splendid — you are born (jāyase). [Kanin after sah; nuṭ by nādyasya.] For what? Devatātaye — for the sacrifice of the gods, which is extended; for that, by the priests of the sacrifices you are produced [?]; or else, being endowed with the qualities stated, you are born — from the two araṇis you are produced. An illustration for his being for the sake of the sacrifice: rayir na devatātaye — as wealth is said to be for the sake of sacrifice: so it is said, 'wealth is produced for the sake of sacrifice'. Moreover, your mada — the delight produced by accepting ghee — is śuṣmintamaḥ — the most powerful; the word hi is of fame: it is well known that Agni is exhilarated by ghee. And your kratu, the special rite, is dyumnintamaḥ — most endowed with glory or with food: 'dyumnaṃ dyoter yaśo vānnaṃ veti' says Yāska (Ni. 5-5). Adha — therefore, O ageless (ajara) Agni, te pari caranti — the sacrificers serve you; an illustration: śruṣṭīvāno na dūtāḥ — as messengers serve a king by delivering particular messages. [Chandasīvanipau gives vanip; the first-syllable acute of the suffix is Vedic.] Ajara — O one who makes his devotees free from old age; pacādi ac after the root with included causative sense; or else ajarāsrotaḥ: jarā is praise: he is one who is not a praiser of anyone, but is himself praised by all: serving such a one, they serve: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. He agne — O Agni; tvam — you; sahasā — by (your) strength; sahantamaḥ — the best subduer (of enemies); śuṣmintamaḥ — most splendid (being so); rayiḥ — wealth; devatātaye na — as it is used for sacrifice; devatātaye — for the sacrifice that is spread out for the gods; jāyase — you are born (from the araṇis); te — your; madaḥ — joy (produced by accepting ghee and the like); śuṣmintamaḥ hi — is most powerful indeed; utaḥ — and; kratuḥ — your rite; dyumnintamaḥ (hi) — most endowed with glory (food); adha — therefore; ajara — O ageless; ajara — O one who makes the devotees ageless, or himself not praising anyone; te — you; śruṣṭīvānaḥ na — like messengers (who serve a king by carrying news); pari caranti sma — (the sacrificers) serve.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Agni, you overpower enemies by your strength; you are extremely splendid; as wealth is useful for sacrifice, so you are born from the araṇis for the sacrifice; your joy, produced by accepting ghee and the like, is most powerful; your rites are full of glory (food); therefore the sacrificers serve you, who are ageless and who make the devotees ageless, as messengers serve a king.

Printed English (as printed, begins): You, Agni, the destroyer (of enemies) by your strength, the possessor of great splendour, are born for the sake of sacrificing to the gods, as
