॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 9).

sahasā sahantamaḥ — balena atiśayena śatrūṇām abhibhavitā: "Agni, by his own strength, overpowers, defeats and conquers enemies greatly": so the meaning. The word sahaḥ is recorded among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9 [numeral as read by the OCR, "३९"]). And —

पिता विश्वा सवना तूतुमा कृणे स्वयं सूनो सहसो यानि दधिषे । वराय ते पात्रं धर्मणे तना यज्ञो मन्त्रो ब्रह्मोद्यतं वचः ॥

pitā viśvā savanā tūtumā kṛṇe svayaṃ sūno sahaso yāni dadhiṣe | varāya te pātraṃ dharmaṇe tanā yajño mantro brahmodyataṃ vacaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-6; the reference numerals are small and doubtful — as read by the OCR "१०-३०-६" [?]; the verse is a small-type quotation, letters partly doubtful: [?].) Here sahasaḥ is explained as balasya, "of strength".

jāyase devatātaye rayir na devatātaye — devānāṃ vistārayuktāya yāgāya tadarthaṃ | yadvā | uktaguṇaviśiṣṭaḥ jāyase araṇyoḥ utpadyase | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | dhanaṃ yathā yajñārthamutpadyate tathā coktaṃ "yajñārthaṃ dravyam utpannam" iti — "For the sacrifice that is extended with the gods, i.e. for that purpose; or: possessing the said qualities you are born from the two araṇis; the example: as wealth is produced for the sake of the sacrifice — and so it is said: 'wealth is produced for the sake of the sacrifice'."

The word devatātā is recorded in the Nirukta (3-19 [?]) among the fifteen names of sacrifice ("yajñaḥ, venaḥ, adhvaraḥ" and so on); devatātā means "sacrifice". And —

शं नो भवन्तु वाजिनो हवेषु देवताता मितद्रवः स्वर्काः । जम्भयन्तोऽहिं वृकं रक्षांसि सनेम्यस्मद्युयवन्नमीवाः ॥

śaṃ no bhavantu vājino haveṣu devatātā mitadravaḥ svarkāḥ | jambhayanto 'hiṃ vṛkaṃ rakṣāṃsi sanemyasmad yuyavann amīvāḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-2; as read by the OCR "२-२०-२" [?].) Here too devatātā is explained as "sacrifice" (Ni. 12-44 [?]). One meaning: Agni appears so that a sacrifice accompanied by many rites may be fulfilled. Or: Agni, accompanied by great glory, produced from the araṇis, makes the sacrifices go on. The example of wealth being produced for the very performance of the sacrifice is given for the birth of Agni, and the statement "material is evident for the sake of sacrifice" is cited as authority. The word rayiḥ is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 [?]; numerals as read by the OCR "२-२४", "३-९"). In "na ca purā ca sadanaṃ rayīṇām" [as printed; letters doubtful] the Nirukta says rayir iti dhananāma rāter dānakarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 4-17 [?]): that rayiḥ denotes "wealth" is explained.

te madaḥ śuṣmintamaḥ — tava ājyasvīkārajanito harṣaḥ atiśayena balavān | ājyena agner mado bhavatīti prasiddhaṃ: "your joy produced by accepting ghee is greatly powerful; it is well known that Agni's exhilaration comes from ghee": the joy produced in Agni by the offering of ghee is greater than the joy produced by offering other oblations; so it is explained.

te kratuḥ dyumnintamaḥ — yaśoyukto 'nnayukto vā: "the sacrifice performed to satisfy Agni brings fame; and for those who sacrifice it is accompanied by plentiful food, so as to bring them fame and food": so the meaning. The word dyumna is recorded among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9 [?]). And —

शतं ते शिप्रिन्नूतयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु । जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥

śataṃ te śiprinn ūtayaḥ sudāse sahasraṃ śaṃsā uta rātir astu | jahi vadhar vanuṣo martyasyāsme dyumnam adhi ratnaṃ ca dhehi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-3, numerals doubtful: the OCR gives "७-३३-३" [?].) In this Ṛk the Niruktakāra explains dyumnam as dyotater yaśo vā annaṃ vā (Ni. 5-[?]; OCR "५-६") — so it is explained that the word conveys the senses "fame" and "food". The Niruktakāra also, —

उतस्य वाजी क्षिपणिं तुरण्यति ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपिकक्ष आसनि । क्रतुं दधिक्रा अनु संतवीत्वत्पथामङ्कांस्यन्वापनीफणत् ॥

utasya vājī kṣipaṇiṃ turaṇyati grīvāyāṃ baddho apikakṣa āsani | kratuṃ dadhikrā anu saṃtavītvat pathām aṅkāṃsy anvāpanīphaṇat ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-4, as read by the OCR "४-४०-४"; the small-type letters are partly doubtful [?].) — explains here kratuṃ karma vā prajñāṃ vā: the meaning of the word kratu, "work or intelligence". The word kratu is also recorded among the names of intelligence (Ni. 3-[?]; OCR "३-१३"). And —

यो जात एव प्रथमो मनस्वान् देवो देवान् क्रतुना पर्यभूषत् ।

yo jāta eva prathamo manasvān devo devān kratunā paryabhūṣat |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-1 as read by the OCR "२-१२-१"; only the first line is printed.) Here kratunā is explained as karmaṇā, "by work". Sāyaṇa also explains kratuḥ as "a particular kind of rite" (karmaviśeṣaḥ).

śruṣṭīvāno na — dūtā iva te yathā vārtāviśeṣapradānena rājānaṃ sevante tadvat — "as messengers serve a king by bringing particular news, so [the sacrificers serve you]": the sacrificers serve the ageless Agni as envoys, who carry the news of what is happening around, serve a king: so it is compared.

In this Ṛk the word ajara is said twice. For the first ajara the meaning "ageless" (free from old age, jarārahita) is given, of Agni. For the second ajara two kinds of meaning are given

(continuing the explanation of the second ajara): in the first meaning, bhaktānām ajarayitaḥ — "he who makes those who serve him ageless". Then, ajara — astotaḥ | jarā stutiḥ | āsau na kasyāpi stotā bhavati kiṃtu sarvaiḥ svayaṃ stūyate [reading as printed in small type, letters partly doubtful: [?]]: "ageless: one who is not a praiser; jarā is praise: he does not praise anyone, but is himself praised by all." Since the word jarā is explained as jarā stutir jaraterh stutikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 10-8 [?]; OCR "१०-८"), it conveys the sense "praise": Agni is one who does not praise anyone and is praised by others; all praise Agni; Agni alone is not to be praised by anyone — so the meaning is given, and it is explained that the sacrificers serve such a glorious Agni.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar page, noted briefly). sahasā — root ṣaha marṣaṇe, suffix asun; since it has n as marker the acute falls on the first syllable; instrumental singular [the Kannada says "plural" in the OCR; as read, doubtful]. sahantamaḥ — root ṣaha; kanin by bahulagrahaṇa; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ gives s; tamap in the sense of excess; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya drops the n; tarastamapau ghaḥ (Pā. 1-1-22) gives tamap the name gha; nādighasya (Pā. 6-3-[?]) the augment nuṭ; tamap has p as marker so it is unaccented. The same procedure is to be understood in śuṣmintamaḥ. jāyase — root janī prādurbhāve, divādi, laṭ second person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. devatātaye — sarvadevāt tātil (Pā. 4-4-142 [?]); liti (Pā. 6-1-193) gives the acute to the syllable before the suffix; dative singular. madaḥ — madī harṣe; mado 'nupasarge (Pā. 3-3-67) gives ap; because of the marker p it is unaccented. dyumnintamaḥ — dyumnaṃ yaśo 'syāsti gives dyumnī; in the possessive sense ata ini-ṭhanau (Pā. 5-2-115) gives ini; then tamap in the sense of excess, as in sahantamaḥ, with the same changes. adha — atha with a Vedic letter-change.

Grammar, continued. caranti — root cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ, laṭ third person plural; since it follows the word adha sma (a non-finite word before it) [?] the nighāta accent. ajara — root jṛṣ vayohānau; with the ṇic operation hidden inside; nandigrahipacādibhyo (Pā. 3-1-134) gives ac; guṇa with raparatva; in the vocative āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19) gives nighāta; or: jarā is praise; na vidyate jarā yasya — "he who has no praise"; "all-praised": vocative. śruṣṭīvānaḥ — chandasi vanip gives vanip in the possessive sense; because of marker p, the accent of the suffix's first syllable; nominative plural. ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे उद्गात्रादयः स्तोतारः वो युष्माकं सम्बन्धि स्तोमः स्तोत्रमग्नये प्र बभूतु । प्रीणयितुं समर्थो भवतु ॥ छान्दसः शपः श्लुः । अत्वं चाभ्यासस्य । भूसुवोस्तिङीति गुणाभावः ॥ कीदृशायाग्नये । महे महते पूज्याय सहसा पराभिभवसामर्थ्येन तद्वते सहस्वते उषर्बुधे उषःकाले प्रबुध्यमानाय ॥ आहरादीनां सत्यादिपूपसंख्यानमिति रत्वं ॥ पशुषे पशुफलप्रदाय । नशब्दोऽत्रापिशब्दार्थः । यद्वा । पशुषे पशुप्रदात्रे प्रभवे यथास्तुतिः क्रियते तद्वत् । किमर्थमिति तदुच्यते । ईमेनमग्निं प्रति लक्ष्मीकृत्य हविष्मान् घृतादिहविर्युक्तो यजमानो विश्वासु क्षासु सर्वासु निवासभूतासु वेदिभूमिषु जोगुवे । अत्यर्थं गच्छति ॥ गुवतेर्यङ्लुगन्ताच्छान्दसो लिट् । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । अमन्त्र इति पर्युदासादामभावः ॥ क्षेति भूनाम क्षा क्षामेति तन्नामसु पाठात् । ऋषूणामागन्तॄणां देवानां मध्ये श्रेष्ठमग्निं जूर्णिः स्तुतिकुशलो होताग्रे इतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वं जरते । स्तौति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । ऋषूणां महतां धनवतामग्रे रेभो न वन्दीव । ऋषतेर्गतौ । औणादिकः कुप्रत्ययः । नामन्यतरस्यामिति नाम उदात्तत्वं ॥ यद्वा ऋषूणामित्येतद्धोतृविशेषणं । ऋषूणां ज्ञानवतां मध्ये श्रेष्ठोऽयं होतेत्यर्थः ॥

he udgātrādayaḥ stotāraḥ vo yuṣmākaṃ sambandhi stomaḥ stotramagnaye pra babhūtu | prīṇayituṃ samartho bhavatu ‖ chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | atvaṃ cābhyāsasya | bhūsuvostiṅīti guṇābhāvaḥ ‖ kīdṛśāyāgnaye | mahe mahate pūjyāya sahasā parābhibhavasāmarthyena tadvate sahasvate uṣarbudhe uṣaḥkāle prabudhyamānāya ‖ āharādīnāṃ satyādipūpasaṃkhyānamiti ratvaṃ ‖ paśuṣe paśuphalapradāya | naśabdo 'trāpiśabdārthaḥ | yadvā | paśuṣe paśupradātre prabhave yathāstutiḥ kriyate tadvat | kimarthamiti taducyate | īmenamagniṃ prati lakṣmīkṛtya haviṣmān ghṛtādihaviryukto yajamāno viśvāsu kṣāsu sarvāsu nivāsabhūtāsu vedibhūmiṣu joguve | atyarthaṃ gacchati ‖ guvateryaṅlugantācchāndaso liṭ | vyatyayenātmanepadaṃ | amantra iti paryudāsādāmabhāvaḥ ‖ kṣeti bhūnāma kṣā kṣāmeti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | ṛṣūṇāmāgantṝṇāṃ devānāṃ madhye śreṣṭhamagniṃ jūrṇiḥ stutikuśalo hotāgre itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ jarate | stauti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | ṛṣūṇāṃ mahatāṃ dhanavatāmagre rebho na vandīva | ṛṣatergatau | auṇādikaḥ kupratyayaḥ | nāmanyatarasyāmiti nāma udāttatvaṃ ‖ yadvā ṛṣūṇāmityetaddhotṛviśeṣaṇaṃ | ṛṣūṇāṃ jñānavatāṃ madhye śreṣṭho 'yaṃ hotetyarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; a few letters of this small, dense page are doubtful: "uṣarbudha uṣaḥkāle", "āharādīnāṃ satyādipūpasaṃkhyānam iti ratvam" [as printed, doubtful: [?]], "kṣeti bhūnāma kṣā kṣāmeti tannāmasu pāṭhāt" [?]. Sense: O Udgātṛ-priests and other praisers, let your hymn become able to please Agni — pra babhūtu, "be able, be sufficient" (the Vedic śap is elided; the doubling syllable a; no guṇa by bhūsuvos tiṅi). To what Agni? mahe — the great, venerable; sahasvate — possessing victory through ability to overpower; uṣarbudhe — awake at the dawn; paśuṣe — the giver of the fruit of cattle: "na" here has the sense of "also"; or, "as one praises a lord who gives cattle, so (do you praise Agni)". Why so? īm — turning to this Agni, the sacrificer haviṣmān — equipped with ghee and other oblations — jonuve [as in the sense: joguve] "goes eagerly" to all altar-grounds, the dwelling places: so viśvāsu kṣāsu, "in all the places of dwelling." kṣā is a name for the earth. ṛṣūṇām — among the gods who are coming: the most excellent Agni — the hotṛ jūrṇiḥ — "skilled in praise" — praises first, before other gods; the example: "as a bard before the wealthy great ones" (rebho na vandīva). Or ṛṣūṇām is an adjective of hotṛ: "this Hotṛ is the best among the wise".

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. yat — because; haviṣmān — [the sacrificer] provided with oblations; īṃ prati — directed to this Agni; viśvāsu kṣāsu — in all the altars; joguve — goes eagerly, repeatedly; ṛṣūṇām — of the wise ones, jūrṇiḥ — skilled in praise; hotā — the invoker priest; ṛṣūṇām — of the wealthy [?]; agre — in front; rebhaḥ na — as a bard praises; ṛṣūṇām — among the gods who come (to the sacrifice), agre — before (the others), the most excellent Agni — jarate — praises. tat — therefore; he udgātrādayaḥ — O Udgātṛ and other praisers; mahe — the venerable; sahasā — with strength (conquering foes); sahasvate — the strong; uṣarbudhe — awake at dawn; agnaye — to Agni; vaḥ — your; stomaḥ — praise; pra babhūtu — may it be able to please; paśuṣe na — as one praises a giver of cattle; agnaye — to Agni (may your praise be pleasing).

original p. 314

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Udgātṛ and other priests: may your praise be pleasing to Agni, who is venerable, strong (conqueror of enemies), awake at dawn and the giver of the fruit of cattle, even as one praises a lord who gives cattle. It is because of this Agni that the sacrificers, supplied with ghee and other oblations, go to every altar; and the Hotṛ, the best of the wise and skilled in praise, praises this very Agni first, before all the gods who come to the sacrifice — as a bard praises the wealthy.

Printed English (as printed): "May your praise (oh priests) become grateful to Agni, who is deserving of laudation [as printed, followed by a full stop after "laudation"], who is of strength to overcome the strong, who is awakened at the dawn; to Agni, as if to a giver of cattle. Inasmuch as the presenter of the oblation repairs assiduously to every altar, the invoking priest, well skilled in (pious) praise, glorifies him (Agni) as the first of the attaining (divinities), as a herald (recites the praises) of illustrious (men)." Printed heading "English Translation".

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 10).

mahe — mahate pūjyāya: Agni is full of greatness, he is venerable. The word mahaḥ is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 2-[?]; OCR "२-२४"). And —

पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम् । यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥

pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīm | yasya trito vy ojasā vṛtraṃ viparvam ardayat ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]; as read by the OCR "१-१८७-१"; small type, letters partly doubtful [?].) Here mahaḥ is explained as mahataḥ, "of great strength" (balasya).

sahasā — parābhibhavasāmarthyena: the word sahaḥ is recorded among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9 [?]); the meaning given is that Agni is endowed with the capacity of overpowering others.

paśuṣe na — na śabdo 'tra apiśabdārthaḥ | paśuphalapradāya yadvā paśupradātre prabhave yathā stutiḥ kriyate tadvat — here the word na is said to have the sense of api "also" (a collective sense) and one meaning is "to Agni who also grants the fruits in the form of cattle (cows and the like)"; in the second meaning, since na is a word of comparison, "as one praises a lord who gives wealth in the form of cows, so we praise Agni".

original p. 315

īm — enam agne: the Niruktakāra says that the particles in the mantras bound by metre are without meaning, anarthakāḥ — "miti akṣareṇa anarthakāḥ karmopasaṃdhāna …" [as printed (Ni. 1-9 [?]; doubtful letters): [?]]. Sāyaṇa explains the particle īm here as "enam agniṃ": with this Agni as the object, the sacrificer, taking the oblation, serves him greatly.

viśvāsu kṣāsu — sarvāsu nivāsabhūtāsu vedibhūmiṣu. The word kṣā is recorded among the twenty-one names of the earth beginning with gauḥ (Ni. 1-[?]; OCR "२-५"). The word kṣā is explained as kṣiyater nivāsakarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 2-[?]; OCR "२६"): though it denotes the earth, the dwelling-place of all, here the meaning "the altar of the sacrifice" is given.

ṛṣūṇāṃ jūrṇir hotā agre jarate — āgantṝṇāṃ devānāṃ madhye śreṣṭham agniṃ stutikuśalo hotā itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvam [(as printed), the Kannada paraphrase]: the Hotṛ, who is expert in praise, praises, before invoking the other deities, Agni, the best among the gods, first, for the sake of the sacrifice. The Niruktakāra has read the word jūrṇiḥ among the eleven names of anger (Ni. 3-9 [?]) and among the twenty-six names of the quick (Ni. 3-9 [?]; numerals as read by the OCR, doubtful). And —

स्वयं सा रिषयध्यै या न उपेषे अत्रैः । [?] (small type, letters doubtful: [?])

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-129-8 as read by the OCR; I do not claim the reading.) Citing this Ṛk he says jūrṇir javater vā dravater vā dunoter vā ("jūrṇi from jū to go quickly, or dru to run, or du to burn", Ni. [?]). Durgācārya explains: javater vā hiṃsārthasya jūrṇiḥ, dravater vā gatyarthasya jūrṇiḥ, dunoter vā hiṃsārthasya jūrṇiḥ [as read, letters partly doubtful]. Thus the word jūrṇi has several meanings: anger, quick, motion, injury. Sāyaṇa has given jūrṇi the meaning "skilled in praise".

ṛṣūṇām agre rebho na — mahatāṃ dhanavatām agre vandīva; or ṛṣūṇām is an adjective of the Hotṛ — "among the wise this Hotṛ is the best". The Hotṛ-priest is compared to one who praises, a bard. In this word ṛṣūṇām is stated twice. In the first meaning it is explained as "those who come" (āgantṝṇām); the second use of ṛṣūṇām, for "many wealthy men", is explained as one meaning, and "the wise" (as an adjective of the Hotṛ) as the other meaning.

rebhaḥ — "bard": since the word rebha is recorded among the thirteen names of praisers (jaritā, kāruḥ…; Ni. 3-19 [?]) it is explained as "one who praises".

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as read by the OCR). mahe — mahate, with Vedic elision of t; or root maha pūjāyām, kvip, dative singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168) gives the acute to the ending. sahasvate — saho 'syāsti; matup; since matup is after a non-a word [as read, doubtful], mādupadhāyāś ca gives va. uṣarbudhe — root budha avagamane, kvip; the s of uṣas becomes r by āhar … upasaṃkhyānam [as read: [?]]; kṛdutarapadaprakṛtisvara. babhūtu — root bhū sattāyām, loṭ second person singular, tip, eru gives u; bahulaṃ chandasi gives tu [?]; doubling of the root; bhavater aḥ (Pā. 7-4-73) gives a to the reduplicative; bhūsuvos tiṅi (Pā. 7-3-88) gives no guṇa; tiṅ-nighāta. joguve — gu śabde, yaṅ, luk; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ; liṭ in the present sense; ātmanepada by vyatyayo bahulam; the augment āṃ is forbidden by amantre (Pā. 3-1-35 [?]); uvaṅ in the third person; no guṇa since the suffix has a k marker; the nighāta accent is absent because of yad; abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the acute to the first syllable. jarate — root jṝṣ vayohānau; here used in the sense of praise; laṭ third person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. ṛṣūṇām — root ṛṣī gatau (verbs of motion also have the sense of knowing); the Uṇādi suffix ku, not guṇa since it has the marker; the form ṛṣu; genitive plural; nāmanyatarasyām (Pā. 6-1-177) gives the acute to nām. jūrṇiḥ — root jvara saṃtāpe; vījyājvaribhyo niḥ (Uṇ. 4-[?]) gives ni; jvaratvarasrivyavimavām (Pā. 6-4-20) gives ūṭh [as read: the va and the upadhā becomes ū]; by vyatyaya the acute on the first syllable. ‖ 10 ‖

भोगायेत्यर्थः । न केवलं यजमानेभ्योऽस्मभ्यमेव अपि तु स्तोतृभ्यः स्तोत्रकर्तृभ्योऽपि हे मघवन्नन्नवन्नग्ने सुवीर्यं शोभनपुत्रभृत्याद्युपेतं धनं शोभनसामर्थ्यं वा कृधि । कुरु । किंच शवसा बलेन युक्तः सन् मथीः । अस्मद्विरोधिनो नाशय ॥ लुङ्यनुदात्तेनेति वृद्धिप्रतिषेधः । कारकपक्षे औणादिक ईकारः । आद्युदात्तश्छान्दसः ॥ यद्वा । मथीर्मथनवानस्मदर्थं शवसा बलेन युक्तो भवेति शेषः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । उग्रो न शवसा । यथा कश्चित् क्रूरः शवसा बलेन मथीर्भवति तद्वत् ॥

Read from the image; the first line begins "भोगायेत्यर्थः" — the continuation of the sentence at the foot of p. 317. "aṣṭāpada" etc. are not here. A few letters ("lupaṅyanudāttena" / luṅy anudāttena) are doubtful [?]. Sense: "…for enjoyment (bhoga) of this earth. And not only to us, the sacrificers, but also to the praisers: O maghavan (owner of food), Agni, make [for them] wealth with good heroism, endowed with good sons, servants and so on, or good ability. And further, being filled with strength, mathīḥ — destroy our enemies. [Grammar: in the aorist, because of the unaccented ending the vṛddhi is forbidden; in the agent-sense the Uṇādi ī; the accent on the first syllable is Vedic.] Or: mathīḥ is "the churner" — "be, for us, one that is possessed of strength": the example ugro na śavasā — "as a fierce man, by strength, is a crusher (mathī)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. agne — O Agni; saḥ — you; naḥ — to us; nediṣṭham — very near; dadṛśānaḥ — visible; devebhiḥ — with the other gods; sacanāḥ — one who has the same food (who accepts food equally with them); mahaḥ — great; rāyaḥ — wealth; sucetunā — with a pure mind; naḥ — for us; ā bhara — bring; śaviṣṭha — O strongest Agni; naḥ — for us; mahi — great glory (wealth); kṛdhi — make; saṃcakṣe — to see well (and); asyai bhuje — for the enjoyment (of this earth); kṛdhi — make; stotṛbhyaḥ — to your praisers (the Udgātṛs etc.); maghavan — O Agni, owner of food; mahi — great; suvīryam — wealth with good sons etc.; (kṛdhi — grant); śavasā — with strength; ugraḥ na — like a fierce man; mathīḥ — destroy our enemies.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Agni, shining visibly very near to us and, like the other gods, accepting oblations, give us — pure-minded — excellent wealth with a good mind; O mighty one, bring us great glory (food) for the enjoyments of this earth and so that we may be seen splendidly, (not for us only) — you, rich in food, give wealth with sons and the like to these praisers too; and with your strength, like a fierce man, destroy our enemies.

Printed English (as printed, begins on p. 318): "Agni, becoming visible close to us, and partaking with benignant intent of (the sacrificial) food along with the gods, bestow upon us abundant riches, with benignant intent. Most mighty Agni, render us

original p. 319

Printed English (continued): "…illustrious, that we may behold and enjoy (this earth); and grant greatness with excellent progeny to those who praise you, possessor of wealth, destroyer of foes, like a fierce (gaint) [sic] in strength."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 11).

dadṛśānaḥ — vedyāṃ dīptatvena dṛśyamānaḥ: "Agni appears on the sacrificial altar, bright with his own flames": so the meaning.

devebhiḥ sacanāḥ — itaradevaiḥ samānānnaḥ: because the shares of the oblation are offered to all the other gods through Agni, he has the same food as those gods: so the meaning.

The word sucetunā is used twice here. For the first sucetunā two kinds of meaning are given: "by excellent knowledge" or "by excellent mind"; for the second sucetunā, "one who has a good mind."

mahi — mahad annaṃ mahatīṃ kīrtiṃ vā: "may Agni grant abundant food and abundant fame": so Agni is prayed. śaviṣṭha — Agni is addressed as "strong"; that, too, is a prayer that Agni should give strength.

saṃcakṣe bhuje asyai — samyag darśanīyāya | asyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ sambandhine bhogāya | yadvā | saṃcakṣe bhuje iti sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ samyagdarśanīyāya bhogāya: "that we may be seen as splendid in the world, and that we may enjoy the enjoyment to be had on this earth: so Agni is prayed to grant it to us, who perform the sacrifice."

suvīryaṃ kṛdhi — śobhanaputrabhṛtyādyupetaṃ dhanaṃ śobhanasāmarthyaṃ vā kuru: Agni is prayed that wealth be granted to us who sacrifice and to those who praise him, with good sons, and with male and female servants.

mathīr ugro na śavasā — repeating the words śavasā and mathīḥ of this clause: śavasā mathīḥ balena yuktas san asmadvirodhino nāśaya: "being filled with strength, destroy our enemies": so the meaning. Or — Read from the image; the word syasmad- is as printed [sic?] and doubtful: [?].

मथीर्मथनवान्स्यस्मदर्थं शवसा बलेन युक्तो भव । यथा कश्चित् क्रूरः शवसा बलेन मथीर्भवति तद्वत् ।

mathīr mathanavān syasmadarthaṃ śavasā balena yukto bhava | yathā kaścit krūraḥ śavasā balena mathīr bhavati tadvat |

original p. 320

(Continuing:) "…born by churning in the araṇis, be strong for us who sacrifice": thus he explains; and the example is given — as a cruel man by his own strength subdues others, so Agni too must be endowed with strength that destroys enemies.

śavasā — balena: "by strength". The word śavas is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as printed "೧-೩೪"?) and among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]; OCR "२-२४" and "३९" — doubtful). And in the Ṛks 1-[?]-[?], 1-[?]-[?], 1-[?]-[?], 1-[?]-[?] and others (the numerals are small and I cannot read them reliably; the OCR gives "१-२७-२, १-३९-८, १-५१-४, १-२-१०" [?]) it is used in the sense of "strength".

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as read by the OCR). nediṣṭham — in the sense of excess the suffix iṣṭhan after antika; when it follows, by antikabāḍhayor nedasādhau (Pā. 5-3-63) the base is replaced by neda; by yasyeti ca the a is elided; the acute on the first syllable since the suffix has the marker n. dadṛśānaḥ — root dṛśir prekṣaṇe; the Vedic liṭ; by liṭaḥ kānajvā (Pā. 3-2-106 [?]) the substitute kānac; because of it the root is doubled; by vyatyaya the acute on the first syllable. bhara — root hṛñ haraṇe; loṭ second person singular; gṛhor bhaś chandasi gives bh for the h of the root; tiṅ-nighāta. devebhiḥ — bahulaṃ chandasi: no ais; by bahuvacane jhaly et (Pā. 7-3-103) the e. sucetunā — root citī saṃjñāne; Uṇādi tun; guṇa of the short penult because of it; śobhanaś cetur yasya saḥ, sucetunā; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the acute on the last syllable of the latter member. mahaḥ — root maha pūjāyām, kvip; accusative plural. rāyaḥ — udāttaṃ padādi [as read: ṛdidam padādi — doubtful, Pā. 6-1-171]; the acute on the ending. mahi — root maha pūjāyām; Uṇādi in; since n-marked the acute on the first syllable. śaviṣṭha — śavo 'syāsti iti śavasvī; atiśayena śavasvī śaviṣṭhaḥ; ā māyām [as read: āsmāyāmedhā… Pā. 5-2-121] gives vin; with iṣṭhan following, vinmatorluk (Pā. 5-3-65) drops it (luk); ṭeḥ (Pā. 6-4-155) drops the ṭi (as); in the vocative āmantritasya ca (Pā. 8-1-19) gives nighāta.

kṛdhi — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; loṭ second person singular, sip; its hi substitute; by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of the vikaraṇa; by śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi (Pā. 6-4-102) hi becomes dhi; being ṅit... (as printed "ಜಿತ್ತಾದುದರಿಂದ": since marked j [?]) no guṇa; tiṅ-nighāta. saṃcakṣe — root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; kvip; here the root is used in the sense of seeing; kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara; dative singular. mathīḥ — root mantha viloḍane; Vedic luṅ in the sense of loṭ; second person singular; if it be taken as a noun, the Uṇādi ī for it; the Vedic acute on the first syllable. ‖ 11 ‖

ನೂರ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೆಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra ippatteṃṭaneya sūktavu (the one hundred and twenty-eighth Sūkta).

॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; several letters doubtful [?]).

अयं जायेत्यष्टर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तम् । अयं जायताष्टावित्यनुक्रमणिका । परुच्छेप ऋषिः । सर्वमात्यष्टमित्युक्तत्वादत्यष्टिश्छन्दः [?] । आग्नेयं स्थिति तुशब्दस्योक्तत्वादिदमप्याग्नेयम् । पृष्ठ्यस्य षष्ठेऽहन्याज्यशस्त्रेण विनियुक्तम् । सूत्रितं च पृष्ठ्यस्येति खण्डे । अयं जायत मनुषो धरीमणीत्याज्यमिति ॥ आ. ८-१ [?]

ayaṃ jāyetyaṣṭarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktam | ayaṃ jāyatāṣṭāvityanukramaṇikā | parucchepa ṛṣiḥ | sarvamātyaṣṭamityuktatvādatyaṣṭiśchandaḥ [?] | āgneyaṃ sthiti tuśabdasyoktatvādidamapyāgneyam | pṛṣṭhyasya ṣaṣṭhe 'hanyājyaśastreṇa viniyuktam | sūtritaṃ ca pṛṣṭhyasyeti khaṇḍe | ayaṃ jāyata manuṣo dharīmaṇītyājyamiti ‖ ā. 8-1 [?]

Kannada anuvāda (translated). Anuvāda — This Sūkta ayaṃ jāyata is the second Sūkta in the nineteenth Anuvāka. In it there are eight ṛks; the Anukramaṇikā says "ayaṃ jāyatāṣṭau". The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Paruccheṣa. Since it is said that all the Sūktas seen by this ṛṣi are in the Atyaṣṭi metre, the metre of this Sūkta too is Atyaṣṭi. Because the word tu is used earlier ("āgneyaṃ tu"), the deity of this Sūkta too is Agni. On the sixth day of the pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha this Sūkta is to be recited among the mantras of the ājya-śastra, as explained in the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra in the section (khaṇḍa) beginning "pṛṣṭhyasya" — by the sūtra ayaṃ jāyata manuṣo dharīmaṇīty ājyam (Āś. 8-1 [?]).

स्वं व्रतमनु स्वकीयं हविःस्वीकारादिरूपं कर्मानुलक्षीकृत्य । पुनः स एव विशेष्यते । विश्वश्रुष्टिर्विश्वविषयकर्मवान् । कस्मै । सखीयते सखित्वमात्मन इच्छते । तथा श्रवस्यते प्रसिद्धमन्नमात्मन इच्छते यजमानाय रयिरिव धनस्थानीयो भवति । धनं यथा सख्यमन्नसमृद्धिं च साधयति तद्वदयमग्निरपि तस्मै द्वयं साधयतीत्यर्थः । किंचायमग्निरिळस्पदे इडाया भूम्याः पदे । अन्त्यलोपश्छान्दसः ॥ धरीमणि सारभूते स्थाने वेदिरूपे । वेदिमाहुः परमन्तं पृथिव्याः । तै. सं. ७-४-१८-२ [?] इति श्रुतेः । एतावती वै पृथिवी यावती वेदिरिति च । पुनस्तदेव विशेष्यते । इळस्पदे इडादेवताया मनोः पुत्र्या गोरूपाया इडोपह्वानमन्त्रप्रतिपादितायाः पदे पादन्यासप्रदेशे । इडा वै मानवी यज्ञानुकाशिन्यासीत् । तै. ब्रा. १-१-४-४ [?] । इडायाः पदे घृतवति स्वाहा । तै. सं. १-२-५-१ [?] । इति च श्रुतेः । नि षदत् निषीदति । कीदृशोऽयमग्निः । अदब्धः केनाप्यहिंसितः होता होमनिष्पादकः परिवीतः ऋत्विग्भिः परिधिभिर्वा परितो वेष्टितः । एवंभूतः सन् नि षदत् ॥

svaṃ vratamanu svakīyaṃ haviḥsvīkārādirūpaṃ karmānulakṣīkṛtya | punaḥ sa eva viśeṣyate | viśvaśruṣṭirviśvaviṣayakarmavān | kasmai | sakhīyate sakhitvamātmana icchate | tathā śravasyate prasiddhamannamātmana icchate yajamānāya rayiriva dhanasthānīyo bhavati | dhanaṃ yathā sakhyamannasamṛddhiṃ ca sādhayati tadvadayamagnirapi tasmai dvayaṃ sādhayatītyarthaḥ | kiṃcāyamagniriḷaspade iḍāyā bhūmyāḥ pade | antyalopaśchāndasaḥ ‖ dharīmaṇi sārabhūte sthāne vedirūpe | vedimāhuḥ paramantaṃ pṛthivyāḥ | tai. saṃ. 7-4-18-2 [?] iti śruteḥ | etāvatī vai pṛthivī yāvatī vediriti ca | punastadeva viśeṣyate | iḷaspade iḍādevatāyā manoḥ putryā gorūpāyā iḍopahvānamantrapratipāditāyāḥ pade pādanyāsapradeśe | iḍā vai mānavī yajñānukāśinyāsīt | tai. brā. 1-1-4-4 [?] | iḍāyāḥ pade ghṛtavati svāhā | tai. saṃ. 1-2-5-1 [?] | iti ca śruteḥ | ni ṣadat niṣīdati | kīdṛśo 'yamagniḥ | adabdhaḥ kenāpyahiṃsitaḥ hotā homaniṣpādakaḥ parivītaḥ ṛtvigbhiḥ paridhibhirvā parito veṣṭitaḥ | evaṃbhūtaḥ san ni ṣadat ‖

Read from the image; the references (Taittirīya Saṃhitā "७-४-१८-२", "१-२-५-१"; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa "१-१-४-४") are small and doubtful [?]; the OCR gives the same. A few small-type letters ("vedim āhuḥ paramantaṃ pṛthivyāḥ") are as read. Sense: this Agni is born from the adhvaryu, a man — churned from the araṇis; he is hotṛ (invoker of the gods), yajiṣṭha (the best sacrificer); born for the sake of the rites of the sacrificers who desire fruit — the Soma sacrifice and the like — and also for his own rite, accepting the oblation. viśvaśruṣṭiḥ — doing work concerning all things; to one who wishes friendship with him or who wishes famous food, he is like wealth — as wealth brings friendship and abundance of food, so does Agni; he sits on the ilaspada — "the footmark of Iḍā" — the earth's essential place, the altar; the Śruti says "they call the altar the farthest end of the earth" and "as large as the earth, so large the altar"; and Iḍā, the daughter of Manu in the form of a cow, followed the sacrifice ("iḍā vai mānavī yajñānukāśinyāsīt") and the formula "iḍāyāḥ pade ghṛtavati svāhā" [as read]; unharmed (adabdhaḥ), the hotṛ, "surrounded" (parivīta) by the priests or by the paridhi-sticks, he sits.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. hotā — invoker of the gods; yajiṣṭhaḥ — most worthy of worship among the sacrifices; ayam agniḥ — this Agni; uśijām — of the sacrificers who desire fruit; vrataṃ anu — with reference to the Soma sacrifices and the like; svaṃ vrataṃ anu — following his own rite (the acceptance of the oblation); manuṣaḥ — from a man (the Adhvaryu), churned in the araṇi; jāyata — was born; sakhīyate — for him who desires his friendship; viśvaśruṣṭiḥ — the doer of all kinds of rites; śravasyate — for him who desires food; rayiḥ iva — like wealth (the means of food); further this Agni — iḷaspade — on the footmark of Iḷā, daughter of Manu in the form of a cow, on the earth; dharīmaṇi — on the essential altar-ground; adabdhaḥ — unobstructed; hotā — accomplisher of the oblations; parivītaḥ — surrounded by the hotṛ-priests and others or enclosed by the paridhis; ni sadat — sits down.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Agni, who calls the gods to the place of sacrifice, who is most worthy of worship in the sacrifices, who grants all that is needed to those who desire his friendship, and who grants wealth — the source of food — to those who seek food: he is born, churned in the araṇi by the man, the Adhvaryu, both for the sake of the sacrificers who desire fruit and for his own oblation-accepting purpose; and having been born he sits, unobstructed, the performer of the oblation, surrounded by the priests, on the altar-ground — the most sacred place on earth, the footmark of Iḷā, daughter of Manu in the form of a cow.

Printed English (as printed; heading "English Translation"): "This Agni, the invoker of the gods, the assiduous offerer of sacrifices, is generated of man, (for the fulfilment of the) duty of those who desire (the fruit of) pious rites, as well as for (the discharge of) his own duty: he is the bestower of all blessings on him who desires his friendship, and is wealth to (such a one) seeking for food: the unobstructed offerer of oblations, he sits down, surrounded (by ministering priests), on the most sacred spot of earth, upon the footmark of Ila."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).

manuṣaḥ — manuṣyasya adhvaryoḥ sakāśāt: Agni is born in the araṇis from the Adhvaryu; the Adhvaryu is one among the priests. The word manuṣaḥ shows that the Adhvaryu too is a man. The Niruktakāra, —

युवं वृकेणाश्विना वपन्तेषं दुहन्ता मनुषाय दस्रा । अभि दस्युं बकुरेणा धमन्तोरु ज्योतिश्चक्रथुरार्याय ॥

yuvaṃ vṛkeṇāśvinā vapanteṣaṃ duhantā manuṣāya dasrā | abhi dasyuṃ bakureṇā dhamantoru jyotiś cakrathur āryāya ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-21, as read; the numerals are small and doubtful [?].) — here explains manuṣāya as manuṣyāya ("for man"). And —

समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान्यजसि जातवेदः । आ च वह मित्रमहश्चिकित्वान्त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः ॥

samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe devo devān yajasi jātavedaḥ | ā ca vaha mitramaś cikitvān tvaṃ dūtaḥ kavir asi pracetāḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-1, as read.) — here too he says manuṣaḥ means manuṣyasya, "of a man". Printed second line "mitramaś" for mitramahaś: I read "ಮಿತ್ರಮಹಶ್ಚಿಕಿತ್ವಾನ್", i.e. mitramahaś cikitvān; the IAST above is given as printed in the second line, "mitramahaś".

In this Ṛk the word hotā is said twice. For the first hotā the meaning "one who invokes the gods for the sacrifice" (devānām āhvātā) is given; for the second hotā, "one who accomplishes the oblation" (homaniṣpādakaḥ), "one who makes the offering."

uśijām — phalasya kāmayitṝṇāṃ yajamānānām: "of the sacrificers who desire fruit": the meaning is given "of those who desire to obtain heaven and other fruits and sacrifice for them".

The word uśik is recorded among the eighteen names of "the radiant act" (kāntikarma; Ni. 3-9 [?]); uśijaḥ is also recorded among the twenty-four names of "the wise" (Ni. 3-19 [?]). And, — The Rik is cut off at the foot of p. 324 and the page ends here; p. 325 begins with auśijaḥ.

कक्षीवन्तं य … (the quotation is cut off at the foot of the page: "ಕಕ್ಷೀವಂತಂ ಯ")

kakṣīvantaṃ ya … (the quotation is cut off at the foot of the page: "ಕಕ್ಷೀವಂತಂ ಯ")**

original p. 325

In auśijaḥ: "uśijaḥ putraḥ auśijaḥ; uśik vaṣṭeḥ kāntikarmaṇaḥ" (Ni. 6-11 [?]) — so the Niruktakāra. Sāyaṇa, however, explains only "the sacrificers who desire fruit".

vrataṃ anu vrataṃ anu — of the two repeated words vrata, the first vrata is explained as "a rite in the form of the Soma sacrifice and the like"; the second vrata as "a rite in the form of acceptance of the oblations". It is described that Agni is born in the araṇis for the fulfilment of the Soma sacrifice performed by those with the purpose of obtaining fruit, and for the acceptance of his own shares of the oblations; that is, Agni fulfils both his own work and the work of others.

sakhīyate śravasyate viśvaśruṣṭir rayir iva — ā prasiddham annam ātmana icchate yajamānāya viśvaviṣayakarmavān dhanasthānīyo bhavati | dhanaṃ yathā sakhyam annasamṛddhiṃ ca sādhayati tadvad agnir api tasmai dvayaṃ sādhayati. (Read from the image.) "To the sacrificer who wishes for abundant famous food and to make friendship with others, Agni — who performs all the rites concerning the world — is like wealth: as wealth brings the friendship of others and good food, so Agni accomplishes both of these desired things for him": so the comparison.

iḷaspade dharīmaṇi — iḍāyāḥ bhūmyāḥ pade sārabhūte sthāne vediṛūpe: "On the earth known by the name Iḍā, in the altar of the sacrifice that is accounted most excellent, this Agni sits at ease." For this purpose the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence "vedim āhuḥ paramantaṃ pṛthivyāḥ" (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-4-3 [?]; as printed "೭-೪-೧೮-೨"? the numerals are doubtful) and "etāvatī vai pṛthivī yāvatī vediḥ" (Tai. Saṃ. 3-5-4-1 [?]) are cited as authority.

iḷaspade pari-vītaḥ ni ṣadat — iḍādevatāyāḥ manoḥ putryāḥ iḍopahvānamantrapratipāditāyāḥ pade pādanyāsapradeśe ṛtvigbhiḥ paridhibhir vā parito veṣṭitaḥ niṣīdati. In this Ṛk the word iḷaspade is said twice. For the first iḷaspada the meaning "the footmark of the earth" is given; for the second iḷaspada the analysis "iḍāyāḥ pade" is given and Iḍā is taken to be the daughter of Manu. This is said in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa: the sentence "iḍā vai mānavī yajñānukāśinyāsīt" (Tai. Br. 1-1-4-4 [?]) is cited; and the Iḍopahvāna mantra "iḍāyāḥ pade ghṛtavati svāhā" (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-5-1 [?]), used for the oblation at the spot where the goddess Iḍā, in the form of a cow, placed her foot. In this way, the greatness of the sacrificial altar is described — the place where Iḍā, in the form of a cow, set her foot: Agni sits on this altar, well purified, surrounded by the priests and by the paridhi sticks, well established.

parivītaḥ — paritaḥ veṣṭitaḥ: "enclosed all round".

adabdhaḥ — kenāpy ahiṃsitaḥ: the word dabdha is formed from the root dabh, which gives the sense of harming, and means "one who can be harmed"; adabdhaḥ means that Agni is one who cannot be harmed by anyone.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as read by the page and the OCR). jāyata — root janī prādurbhāve, luṅ third person singular; by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75) no augment aṭ; tiṅ-nighāta. manuṣaḥ — root mana jñāne; manyate jānātīti manuḥ prajāpatiḥ; janer usiḥ (Uṇ. 2-[?]) with bahulam anyatrāpi; the Uṇādi usi; since it has i-marker [as read: "nittādudariṃda"] the acute falls on the first syllable; genitive singular. dharīmaṇi — root dhṛṅ dhāraṇe; Uṇādi suffix imanic [Uṇ. 4-[?]]; Vedic lengthening of i; by vyatyaya the acute on the first syllable; locative singular. uśijām — root vaśa kāntau; vaśeḥ kit (Uṇ. 3-[?]) gives iji; since it is kit, grahijyāvayi… (Pā. 6-1-16) gives saṃprasāraṇa to the root; acute on the first syllable of the suffix. sakhīyate — sakhitvam ātmana icchati sakhīyati; supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8); after the kyac-ending a śatṛ in the present sense; dative singular; with the num-less śatṛ before the ending, śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173) gives the acute on the ending; so also in śravasyate, kyac and the accent. adabdhaḥ — dambhu dambhane; the suffix kta in the passive; anidītāṃ drops the penult nasal; jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (Pā. 8-2-40) gives dh to the suffix; the root's bh becomes b (jaś); in the tatpuruṣa compound, tatpuruṣe (Pā. 6-2-2 [?]) the accent of the first member (the indeclinable) remains. sadat — root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ gives luṅ in the present sense; with the third person singular the cli is replaced by aj by puṣādidyutādi (Pā. 3-1-55); by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge there is no augment aṭ; tiṅ-nighāta.

Grammar, concluded. iḷaspade — iḍāyāḥ padam, tasmin; the Vedic loss of the end; locative singular. parivītaḥ — root vī gatyādiṣu, kta in the passive by niṣṭhā; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49) gives the accent of the preceding member [as read, the preverb keeps its accent]. ‖ 1 ‖

यज्ञसाधं यज्ञस्य साधकम् ॥ साध्नोतेः क्विपि कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ तमग्निं वेद्यां स्थापितमपि वातयामसि । अपिः सम्भावनार्थः । आ परितोषं सेवामहे ॥ वात गतिसुखसेवनयोः । चौरादिकः । इदन्तो मसिः ॥ केनोपायेनेति तदुच्यते । ऋतस्य पथा यागस्य मार्गेण यागानुष्ठानेन । यज्ञेन देवेभ्य इति

yajñasādhaṃ yajñasya sādhakam ‖ sādhnoteḥ kvipi kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ‖ tamagniṃ vedyāṃ sthāpitamapi vātayāmasi | apiḥ sambhāvanārthaḥ | ā paritoṣaṃ sevāmahe ‖ vāta gatisukhasevanayoḥ | caurādikaḥ | idanto masiḥ ‖ kenopāyeneti taducyate | ṛtasya pathā yāgasya mārgeṇa yāgānuṣṭhānena | yajñena devebhya iti

यज्ञेन देवेभ्य इति श्रुतेर्यज्ञेन देवस्य महती प्रीतिर्भवति । यद्वा । ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य पथा । मार्गस्तीर्थाख्यः पूर्वेणोत्करमपरेण प्रणीताः । आ. १-१ [?] । इत्यादिसूत्रोक्तः । तेन मार्गेण गत्वा । पुनः केन । हविष्मताज्यादिप्रदेयद्रव्यवता नमसा नमस्कारलक्षणेन स्तोत्रोपस्थानेन वा । तदुभयेनेत्यर्थः । कुत्रेति तदुच्यते । हविष्मता हविष्मत्याज्यपुरोडाशादिबहुहविर्युक्ते देवताता देवानां विस्तारयुक्ते यज्ञे । किंच सोऽग्निर्नोऽस्मत्सम्बन्धिनामूर्जां हविर्लक्षणानामन्नानामुपाभृत्यया उपाहरणे तत्कारविषये [?] । उपाज्जुपसृष्टाद्धरतेः क्रिन् [?] । दृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वम् । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । ताद् चेत्यनन्तरस्य गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ अया कृपानया सामर्थ्यलक्षणया कल्पनया हविःस्वीकरणरूपया न जूर्यति । यज्ञसमाप्तिपर्यन्तं न नश्यति । अजरो वर्तत इत्यर्थः । स इत्युक्तम् । क इत्याह । यमग्निं देवं द्योतनशीलं मातरिश्वान्तरिक्षसंचारी वायुः पूर्वं मनवे मनोरर्थाय परावतोऽतिदूरं गतवतः आदित्याद्भाः अभासीत् । औचित्येन भूमौ स्थापितवान् । इत्यर्थः । तद्वत्परावतो दूराद्देवमग्निमस्मद्देवयजनं प्रति स्थापयत्वित्यर्थः ॥

yajñena devebhya iti śruteryajñena devasya mahatī prītirbhavati | yadvā | ṛtasya yajñasya pathā | mārgastīrthākhyaḥ pūrveṇotkaramapareṇa praṇītāḥ | ā. 1-1 [?] | ityādisūtroktaḥ | tena mārgeṇa gatvā | punaḥ kena | haviṣmatājyādipradeyadravyavatā namasā namaskāralakṣaṇena stotropasthānena vā | tadubhayenetyarthaḥ | kutreti taducyate | haviṣmatā haviṣmatyājyapuroḍāśādibahuhaviryukte devatātā devānāṃ vistārayukte yajñe | kiṃca so 'gnirno 'smatsambandhināmūrjāṃ havirlakṣaṇānāmannānāmupābhṛtyayā upāharaṇe tatkāraviṣaye [?] | upājjupasṛṣṭāddharateḥ krin [?] | dṛgrahorbha iti bhatvam | supāṃ sulugiti saptamyā luk | tād cetyanantarasya gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam ‖ ayā kṛpānayā sāmarthyalakṣaṇayā kalpanayā haviḥsvīkaraṇarūpayā na jūryati | yajñasamāptiparyantaṃ na naśyati | ajaro vartata ityarthaḥ | sa ityuktam | ka ityāha | yamagniṃ devaṃ dyotanaśīlaṃ mātariśvāntarikṣasaṃcārī vāyuḥ pūrvaṃ manave manorarthāya parāvato 'tidūraṃ gatavataḥ ādityādbhāḥ abhāsīt | aucityena bhūmau sthāpitavān | ityarthaḥ | tadvatparāvato dūrāddevamagnimasmaddevayajanaṃ prati sthāpayatvityarthaḥ ‖

Read from the image; the beginning continues the sentence at the foot of p. 327 — "yajñena devebhya" is the śruti citation, "by sacrifice [for the gods]". The small-type sūtra reference "आ. १-१" (Āśvalāyana 1-1) is as printed; the bhāṣya's grammar tail is characterized only: "upābhṛtyayā — [a kri-suffix on hṛ after upa-ā; dṛgrahor bhaḥ gives bh; supāṃ sulug elides the locative; the preceding preverb keeps its accent]". Several small letters are doubtful: [?]. Sense: "By the sacrifice, [says] the śruti, the god's great pleasure arises. Or: ṛtasya — of the sacrifice; pathā — by the path, i.e. the way (named tīrtha) described in the sūtra 'pūrveṇotkaram aparaṇa praṇītāḥ'; going by that path. And by what further? by namasā — homage (the praise-recitations) — and by the haviṣmatā, oblation-bearing; both together; where? in the sacrifice (devatātā) that is extended with the gods and full of ghee, puroḍāśa and other oblations. And further this Agni, in the bringing near of our foods in the form of oblations, by ayā kṛpā, this power of will (of accepting the oblations), does not wear out (na jūryati) — does not perish until the end of the sacrifice, is ageless. Who is that? The god whom Mātariśvan, the wind that moves in the sky, formerly, for Manu, from the far-away sun [or: from afar], made shine on earth: and for our sacrifice may he likewise place that Agni, from far away, at our place of worship."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. devatātā — in the sacrifice, with the host of gods, extended; haviṣmatā — with oblations (ghee, puroḍāśa etc.); ṛtasya pathā — by the path of the sacrifice (the course of the sacrifice); haviṣmatā — with the substances of oblation; namasā — with homage (the offering of praise); yajñasādham — the accomplisher of the sacrifice; tam — him (Agni, established on the altar); api vātayāmasi — let us serve until he is pleased; yam — whom; devam — the shining one (the god Agni); mātariśvā — the wind; manave — for Manu; parāvataḥ — from the very distant (from the near of the sun); bhāḥ — he made shine (on the earth); saḥ — that Agni; naḥ — our; ūrjām — of the foods (in the form of oblations); upābhṛtyayā — in the matter of acceptance; ayā kṛpā — by the will (of accepting oblations); na jūryati — does not decay (is not destroyed) until the end of the sacrifice; parāvataḥ — from a distant place (may Agni come from afar for our sacrifice).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. In the sacrificial hall provided with the host of gods and with substances like ghee and puroḍāśa, by the course of the sacrifice and by offerings and homage, let us serve this Agni until he is satisfied. The wind made this shining Agni appear on the earth from the sun far away, for Manu; may this Agni, by his will to accept our oblations, not decay until the end of the sacrifice, and may he come from afar for our sacrifice.

Printed English (as printed; heading "English Translation"): "We propitiate that instrument of sacrifice by the path of sacrifice, by reverential salutation, and by oblations of clarified butter; by oblations (offered) to the gods: and he accepts our offerings, and through his benignity quits not (the rite until its close), the divinity whom the wind brought from afar for the service of Manu: (may he come) from afar (to our sacrifice)." The first sentence of the Bhāvārtha-closing line, "(sāmarthyarūpavāda) kṛpeyiṃda yajña mugiyuvavaregū nāśavāgadirali; (mattu) dūradiṃda (namma yāgārthavāgi) āgamisali", at the head of p. 329 completes the Bhāvārtha: "through (his power of will) may he not perish until the end of the sacrifice; and may he come from afar for our sacrifice."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).

yajñasādham api vātayāmasi — yajñasya sādhakaṃ tam agniṃ vedyāṃ sthāpitam āparitoṣaṃ sevāmahe: Agni, who is able to accomplish the sacrifice, is established on the sacrificial altar; "we, the sacrificers, serve him until he is satisfied": so the meaning.

ṛtasya pathā — yāgasya mārgeṇa yāgānuṣṭhānena yajñena devasya mahatī prītir bhavati: "by the course of the sacrifice, that is, by performing the sacrifice; for by sacrifice the god's great pleasure arises": and among the ways of pleasing Agni the performance of the sacrifice is the chief. The śruti "yajñena devebhyaḥ" (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-10-5 [as read; numerals doubtful]) is the authority here. In one sense it is explained that through sacrifice itself Agni's pleasure arises with respect to the sacrificers, and the offering of the oblation to Agni at the time of the sacrifice gives him satisfaction. In the second meaning, following the order stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, "pūrveṇotkaram aparaṇa praṇītāḥ" (Āśv. Sū. 1-1 [as read]), Agni is to be pleased by the sacrifice by the pure (properly ordered) path.

The means of pleasing Agni are haviṣmatā — pouring oblations and ghee; namasā — salutations and the praise of Agni, and meditating on Agni while reciting the stotra. So it is explained by the words haviṣmatā, namasā. The word haviṣmatā — said for the second time — is explained as an adjective of the word devatātā; from this Sāyaṇa —

(continued from p. 329:) haviṣmatā — haviṣmati ājyapuroḍāśādibahuhaviryukte devatātā — devānāṃ vistārayukte yajñe: has explained "in the sacrifices which have many oblations such as ghee and puroḍāśa and are carried out by rites in which many gods are invoked, Agni is gratified by rites that bring him joy."

For the word ṛtasya the Niruktakāra explains "water" (Ni. 1-[?]; as printed "೨-೧೪"?) and "sacrifice, truth" (Ni. 4-19 [?]). The word devatātā too is recorded among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-19 [?]). And —

शं नो भवन्तु वाजिनो हवेषु देवताता मितद्रवः स्वर्काः । जम्भयन्तोऽहिं वृकं रक्षांसि सनेम्यस्मद्युयवन्नमीवाः ॥

śaṃ no bhavantu vājino haveṣu devatātā mitadravaḥ svarkāḥ | jambhayanto 'hiṃ vṛkaṃ rakṣāṃsi sanemyasmad yuyavann amīvāḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-2; as read "೨-೩೪-೨" [?].) In this Ṛk the Nirukta explains devatātā as "sacrifice".

ūrjām — havirlakṣaṇānām annānām: "of foods in the form of oblations". The word ūrj is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 3-9 [?]). And —

देवी ऊर्जाहुती इषमूर्जमन्यावक्षत्सग्धिं सपीतिं मन्यानेवेन पूर्वं दयमानाः स्याम पुराणेन नवं तामूर्जमूर्जाहुती ऊर्जयमाने अधाताम् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ।

devī ūrjāhutī iṣam ūrjam anyāvakṣat sagdhiṃ sapītiṃ manyānevena pūrvaṃ dayamānāḥ syāma purāṇena navaṃ tām ūrjam ūrjāhutī ūrjayamāne adhātāṃ vasuvane vasudheyasya vītāṃ yaja |

(Vāj. Saṃ. 28-18 [?] and 8-43 [?], as read; small-type, letters doubtful — I record it as read from the Kannada letters and do not claim the text: [?].) Here iṣam ūrjam is explained as "food and sap" (annaṃ rasaṃ ca): meaning "food".

ayā kṛpā na jūryati — anayā sāmarthyalakṣaṇayā kalpanayā haviḥsvīkaraṇarūpayā yajñasamāptiparyantaṃ na naśyati ajaro vartate ity arthaḥ: "Agni, in the matter of accepting the oblations of ghee and puroḍāśa offered by the sacrificers, stays young until the sacrifice ends — that is, unwearied": so the meaning.

The Niruktakāra reads kṛpaḥ kṛpater vā kalpater vā (Ni. 6-8 [?]); Sāyaṇa takes the word, which comes from the root kṛp sāmarthye, as "ability".

devaṃ mātariśvā manave parāvataḥ bhāḥ — dyotanaśīlam antarikṣasaṃcārī vāyuḥ pūrvaṃ manave manorarthāya atidūraṃ gatavataḥ ādityād bhāḥ abhāsīt | aucityena bhūmau sthāpitavān: "the wind that moves in the sky, for the sake of Manu, made the shining Agni appear on the earth, bringing him from the far-away sun; he placed him on the earth in a suitable place".

(continued): "— the wind brought (the shining Agni) from the far-away sun, set him apart on earth, established him in suitable places in accord with the rites, for Manu": so the meaning.

The word parāvataḥ is recorded among the five names of "far" (Ni. 3-20 [?]). And —

अपामुपस्थे महिषा अगृभ्णत विशो राजानमुप तस्थुरृग्मियम् । आ दूतो [?] अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥

apām upasthe mahiṣā agṛbhṇata viśo rājānam upa tasthur ṛgmiyam | ā dūto [?] agnim abharad vivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4, as read. The word after "ā" in the second line is not clearly legible in my image; the OCR reads "dūto"; I record "dūto [?]".) and —

एतदस्या अनः शये सुसंपिष्टं विपाश्या । ससार सीं परावतः ॥

etad asyā anaḥ śaye susaṃpiṣṭaṃ vipāśyā | sasāra sīṃ parāvataḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-11, as read.) — in these Ṛks too the Nirukta explains parāvataḥ as preritavataḥ parāgatād vā ("sent" or "come from afar"); Sāyaṇa here explains "from the sun who is far away".

mātariśvā — mātariśvā vāyur mātary antarikṣe śvasiti mātari aśvanitīti vā (Ni. 7-26 [?]): the Niruktakāra: the word mātariśvan denotes "the wind": mātari — in the sky — he breathes (moves), or he moves quickly in the sky. For this reason the idea stated in the Brāhmaṇa "asyāgner vaiśvānarasya mātariśvānam āhartāram āha" (as read) — that the Vaiśvānara fire, which is in all beings on earth as the digestive fire, was set apart from the sun as is suitable for the sacrifice — is meant here too, as Sāyaṇa says.

parāvataḥ — tadvat dūrād devam agnim asmad devayajanaṃ prati sthāpayatv ity arthaḥ: the word parāvataḥ is explained as "far", and "may the wind, who has brought Agni from the far-away sun and set him on earth, make Agni stay firm in the sacrificial altar of the sacrificers who sacrifice": so it is explained.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly). yajñasādham — root sādha saṃsiddhau; kvip in the agent sense by kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76 [?]); yajñaṃ sādhnotīti yajñasāt, accusative tam; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the final member of the compound. vātayāmasi — root vāta gatisukhasevanayoḥ, curādi; laṭ first person plural, masi [the Kannada: mas suffix]; satyāpapāśa… (Pā. 3-1-25) gives ṇic in the self sense [(the rest of the entry continues on p. 332)].

Grammar of Ṛk 2, continued; numbers as printed, noted briefly. vātayāmasi (cont.) — guṇa and ayādeśa because of the śap (ṇic) ending; idanto masiḥ (Pā. 7-1-46) gives the augment iṭ to the suffix; tiṅ-nighāta since it follows a non-finite word. pathā — the stem pathin; when the instrumental singular follows, bhasyāṭ ṭelopaḥ (Pā. 7-1-88 [?]) elides the ṭi; anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (Pā. 6-1-161) gives the acute to the ending. devatātā — sarvadevāt tātil (Pā. 4-4-142 [?]) gives tātil; liti (Pā. 6-1-193) gives the acute on the syllable before the suffix; supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39) gives ā in place of the locative ending; likewise in haviṣmatā, the locative ending becomes ā. ūrjām — ūrk is a name for food; genitive plural; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168) gives the acute on the ending. upābhṛtyā — upa and ā are preverbs; root hṛñ haraṇe; striyāṃ kriṇ (Pā. 3-3-94 [?]) gives the suffix kriṇ; since k-marked no guṇa; gṛhor bhaś chandasi gives bh for the root's h; the following locative ending drops by supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39); tāddhe ceti [as read: "tādau ca niti"] (Pā. 6-2-50) gives the preverb (ā) its own accent; gatir gatau (Pā. 8-1-70) gives the earlier preverb (upa) the anudātta. āyā — the form anayā, with the Vedic loss of the letter n. jūryati — root jṝṣ vayohānau, divādi, laṭ third person singular, tip, śyan; bahulaṃ chandasi gives u in place of the root-vowel with rapara; hali ca lengthens the penult; tiṅ-nighāta. bhāḥ — root bhā dīptau; luṅ third person singular, sip by vyatyaya; itaś ca drops i; luk for śap; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75) — no augment aṭ; because of yad no nighāta; the final-acute of the root remains; the s of the suffix becomes ru, visarga. ‖ 2 ‖

अयमग्निरेवेन गमनसाधनेन गमनेन वा सद्योऽस्मदाह्वानानन्तरं पार्थिवं पृथिवीसम्बन्धि स्थानं वेदिलक्षणमेव परि परितः । यद्वा । अनर्थक अभिमुख्यार्थो वा परि । एति । गच्छति । कीदृशोऽग्निः । मुहुर्गीः सर्वदा गीयमानः । रेतःशब्देन तत्कार्यं हविरूपमन्नमुच्यते । तद्वान् ॥ मत्वर्थीयो लुप्यते ॥ वृषभः कामानां वर्षिता कनिक्रदत् शब्दयन् पर्येति । पुनः स एव विशेष्यते । रेतो दधदाज्यादिस्वीकारेणात्यधिकं सामर्थ्यं दधानः कनिक्रदत् शब्दयन् पर्येतीति शेषः । पुनः स एव विशेष्यते । अयमग्निर्देवो वनेषु सम्भजनेषु स्तोत्रेषु निमित्तभूतेष्वक्षस्थानीयाभिर्ज्वालाभिः शतं चक्षाणः सर्वतः प्रकाशमानः । यद्वा । ज्वालोत्कर्षेण यजमानेन कृतं शतगुणितं प्रख्यापयन् । तथा तुर्वणिः शीघ्रगन्ता शत्रूणां हिंसको वा । तुर्वणिस्त्वर्वणिरिति यास्कः । नि. ६-१४ [?] । किंच सानुषु समुच्छ्रितेषु । सानु समुच्छ्रितं भवतीति यास्कः । नि. २-३१ [?] । तेष्वपरेषु । उपरमन्त इत्युपरा [?]

ayamagnirevena gamanasādhanena gamanena vā sadyo 'smadāhvānānantaraṃ pārthivaṃ pṛthivīsambandhi sthānaṃ vedilakṣaṇameva pari paritaḥ | yadvā | anarthaka abhimukhyārtho vā pari | eti | gacchati | kīdṛśo 'gniḥ | muhurgīḥ sarvadā gīyamānaḥ | retaḥśabdena tatkāryaṃ havirūpamannamucyate | tadvān ‖ matvarthīyo lupyate ‖ vṛṣabhaḥ kāmānāṃ varṣitā kanikradat śabdayan paryeti | punaḥ sa eva viśeṣyate | reto dadhadājyādisvīkāreṇātyadhikaṃ sāmarthyaṃ dadhānaḥ kanikradat śabdayan paryetīti śeṣaḥ | punaḥ sa eva viśeṣyate | ayamagnirdevo vaneṣu sambhajaneṣu stotreṣu nimittabhūteṣvakṣasthānīyābhirjvālābhiḥ śataṃ cakṣāṇaḥ sarvataḥ prakāśamānaḥ | yadvā | jvālotkarṣeṇa yajamānena kṛtaṃ śataguṇitaṃ prakhyāpayan | tathā turvaṇiḥ śīghragantā śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsako vā | turvaṇistvarvaṇiriti yāskaḥ | ni. 6-14 [?] | kiṃca sānuṣu samucchriteṣu | sānu samucchritaṃ bhavatīti yāskaḥ | ni. 2-31 [?] | teṣvapareṣu | uparamanta ityuparā [?]

सदो दधानः स्थानं धारयमानोऽग्निः सद्यः पर्येतीति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । किमर्थम् । परेषूत्कृष्टेषु सानुषु समुच्छ्रितेषु कर्मसु हवीःषु वा निमित्तभूतेषु ॥

sado dadhānaḥ sthānaṃ dhārayamāno 'gniḥ sadyaḥ paryetīti pūrvatrānvayaḥ | kimartham | pareṣūtkṛṣṭeṣu sānuṣu samucchriteṣu karmasu havīḥṣu vā nimittabhūteṣu ‖

Read from the image; "dadhānaḥ… pūrvatrānvayaḥ" connects with the earlier clause: "Agni, holding his seat, comes at once". For what? for the sake of the highest exalted rites or oblations. Sense: "This Agni comes at once, soon after our invocation, by his eva (his way of going, or going), to the earth-place, the altar, all around — or the particle pari is without meaning or has the sense 'facing'; eti — goes. What kind of Agni? muhurgīḥ — constantly sung; the word retas here means the oblation-food that is its product — [Agni is] 'possessing that' (the possessive suffix is dropped); vṛṣabhaḥ — the showerer of desires; kanikradat — sounding, comes round. Again, the same Agni, bearing great power (retas) through accepting ghee etc., roaring, comes. Again: this god Agni, among the praises (vaneṣu) that are the occasion of worship, with flames like eyes (akṣa) śataṃ cakṣāṇaḥ — shining on all sides, or making known the sacrifice performed by the sacrificer as a hundred-fold through the greatness of his flames; swift-going (turvaṇiḥ) or destroyer of enemies — 'Yāska: turvaṇiḥ is tvarvaṇiḥ' [as read: Ni. 6-14 [?]]; and sānuṣu — in the high places — 'Yāska: sānu is "elevated"' [Ni. 2-31 [?]] — in the lower (upareṣu) ones…"

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. muhurgīḥ — ever praised; vṛṣabhaḥ — showerer of desires; retaḥ — endowed with food in the form of oblation; kanikradat — the roaring Agni; evena — by going; sadyaḥ — immediately after our invocation; pārthivam — belonging to the earth (the altar-ground); pari eti — comes facing; retaḥ dadhat — bearing strength (by accepting ghee etc.); kanikradat — roaring (greatly); (pari eti — comes facing); agniḥ devaḥ — the god Agni; vaneṣu — when praises are used; akṣabhiḥ — by flames in the form of eyes; śataṃ cakṣāṇaḥ — shining well (making the sacrifice done by the sacrificer known a hundred-fold); turvaṇiḥ — destroyer of enemies (swift-going); sānuṣu — in the raised; upareṣu — in the altar-grounds (in the houses of the sacrificers); sadaḥ dadhānaḥ — taking his place; pareṣu — in the excellent; sānuṣu — in the rites (turning to the rites); (pari eti — comes facing).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Agni, ever praised, rich in oblations, showerer of what is desired and full of sound, comes directly after our invocation to this earthly altar, powerful by acceptance of the oblations, roaring greatly; and this Agni, praised, blazing greatly with his flames (making the sacrificer's work a hundred-fold famed), slaying enemies (swift), taking his place on the exalted altar-grounds, comes to the excellent rites.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Agni, who is ever to be hymned, the giver of food, the showerer (of benefits), comes immediately (upon our invocation), in approach to (the altar of) earth, loud-sounding, vigorous, and loud-sounding: the rapid and divine (Agni, incited by praise), manifests himself a hundred-fold by his flames; Agni, having his abode in high places, (comes quickly) to pious rites."

original p. 335

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).

evena — paryeti gamanasādhanena gamanena vā paritaḥ | yadvā anarthaka abhimukhyārtho vā pari eti gacchati. The Niruktakāra says that the particles in the mantras bound by metre are meaningless (anarthakāḥ; as read in small type, mitākṣarepy anarthakāḥ [?]); the Vṛttikāra explains "nipātaḥ pādapūraṇaḥ", that the indeclinable is a filler of the foot. Following this Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of meaning to the indeclinable pari in pari + eti: "meaningless", or "facing". Since the word eva is formed from the root iṇ gatau he explains evena as "by going".

When Agni comes to the place of sacrifice, whether by means of a conveyance for going or on foot, he comes and takes up a position facing the sacrificer at the altar: so the meaning.

The Niruktakāra says that eva and evam are particles; the word evaḥ, with the case-endings of nouns, alone conveys the meanings "going" and the like. —

विश्वानरस्य वस्तिमनानतस्य शवसः । एवैश्च चर्षणीनामूती हुवे रथानाम् ॥

viśvānarasya vastim anānatasya śavasaḥ | evaiś ca carṣaṇīnām ūtī huve rathānām ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-4, as read; numerals doubtful. The first word is printed "viśvānarasya", not "vaiśvānarasya" — as printed: [sic?].) Here he explains evaiḥ as kāmyair ayanair avanair vā (Ni. 12-22 [?]). Durgācārya explains: kāmyaiḥ ayanaiḥ, avanaiḥ gamanaiḥ — "by the desired goings (or: protections), the goings". By this too Sāyaṇa's explanation of evena is confirmed.

The words retaḥ kanikradat are used twice. For the first retaḥ he gives, tatkāryaṃ haviḥrūpam annam ucyate tadvān: since the word retas is recorded among the hundred-and-one names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೧೨"? [?]) it conveys the sense "water"; the grain and the like, produced by water, are used in the form of oblations; so they are results of retas; it is described thus; and Agni is "the possessor of food in the form of oblation".

For the second retas, the first meaning is explained again: since ghee and the like are oblations, by offering ghee and the like as oblations Agni accepts them and possesses extraordinary strength: so the meaning.

kanikradat — śabdayan paryeti: because Agni accepts the oblation, he comes making a loud sound — i.e. there is a crackling sound when Agni burns.

original p. 336

कनिक्रदज्ज्ञनुषं [?] प्रब्रुवाण इयर्ति वाचमरितेव नावम् । सुमङ्गलश्च शकुने भवासि मा त्वा का चिदभिभा विश्व्या [?] विदत् ॥

kanikradaj-jñanuṣaṃ [?] prabruvāṇa iyarti vācam ariteva nāvam | sumaṅgalaś ca śakune bhavāsi mā tvā kā cid abhibhā viśvyā [?] vidat ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-43-1, as printed; the first word and the last words are doubtful in my reading: [?].) In this Ṛk the Vṛttikāra explains the word kanikradat as punaḥ punaḥ bhṛśaṃ vā akradat, and Sāyaṇa's meaning is explained.

vṛṣabhaḥ — kāmānāṃ varṣitā: "Agni is the fulfiller of the desires of the sacrificers": so the meaning. The Niruktakāra gives the meaning of the word vṛṣabha and illustrates it: prajāṃ varṣatīti vā bṛhati reta iti vā tat vṛṣakarmā varṣaṇāt vṛṣabhaḥ [as read; small type: [?]] — this is the Niruktakāra's etymology; the Vṛttikāra explains: "the emission of semen, which is the cause of offspring, and the free use of his body for the sake of seminal emission — vṛṣakarma"; vṛṣaṇāt retovarṣaṇāt — "from the pouring out of semen, a vṛṣabha (bull)": the meaning of the word vṛṣabha is explained so. Here Agni is called vṛṣabha from performing only the act of "raining" (varṣaṇa). The word vṛṣabha is used in the Nirukta in another sense as well. —

मरुत्वाँ इन्द्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोमं अनुष्वधं [?] मदाय । आ सिञ्चस्व जठरे मध्व ऊर्मिं त्वं राजासि प्रदिवः सुतानाम् ॥

marutvām̐ indra vṛṣabho raṇāya pibā somam anuṣvadhaṃ [?] madāya | ā siñcasva jaṭhare madhva ūrmiṃ tvaṃ rājāsi pradivaḥ sutānām ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-32-1, as printed "೩-೩೨-೧".) Here vṛṣabhaḥ is explained as varṣitā apām — "the one who rains the waters". In the same way —

प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचन्ते । वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वाँ अधूनोत्काष्ठा अव शम्बरं भेत् ॥

pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacante | vaiśvānaro dasyum agnir jaghanvām̐ adhūnot kāṣṭhā ava śambaraṃ bhet ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6, as printed.) — here too vṛṣabhasya is explained as varṣituḥ apām, "of the rainer of the waters, of one who sends rain".

devaḥ vaneṣu akṣabhiḥ śataṃ cakṣāṇaḥ — sambhajaneṣu stotreṣu nimittabhūteṣu akṣasthānīyābhir jvālābhiḥ sarvataḥ prakāśamānaḥ | yadvā | jvālotkarṣeṇa yajamānena kṛtaṃ śataguṇitaṃ prakhyāpayan: "Agni, when the praise-hymns are recited by the sacrificers, shines on all sides by his flames, suitable for filling every direction with light; or by the greatness of his flames he declares that what the sacrificers have offered him is a hundred-fold": so he explains.

The Niruktakāra explains the word akṣa — aśnoter ity eke ("some say from aś, to pervade"): the word akṣa is formed from the root aś of the sense "to pervade": the meaning "pervading" is stated. And —

अनूपे गोमान् गोभिरक्षाः सोमो दुग्धाभिरक्षाः ।

anūpe gomān gobhir akṣāḥ somo dugdhābhir akṣāḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-107-[?], as printed: the numerals "೯-೧೦೭" and the pāda are small and doubtful: [?].) and —

न यस्य द्यावापृथिवी न धन्व नान्तरिक्षं नाद्रयः सोमो अक्षाः । [?]

na yasya dyāvāpṛthivī na dhanva nāntarikṣaṃ nādrayaḥ somo akṣāḥ [?]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]; as read from the OCR. The passage is cut off at the page end and small-type letters are doubtful; the quotation is not claimed: [?].)

अनूपे गोमान् गोभिरक्षाः सोमो दुग्धाभिरक्षाः ।

anūpe gomān gobhir akṣāḥ somo dugdhābhir akṣāḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-107-9, as printed "೯-೧೦೭-೯".)

न यस्य द्यावापृथिवी न धन्व नान्तरिक्षं नाद्रयः सोमो अक्षाः । [?]

na yasya dyāvāpṛthivī na dhanva nāntarikṣaṃ nādrayaḥ somo akṣāḥ [?]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-6 [?], as read "೧೦-೯೪-೬"; the text of the line is as read and doubtful.) These Ṛks he gives as illustrations; and he explains another meaning of akṣa by "akṣāḥ — aśnuvate etān iti vā abhyaśnuvate ebhir iti vā" ("because people pervade them, or because with them people pervade [the stakes of others]"). Durgācārya: "dīvyantaḥ kitavāḥ etān akṣān pāṇibhiḥ aśnuvate | abhyaśnuvate ebhiḥ kitavāḥ pratikitavaṃ dhanam": the gamblers cast these dice with their hands while playing; or with them they take hold of another's wealth and make it their own; hence the word akṣa means the "instrument" (material) of gamblers.

vaneṣu — sambhajanīyeṣu: "vanaṃ vanoteḥ" (Ni. 9-4 [?]): since the word vana is formed from the root vanu of the sense "to worship", Sāyaṇa too explains the same meaning. But in

नि यद्वृणक्षि श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि शुष्णस्य चिद्ब्रन्दिनो रोरुवद्वना । प्राचीनेन मनसा बर्हणावता यदद्या चित्कृणवः कस्त्वा परि ॥

ni yad vṛṇakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani śuṣṇasya cid brandino roruvad vanā | prācīnena manasā barhaṇāvatā yad adyā cit kṛṇavaḥ kas tvā pari ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-3, as printed.) — Yāska says that vanāni is used in another sense: "waters", or, as vanāni, "by the striking of the cloud".

turvaṇiḥ — śīghragantā śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsako vā: "one who goes quickly, or who destroys enemies": Agni is described as endowed with these qualities. —

स तुर्वणिर्महाँ अरेणु पौंस्ये गिरेर्भृष्टिर्न भ्राजते तुजा शवः । येन शुष्णं मायिनमायसो मदे दुध्र आभूषु रामयन्नि दामनि ॥

sa turvaṇir mahām̐ areṇu pauṃsye girer bhṛṣṭir na bhrājate tujā śavaḥ | yena śuṣṇaṃ māyinam āyaso made dudhra ābhūṣu rāmayan ni dāmani ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-3, as printed.) Here Durgācārya explains the word turvaṇi as "tūrṇaṃ hi yaḥ sambhajate sa tūrṇavanitā sa tūrṇavanir ity uktaḥ" ("who quickly gets, and is called tūrṇavani"). Yāska too, "turvaṇis tūrṇavaniḥ" (Ni. 6-14 [?]), has explained as Sāyaṇa does.

sānuṣu — samucchritesu: "in the high place". —

इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत् सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः । पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेमधीतिभिः ॥

iyaṃ śuṣmebhir bisakhā ivārujat sānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhir ūrmibhiḥ | pārāvataghnīm avase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīm ā vivāsema dhītibhiḥ ‖

(The Ṛk stands at the foot of p. 337 and runs over to p. 338; the reference is not printed with it; letters read as printed. Readings iyaṃ…bisakhā are doubtful: [?].)

original p. 338

Yāska explains the word sānu in this Ṛk: sānu samucchritaṃ bhavati samunnunnam iti vā (Ni. 2-21 [?]). Durgācārya: "sānu samastaṃ hi tad ucchritaṃ bhavati" — "high ground is called sānu because it is samam ūrdhvaṃ nunnam, i.e. pushed upward evenly."

upareṣu — upāramante [?] eṣv iti upārāḥ tiṣṭhyāḥ [?] yajamānagṛhā vā: "the places where Agni sits at ease at the sacrifice, the altars, or the houses of the sacrificers". The word upara is recorded among the eight names of the quarters (Ni. 2-16 [?]; as read "೨-೧೬") and among the names of cloud (Ni. 3-21 [?]). The meaning: Agni is established in high altars of sacrifice and in the houses of the sacrificers.

pareṣu sānuṣu — utkṛṣṭeṣu samucchriteṣu karmasu haviḥṣu vā nimittabhūteṣu. In this Ṛk the word sānuṣu is said twice. The one is said as a specification of the word upara. For the second sānuṣu it is explained that Agni takes his seat on the altar at the time of exalted rites or exalted oblations.

sadaḥ — sthānam — a comfortable place. The word sadas is recorded as sadasī among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-30 [?]); Sāyaṇa gives the sense "place".

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as read from the page). evena — root iṇ gatau; iṇ śībhyāṃ van (Uṇ. 1-150 [?]) gives van; because of it guṇa of the root; jñitsvarādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) the acute on the first syllable; instrumental singular. eti — the same root, laṭ third person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. pārthivam — pṛthivyā idam; pṛthivyā añ [as read: pṛthivyā ñāñau] gives añ; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ gives vṛddhi of the first syllable; yasyeti ca drops ī; the ñ-marker gives the acute on the first syllable. muhurgīḥ — gṝ nigaraṇe; when muhuḥ is the upapada, kvip ca gives kvip; ṛta id dhātoḥ gives i to the root; the nominative singular, rvor upadhāyāḥ gives lengthening of the penult; kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara. retaḥ — root rīṅ śleṣaṇe; surībhyāṃ tuṭ ca (Uṇ. 4-[?]) gives asun with the augment tuṭ; acute on the first syllable. dadhat — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; śatṛ in the present sense; by nābhyastācchatuḥ no num; abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the acute on the first syllable. cakṣāṇaḥ — root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci, adādi; here used in the sense of light; śānac in the present sense; because śānac is unaccented (lasārvadhātuka) the root's accent remains. upareṣu — upaviramante eṣu iti upārāḥ; root ramu krīḍāyām; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate gives ḍa; since ḍ-marked the ṭi (ām) is dropped; locative plural. ‖ 3 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स सुक्रतुः पुरोहितो दमेदमेऽग्निर्यज्ञस्याध्वरस्य चेतति । क्रत्वा यज्ञस्य चेतति । क्रत्वा वेधा इषूयते विश्वा जातानि पस्पशे । यतो घृतश्रीरतिथिरजायत वह्निर्वेधा अजायत ॥ ४ ॥

sa sukratuḥ purohito damedame 'gniryajñasyādhvarasya cetati | kratvā yajñasya cetati | kratvā vedhā iṣūyate viśvā jātāni paspaśe | yato ghṛtaśrīratithirajāyata vahnirvedhā ajāyata ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image: dame-dame, yajñasya, adhvarasya, cetati; iṣu-yate; pas-paśe; ghṛta-śrīḥ.

original p. 340

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सोऽग्निः सुक्रतुः शोभनकर्मा पुरोहितः पुरो धार्यमाणः । यद्वा । पुरोहितवद्यागनिर्वाहकः सन् । दमे दमे तत्र तत्र यजमानगृहे सर्वेषु देवयजनेषु वाध्वरस्य नाशरहितस्य फलप्रदस्य यज्ञस्य तदर्थं चेतति । जानाति । प्रबुध्यत इत्यर्थः । किंचायं यजमानोऽपि क्रत्वा शोभनेन कर्मणा यज्ञस्य चेतः । कर्तव्यतामवजानाति । किंचायमग्निरपि क्रत्वा प्रकृष्टेन कर्मणा वेधा विविधानां फलानां कर्ता सन्निषूयते । इष्यत इतीषुरन्नमागमनं वा । तदिच्छते यजमानार्थं विश्वा जातानि सर्वाणि सम्पादितानि हविरादीनि पस्पशे । अत्यर्थं स्पृशति । स्वीकरोति । यतोऽयं घृतश्रीर्घृतं सेवमानोऽतिथिरतिथिवत्पूज्यश्चाजायत उत्पन्नः । यतः कारणात् घृतमत्यर्थं सेवमानः प्रवृद्धोऽभवत् । अतः पस्पश इत्यर्थः । एवमग्नौ प्रवृद्धे सति यजमानोऽपि वह्निर्हविषां वोढा वेधा विविधस्य फलस्य कर्तोत्पादयिताजायत । समर्थोऽभवत् ॥

so 'gniḥ sukratuḥ śobhanakarmā purohitaḥ puro dhāryamāṇaḥ | yadvā | purohitavadyāganirvāhakaḥ san | dame dame tatra tatra yajamānagṛhe sarveṣu devayajaneṣu vādhvarasya nāśarahitasya phalapradasya yajñasya tadarthaṃ cetati | jānāti | prabudhyata ityarthaḥ | kiṃcāyaṃ yajamāno 'pi kratvā śobhanena karmaṇā yajñasya cetaḥ | kartavyatāmavajānāti | kiṃcāyamagnirapi kratvā prakṛṣṭena karmaṇā vedhā vividhānāṃ phalānāṃ kartā sanniṣūyate | iṣyata itīṣurannamāgamanaṃ vā | tadicchate yajamānārthaṃ viśvā jātāni sarvāṇi sampāditāni havirādīni paspaśe | atyarthaṃ spṛśati | svīkaroti | yato 'yaṃ ghṛtaśrīrghṛtaṃ sevamāno 'tithiratithivatpūjyaścājāyata utpannaḥ | yataḥ kāraṇāt ghṛtamatyarthaṃ sevamānaḥ pravṛddho 'bhavat | ataḥ paspaśa ityarthaḥ | evamagnau pravṛddhe sati yajamāno 'pi vahnirhaviṣāṃ voḍhā vedhā vividhasya phalasya kartotpādayitājāyata | samartho 'bhavat ‖

Read from the image; a few letters of the small type ("cetaḥ", "iṣūyate… iṣyata itīṣur annam āgamanaṃ vā") are doubtful: [?]. Sense: "That Agni, sukratu — one of good works; purohita — placed in front; or, accomplishing the sacrifice like a family-priest; dame dame — in each house of the sacrificers or in all places of divine worship — cetati — knows, awakes, for the sake of the imperishable (adhvara), fruit-giving sacrifice. And this sacrificer too, by kratu, good work, understands what is to be done for the sacrifice. Further this Agni, by his excellent work, being the maker (vedhā) of various fruits, iṣūyate — is desired (iṣu = food or coming) — he, for the sake of the sacrificer, paspaśe — takes hold of all the produced offerings, accepts them; since he, ghṛtaśrīḥ — serving ghee — has become born as a guest, honourable like a guest; because he has grown by consuming ghee so much; therefore paspaśe. And when Agni has thus grown, the sacrificer too, the bearer of the oblations (vahniḥ), became vedhā, the maker of various fruits — became capable."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. saḥ agniḥ — that Agni; sukratuḥ — of good works; purohitaḥ — placed in front (carrying out the sacrifice like a family-priest); dame dame — in every house; adhvarasya — of the imperishable (fruit-giving) sacrifice; yajñasya — for the sake of the sacrifice; cetati — awakes, understands (and the sacrificer too); kratvā — by good works; yajñasya — in regard to the sacrifice; cetati — becomes aware of what is to be done; yataḥ — because; (ayam — this Agni); ghṛtaśrīḥ — one who partakes of ghee; atithiḥ — like a guest (honoured); ajāyata — became; (tataḥ — therefore; ayam agniḥ — this Agni); kratvā — by excellent works; vedhāḥ — the maker of various fruits; iṣūyate — to the sacrificer who desires food (or desires the coming of Agni); viśvā jātāni — all the produced things (the whole of what has been provided); paspaśe — touches (accepts) greatly; so Agni grows, and the sacrificer; vahniḥ — he who carries the oblations to Agni's neighbourhood; vedhāḥ — the master of various fruits; ajāyata — became.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Agni, the doer of good works, carrying out the sacrifice like a family-priest, awakes in each house of the sacrificers for the sake of the sacrifice; the sacrificer too, by his good rites, becomes aware of what he has to do; having taken ghee, honoured like a guest, Agni takes the oblations in greater measure and, by his excellent works, becomes the bestower of various fruits; the sacrificer, offering oblations, becomes the enjoyer of various fruits.

original p. 341

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "That Agni, who is (the performer of) holy acts, the priest of the family, thinks in every dwelling of the imperishable sacrifice; he thinks of the sacrifice (reminded) by (its) celebration: for through such pious rite, he, the bestower of (fit) rewards, accepts all the offered oblations for (the good of) the worshipper; whence he has become as a guest, fed abundantly with butter; and the offerer (of the oblations) has become the realizer of the rewards (of the worship)."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).

sukratuḥ — śobhanakarmā: "one who performs works that are good for the sacrificers": so the meaning. —

नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुप स्तोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः । ये सुक्रतेवः शुचयो धियंधाः स्वदन्ति देवा उभयानि हव्या ॥

narāśaṃsasya mahimānam eṣām upa stoṣāma yajatasya yajñaiḥ | ye sukratevaḥ śucayo dhiyaṃdhāḥ svadanti devā ubhayāni havyā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-2, as read; "sukratevaḥ" as printed [sic?].) Here Yāska explains the word sukratevaḥ as śobhanakarmāṇaḥ.

purohitaḥ — purodhāryamāṇaḥ | yadvā purohitavad yāganirvāhakaḥ: "Agni is placed in front in the sacrifices; or, like a family-priest, he conducts the rites by reciting the mantras and having the various rites done": Yāska explains the word purohita — puraḥ enaṃ dadhāti (Ni. 2-12 [?]).

dame dame — tatra tatra yajamānagṛhe sarveṣu devayajaneṣu vā: "in each house of the sacrificers, or in every place of sacrifice to the gods". The word dama is recorded among the names of house (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೩"), and explained "dama iti gṛhanāma" (Ni. 4-4 [?]). Sāyaṇa describes that Agni is awake in the houses of the several sacrificers and in the places where the gods are worshipped.

adhvarasya — nāśarahitasya phalapradasya: "for a sacrifice that produces imperishable fruit".

The word adhvara — "adhvara iti yajñanāma dhvaratir hiṃsākarmā tatpratiṣedhaḥ" (Ni. 1-8 [?]): the word adhvara conveys the sense "sacrifice"; the roots dhvarati, dhūrvati have the sense of harming; the Niruktakāra explains that from adhvara the meaning "a rite without harm" arises.

Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check): 2-12; 3-13; 4-4; 1-8

original p. 342

And the word adhvara is recorded among the sixteen names of the middle space (Ni. 2-10 [?]) and among the fifteen names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-19 [?]). And —

ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमाः सधस्थं विश्वे अभि सन्ति देवाः । ताँ अध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टी भगं नासत्या पुरंधिम् ॥

te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmāḥ sadhasthaṃ viśve abhi santi devāḥ | tām̐ adhvara uśato yakṣy agne śruṣṭī bhagaṃ nāsatyā puraṃdhim ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-31-4 [?], as read "೨-೩೧-೪"; the numerals are small.) Here adhvare — "in the sacrifice" — the word adhvara is explained as "sacrifice". The word kratvā is used twice. For the first kratvā the meaning "by a good work, an auspicious work", and for the second kratvā "by an excellent work, by many actions" is given.

vedhāḥ — vividhānāṃ phalānāṃ kartā: "one who gives the sacrificers many kinds of fruits". This word is recorded among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19 [?]).

iṣūyate — iṣyata iti iṣuḥ annaṃ āgamanaṃ vā: the word iṣu, formed from the root īṣ, means "food" or "coming". The Niruktakāra, —

सुपर्णं वस्ते मृगो अस्या दन्तो गोभिः सन्नद्धा पतति प्रसूता । यत्रा नरः सं च वि च द्रवन्ति तत्रास्मभ्यमिषवः शर्म यंसन् ॥

suparṇaṃ vaste mṛgo asyā danto gobhiḥ sannaddhā patati prasūtā | yatrā naraḥ saṃ ca vi ca dravanti tatrāsmabhyam iṣavaḥ śarma yaṃsan ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-11, as printed.) — citing this Ṛk, explains iṣur īṣater gatikarmaṇo vadhakarmaṇo vā: from the root īṣ of the sense "going", the word iṣu means "going" or "the weapon that kills creatures": as the arrow that kills living beings quickly reaches its target, Agni comes, following the wish of the sacrificer who desires him to come for the sacrifice.

ghṛtaśrīḥ atithir ajāyata — ghṛtaṃ sevamānaḥ atithivat pūjyaś ca: "since Agni consumes ghee in plenty, and since he is worthy of honour like a guest, growing on the altar, he takes in abundance the oblations — the sacrificer's offerings — that are poured in."

vahniḥ vedhāḥ ajāyata — evam agnau pravṛddhe sati yajamāno 'pi haviṣāṃ voḍhā vividhasya phalasya kartā utpādayitā samarthaḥ abhavat: "when Agni, with the acceptance of the oblations, has thus grown and is satisfied, the sacrificer too becomes the bearer of the oblations to Agni, and is endowed with such greatness as to produce many kinds of fruit, like Agni": so it is explained.
