सः । श्रुधि । यः । स्म । पृतनासु । कासु । चित् । दक्षाय्यः । इन्द्र । भरऽहूतये । नृऽभिः । असि । प्रऽतूर्तये । नृऽभिः । यः । शूरैः । स्वरिति स्वः । सऽनिता । यः । विप्रैः । वाजम् । तरुता । तम् । ईशानासः । इरधन्त । वाजिनम् । पृक्षम् । अत्यम् । न । वाजिनम् ॥ २ ॥

saḥ | śrudhi | yaḥ | sma | pṛtanāsu | kāsu | cit | dakṣāyyaḥ | indra | bhara 'hūtaye | nṛ 'bhiḥ | asi | pra 'tūrtaye | nṛ 'bhiḥ | yaḥ | śūraiḥ | svariti svaḥ | sa 'nitā | yaḥ | vipraiḥ | vājam | tarutā | tam | īśānāsaḥ | iradhanta | vājinam | pṛkṣam | atyam | na | vājinam ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (small type; read from the image, many letters doubtful: [?]). Sense. "O Indra, such as is described, hear (śrudhi; the hi becomes dhi) our invocation or praise. You, who with men — nṛbhiḥ — in whatever battles, and afterwards with the gods, the Maruts [?] — the leaders of battle, the Maruts, helpers of Indra — 'Indra with the Maruts' (Tai. Saṃ. [?], Ait. Br. [?]: 'the Maruts called him to the contest') — in all engagements, for the call to battle (bharahūti) and for the great slaying (pratūrti) of the enemies, you are dakṣāyya — of growing power; or, asked by the sacrificers, the leaders, you are able to slay foes greatly. And you who, together with the heroic Maruts, are the winner (sanitā) of heaven and of what is desired — tarutā — are the giver of food (vājam) to the sages, the priests praising you: that Indra, swift, with food (pṛkṣam) in the form of oblation, the lords (īśānāsaḥ), the priests able to seek well, serve (iradhanta); as people nourish a swift horse (atyam) with sweet fodder: 'the word atya is a name for horse', since it is read among those names." The grammar tail on tarutā, hedhibhāva, etc., is only characterized.

हे इन्द्र स वक्ष्यमाणगुणविशिष्टस्त्वं श्रुधि । अस्माकमाह्वानं स्तोत्रं वा शृणु ॥ हेर्धिभावः ॥ यः स्म यः खलु त्वं नृभिर्मनुष्यैरेव सद्भिः पश्चाद्देवैर्मरुद्भिः [?] । पुनस्त एव विशेष्यन्ते । नृभिः सङ्ग्रामनयनशीलैः । इन्द्रस्य मरुतां साहाय्यमिन्द्रो मरुद्भिः । तै. सं. २-३-१-१ [?] । मरुतो ह्येनं वाजहुः । ऐ. ब्रा. २-२० [?] इत्यादिषु प्रसिद्धम् । तैः सहितः सन् कासु चित्पृतनासु सर्वासु प्रवृत्तासु सङ्ग्रामेषु भरहूतये भरणहविष्प्राह्वानायुक्ताय प्रतूर्तये प्रकृष्टहिंसनाय । यद्वा । भरहूतये शूरो भव प्रहरेत्येवमादिभरणयुक्ताह्वानाय च शूराणां प्रकृष्टवधाय च । दक्षाय्योऽसि प्रवर्धनशीलोऽसि । यद्वा । नृभिर्नेतृभिर्यजमानैः प्रार्थितः सन् प्रतूर्तये शत्रूणां प्रकृष्टहिंसनाय दक्षाय्योऽसि समर्थोऽसि । किंच यस्त्वं शूरैः शौर्योपेतैर्मरुद्भिर्नृभिर्भर्तृभिः सहितः सन् स्वः स्वयमेव सनिता सङ्ग्रामयस्य [?] अस्यान्यस्य वा मनीषितस्य सनिता सम्भक्तासि [?] । सत्स्वपि तेषां साहित्येऽन्यैरनपेक्ष्येव [?] । तरुतासीत्यर्थः । तरतेस्तृनि ग्रसितस्कभितेति वा निपात्यते ॥ यस्त्वं विप्रैर्मेधाविभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः स्तुतः सन् वाजं तरुता तेभ्यो ऽन्नस्य दातासि । विप्रैर्मरुद्भिः सहित इति सम्बन्धः । तं तादृशं वाजिनं गमनवन्तं पृक्षं हविर्लक्षणान्नवन्तमिन्द्रमीशानासः सम्यग्गभ्यर्थयितुं समर्था ऋत्विज इरधन्त । संराधयन्ति । सेवन्ते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वाजिनं वेजनवन्तं गमनवन्तं पृक्षं घासाद्यन्नवन्तमत्यं न नाश्वमिव । तं यथा समर्थाः स्वादुघासप्रदानादिना पोषयन्ति तद्वत् ॥ अत्य इत्यश्वनाम अत्यो हय इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥

he indra sa vakṣyamāṇaguṇaviśiṣṭastvaṃ śrudhi | asmākamāhvānaṃ stotraṃ vā śṛṇu ‖ herdhibhāvaḥ ‖ yaḥ sma yaḥ khalu tvaṃ nṛbhirmanuṣyaireva sadbhiḥ paścāddevairmarudbhiḥ [?] | punasta eva viśeṣyante | nṛbhiḥ saṅgrāmanayanaśīlaiḥ | indrasya marutāṃ sāhāyyamindro marudbhiḥ | tai. saṃ. 2-3-1-1 [?] | maruto hyenaṃ vājahuḥ | ai. brā. 2-20 [?] ityādiṣu prasiddham | taiḥ sahitaḥ san kāsu citpṛtanāsu sarvāsu pravṛttāsu saṅgrāmeṣu bharahūtaye bharaṇahaviṣprāhvānāyuktāya pratūrtaye prakṛṣṭahiṃsanāya | yadvā | bharahūtaye śūro bhava praharetyevamādibharaṇayuktāhvānāya ca śūrāṇāṃ prakṛṣṭavadhāya ca | dakṣāyyo 'si pravardhanaśīlo 'si | yadvā | nṛbhirnetṛbhiryajamānaiḥ prārthitaḥ san pratūrtaye śatrūṇāṃ prakṛṣṭahiṃsanāya dakṣāyyo 'si samartho 'si | kiṃca yastvaṃ śūraiḥ śauryopetairmarudbhirnṛbhirbhartṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ san svaḥ svayameva sanitā saṅgrāmayasya [?] asyānyasya vā manīṣitasya sanitā sambhaktāsi [?] | satsvapi teṣāṃ sāhitye 'nyairanapekṣyeva [?] | tarutāsītyarthaḥ | taratestṛni grasitaskabhiteti vā nipātyate ‖ yastvaṃ viprairmedhāvibhirṛtvigbhiḥ stutaḥ san vājaṃ tarutā tebhyo 'nnasya dātāsi | viprairmarudbhiḥ sahita iti sambandhaḥ | taṃ tādṛśaṃ vājinaṃ gamanavantaṃ pṛkṣaṃ havirlakṣaṇānnavantamindramīśānāsaḥ samyaggabhyarthayituṃ samarthā ṛtvija iradhanta | saṃrādhayanti | sevante | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vājinaṃ vejanavantaṃ gamanavantaṃ pṛkṣaṃ ghāsādyannavantamatyaṃ na nāśvamiva | taṃ yathā samarthāḥ svādughāsapradānādinā poṣayanti tadvat ‖ atya ityaśvanāma atyo haya iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (begins at the foot of p. 371). indra — O Indra; saḥ — you, of the qualities stated; śrudhi — hear (our praise) or (pardon our invocation); yaḥ sma — you who; nṛbhiḥ — with men [the print continues on p. 372].

original p. 372

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 371: "…nṛbhiḥ — with men; being men first, then having obtained divinity [i.e. the Maruts]; nṛbhiḥ — with the leaders (in battle), the Maruts; kāsu cit pṛtanāsu — in various battles; bharahūtaye — with cries of encouragement (calling to battle); pratūrtaye — for the very great slaying (of enemies); dakṣāyyaḥ asi — you are capable [for encouraging the call, and for slaying the enemies]; or, nṛbhiḥ — being prayed to by the sacrificers; pratūrtaye — to destroy enemies or sins; dakṣāyyaḥ asi — you are capable; kiṃ ca — and); yaḥ (tvam — you who; śūraiḥ — with the brave (Maruts or other warriors), svaḥ — by yourself; sanitā — can give victory in battle or other desired things; yaḥ (tvam) — you who; vipraiḥ — praised by the wise priests, or endowed with the wise Maruts; vājam — food (to those priests); tarutā — can give; tam — such; vājinam — swift; pṛkṣam — possessed of food in the form of oblation, Indra; īśānāsaḥ — the priests able in prayer; vājinam — swift (and possessed of fodder, grass and so on); atyam — a horse; na — as (people able to) nourish; iradhanta — worship (serve)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra, hear our praise (grant our invocation): you, first men and afterwards gods, are able to destroy the enemies through the encouraging cries made by the Maruts, the leaders of battle; accompanied by the brave (the Maruts or warriors), or yourself, without the help of others, giving victory in battle; prayed to by the wise priests, giving them food; such you, endowed with these qualities, going to sacrifices, giver of food in the form of oblations — the priests skilled in prayer serve, as brave men tend a swift horse with grass and the like.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Hear our invocation, Indra: you, who in various battles (associated with the Maruts, are animated through their encouragement; (and are able), with the Maruts, to destroy (your foes): (for you are) he, who, (aided) by heroes, are of yourself the giver (of victory); or, (when praised) by the pious, the giver of food, and whom the lords (of prayer) celebrate, as swift-moving and eager (for sacrificial food), like a fleet courser (eager for forage)." The printed parentheses are unbalanced here, as printed.

original p. 373

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).

nṛbhiḥ — manuṣyair eva sadbhiḥ paścāt devatvam āpannair marudbhiḥ; nṛbhiḥ — saṅgrāmanayanaśīlaiḥ: "Indra's help from the Maruts; 'Indra with the Maruts' (Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-5-1 [?], as read; numerals doubtful); 'for the Maruts called him to the contest' (Ait. Br. 3-20 [?])" — thus well known. The word nara is recorded among the names of horse (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೨೭") and among the names of man (Ni. 3-[?], "೩-೭"). So Indra is with the Maruts — the groups of gods who, though they were men, performed the sacrifice and obtained, as its fruit, the state of gods; or, he grows in company of the groups of gods who help him in fighting: so the meaning. That the Maruts help Indra is well known from the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence "indro marudbhiḥ" and the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence "maruto hainaṃ vājahuḥ" [as read: vāja-, doubtful].

pṛtanāsu bharahūtaye pratūrtaye dakṣāyyaḥ — sarvāsu prauḍhāsv api saṅgrāmeṣu bharaṇaviśiṣṭāhvānayuktāya prakṛṣṭahiṃsanāya | yadvā śūro bhava prahara ity evamādi bharaṇayuktāhvānāya śūrāṇāṃ prakṛṣṭavadhāya ca pravardhanaśīlaḥ asi: one meaning is that in the places where fierce battles go on, Indra is called by the others, "protect us, kill the enemies"; in another sense: "O Indra, be brave, subdue the enemies" — to the call of all the brave soldiers worthy of protection and for the great slaying of the enemies Indra, competent, is by nature one who grows. For nṛbhiḥ pṛtanāsu Sāyaṇa gives another meaning: "following the prayer of the sacrificer, Indra is able to subdue enemies and evil-doers": thus Indra's greatness is described.

Following the explanation of the word indra given by Yāska, Durgācārya says, "irādāro 'ndra iti parokṣeṇocyate" [reading doubtful: [?]]: though Indra does not show his form directly, he is recognized by his work. In all words that name deities, though the several deities are the thing denoted, they remain unseen to those who serve them and accomplish their respective works; and the deities hide their own true forms and greatness: "parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ pratyakṣadviṣaḥ" (as read) — "the gods are, as it were, fond of the unseen and averse to the seen"; for this reason the gods are not willing to show themselves in their own visible form; the Śruti also says their attachment is greater to the unseen. The wise, knowing this secret of the gods, from the derivations of the words that denote the deities,

original p. 374

learn well the nature, qualities, greatness and works of the several deities, serve them, meditate on them, and by identification with them accomplish their respective desires. From this, all deities have both an inner (ādhyātmika) and a divine (ādhidaivata) form; Yāska describes how these become manifest to the worshippers of the several deities. Indra too, being very powerful in this matter, performs protection and the like: so his nature and greatness are described.

yaḥ śūraiḥ svaḥ sanitā tarutā — "Indra, accompanied by the heroic Maruts or by other soldiers, accomplishes his desire, either himself in battle or in some other way. Though there may be much help to assist him, he does not depend on it but, by his greatness, can accomplish the works alone": so the meaning is stated.

vipraiḥ vājaṃ tarutā — medhāvibhir ṛtvigbhiḥ stutaḥ sann tebhyo 'nnasya dātāsi | vipraiḥ marudbhiḥ iti sambandhaḥ: the word vipra is recorded among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19 [?]). By repeating the word vipraiḥ he gives one meaning "by the wise priests" and another "by the Maruts": Indra, accompanied by the Marut gods and praised by the priests, gives food to the priests: so it is described.

pṛkṣaṃ havirlakṣaṇānnavantam indram — the word pṛkṣa is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?], "೨-೯"); used as an epithet of Indra: "Indra is the possessor of food in the form of oblations."

atyaṃ na — aśvam iva: the word atya is recorded among the names of horse (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೨೨"). The word na is recorded among the particles of comparison; in "nendraṃ devam amaṃsata" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3 [?], numerals unreadable) it is used in the sense of negation, and in —

हृत्सु पीतासो युध्यन्ते दुर्मदासो न सुरायाम् । ऊधर्न नग्ना जरन्ते ॥

hṛtsu pītāso yudhyante durmadāso na surāyām | ūdhar na nagnā jarante ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2-12, as printed "೮-೨-೧೨".) in the sense of comparison, as Yāska explains; so in atyaṃ na the word na is a particle of comparison: "like a horse".

vājinaṃ pṛkṣam atyaṃ na — vejanavantaṃ ghāsādyannavantam aśvam iva: this sentence is used as an illustration (upamāna-vākya) for the sentence vājinaṃ pṛkṣam īśānāsaḥ: as people in the world nourish a swift horse by giving it palatable grass, so the priests able to serve Indra, who moves with food in the form of oblation, serve him: so it is compared. Since this usage is in the Veda, there is no room for the charge that it is a base comparison.

original p. 375

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). śrudhi — root śru śravaṇe; loṭ second person singular; the hi by śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi (Pā. 6-4-102) becomes dhi; by the Vedic luk the śnu-suffix is dropped; tiṅ-nighāta since it follows a finite word. sma — nipātasya ca (Pā. 6-3-136) gives the long vowel in the Saṃhitā. dakṣāyyaḥ — root dakṣa vṛddhau; Uṇādi āyyac (Uṇ. 3-[?]); the acute on the first syllable of the suffix. bharahūtaye — bharo hūtir yasyāṃ sā bharahūtiḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam gives the accent of the first member; dative singular. pratūrtaye — root turvī hiṃsāyām; striyāṃ ktin gives ktin; upadhāyāś ca (Pā. 7-1-101) lengthens u; where lopo vyor vali would drop the v, rāllopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-21) prevents it; tāddau ca niti (Pā. 6-2-50) gives the prefix (pra) its natural accent. śūraiḥ — śū is a sautra root; root śū gatau; kuśīsyamīnāṃ… (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives ran, lengthening; since n-marked the acute on the first syllable. svaḥ — svar becomes svarit (Phiṭ-sūtra 4 [as read]). sanitā — root ṣaṇa sambhaktau; tṛn in the agent sense, with the augment iṭ; the acute on the first syllable. tarutā — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; tṛn in the agent sense, grasitaskabhita… (Pā. 6-2-[?]) gives the irregular form tarutṛ. īśānāsaḥ — root īśa aiśvarye; śānac in the present sense; citaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the acute on the last syllable; with jas following, ājjaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50) gives the augment asuk.

original p. 376

Grammar of Ṛk 2, concluded. iradhanta — iradha is a sautra root, used in the sense of serving; by the Vedic usage a laṅ in the present sense; third person plural; by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi the augment aṭ does not occur; tiṅ-nighāta. ‖ 2 ‖

(ornamental rule)

Rik 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

दस्मो हि ष्मा वृषणं पिन्वसि त्वचं कं चिद्यावीररुं शूर मर्त्यम् । परिवृणक्षि मर्त्यम् । इन्द्रोत तुभ्यं तद्दिवे तद्रुद्राय स्वयशसे । मित्राय वोचं वरुणाय सप्रथः सुमृळीकाय सप्रथः ॥ ३ ॥

dasmo hi ṣmā vṛṣaṇaṃ pinvasi tvacaṃ kaṃ cidyāvīraruṃ śūra martyam | parivṛṇakṣi martyam | indrota tubhyaṃ taddive tadrudrāya svayaśase | mitrāya vocaṃ varuṇāya saprathaḥ sumṛḷīkāya saprathaḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image: Saṃhitā "yāvīr arum"; Pada yāvīḥ | arum; sa-prathaḥ, su-mṛḷīkāya.

दस्मः । हि । स्म । वृषणम् । पिन्वसि । त्वचम् । कम् । चित् । यावीः । अरुम् । शूर । मर्त्यम् । परिऽवृणक्षि । मर्त्यम् । इन्द्र । उत । तुभ्यम् । तत् । दिवे । तत् । रुद्राय । स्वऽयशसे । मित्राय । वोचम् । वरुणाय । सऽप्रथः । सुऽमृळीकाय । सऽप्रथः ॥ ३ ॥

dasmaḥ | hi | sma | vṛṣaṇam | pinvasi | tvacam | kam | cit | yāvīḥ | arum | śūra | martyam | pari 'vṛṇakṣi | martyam | indra | uta | tubhyam | tat | dive | tat | rudrāya | sva 'yaśase | mitrāya | vocam | varuṇāya | sa 'prathaḥ | su 'mṛḷīkāya | sa 'prathaḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे इन्द्र त्वं दस्मो हि । शत्रूणामुपक्षपणकर्ता खलु । अत एव कारणाद्वृषणं स्वतो वर्षणशीलं त्वचं संवरणवन्तं पुटबन्धनवदुदकवेष्टनवन्तं कं चिन्मेघं पिन्वसि । निर्भिद्य सेचयसि । किंच मर्त्यं मर्त्यवदरुमरणशीलं गमनस्वभावं कंचिन्मेघं हे शूर विक्रान्त यावीः । मिश्रयसि ॥ यौतेश्छान्दसे लुङि [?] छान्दसोऽडभावः ॥ आवर्षणेन गच्छन्तं बलान्निगृह्य वर्षयसीत्यर्थः ।

he indra tvaṃ dasmo hi | śatrūṇāmupakṣapaṇakartā khalu | ata eva kāraṇādvṛṣaṇaṃ svato varṣaṇaśīlaṃ tvacaṃ saṃvaraṇavantaṃ puṭabandhanavadudakaveṣṭanavantaṃ kaṃ cinmeghaṃ pinvasi | nirbhidya secayasi | kiṃca martyaṃ martyavadarumaraṇaśīlaṃ gamanasvabhāvaṃ kaṃcinmeghaṃ he śūra vikrānta yāvīḥ | miśrayasi ‖ yauteśchāndase luṅi [?] chāndaso 'ḍabhāvaḥ ‖ āvarṣaṇena gacchantaṃ balānnigṛhya varṣayasītyarthaḥ |

original p. 377

यथा शूरः कश्चिद्बलवन्तं गच्छन्तं वैरिणं निगृह्य स्वीकरोति तद्वदित्यर्थः । तथा मर्त्यं मरणशीलं शीर्यमाणस्वभावं निरुदकं कंचिन्मेघं परिवृणक्षि । सर्वतो वर्जयसि । औदासीन्यं करोषीत्यर्थः । हे इन्द्र तादृशं कर्म वर्षणरूपं सप्रथः सर्वतः पृथु यथा भवति तथा तुभ्यं वोचम् । ब्रवीमि । इन्द्र एव विशेष्यते । स्वयशसे स्वकीययशोयुक्ताय । तथा दिवे उत त्वदाश्रयभूताय द्युलोकदेवताया अपि तत्तादृशं कर्म वोचम् । ब्रवीमि । उतशब्दोऽपिशब्दार्थः । वर्षणकर्मणो द्युदेवताया आनुकूल्यात्तस्या अपि वचनं युक्तम् । तथा रुद्राय जगतां दुःखद्रावयित्रे रोदनशीलाय वाग्नये तद्वोचम् । रुद्रो वै क्रूरो यदयमग्निरिति श्रुतेः रुद्रत्वम् । [small type, doubtful:] रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वम् । तै. सं. १-५-१-१ [?] इति श्रुतेः । रोदनस्वभावत्वं प्रसिद्धम् । तस्य चापि द्वारा वृष्ट्यनुकूलत्वात्तस्यापि कथनं युक्तम् । स्वयशस इत्यस्य रुद्रायेत्यनेन वा सम्बन्धः सन्निहितत्वाद्द्योर्गृह्यत्वाच्च । स्वकीययशोयुक्ताय [?] । तथा मित्राय अहरभिमानिदेवतायै तद्वोचम् । वरुणाय रात्र्यभिमानिदेवतायै तद्वोचम् । अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणौ । ताण्ड्य… १३-१०-१० [?] अहोरात्राभ्यां खलु वै पर्जन्यो वर्षति । तै. सं. … इति तथा मैत्रं वा अहर्वारुणी रात्रिरित्यादिश्रुतिभ्यो मित्रावरुणयोरहोरात्राभिमानिदेवत्वम् । अत एव श्रुतेर्वृष्टिप्रदात्वात्ताभ्यामपि प्रार्थनं युक्तम् । सुमृळीकाय शोभनसुखयित्रे प्रजानाम् । एतत्सर्वत्र सम्बध्यते । उक्तेभ्यो देवेभ्यः सप्रथः सर्वतः पृथिवीविस्तीर्णं यथा भवति तथा तद्वर्षणकर्म ब्रवीमि ॥

yathā śūraḥ kaścidbalavantaṃ gacchantaṃ vairiṇaṃ nigṛhya svīkaroti tadvadityarthaḥ | tathā martyaṃ maraṇaśīlaṃ śīryamāṇasvabhāvaṃ nirudakaṃ kaṃcinmeghaṃ parivṛṇakṣi | sarvato varjayasi | audāsīnyaṃ karoṣītyarthaḥ | he indra tādṛśaṃ karma varṣaṇarūpaṃ saprathaḥ sarvataḥ pṛthu yathā bhavati tathā tubhyaṃ vocam | bravīmi | indra eva viśeṣyate | svayaśase svakīyayaśoyuktāya | tathā dive uta tvadāśrayabhūtāya dyulokadevatāyā api tattādṛśaṃ karma vocam | bravīmi | utaśabdo 'piśabdārthaḥ | varṣaṇakarmaṇo dyudevatāyā ānukūlyāttasyā api vacanaṃ yuktam | tathā rudrāya jagatāṃ duḥkhadrāvayitre rodanaśīlāya vāgnaye tadvocam | rudro vai krūro yadayamagniriti śruteḥ rudratvam | [small type, doubtful:] rorūyamāṇo dravatīti rudrasya rudratvam | tai. saṃ. 1-5-1-1 [?] iti śruteḥ | rodanasvabhāvatvaṃ prasiddham | tasya cāpi dvārā vṛṣṭyanukūlatvāttasyāpi kathanaṃ yuktam | svayaśasa ityasya rudrāyetyanena vā sambandhaḥ sannihitatvāddyorgṛhyatvācca | svakīyayaśoyuktāya [?] | tathā mitrāya aharabhimānidevatāyai tadvocam | varuṇāya rātryabhimānidevatāyai tadvocam | ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇau | tāṇḍya… 13-10-10 [?] ahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣati | tai. saṃ. … iti tathā maitraṃ vā aharvāruṇī rātrirityādiśrutibhyo mitrāvaruṇayorahorātrābhimānidevatvam | ata eva śrutervṛṣṭipradātvāttābhyāmapi prārthanaṃ yuktam | sumṛḷīkāya śobhanasukhayitre prajānām | etatsarvatra sambadhyate | uktebhyo devebhyaḥ saprathaḥ sarvataḥ pṛthivīvistīrṇaṃ yathā bhavati tathā tadvarṣaṇakarma bravīmi ‖

Read from the image; the Śruti quotations in this long small-type passage (the Rudra etymology, the Tāṇḍya and Taittirīya references "१३-१०-१०", "१-५-१-१") are partly illegible and are given only as read, with [?]: I do not claim them. Sense: "O Indra, you are dasma — destroyer of enemies; therefore you pierce (pinvasi) any cloud, which by itself is of a raining nature, covered (tvacam) as with a skin — wrapped in water like a bundle — and make it pour; and any cloud of the nature of a mortal, i.e. going, moving, you, O hero, mix (yāvīḥ): you make it rain by force, though it goes on without raining; as a hero seizes a strong enemy who goes by and takes him, so also the mortal cloud — dying, wasting away without water — you avoid altogether (parivṛṇakṣi), i.e. you are indifferent to it. O Indra, I tell you (vocam) such a deed, the raining, saprathaḥ — so that it becomes widely spread; to Indra himself (svayaśase — the self-glorious); and also to heaven (dive), the deity of the heaven world that is your support; the word uta has the sense of api; since the work of raining is helped by the deity of heaven, speaking to heaven also is proper; and to Rudra, the one who makes the world's sorrows flee, the crier, or Agni (the Śruti: 'Rudra is cruel; this is Agni'); and to Mitra, the deity of the day, and to Varuṇa, the deity of the night ('Mitra and Varuṇa are day and night'; 'by day and night Parjanya rains'); and to sumṛḷīka, the giver of good happiness to the people: this is connected with each. To these gods I tell this deed of raining, so that it spreads widely over the earth."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (he indra — O Indra; tvam — you); dasmaḥ hi — the destroyer of enemies, therefore; vṛṣaṇam — raining by nature; tvacam — covered (with a skin of water); kaṃ cit — some cloud; pinvasi sma — you pierce and make it rain; martyam — like a man; arum — going (a cloud that goes without raining); śūra — O hero; yāvīḥ — you mix (make it rain); martyam — like a mortal (without water); pari vṛṇakṣi — you leave indifferently; he indra — O Indra; tat — that deed of rain; saprathaḥ — so that it is renowned everywhere; tubhyam — to you; vocam — I tell; (tathā — likewise); svayaśase — to you, endowed with your own glory; dive uta — to the deity of the heaven world; tat — that deed; vocam — I tell; svayaśase — endowed with own glory; Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 29 Sū. 129" [as read: "೧೯"].

original p. 378

rudrāya — to Agni (Rudra), remover of the world's sorrows; (vocam — I tell); mitrāya — to Mitra (the deity of the day); varuṇāya — to Varuṇa (the deity of the night); (vocam — I tell); sumṛḷīkāya — to the giver of happiness and delight to the people (to each of the gods stated above); saprathaḥ — so that it becomes renowned everywhere; (vocam — I tell).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra, destroyer of enemies, you pierce the skin of a cloud that holds the rain; you overtake the cloud that moves on (to make it rain); the one without water you leave aside with indifference; O Indra, I tell this deed of rain so that it is known everywhere; to the deity of the heaven world, who gives the people happiness and delight, to Rudra (Agni), the remover of sorrow, to Mitra (of the day) and Varuṇa (of the night), I make known your deed of raining.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed, beginning in lower case): "you, the subduer (of adversaries), piercest every rain (confining) skin; you overtake, hero, every flying mortal (cloud), and abandone [sic] (it) when exhausted (of its water); for such glorious deed, Indra, I offer praise to your [sic]; to heaven; to the self-glorifying Rudra; to Mitra; (to each) the benefactor (of mankind) for such glorious (deed)."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).

dasmo vṛṣaṇaṃ tvacaṃ kaṃ cit pinvasi — śatrūṇām upakṣapaṇakartā | svataḥ varṣaṇaśīlaṃ puṭabandhanavad udakaveṣṭanavantaṃ jaladhāriṇaṃ megham nirbhidya secayati: "Indra, the subduer of enemies, pierces the cloud, which holds water enclosed round it like a rampart round a city; though it is by nature a raining thing, Indra sends it to rain as a cloud pours its rain": so the meaning.

arum martyaṃ yāvīḥ — martyavad gamanaśīlaṃ kaṃcin megham miśrayasi: "as a man who has no object wanders about without purpose, there is a cloud wandering about; Indra compels the cloud by force and makes it pour rain, even from the cloud that gives no rain": so the meaning. By this the worldly custom is described in Indra's case, namely that a hero, seeing his strong enemy moving about of his own will, seizes him and keeps him under his control.

original p. 379

martyaṃ parivṛṇakṣi — maraṇaśīlaṃ śīryamāṇasvabhāvaṃ kaṃcin meghaṃ nirudakaṃ sarvato varjayasi audāsīnyaṃ karoṣi: the word martya is recorded among the names of men (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೮"). "When a cloud has no water and is perishing by itself, Indra does nothing at all about it, he remains indifferent": so the meaning.

saprathaḥ — sarvataḥ pṛthu yathā bhavati tathā: "I shall praise Indra so that it may be in every way exceeding": the word is used as an adverb. Explaining the meaning sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ (Ni. 6-[?]; as read "೬-೮"), the Niruktakāra cites —

त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असि जुष्टो होता वरेण्यः । त्वया यज्ञं वि तन्वते ॥

tvam agne saprathā asi juṣṭo hotā vareṇyaḥ | tvayā yajñaṃ vi tanvate ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-14-4 [?], as read "೩-೧೪-೪".) and —

योना [?] पृथिवि भवानृक्षरा निवेशनी । यच्छा नः शर्म सप्रथः ॥

yonā [?] pṛthivi bhavānṛkṣarā niveśanī | yacchā naḥ śarma saprathaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-15, as read; the first word of the first line is printed "ಸೋನಾ" and I give it as read: [?].) Yāska cites these Ṛks for this meaning.

dive uta tat vocam — dyulokadevatāyai api tvadāśrayabhūtāyai tādṛśaṃ karma bravīmi: "the heaven-world is protected through Indra's support, and the work of raining done by Indra is favourable to the deity of heaven; therefore the ṛṣi of the mantra says that he will make Indra's deed known (to her too)."

rudrāya — jagatāṃ duḥkhadrāvayitre rodanaśīlāya vā agnaye tat vocam: "He explains the word rudra as 'one who makes sorrow flee' or 'one given to weeping', and says that Agni is meant by the word rudra. That Rudra is Agni is stated in Tai. Saṃ. 5-2-3-2 [?, as read "೬-೨-೩-೨"], and that Rudra wept in Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-1-1 [?], in the sentences 'rudro vai krūro yad ayam agniḥ' and 'so 'rodīd yad arodīt tad rudrasya rudratvam' (he wept; that is the Rudra-ness of Rudra)." Because Agni, by offering the oblations, is favourable to the work of raining, and because he is renowned for the greatness of his work, it is proper to tell Agni of the raining deed that Indra performs. This clearer printing corrects the garbled small-type reading of the Rudra quotation on p. 377: the Śruti words are "rudro vai krūro yad ayam agniḥ" and "so 'rodīd yad arodīt tad rudrasya rudratvam". By saying that Rudra and Agni are not different, Rudra too is described as svayaśas, "possessing his own glory".

mitrāya varuṇāya tad vocam — aharabhimānidevatāyai rātryabhimānidevatāyai: Mitra is the deity of the day, Varuṇa the deity of the night: "ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇau" (Tāṇḍya Br. 25-10-10 [?], as read "೨೫-೧೦-೧೦" or "೨೩-…"), "maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ" (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-7-3 [?]); from these Śruti sentences Mitra and Varuṇa are known as the deities of day and night;

original p. 380

well known. "ahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣati" (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-7-3 [?]): by this sentence it is said that the rain comes from these deities, the deities of day and night. It is described here that it is proper to make known the deeds of Indra to Mitra and Varuṇa, the givers of rain.

sumṛḷīkāya saprathaḥ — "Indra's rain-favouring deeds will be described at length to all the deities who bring great happiness to the people": so he explains.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). dasmaḥ — root dasu upakṣaye; iṣiyudhīndhidabhi… [as printed] (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives makan; acute on the last syllable by the suffix's accent. pinvasi — root pivi secane, bhvādi; idito num dhātoḥ gives num; laṭ second person singular, sip, śap; because of hi [the particle] hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34) forbids nighāta; the root's accent remains because śap and sip are p-marked. yāvīḥ — root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6) gives luṅ in the present sense; second person singular sip; itaś ca drops its i; cli is replaced by siṭ; the augment iṭ by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ; astisico 'prkte (Pā. 7-3-96) gives īṭ to the suffix; sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. 7-2-1) gives vṛddhi of the root's u; iṭa īṭi (Pā. 8-2-28) drops sic; āv substitution; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi — no augment aṭ; tiṅ-nighāta. arum — root ṛ gatau; ārter ruḥ [as read: Uṇ. 4-[?]] gives ru; guṇa with raparatva; acute on the first syllable of the suffix. parivṛṇakṣi — root vṛjī varjane, rudhādi; laṭ second person singular, sip; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam (Pā. 3-1-78) gives śnam, which, being m-marked, comes after the last vowel; coḥ kuḥ gives k for the j of the root, ś…; ṣatva for the s; since cādilope vibhāṣā (Pā. 8-1-63) forbids nighāta, the vikaraṇa's accent remains; tiṅ ca… [as read: tiṅ codāttavati, Pā. 8-1-71] gives nighāta of the preverb (pari).

original p. 381

Grammar, concluded. dive — ūḍidaṃ padādi (Pā. 6-1-171) gives the acute to the dative ending. rudrāya — rodayatīti rudraḥ; root rudir aśruvimocane; roder ṇilug ca (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives rak, with luk of ṇi; because of this no guṇa by pratyayalakṣaṇa; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. svayaśase — svīyaṃ yaśo yasya saḥ svayaśāḥ, tasmai; in the bahuvrīhi the accent of the first member remains. vocam — root brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; the Vedic luṅ in the present sense; bruvo vaciḥ (Pā. 2-4-53) gives the substitute vac; asti-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ (Pā. 3-1-52) gives aṅ for cli; vaca um gives the augment um; when it comes after the last vowel, guṇa; tiṅ-nighāta. saprathaḥ — root pratha prakhyāne, suffix asun; prathasā saha vartata iti saprathaḥ; tena saheti tulyayoge (Pā. 2-2-28) makes the compound; vopasarjanasya (Pā. 6-3-82) gives sa in place of saha; kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara. sumṛḷīkāya — nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the acute on the last syllable of the latter member; dative singular. ‖ 3 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ Read from the image; the first line begins "asmākaṃ va indram uśmasīṣṭaye"; the second line is printed "asmākaṃ brahmotayevā pṛtsuṣu kāsu cit" — the division "brahmotaye 'vā" is mine and doubtful until the Pada is read: [?]. The Pada is on the next page.

अस्माकं व इन्द्रमुश्मसीष्टये सखायं विश्वायुं प्रासहं युजं वाजेषु प्रासहं युजम् । अस्माकं ब्रह्मोतयेऽवा पृत्सुषु कासु चित् [?] । नहि त्वा शत्रुः स्तरते स्तृणोषि यं विश्वं शत्रुं स्तृणोषि यम् ॥ ४ ॥

asmākaṃ va indramuśmasīṣṭaye sakhāyaṃ viśvāyuṃ prāsahaṃ yujaṃ vājeṣu prāsahaṃ yujam | asmākaṃ brahmotaye 'vā pṛtsuṣu kāsu cit [?] | nahi tvā śatruḥ starate stṛṇoṣi yaṃ viśvaṃ śatruṃ stṛṇoṣi yam ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Read from the image; a few letters are doubtful, in particular the clause on brahma parivṛḍhaṃ karma and "hiṃsati"/"virodham ācarati": [?]. Sense: "O priests, for the sake of ourselves and of you, for the sacrifice (iṣṭaye) or for the attainment of the desired, we desire (uśmasi) Indra — we wish for what is wished. [Grammar: root vaś kāntau, adādi; masi with iṭ; saṃprasāraṇa by grahijyā…]. Or, 'our friend' is the connection: what Indra? sakhāyam — a very beneficent friend, or of the same renown; viśvāyum — the goer to all sacrifices; prāsaham — the great endurer of enemies; yujam — always joined, helping; again, in the food-oblations (vājeṣu) or in the sacrifices that have them, prāsaham — overcoming those who spoil the sacrifice; yujam — joined with desired fruits, or with the Maruts. And, O Indra, for our protection (ūtaye) protect (ava) our great rite (brahma). Where in particular? In whatever battles (pṛtsu, recorded among names of battle): in them no enemy harms you; whichever enemy you oppose you ward off: not any enemy harms you: by your greatness all are afraid and become obedient; no one takes up enmity, since you are without a born enemy."

हे ऋत्विजः अस्माकमस्मदर्थं वो युष्मदर्थं चेष्टये यागायाभिमतप्राप्तये वेन्द्रमुश्मसि । अभिमतं कामयामहे ॥ वश कान्तौ । अदादिकः । इदन्तो मसिः । ग्रहिज्यादिना सम्प्रसारणम् ॥ यद्वा । अस्माकं सखायमिति सम्बन्धः । कीदृशमिन्द्रम् । सखायं सखिवदत्यन्तहितकारिणं समानख्यानं वा । विश्वायुं विश्वेषां यागानां गन्तारं प्रासहं प्रकर्षेण शत्रूणां मर्षयितारम् । सहेः क्विप् । नहिवृत्यादिनोपसर्गस्य दीर्घः ॥ युजं सर्वदा युक्तं सहायभूतमित्यर्थः । पुनः स एव विशेष्यते । वाजेषु हविरूपान्नेषु तद्वत्सु यज्ञेषु वा निमित्तभूतेषु प्रासहं यज्ञविघातिनः सहमानं युजमभिमतफलैर्युक्तं मरुद्भिर्वा । किंच हे इन्द्र अस्माकमूतये रक्षणाय ब्रह्म परिवृढं कर्माव । रक्ष । कुत्र विशेष इति तदाह । कासु चित् पृत्सु सङ्ग्रामेषु । पृत्सु समत्सु सङ्ग्रामनामसु पाठात् । तेषु त्वां शत्रुर्नहि स्तरते न हिनस्ति । स विरोधमाचरति । यं विश्वं शत्रुं स्तृणोषि वारयसि स कश्चिदपि शत्रुर्न हिनस्ति । तव माहात्म्येन सर्वे भीता विधेया भवन्ति शत्रुभावं न कोऽप्याचरति । अजातशत्रुत्वादित्यर्थः ॥

he ṛtvijaḥ asmākamasmadarthaṃ vo yuṣmadarthaṃ ceṣṭaye yāgāyābhimataprāptaye vendramuśmasi | abhimataṃ kāmayāmahe ‖ vaśa kāntau | adādikaḥ | idanto masiḥ | grahijyādinā samprasāraṇam ‖ yadvā | asmākaṃ sakhāyamiti sambandhaḥ | kīdṛśamindram | sakhāyaṃ sakhivadatyantahitakāriṇaṃ samānakhyānaṃ vā | viśvāyuṃ viśveṣāṃ yāgānāṃ gantāraṃ prāsahaṃ prakarṣeṇa śatrūṇāṃ marṣayitāram | saheḥ kvip | nahivṛtyādinopasargasya dīrghaḥ ‖ yujaṃ sarvadā yuktaṃ sahāyabhūtamityarthaḥ | punaḥ sa eva viśeṣyate | vājeṣu havirūpānneṣu tadvatsu yajñeṣu vā nimittabhūteṣu prāsahaṃ yajñavighātinaḥ sahamānaṃ yujamabhimataphalairyuktaṃ marudbhirvā | kiṃca he indra asmākamūtaye rakṣaṇāya brahma parivṛḍhaṃ karmāva | rakṣa | kutra viśeṣa iti tadāha | kāsu cit pṛtsu saṅgrāmeṣu | pṛtsu samatsu saṅgrāmanāmasu pāṭhāt | teṣu tvāṃ śatrurnahi starate na hinasti | sa virodhamācarati | yaṃ viśvaṃ śatruṃ stṛṇoṣi vārayasi sa kaścidapi śatrurna hinasti | tava māhātmyena sarve bhītā vidheyā bhavanti śatrubhāvaṃ na ko 'pyācarati | ajātaśatrutvādityarthaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (he ṛtvijaḥ — O priests); asmākam — our (and); vaḥ — your; iṣṭaye — for the sake of the sacrifice (for the desired object); sakhāyam — as a friend (beneficent); viśvāyum — who goes to the sacrifices of all; prāsaham — the able endurer of enemies; yujam — always together (helper); vājeṣu — in the sacrifice of food in the form of oblations; prāsaham — destroyer of the spoilers of the sacrifice; yujam — joined with desired fruit (with the Maruts); indram — Indra; uśmasi — we desire; (kiṃ ca indra — and, O Indra); asmākam — our; ūtaye —

original p. 383

for protection; brahma — the great rite; ava — protect; why: yam — whom; stṛṇoṣi — you ward off; (saḥ — he); kāsu cit pṛtsuṣu — in all battles; tvā — you; na hi starate — he does not harm; yam — whichever; viśvaṃ śatrum — all enemies; stṛṇoṣi — you oppose; (saḥ — that) śatruḥ — enemy; na hinasti — does not harm you.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O priests, let us desire at our and your sacrifices Indra, who like a friend is beneficent, goes to all sacrifices, is able to endure enemies, is always at hand as a helper, destroys the foes in the food-oblation sacrifices, and is endowed with the desired fruit (accompanied by the Maruts). O Indra, protect this rite of ours (since the enemy warded off by you does not harm you in any battle, does not stand against you; and no enemy you oppose can harm you — you are without a born enemy).

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "We desire, (priests), Indra to be present at your sacrifice, (he who is) our friend, the [sic: "the the"] frequenter of all (ceremonies), the endurer (of enemies), the ally (of his worshippers), the patient expecter of (sacrificial) viands, associated (with the Maruts); Indra, guard our holy rite for our preservation, for in whatsoever contests (you may engage), no enemy, whom you oppose prevails against you; you prevail over every enemy whom (you oppose)."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).

iṣṭaye — yāgāya abhimatāya vā: the ṛṣi who saw the mantra says, "we desire Indra for the priests in the sacrifice, for the sacrificers, for the completion of the sacrifice, and for the fulfilment of what is desired."

sakhāyam — sakhivad atyantahitakāriṇaṃ samānakhyānaṃ vā: "Indra does good to the sacrificers, or gives the sacrificers a renown equal to his own": so the meaning.

prāsahaṃ vājeṣu prāsaham — prakarṣeṇa śatrūṇāṃ marṣayitāraṃ haviḥrūpānneṣu tadvatsu yajñeṣu vā nimittabhūteṣu yajñavighātinaḥ sahamānam: "for the sake of the food-oblations and the sacrifices accompanied by the oblations, he who strongly subdues the enemies,

original p. 384

who spoil the sacrifice, and prevents them from fulfilling their wishes": so the meaning is explained.

yujam — abhimataphalaiḥ marudbhir vā yuktam: "Indra gives the sacrificers the desired fruit, or is joined with the Maruts"; and asmākam ūtaye brahma parivṛḍhaṃ karmāva — rakṣa — "May Indra protect the rite, the sacrifice, which we perform for our protection": so he prays.

pṛtsu — saṅgrāmeṣu: the word pṛtsu is recorded among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"): "battle".

yaṃ viśvaṃ śatruṃ stṛṇoṣi (kiṃ ca) yaṃ tvā śatruḥ nahi starate — "In battles no one acts as an opponent of Indra. Because Indra subdues enemies in the battles, the enemy is not able to strike Indra. By Indra's greatness all are afraid and become obedient to him. Because there is no enemy at all, Indra is ajātaśatru (one who has no enemy born), and so no one takes up the attitude of an enemy toward Indra": so Indra's greatness is described.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). uśmasi — root vaśa kāntau, adādi; laṭ first person plural, suffix mas; idanto masi (Pā. 7-1-46) gives iṭ; since the suffix is sārvadhātukam apit [i.e. ṅit-like], grahijyāvayi… (Pā. 6-1-16) gives saṃprasāraṇa and pūrvarūpa to the root; the form uśmasi; because it follows a finite verb nighāta. iṣṭaye — root yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; the suffix ktic; vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti (Pā. 6-1-15) gives saṃprasāraṇa, pūrvarūpa; vraścabhrasja… (Pā. 8-2-36) gives ṣ for the j; because of it ṣṭutva of the suffix; since c-marked the acute on the last syllable. prāsaham — root ṣaha marṣaṇe; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ gives s; kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76) gives kvip; nahivṛtivṛṣivyadhi… (Pā. 6-3-116) gives lengthening of the preposition when it follows; kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara; accusative singular.

original p. 385

yujam — root yujir yoge; ṛtvigdadhṛk… (Pā. 3-2-59) gives kvin. ūtaye — ūtiyūtijūti… (Pā. 3-3-97) is irregularly formed with the acute on the last syllable (kṛdanta); dative singular. starate — root stṛ hiṃsāyām; laṭ third person singular; since hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34) forbids nighāta, and since the lasārvadhātuka is unaccented by tāsyanudāttenṅidvidāder… (Pā. 6-1-186), the root's accent remains. stṛṇoṣi — root stṛñ ācchādane, svādi; laṭ second person singular; because it follows a finite verb, nighāta is forbidden; since the suffix is p-marked the accent of the vikaraṇa remains. ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 5; read from the image; a few letters of the small type are doubtful: [?]. Sense: "O Indra, bend down thoroughly — ni ṣū nama, make bow to us — the enemy atimati ('of excessive or hostile mind') of any (kayasya cit) sacrificer devoted to you. [This root has the causative sense hidden in it.] O fierce (ugra) Indra, of mighty strength, endowed with protections or affection, by your radiant (tejiṣṭhābhiḥ) ways such as war, as by paths: as you bent down Vṛtra and the like, so bend the one who is hostile to us. Or taking with what follows: as you have yoked us to the paths of sacrifice that are full of splendour, so lead us (neṣi) by your shining protections, the fruit of the sacrifice, to the desired heaven and the like. Example: as in former times you led our fathers and the others by your protections; so now. O brave one, you are anenāḥ — known by all as sinless, since you give heaven and what is desired; or, you think us sinless. And O Indra, as the vahni — sustaining the world by giving rain and so on — you remove all the sins of pūru, i.e. man, the sacrificer (the word pūru is recorded among the names of man — pūravo jagataḥ); you protect him. Therefore, coming facing us, near, at the sacrificial place, as bearer of what is wished, you remove what is not wished and fulfil what is wished."

हे इन्द्र कयस्य कस्य चित् त्वद्भक्तस्य यजमानस्यातिमतिमतिक्रान्तमननं विरुद्धमनस्कं शत्रुं नि षू नम । नितरां सुष्ठु नामय । अस्मत्प्रणतं कुरु ॥ अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थोऽयम् ॥ हे उग्र उद्गूर्णबल ऊतिभी रक्षणैः प्रीतिभिर्वा युक्तः सन् तेजिष्ठाभिररणिभिर्नातिशयेन तेजस्विभिर्युद्धादिरूपैर्मार्गैरिव ॥ तेजस्वच्छब्दादतिशायनिक इष्ठन् । विन्मतोर्लुक् । टेरिति टिलोपः ॥ अतिमतिं वृत्रादिं यथा नामितवान् तथास्मद्विरोधिनमप्रीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । उत्तरान्वयः । तेजिष्ठाभिररणिभिर्न तेजोयुक्तैर्गमनसाधनैर्यज्ञादिमार्गैर्यथास्मान्योजितवानसि तथोग्राभिः प्रकाशकाभिरूतिभी रक्षणैर्यागफलभूतैर्नोऽस्मान्नेषि । नयसि । अभिमतस्वर्गादिफलं प्रापयसीत्यर्थः ॥ नयतेश्छान्दसः शपो लुक् ॥ तत्र दृष्टान्तः । पुरा पूर्वस्मिन् काले अस्मत्पित्रादीन् [?] ऊतिभिर्नीतवानसि । तथा नेतीत्यर्थः । हे शूर विक्रान्त त्वमनेना मन्यसे । सर्वैरपापत्वेनावबुध्यसे । स्वर्गाद्यभिमतसाधकत्वादिति भावः । यद्वा । अनेना अस्मानेनसो मन्यसे । किंच हे इन्द्र वह्निर्वृष्ट्यादिप्रदानेन जगतां निर्वाहकः सन् पूरोर्मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य । पूरुरिति मनुष्यनाम पूरवो जगत इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तस्य विश्वानि सर्वाण्येनांस्यप पर्षि । अपकृष्य पालयसि । पृणोतेश्छान्दसः शपो लुक् ॥ अतो नोऽस्माकमप्यासान्तिके देवयजनदेशेऽच्छाभिमुख्येनागत्य वह्निरभिमतानां वोढा सन्ननभिमतमपकृष्याभिमतं पूरयसि ॥

he indra kayasya kasya cit tvadbhaktasya yajamānasyātimatimatikrāntamananaṃ viruddhamanaskaṃ śatruṃ ni ṣū nama | nitarāṃ suṣṭhu nāmaya | asmatpraṇataṃ kuru ‖ antarbhāvitaṇyartho 'yam ‖ he ugra udgūrṇabala ūtibhī rakṣaṇaiḥ prītibhirvā yuktaḥ san tejiṣṭhābhiraraṇibhirnātiśayena tejasvibhiryuddhādirūpairmārgairiva ‖ tejasvacchabdādatiśāyanika iṣṭhan | vinmatorluk | ṭeriti ṭilopaḥ ‖ atimatiṃ vṛtrādiṃ yathā nāmitavān tathāsmadvirodhinamaprītyarthaḥ | yadvā | uttarānvayaḥ | tejiṣṭhābhiraraṇibhirna tejoyuktairgamanasādhanairyajñādimārgairyathāsmānyojitavānasi tathogrābhiḥ prakāśakābhirūtibhī rakṣaṇairyāgaphalabhūtairno 'smānneṣi | nayasi | abhimatasvargādiphalaṃ prāpayasītyarthaḥ ‖ nayateśchāndasaḥ śapo luk ‖ tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | purā pūrvasmin kāle asmatpitrādīn [?] ūtibhirnītavānasi | tathā netītyarthaḥ | he śūra vikrānta tvamanenā manyase | sarvairapāpatvenāvabudhyase | svargādyabhimatasādhakatvāditi bhāvaḥ | yadvā | anenā asmānenaso manyase | kiṃca he indra vahnirvṛṣṭyādipradānena jagatāṃ nirvāhakaḥ san pūrormanuṣyasya yajamānasya | pūruriti manuṣyanāma pūravo jagata iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tasya viśvāni sarvāṇyenāṃsyapa parṣi | apakṛṣya pālayasi | pṛṇoteśchāndasaḥ śapo luk ‖ ato no 'smākamapyāsāntike devayajanadeśe 'cchābhimukhyenāgatya vahnirabhimatānāṃ voḍhā sannanabhimatamapakṛṣyābhimataṃ pūrayasi ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. ugra — O fierce Indra; kayasya cit — (of your devotee) the sacrificer; atimatim — the hostile-minded one (enemy); ūtibhiḥ — by your protections; tejiṣṭhābhiḥ — by the exceedingly brilliant; araṇibhiḥ na — (like) the paths (of war and the like); ni ṣū nama — bend well, make him bow; tejiṣṭhābhiḥ — splendid; araṇibhiḥ na — as by means of going (the paths of sacrifice, in which you set us); ugrābhiḥ — shining; ūtibhiḥ — by protections (the fruits of sacrifice); naḥ — us; purā — formerly (our fathers and the rest); yathā — as (you protected and led); (tathā — so); neṣi — lead us (so that we obtain heaven and the like); śūra — O hero; anenāḥ — sinless; manyase — you are known; anenāḥ — you who are sinless; manyase — you think (us too sinless); (indra — O Indra); vahniḥ — the sustainer of the world by rain and the like; pūroḥ — of the man (the sacrificer); viśvāni — all (sins); apa parṣi — you remove, protect; (ataḥ — therefore); naḥ — for us; āsā — near (at the sacrificial hall); accha — facing (coming); vahniḥ — the bearer of the desired; (apa parṣi — you remove the undesired and protect). Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 18 [as read: "೧೮"].

original p. 387

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O fierce Indra, by your protecting acts, as by the fierce paths of war, make the enemies of the sacrificer bow down; as formerly you led our fathers and the others by your shining protections that are the fruit of the sacrifice, so now grant us the desired heaven and the like; all call you the heroic, sinless one; you, sinless, regard us too as sinless. O Indra, sustainer of the world by rain and the like, you remove all the sins of the sacrificer and protect him; therefore come near our sacrificial hall, bearing what we desire, and, removing the undesired, guard us.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Humble the adversary of every one (your worshipper), fierce (Indra), by your aids, like radiant paths, (to glory); by your powerful aids, guide us, hero, as you have guided our forefather, for you are honoured (by all). You, (Indra), who are the sustainer (of the world), remove all (the sins) of man: present at our sacrifice, you are the bearer (of good things)."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).

kayasya cit atimatiṃ ni ṣū nama — kasyacit tvadbhaktasya yajamānasya viruddhamanaskaṃ śatruṃ asmatpraṇataṃ kuru: the ṛṣi prays Indra to make hostile, ill-minded one — an enemy like one who acts contrary to a sacrificer devoted to him and eager to win his favour — obedient to the sacrificer.

ūtibhiḥ tejiṣṭhābhir araṇebhir na — this sentence is given as an illustration of how an enemy is made obedient. Sāyaṇa gives two meanings for it. In one: Indra, endowed with complete strength, with the many splendid means (war and the rest) by which he protects those who depend on him, and with affection toward them, subdued Vṛtra and others who acted contrary to the world; so he is asked to subdue the opponents of the sacrificers. In the second meaning, he is asked to protect us who sacrifice with his shining protections, in whom he has made the sacrificers eager in the performance of sacrifices that give an excellent course by greatly increasing splendour; and to grant us the fruit of the sacrifice, our desired attainment of heaven and the like.

original p. 388

purā yathā — this clause too is given in the manner of an illustration: as Indra formerly protected the fathers and others of the sacrificers and brought about their desired attainments, so now may he fulfil our wishes.

anenāḥ manyase — sarvair apāpatvena avabudhyase yadvā anenāḥ tvam asmān anenaso manyase: "Indra is known as great and sinless, because he accomplishes the merits such as heaven according to the sacrificers' wishes; or: Indra regards the sacrificers who satisfy him by sacrificing as sinless." The word anenāḥ is repeated and is used as an epithet of Indra and of the sacrificers respectively, so that these two meanings can be given.

vahnir pūroḥ viśvāni enāṃsi apa parṣi — vṛṣṭyādipradānena jagatāṃ nirvāhakaḥ san yajamānasya sarvāṇi enāṃsi apakṛṣya pālayasi: the word vahni is applied to Indra; he is described as one who carries on the work of protecting the world by giving rain and what dependants need; and it is said that, to protect the sacrificer, he removes all his sins.

The word pūru is recorded among the names of men (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೮"). And —

प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचन्ते । वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वाँ अधूनोत्काष्ठा अव शम्बरं भेत् ॥

pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacante | vaiśvānaro dasyum agnir jaghanvām̐ adhūnot kāṣṭhā ava śambaraṃ bhet ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6, as printed.) In this Ṛk the Niruktakāra explains pūravaḥ as pūrayitavyāḥ manuṣyāḥ (Ni. 7-[?]; as read "೭-೨೩"): "men who are to be filled".

āsā — āsāt is recorded among the names of near (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೯"): "near, in the place of divine worship."

naḥ āsā accha — abhimukhenāgatyābhimatānāṃ voḍhā san anabhimatam apakṛṣya abhimataṃ pūrayasi: "Indra comes to the place of the sacrifice, to accomplish the wishes of the priests and sacrificers, removes their unwished things and fulfils their wishes": so the meaning. Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 18 [as read].

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). nama — root ṇamu prahvatve; ṇo naḥ (Pā. 6-1-65) gives n for the first letter; since the causative sense is hidden in the root, loṭ second person singular gives the form nama. atimatim — atikrāntā matir yasmāt saḥ atimatiḥ, tam; in the bahuvrīhi the accent of the first member remains. tejiṣṭhābhiḥ — tejo 'sya asti iti tejasvī; asmāyāmedhāsrajo viniḥ (Pā. 5-2-121) gives vini; atiśayena tejasvī tejiṣṭhaḥ; when excess is meant, atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau (Pā. 5-3-55) gives iṣṭhan; with it following, vinmator luk (Pā. 5-3-65) drops vin; ṭeḥ (Pā. 6-4-155) drops ṭi; ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the acute on the first syllable; feminine ṭāp; instrumental plural. ugrābhiḥ — root uca samavāye; ujjer ndra… [as read: ucer rak, Uṇ. 2-[?]] gives the suffix ran by irregular formation; feminine ṭāp; in ugra the vocative āmantrita-nighāta. neṣi — root ṇīñ prāpaṇe; ṇo naḥ gives n; laṭ second person singular, sip; by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of śap; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa of the root's ī; since it stands at the beginning of the pāda [as read] there is no nighāta; since the suffix is p-marked the root's accent remains. anenāḥ — na vidyate enaḥ yasya saḥ anenāḥ; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the acute on the last syllable of the latter member. manyase — root manu avabodhane, divādi; laṭ second person singular; because of yathā no nighāta; śyan, being n-marked, gives the acute on the first syllable. parṣi — root pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ; laṭ second person singular, sip; by bahulaṃ chandasi the luk of śap; because of sip guṇa of the root; ra follows; because it follows a finite verb, nighāta. ‖ 5 ‖

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

प्र तद्वोचेयं भव्यायेन्दवे हव्यो न य इषवान्मन्म रेजति रक्षोहा मन्म रेजति । स्वयं सो अस्मदा निदो वध्रैरजेत दुर्मतिम् । अव स्रवेदघशंसोऽवतरमव क्षुद्रमिव स्रवेत् ॥ ६ ॥

pra tadvoceyaṃ bhavyāyendave havyo na ya iṣavānmanma rejati rakṣohā manma rejati | svayaṃ so asmadā nido vadhrairajeta durmatim | ava sravedaghaśaṃso 'vataramava kṣudramiva sravet ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image. Ṛk 6 is addressed to Indu, i.e. Soma — the sūkta table gives "Ṛk 6 Indu". Pada: iṣa-vān, rakṣaḥ-hā, aghaśaṃsaḥ, ava-taram, kṣudram-iva.

प्र । तत् । वोचेयम् । भव्याय । इन्दवे । हव्यः । न । यः । इषऽवान् । मन्म । रेजति । रक्षःऽहा । मन्म । रेजति । स्वयम् । सः । अस्मत् । आ । निदः । वध्रैः । अजेत । दुःऽमतिम् । अव । स्रवेत् । अघऽशंसः । अवऽतरम् । अव । क्षुद्रम्ऽइव । स्रवेत् ॥ ६ ॥

pra | tat | voceyam | bhavyāya | indave | havyaḥ | na | yaḥ | iṣa 'vān | manma | rejati | rakṣaḥ 'hā | manma | rejati | svayam | saḥ | asmat | ā | nidaḥ | vadhraiḥ | ajeta | duḥ 'matim | ava | sravet | agha 'śaṃsaḥ | ava 'taram | ava | kṣudram 'iva | sravet ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, some letters doubtful: [?]).

भव्याय भवनशीलाय प्रतिदिनं कलाभिवृद्ध्या वर्धनशीलायेन्दवेऽमृतेन सर्वस्य क्लेदयित्रे तदर्थं तद्वक्ष्यमाणं कर्म स्तोत्रं वा प्र वोचेयम् । प्रकर्षेण वक्तुं शक्तो भूयासम् । स्तुतेरतिमहत्त्वादिति भावः ॥ वचेर्लिङ्याशिष्यङ् [?] । वच उम् ॥ कस्य तदिति । य इन्दुरिषवानेषणवान् मन्म मननीयं स्तोत्रं कर्म वोद्दिश्य रेजति गच्छति । रेजतिर्गत्यर्थः रेजति दभ्रोतीति तन्नामसु पाठात् [?] । आगमने दृष्टान्तः । हव्यो न होतव्य आह्वातव्यो वा हव्य इन्द्र इव । प्रायेणेन्द्र आगच्छेत्यादिनेन्द्र एवाह्वयते । स इव । स एव विशेष्यते । रक्षोहा यज्ञविघातकानां रक्षसां हन्ता मन्म तेषामेव कर्म हननादिरूपं रेजति गच्छति । चालयति नाशयतीत्यर्थः । स एवेन्दुः स्वयं निदः । णिदि कुत्सायाम् । क्विप् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तता ॥ अस्मन्निन्दितुर्वैरिणो वध्रैर्हननोपायैः ॥ हनेर्वध इति भावे [?] । तस्य नियोगेन वधादेशः । न चान्तोऽन्तोदात्तः [?] ॥ दुर्मतिं दुर्बुद्धिमस्मद्द्वेष्टारम् आ अजेत । अक्षिपेत् । आवनयेत् [?] । किंचाघशंसोऽघानां पापानां हिंसादीनां

bhavyāya bhavanaśīlāya pratidinaṃ kalābhivṛddhyā vardhanaśīlāyendave 'mṛtena sarvasya kledayitre tadarthaṃ tadvakṣyamāṇaṃ karma stotraṃ vā pra voceyam | prakarṣeṇa vaktuṃ śakto bhūyāsam | stuteratimahattvāditi bhāvaḥ ‖ vacerliṅyāśiṣyaṅ [?] | vaca um ‖ kasya taditi | ya induriṣavāneṣaṇavān manma mananīyaṃ stotraṃ karma voddiśya rejati gacchati | rejatirgatyarthaḥ rejati dabhrotīti tannāmasu pāṭhāt [?] | āgamane dṛṣṭāntaḥ | havyo na hotavya āhvātavyo vā havya indra iva | prāyeṇendra āgacchetyādinendra evāhvayate | sa iva | sa eva viśeṣyate | rakṣohā yajñavighātakānāṃ rakṣasāṃ hantā manma teṣāmeva karma hananādirūpaṃ rejati gacchati | cālayati nāśayatītyarthaḥ | sa evenduḥ svayaṃ nidaḥ | ṇidi kutsāyām | kvip | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatā ‖ asmanninditurvairiṇo vadhrairhananopāyaiḥ ‖ hanervadha iti bhāve [?] | tasya niyogena vadhādeśaḥ | na cānto 'ntodāttaḥ [?] ‖ durmatiṃ durbuddhimasmaddveṣṭāram ā ajeta | akṣipet | āvanayet [?] | kiṃcāghaśaṃso 'ghānāṃ pāpānāṃ hiṃsādīnāṃ

original p. 391

शंसिता स्तेनोऽवतरमत्यन्तनिकृष्टमव स्वस्थानादवाङ्मुखो भूत्वा स्रवेत् । गच्छतु । अधः पततु इत्यर्थः । अघशंसः स्तेनः अघशंसो वृक इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । अवस्रवणमेव प्रार्थ्यते । क्षुद्रमिव क्षेप्तुं शक्यमुदकादिकमिव । उदकं यथा तिष्ठति प्रवत्नश्यति [?] तथासावित्यर्थः ॥

śaṃsitā steno 'vataramatyantanikṛṣṭamava svasthānādavāṅmukho bhūtvā sravet | gacchatu | adhaḥ patatu ityarthaḥ | aghaśaṃsaḥ stenaḥ aghaśaṃso vṛka iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | avasravaṇameva prārthyate | kṣudramiva kṣeptuṃ śakyamudakādikamiva | udakaṃ yathā tiṣṭhati pravatnaśyati [?] tathāsāvityarthaḥ ‖

Sense: "For Indu — that is, Soma — who is of a nature to come into being, who grows each day by the increase of his phases and moistens everyone with nectar, may I be able to speak (pra voceyam) that rite or praise, to be told now; may I be able to speak it excellently, since praise is of very great (ati-mahat) worth. [Grammar: precative of vac, augment um.] For whom? The Soma-juice that, abounding in food (iṣavān) or desire, rejati — goes toward manma, the praiseworthy hymn or rite; (rejati is a verb of motion). The example of coming: havyo na — like the one to be invoked, Indra: Indra is called with 'come, Indra' and so on; like him. The same is further described: rakṣohā — the killer of the Rākṣasas who harm sacrifices — rejati — sets going, i.e. destroys, their work of killing and the like. May that Soma himself repel by the means of destruction (vadhraiḥ) the enemy who reviles us (nidaḥ), the one with an evil mind. And may the thief (aghaśaṃsaḥ, the 'proclaimer of sins' — the word aghaśaṃsa is recorded among the names of thief and of wolf), go downwards (ava sravet), to the lowest place, from his place, headlong, fall down: this fall is prayed for — as little water, that can be thrown, runs down and is lost."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. yaḥ — which Soma-juice; iṣavān — accompanied by as much food as desired; manma — the praise (the rite), for it; havyaḥ na — like Indra, who is fit for the oblation or who is called; rejati — goes (such); bhavyāya — to the growing; indave — the Soma-juice which moistens all with nectar; tat — that rite; pra voceyam — may I be able to speak much (in praise); rakṣohā — (Indra) the destroyer of the Rākṣasas who harm the sacrifice; manma — their work of killing and the like; rejati — destroys; saḥ — that Soma-juice; nidaḥ — the reviling enemies; durmatim — the evil mind; vadhraiḥ — by means of destruction; asmat — from us; svayam — by itself; ā ajeta — drive away; (kiṃ ca — and); aghaśaṃsaḥ — the thief who proclaims sin; kṣudram — like a little (water); ava sravet iva — as it flows downwards and disappears; avataram — very low; ava sravet — let him go headlong from his place (and perish).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Let us praise the rite of Soma-juice, which goes toward the hymn like Indra who is invoked, giving food without measure, which grows, and is the sustenance of all. Indra destroys the Rākṣasas who harm the sacrifice and brings to naught their acts of violence; and may the Soma-juice itself repel from us, by means of destruction, the evil mind of those who revile us; may the thief who speaks of sin fall headlong and perish, as a little water flows away and disappears.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "May I be competent to utter (praise) for the (Soma) libation, sustaining existence, which, like the (deity) to be invoked, (Indra), goes abounding with food to (each) venerable (rite); the destroyer of Rakshasas at (each) venerable (rite); may that (libation) of itself repress with chastisement the malevolence of him who reviles us: let the thief fall downwards (and) perish), like a little (water) running down (a declivity)." Printed with the unbalanced parentheses as given.

original p. 392

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).

bhavyāya indave tat pra voceyam — bhavanaśīlāya kalābhivṛddhyā pratidinaṃ vardhanaśīlāya amṛtena sarvasya kledayitre vakṣyamāṇaṃ karma stotraṃ vā prakarṣeṇa vaktuṃ śakto bhūyāsam. The Niruktakāra considers the derivation of the word indra: indave dravatīti indraḥ (Ni. 10-8 [?]; as read "೧೦-೮"): indu means Soma; because he runs to drink the Soma-juice he is called Indra. Or, as said, indau ramata iti vā: because he sports in the drinking of Soma. Following this derivation, this Ṛk explains the greatness of Soma and also describes the greatness of Indra, which has to be told in context.

"Soma, who rises on the several days, grows with the increase of his phases, and, giving nectar to all, makes all rejoice — since his (the Soma's) greatness is proposed, the ṛṣi who saw the mantra says: may I be able to explain, in praise or in rite, that which belongs to Soma": so it is described. The Niruktakāra explains the word indu — indur indheḥ undater vā ("indu from indh, to shine, or from und, to moisten"); Durgācārya says the word indu is formed either from the root indhi denoting light or from the root ud denoting moistening, and means "moon". And the Niruktakāra, citing this same Ṛk, explains:

प्रब्रवीमि तद्भव्यायेन्दवे हवनार्ह इव य इषवानन्नवान् कामवान् वा मननानि च नो रेजयति रक्षोहा च बलेन रेजयति स्वयं सोऽस्मदभिनिन्दितारं वध्रैरजेत दुर्मतिम् । अवस्रवेदघशंसः । ततोऽवतरं क्षुद्रमिवावस्रवेत् ॥

prabravīmi tad bhavyāyendave havanārha iva ya iṣavān annavān kāmavān vā mananāni ca no rejayati rakṣohā ca balena rejayati svayaṃ so 'smad abhinindi­tāraṃ vadhrair ajeta durmatim | avasraved aghaśaṃsaḥ | tato 'vataraṃ kṣudram ivāvasravet ‖

Nirukta, as read from the small Kannada type; the passage is doubtful in places: [?]. And he says —

अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते यथाहो दर्शनीयाहो दर्शनीयेति । तत्परुच्छेपस्य शीलम् ॥

abhyāse bhūyāṃsam arthaṃ manyante yathāho darśanīyāho darśanīyeti | tat parucchepasya śīlam ‖

(Ni. 10-43, as read "೧೦-೪೩".) Durgācārya says: "I shall speak words that are dear to Indu: and this utterance too is a means of pleasing the moon; the moon fulfils the wishes of those who desire things."

original p. 393

(Durga's explanation, continued:) "…so one meaning is that he is ātmavān, a thing to be meditated upon, who is to be contemplated only through the oblation; and the second, that he is not to be contemplated since he is not a sharer of oblations." "Like the deity who receives an offering through homa, he is not summoned again by sacrifice: always he possesses food, fulfils the wishes of the desirous, and makes our knowledge grow. But one fears that praising him who turns our minds toward desire is improper. He destroys the Rākṣasas by his power; and, striking those who revile us with the thunderbolt, he conquers them and destroys those of evil mind. He who defames us, though famed in his regions, goes to a low state. As a thing grown in a small measure perishes little by little and wholly disappears, so one of base mind among us goes little by little to a low state." This is the meaning explained. And the Niruktakāra explains that because the ṛṣi Paruccheṣa repeats words, the meaning becomes intensive, with the illustration aho darśanīyā aho darśanīyā ("how beautiful! how beautiful!").

manma — mananīyaṃ stotraṃ karma vā. —

उप प्रागात्सुमन्मे [?] धायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीतपृष्ठः । अन्वेनं विप्रा ऋषयो मदन्ति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबन्धुम् ॥

upa prāgāt sumanme [?] dhāyi manma devānām āśā upa vītapṛṣṭhaḥ | anv enaṃ viprā ṛṣayo madanti devānāṃ puṣṭe cakṛmā subandhum ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೮೩-೨" [?]; small type, doubtful letters: [?].) In this Ṛk the word manma is explained as mananīyam arthajātam — "that which is worthy of meditation".

For the second manma: teṣām eva karma hananādirūpam — "the work of subduing the Rākṣasas who obstruct the sacrifice".

aghaśaṃsaḥ avataram ava sravet — aghānāṃ pāpānāṃ hiṃsādīnāṃ śaṃsitā stenaḥ atyantaniṣkṛṣṭam avāṅmukho bhūtvā adhaḥ patatu: "May the thief who commits sinful acts, violence and the like, go to a lower state than his present one." In this connection he gives the illustration kṣudram iva — kṣeptuṃ śakyam udakādikam iva: "like water that can be thrown away; as water flows from its place little by little and perishes, so may the thief perish."

original p. 394

(Continuing from p. 393:) …"as water goes little by little and perishes, so the thief too": so he explains. The word aghaśaṃsa is recorded among the fourteen names of thief — tṛpuḥ, takvā and so on (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೯"). And —

इन्द्रासोमा समघशंसमभ्यघं तपुर्ययस्तु चरुरग्निवाँ इव । ब्रह्मद्विषे क्रव्यादे घोरचक्षसे द्वेषो धत्तमनवायं किमीदिने ॥

indrāsomā samaghaśaṃsam abhy aghaṃ tapur yayastu carur agnivām̐ iva | brahmadviṣe kravyāde ghoracakṣase dveṣo dhattam anavāyaṃ kimīdine ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-2, as read "೭-೧೦೪-೨".) Citing this Ṛk, Yāska explains the words aghaśaṃsam abhy agham as "aghasya śaṃsitāram, agham hanter nirhasitopasarga āhantīti"; Durgācārya says: aghasya śaṃsitāram — one who praises sins; abhy agham — one who uses his lifetime for doing sins alone.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). voceyam — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; liṅ first person singular; mip gets am by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ [as read: Pā. 3-4-101]; the augment yāsuṭ; liṅy āśiṣy aṅ (Pā. 3-1-86) gives aṅ, with which following vacaḥ um (Pā. 7-4-20 [?]) gives the augment um to the root; āyeyaḥ [as read: ato yeyaḥ, Pā. 7-2-80] gives iya for yāsuṭ; when um follows, guṇa; tiṅ-nighāta since it follows a finite verb. bhavyāya — root bhū sattāyām; bhavyageyapravacanīya… (Pā. 3-4-68) gives the form with yat, irregular; yato nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213) gives the acute on the first syllable. indave — root undī kledane; undeḥ icca ādeḥ (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives u → i and the suffix un; undati kledayati iti induḥ; since n-marked the acute on the first syllable. rejati — root reja gatau; rejati dabhrotīti (Ni. 2-14 [?]) is among the verbs of motion; laṭ third person singular; because of the connection with yad no nighāta; since śap and tip are unaccented the root's accent remains. rakṣohā — root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; rakṣasāṃ hantā rakṣohā; kvip ca gives kvip; nominative singular; kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara. asmat — supāṃ sulug drops the ending.

original p. 395

nidaḥ — root ṇidi kutsāyām; ṇo naḥ (Pā. 6-1-65) gives n; kvip; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ gives the acute to the ending. vadhraiḥ — root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; hanaś ca vadhaḥ (Pā. 3-3-76) gives the suffix ap in the abstract sense with the substitute vadha for the root; the suffix ima [as printed], acute on the last syllable; instrumental plural. ajeta — root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ; the ātmanepada by vyatyaya; liṅ third person singular; nighāta since it follows a finite verb. sravet — root sru prasravaṇe; liṅ third person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. aghaśaṃsaḥ — aghe pāpe śaṃsaḥ manasi abhilāṣaḥ yasya saḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam gives the accent of the first member. kṣudram — root kṣudir saṃpeṣaṇe; sthāyitañcivañci… (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives rak; since k-marked no guṇa; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. ‖ 6 ‖

वनेम तद्धोत्रया चितन्त्या वनेम रयिं रयिवः सुवीर्यं रण्वं सन्तं सुवीर्यम् । दुर्मन्मानं सुमन्तुभिरेमिषा पृचीमहि । आ सत्याभिरिन्द्रं द्युम्नहूतिभिर्यजत्रं द्युम्नहूतिभिः ॥ ७ ॥

vanema taddhotrayā citantyā vanema rayiṃ rayivaḥ suvīryaṃ raṇvaṃ santaṃ suvīryam | durmanmānaṃ sumantubhiremiṣā pṛcīmahi | ā satyābhirindraṃ dyumnahūtibhiryajatraṃ dyumnahūtibhiḥ ‖ 7 ‖

vanema | tat | hotrayā | citantyā | vanema | rayim | rayi 'vaḥ | su 'vīryam | raṇvam | santam | su 'vīryam | duḥ 'manmānam | sumantu 'bhiḥ | ā | īm | iṣā | pṛcīmahi | ā | satyābhiḥ | indram | dyumna 'hūti 'bhiḥ | yajatram | dyumna 'hūti 'bhiḥ ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे इन्द्र वयं यजमानास्त्वत्प्रशंसकं स्तुत्यं तव रूपं यद्वा तत्ते वयं चितन्त्या तव गुणान् ज्ञापयन्त्या ॥ चिती संज्ञाने । अस्माण्यन्ताच्छतरि व्यत्ययेन शः ॥ होत्रया होमसाधनभूतया स्तुतिरूपया वाचा वनेम । सम्भजेम । यद्वा । शब्दयेम । स्तुतिं करवामेत्यर्थः । होत्रेति वाङ्नाम होत्रा गीरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । किंचैवं स्तोतारो वयमपि हे रयिवो विशिष्टधनवन्निन्द्र रयिं धनं वनेम । सम्भजेम । कीदृशं रयिम् । सुवीर्यं शोभनसामर्थ्योपेतं रण्वं रमणीयं गन्तव्यं वार्थिभिः सन्तं सर्वदा वर्तमानं यज्ञादिद्वारा बहुशो दीयमानमपि प्रवर्धमानम् । पुनस्तदेव विशेष्यते । सुवीर्यं शोभनपुत्रभृत्याद्युपेतं धनेन तेषां सम्पादयितुं शक्यत्वात् । वीरवीर्ये चेत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ किंच हे इन्द्र दुर्मन्मानं दुःखेन मन्तुं शक्यं त्वां तव महिम्नोऽतिमहत्त्वात् सुमन्तुभिः शोभनैर्मननैः स्तुतिसाधनैः स्तोत्रैरिषा हविरूपेणान्नेन च पृचीमहि । सर्वतः सम्पृक्ता भूयास्म । यद्वा । इषान्नेन निमित्तेन । पूर्वं धनस्य प्रार्थितत्वादिदानीमन्नं प्रार्थ्यते । पृची सम्पर्के । लिङि छान्दसो विकरणस्य लुक् ॥ किंच यजत्रं यागनिष्पादकमिन्द्रं सत्याभिरविसंवादिनीभिर्यथाभिलाषमुपजायमानफलाभिर्द्युम्नहूतिभिः । हरिव आगच्छ मेधातिथेर्मेषेत्याह्वानैरित्यर्थः । पुनस्ता एव विशेष्यन्ते । द्युम्नहूतिभिर्हविर्लक्षणान्ननिमित्तैराह्वानैरा पृचीमहीति शेषः । द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वा । नि. ५-५ [?] इति यास्कः ॥

he indra vayaṃ yajamānāstvatpraśaṃsakaṃ stutyaṃ tava rūpaṃ yadvā tatte vayaṃ citantyā tava guṇān jñāpayantyā ‖ citī saṃjñāne | asmāṇyantācchatari vyatyayena śaḥ ‖ hotrayā homasādhanabhūtayā stutirūpayā vācā vanema | sambhajema | yadvā | śabdayema | stutiṃ karavāmetyarthaḥ | hotreti vāṅnāma hotrā gīriti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | kiṃcaivaṃ stotāro vayamapi he rayivo viśiṣṭadhanavannindra rayiṃ dhanaṃ vanema | sambhajema | kīdṛśaṃ rayim | suvīryaṃ śobhanasāmarthyopetaṃ raṇvaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ gantavyaṃ vārthibhiḥ santaṃ sarvadā vartamānaṃ yajñādidvārā bahuśo dīyamānamapi pravardhamānam | punastadeva viśeṣyate | suvīryaṃ śobhanaputrabhṛtyādyupetaṃ dhanena teṣāṃ sampādayituṃ śakyatvāt | vīravīrye cetyuttarapadādyudāttatvam ‖ kiṃca he indra durmanmānaṃ duḥkhena mantuṃ śakyaṃ tvāṃ tava mahimno 'timahattvāt sumantubhiḥ śobhanairmananaiḥ stutisādhanaiḥ stotrairiṣā havirūpeṇānnena ca pṛcīmahi | sarvataḥ sampṛktā bhūyāsma | yadvā | iṣānnena nimittena | pūrvaṃ dhanasya prārthitatvādidānīmannaṃ prārthyate | pṛcī samparke | liṅi chāndaso vikaraṇasya luk ‖ kiṃca yajatraṃ yāganiṣpādakamindraṃ satyābhiravisaṃvādinībhiryathābhilāṣamupajāyamānaphalābhirdyumnahūtibhiḥ | hariva āgaccha medhātithermeṣetyāhvānairityarthaḥ | punastā eva viśeṣyante | dyumnahūtibhirhavirlakṣaṇānnanimittairāhvānairā pṛcīmahīti śeṣaḥ | dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vānnaṃ vā | ni. 5-5 [?] iti yāskaḥ ‖

Read from the image; some small-type letters are doubtful: [?] — e.g. "vīravīrye ca", "harivaḥ āgaccha medhātither meṣa" (the cited invocation), and the Nirukta number "५-५". Sense: "O Indra, we sacrificers vanema — praise, or serve — with hotrayā, the sacrificial praise-speech, that praiseworthy form of yours, or [that] making known your qualities (citantyā). Hotrā is a name of speech, 'hotrā, gīḥ'. And thus, we who praise, O possessor of wealth (rayivaḥ), may we obtain (vanema) wealth (rayim) — which is suvīryam (with good ability), raṇvam (delightful, to be sought by petitioners), santam (always existing, increasing though given away often through sacrifices); again, suvīryam — endowed with good sons, servants and the like, since they can be obtained with wealth. And, O Indra, hard to think of (durmanmānam) because of your exceeding greatness, we would be united (pṛcīmahi) with you by good thoughts — praise-hymns — and by food in the form of oblations (iṣā): we pray now for food, since wealth was prayed for before. And the sacrificer-fulfilling (yajatram) Indra, with true (unfailing) invocations (satyābhiḥ, dyumnahūtibhiḥ): 'come, harivaḥ, come…' — invocations — again with invocations offering food; dyumna is 'fame or food' (Yāska)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he indra — O Indra); tat — that (praiseworthy form of yours); citantyā — making known your qualities; hotrayā — by speech (in the form of praise) that is the means of homa; vanema — let us praise; rayivaḥ — O Indra, possessed of special wealth; (kiṃ ca — and, we who praise); suvīryam — of good strength; raṇvam — delightful (to be approached by petitioners); santam — lasting (growing though given freely at the sacrifice); suvīryam — endowed with good heroic sons and the like; rayim — wealth; vanema — may we obtain; (kiṃ ca — and); durmanmānam — difficult to know; īm — you; sumantubhiḥ — by good thoughts (praises); iṣā (ca — also by food in the form of oblations (for food); ā pṛcīmahi — may we be well united; (kiṃ ca — and); yajatram — worthy of sacrifice (the accomplisher of the sacrifice); indram — Indra; satyābhiḥ — by true (fruit-giving); dyumnahūtibhiḥ — by invocations in praise, for fame (and); dyumnahūtibhiḥ — by invocations that provide the food of oblation; ā pṛcīmahi — may we be united.

original p. 397

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra, we praise you with speech that makes known your qualities and is the means of homa; O Indra, possessed of wealth, we ask for the wealth that gives heroism, is desirable and lasting (always growing though given), and gives heroic sons and so on; difficult to know, we approach you with praises and with food in the form of oblations; O Indra, worthy of worship, we approach you with true, fruit-giving invocations and with praise that carries oblations.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "We praise you, Indra, with praises, making known (your glory): we solicit, giver of riches, the wealth that bestows vigour, that is agreeable, durable, and the support of progeny. May we (ever) be possessed of (abundant) food, through the praises of you, whom it is difficult adequately to honour: may we attain the adorable (Indra) by true and earnest invocation; by invocations (offering sacrificial) food."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 7).

tat citantyā hotrayā vanema — here the word tat is explained in two ways: as the form of Indra worthy of praise, and as the sacrificers (yajamānāḥ) well known in performing sacrifice.

original p. 398

(Special Topics of Ṛk 7, continued:) The word hotrā is recorded among the fifteen names of sacrifice, yajñaḥ, venaḥ and so on (Ni. 3-19 [?]), and among the fifty-seven names of speech, ślokaḥ, dhārā (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೩೨"?). Here homasādhanabhūtayā stutirūpayā vācā gives the sense "speech in the form of praise recited while the oblation is made". The meaning is stated: "those who are skilled in the performance of sacrifice praise Indra with the mantras recited at the time of homa that make known the form and the qualities of Indra worthy of praise." So the prayer is that they may be fit to praise.

raṇvaṃ suvīryaṃ santaṃ rayiṃ vanema — the word rayi is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೩-೩೪") and of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]; "೩-೯"): "rayir iti dhananāma rāter dānakarmaṇaḥ" (Ni. 4-17 [?]); from the root rā in the sense of giving, the word rayi means wealth.

The word suvīryam is an adjective of dhana: the wealth that produces excellent and great strength and also gives sons and servants. For the word santam he explains: though it is spent on good works such as sacrifices, wealth increases. The prayer is that they may obtain from Indra, the wealthy, wealth that is delightful, gives happiness and grows by good works fit to be given to petitioners.

durmanmānaṃ sumantubhir iṣā ā pṛcīmahi — "Because Indra's greatness cannot be known nor meditated upon, the sacrificers pray, with praises worthy of meditation even with great effort, and by offering oblations, to obtain food. The previous sentence prayed for wealth; this sentence, it is explained, prays for food."

The word dyumnahūtibhiḥ is used twice, and two kinds of meaning are given. The first meaning is "the manner of invoking Indra, who gives fixed results, in the sacrifice: harivaḥ, āgaccha, medhātither meṣa [as read, doubtful: [?]]". In the second, since the word dyumna is recorded among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೯") and has been explained by Yāska as dyumnaṃ dyoter yaśo vā annaṃ vā (Ni. 5-[?]; as read "೫-೬"), it is explained here as "food": with such invocations, they pray that, having invoked Indra at the sacrifice, they may offer oblations and obtain food.

original p. 399

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). vanema — root vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; liṅ first person plural; since at the beginning of the pāda there is no nighāta; the yāsuṭ is acute; the substitute coming from it too; by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ (Pā. 8-2-5) the e becomes acute. citantyā — root citī saṃjñāne; after the causative ṇic, śatṛ in the present sense; by vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85) the śa as the vikaraṇa; sārvadhātukam apit — since ṅit, no guṇa of the penult; when the feminine is intended after the śatṛ ending, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp; accent of the vikaraṇa; instrumental singular. rayivaḥ — rayiḥ asya asti iti rayivān; chandasīraḥ (Pā. 8-2-15) gives va in place of the m of matup; matuvasor ruḥ sambuddhau gives ru in the vocative; āmantritasya ca gives nighāta. suvīryam — śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasya tam; vīravīryau ca (Pā. 6-2-120) gives, against the accent of su, the acute on the first syllable of the latter member. durmanmānam — duḥkhena mantuṃ śakyaḥ durmanmā, tam; root mana jñāne; the suffix manin; since n-marked, the acute on the first syllable; in the compound kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara; accusative singular. sumantubhiḥ — śobhanāḥ mantavaḥ sumantavaḥ; root mana jñāne; Uṇādi tun; since n-marked, the acute on the first syllable; the compound as before; instrumental plural. iṣā — instrumental singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ gives the acute to the ending. pṛcīmahi — root pṛcī saṃparke; liṅ first person plural, suffix mahiṅ; liṅaḥ sīyuṭ (Pā. 3-4-102) gives the augment sīyuṭ; lopo vyor vali drops the y of sīyuṭ [as read]; sko… drops the s [as read: Pā. 6-2-69?]; bahulaṃ chandasi gives luk of the vikaraṇa; tiṅ-nighāta. dyumnahūtibhiḥ — bahuvrīhi compound; the accent of the first member.

original p. 400

yajatram — root yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; amiṇakṣiyaji… (Uṇ. 3-[?]) gives atran; jñityādir nityam gives the acute on the first syllable. ‖ 7 ‖
