॥ पदपाठः ॥

इन्द्रः । समत्ऽसु । यजमानम् । आर्यम् । प्र । आवत् । विश्वेषु । शतम्ऽऊतिः । आजिषु । स्वःऽमीळ्हेषु । आजिषु । मनवे । शासत् । अव्रतान् । त्वचम् । कृष्णाम् । अरन्धयत् । दक्षत् । न । विश्वम् । ततृषाणम् । ओषति । नि । अर्शसानम् । ओषति ॥ ८ ॥

indraḥ | samat 'su | yajamānam | āryam | pra | āvat | viśveṣu | śatam 'ūtiḥ | ājiṣu | svaḥ 'mīḷheṣu | ājiṣu | manave | śāsat | avratān | tvacam | kṛṣṇām | arandhayat | dakṣat | na | viśvam | tatṛṣāṇam | oṣati | ni | arśasānam | oṣati ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, a few doubtful places: [?]). Sense: "This Indra protects (prāvat) in samatsu — battles — the worshipper, the Ārya, worthy of being approached by all; (samatsu is among the names of battle). And śatamūtiḥ — of hundredfold protections for his own devotees — Indra protects the sacrificer in all contests (ājiṣu) and in the great battles (svarmīḷheṣu) that sprinkle happiness [lead to heaven]; he protects by granting heaven; of heroes slain facing the enemy it is heard in the world: 'These two men pierce the orb of the sun: the ascetic joined in yoga, and the one slain facing the enemy.' (Parāśara [?]). It is told in history: on the bank of the river Aṃśumatī the black demon Kṛṣṇa, with ten thousand followers, was afflicting the (respectable people) of the (four) castes: there Indra, urged by Bṛhaspati, with the Maruts, stripped the black skin and killed him with his followers: 'the drop (drapsa) stood on the Aṃśumatī' (Ṛ. 8-96-13 [?]) etc. — to be seen later. Here it is said: this Indra, for Manu (for men), punished (śāsat) the avratān — those without vrata (rites), who hate the sacrifice; and he destroyed (arandhayat) the black skin of the demon Kṛṣṇa; and as to how: dakṣan na viśvam — he burns the whole of them, the entire host of followers; not leaving anything: he burns (oṣati) all the harming ones, whatever is left of the sinful arśasāna [the wicked], utterly."

अयमिन्द्रः समत्सु रणेषु प्रहारनिमित्तेषु यजमानं यष्टारमार्यमरणीयं सर्वैर्गन्तव्यं प्रावत् । रक्षति ॥ समत्सु समरणे [?] सङ्ग्रामनाम समत्स्विति सङ्ग्रामनामसु पाठात् ॥ किंच शतमूतिः स्वभक्तरक्षणेषु बहुविधरक्षण इन्द्रो विश्वेषु ॥ लिङ्गव्यत्ययः ॥ आजिषु सर्वेषु स्पर्धानिमित्तेषु सङ्ग्रामेषु यजमानं प्रावत् । तथा स्वर्मीळ्हेषु स्वर्गदेशेषु सुखस्य सेचयत्सु वाजिषु महासङ्ग्रामेषु प्रावत् । स्वर्गप्रदानेन रक्षति । रण अभिमुखेन हतानां वीराणां स्वर्गे परारूढेन [?] श्रूयते । द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके सूर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ । परिव्राड्योगयुक्तश्च रणे चाभिमुखो हतः । पराशर [?] इति । अश्रूतेहासमाचक्षते । अंशुमती नाम नदी । तस्यास्तीरे कृष्णनामासुरो वर्णतश्च कृष्णो दशसहस्रैरनुचरैरुपेतस्त्रेषा वर्णिनः पीडयन्नास्ते । तत्रेन्द्रो बृहस्पतिना प्रेरितः सन् मरुद्भिः सहितः कृष्णां त्वचमुत्कृत्य सानुचरमवधीत् । आयमर्थोव्य ... द्रप्सो अंशुमतीमतिष्ठत् । ऋ. ८-९६-१३ [?] इत्यादिनोपरिष्टाद्द्रष्टव्यम् । तदत्रोच्यते । अयमिन्द्रो मनवे मनुष्याय । विभक्तिव्यत्ययः । मनुष्याणामर्थायाव्रतान् । व्रतमिति कर्मनाम तद्रहितान् । यागविद्वेषिणः शासत् शिक्षितवान् । हिंसितवान् । शासेर्लेट्यडागमः । तथा कृष्णां त्वचं कृष्णनाम्नोऽसुरस्य कृष्णवर्णां त्वचमुत्कृत्यारन्धयत् । हिंसितवान् । रध हिंसायां रधिजभोरचि नुम् । केन प्रकारेणेति तदुच्यते । दक्षन्न विश्वम् । तत्तृषाणं ततृषाणमोषति । सर्वमपि हिंसकं तदनुचरसंघं दहति । यत्किंचिदनिशिष्टमिति नेत्याह । अर्कसानं हिंसारुचिं [?] दशावशिष्टं सर्वमपि न्योषति । निःशेषेण दहति ॥

ayamindraḥ samatsu raṇeṣu prahāranimitteṣu yajamānaṃ yaṣṭāramāryamaraṇīyaṃ sarvairgantavyaṃ prāvat | rakṣati ‖ samatsu samaraṇe [?] saṅgrāmanāma samatsviti saṅgrāmanāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ kiṃca śatamūtiḥ svabhaktarakṣaṇeṣu bahuvidharakṣaṇa indro viśveṣu ‖ liṅgavyatyayaḥ ‖ ājiṣu sarveṣu spardhānimitteṣu saṅgrāmeṣu yajamānaṃ prāvat | tathā svarmīḷheṣu svargadeśeṣu sukhasya secayatsu vājiṣu mahāsaṅgrāmeṣu prāvat | svargapradānena rakṣati | raṇa abhimukhena hatānāṃ vīrāṇāṃ svarge parārūḍhena [?] śrūyate | dvāvimau puruṣau loke sūryamaṇḍalabhedinau | parivrāḍyogayuktaśca raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ | parāśara [?] iti | aśrūtehāsamācakṣate | aṃśumatī nāma nadī | tasyāstīre kṛṣṇanāmāsuro varṇataśca kṛṣṇo daśasahasrairanucarairupetastreṣā varṇinaḥ pīḍayannāste | tatrendro bṛhaspatinā preritaḥ san marudbhiḥ sahitaḥ kṛṣṇāṃ tvacamutkṛtya sānucaramavadhīt | āyamarthovya ... drapso aṃśumatīmatiṣṭhat | ṛ. 8-96-13 [?] ityādinopariṣṭāddraṣṭavyam | tadatrocyate | ayamindro manave manuṣyāya | vibhaktivyatyayaḥ | manuṣyāṇāmarthāyāvratān | vratamiti karmanāma tadrahitān | yāgavidveṣiṇaḥ śāsat śikṣitavān | hiṃsitavān | śāserleṭyaḍāgamaḥ | tathā kṛṣṇāṃ tvacaṃ kṛṣṇanāmno 'surasya kṛṣṇavarṇāṃ tvacamutkṛtyārandhayat | hiṃsitavān | radha hiṃsāyāṃ radhijabhoraci num | kena prakāreṇeti taducyate | dakṣanna viśvam | tattṛṣāṇaṃ tatṛṣāṇamoṣati | sarvamapi hiṃsakaṃ tadanucarasaṃghaṃ dahati | yatkiṃcidaniśiṣṭamiti netyāha | arkasānaṃ hiṃsāruciṃ [?] daśāvaśiṣṭaṃ sarvamapi nyoṣati | niḥśeṣeṇa dahati ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (ayam) indraḥ — this Indra; samatsu — in battles; yajamānam — the sacrificer; āryam — the Ārya (the one worth approaching); pra āvat — protects; (kiṃ ca — and); śatam ūtiḥ — [Indra] of a hundred protections for his devotees;

original p. 452

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 8, continued from p. 451: "…viśveṣu — in all; ājiṣu — in battles; (pra āvat — protects the sacrificer); (tathā — likewise); svarmīḷheṣu — in those that lead to heaven; ājiṣu — in battles; (prāvat — protects); (kiṃ ca — and); (ayam) indraḥ — this Indra; manave — for the sake of men; avratān — the people without rites (haters of the sacrifice); śāsat — punishes; (tathā — likewise); kṛṣṇām — the black (of the demon named Kṛṣṇa); tvacam — skin; (utkṛtya — having stripped); dakṣat na — as if burning to ashes; arandhayat — destroyed; tatṛṣāṇam — the harming; viśvam — all (his followers); oṣati — burns; arśasānam — the one who delights in cruelty, or [one who has] whatever is left of sin — everything; ni oṣati — utterly burns."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Indra, who protects his devotees in many ways, protects the sacrificer who worships him in all battles; in all battles that give the happiness of heaven he protects; he punishes for the sake of men those who hate the sacrifice; stripping the black skin of the demon named Kṛṣṇa, he destroyed those Rākṣasas; like fire, blazing, he destroys all the harmful (with his followers); he destroys utterly those who delight in cruelty.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Indra, the manifold protector (of his votaries) in battles, defends his Arya worshipper in all conflicts; in conflicts that confer heaven: he punished for (the benefit of) man the neglecters of religious rites: he tore off the black skin (of the aggressor): as if burning (with flame), he consumes the malignant; he utterly consumes him who delights in cruelty."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 8).

samatsu — raṇeṣu prahāranimittṛeṣu: "in places where harm may happen — in places of danger or in battles". The word samatsu is recorded among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯").

yajamānam āryam — araṇīyaṃ yaṣṭāram: "the sacrificer who is an object of honour to all".

śatamūtiḥ viśveṣu ājiṣu prāvat — sarveṣu spardhānimitteṣu indro yajamānaṃ prāvat: "In all the contests in which people dispute with one another, Indra, expert in many kinds of protection, protects the sacrificer, who seeks to increase his prosperity, in every way": so the meaning. The word āji is recorded among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯").

original p. 453

svarmīḷheṣu ājiṣu prāvat — svargadeśeṣu sukhasya secayatsu vā mahāsaṅgrāmeṣu svargapradānena rakṣati: "In this Ṛk the word āji is used twice. The Niruktakāra explains it as 'battle'; Sāyaṇa, from the connection with the adjectives, explains āji as 'the great battle that makes heaven attainable (svargaprāpaka), the contest that is the occasion of rivalry'. The word svarmīḷha denotes what gives the happiness of heaven." To those who fight in battles with courage — and who, by indifference, take no care of their lives — Indra gives the comfort of heaven and so protects them: so he says. Parāśara —

द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके सूर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ । परिव्राड्योगयुक्तश्च रणे चाभिमुखो हतः ॥

dvāv imau puruṣau loke sūryamaṇḍalabhedinau | parivrāḍ yogayuktaś ca raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ ‖

(Parāśara-smṛti 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೨" [?]) — the sage in yoga, who in the contemplation of the self constantly dwells in detachment from the happiness of this world and the warrior who gave up hope for his life in great battles and, not turning back, fought and fell in battle, both are said by the Parāśara-smṛti to reach, on the birth cycle ceasing, the state of passing through the orb of the sun. By this it is indicated that the happiness of heaven too, which has the form of non-return (apunarāvṛtti) according to the Śāstra, is attainable for them. And Indra, by honouring such heroes, gives them the happiness of heaven and protects them; so the greatness of Indra's protection is described.

manave śāsad avratān tvacaṃ kṛṣṇām arandhayat — manuṣyāṇām arthāya yāgavidveṣiṇaḥ hiṃsitavān | kṛṣṇanāmno 'surasya kṛṣṇavarṇāṃ tvacam utkṛtya hiṃsitavān: the word manu is explained as "men". "To bring about the welfare and happiness of men, Indra [punishes] the thorns of the sacrifice and destroys them; stripping the black skin of the demon named Kṛṣṇa, he killed him": so it is explained. On this Sāyaṇa cites a legend:

अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । अंशुमती नाम नदी । तस्यास्तीरे कृष्णनामासुरो वर्णतश्च कृष्णो दशसहस्रैरनुचरैरुपेतस्तद्देशवर्तिनः पीडयन्नास्ते । तत्रेन्द्रो बृहस्पतिना प्रेरितस्सन् मरुद्भिः सहितः कृष्णां तदीयां त्वचमुत्कृत्य सानुचरमवधीत् । अयमर्थः ॥

atretihāsam ācakṣate | aṃśumatī nāma nadī | tasyās tīre kṛṣṇanāmāsuro varṇataś ca kṛṣṇo daśasahasrair anucarair upetas taddeśavartinaḥ pīḍayann āste | tatrendro bṛhaspatinā preritas san marudbhiḥ sahitaḥ kṛṣṇāṃ tadīyāṃ tvacam utkṛtya sānucaram avadhīt | ayam arthaḥ ‖

original p. 454

अव द्रप्सो अंशुमतीमतिष्ठदियानः कृष्णो दशभिः सहस्रैः । आवत्तमिन्द्रः शच्या धमन्तमप स्नेहितीर्नृमणा अधत्त ॥

ava drapso aṃśumatīm atiṣṭhad iyānaḥ kṛṣṇo daśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ | āvat tam indraḥ śacyā dhamantam apa snehitīr nṛmaṇā adhatta ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-13, as read "೮-೯೬-೧೩".) "Etc.; this will be seen later": so it is told. "On the bank of the well-known river called Aṃśumatī, in the region of the Yamunā [as read: hariyuttaravuḍa, doubtful: [?]], there lived an asura named Kṛṣṇa. He was black in colour, and with ten thousand followers he afflicted the people of that country, doing violence to the inhabitants and killing them. Bṛhaspati, the priest of all the gods, learned of this, and informed Indra that the demon and his followers, thorns of the sacrifice, must be subdued quickly. Then Indra, accompanied by the Marut gods, fought against that demon, stripped off the black skin of Kṛṣṇa, killed him and his followers and protected all the people of that country": it is explained that this story is told in the interpretation of the Ṛk "ava drapso aṃśumatīm atiṣṭhat".

dakṣat — bhasmīkaroti: "Indra kills the thorns of the sacrifice who harm others in the world."

tatṛṣāṇam oṣati — nyarśasānam oṣati — the word oṣati is used twice. Sarvam api hiṃsakaṃ tadanucarasaṅghaṃ dahati — "Indra destroys both those who do violence and their followers"; and arśasānaṃ hiṃsārucim hatāvaśiṣṭaṃ sarvam api niḥśeṣeṇa dahati — "he destroys all who delight in violence, without leaving any remainder".

āryam — araṇīyaṃ, sarvair gantavyam: "worthy of being attained by all". The Niruktakāra —

युवं वृकेणाश्विना वपन्तेषं दुहन्ता मनुषाय दस्रा । अभि दस्युं बकुरेणा धमन्तोरु ज्योतिश्चक्रथुरार्याय ॥

yuvaṃ vṛkeṇāśvinā vapanteṣaṃ duhantā manuṣāya dasrā | abhi dasyuṃ bakureṇā dhamantoru jyotiś cakrathur āryāya ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-21, as read "೧-೧೧೭-೨೧".) — explains āryāya in this Ṛk as "the son of Īśvara [?]" [as read]; Sāyaṇa explains āryāya as "to the one who knows".

original p. 455

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). āryam — root ṛ gatau; ṛhaloṇyat (Pā. 3-1-124) gives ṇyat; ñit-marked, so vṛddhi, and raparatva. āvat — root ava rakṣaṇe; laṅ third person singular; because it follows a finite verb, nighāta. śatamūtiḥ — śatam aparimitam ūtiḥ rakṣaṇaṃ yasya saḥ; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam gives the accent of the first member. viśveṣu — as an epithet of ājiṣu the feminine would be required by the rule yal liṅgaṃ yad vacanam…; but by vyatyaya it is used in the masculine. svarmīḍheṣu — root mihaḥ secane; kta; hoḍhaḥ gives ḍh for h; jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (Pā. 8-2-40) gives dh for the t of the suffix; ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ (Pā. 8-3-13) drops the earlier ḍh; ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ (Pā. 6-3-111) lengthens the i; pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara. śāsat — root śāsu anuśiṣṭau; leṭ third person singular, tip; itaś ca lope (Pā. 3-4-97) drops i; leṭo 'ḍāṭau gives the augment aṭ; cādilope vibhāṣā (Pā. 8-1-63) forbids nighāta; the root's accent remains. avratān — na vidyate vrataṃ yeṣāṃ te avratāḥ; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the acute on the last syllable. kṛṣṇām — root kṛṣa vilekhane; kṛṣer varṇe [as read: Uṇ. 3-[?]] gives naka; ṣṇu… the n replaces the k of the suffix; the acute on the last syllable; feminine ṭāp since it ends in a; accusative singular. manave — by vyatyaya the dative is used for the genitive. arandhayat — root radha hiṃsāyām; after ṇic, luṅ third person singular, tip; itaś ca lopaḥ; śap [as read]; radhijabhor aci (Pā. 7-1-61) gives the augment num to the root; since m-marked it comes after the last vowel; guṇa because of śap, ayādeśa; the augment aṭ; because it follows a finite verb, nighāta. dakṣat — root daha bhasmīkaraṇe; leṭ third person singular, tip, loss of i, augment aṭ; sibbahulaṃ leṭi (Pā. 3-1-34) gives sip; dādher dhātor ghaḥ [as read: dādhe… ḥaḥ] gives…

original p. 456

Grammar of Ṛk 8, concluded; numbers as printed. dakṣat (cont.) — the h of the root becomes gh/k… by dādher ghoḥ [as read]; ṣatva of the s following the k; ekāco baśo bhaṣ jhaṣantasya sdhvoḥ (Pā. 8-2-37) gives bh for the root-initial; the form dakṣat; because it follows a finite verb nighāta is not applied; the root's accent remains since the suffix is p-marked. tatṛṣāṇam — root ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām; when liṭ follows, kānac replaces it; citaḥ (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the acute on the last syllable; accusative singular. oṣati — root uṣa dāhe; laṭ third person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. arśasānam — root ṛ gatau; arter guṇaḥ śuṭ ca (Uṇ. 3-[?]) gives the suffix āsānac; guṇa of the root; the augment śuṭ; because ṭ-marked the augment comes at the beginning of the suffix; citaḥ gives the acute on the last syllable. ‖ 8 ‖

(ornamental rule)

Rik 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सूरश्चक्रं प्र वृहज्जात ओजसा प्रपित्वे वाचमरुणो मुषायति । ईशान आ मुषायति । उशना यत्परावतोऽजगन्नूतये कवे । सुम्नानि विश्वा मनुषेव तुर्वणिरहा विश्वेव तुर्वणिः ॥ ९ ॥

sūraścakraṃ pra vṛhajjāta ojasā prapitve vācamaruṇo muṣāyati | īśāna ā muṣāyati | uśanā yatparāvato 'jagannūtaye kave | sumnāni viśvā manuṣeva turvaṇirahā viśveva turvaṇiḥ ‖ 9 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image. Saṃhitā "pra vṛhaj jāta ojasā" as printed, the Pada giving jātaḥ; tuvarṇiḥ is printed "turvaṇiḥ".

सूरः । चक्रम् । प्र । वृहत् । जातः । ओजसा । प्रऽपित्वे । वाचम् । अरुणः । मुषायति । ईशानः । आ । मुषायति । उशना । यत् । पराऽवतः । अजगन् । ऊतये । कवे । सुम्नानि । विश्वा । मनुषाऽइव । तुर्वणिः । अहा । विश्वाऽइव । तुर्वणिः ॥ ९ ॥

sūraḥ | cakram | pra | vṛhat | jātaḥ | ojasā | pra 'pitve | vācam | aruṇaḥ | muṣāyati | īśānaḥ | ā | muṣāyati | uśanā | yat | parā 'vataḥ | ajagan | ūtaye | kave | sumnāni | viśvā | manuṣā 'iva | turvaṇiḥ | ahā | viśvā 'iva | turvaṇiḥ ‖ 9 ‖

original p. 457

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, many places doubtful: [?]). Sense: "Here also they relate an itihāsa: certain demons formerly, having obtained from Brahmā the boon 'let there be no death by Indra's thunderbolt', became arrogant, disregarding Indra. To kill them Indra took the wheel of the Sun's chariot and slew them. That is told here: this Indra — sūraḥ, 'the Sun', the first case for the genitive — taking the wheel (cakram) of the chariot, grown (jātaḥ) in bodily strength (ojasā), pra vṛhat — tore out. Further, aruṇaḥ — reddish, exceedingly brilliant, or moving — at prapitve, near them, comes up and muṣāyati — takes away their breath marked by speech; or he stops the sound of their blows. Or: Indra himself, standing in heaven, is praised in the form of the Sun. When sūra the sun has risen, endowed with his own splendour, he lifts the wheel-marked chariot to dispel darkness or to conquer the demons. Then, before, aruṇa — the sun's charioteer — near the demons … īśānaḥ — able to remove all darknesses or the demons — ā muṣāyati, carries off all around. Now to the context: O sage (kave, far-seeing), since you came (ajagan) from afar (parāvataḥ), from the heavenly abode, for protection (ūtaye), joined with Uśanā [or: uśanā kaviḥ — the sage Uśanas]; coming, bring all (viśvā) the means of happiness (sumnāni), wealth, and be quick (turvaṇiḥ — 'quickly sharing', Nirukta) for us; as for man (manuṣeva) — as for other priests you bring all wealth, so for us too; and not only on one day of the sacrifice but on all days (ahā viśveva): or as you give long life, so give happiness: give both.") (Doubtful readings in the small type are marked [?]; the grammar tail on muṣāyati and ajagan is characterized only.

अत्रापीतिहासमाचक्षते । केचनासुराः पूर्वमिन्द्रवज्रेण वधो मा भूदिति ब्रह्मणो वरं लब्ध्वेन्द्रमगणयित्वोद्वृत्ता आसन् । तान् हन्तुमिन्द्रः सूर्यरथस्य चक्रमादायावधीदिति । तदिदमुच्यते । अयमिन्द्रः सूरः सूर्यस्य षष्ठ्यर्थे प्रथमा । चक्रं रथस्य चक्रमादायौजसा शारीरेण बलेन जातः सम्वृद्धः सन् प्र वृहत् । प्रकृष्टं वृक्णवान् । वृहू उद्यमने । तौदादिकः । किंचारुणोऽरुणवर्णोऽत्यन्तं तेजोयुक्तः सन् यद्वा गमनशीलः सन् प्रपित्वे तेषां समीपे [?] तेषामुपगम्य वाचं वागुपलक्षितं प्राणं मुषायति । मुमोष मुष्णाति वा । प्रपित्व इत्याद्यनामाम [?] । यद्वा । वाचं तेषां प्रहारध्वनिं मुषायति । तेषु हतेषु ध्वनिः स्वयमेव विश्रान्तो भवति । अवधीदित्यर्थः । अथवा । इन्द्र एव द्युस्थानः सन्नादित्यात्मना स्तूयते । सूरः सूर्यो जाते उदिते सन्नोजसा स्वकीयेन तेजसा युक्तश्चक्रं प्र वृहत् । तमोनिवारणार्थमसुरजयाय वा चक्रोपलक्षितं रथं प्रकर्षेणोद्यतं करोति । ततः पूर्वमरुणस्सूरथयन्ता प्रपित्वे मन्देहादीनामसुराणां प्रपित्वे समीपे वाचं तेषां जहद्भिन्दतीति दध्यनिं मुषायति । मुष्णाति । मुषेरुत्तरस्य क्ष्णोऽवानः । श्छन्दसि शायजपीति शायजादेशः ॥ तदनन्तरं सूर्य ईशानः सर्वाणि तमांस्यसुरान्वा निराकर्तुं समर्थः सन् आ मुषायति । समन्तान्मुष्णाति । अथ प्रकृतम् ॥ हे कवे क्रान्तदर्शिन् यद्यस्मात्त्वमुशनोऽनसा [?] युक्तः सन् परावतो दूरात्स्वर्गस्थानादजगन् [?] । उशना कविः तदुपेतमूतये रक्षणाय । परावतो दूरात्स्वर्गस्थानादजगन् गतवानसि प्राप्तवानसि ॥ गमेर्लुङि सिचि छान्दसः शपः श्लुः । हल्ङ्यादिलोपे [?] इति सलोपः ॥ यद्वा । उशना उशनसा ऋषिणा युक्तः सन् जगन् आगच्छ । आगत्य च विश्वा विश्वानि सुम्नानि सुखसाधनानि धनान्यादायास्माकं तुर्वणिः शीघ्रं सम्भक्ता भवेति शेषः । तुर्वणिः शीघ्रं सम्भक्तेति निरुक्तम् । नि. ६-१४ [?] । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । मनुषेव मनुष्येण । स यथा सम्भक्त्रेण [?] । यद्वा । मनुष्येण मनुष्याणामिव । इतरेषामृत्विजां विश्वा सुम्नानि सर्वाणि धनान्यादाय तुर्वणिर्भवसि । तद्वदस्माकमपि । न केवलमेकस्मिन्नेव यागादिने किंत्विहा विश्वेव विश्वस्यान्यहानि [?] सर्वेष्वप्यहःसु तुर्वणिर्भव । यद्वा । तुर्वणिस्त्वमहा विश्वेव विश्वस्यान्यहानीव । यथा दीर्घायुष्यं यथा ददासि तथा सुम्नान्यपि । उभयमपि देहीत्यर्थः ॥

atrāpītihāsamācakṣate | kecanāsurāḥ pūrvamindravajreṇa vadho mā bhūditi brahmaṇo varaṃ labdhvendramagaṇayitvodvṛttā āsan | tān hantumindraḥ sūryarathasya cakramādāyāvadhīditi | tadidamucyate | ayamindraḥ sūraḥ sūryasya ṣaṣṭhyarthe prathamā | cakraṃ rathasya cakramādāyaujasā śārīreṇa balena jātaḥ samvṛddhaḥ san pra vṛhat | prakṛṣṭaṃ vṛkṇavān | vṛhū udyamane | taudādikaḥ | kiṃcāruṇo 'ruṇavarṇo 'tyantaṃ tejoyuktaḥ san yadvā gamanaśīlaḥ san prapitve teṣāṃ samīpe [?] teṣāmupagamya vācaṃ vāgupalakṣitaṃ prāṇaṃ muṣāyati | mumoṣa muṣṇāti vā | prapitva ityādyanāmāma [?] | yadvā | vācaṃ teṣāṃ prahāradhvaniṃ muṣāyati | teṣu hateṣu dhvaniḥ svayameva viśrānto bhavati | avadhīdityarthaḥ | athavā | indra eva dyusthānaḥ sannādityātmanā stūyate | sūraḥ sūryo jāte udite sannojasā svakīyena tejasā yuktaścakraṃ pra vṛhat | tamonivāraṇārthamasurajayāya vā cakropalakṣitaṃ rathaṃ prakarṣeṇodyataṃ karoti | tataḥ pūrvamaruṇassūrathayantā prapitve mandehādīnāmasurāṇāṃ prapitve samīpe vācaṃ teṣāṃ jahadbhindatīti dadhyaniṃ muṣāyati | muṣṇāti | muṣeruttarasya kṣṇo 'vānaḥ | śchandasi śāyajapīti śāyajādeśaḥ ‖ tadanantaraṃ sūrya īśānaḥ sarvāṇi tamāṃsyasurānvā nirākartuṃ samarthaḥ san ā muṣāyati | samantānmuṣṇāti | atha prakṛtam ‖ he kave krāntadarśin yadyasmāttvamuśano 'nasā [?] yuktaḥ san parāvato dūrātsvargasthānādajagan [?] | uśanā kaviḥ tadupetamūtaye rakṣaṇāya | parāvato dūrātsvargasthānādajagan gatavānasi prāptavānasi ‖ gamerluṅi sici chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | halṅyādilope [?] iti salopaḥ ‖ yadvā | uśanā uśanasā ṛṣiṇā yuktaḥ san jagan āgaccha | āgatya ca viśvā viśvāni sumnāni sukhasādhanāni dhanānyādāyāsmākaṃ turvaṇiḥ śīghraṃ sambhaktā bhaveti śeṣaḥ | turvaṇiḥ śīghraṃ sambhakteti niruktam | ni. 6-14 [?] | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | manuṣeva manuṣyeṇa | sa yathā sambhaktreṇa [?] | yadvā | manuṣyeṇa manuṣyāṇāmiva | itareṣāmṛtvijāṃ viśvā sumnāni sarvāṇi dhanānyādāya turvaṇirbhavasi | tadvadasmākamapi | na kevalamekasminneva yāgādine kiṃtvihā viśveva viśvasyānyahāni [?] sarveṣvapyahaḥsu turvaṇirbhava | yadvā | turvaṇistvamahā viśveva viśvasyānyahānīva | yathā dīrghāyuṣyaṃ yathā dadāsi tathā sumnānyapi | ubhayamapi dehītyarthaḥ ‖

original p. 458

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. ayam) indraḥ — this Indra; sūraḥ — of the Sun; cakram — the wheel of the chariot (taking it); ojasā — by bodily strength; jātaḥ — grown; pra vṛhat — tore out against (the demons' bodies); (kiṃ ca — and); aruṇaḥ — reddish or moving; prapitve — near (them, going to them); vācam — speech or breath; muṣāyati — takes away [or:* (athavā) sūraḥ — Indra in the form of the Sun; jātaḥ — risen; ojasā — with his own splendour; cakram — the wheel (chariot); pra vṛhat — lifts up (to remove darkness); aruṇaḥ — the sun's charioteer, named Aruṇa; prapitve — near the demons (Mandeha and the rest); vācam — their voice (the sound of demons, by the wheel); muṣāyati — makes them silent; īśānaḥ — able to remove darkness (or the demons); ā muṣāyati *— destroys them entirely]; (he) kave — O sage; uśanā — joined with the sage named Uśanas; ūtaye — for our protection; parāvataḥ — from a very distant place (from the world of heaven); ajagan — came (or: yat — that you; uśanā — to Uśanas' protection; parāvataḥ — from heaven; ajagan — you came); viśvā sumnāni — all the means of happiness (taking); manuṣā iva — as (from a distant place) for a man the desired things are brought, or as for the other priests [wealth is granted]; turvaṇiḥ (bhava — be quick to favour; viśvā ahā iva — on all days; turvaṇiḥ (bhava) — be quick to favour [or: turvaṇiḥ — you who give; viśvā ahā iva — as long life; viśvā sumnāni — all the means of happiness; turvaṇiḥ (bhava) — be one who favours quickly].

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Indra, endowed with extraordinary bodily strength, took up the wheel of the Sun's chariot and slew the demons; reddish, he destroyed them completely, being able (to destroy the Rākṣasas) — he made them lifeless; O wise Indra, as you came from the heavenly world, from far away, for the protection of Uśanas, so come and bring all the means of happiness for us and for the other priests; be quick to favour us, giving the means of happiness, every day.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed; begins here and continues on p. 459): "Endowed with augmented vigour, he hurled (against the foes) the wheel (of the chariot) of the sun; and, ruddy of hue, deprived them of existence; he, the sovereign lord, deprived them of existence. As you, sage Indra, come from afar to the succour of Ushanas, so do you come quickly, bearing all good things (to us), as you bear to (other) men; come quickly (to us) every day."

original p. 459

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 9).

sūraś cakraṃ ojasā pravṛhat — sūryasya rathasya cakram ādāya śārīreṇa balena samṛddhaḥ san prakṛṣṭavān: "taking the wheel of the Sun's chariot, strong in body, Indra tore it out." Here too a legend is told: kecana asurā indrasya vajrāyudhena asmākaṃ vadho mā bhūd iti brahmaṇā varaṃ labdhvā indram āgaṇayitvā uddhṛttāḥ sthitāḥ | tān hantum indraḥ sūryarathasya cakram ādāyāvadhīt iti — "some demons, having obtained from Brahmā the boon that they should not die by Indra's thunderbolt, became arrogant, disregarding Indra, and Indra, taking the wheel of the Sun's chariot as his weapon, slew them all."

यमेन दत्तं त्रित एनमायुनगिन्द्र एणं प्रथमो अध्यतिष्ठत् । गन्धर्वो अस्य रशनामगृभ्णात्सूरादश्वं वसवो निरतष्ट ॥

yamena dattaṃ trita enam āyunag indra eṇaṃ prathamo adhyatiṣṭhat | gandharvo asya raśanām agṛbhṇāt sūrād aśvaṃ vasavo nir ataṣṭa ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-163-2, as read "೧-೧೬೩-೨"; the first line has a doubtful word at its start: yamena [?]. The numerals "1-163-2" are the reading of the small type and are not confirmed by the numeral tool.) In this Ṛk Durgācārya has explained the word sūrāt as "from the Sun". Here Sāyaṇa explains sūraḥ as sūryasya, and for ojasā, recorded among the names of strength in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"), the meaning "bodily strength".

aruṇaḥ prapitve vācaṃ muṣāyati — aruṇavarṇaḥ atyantatejoyuktaḥ | yadvā gamanaśīlaḥ san prapitve teṣāṃ samīpam upāgatya vāgupalakṣitaṃ prāṇaṃ mumoṣa muṣṇāti vā — three kinds of meaning are given by Sāyaṇa. In the first, Indra, very radiant and reddish in colour, or constantly moving, approaches the demons and takes away their very breath (so that they cannot even speak); the explanation is that he kills them.

In the second meaning: vācaṃ teṣāṃ prahāradhvaniṃ muṣāyati | teṣu hateṣu dhvaniḥ svayam eva viśrānto bhavati | avadhīd ity arthaḥ — "Indra, at the time of battle, strikes the demons with his weapon so that they do not utter even a sound; and their breath, along with the sound of their blows, ceases": thus it is described. In the third meaning: athavā indra iva dyusthānaḥ sann ādityātmanā stūyate — "Indra, who is the deity of the heaven-region, is praised in the form of the Sun". The description of Indra's greatness is explained in this way. The remainder of this page and the explanation of the third meaning continue on p. 460.

original p. 460

Special Topics of Ṛk 9, continued — the third meaning: sūraḥ sūryo jātaḥ udita san ojasā svakīyena tejasā yukta ś cakraṃ pravṛhat | tamo nivāraṇārtham asurajayāya vā cakropalakṣitaṃ rathaṃ prakarṣeṇa udyataṃ karoti | tataḥ pūrvam aruṇaḥ sūrathayantā prapitve mandehādyasurāṇāṃ samīpe vācaṃ teṣāṃ jahad bhindati ity ādidhvaniṃ muṣāyati muṣṇāti: "As soon as the Sun has risen, endowed with his own splendour, he makes the chariot, marked by its wheel, speed along, to dispel darkness or to conquer the demons; before that, Aruṇa, the Sun's charioteer, near the demon-hosts such as Mandeha, silences the sound of their words — he breaks it": so it is explained. The Niruktakāra —

यदुदञ्चो वृषाकपे गृहमिन्द्राजगन्तन । क्वस्य पुल्वघो मृगः कमगञ्जनयोपनो विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ॥

yad udañco vṛṣākape gṛham indrājagantana | kvasya pulvagho mṛgaḥ kam agañ janayopano viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-[?], as read "೧೦-೮೬-೨೩" [?]; the small type is hard to read: [?].) — citing this Ṛk, he explains kam agam uddiśya janayopanaḥ sarvasmād indra uttaraḥ, and (Ni. 12-[?]) says that Indra is invisible, while Āditya (the Sun) is visible; the wise know the identity of the two from the "knowledge of the form of the Sun" in the sacrificer; among the gods Indra is the foremost; therefore it is described that Indra is called by the name Āditya.

prapitve — teṣāṃ samīpe prapitve abhīke ity āsannasya | prapitve prāpte: the Niruktakāra reads prapitve prāpte, abhīke abhyakte (Ni. 3-30 [?]) and explains prapitve abhīke ity āsannasya — both words denote nearness. And —

यथा गौरो अपा कृतं तृष्यन्नेत्यवेरिणम् । आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमा गहि कण्वेषु सु सचा पिब ॥

yathā gauro apā kṛtaṃ tṛṣyann ety averiṇam | āpitve naḥ prapitve tūyam ā gahi kaṇveṣu su sacā piba ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-4-3, as read "೮-೪-೩".) From this Ṛk the word prapitve is explained as prāpte; by this it is stated that a word meaning "near" is used without a gap.

īśānaḥ ā muṣāyati — sarvāṇi tamāṃsi asurān vā nirākartuṃ samarthaḥ san samantāt muṣṇāti: "the Sun is able to remove all darkness, or the demons."

original p. 461

(…) "while he is risen, the Sun destroys the darkness or the demons entirely, as one endowed with the means and power to subdue them."

kave yat uśanā ūtaye parāvataḥ ajagan — krāntadarśin uśanas iti nāmnaḥ maharṣeḥ rakṣaṇāya dūrāt svargasthānāt prāptavān asi: two kinds of meaning are given. Indra is addressed as kavi, "one who sees everything directly". "When the sage named Uśanas prayed to Indra for protection, Indra came from the far-off heaven and protected him": this story is alluded to; one meaning. In the second, the word uśanā is explained as uśanasā — together with Bhārgava (Śukrācārya), the coming of Indra is prayed for, and his protection.

viśvā sumnāni turvaṇiḥ — sarvāṇi sukhasādhanāni dhanāni ādāya asmākaṃ kṣipraṃ saṃbhaktā bhava: the word sumna is recorded among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೪"); turvaṇi is explained as turvaṇis tūrṇavaniḥ (Ni. 6-[?]; as read "೬-೧೪"). "Indra is prayed to bring wealth, the means of happiness, to us and to give us happiness carefully."

manuṣeva turvaṇiḥ — manuṣyeṇeva yathā tvoteṇa parivṛḍhāya deśāntarād abhimataṃ dhanam ānīyate tadvat | yadvā manuṣeva manuṣyāṇām iva itareṣām ṛtvijāṃ viśvā sumnāni sarvāṇi dhanāny ādāya turvaṇir bhavasi tadvad asmākam api: "as a man goes to another country and brings the wealth he needs, so Indra is asked to bring wealth for the sacrificers; or, as Indra brings all the wealth that the other priests desire, so for us".

ahā viśveva turvaṇiḥ — sarveṣv apy ahaḥsu turvaṇir bhava | yadvā turvaṇis tvam ahā viśveva atidīrghāyuṣyaṃ yathā dadāsi tathā sumnāny api ubhayam api dehi: "on all days be the quick giver; or, as you give very long life, give happiness too — give both": so it is prayed that when the sacrifice is being performed Indra give wealth and, on all other days, favour us.

original p. 462

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). sūraḥ — root ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane [as read], suffix kran by susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran (Uṇ. 2-[?]); no guṇa since k-marked; by n-marker the acute on the first syllable; first case in the sense of the genitive. bṛhat — root vṛhū udyamane, tudādi; laṅ third person singular; itaś ca drops i; tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ gives śa; since sārvadhātukam apit no guṇa of the penult; bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi gives no augment aṭ; tiṅ-nighāta. muṣāyati — root muṣa steye; by the statement ghuṇarthakaviṣaya [as read] ṇic…; muṣam ātmana icchati, supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8); na chandasy aputrasya (Pā. 7-4-35) forbids lengthening, but by vyatyaya the preceding lengthening occurs; after the kyac-ending laṭ third person singular; or by bahulaṃ chandasi the ṇic as vikaraṇa; by the statement sañjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ no guṇa of the penult; tiṅ-nighāta; or when śāyac … chandasi śāyajapi (Pā. 3-1-84) gives śāyac. īśānaḥ — root īśa aiśvarye; śānac in the present sense; citaḥ gives the acute on the last syllable. uśanā — root vaśa kāntau; vaśeḥ kanasi (Uṇ. 4-[?]) gives kanasi; grahijyāvayi… (Pā. 6-1-16) gives saṃprasāraṇa, pūrvarūpa; the stem uśanas; acute on the first syllable by the suffix; by vyatyaya the first case. ajagan — root gamḷ gatau; luṅ second person singular, sip; bahulaṃ chandasi gives śap→śluh; ślau doubles the root; kuhoś cuḥ (Pā. 7-4-62) gives j for the reduplicative g; hal ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt… drops sip; no no dhātoḥ [as read: Pā. 8-2-64?] gives n for the m; since yad is connected, nighāta does not occur; the augment aṭ is acute so that the first syllable is acute.

original p. 463

turvaṇiḥ — root turvī hiṃsāyām; Uṇādi ani; the acute on the first syllable of the suffix. ahā — in the neuter plural śeś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70) drops śi. ‖ 9 ‖

(ornamental rule)

Rik 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स नो नव्येभिर्वृषकर्मन्नुक्थैः पुरां दर्तः पायुभिः पाहि शग्मैः । दिवोदासेभिरिन्द्र स्तवानो वावृधीथा अहोभिरिव द्यौः ॥ १० ॥

sa no navyebhirvṛṣakarmannukthaiḥ purāṃ dartaḥ pāyubhiḥ pāhi śagmaiḥ | divodāsebhirindra stavāno vāvṛdhīthā ahobhiriva dyauḥ ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image: the Saṃhitā's first line is printed over two lines; the Triṣṭubh metre of the last ṛk is as stated in the table.

सः । नः । नव्येभिः । वृषकर्मन् । उक्थैः । पुराम् । दर्तः । दर्तरिति दर्तः । पायुऽभिः । पाहि । शग्मैः । दिवःऽदासेभिः । इन्द्र । स्तवानः । ववृधीथाः । अहःऽभिःऽइव । द्यौः ॥ १० ॥

saḥ | naḥ | navyebhiḥ | vṛṣakarman | ukthaiḥ | purām | dartaḥ | dartariti dartaḥ | pāyu 'bhiḥ | pāhi | śagmaiḥ | divaḥ 'dāsebhiḥ | indra | stavānaḥ | vavṛdhīthāḥ | ahaḥ 'bhiḥ 'iva | dyauḥ ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?]). Sense: "O Indra, vṛṣakarman — whose work is the showering of the desired — purāṃ dartaḥ — the splitter of the cities of demons: you, such a great one, pleased by our new (navyebhiḥ) hymns (ukthaiḥ) as now stated, protect us with protections (pāyubhiḥ) and with the happiness (śagmaiḥ) of this world and the next. And, O Indra, praised by us, the Paruccheṣas, born in the line of Divodāsa — the plural is of respect — increase (vāvṛdhīthāḥ): as dyauḥ — the shining Sun — grows by the days, so you grow by our praise."

हे इन्द्र वृषकर्मन्नभिमतवर्षणव्यापारवन् पुरां दर्तरसुरपुराणां दारयिता ॥ सुबामन्त्रिते [?] इति षष्ठ्याः पराङ्गवद्भावात्षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितसमुदायस्य पादादित्वादाष्टमिकमाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ स तादृशो महानुभावस्त्वं नोऽस्मत्सम्बन्धिभिर्नव्येभिर्नूतनैरुक्थैरिदानीं प्रतिपादितप्रकारैः स्तोत्रैस्तुष्टः सन् पायुभिः पालनप्रकारैः शग्मैः सुखैश्चैहिकामुष्मिकरूपैः पाहि । पालय । किंच हे इन्द्र दिवोदासेभिर्दिवोदासगोत्रोत्पन्नैरस्माभिः पारुच्छेपैः ॥ अश आदिभ्योऽच् । यद्वा । पूजार्थं बहुवचनम् ॥ स्तवानः स्तूयमानः कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः । वावृधीथाः प्रवृद्धो भव । वृधेर्लिङि छान्दसः शपः श्लुः । किमिव । अहोभिरिव द्यौः । द्योतनशीलः आदित्योऽहोभिः प्रसिद्धैर्यथा प्रवृद्धो भवति । तथास्मत्स्तुत्या त्वमपि प्रवृद्धो भवेत्यर्थः ॥

he indra vṛṣakarmannabhimatavarṣaṇavyāpāravan purāṃ dartarasurapurāṇāṃ dārayitā ‖ subāmantrite [?] iti ṣaṣṭhyāḥ parāṅgavadbhāvātṣaṣṭhyāmantritasamudāyasya pādāditvādāṣṭamikamādyudāttatvam ‖ sa tādṛśo mahānubhāvastvaṃ no 'smatsambandhibhirnavyebhirnūtanairukthairidānīṃ pratipāditaprakāraiḥ stotraistuṣṭaḥ san pāyubhiḥ pālanaprakāraiḥ śagmaiḥ sukhaiścaihikāmuṣmikarūpaiḥ pāhi | pālaya | kiṃca he indra divodāsebhirdivodāsagotrotpannairasmābhiḥ pārucchepaiḥ ‖ aśa ādibhyo 'c | yadvā | pūjārthaṃ bahuvacanam ‖ stavānaḥ stūyamānaḥ karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ | vāvṛdhīthāḥ pravṛddho bhava | vṛdherliṅi chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | kimiva | ahobhiriva dyauḥ | dyotanaśīlaḥ ādityo 'hobhiḥ prasiddhairyathā pravṛddho bhavati | tathāsmatstutyā tvamapi pravṛddho bhavetyarthaḥ ‖

original p. 464

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (he) indra — O Indra; vṛṣakarman — shower of the desired; puraṃ dartaḥ — destroyer of the cities of enemies (and so); saḥ — that (great one); naḥ — us; navyebhiḥ ukthaiḥ — pleased with new praises; pāyubhiḥ — with protective acts; śagmaiḥ — with happiness in this world and the next; pāhi — protect; (he indra — O Indra); divodāsebhiḥ — by us of the line of Divodāsa (Paruccheṣa) or by Divodāsa; stavānaḥ — praised; dyauḥ — the Sun; ahobhiḥ iva — as by days; vāvṛdhīthāḥ — increase.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra, giver of the desired, destroyer of the cities, great one: pleased by our new praises, protect us with protective acts and with happiness in this world and the next; and, as the Sun grows by days, so, praised by us of Divodāsa's line, grow and increase.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Showerer of benefits, destroyer of cities, propitiated by our new songs, reward us with gratifying blessings: glorified, Indra, by the descendants of Divodasa, increase (in power), like the sun in (revolving) days."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 10).

vṛṣakarman — abhimatavarṣaṇavyāpāravān: "Indra performs the work of showering rain that is desired by the world."

purāṃ dartaḥ — asurapurāṇāṃ dārayitā: "the destroyer of the cities where the demons live."

navyebhir ukthaiḥ pāyubhiḥ śagmaiḥ pāhi — "Indra, satisfied by praises recited in a new manner by the ṛṣi who saw the mantra, is prayed to protect us by the various kinds of protective acts and by the happiness of this world and the next."

original p. 465

ahobhir iva dyauḥ — dyotanaśīla ādityo 'hobhiḥ prasiddhair yathā pravṛddho bhavati kathā asmatstutyā tvam api pravṛddho bhava: "as the Sun grows through days, so may Indra, praised by Paruccheṣa, who is born in the line of Divodāsa, grow through the days and become mighty": so he wishes.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). navyebhiḥ — bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110) gives yat; yato nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213) gives the acute on the first syllable; bahulaṃ chandasi gives no ais for bhis; bahuvacane jhaly et (Pā. 7-3-103) gives e. vṛṣakarman — ṇaja sambuddhyoḥ (Pā. 8-2-8) gives no loss of n in the vocative; āmantritasya ca gives nighāta. ukthaiḥ — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; pātṛtudivaci… (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives thak; since k-marked, vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti (Pā. 6-1-15) gives saṃprasāraṇa, pūrvarūpa; coḥ kuḥ gives k for c; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. purāṃ dartaḥ — root dṝ vidāraṇe; tṛc in the agent sense; guṇa of the root because of it; in the vocative dartaḥ; by subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare (Pā. 2-1-2) the word purām is treated as part of the following so that, being at the beginning of the pāda, the aṣṭamika [i.e. āmantrita] nighāta does not occur; āmantritasya ca (Pā. 6-1-198) gives the acute on the first syllable. pāyubhiḥ — root pā rakṣaṇe; kṛvāpā… (Uṇ. 1-1) gives uṇ; ato yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ (Pā. 7-3-33) gives the augment yuk; acute on the last syllable by the suffix; instrumental plural. pāhi — as before: a loṭ second person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. divodāsebhiḥ — divodāse ṣaṣṭhyā aluk (Kāśikā 6-3-21 [?], as read "೬-೩-೨೧-೨೫") gives no loss of the genitive of divaḥ; divodāso 'sya asti iti divodāsaḥ; arśa ādibhyo 'c (Pā. 5-2-127) gives ac in the possessive sense; yasyeti ca drops a; by the suffix's accent the acute on the last syllable; by the optional rule bhis → ais for the a-ending is not required, hence ebhiḥ. Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131" [as read: "೧೩೧"].

original p. 466

stavānaḥ — root ṣṭuñ stutau; vyatyayo bahulam gives the suffix of the agent in the passive; śānac in the present sense; guṇa; avādeśa; because it follows a [word with] anudātta [as read], the lasārvadhātuka is unaccented and the root's accent remains. vāvṛdhīthāḥ — root vṛdhu vṛddhau; liṅ second person singular, suffix thās; bahulaṃ chandasi gives śluḥ for śap; ślau doubles the root; urat gives at, raparatva, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; liṅaḥ sīyuṭ (Pā. 3-4-102) gives sīyuṭ; sutiṅopor… [as read: suṭ tithoḥ, Pā. 3-4-107] gives suṭ; liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya (Pā. 7-2-79) drops both s; lopo vyor vali drops y; because at the beginning of the pāda no nighāta; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. ‖ 10 ‖

Here ends the 130th Sūkta. Kannada closing line: "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮುಗಿದುದು".

Sūkta 131 — indrāya hi dyaur asuro (begins on printed p. 466; Anuvāka 19, fifth Sūkta)

original p. 466

ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra mūvattoṃdaneya sūktavu (the one hundred and thirty-first Sūkta).

॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; several letters doubtful [?]). The Sanskrit introduction is small and in several places unreadable to me; I give what is legible and mark [?]; the sense follows.

इन्द्राय हि सप्तर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तम् । इन्द्राय सप्तेत्यनुक्रमणिका । पारुच्छेपमात्यष्टिच्छन्दः । इन्द्रो देवता ॥ पृष्ठ्यस्य षष्ठेऽहनि माध्यन्दिनसवने होत्रकाः सस्स्तशस्त्रे एतत्सूक्तं तृचत्रयं कृत्स्नारम्भणीयाभ्य ऊर्ध्वं मावपेयुः । आश्रायणं विभागः । आद्यास्तिस्त्रो मैत्रावरुणस्य । तृतीयाद्यास्तिस्रो ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः । पञ्चम्याद्यास्तिस्र उक्थावाकस्य । एतच्चतुर्थेऽहनीति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । पष्ठेऽहनीन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेत्येवमेव । आ. ८-११ [?] इति ॥ शस्त्रेऽहनि तस्मिन्नेव सवने प्रशास्त्रादीनां प्रस्थितयाज्याभ्यः पुरस्ताद्यादिते [?] … पष्ठस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेति षट् । आ. ८-१ [?] इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये इन्द्राय हीति तृचो नैकल्पिकानुरूपत्पद्यतीयः [?] । महाव्रतस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्रं याह्युप नः परावत इन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नत । ऐ. आ. ५-१-१ [?] इति ॥

indrāya hi saptarcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktam | indrāya saptetyanukramaṇikā | pārucchepamātyaṣṭicchandaḥ | indro devatā ‖ pṛṣṭhyasya ṣaṣṭhe 'hani mādhyandinasavane hotrakāḥ sasstaśastre etatsūktaṃ tṛcatrayaṃ kṛtsnārambhaṇīyābhya ūrdhvaṃ māvapeyuḥ | āśrāyaṇaṃ vibhāgaḥ | ādyāstistro maitrāvaruṇasya | tṛtīyādyāstisro brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ | pañcamyādyāstisra ukthāvākasya | etaccaturthe 'hanīti khaṇḍe sūtritam | paṣṭhe 'hanīndrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnatetyevameva | ā. 8-11 [?] iti ‖ śastre 'hani tasminneva savane praśāstrādīnāṃ prasthitayājyābhyaḥ purastādyādite [?] … paṣṭhasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnateti ṣaṭ | ā. 8-1 [?] iti ‖ mahāvrate niṣkevalye indrāya hīti tṛco naikalpikānurūpatpadyatīyaḥ [?] | mahāvratasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indraṃ yāhyupa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnata | ai. ā. 5-1-1 [?] iti ‖

Kannada anuvāda (translated). Anuvāda — This Sūkta indrāya hi dyaur asuraḥ is the fifth Sūkta in the nineteenth Anuvāka. It has seven ṛks; the Anukramaṇikā says "indrāya sapta". The ṛṣi is Paruccheṣa; the deity is Indra; the metre is Atyaṣṭi. On the sixth day of the pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha sacrifice, at the midday pressing, the ṛks seen by this ṛṣi, which the hotrakas recite as sasta-śastra mantras, are used; of these ṛks the first three are for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest, the next three for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the last three for the Ukthāvāka [as read; the allotment is doubtful: [?]]. This is expounded in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning "ṣaṣṭhe 'hani", by the sūtra indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata (Āś. 8-1 [?]; as read "೮-೧೧" in one place and "೮-೧" in another). In the mahāvrata sacrifice, in the niṣkevalya śastra, the three ṛks beginning indrāya hi are used as anurūpa — as stated by Śaunaka in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, in the section mahāvratasya, by the sūtra indraṃ yāhy upa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata (Ait. Ār. 5-1-1 [?]). Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read: "೨೦"]. The Kannada anuvāda of the introduction, continued from p. 466: at the midday pressing this Sūkta is made into three tṛcas (groups of three ṛks) and recited, and the stomāvāpa is done after them; the division is: the first three ṛks for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest, the next three for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the last for the Acchāvāka — as stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section caturthe 'hani, by the sūtra ṣaṣṭhe 'hani indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata (Āś. 8-11 [?], as read). On the same day, at the same pressing, the six ṛks of this Sūkta are recited one by one by the Praśāstṛ and others as preliminary to the prasthitayājyā mantras, by the sūtra indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnateti ṣaṭ in the section ṣaṣṭhasya (Āś. 8-1 [?]). In the mahāvrata, at the niṣkevalya śastra, the three ṛks beginning indrāya hi are recited as alternative anurūpa ṛks, by Śaunaka's Aitareya Āraṇyaka sūtra indraṃ yāhy upa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata (Ait. Ār. 5-1-1 [?]).

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".

इन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेन्द्राय मही पृथिवी वरीमभिः । द्युम्नसाता वरीमभिः । इन्द्रं विश्वे सजोषसो देवासो दधिरे पुरः । इन्द्राय विश्वा सवनानि मानुषा रातानि सन्तु मानुषा ॥ १ ॥

indrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnatendrāya mahī pṛthivī varīmabhiḥ | dyumnasātā varīmabhiḥ | indraṃ viśve sajoṣaso devāso dadhire puraḥ | indrāya viśvā savanāni mānuṣā rātāni santu mānuṣā ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

इन्द्राय । हि । द्यौः । असुरः । अनम्नत । इन्द्राय । मही । पृथिवी । वरीमऽभिः । द्युम्नऽसाता । वरीमऽभिः । इन्द्रम् । विश्वे । सऽजोषसः । देवासः । दधिरे । पुरः । इन्द्राय । विश्वा । सवनानि । मानुषा । रातानि । सन्तु । मानुषा ॥ १ ॥

indrāya | hi | dyauḥ | asuraḥ | anamnata | indrāya | mahī | pṛthivī | varīma 'bhiḥ | dyumna 'sātā | varīma 'bhiḥ | indram | viśve | sa 'joṣasaḥ | devāsaḥ | dadhire | puraḥ | indrāya | viśvā | savanāni | mānuṣā | rātāni | santu | mānuṣā ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?]). Sense: "Heaven (dyauḥ, the shining heaven-world, or the host of gods who dwell there) and the asura (the repeller of enemies, because the dwellers there are the righteous) bows (anamnata) to Indra alone, of its own accord. [Grammar: the Vedic luṅ of nam, the ātmanepada in the intransitive sense; na duhasnunamām yag abhāvaḥ (Pā. 3-1-89 [?]); śluḥ for śap; no halādiśeṣa; loss of the nasal.] hi is for emphasis. So for Indra the great earth (mahī pṛthivī) — or all people dwelling on it — bows; the words naming the support stand for the supported, as in 'the village has come'. By what means? varīmabhiḥ — by choice praises or oblations. And when there is dyumnasātā — winning food or fame — the sacrificers, furnished with choice oblations, bow. And all the gods (viśve devāsaḥ), united in affection (sajoṣasaḥ), of one mind, formerly put Indra in front (puro dadhire) to conquer the demons: they conquered the demons through Indra. Likewise may the human pressings (mānuṣā savanāni), the morning and other pressings, be for Indra alone; and the offerings to be given by the human priests, the puroḍāśa and the rest, be for Indra, able to please him."

द्यौर्द्योतनशीलो द्युलोकस्तन्निवासी देवसंघो वा स चासुरो निरसनशीलः शत्रूणां पुण्यकृतामेव तन्निवासात् । इन्द्रायै हीन्द्रायैवानम्नत । स्वयमेव प्रह्वीभवति ॥ नमेश्छान्दसे लुङ् [?] कर्मकर्तर्यात्मनेपदम् । न दुहस्नुनमामिति यगभावः । पा. ३-१-८९ ॥ छान्दसः शपः श्लुः । हलादिशेषाभावश्च । अनुनासिकलोपः ॥ हिशब्दः प्रसिद्ध्यर्थो वा । तथेन्द्रायेन्द्रार्थं मही महती पृथिवी भूमिस्तत्रत्यः सर्वो जनो वानम्नत । उभयत्राश्रयवाचिशब्देनाश्रया लक्ष्यन्ते ग्राम आगत इतिवत् । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । वरीमभिर्वरणीयैः स्तोत्रैर्हविर्भिर्वा । किंच द्युम्नसाता द्युम्नसातावन्नस्य यशसो वा लाभे सति वरीमभिर्वरणीयैर्हविर्भिर्युक्ता यजमानाः प्रह्वा भवन्ति । किंचेन्द्रमेव विश्वे सर्वे देवासो देवाः सजोषसः समानप्रीतियुक्ता ऐकमत्यभाजः पूर्वमसुरजयार्थं पुरो दधिरे । पुरतः स्थापितवन्तः । इन्द्रमुखेनैवासुराञ्जितवन्त इत्यर्थः । तथा मानुषा सवनानि मनुष्याणां सम्बन्धीन्यभिषवयुक्तानि प्रातरादिसवनानीन्द्रायैव सन्तु । इन्द्रायैव भवन्तु । तथा मानुषा मनुष्याणामृत्विजां सम्बन्धीनि रातानि दातव्यानि पुरोडाशादीनीन्द्रायैव सन्तु । इन्द्रं प्रीणयितुं समर्थानि भवन्तित्यर्थः ॥

dyaurdyotanaśīlo dyulokastannivāsī devasaṃgho vā sa cāsuro nirasanaśīlaḥ śatrūṇāṃ puṇyakṛtāmeva tannivāsāt | indrāyai hīndrāyaivānamnata | svayameva prahvībhavati ‖ nameśchāndase luṅ [?] karmakartaryātmanepadam | na duhasnunamāmiti yagabhāvaḥ | pā. 3-1-89 ‖ chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | halādiśeṣābhāvaśca | anunāsikalopaḥ ‖ hiśabdaḥ prasiddhyartho vā | tathendrāyendrārthaṃ mahī mahatī pṛthivī bhūmistatratyaḥ sarvo jano vānamnata | ubhayatrāśrayavāciśabdenāśrayā lakṣyante grāma āgata itivat | kena sādhaneneti taducyate | varīmabhirvaraṇīyaiḥ stotrairhavirbhirvā | kiṃca dyumnasātā dyumnasātāvannasya yaśaso vā lābhe sati varīmabhirvaraṇīyairhavirbhiryuktā yajamānāḥ prahvā bhavanti | kiṃcendrameva viśve sarve devāso devāḥ sajoṣasaḥ samānaprītiyuktā aikamatyabhājaḥ pūrvamasurajayārthaṃ puro dadhire | purataḥ sthāpitavantaḥ | indramukhenaivāsurāñjitavanta ityarthaḥ | tathā mānuṣā savanāni manuṣyāṇāṃ sambandhīnyabhiṣavayuktāni prātarādisavanānīndrāyaiva santu | indrāyaiva bhavantu | tathā mānuṣā manuṣyāṇāmṛtvijāṃ sambandhīni rātāni dātavyāni puroḍāśādīnīndrāyaiva santu | indraṃ prīṇayituṃ samarthāni bhavantityarthaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. asuraḥ — the repeller of enemies (that gives no room for enemies); dyauḥ — the heaven-world; indrāya hi — to Indra only; anamnata — bows [becomes submissive]; indrāya — to Indra; mahī — the great; pṛthivī — the earth (the people on it); varīmabhiḥ — by praises (oblations); anamnata — bow; dyumnasātā — for food or the winning of fame; varīmabhiḥ — with oblations; (anamnata — they bow); viśve devāsaḥ — all the gods; sajoṣasaḥ — with equal affection (in unity, for conquering the demons); puraḥ dadhire — placed in front (made Indra the leader and conquered the demons by him); mānuṣā — belonging to men; viśvā savanāni — all pressings (connected with extraction, the morning and others); indrāya santu — be for Indra; mānuṣā — belonging to men (the priests); rātāni — offerings to be given (the puroḍāśa and the rest); (indrāya santu — be for Indra). Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].

original p. 469

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The heaven-world, that gives no room to the wicked, is subject to Indra alone; with offerings that have no equal this great earth is submissive to Indra; for food or fame, the sacrificers worship Indra; the gods, united in affection (in agreement, for conquering the demons), gave Indra the first place; may the pressings of men be for Indra; may the puroḍāśa and other offerings made by men be for Indra.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "To Indra heaven, that excludes the wicked, verily has bowed: to Indra the wide-spread earth (has offered homage) with acceptable (praises); with acceptable praises (the worshipper has propitiated Indra) for the sake of food: all the gods well pleased have given precedence to Indra: let all the sacrifices of men (be appropriated) to Indra; let all the offerings of men be (presented to him)."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).

dyauḥ — dyotanaśīlaḥ dyulokaḥ tannivāsī devasaṅgho vā: "the shining heaven-world, or the company of gods who dwell there." The word dyauḥ is recorded among the twelve names of day (vastoḥ, dyauḥ, bhānuḥ etc.; Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೨೦" [?]). And —

त्वमग्ने द्युभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिस्त्वमद्भ्यस्त्वमश्मनस्परि । त्वं वनेभ्यस्त्वमोषधीभ्यस्त्वं नृणां नृपते जायसे शुचिः ॥

tvam agne dyubhis tvam āśuśukṣaṇis tvam adbhyas tvam aśmanas pari | tvaṃ vanebhyas tvam oṣadhībhyas tvaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛpate jāyase śuciḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-1, as read "೨-೧-೧"; the same Ṛk was cited on p. 430.) Here dyubhiḥ is explained as ahobhiḥ ("by days").

original p. 470

उप श्वासय पृथिवीमुत द्यां पुरुत्रा ते मनुतां विष्ठितं जगत् । स दुन्दुभे सजूरिन्द्रेण देवैर्दूराद्दवीयो अप सेध शत्रून् ॥

upa śvāsaya pṛthivīm uta dyāṃ purutrā te manutāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat | sa dundubhe sajūr indreṇa devair dūrād davīyo apa sedha śatrūn ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-29, as read "೬-೪೭-೨೯".) In this Ṛk dyām is explained as divam. Sāyaṇa explains dyauḥ as "the heaven-world", very bright, or as "the company of the gods who live in the heaven-world".

asuraḥ indrāya hi anamnata — śatrūṇāṃ nirasanaśīlaḥ indrāyaiva svayam eva prahvo bhavati: the word asura is recorded among the names of cloud (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೩೧"). The Niruktakāra —

तदिद्ध्यस्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीयं येनासुरां अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जादः उत यज्ञियासः पञ्च जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वम् ॥

tad id dhy asya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīyaṃ yenāsurām̐ abhi devā asāma | ūrjādaḥ uta yajñiyāsaḥ pañca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4, as read "೧೦-೫೩-೪".) — citing this Ṛk, explains asurāḥ asuratāḥ sthāneṣu sthāneṣu [?] — "the asuras are so called because (asu = breath) or because they are 'not set' (a-sthita)": "asuḥ prāṇaḥ tena tadvantaḥ", and by so 'deva… sa devān asṛjata tat surāṇāṃ suratvam: "he created the gods; that is the god-hood of the gods; asor asurān asṛjata tad asurāṇām asuratvam": so it is known (Ni. 3-[?]). Durgācārya says, "one who stands in one place, firm, as persons of fickle mind who flee to other places, are gods or ... ; because they stand firmly (asthitāḥ) they are asuras"; or, as stated in the Śruti "ūrdhvam udait pūrvapakṣaḥ … tena sa devān asṛjata tat surāṇāṃ suratvam": "Brahmā, by his excellent self, created gods; therefore they are suras"; "arvāñjyotir … aparapakṣaḥ … tenāsurān asṛjata": "the later half [of the day] has the name asu, hence he created the asuras": so he explains (see Ṛg-Saṃhitā vol. 10, pp. 8–9 in this edition).

Sāyaṇa explains asura as "one who is cast out by the company of the gods", and so as "one who is not suited to dwell in the heaven-world, where only the righteous have a place"; thus he points out the greatness of Indra, to whom the great heaven-world is itself subservient.

indrāya mahī pṛthivī anamnata — indrārthaṃ mahatī pṛthivī tatratyaḥ sarvo jano vā anamnata | ubhayatrāśrayavācī śabdenāśrayā lakṣyate | grāmaḥ āgata itivat: "heaven and the earth, the dwelling-places of the gods and of men, are named by the words dyauḥ and pṛthivī; here the dwellers are meant by these words."

original p. 471

(…) As one says, "the village has come" — when what comes is the people of the village; so here the people living on the earth are meant by the word "earth". The gods too are subject to Indra; the people on the earth also are submissive to Indra of their own accord; and the earth is subject to Indra in every way.

varīmabhiḥ dyumnasātā varīmabhiḥ — stotraiḥ havirbhir vā annasya yaśaso vā lābhe sati havirbhir yuktāḥ yajamānāḥ prahvā bhavanti: "the sacrificers, who are fit to propitiate the god they desire, by praises or by oblations bow down again to the gods, to offer oblations, because they have obtained food and fame." The words varīmabhiḥ are used twice; in the one the meaning is varaṇīya, "to be chosen"; in the second varaṇīyair havirbhiḥ, "with oblations that are choice".

The word dyumna is recorded among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯") and in dyumnam adhiraṣmaṃ ca dhehi [as read] dyumnaṃ dyoter yaśo vā annaṃ vā (Ni. 5-[?]; as read "೫-೬") the word is explained: dyumna from the root dyut gives the many senses "fame" or "food", as Yāska says.

sajoṣasaḥ puro dadhire — samānaprītiyuktā aikamatyabhājaḥ: "gods, united in affection for each other, in agreement, to conquer the demons, made Indra their leader and by him obtained victory". The word sajoṣas is explained in the Nirukta as "joined" (Ni. 8-[?]; as read "೮-೮"). —

आजुह्वान ईड्यो वन्द्यश्चा याह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः । त्वं देवानामसि यह्व होता स एनान्यक्षीषितो यजीयान् ॥

ājuhvāna īḍyo vandyaś cā yāhy agne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ | tvaṃ devānām asi yahva hotā sa enān yakṣīṣito yajīyān ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-[?], as read "೧೦-೧೧೦-೩".) Here sajoṣāḥ is explained as saha joṣaṇaḥ samānaprītiyuktaḥ. And —

आ रुद्रासः इन्द्रवन्तः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गन्तन । इयं वो अस्मत्प्रति हर्यते मतिस्तृणाजे [?] न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ॥

ā rudrāsa indravantaḥ sajoṣaso hiraṇyarathāḥ suvitāya gantana | iyaṃ vo asmat prati haryate matis tṛṇāje [?] na diva utsā udanyave ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-[?] as read "೫-೩-೧-೧"? [?]; small type, doubtful.) Here, indreṇa saha joṣaṇāḥ sajoṣasaḥ, "served together with Indra in the greatness of lordship": as the reading in small type is unclear, the explanation is given only as read.

original p. 472

mānuṣā savanāni indrāya santu — "May the pressings (extracting the Soma-juice), by which men bring the Soma and grind it and prepare the morning libation, be for Indra."

mānuṣā rātāni — "The mantra-seer prays, in a fit of inspiration, that the puroḍāśa and other offerings made by the priests may be able to please Indra alone."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). asuraḥ — root asu kṣepaṇe; āser uraN (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives uran; jñityādir nityam gives the acute on the first syllable. anamnata — root ṇamu prahvatve śabde ca; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6) gives laṅ in the present sense; since the agent of the middle-sense is intended, karmavat karmaṇā tulyakriyaḥ (Pā. 3-1-87) gives the ātmanepada; third person singular ta; namatiśapo… [as read: na duhasnunamāṃ yag …] — no yak; śluḥ in place of śap; the root is doubled; no halādiśeṣa in the reduplicative; anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti (Pā. 6-4-37) drops the nasal; the augment aṭ; because hi is connected, hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34) forbids nighāta; the augment being acute, the first syllable is acute. pṛthivī — root pratha prakhyāne; pratheḥ ṣivan saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives ṣivan; in the feminine ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca (Pā. 4-1-41) gives ṅīṣ; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. varīmabhiḥ — root vṛñ varaṇe; Uṇādi īman with ninc; guṇa of the root by the suffix with raparatva; since n-marked the acute on the first syllable. dadhire — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; liṭ third person plural; tiṅ-nighāta. savanāni — root ṣuñ abhiṣave; lyuṭ; yuvor anākau gives ana; liti gives the acute before the suffix.

original p. 473

Grammar of Ṛk 1, concluded; numbers as printed. mānuṣā — manuṣyasya imāni mānuṣāṇi; the suffix aṇ in the sense of relation; acute on the last syllable by the suffix; in the neuter plural śeś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70) drops śi. rātāni — root rā ādāne; kta; accent by the suffix. santu — root as bhuvi; loṭ third person plural; tiṅ-nighāta. ‖ 1 ‖

(ornamental rule)

Rik 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

विश्वेषु हि त्वा सवनेषु तुञ्जते समानमेकं वृषमण्यवः । पृथक् स्वः सनिष्यवः पृथक् । तं त्वा नावं न पर्षणिं शूषस्य धुरि धीमहि । इन्द्रं न यज्ञैश्चितयन्त आयवः स्तोमेभिरिन्द्रमायवः ॥ २ ॥

viśveṣu hi tvā savaneṣu tuñjate samānamekaṃ vṛṣamaṇyavaḥ | pṛthak svaḥ saniṣyavaḥ pṛthak | taṃ tvā nāvaṃ na parṣaṇiṃ śūṣasya dhuri dhīmahi | indraṃ na yajñaiścitayanta āyavaḥ stomebhirindramāyavaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image: the Pada gives vṛṣa-manyavaḥ, svar iti svaḥ, sanisyavaḥ; the Saṃhitā's first line prints "tuñjate samānam ekaṃ vṛṣamaṇyavaḥ", and in the Pada "vṛṣamanyavaḥ" — the Saṃhitā spelling with ṇ is as printed.

विश्वेषु । हि । त्वा । सवनेषु । तुञ्जते । समानम् । एकम् । वृषऽमन्यवः । पृथक् । स्वः । सनिष्यवः । पृथक् । तम् । त्वा । नावम् । न । पर्षणिम् । शूषस्य । धुरि । धीमहि । इन्द्रम् । न । यज्ञैः । चितयन्तः । आयवः । स्तोमेभिः । इन्द्रम् । आयवः ॥ २ ॥

viśveṣu | hi | tvā | savaneṣu | tuñjate | samānam | ekam | vṛṣa 'manyavaḥ | pṛthak | svaḥ | saniṣyavaḥ | pṛthak | tam | tvā | nāvam | na | parṣaṇim | śūṣasya | dhuri | dhīmahi | indram | na | yajñaiḥ | citayantaḥ | āyavaḥ | stomebhiḥ | indram | āyavaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, doubtful places [?]).

हे इन्द्र त्वा त्वामेकमेकमेव सन्तं विश्वेषु सर्वेषु सवनेषु तद्वत्सु स्वैः [?] काहाहीनसत्ररूपेषु सर्वेषु सोमयागेषु यजमानास्तुञ्जते । त्वरयन्ति । हविरादीनि ददते । कीदृशं त्वाम् । समानं सर्वेषामेकरूपम् । कीदृशा यजमानाः । वृषमण्यवो वृषमन्यवः । अभिमतवर्षणाय त्वामेव मन्यमानाः । पृथग्भिन्नरूपैः [?] । पृथगेव त्वरयन्ति । पृथक् प्रत्येकं तत्तद्यागेषु हविरादीनि दद्युः । तुञ्जतिर्दानार्थः । शिक्षति तुञ्जत इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तं तादृशं त्वा त्वां शूषस्य बलस्य सेनारूपस्य धुरि वहने तज्जयाय धीमहि । स्थापयामः । यद्वा । शूषस्य सुखस्य । शरीरबलस्य [?] धुरि धीमहि । शूषमिति बलनाम । शूषं सह इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । पर्षणिं नावं न पारस्य सम्भक्त्रीं पूरयित्रीं वा फलस्य नावमिव । तां यथा भारवहने स्थापयन्ति । पारतीरं कर्मसमाप्तौ [?] । छन्दसि वनसनेति सनेरिन्प्रत्ययः । पृषोदरादित्वाद् [?] । पिपर्तेर्वौणादिकः सनिप्रत्ययो वा ॥ कीदृशा वयम् । आयवो मनुष्या यजमाना यज्ञैः साधनैरिन्द्रं न चितयन्तः परमेश्वरमिव त्वां चेतयन्तः । परमेश्वरबुद्ध्या भावयन्त इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । नशब्द उपमार्थः । इन्द्रमेव त्वां जानन्तः । तथा स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैरिन्द्रमिन्द्रमेवायवो गच्छन्तो वयं धीमहि ॥ दधातेर्लिङि [?] छान्दसः शपो लुक् ॥

he indra tvā tvāmekamekameva santaṃ viśveṣu sarveṣu savaneṣu tadvatsu svaiḥ [?] kāhāhīnasatrarūpeṣu sarveṣu somayāgeṣu yajamānāstuñjate | tvarayanti | havirādīni dadate | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | samānaṃ sarveṣāmekarūpam | kīdṛśā yajamānāḥ | vṛṣamaṇyavo vṛṣamanyavaḥ | abhimatavarṣaṇāya tvāmeva manyamānāḥ | pṛthagbhinnarūpaiḥ [?] | pṛthageva tvarayanti | pṛthak pratyekaṃ tattadyāgeṣu havirādīni dadyuḥ | tuñjatirdānārthaḥ | śikṣati tuñjata iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | taṃ tādṛśaṃ tvā tvāṃ śūṣasya balasya senārūpasya dhuri vahane tajjayāya dhīmahi | sthāpayāmaḥ | yadvā | śūṣasya sukhasya | śarīrabalasya [?] dhuri dhīmahi | śūṣamiti balanāma | śūṣaṃ saha iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | parṣaṇiṃ nāvaṃ na pārasya sambhaktrīṃ pūrayitrīṃ vā phalasya nāvamiva | tāṃ yathā bhāravahane sthāpayanti | pāratīraṃ karmasamāptau [?] | chandasi vanasaneti sanerinpratyayaḥ | pṛṣodarāditvād [?] | pipartervauṇādikaḥ sanipratyayo vā ‖ kīdṛśā vayam | āyavo manuṣyā yajamānā yajñaiḥ sādhanairindraṃ na citayantaḥ parameśvaramiva tvāṃ cetayantaḥ | parameśvarabuddhyā bhāvayanta ityarthaḥ | yadvā | naśabda upamārthaḥ | indrameva tvāṃ jānantaḥ | tathā stomebhiḥ stotrairindramindramevāyavo gacchanto vayaṃ dhīmahi ‖ dadhāterliṅi [?] chāndasaḥ śapo luk ‖

(Sense: "O Indra, in all pressings (savaneṣu) — the Soma sacrifices of all kinds, the one-day, the several-day, the long sessions — the sacrificers, regarding you alone, samānam ekam* — the same for all, of one form — urge (tuñjate) and give oblations; they are vṛṣamanyavaḥ, thinking of you as the showerer of the desired; pṛthak — each separately, in their own several sacrifices, giving oblations (tuñj is a verb of giving: 'śikṣati tuñjate' in the lists of its names); svaḥ sanisyavaḥ — each desiring heaven. Such as you are we place (dhīmahi) at the yoke of śūṣa — strength, in the form of an army — for victory over it; or śūṣa is happiness or bodily strength (the word śūṣa is recorded among the names of strength). The example: like a boat (nāvaṃ na parṣaṇim) that carries one across — a ferry that is placed to bear the burden to the other bank, or fills the fruit; we the āyavaḥ, men, sacrificers, by sacrifices thinking of you as the Supreme Lord, or na is a word of comparison: knowing you as Indra alone; and with stomas, going to Indra alone, we meditate."*)

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (he indra — O Indra); viśveṣu savaneṣu — in all Soma sacrifices; (yajamānāḥ — the sacrificers); pṛthak — each separately (in their own sacrifices); vṛṣamanyavaḥ — thinking of you as the showerer of desires; samānam — the same for all; ekam — one; tvā — you; tuñjate — urge (and give oblations); hi — indeed; svaḥ — heaven; sanisyavaḥ — those desiring to obtain; pṛthak — separately (urge you); tam — such; tvā — you; śūṣasya — of strength (of the army); dhuri — at the yoke (to bear it, for victory); parṣaṇim — one who carries across; nāvaṃ na — like a boat (put to bear the load); dhīmahi — we place; āyavaḥ — we men (sacrificers); yajñaiḥ — by sacrifices; indraṃ na — as the Supreme Lord; citayantaḥ — meditating; kathā — likewise; stomebhiḥ — with hymns; indram — Indra; āyavaḥ — going to him (we place, delighting him).

original p. 474

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Your worshippers, regarding you alone as the showerer of the desired, offer oblations to you in all the sacrifices, each separately, in their several sacrifices; each, desiring heaven (happiness), regards you; we too, regarding you as the Supreme Lord, thinking of you — you who are the support of our strength, like a boat that carries men across — we please you with hymns and with the means of sacrifice; we, the sacrificers, regarding you as Indra, meditate on you, going to you alone with hymns. The Kannada bhāvārtha as printed is rendered above: "(Your worshippers), regarding you alone as the bestower of what is wished, each separately in each sacrifice regard you; each desiring heaven, seeking your protection; we, regarding you as Indra, praise you only, as the support of our strength, like a ferry-boat that carries (people) across…" Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read: "೨೧"].

original p. 475

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Hoping to partake of your bounties, (your worshippers) hasten severally in every rite to (adore) you, who ask one and all; each severally seeking heaven. We meditate on you, the sustainer of our strength, like a boat that bears (passengers) across (a stream): mortals, indeed, knowing Indra, propitiate him with sacrifices: mortals (propitiate him) with hymns."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).

vṛṣamanyavaḥ samānam ekaṃ viśveṣu savaneṣu tuñjate — abhimatavarṣaṇāya tvām eva manyamānāḥ sarveṣām ekarūpam ekam eva santam ekāhīnasatrarūpeṣu somayāgeṣu tvarayanti havirādīni dadate: "regarding you alone as the one who gives what is wished, the sacrificers, in the one-day (ekāha), several-day (ahīna) and long (satra) Soma sacrifices, urge you and give you oblations. In the matter of fulfilling their desires every one is equally partial to Indra: they believe he is the only one. In the Soma sacrifices of one day etc., consisting of the three pressings in morning and the rest, they offer oblations to Indra": so the meaning.

The Niruktakāra says that tuñjati is recorded among the ten verbs of giving beginning dāti, dāśati (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೯"). And —

तुञ्जेतुञ्जे य उत्तरे स्तोमा इन्द्रस्य वज्रिणः । न विन्धे अस्य सुष्टुतिम् ॥

tuñje-tuñje ya uttare stomā indrasya vajriṇaḥ | na vindhe asya suṣṭutim ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೭-೭" [?]; small type.) citing this, he explains tuñje tuñje as dāne dāne; Durgācārya says the word tuj is a synonym of dāna, "giving".

pṛthak svaḥ sanisyavaḥ — "the sacrificers, who perform the sacrifices separately, each offering oblations to Indra in their own sacrifices, desire heaven or extraordinary happiness". The word svaḥ is recorded among the six common names svaḥ, pṛśniḥ (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೩") and is explained: svar ādityo bhavati, su araṇaḥ, su īraṇaḥ, svato rasān, svato bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām, svato bhāsety vā (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೧೪"), recorded also among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; "೧-೩೪"). And —

original p. 476

परं मृत्यो अनु परेहि पन्थां यस्ते स्व इतरो देवयानात् । चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते ते ब्रवीमि मा नः प्रजां रीरिषो मोत वीरान् ॥

paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi panthāṃ yas te sva itaro devayānāt | cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi mā naḥ prajāṃ rīriṣo mota vīrān ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-18-1, as read "೧೦-೧೮-೧".) In this Ṛk the word sva is explained as "your own".

śūṣasya dhuri dhīmahi — senārūpasya balasya vahane jayāya sthāpayāmaḥ | yadvāsmadīyaśārīrabalasya dhuri dhīmahi: two meanings are given for the word śūṣa. In the first, the strength in the form of an army; that we the sacrificers may be in the front in conquering the army; in the second, to increase greatly the strength of our body, as sacrificers, Indra is first prayed to. Since the word śūṣa is recorded among the eight names of strength (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"), Sāyaṇa gives two meanings of "strength": army, or bodily strength.

parṣaṇiṃ nāvaṃ na — pārasya sambhaktrīṃ pūrayitrīṃ vā phalasya nāvam iva: "as a boat that carries a heavy load and countless things is placed to bring it to the far shore of the sea, and gives the fruit": so Indra is compared; he gives the sacrificer the completion of the sacrifice and its fruit.

āyavaḥ indraṃ na citayantaḥ — manuṣyāḥ yajamānāḥ parameśvaram iva tvāṃ bhāvayantaḥ | yadvā na śabda upamārthaḥ | indram eva tvāṃ jānantaḥ: "men, sacrificers, regarding you as the Supreme Lord; or na is in the sense of emphasis: knowing you, the very Indra." The word āyavaḥ is used twice. The Niruktakāra reads āyavaḥ among the names of men (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೮"). In the first meaning, "sacrificers"; "regarding Indra as the Supreme Lord, they satisfy him by sacrifices". Indater aiśvaryakarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 10-[?]; as read "೧೦-೮") — the word indra is formed from the root ind, expressing lordship, so that indra gives the sense "one who has lordship and gives it"; and, since those who sacrifice regard him as the Supreme Lord, it is explained. Or, when the Niruktakāra explains the word indra: idaṃ bhūtānīti vā [as read: indhe bhūtāni], "tad yad enaṃ prāṇaiḥ samaindhaṃs tad indrasyendratvam iti vijñāyate" — "he kindles creatures; because the gods kindled him with the vital breaths, that is Indra's Indra-ness": it is explained that he makes living beings brilliant. Durgācārya: "bhūtāni hy asya adhidevatvena adhyātmatvena abhyavahārayan vibhajamānaś ca dīpayati dyumantaṃ karoti" — he is within beings as presiding deity and within the self, and, dividing, kindles and makes them brilliant. Therefore, the meaning of the word indra is stated: that he is the Supreme Lord. Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read].

original p. 477

In the second meaning the word āyavaḥ is explained as "those who know"; Indra, who has the nature of supreme lordship, is known as the Supreme Lord, and we, the sacrificers, meditate on him by sacrifices and by hymns. And since particles have many meanings, na is explained as having the sense of comparison and of emphasis.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). tuñjate — tuja is a sautra root of the sense "giving"; śikṣati tuñjate (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೨೦-೮"?) is read among the verbs of giving; laṭ third person plural; hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34) forbids nighāta; acute on the first syllable of the suffix. vṛṣamanyavaḥ — root mana jñāne; yaji-mani… (Uṇ. 3-[?]) gives yuc; in the compound the acute on the first syllable; nominative plural. svaḥ — svar becomes svarita by Phiṭ-sūtra 4 [as read]. sanisyavaḥ — root ṣaṇu dāne; in sarvadhātubhyaḥ [as read: iṇ sarvadhātubhyaḥ, Uṇ. 4-[?]] gives iṇ; when "desiring to give" is intended, supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8) gives kyac; sarvaprātipadikebhyo lālasāyām asuk vaktavyaḥ… [as read: Kāś. 3-1-8 vārttika] gives suk; after the kyac-ending, kyāc chandasi (Pā. 3-2-170) gives u; ato lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-48) drops the a of kyac; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. parṣaṇim — root pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ or paṇa sambhaktau; chandasi vanasana… (Pā. 3-2-27) gives in; with pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam the form is obtained; the acute on the first syllable by the suffix. dhīmahi — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; liṅ first person plural, mahiṅ; bahulaṃ chandasi gives luk of the vikaraṇa; since the suffix is j-marked, ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali (Pā. 6-4-66) gives ī; tiṅ-nighāta.

original p. 478

Grammar, concluded. citayantaḥ — root citī saṃjñāne; satyāpapāśa… (Pā. 3-1-25) gives ṇic in the proper sense; by the statement saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ no guṇa; after the ṇic-ending, śatṛ in the present sense; guṇa, ayādeśa of the ṇic; the acute of ṇic. āyavaḥ — root iṇ gatau; chandasīṇaḥ (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives uṇ; aco ñṇiti gives vṛddhi; ayādeśa; nominative plural. stomebhiḥ — by bahulaṃ chandasi, bhis takes ais optionally; since it is optional, bahuvacane jhaly et (Pā. 7-3-103) gives e. ‖ 2 ‖

Rik 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

वि त्वा ततस्रे मिथुना अवस्यवो व्रजस्य साता गव्यस्य निःसृजः । सक्षन्त इन्द्र निःसृजः । यद्गव्यन्ता द्वा जना स्वर्यन्ता समूहसि । आविष्करिक्रद्वृषणं सचाभुवं वज्रमिन्द्र सचाभुवम् ॥ ३ ॥

vi tvā tatasre mithunā avasyavo vrajasya sātā gavyasya niḥsṛjaḥ | sakṣanta indra niḥsṛjaḥ | yadgavyantā dvā janā svaryantā samūhasi | āviṣkarikradvṛṣaṇaṃ sacābhuvaṃ vajramindra sacābhuvam ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image; in the Saṃhitā's third line the print has "gavyantā dvā janā svaryantā samūhasi"; the Pada writes dvā as a separate word. Doubtful letters in the Saṃhitā: "ततस्रे" is the form as printed.

वि । त्वा । ततस्रे । मिथुनाः । अवस्यवः । व्रजस्य । साता । गव्यस्य । निःऽसृजः । सक्षन्तः । इन्द्र । निःऽसृजः । यत् । गव्यन्ता । द्वा । जना । स्वःऽयन्ता । सम्ऽऊहसि । आविः । करिक्रत् । वृषणम् । सचाऽभुवम् । वज्रम् । इन्द्र । सचाऽभुवम् ॥ ३ ॥
