Rik 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

त्वं तमिन्द्र वावृधानो अस्मयुरमित्रयन्तं तुविजात मर्त्यम् । वज्रेण शूर मर्त्यम् । जहि यो नो अघायति शृणुष्व सुश्रवस्तमः । रिष्टं न यामन्नप भूतु दुर्मतिर्विश्वाप भूतु दुर्मतिः ॥ ७ ॥

tvaṃ tamindra vāvṛdhāno asmayuramitrayantaṃ tuvijāta martyam | vajreṇa śūra martyam | jahi yo no aghāyati śṛṇuṣva suśravastamaḥ | riṣṭaṃ na yāmannapa bhūtu durmatirviśvāpa bhūtu durmatiḥ ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image: the Pada gives vavṛdhānaḥ, asmayuḥ; the Saṃhitā prints "vāvṛdhāno".

त्वम् । तम् । इन्द्र । ववृधानः । अस्मयुः । अमित्रयन्तम् । तुविऽजात । मर्त्यम् । वज्रेण । शूर । मर्त्यम् । जहि । यः । नः । अघऽयति । शृणुष्व । सुश्रवःऽतमः । रिष्टम् । न । यामन् । अप । भूतु । दुःऽमतिः । विश्वा । अप । भूतु । दुःऽमतिः ॥ ७ ॥

tvam | tam | indra | vavṛdhānaḥ | asmayuḥ | amitrayantam | tuvi 'jāta | martyam | vajreṇa | śūra | martyam | jahi | yaḥ | naḥ | agha 'yati | śṛṇuṣva | suśravaḥ 'tamaḥ | riṣṭam | na | yāman | apa | bhūtu | duḥ 'matiḥ | viśvā | apa | bhūtu | duḥ 'matiḥ ‖ 7 ‖

original p. 498

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?]). Sense: "O Indra, tuvijāta — taking many forms — brave, you, growing (vāvṛdhānaḥ), desiring us (asmayuḥ), strike with your thunderbolt that mortal, acting as an enemy (amitrayantam) toward us, mortal by nature. [Grammar: jahi with the substitute jā for han; the hi is not dropped by asiddhavad atrābhāt.] Which mortal? Whoever wishes us harm (aghāyati: agha is sin or pain); strike him. And hear (śṛṇuṣva), you most renowned (suśravastamaḥ). How? O Indra, by your grace may the evil intent (durmatiḥ) — the mind bent on harm — be gone (apa bhūtu); not only that of harm but all evil intent in the form of anger or abuse. The example: as a weary traveller on the road (yāmann riṣṭaṃ na) is attacked, harmed by the toil of the way, by hunger and the like, so may the evil intent that harms us go away; or, as on the path of the sacrifice you remove the obstruction in the form of violence caused by the asuras and rākṣasas."

हे इन्द्र तुविजात बहुभावमापन्न शूर विक्रान्त त्वं वावृधानो वर्धमानोऽस्मयुरस्मान् कामयमानस्तम् ॥ अमित्रयन्तमस्मासु शत्रुमाचरन्तं मर्त्यं मरणस्वभावं तं मर्त्यं वज्रेण जहि ॥ हन्तेर्जादेशः । तस्यासिद्धवदत्राभादित्यसिद्धत्वाद्धेर्लुग्भावः ॥ तमित्युक्तं कमित्याह । यो मर्त्यो नोऽस्माकमघायति । अघं पापं दुःखं वेच्छति तं जहि । अश्वाघस्यात्मनः क्यङ् [?] । किंच सुश्रवस्तमोऽतिशयेन शोभनश्रवस्त्वं शृणुष्व । श्रावयोऽस्माकम् [?] । कीदृशं तदित्युच्यते । हे इन्द्र स्वत्प्रसादाद्दुर्मतिर्दुष्टा बुद्धिर्हिंसाविषया दुष्कर्मणि बुद्धिरप भूतु । अपगता भवतु ॥ छान्दसः शपो लुक् । भूसुवोस्तिङीति गुणप्रतिषेधः ॥ न केवलं हिंसारूपा अपि तु विश्वा सर्वापि क्रोधपरिवादादिरूपा दुर्मतिरप भूतु । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । यामन् यामन्यध्वनि रिष्टं न । अध्वनः श्रमेण हिंसितं परिश्रान्तं यथा दुर्मतिः क्षुधादिविषया बाधते तद्वदस्मान्बाधमाना दुर्मतिरपगच्छतु । यद्वा । यामनि मार्गे यज्ञादिरूपे रिष्टमसुररक्षः कृतहिंसादिरूपं विघ्नं परिहरसि तद्वत् ॥

he indra tuvijāta bahubhāvamāpanna śūra vikrānta tvaṃ vāvṛdhāno vardhamāno 'smayurasmān kāmayamānastam ‖ amitrayantamasmāsu śatrumācarantaṃ martyaṃ maraṇasvabhāvaṃ taṃ martyaṃ vajreṇa jahi ‖ hanterjādeśaḥ | tasyāsiddhavadatrābhādityasiddhatvāddherlugbhāvaḥ ‖ tamityuktaṃ kamityāha | yo martyo no 'smākamaghāyati | aghaṃ pāpaṃ duḥkhaṃ vecchati taṃ jahi | aśvāghasyātmanaḥ kyaṅ [?] | kiṃca suśravastamo 'tiśayena śobhanaśravastvaṃ śṛṇuṣva | śrāvayo 'smākam [?] | kīdṛśaṃ tadityucyate | he indra svatprasādāddurmatirduṣṭā buddhirhiṃsāviṣayā duṣkarmaṇi buddhirapa bhūtu | apagatā bhavatu ‖ chāndasaḥ śapo luk | bhūsuvostiṅīti guṇapratiṣedhaḥ ‖ na kevalaṃ hiṃsārūpā api tu viśvā sarvāpi krodhaparivādādirūpā durmatirapa bhūtu | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | yāman yāmanyadhvani riṣṭaṃ na | adhvanaḥ śrameṇa hiṃsitaṃ pariśrāntaṃ yathā durmatiḥ kṣudhādiviṣayā bādhate tadvadasmānbādhamānā durmatirapagacchatu | yadvā | yāmani mārge yajñādirūpe riṣṭamasurarakṣaḥ kṛtahiṃsādirūpaṃ vighnaṃ pariharasi tadvat ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. tuvijāta — O Indra of many forms (by our praises); śūra — O brave (Indra); (he) indra — O Indra; tvam — you; vāvṛdhānaḥ — greatly growing; asmayuḥ — loving us; yaḥ — whoever; naḥ — to us; aghāyati — wishes sin or sorrow; tam — that; amitrayantam — acting as an enemy; martyam — the mortal, of the nature of death; vajreṇa — with the thunderbolt; jahi — strike; (kiṃ ca — and); suśravastamaḥ — you who listen to prayers with special attention; śṛṇuṣva — hear (our prayer); durmatiḥ — the evil intent (to harm us); apa bhūtu — be removed; yāmann riṣṭaṃ na — as on the road a harm due to robbers and the like; yāmann — on the path of the sacrifice; riṣṭaṃ na — as harm due to demons and the like; viśvā — all (anger and the like); durmatiḥ — evil intents; apa bhūtu — be removed.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (its first lines are at the foot of p. 498). O Indra, of many forms, growing by our praises, loving us: with the thunderbolt kill the mortals who are our enemies and wish us harm; hear our prayer with special attention; may their evil intent to harm us be removed;

original p. 499

…may the intent be removed by your grace, as on the road the harm [of robbers] is removed (when one is weary of travel), or, as in the sacrifice, the harm caused by the demons is removed; may all intents of anger and the like be removed.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Indra, endowed with many (excellences), you are exalted (by our praises), and are well disposed towards us, (slay) the man who is unfriendly to us; (slay) such a man, hero, with your thunderbolt: kill him who sins against us; ever most prompt to hear, hear (us): let every ill-intent (towards us, such as alarms) a wearied (traveller) on the road, be counteracted; let every ill-intent be counteracted."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 7).

Indra grows by the praises recited by the priests and the sacrificers; he has many forms: this is the explanation of tuvijāta and vāvṛdhānaḥ. By the epithet asmayuḥ it is said that Indra regards as his own devotees those who praise him with a pure mind.

The word martyam is used twice; the first is explained as "one who is by nature subject to death", and in the second martya is qualified by amitrayantam; the prayer is that Indra regard as enemies, and destroy with the thunderbolt, the men who regard the priests and the sacrificers as enemies. The word amitra conveys "not a friend"; the suffix kyac in the sense of conduct (ācāra) is applied after this word; "one who acts as an enemy" is the explanation. The word martya is recorded among the names of men (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೮").

aghāyati — aghaṃ pāpaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā icchati: the word agha is formed from the root han with the prefix removed — aghaṃ hanter nirhasitopasarga āhantīti (Ni. 6-[?]; as read "೬-೧೧"): it denotes an action which brings men to sorrow, to sin. Here, "a person who wishes to cause sorrow or sin to the priests or the sacrificers": Indra is asked to destroy him.

suśravastamaḥ — Indra's strength and renown are extremely great and, he is described, by his mere hearing (śravaṇa) he gives welfare.

original p. 500

durmatiḥ apa bhūtu — duṣṭabuddhir apagatā bhavatu: "the intent, with anger, to do harm to the sacrificer — to utter abuses — may it be destroyed by Indra's grace": so he prays.

yāman riṣṭaṃ na — adhvanaḥ śrameṇa hiṃsitaṃ pariśrāntaṃ yathā durmatiḥ kṣudhādiviṣayā bādhate tadvad asmān bādhamānā durmatir apagacchatu | yadvā yāmani yajñādimārge … riṣṭam asurarakṣaḥkṛtahiṃsādirūpaṃ vighnaṃ pariharasi tadvat: Sāyaṇa gives two meanings for this sentence. "As the hunger and the like of a traveller who is weary of the road, and the fear of robbers, harass him, so may the evil intent that harasses us — of those who injure the priests and the sacrificers — go by Indra's grace": by this familiar example; in the second meaning, "in the path of the sacrifice and the like, the harm caused by the demons and Rākṣasas is warded off as Indra protects the sacrificer."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). vāvṛdhānaḥ — root vṛdhu vṛddhau; when liṭ follows, liṭaḥ kānajvā (Pā. 3-2-106) gives kānac; the root is doubled; citaḥ gives the acute on the last syllable. asmayuḥ — asmān ātmana icchati; supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8); kyāc chandasi (Pā. 3-2-170) gives u after the kyac-ending; ato lopaḥ drops the a of kyac; the acute on the last syllable by the suffix. amitrayantam — after the kyac-ending as before, śatṛ in the present sense; the kyac's accent remains; accusative singular, with the augment num. tuvijāta — in the vocative, āmantrita-nighāta. jahi — root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; loṭ second person singular, sip, replaced by hi; the luk of the vikaraṇa; hanter jaḥ (Pā. 6-4-36) gives ja for the root; asiddhavad atrābhāt (Pā. 6-4-22) makes the ja-substitution as if not effective, so ato heḥ (Pā. 6-4-105) does not give luk to hi. Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read]; the Sūkta-heading block below gives Varga 22 [as read: "೨೨"?].

original p. 501

Grammar of Ṛk 7, concluded; numbers as printed. aghāyati — aghaṃ ātmana icchati; when this sense is intended, supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8) gives kyac; na chandasy aputrasya (Pā. 7-4-35) forbids lengthening of the a; when kyac follows an a-ending stem akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ (Pā. 7-4-25) lengthens it; because yad is connected, no nighāta; the kyac-accent remains. śṛṇuṣva — root śru śravaṇe; loṭ second person singular, ātmanepada; because it follows a finite verb, nighāta; by the suffix the acute falls on the last syllable. yāman — supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39): the locative ending is dropped. riṣṭam — root riṣa hiṃsāyām; the suffix kta; ṣ-marker gives ṣṭutva to the t; the suffix's accent. bhūtu — root bhū sattāyām; loṭ third person singular, tip, replaced by tu by eru; bahulaṃ chandasi gives luk of the vikaraṇa; bhūsuvos tiṅi (Pā. 7-3-88) forbids guṇa; tiṅ-nighāta is not applied. viśvā — in the neuter plural śeś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70) drops śi. ‖ 7 ‖

Here ends the 131st Sūkta. Kannada closing line: "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತೊಂದನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮುಗಿದುದು".

Sūkta 132 — tvayā vayaṃ maghavan (begins on printed p. 501; Anuvāka 19, sixth Sūkta)

original p. 501

ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra mūvatteraḍaneya sūktavu (the one hundred and thirty-second Sūkta).

॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image).

त्वया वयमिति षडृचं षष्ठं सूक्तं पारुच्छेपमात्यष्टमैन्द्रम् । युवं तमित्यर्धर्चस्येन्द्रापर्वतदेवताकम् । त्वया वयं षडित्यनुक्रमणिका । त्वया वयं षड्युवं तमैन्द्रापार्वतोत्तरार्धर्चः इत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ विनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

tvayā vayamiti ṣaḍṛcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ pārucchepamātyaṣṭamaindram | yuvaṃ tamityardharcasyendrāparvatadevatākam | tvayā vayaṃ ṣaḍityanukramaṇikā | tvayā vayaṃ ṣaḍyuvaṃ tamaindrāpārvatottarārdharcaḥ ityanukramaṇikā ‖ viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖

Kannada anuvāda (translated). Anuvāda — This Sūkta tvayā vayam is the sixth Sūkta in the nineteenth Anuvāka. It has six ṛks. The ṛṣi is Paruccheṣa; the deity is Indra; the metre is Atyaṣṭi. The deity of the second half of the ṛk beginning yuvaṃ taṃ is Indra and Parvata. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "tvayā vayaṃ ṣaṭ; yuvaṃ taṃ aindrāparvatottarārdharcaḥ". Its use in the rites is by inference (laiṅgika). Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 132".

original p. 502

ಸೂಕ್ತ—೧೩೨ — Sūkta 132. Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 19 ‖ Sūkta 132 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 1 ‖ Varga 22 [as read: "೨೨"?] ‖ Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 6 ‖ Ṛṣi: Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi ‖ Devatā: Ṛks 1–5 and the first half of Ṛk 6 Indra; the latter half of Ṛk 6, Indra and Parvata ‖ Chandas: Atyaṣṭi.

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

त्वया वयं मघवन्पूर्व्ये धन इन्द्रत्वोताः सासह्याम पृतन्यतः । वनुयाम वनुष्यतः । नेदिष्ठे अस्मिन्नहन्यधि वोचा नु सुन्वते । अस्मिन्यज्ञे वि चयेमा भरे कृतं वाजयन्तो भरे कृतम् ॥ १ ॥

tvayā vayaṃ maghavanpūrvye dhana indratvotāḥ sāsahyāma pṛtanyataḥ | vanuyāma vanuṣyataḥ | nediṣṭhe asminnahanyadhi vocā nu sunvate | asminyajñe vi cayemā bhare kṛtaṃ vājayanto bhare kṛtam ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image; the Pada prints "indra-tvā-ūtāḥ" with the compound as I give it, and "vocā" [for voca] is printed as in the Saṃhitā.

त्वया । वयम् । मघऽवन् । पूर्व्ये । धने । इन्द्रऽत्वाऽऊताः । ससह्याम । पृतन्यतः । वनुयाम । वनुष्यतः । नेदिष्ठे । अस्मिन् । अहनि । अधि । वोच । नु । सुन्वते । अस्मिन् । यज्ञे । वि । चयेम । भरे । कृतम् । वाजऽयन्तः । भरे । कृतम् ॥ १ ॥

tvayā | vayam | magha 'van | pūrvye | dhane | indra 'tvā 'ūtāḥ | sasahyāma | pṛtanyataḥ | vanuyāma | vanuṣyataḥ | nediṣṭhe | asmin | ahani | adhi | voca | nu | sunvate | asmin | yajñe | vi | cayema | bhare | kṛtam | vāja 'yantaḥ | bhare | kṛtam ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, doubtful places [?]). The bhāṣya continues on p. 503; the sense follows there. Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 22 [as read].

हे मघवन् । मघं सौख्यं तद्वन्निन्द्र । मघ शब्दो मघमिति धनस्य नामधेयम् [?] ॥ त्वया साधनेन युक्ता वयम् । अत एवेन्द्रत्वोता अतिप्रबलेनेन्द्रेण त्वया रक्षिताः सन्तः ॥ प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्चेत्यादेशः । छान्दसमात्वम् ॥ पृतन्यतः पृतनामात्मन इच्छतः प्रबलसेनायुक्ताञ्छत्रून् ससह्याम । अभिभवेम । तथा वनुष्यतो वनुष्यन्ति हिंसन्ति तद्वतः शत्रून् वनुयाम । हिंसेम । तेषामागमनात्पूर्वमेव वयं सम्भजेम । किंचो पूर्व्ये धने ऽस्मिन्नेव यज्ञे ॥

he maghavan | maghaṃ saukhyaṃ tadvannindra | magha śabdo maghamiti dhanasya nāmadheyam [?] ‖ tvayā sādhanena yuktā vayam | ata evendratvotā atiprabalenendreṇa tvayā rakṣitāḥ santaḥ ‖ pratyayottarapadayoścetyādeśaḥ | chāndasamātvam ‖ pṛtanyataḥ pṛtanāmātmana icchataḥ prabalasenāyuktāñchatrūn sasahyāma | abhibhavema | tathā vanuṣyato vanuṣyanti hiṃsanti tadvataḥ śatrūn vanuyāma | hiṃsema | teṣāmāgamanātpūrvameva vayaṃ sambhajema | kiṃco pūrvye dhane 'sminneva yajñe ‖

original p. 503

Bhāṣya of Ṛk 1, continued from p. 502 — small type, read from the image; doubtful places [?]. "…sasahyāma — may we overcome; and vanuṣyataḥ — enemies who wish to harm us — vanuyāma — may we strike, may we anticipate them before they come. And in this very former wealth, in this sacrifice, nediṣṭhe asmin ahani — on this day very near, adhi voca nu sunvate — speak quickly, encouragingly to the sacrificer who presses Soma — you, Indra, say to him: 'Be quick, give the oblation' (tuṃ havispradaṃ yajamānaṃ yajñaṃ vā kṣipram adhikaṃ brūhi). [Grammar: loṭ, the Vedic aṅ, vaca with the augment um.] And, O Indra, in this sacrifice, bhare kṛtam — in battle, made victorious, we, desiring food, vi cayema — may we gather, offer to you, the doer of victory, the oblations and praises (stotrādikaṃ haviradikaṃ vā): ci with śap in the sense of collecting; and what kind of you? bhare devānāṃ saṅgrāme 'surajaye devānāṃ samyaggamane kṛtaṃ kartāram — the doer in the battle of the gods against the demons, in the meeting of gods. 'Bhara' is a name for battle (bharati or haratīti, Ni. 4-[?], as read "೪-೨೪", Yāska)."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (he) maghavan — O Indra of excellent happiness; tvayā — by you (who are able); vayam — we; indratvotāḥ — protected by Indra (so that we may win in battle); pṛtanyataḥ — enemies who come with powerful armies; sasahyāma — may we overcome; vanuṣyataḥ — those who come to attack us; vanuyāma — may we first meet (them); kiṃ ca — and; pūrvye dhane — in the earlier, special wealth; asmin yajñe — in this sacrifice; nediṣṭhe asmin ahani — on this day, very near (the day of pressing); sunvate — to the sacrificer who presses; nu adhi voca — speak quickly (encouragingly); (he indra — O Indra); vayam — we; bhare — in battle; kṛtam — you, the maker of victory; (uddiśya — for you); vājayantaḥ — bringing the oblation-food; vi cayema — may we gather together (oblations and the rest); bhare — in the battle of gods and demons (in the matter of the means of battle for the gods); kṛtam — you, the accomplisher; (vi cayema — may we gather the oblations).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra of excellent happiness, protected by you, may we overcome the enemies who come with powerful armies, and may we be the first to meet those who come to attack us. As before, in this sacrifice, which is near on this day, speak encouragingly to the sacrificer who presses Soma; we who serve you with oblations and the like for the sake of victory, you the victory-maker, gather these for you; and in the matter of the defeat of demons, for you who are able to give the gods the means, we offer oblations.

original p. 504

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "(Possessed of) former opulence, Maghavan, (through your bounty), protected, Indra, by you, may we overcome those who are arrayed in (hostile) hosts: may we anticipate (our) assailants. (The sacrifice) of to-day being nigh, speak encouragingly to the presenter of the libation: May we bring together at this rite (suitable offerings and praises) to you, the victor in war; worshipping you, the victor in war."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).

maghavan — maghaḥ saukhyaṃ tadvan indra: the word magha is explained maghaṃ iti dhananāmadheyam mahater dānakarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೭"): "magha is a name of wealth, from mah, in the sense of giving"; the word is also recorded among the twenty-eight names of wealth, maghaṃ rekṇaḥ (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೯"). Sāyaṇa gives the word magha the sense "happiness" and describes Indra as endowed with happiness.

indratvotāḥ — atiprabalena indreṇa tvayā rakṣitāḥ: the word indra is explained in many ways in the earlier ṛks — irāṃ dṛṇātīti vā, and so on (Ni. 10-[?]; as read "೧೦-೮"). Here Sāyaṇa describes Indra as very powerful, and the ṛṣis as those who obtained protection by his grace.

pṛtanyataḥ sasahyāma — prabalasenāyuktān śatrūn abhibhavema: the word pṛtanā is recorded among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"). As pṛtanā is a word for the army which is eager for battle, Sāyaṇa explains pṛtanā as "army"; pṛtanām ātmana icchati is pṛtanyati: "enemies who desire an army": "may we, protected by Indra, overcome the powerful enemies without being overpowered".

vanuṣyataḥ vanuyāma — "from this sentence the enemies rush up in order to harm; may we, protected by Indra, the sacrificers and the priests, strike them down and defeat them first": so Indra's protection is described.

nu — nu taṃ havispradaṃ yajamānaṃ yajñaṃ vā kṣipram adhikaṃ brūhi: the Niruktakāra says nu ity eṣo 'nekakarmā — "the particle nu conveys many senses" (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೪"). The words nu and sma are recorded among the eight names of "quickly" (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೯"). —

original p. 505

continued: "idaṃ nu kariṣyati iti hetusaṃdeśe [as read]; kathaṃ nu kariṣyatīty anuprapte" — in idaṃ nu kariṣyati the nu shows a reason; in kathaṃ nu kariṣyati it is a question. Here the particle is in the sense of comparison as well. —

अक्ष्णो न चक्रयोः शूर बृहन्ते महान्न रिरिचे रोदस्योः । वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यू३तयो रुरुहुरिन्द्र पूर्वीः ॥

akṣo na cakrayoḥ śūra bṛhan te mahān na ririce rodasyoḥ | vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayā vy ū3 tayo ruruhur indra pūrvīḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-24-5, as read "೬-೨೪-೫"; the second line has a doubtful word at its start: [?].) In this Ṛk vṛkṣasya nu is explained, in the Kannada, as meaning "like a tree": the word nu is in the sense of comparison. Sāyaṇa explains nu as kṣipram (jāgarte): that Indra must be told quickly — whether it be the sacrificers or the sacrifice — to show his greatness.

bhare kṛtaṃ vājayantaḥ vi cayema — saṅgrāme jayasya kartāraṃ tvām uddiśya havirlakṣaṇānnam upācarantaḥ stotrādikaṃ haviradikaṃ vā vicinuyāma: the Niruktakāra explains bhara iti saṅgrāmanāma bharater harater vā (Ni. 4-[?]; as read "೪-೨೪"); Durgācārya: "bhriyante tasmin yoddhāraḥ — the warriors are supported in it; hriyante hi tasmin jīvitāni vasūni ca — lives and wealth are taken away in it": the word bhara is thus explained as "battle". "The sacrificers offer oblation-food to Indra, the one who brings about victory in battle. The word vāja is explained by the Niruktakāra as food, water, battle." Sāyaṇa explains it here as "praise".

The word bhare is used twice; in the second meaning, it is said that Indra is ready to bring about victory in the battle of the gods and demons, or to protect the gods.

The word kṛta is formed from the root ḍukṛñ karaṇe with the suffix kta; Sāyaṇa explains it as "agent".

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). pūrvye — pūrve bhavaṃ pūrvyam; bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110) gives yat; yasyeti ca drops the a; yato nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213) gives the acute on the first syllable. indratvotāḥ — indreṇa tvayā ūtāḥ; pratyayottarapadayoś ca (Pā. 7-2-98) gives tva for the tvad stem up to its last letter; tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… (Pā. 6-2-2)

original p. 506

— the accent of the first member remains. sasahyāma — root ṣaha marṣaṇe; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ gives s; liṅ first person plural, mas; niścaṃ jāte [as read]: the s is dropped; by bahulaṃ chandasi the śa-affix on the suffix; the suffix gets yāsuṭ; the root is doubled; the reduplicative lengthened by Vedic usage; since it follows a finite verb nighāta. pṛtanyataḥ — pṛtanām ātmana icchati pṛtanyati; supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8); sanādyantā dhātavaḥ (Pā. 3-1-32) gives the name dhātu; supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ (Pā. 2-4-71) drops the supa (am); kyaci ca (Pā. 7-4-33) with kavatyadṛpṛṣaṅgena [as read] drops the a; pṛtanya becomes a root; the acute on the last syllable by the suffix; after it laṭ, śatṛ in the place of the suffix; śap; accusative plural; since num-less śatṛ, śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173) gives the acute to the ending. vanuyāma — root vana sambhaktau; liṅ first person plural; by Vedic usage no nighāta; since yāsuṭ is acute, the ā following is acute. vanuṣyataḥ — a root with many senses; laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe (Pā. 3-2-124) gives śatṛ; accusative plural; śatur anumo… gives the acute to the ending. nediṣṭhe — when the sense of excess is shown, iṣṭhan; antikabāḍhayor nedasādhau (Pā. 5-3-63) gives neda for antika; ṭeḥ drops; acute on the first syllable because n-marked. voca — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; loṭ second person singular, sip, hi; by vyatyaya the aṅ; aṅ following, vaca um (Pā. 7-4-20) gives the augment um to the root; guṇa when um is in the last place; ato heḥ drops hi; tiṅ-nighāta. sunvate — root ṣuñ abhiṣave; śatṛ in the present sense; the vikaraṇa śnu; dative singular; śatur anumo… gives the acute to the ending.

original p. 507

Grammar, concluded. cayema — root ciñ cayane, svādi; liṅ first person plural; by vyatyayo bahulam the śap [for śnu]; by it guṇa of the root's i, ayādeśa; the suffix gets yāsuṭ, with iya; yalopa; guṇa; tiṅ-nighāta. vājayantaḥ — after vāja in the sense of ātmanaḥ [as read], kyac; after it laṭ with śatṛ; nominative plural. ‖ 1 ‖

(ornamental rule)

Rik 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स्वर्जेषे भर आप्रस्य वक्मन्युषर्बुधः स्वस्मिन्नञ्जसि क्राणस्य स्वस्मिन्नञ्जसि । अहन्निन्द्रो यथा विदे शीर्ष्णाशीर्ष्णोपवाच्यः । अस्मत्रा ते सध्र्यक्सन्तु रातयो भद्रा भद्रस्य रातयः ॥ २ ॥

svarjeṣe bhara āprasya vakmanyuṣarbudhaḥ svasminnañjasi krāṇasya svasminnañjasi | ahannindro yathā vide śīrṣṇāśīrṣṇopavācyaḥ | asmatrā te sadhryaksantu rātayo bhadrā bhadrasya rātayaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image; the Saṃhitā prints "svarjeṣe bhara āprasya", and the Pada prints "vakmani" as the word in the Saṃhitā: I give what is printed; the line "aham indro" in the Saṃhitā is printed "ahann indro yathā vide" [vide as printed].

स्वःऽजेषे । भरे । आप्रस्य । वक्मनि । उषःऽबुधः । स्वस्मिन् । अञ्जसि । क्राणस्य । स्वस्मिन् । अञ्जसि । अहन् । इन्द्रः । यथा । विदे । शीर्ष्णाऽशीर्ष्णा । उपऽवाच्यः । अस्मत्रा । ते । सध्र्यक् । सन्तु । रातयः । भद्राः । भद्रस्य । रातयः ॥ २ ॥

svaḥ 'jeṣe | bhare | āprasya | vakmani | uṣaḥ 'budhaḥ | svasmin | añjasi | krāṇasya | svasmin | añjasi | ahan | indraḥ | yathā | vide | śīrṣṇā 'śīrṣṇā | upa 'vācyaḥ | asmatrā | te | sadhryak | santu | rātayaḥ | bhadrāḥ | bhadrasya | rātayaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (begins at the foot of p. 507; read from the image).

अयमिन्द्रः स्वर्जेषे स्वर्गगमनसाधने भरे सङ्ग्रामे । युद्धे ह्यभिमुखेन हतस्य स्वर्गो द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके सूर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ । परा. ३-२३ [?] इत्यादिस्मृतिषु प्रसिद्धः ॥ आप्रस्याप्नुवतः शत्रुवधायेतस्ततो व्याप्नुवतः ॥ ओणादिकः रः । शूरस्य वक्मनि मार्गभूते स्वस्मिन्नञ्जसि स्वभूतेऽञ्जसि व्यक्तिकृति तमादिरहिते । पुनः स एव विशेष्यते । स्वस्मिन्नञ्जसि स्वकीये ऽञ्जसि मुख्ये महति सङ्ग्रामे । यद्वा ।

ayamindraḥ svarjeṣe svargagamanasādhane bhare saṅgrāme | yuddhe hyabhimukhena hatasya svargo dvāvimau puruṣau loke sūryamaṇḍalabhedinau | parā. 3-23 [?] ityādismṛtiṣu prasiddhaḥ ‖ āprasyāpnuvataḥ śatruvadhāyetastato vyāpnuvataḥ ‖ oṇādikaḥ raḥ | śūrasya vakmani mārgabhūte svasminnañjasi svabhūte 'ñjasi vyaktikṛti tamādirahite | punaḥ sa eva viśeṣyate | svasminnañjasi svakīye 'ñjasi mukhye mahati saṅgrāme | yadvā |

original p. 508

Bhāṣya of Ṛk 2, continued — small type, read from the image; doubtful places [?]. "…yadvā — or: svasmin añjasi śatrau svayam evāprecchann eveṇāgate sati: when the enemy himself comes, without asking [? the way]; ahan — śatrūn hinasti: Indra destroys the enemies in battle. āprasya — of the one who goes about intent on killing enemies (āpanaśīlasya), or of Indra who is to be pleased; uṣarbudhaḥ — of the sacrificer who, awake at dawn, for the performance of the sacrifice, prabudhyamānasya, krāṇasya — doing the sacrifice (kurvāṇasya; karoteḥ śānac, Vedic śap loss) — of this sacrificer, Indra destroys the enemies. yathā vide — as [one] knows. śīrṣṇā-śīrṣṇopavācyaḥ — sarvaiḥ śirasā praṇamya stutyaḥ — to be praised by all, bowing the head. [Grammar: śīrṣan with chandasi ca, Pā. 6-1-60; the acute on the last syllable by the udāttanivṛtti accent; nityavīpsayoḥ gives doubling.] The example: yathā vide sarvajñāya śirasā praṇatiḥ kriyate stūyate ca tathaiveti — as bowing with the head and praise are offered to the all-knowing; or yathā vide yena prakāreṇa pañcamaṃ śatruṃ jānāsi taṃ taṃ prahaṃsi: by whatever way you know the enemy, you strike him; or yaṃ yaṃ vindase labhase śatruṃ taṃ taṃ mārayasi — whichever enemy you meet, you kill: for this reason he is to be praised. [Grammar: vide, ātmanepada; talopa.] And te ratayaḥ — your gifts of wealth, asmatrā — among us, sadhryak — together (sahāñcati), santu — may they be; bhadrasya — of you the auspicious, the gifts bhadrāḥ — may they be auspicious and firm."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. indraḥ — Indra; svarjeṣe — which is the means of obtaining heaven; bhare — in battle; āprasya — of the hero who goes about to kill enemies; svasmin añjasi — in the straight path suited to him; vakmani — [in the path]; svasmin añjasi — in the great path of battle of straight direction, which suits Indra and which is directly facing the enemies; uṣarbudhaḥ — of the one who awakes at dawn; krāṇasya — of the one who does the sacrifice (the sacrificer); ahan — kills (the enemies); yathā vide — as to a great person who is all-knowing (one bows the head); śīrṣṇā-śīrṣṇā — with the bowing of the head, with salutations; upavācyaḥ — he is worthy of praise (O Indra); asmatrā — our protector; te — your; rātayaḥ — the gifts of wealth; sadhryak — all together; santu — be; bhadrasya — of the auspicious one; te rātayaḥ — your gifts; bhadrāḥ — auspicious, and firm; (santu — be).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (its first lines at the foot of p. 508). In the battle that is the means to heaven, Indra, fit for the valiant, goes by the straight path and faces the enemies directly; going so, he destroys the enemies of the sacrificers who, awake at dawn, perform the sacrifice, (…

original p. 509

Bhāvārtha, concluded: "…) therefore, as one bows with the head to a great all-knowing person and praises him, so Indra too should be praised with salutations; O Indra, our protector, may all your wealth be together with us; and may all your auspicious wealth be firmly with us, bringing us welfare."

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "In the combat which secures heaven, Indra, (treading) in the appropriate and straight path of the active (combatant), as well as in his own appropriate and straight (path), destroys (the adversary) of him who wakes at dawn and celebrates (pious rites); he is therefore to be adored with the head (bowed down), as reverence is paid by prostration to a holy sage. May your treasures, (Indra), be accumulated upon us; may the treasures of you who are auspicious be auspicious (to us)."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).

svarjeṣe bhare — svargagamanasādhane saṅgrāme: "when the hero fights, he gives up his life without fear and gets heaven" — the Smṛtikāra explains battle as a place fit for the attainment of heaven. The word bhara (battle) is explained by the Niruktakāra as bharater vā harater vā (Ni. 4-[?]; as read "೪-೨೪"). Parāśara-smṛti says that the hero who lays down his life in battle obtains heaven —

द्राविमौ पुरुषौ लोके सूर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ । परिव्राड्योगयुक्तश्च रणे चाभिमुखो हतः ॥

dvāv imau puruṣau loke sūryamaṇḍalabhedinau | parivrāḍ yogayuktaś ca raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ ‖

(Parāśara-smṛti 3-23 [?], as read "೩-೨೩"; the same verse as on p. 453, where the first word is printed "dvāv" — here printed "द्रा" [sic?].) "The ascetic who gives up his life with no hope of it, by yoga, and the hero who fights the enemy and dies in battle, both obtain the highest state — they pierce the orb of the Sun. So it is said, taking battle as the means of reaching heaven: Indra gives such heroes heaven."

āprasya — āpanaśīlasya: "of one who goes about in battle for victory over enemies, spreading widely by his valour in all places". The Niruktakāra —

चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अन्तरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥

citraṃ devānām ud agād anīkaṃ cakṣur mitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatas tasthuṣaś ca ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1, as read "೧-೧೧೫-೧".) — citing this explains āprāḥ as apūpurat — "filled" the heaven, the earth and the sky by his greatness: "the Sun, by his greatness, pervades heaven, earth and the middle region". Sāyaṇa too explains āprasya as śatruvadhāya itas tato vyāpnuvataḥ: "who pervades the battlefield to kill the enemy".

original p. 510

svasmin añjasi — the words are used twice. For the word añjasi the first meaning is, as an adjective of vakmani, "free from deceit" (kapaṭarahite): "the hero's way of fighting is, it is described, without trickery." The second meaning has two parts: svakīye 'ñjasi mukhye mahati saṅgrāme, "in his own great, principal battle"; or yadvā śatrau svayam eva aprecchann eveṇāgate sati śatrūn hinasti — "when the enemy himself comes, without hiding his coming under another disguise, then Indra kills the enemies": in a powerful battle, or when the enemy, without concealing his coming, himself comes to face him. In both meanings the word is explained as an adjective of bhare. All this is connected by taking the word āprasya as an epithet of vakmani, in the sense of "the path of the hero who pervades".

For the word āpra the explanation is given by taking āpnoti — āprā vyāpnoti — "one who pervades"; and āsamantāt prīṇayatīti — "one who gratifies greatly": taken in the latter sense, it is an epithet of the sacrificer who pleases Indra. From this:

āprasya uṣarbudhaḥ krāṇasya ahan — the sentence is thus formed; Sāyaṇa explains: āpanaśīlasya indrasya prīṇayitur vā uṣaḥkāle yogānuṣṭhānāya prabudhyamānasya yāgaṃ kurvāṇasya asya yajamānasya śatrūn hinasti: "the sacrificer, being of a pervading nature and one who pleases Indra, is awake at dawn to perform sacrifices; Indra destroys the enemies of this sacrificer, who offers sacrifices to satisfy Indra". The Niruktakāra —

original p. 511

त्वामिन्द्र मितिभिः सुते सुनीथासो वसूयवः । गोभिः क्राणा अनोषत ॥

tvām indra mitibhiḥ sute sunīthāso vasūyavaḥ | gobhiḥ krāṇā anoṣata ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?], as read "೮-೪-[?]" [?]; the reference is not clear; small type. The line is given as read: [?].) — citing this he explains gobhiḥ krāṇāḥ as gobhiḥ kurvāṇāḥ ("making with cows"); Durgācārya explains krāṇāḥ as kurvāṇāḥ (Ni. 4-[?]; as read "೪-೧೯").

śīrṣṇā-śīrṣṇopavācyaḥ — sarveṣāṃ śirasā praṇamya stutyaḥ: "Indra is worthy of being saluted by all and of being praised by all."

yathā vide — sarvajñāya śirasā praṇatiḥ kriyate stūyate ca tathaiveti | yadvā yena prakāreṇa hantavyaṃ śatruṃ jānāsi taṃ taṃ prahaṃsi: this sentence is used as an illustration of the point that Indra is to be saluted or praised. The word vide is formed from the roots vidḷ lābhe and vida jñāne; in the sense of knowing, the meaning "to the all-knowing" is given; "as all bow to a great all-knowing man, so all bow to Indra". In the second meaning: "Indra, knowing in what way the enemy should be killed, destroys him by that means alone." In the third meaning, vide is explained as a word of obtaining: "whoever the enemy may be who meets Indra in battle, he receives death from Indra"; so Indra's greatness is described, and the reason for his being worthy of salutation or praise is that he gets the enemy as the object of his attack.

te ratayaḥ asmatrā sadhryak santu — tava sambandhīni dhanāni dānāny asmāsv eva sahaikodyogena bhavantu: "may the wealth and the gifts given to us by Indra be with us in one accord: the wealth given by Indra, and our offerings made for Indra's satisfaction, be suited to the sacrificer's purpose": so Indra is prayed.

The Niruktakāra reads the word rāti among the ten names of the acts of giving beginning with dāti, dāśati (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೯"), which means giving. And —

शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि । विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥

śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te anyad viṣurūpe ahanī dyaur ivāsi | viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣann iha rātir astu ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1, as read "೬-೫೮-೧".) In this Ṛk the word rāti is explained as dattiḥ, "giving".

original p. 512

bhadrasya rātayaḥ bhadrāḥ — stutyasya asmāsu datsāni dānāni atisthirāṇi santu: "may the wealth given to the sacrificers by Indra, who is praised, be well praised and firm": so he is prayed. In explaining the sense of the word bhadra the Niruktakāra (Ni. 4-[?]; as read "೪-೯") says —

सक्तुमिव तितउना पुनन्तो यत्र धीरा मनसा वाचमक्रत । अत्रा सखायः सख्यानि जानते भद्रैषां लक्ष्मीर्निहिताधि वाचि ॥

saktum iva titaunā punanto yatra dhīrā manasā vācam akrata | atrā sakhāyaḥ sakhyāni jānate bhadraiṣāṃ lakṣmīr nihitādhi vāci ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-2, as read "೧೦-೭೧-೨".) — citing this Ṛk: bhadraṃ bhageṇa vyākhyātam | bhajanīyam, bhūtānām abhidravaṇīyam, bhavadramayītī vā, bhājanavad vā ("bhadra is explained in terms of bhaga: that which is to be resorted to, that to which beings run, that which brings about being [?], that which is a vessel"): to understand the word bhadra in four ways: that which gives happiness to beings, that which gives satisfaction, that which is fit to be sought as the result of merit. Sāyaṇa explains that such is the wealth given by Indra to the sacrificers.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). svarjeṣe — root jeṣa gatau; since it belongs to the pacādi group, nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (Pā. 3-1-134) gives ac; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the latter member of the compound; locative singular. āprasya — root āpḷ vyāptau; Uṇādi ra; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. uṣarbudhaḥ — root budha avagamane; kvip ca gives kvip; the accent of the latter member; genitive singular. añjasi — root añju vyaktimrakṣaṇakāntigatiṣu; Uṇādi asun; since n-marked the acute on the first syllable; locative singular. krāṇasya — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; laṭ… śatṛ [as read: śānac] by Vedic usage; bahulaṃ chandasi gives luk of the vikaraṇa; since j-marked [as read] no guṇa; yaṇ-substitution; āṭ kupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi (Pā. 8-4-2) gives ṇ for the n of the suffix; citaḥ gives the acute on the last syllable; genitive singular. ahan — root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; laṅ third person singular, tip; itaś ca drops i; śap's luk; hal ṅyābbhyo… drops the suffix; the augment aṭ; at the beginning of the pāda no nighāta; the acute on the first syllable.

Or, root vidḷ lābhe, laṭ; by vyatyaya, the third person singular suffix ta in the place of the second person; by vyatyaya the ātmanepada; lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (Pā. 7-1-41) drops the t; because yathā is connected no nighāta; by the suffix the acute on the last syllable. तत्तु प्रयः प्रत्नथा ते शुशुक्वनं यस्मिन्यज्ञे वारमकृण्वत क्षयमृतस्य वारसि क्षयम् । वि तद्वोचेरध द्वितान्तः पश्यन्ति रश्मिभिः । स घा विदे अन्विन्द्रो गवेषणो बन्धुक्षिद्भ्यो गवेषणः ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, doubtful places [?]).

हे इन्द्र तत्तु खलु प्रसिद्धं प्रयो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं शुशुक्वनमाज्यादिसंयोगेन भृशं दीप्तं ॥ शुचेर्दीप्तिकर्मणः क्वनिप् [?] । तव स्वभूतकं । प्रत्नथा पूर्वमिव पूर्वं यथा योगकाले हविस्ते तव स्वं भवति तथाद्यत्वेऽपि । सर्वदा त्वामेव यजन्त इति भावः ॥ प्रत्नपूर्वविश्वेमात्थाल् [?] इत्यादिनेवार्थे थाल् । लिति स्वरः ॥ कीदृशं तदित्युच्यते । यस्मिन्यज्ञे यागे यस्मिन् हविषि दातव्ये सति वारं वरणीयं क्षयं स्थानं वेदिलक्षणमकृण्वत कुर्वन्ति ऋत्विजः । कस्य विशेष इति चेदुच्यते । ऋतस्य सत्यफलस्य यज्ञस्य वारसि क्षयं निवासस्थानं सम्भक्तासि । यद्वा । ऋतमित्युदकनाम । तस्य क्षयं स्थानं प्राप्तासि । वृष्टिप्रदोऽसीत्यर्थः । अथवा ऋतस्यादित्यस्य क्षयं स्थानं द्युलोकाख्यं वारसि यजमानं गमयितासि । तस्मादृशं वक्ष्यमाणं कर्म वि वोचेः । विब्रूहि । अधातः कारणाद्द्वितान्तर्द्वयोः ... कान्तर्द्यावापृथिव्योर्मध्येऽन्तरिक्षे रश्मिभिरादित्यकिरणैः पश्यन्ति ।

he indra tattu khalu prasiddhaṃ prayo havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ śuśukvanamājyādisaṃyogena bhṛśaṃ dīptaṃ ‖ śucerdīptikarmaṇaḥ kvanip [?] | tava svabhūtakaṃ | pratnathā pūrvamiva pūrvaṃ yathā yogakāle haviste tava svaṃ bhavati tathādyatve 'pi | sarvadā tvāmeva yajanta iti bhāvaḥ ‖ pratnapūrvaviśvemātthāl [?] ityādinevārthe thāl | liti svaraḥ ‖ kīdṛśaṃ tadityucyate | yasminyajñe yāge yasmin haviṣi dātavye sati vāraṃ varaṇīyaṃ kṣayaṃ sthānaṃ vedilakṣaṇamakṛṇvata kurvanti ṛtvijaḥ | kasya viśeṣa iti ceducyate | ṛtasya satyaphalasya yajñasya vārasi kṣayaṃ nivāsasthānaṃ sambhaktāsi | yadvā | ṛtamityudakanāma | tasya kṣayaṃ sthānaṃ prāptāsi | vṛṣṭiprado 'sītyarthaḥ | athavā ṛtasyādityasya kṣayaṃ sthānaṃ dyulokākhyaṃ vārasi yajamānaṃ gamayitāsi | tasmādṛśaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ karma vi voceḥ | vibrūhi | adhātaḥ kāraṇāddvitāntardvayoḥ ... kāntardyāvāpṛthivyormadhye 'ntarikṣe raśmibhirādityakiraṇaiḥ paśyanti |

original p. 515

निर्भिद्य रश्मिद्वारा प्रवर्षणरूपं कर्म सर्वे जनाः प्रत्यक्षतः पश्यन्ति । अस्मद्दत्तं हविरादित्यं प्रापयित्वा तद्द्वारा वृष्टिं जनयसीत्येतत्सर्वैर्दृश्यत इत्यर्थः ॥ इदानीं परोक्षतया स्तौति । स घ स खलु इन्द्रो गवेषण उदकस्यान्वेषणशीलः । तथा बन्धुक्षिद्भ्यो हविष्प्रदानादिना बन्धुभावं प्राप्तवद्भ्यो यजमानेभ्यो गवेषणो गवां प्रसिद्धानामेषणकर्ता । इषेर्बाहुलकात्कर्तरि ल्युट् ॥ यद्वा । गवेषं मार्गणे [?] । पूर्ववल्ल्युट् ॥ यजमानफलस्य मृगयितेत्यर्थः ॥ अनु उक्तक्रमेणैव कर्ता सन् विदे । विन्दते । उदकप्राप्तिप्रकारं जानाति ॥

nirbhidya raśmidvārā pravarṣaṇarūpaṃ karma sarve janāḥ pratyakṣataḥ paśyanti | asmaddattaṃ havirādityaṃ prāpayitvā taddvārā vṛṣṭiṃ janayasītyetatsarvairdṛśyata ityarthaḥ ‖ idānīṃ parokṣatayā stauti | sa gha sa khalu indro gaveṣaṇa udakasyānveṣaṇaśīlaḥ | tathā bandhukṣidbhyo haviṣpradānādinā bandhubhāvaṃ prāptavadbhyo yajamānebhyo gaveṣaṇo gavāṃ prasiddhānāmeṣaṇakartā | iṣerbāhulakātkartari lyuṭ ‖ yadvā | gaveṣaṃ mārgaṇe [?] | pūrvavallyuṭ ‖ yajamānaphalasya mṛgayitetyarthaḥ ‖ anu uktakrameṇaiva kartā san vide | vindate | udakaprāptiprakāraṃ jānāti ‖

Sense: "O Indra, that well-known prayaḥ — food in the form of oblation, much kindled by contact with ghee and the like — is yours (te); pratnathā — as formerly, whenever at the time of sacrifice the oblation is yours, so now too; they always sacrifice to you alone. How is it? In which sacrifice, when the oblation is to be given, the priests make a choice kṣaya — a place, the altar; of whom? you reach (vārasi) the dwelling-place of the sacrifice (ṛta) — the truth-fruited: or ṛta is a name of water — you reach the place of water — you are a rain-giver; or you take the sacrificer to the place of the Sun (ṛta) — the heaven world. Therefore declare (vi voceḥ) such a deed. Then, because of this, all men see directly, through the Sun's rays, the rain-giving deed in the midst — between heaven and earth — in the sky; by sending to the Sun the oblation given by us, you produce rain through it: so all see it. Now he praises indirectly: that Indra is goveṣaṇaḥ — the seeker of water; also bandhukṣidbhyaḥ goveṣaṇaḥ — for the sacrificers who have become kin through offering oblations, the seeker of the well-known cows; [grammar: iṣ with the lyuṭ by bāhulaka]; or gaveṣa in the sense of searching. He is the doer in the manner stated; vide — he finds, he knows the way of obtaining water."

original p. 515

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (he indra — O Indra); yajñe — in the sacrifice; yasmin — in which oblation (context); vāram — desirable; kṣayam — the place of the altar; akṛṇvata — [the priests] make; tat tu — that well-known; prayaḥ — the food in the form of oblation; śuśukvanam — greatly bright by contact with ghee and the like; pratnathā — as formerly (as in earlier times); te — yours; ṛtasya — of the sacrifice that gives true fruit; kṣayam — the place; vāḥ asi — you have reached; or [ṛtasya* — of water; kṣayam — the place; vāḥ asi — you reach (giving rain)]; or [ṛtasya* — of the Sun; kṣayam — the place (the heaven-world); vāḥ asi — you take the sacrificer to]; tat — such (deed of rain); vi voceḥ — make known; adha — therefore; dvitā antaḥ — in the middle of the two (heaven and earth, in the sky); raśmibhiḥ — with the rays of the Sun; paśyanti — (people) see (your deed of rain); saḥ ghā indraḥ — that very Indra; goveṣaṇaḥ — the seeker of water; bandhukṣidbhyaḥ — for the sacrificers who have become kin (through oblations); goveṣaṇaḥ — the seeker of cows; anu vide — in due order he knows (the way of the water).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. begins at the foot of p. 515 "The sacrificial food, greatly kindled by ghee and the like, which the priests offer to you, Indra, on the altar of the sacrifice, is yours as it was formerly; you go to the place of the sacrifice that gives true fruit; or you go to the place of water, giving rain; or you take the sacrificer to the heaven of the Sun; make known your deed of rain; (and) all people see by the rays of the Sun, in the sky between heaven and earth, the rain you cause; and Indra, who seeks water, seeks also cows for the sacrificers who are his kin; and he knows in due order the way to obtain them."

original p. 516

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Indra, in whatsoever rite (the priests) from of old have placed the brilliant (sacrificial) food for you upon the altar, in that place of sacrifice you abide: you declare that (rite), that men may thence behold the intermediate (firmament bright) with the rays (of the sun): for this, Indra, the searcher (of rain, is) the searcher after cattle, for (the benefit of) his kindred (worshippers), and knows in due course (the season of the rain)."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).

prayaḥ śuśukvanam — havirlakṣaṇam annam ājyādisaṃyogena bhṛśaṃ dīptam: the word prayas is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"); the root śuc gives the sense of radiance, and śuśukvanam is formed by the suffix vanip after the doubled-root (yaṅ-luk) form; so it means "greatly bright". Sāyaṇa explains it as the food, the oblation, made very bright by ghee and other substances.

pratnathā — itaḥ pūrvaṃ yathā yāgaśāle haviḥ tava svaṃ bhavati tathādyatanam api: "as the sacrificer offers oblations to Indra, hoping to please him, in the past, so now too": the sense is that, without distinguishing between past and present times, they always offer oblations to Indra.

vāraṃ kṣayam akṛṇvata — varaṇīyaṃ vedilakṣaṇaṃ sthānaṃ ṛtvijaḥ kurvanti: "the priests make the altar, the place where oblations are made to Indra, the best place in the sacrificial hall". The Niruktakāra —

अञ्जन्ति त्वामध्वरे देवयन्तो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन । यदूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा द्रविणेह धत्तादयद्वा क्षयो मातुरस्या उपस्थे ॥

añjanti tvām adhvare devayanto vanaspate madhunā daivyena | yad ūrdhvas tiṣṭhā draviṇeha dhattād yad vā kṣayo mātur asyā upasthe ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1, as read "೩-೮-೧".) — in this Ṛk explains the word kṣaya as nivāsasthāna ("dwelling-place").

ṛtasya vārasi kṣayam — satyaphalasya yajñasya nivāsasthānaṃ sambhaktāsi | yadvā ṛtam ity udakanāma, tasya kṣayaṃ sthānaṃ prāptāsi | athavā ṛtasyādityasya kṣayaṃ sthānaṃ dyulokākhyaṃ yajamānaṃ gamayitāsi: the word ṛta is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೧೪"?) and is explained as "truth" or "sacrifice" (Ni. 4-19 [?]). Indra is said to dwell at the sacrifice that gives true fruit; or to be the giver of rain; or to take the sacrificer to the place of the Sun in the heaven-world: by these three meanings Indra's greatness is described.

original p. 517

dvitā antaḥ raśmibhiḥ paśyanti — dvayor dyāvāpṛthivyor madhye antarikṣe ādityakiraṇaiḥ paśyanti | megham nirbhidya raśmidvārā pravarṣaṇarūpaṃ karma sarve janāḥ pratyakṣataḥ paśyanti: "Indra produces rain in order to nourish the world. Heaven and earth always exist together; in the sky between them, people everywhere see, through the Sun's rays, the rain falling from the clouds, which are split by the rays": so in the Manu-smṛti —

अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः ॥

agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyag ādityam upatiṣṭhate | ādityāj jāyate vṛṣṭir vṛṣṭer annaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ ‖

(Manu 3-76, as read "೩-೭೬".) The oblations offered in the fire for Indra and the other gods reach the Sun; since the Śruti says Indra and the Sun are one in nature, Indra receives the oblations in the form of the Sun, gives rain, food and prosperity to the people. Sāyaṇa explains: "asmaddattaṃ havir ādityaṃ prāpayitvā tadadvārā vṛṣṭiṃ janayasīty etat sarvair dṛśyate" — "you send to the Sun the oblation given by us and through it produce rain; this all see".

goveṣaṇaḥ bandhukṣidbhyo goveṣaṇaḥ — udakasyānveṣaṇaśīlaḥ havispradānādinā bandhubhāvaṃ prāptavadbhyo yajamānebhyo gavāṃ praśiddhānām eṣaṇakartā | yadvā yajamānaphalasya mṛgayitā: "the sacrificers become, as it were, relations of Indra through offering oblations; Indra, out of kindness, produces rain for them". The word goveṣaṇa is used twice: in the first the meaning is "one who seeks water (rain-water)", i.e. "one who gives it"; in the second, "one who gives the sacrificers the fruit of sacrifice"; these are explained as epithets of Indra.

sa ghā vide anu — "as stated above, Indra himself knows well how to give the sacrificers rain and the other fruits of the sacrifice."

original p. 518

"Indra acts like a friend and a kinsman toward the sacrificer — this is described in many Ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?]; 3-[?]; 5-[?]; 8-[?]…: the list of numerals is small and not reliably read: [?])."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). pratnathā — pratnapūrvaviśvemāt thāl chandasi (Pā. 5-3-111) gives thāl in the sense of similarity; thāl is l-marked, so liti (Pā. 6-1-193) gives the acute before the suffix. śuśukvanam — root śuca dīptau; after the yaṅ-luk form, vanip; am following, the Vedic lengthening does not occur; by vyatyaya the acute on the last syllable. vāram — root vṛñ varaṇe; suffix ghañ; aco ñṇiti gives vṛddhi; ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the acute on the first syllable. akṛṇvata — root kṛñ hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca; the Vedic laṅ in the present sense; third person plural; ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ (Pā. 7-1-5) gives at; dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca (Pā. 3-1-80) gives u as vikaraṇa and a ending; since it-marked, num; ato lopaḥ drops the a; the augment aṭ; because yad is connected no nighāta; the acute on the first syllable. kṣayam — root kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ; puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa gives gha [Pā. 3-3-118]; guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ, ayādeśa; kṣayo nivāse (Pā. 6-1-201) gives the acute on the first syllable. asi — root as bhuvi; loṭ… [as read: laṭ] second person singular; tiṅ-nighāta. voceḥ — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; luṅ second person singular, sip; itaś ca drops i; by vyatyaya the aṅ; since aṅ follows, vaca um (Pā. 7-4-20) gives um; guṇa; yāsuṭ with iya by ato yeyaḥ (Pā. 7-2-80); lopo vyor vali drops y; s becomes ru, visarga; tiṅ-nighāta.

original p. 519

ghā — ṛtitghā… [as read: ṛcitunughākṣuttutāṃ…, Pā. 6-3-133] gives lengthening in the Saṃhitā. vide — explained in two ways in the earlier mantra. goveṣaṇaḥ — by bahulagrahaṇa (kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam, Pā. 3-3-113) lyuṭ in the agent sense after the root iṣ; yuvor anākau gives ana; because of the suffix guṇa of the root; since aj follows, anādeśa; or the root gaveṣa mārgaṇe; lyuṭ as before; kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara. bandhukṣidbhyaḥ — root kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ; kvip; hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk (Pā. 6-1-71) gives tuk to the root; kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara. ‖ 3 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

नू इत्था ते पूर्वथा च प्रवाच्यं यदङ्गिरोभ्योऽवृणोरप व्रजम् । इन्द्र शिक्षन्नप व्रजम् । ऐभ्यः समान्या दिशास्मभ्यं जेषि योत्सि च । सुन्वद्भ्यो रन्धया कं चिदव्रतं हृणायन्तं चिदव्रतम् ॥ ४ ॥

nū itthā te pūrvathā ca pravācyaṃ yadaṅgirobhyo 'vṛṇorapa vrajam | indra śikṣannapa vrajam | aibhyaḥ samānyā diśāsmabhyaṃ jeṣi yotsi ca | sunvadbhyo randhayā kaṃ cidavrataṃ hṛṇāyantaṃ cidavratam ‖ 4 ‖

original p. 520

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?]). Sense: "O Indra, this deed of yours, of the kind stated or to be stated, should be praised by all (pravācyam) quickly, as in former times (pūrvathā), so now too. What is it? That you opened (apāvṛṇoḥ) the cloud (vraja — recorded among the names of cloud — "vrajo varāha" as read) that moved in the sky for the sake of those Aṅgirases, the great ṛṣis, and produced rain; and O Indra, taking away from the Paṇis (pāyāpsya?) the herd of cows, you gave it to them and protected them; or you opened the door of the cave where the cattle stolen by the Paṇis were kept. And as you give to these ṛṣis in one manner, so conquer for us wealth or battle, and fight (yotsi) for us. And for us who press Soma, subdue (randhaya) any avrata — one who does not perform the rites, an enemy of the sacrifice; make him subject to us. Not only the non-sacrificer, but the hṛṇāyantam cit avratam — the one who, being avrata, is furious at us (cit in the sense of contempt); subdue also him who rages, and make him unable to harm again."

हे इन्द्र ते तव सम्बन्धि कर्मार्तृत्वाद्युक्तप्रकारं वक्ष्यमाणरूपं वा पूर्वथा पूर्वमिव पूर्वं यथा नु क्षिप्रं प्रवाच्यं सर्वैः स्तोतव्यं तद्वदिदानीमपि स्तुत्यम् ॥ नू इत्थेत्येषामक्षराद्यित्वात्प्रकृतिभावः ॥ कीदृशं तदित्युच्यते । यत्त्वमङ्गिरोभ्य एतन्नाम्नेभ्यो महर्षिभ्यस्तेषामर्थाय व्रजमन्तरिक्षे गच्छन्तं मेघमपावृणोः अपावृतवानसि । मेघमुत्पाट्य वृष्टिमुत्पादितवानसि । व्रज इति मेघनाम । व्रजो वराह इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ किंच हे इन्द्र व्रजं गवां समूहमपायाप्स्यभ्योऽपहृत्य तेभ्य इवाङ्गिरोभ्यः शिक्षन् वितरन् रक्षितवानसि । यद्वा । पणिभिरपहृतं बिले स्थितं गवां व्रजमपहर्तुमपावृणोः । अपावृतद्वारमकरोः । किंच हे इन्द्र एभ्य उक्तेभ्य ऋषिभ्यः समान्या दिशा समानया रीत्या तेभ्यो यथा ददासि तद्वदस्मभ्यमपि जेषि । धनं सङ्ग्रामं वा जय । तदर्थं योत्सि । युध्यस्व च ॥ छान्दसो विकरणस्य लुक् । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदम् ॥ किंच त्वं सुन्वद्भ्यः सोमाभिषवं कुर्वद्भ्योऽस्मभ्यं कं चिदव्रतं सर्वमुप्यज्ञानं यागविरोधिनं रन्धय । बाधय । मदधीनं कुर्विति भावः । न केवलमयज्ञानं किंतु हृणायन्तं चिदव्रतम् ॥ चिदित्यवकुत्सन इत्यर्थः । अस्मासु रोषं कुर्वन्तं तमेवायाप्सारं स्वयं रोषवन्तं कं वा । यद्वा । हृणायन्तं चित् रोषं कुर्वन्तमप्यव्रतमकर्माणं पुनर्हननासमर्थं कुर्वन् रन्धय ॥ हृणीङ् रोषे कण्ड्वादिः । व्यत्ययेनाकारः ॥

he indra te tava sambandhi karmārtṛtvādyuktaprakāraṃ vakṣyamāṇarūpaṃ vā pūrvathā pūrvamiva pūrvaṃ yathā nu kṣipraṃ pravācyaṃ sarvaiḥ stotavyaṃ tadvadidānīmapi stutyam ‖ nū itthetyeṣāmakṣarādyitvātprakṛtibhāvaḥ ‖ kīdṛśaṃ tadityucyate | yattvamaṅgirobhya etannāmnebhyo maharṣibhyasteṣāmarthāya vrajamantarikṣe gacchantaṃ meghamapāvṛṇoḥ apāvṛtavānasi | meghamutpāṭya vṛṣṭimutpāditavānasi | vraja iti meghanāma | vrajo varāha iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ kiṃca he indra vrajaṃ gavāṃ samūhamapāyāpsyabhyo 'pahṛtya tebhya ivāṅgirobhyaḥ śikṣan vitaran rakṣitavānasi | yadvā | paṇibhirapahṛtaṃ bile sthitaṃ gavāṃ vrajamapahartumapāvṛṇoḥ | apāvṛtadvāramakaroḥ | kiṃca he indra ebhya uktebhya ṛṣibhyaḥ samānyā diśā samānayā rītyā tebhyo yathā dadāsi tadvadasmabhyamapi jeṣi | dhanaṃ saṅgrāmaṃ vā jaya | tadarthaṃ yotsi | yudhyasva ca ‖ chāndaso vikaraṇasya luk | vyatyayena parasmaipadam ‖ kiṃca tvaṃ sunvadbhyaḥ somābhiṣavaṃ kurvadbhyo 'smabhyaṃ kaṃ cidavrataṃ sarvamupyajñānaṃ yāgavirodhinaṃ randhaya | bādhaya | madadhīnaṃ kurviti bhāvaḥ | na kevalamayajñānaṃ kiṃtu hṛṇāyantaṃ cidavratam ‖ cidityavakutsana ityarthaḥ | asmāsu roṣaṃ kurvantaṃ tamevāyāpsāraṃ svayaṃ roṣavantaṃ kaṃ vā | yadvā | hṛṇāyantaṃ cit roṣaṃ kurvantamapyavratamakarmāṇaṃ punarhananāsamarthaṃ kurvan randhaya ‖ hṛṇīṅ roṣe kaṇḍvādiḥ | vyatyayenākāraḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he) indra — O Indra; yat (tvam — you who; aṅgirobhyaḥ — for the Aṅgirases; vrajam — the cloud moving in the sky; apa avṛṇoḥ — opened (and made it rain); (kiṃ ca — and); vrajam — the herd of cattle (stolen by the Paṇis); apa — [you] took away from those who stole it (breaking open the door); śikṣan — gave them; tat — such; te — your; ittham — of the stated kind; karma — deed; pūrvathā — as formerly (praised); nu ca — and now quickly too; pravācyam — must be praised; (kiṃ ca — and); (he indra — O Indra); ebhyaḥ — to these (ṛṣis above-mentioned); samānyā diśā — in one manner (as you give); asmabhyam — to us too; ā jeṣi — conquer wealth or victory in battle; yotsi ca — and fight; sunvadbhyaḥ — for us who press Soma (for you); avratam — one who does not perform the sacrifice (and is hostile to it); randhaya — subdue; kaṃ cit — any; hṛṇāyantam — who is angry at us; avratam — the non-sacrificer (and sacrifice-hating); cit — also; (randhaya — subdue, make subject to us).

original p. 521

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra, your brave deeds are worthy to be praised; as formerly, breaking the cloud that moves in the sky, you gave water and the cows to the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis, so now too you must be praised. O Indra, as you won wealth and victory for those ṛṣis and fought for them, so fight for us, who press Soma for you; subdue the non-sacrificers who are hostile to the rites and who rage against us, and make them subject to us.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Your exploits, Indra, are worthy to be glorified; now, verily, as well as in former times, when you opened the cloud for the Angirasas, restoring to them their cattle — conquer for us, fight for us, as you did for them: humble in behalf of those who present libations, him who offers no worship; him who rages against us, and offers no worship."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).

nū itthā te pūrvathā ca pravācyam — "the ṛṣis of former times described the greatness of Indra's deeds in many Ṛks — as in indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-1) and the like; so too it must now be done." Among these heroic deeds one that is chief is the story of how the demon called Vala carried off the cows of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis and hid them in a cave, and Indra released them and gave them back to the ṛṣis: this heroic deed is to be well praised: so the purport.

yad aṅgirobhyo 'vṛṇor apa vrajam indra śikṣann apa vrajam — the commentator gives two meanings for this sentence. The word vraja is explained as the cloud that moves in the sky: "Indra, for the delight of the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis, opened the cloud and made rain"; or, the cattle-herd (go-samūha) of the ṛṣi, stolen by the Paṇis, hidden in the cave: "Indra found them, opened the door of the cave and brought them out and gave them to the Aṅgirases." The word vraja is used twice in this Ṛk; one is the cloud, the other the herd of cattle stolen by the Paṇis. These points — the help Indra gave the Aṅgirases when he released the cows from the Paṇis — are told in Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] (as read "೧೦-೧೦೨-೩" [?]), etc.

original p. 522

aṅgirobhyaḥ — though the ṛṣi Aṅgiras is the first ancestor of the family of that name, the Ṛgveda says little about that ṛṣi himself; there are mentions of this ṛṣi in places such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]; 8-[?]-[?]; 3-[?]-[?]; Bṛhad-devatā [?], Aitareya Brāhmaṇa [?], Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 20-[?]-[?]; Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2-[?]-[?] and the like the numerals of this list are small and are not given: [?]. In places where the plural aṅgirobhyaḥ occurs, it should be taken as referring to the line of this ṛṣi.

ebhyaḥ samānyā diśā asmabhyaṃ jeṣi yotsi ca — "samānyā diśā, that is, samānayā rītyā — in the same way, the commentator explains. Therefore, the ṛṣi prays: 'As you helped the descendants of Aṅgiras, so help us too, fight our enemies and conquer them'."

sunvadbhyaḥ randhaya cit avratam — "sunvadbhyaḥ — for us who press Soma, or who perform the soma-yāga for your satisfaction, to be freed from distress. Avrata — those without vows, who do not perform rites (sacrificial rites). Therefore Indra is prayed to subdue the wicked who do not perform sacrifices for his satisfaction, and who cause us distress, and to destroy them, and to help us in a manner favourable to us."

hṛṇāyantaṃ cit avratam — here the word cit is used in the sense of contempt or reproach: "subdue the wicked who revile us in anger and do not perform sacrifices and other rites."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). nū — nṛtitunughaḥ… [as read: ṛcitunughamakṣutaṅ…, Pā. 6-3-133] gives lengthening in the Saṃhitā; nū + itthā, being īṣā-akṣādi [as read], prakṛtibhāva. pūrvathā — pratnapūrvaviśvemāt thāl chandasi (Pā. 5-3-111) gives thāl in the sense of similarity; liti (Pā. 6-1-193) gives the acute before the suffix.

original p. 523

pravācyam — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; ṛhalor ṇyat (Pā. 3-1-124) gives ṇyat; ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116) gives vṛddhi of the penult; ścuyoś ca… [as read: cajoḥ kughiṇṇyatoḥ, Pā. 7-3-52] would give kutva but the prohibition applies; since t-marked, the svarita — by vyatyaya the acute on the first syllable; or, after the ṇic-ending, yat with yato nāvaḥ gives the acute on the first syllable. avṛṇoḥ — root vṛñ varaṇe; laṅ second person singular; because yad is connected no nighāta; the first syllable acute by the augment. śikṣan — root śikṣa vidyopādāne [as read: dāne], recorded among the verbs of giving; śatṛ in the present sense; since lasārvadhātuka is unaccented the root's accent remains. samānyā — samānī + ā; yaṇ substitution; in place of the acute yaṇ; after it the case-ending, udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (Pā. 6-1-174) gives the acute to the ending; diśā — sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ gives the acute to the ending. jeṣi — root ji jaye; loṭ second person singular; because it follows [a non-finite word], by bahulaṃ chandasi luk of the vikaraṇa; since sip guṇa of the root's i; ādeśapratyayayoḥ gives ṣatva; tiṅ-nighāta. yotsi — root yudha saṃprahāre; vyatyayo bahulam gives the parasmaipada; as before luk of the vikaraṇa; short-vowel guṇa; khari ca (Pā. 8-4-55) gives car; because it follows a finite verb nighāta does not occur; since sip is p-marked the root's accent remains. sunvadbhyaḥ — root ṣuñ abhiṣave; śatṛ in place of laṭ; śnu as vikaraṇa; the vikaraṇa's accent remains. randhaya — root radha hiṃsāsaṃrādhyoḥ, divādi; hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26) gives ṇic; radhijabhor aci (Pā. 7-1-61) gives the augment num to the root; after the ṇic-ending, loṭ second person singular gives randhaya; tiṅ-nighāta. avratam — na vidyate vrataṃ yasya saḥ, tam; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the acute on the last syllable of the latter member.

original p. 524

Grammar of Ṛk 4, concluded. hṛṇāyantam — root hṛṇīṅ roṣe; kaṇḍvādi; kaṇḍvādibhyo yak (Pā. 3-1-27) gives yak in the proper sense; by vyatyaya the root takes ā; śatṛ in the present sense; the yak's accent remains; accusative singular. ‖ 4 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सं यज्जनान्क्रतुभिः शूर ईक्षयद्धने हिते तरुषन्त श्रवस्यवः । प्र यक्षन्त श्रवस्यवः । तस्मा आयुः प्रजावदिद्बाधे अर्चन्त्योजसा । इन्द्र ओक्यं दिधिषन्त धीतयो देवाँ अच्छा न धीतयः ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?]). Sense: "Since the hero Indra, brave, samīkṣayat — looks well on all creatures through their kratus (knowledge or deeds): staying within all, as the inner controller, he makes them look at their objects; or he impels them by their good and bad deeds to their results; and when he so impels, the sacrificers desiring food (śravasyavaḥ), when wealth, in the form of cattle and the like, is desired (hite dhane), tarūṣanta — destroy enemies. For this reason, desiring food or the oblation for themselves or for Indra, they sacrifice (pra yakṣanta) abundantly. Moreover for that Indra alone they present āyuḥ — the food in the form of oblation, accompanied by sons and the like; when there is bādhe — the harassing of enemies; or: bādhe is a name of strength: obtaining life and food accompanied by progeny, endowed with ojas — strength — they worship Indra. And the dhītayaḥ — the active sacrificers — dadhiṣanta — hold (aspire to) okyam — a dwelling-place in Indra's neighbourhood (as in 'a cowherd settlement on the Gaṅgā' the nearness is meant): the world of Indra; the pious ones, doing works that lead to heaven, aspire to dwell in front of the gods, as if reaching them."

यद्यस्मात्कारणादिन्द्रः शूरो विक्रान्तः सन् जनान् सर्वान्प्राणिनः क्रतुभिः प्रज्ञाभिः समीक्षयत् सम्यग्गिच्छति तत्तत्कर्मसमीक्षणान् । अन्तर्यामिरूपेण सर्वेषां बुद्धिषु स्थित्वा तैर्विषयानुल्लेखयतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । क्रतुभिः कर्मभिः सुकृतदुष्कृतरूपैस्तत्तत्फलेषु प्रेरयति । एवं प्रेरयति सति श्रवस्यवोऽन्नमिच्छन्तो यजमाना धने गवादिरूपे हिते ऽभिमते सति । यद्वा । हिते धने ऽभिप्रेते सति तरुषन्त हिंसन्ति शत्रून् ॥ तरुषतिर्वधकर्मा । छान्दसे लुङि व्यत्ययेन [?] ॥ अतः कारणात् श्रवस्यवोऽन्नमिच्छन्तो हविर्लक्षणमिन्द्रायात्मने वेच्छन्तः सन्तः प्र यक्षन्त । प्रकर्षेण यजन्ते ॥ छान्दसे लुङि व्यत्ययेन क्सः ॥ किंच तस्मा इत्तस्मै प्रसिद्धायेन्द्रायैव आयुः हविर्लक्षणमन्नं प्रजावत् पुत्रादिसहितमायुः [?] यजमानाः । बाधे बाधने शत्रूणां बाधने निमित्तभूते सति बाधितुं वा ॥ कृत्यार्थे तवै केन्केन्यत्वसनः इति केनन् प्रत्ययः ॥ अर्चन्ति । पूजयन्ति । यद्वा । तस्मा इद्यजमानायैव बाधे बले निमित्तभूते सति । बाध इति बलनाम बाधस्वेति तन्नामसु पाठात् । प्रजावत् पुत्राद्युपेतमायुरन्नं लब्ध्वोजसा बलेन युक्ता अर्चन्ति । इन्द्रं पूजयन्ति ऋत्विज इति शेषः ॥ किंच धीतयः कर्मवन्तो यजमाना इन्द्र इन्द्रसमीपे ओक्यं गङ्गायां घोष इतिवत् तत्सामीप्यं लक्ष्यते । इन्द्रलोक इत्यर्थः । तत्रैकमोकः निवासस्थानम् । स्वार्थे यत् ॥ दिधिषन्त । धारयन्ति । धिष शब्दे । अत्र धारणार्थः । जौहोत्यादिकः । वृत्त्यादिना[?] ॥ ते एव पुनर्विशेष्यन्ते । धीतयः स्वर्गसाधनकर्मवन्तः सन्तो देवान् अच्छ न देवानामभिमुखेन प्राप्तुमिवौक्यं दिधिषन्तेत्यन्वयः ॥

yadyasmātkāraṇādindraḥ śūro vikrāntaḥ san janān sarvānprāṇinaḥ kratubhiḥ prajñābhiḥ samīkṣayat samyaggicchati tattatkarmasamīkṣaṇān | antaryāmirūpeṇa sarveṣāṃ buddhiṣu sthitvā tairviṣayānullekhayatītyarthaḥ | yadvā | kratubhiḥ karmabhiḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛtarūpaistattatphaleṣu prerayati | evaṃ prerayati sati śravasyavo 'nnamicchanto yajamānā dhane gavādirūpe hite 'bhimate sati | yadvā | hite dhane 'bhiprete sati taruṣanta hiṃsanti śatrūn ‖ taruṣatirvadhakarmā | chāndase luṅi vyatyayena [?] ‖ ataḥ kāraṇāt śravasyavo 'nnamicchanto havirlakṣaṇamindrāyātmane vecchantaḥ santaḥ pra yakṣanta | prakarṣeṇa yajante ‖ chāndase luṅi vyatyayena ksaḥ ‖ kiṃca tasmā ittasmai prasiddhāyendrāyaiva āyuḥ havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ prajāvat putrādisahitamāyuḥ [?] yajamānāḥ | bādhe bādhane śatrūṇāṃ bādhane nimittabhūte sati bādhituṃ vā ‖ kṛtyārthe tavai kenkenyatvasanaḥ iti kenan pratyayaḥ ‖ arcanti | pūjayanti | yadvā | tasmā idyajamānāyaiva bādhe bale nimittabhūte sati | bādha iti balanāma bādhasveti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | prajāvat putrādyupetamāyurannaṃ labdhvojasā balena yuktā arcanti | indraṃ pūjayanti ṛtvija iti śeṣaḥ ‖ kiṃca dhītayaḥ karmavanto yajamānā indra indrasamīpe okyaṃ gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa itivat tatsāmīpyaṃ lakṣyate | indraloka ityarthaḥ | tatraikamokaḥ nivāsasthānam | svārthe yat ‖ didhiṣanta | dhārayanti | dhiṣa śabde | atra dhāraṇārthaḥ | jauhotyādikaḥ | vṛttyādinā[?] ‖ te eva punarviśeṣyante | dhītayaḥ svargasādhanakarmavantaḥ santo devān accha na devānāmabhimukhena prāptumivaukyaṃ didhiṣantetyanvayaḥ ‖

original p. 525

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. yat — because; śūraḥ — the heroic (Indra); janān — all creatures; kratubhiḥ — by their deeds (or by their intelligence); saṃ īkṣayat — looks well at (clearly makes seen) [or, impels well to the results, good and bad]; śravasyavaḥ — those desiring food (the sacrificers); dhane hite — when wealth, in the form of cattle, is desired [or: hite dhane — when wealth is the object]; taruṣanta — destroy the enemies; ataḥ — therefore; śravasyavaḥ — desiring food (for themselves or for Indra); pra yakṣanta — sacrifice abundantly; kiṃ ca — and; tasmā it — for that Indra alone; āyuḥ — the food in the form of oblation; prajāvat — accompanied by progeny (comes to you); or the sacrificers (give it); bādhe — to harass the enemies; arcanti — worship (Indra); or tasmā it — for that sacrificer; bādhe — when strength is the cause; prajāvat — accompanied by sons and the like; āyuḥ — food (for obtaining); ojasā — endowed with strength; the priests; arcanti — worship (Indra); dhītayaḥ — the sacrificers who do works; indre — near Indra; okyam — a dwelling-place; dadhiṣanta — they hold (they seek); devān accha na — as facing the gods; dhītayaḥ — the sacrificers who do works leading to heaven; okyam dadhiṣanta — aspire to a dwelling-place (in front of the gods).

original p. 526

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Indra, the hero, looks upon men, giving each the good and bad fruit according to his deeds; therefore, to defeat those who oppose them, the sacrificers who desire cattle and other wealth perform sacrifices for him and, desiring food, offer him oblations for his satisfaction; to conquer enemies by their own strength, they worship him; those who do works that lead to heaven aspire to a place near Indra, in front of the gods.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Inasmuch as the hero, (Indra), rightly judges men by their deeds, therefore do the (pious), sacrificing (to him) for sustenance, become enabled, by the wealth that has been attained, to overcome (their foes): desirous of food, they diligently worship (him): the (sacrificial) food offered to him is the source of progeny (to the worshipper), and (men) worship him, that by their own strength they may overcome (their foes): pious sacrificers enjoy residence in the heaven of Indra; pious sacrificers are, as it were, in the presence of the gods."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).

yat śūraḥ janān kratubhiḥ saṃ īkṣayat — here Sāyaṇa explains the word kratu in two ways: as prajñā ("intelligence", Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೩") and as karma ("work", Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೧"). In the sense "intelligence": "Indra, the hero, dwelling in all creatures as the inner controller, carefully looks upon and knows well the works they do and the thoughts in their minds"; in the sense "work": "Indra, who is the inner ruler in all, impels all the good and evil deeds that they do."

dhane hite taruṣanta śravasyavaḥ pra yakṣanta śravasyavaḥ — here the commentator explains the words dhane hite in two ways: "when wealth in the form of cattle is desired" — that is, to obtain wealth such as cows, or to obtain wealth, battle with enemies takes place, and it is proper (hita); the sacrificers obtain the wealth of their enemies by fighting and conquering them, and such wealth comes to us. Therefore war is the means of getting wealth. Because such a war is waged by the sacrificers together, to destroy their enemies, they prepare the food and oblations for the satisfaction of Indra and satisfy him with sacrifices and the like: so the meaning. The word śravaḥ is recorded among the names of wealth, maghaṃ rekṇaḥ and so on (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೯"), and the commentator explains it as wealth in the form of cattle or as food (in the form of oblation). Śravasyavaḥ means "those who desire food": since this word is repeated, in the first the meaning is "the sacrificers who desire food for themselves by Indra's grace"; in the second "the sacrificers who have prepared food in the form of oblation to offer to Indra".

original p. 527

"…with the wealth thus obtained, and by performing sacrifices, they satisfy Indra."

tasmai āyuḥ prajāvat it bādhe arcanti ojasā — here āyuḥ means "food": the word āyu is recorded among the eight names of food beginning with vājaḥ (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೯"). Therefore āyuḥ prajāvat means "food accompanied by sons and grandsons" — "life with sons and grandsons, and food". When the sacrificers are harassed by enemies, or in order to defeat and destroy those enemies, they offer oblations to Indra, with sons and grandsons, and worship him with their own power, that is, by sacrifices and the like, and by hymns: so one meaning. The word bādhā is recorded among the eight names of strength beginning with ojaḥ (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"): the meaning "strength". By offering oblations to Indra for the obtaining of sons and grandsons and for the gaining of food and the like, they worship Indra by sacrifices and by hymns: these are the two meanings, which the commentator explains.

indre okyaṃ dadhiṣanta dhītayaḥ — indre means "near Indra". Okya is "dwelling-place" (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೩"). Since the word dhī is recorded among the names of work (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೧"), dhītayaḥ means "sacrificers who do works such as sacrifices". "Such sacrificers wish to dwell near Indra." The word dhītayaḥ is used twice. In the second meaning, "the sacrificers who perform sacrifices leading to heaven wish to dwell in the presence of the gods; therefore they satisfy Indra by sacrifices and the like": so the purport.

devān accha na dhītayaḥ — "persons who wish for heaven perform sacrificial works that lead to heaven and wish to dwell facing the gods, that is, near the gods, in Indra's world": so the meaning.

original p. 528

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). īkṣayat — root īkṣa darśane; after the ṇic-ending the Vedic laṅ in the present sense; by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi (Pā. 6-4-75) no augment aṭ; third person singular; because yad is connected, no nighāta; the ṇic-accent remains. hite — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; suffix kta; dadhāter hiḥ (Pā. 7-4-42) gives hi to the root; acute on the last syllable by the suffix; locative singular. taruṣanta — root taruṣa [as read] is used in the sense of killing; by Vedic usage luṅ; third person plural, ant substituted; by vyatyaya cli gets aj; by Vedic usage no augment aṭ; or the root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, with the Vedic luṅ as before; by vyatyaya the u, sip, śap — thus three vikaraṇas; because it follows a finite verb nighāta does not occur. śravasyavaḥ — after the word śravas, in the sense of ātmecchā, kyac; after the kyac-ending u; acute on the last syllable by the suffix; nominative plural. yakṣanta — root yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ gives luṅ in the present sense; by vyatyaya cli is replaced by ksa; ant replaces jhi; vraścabhrasja… (Pā. 8-2-36) gives ṣ for j; ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (Pā. 8-2-41) gives k for it; because of that ṣatva of the s; ato guṇe gives pararūpa; by Vedic usage no augment; because it follows a finite verb, nighāta. bādhe — root bādhṛ viloḍane; kṛtyārthe tavaikenkeny… (Pā. 3-4-14) gives kenan; the e is left [as read]; ñnityādir nityam gives the acute on the first syllable; because it ends in e, kṛnmejantaḥ (Pā. 1-1-39) gives the name of an indeclinable. arcanti — root arca pūjāyām; laṭ third person plural; tiṅ-nighāta. okyam — oka means "place"; yat in the proper sense; yasyeti ca drops the a; tit svaritam (Pā. 6-1-185) gives the svarita accent. dadhiṣanta — root dhiṣa śabde; since roots have many meanings, here used in the sense of holding; juhotyādi; by Vedic usage luṅ in the present sense; third person plural

original p. 529

… [the suffix] ant by the substitute; by vyatyaya the ṛ… doubling of the root; because it is j-marked [as read] no guṇa of the penult; by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi no augment aṭ; tiṅ-nighāta. accha — nipātasya ca (Pā. 6-3-136) gives the long vowel. ‖ 5 ‖

(ornamental rule)

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

युवं तमिन्द्रापर्वता पुरोयुधा यो नः पृतन्यादप तंतमिद्धतं वज्रेण तंतमिद्धतम् । दूरे चत्ताय च्छन्त्सद्गहनं यदिनक्षत् । अस्माकं शत्रून्परि शूर विश्वतो दर्मा दर्षीष्ट विश्वतः ॥ ६ ॥

yuvaṃ tamindrāparvatā puroyudhā yo naḥ pṛtanyādapa taṃtamiddhataṃ vajreṇa taṃtamiddhatam | dūre cattāya cchantsadgahanaṃ yadinakṣat | asmākaṃ śatrūnpari śūra viśvato darmā darṣīṣṭa viśvataḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Read from the image. In the Saṃhitā's second line the print "dūre cattāya chantsad gahanaṃ yad inakṣat" is partly doubtful ("cattāya", "chantsat"): given as printed [?]; the Pada divides chantsat, inakṣat. The upper half of Ṛk 6 is addressed to Indra and Parvata, the second half to Indra alone.

युवम् । तम् । इन्द्रापर्वता । पुरःऽयुधा । यः । नः । पृतन्यात् । अप । तम्ऽतम् । इत् । हतम् । वज्रेण । तम्ऽतम् । इत् । हतम् । दूरे । चत्ताय । छन्त्सत् । गहनम् । यत् । इनक्षत् । अस्माकम् । शत्रून् । परि । शूर । विश्वतः । दर्मा । दर्षीष्ट । विश्वतः ॥ ६ ॥

yuvam | tam | indrāparvatā | puraḥ 'yudhā | yaḥ | naḥ | pṛtanyāt | apa | tam 'tam | it | hatam | vajreṇa | tam 'tam | it | hatam | dūre | cattāya | chantsat | gahanam | yat | inakṣat | asmākam | śatrūn | pari | śūra | viśvataḥ | darmā | darṣīṣṭa | viśvataḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (begins at the foot of p. 529; read from the image). Sense: "On a non-vivākya day, after the drinking of the mānasa-grahas [?], when the stars are seen, all, with the Adhvaryu at their head, are to mutter this yuvaṃ tam indra [Ṛk]; stated in the Śrauta-sūtra, section 'gārhapatye juṣṭastīti' [?]: 'muttering yuvaṃ tam indrāparvatā purojudhā' (Āś. 8-13 [?], as read "೮-೧೩")." The reading of this small-type sūtra reference is doubtful: [?].

अविवाक्येऽहनि मानसग्रहभक्षणानन्तरं नक्षत्रेषु दृश्यमानेष्वध्वर्युप्रमुखाः सर्वे युवं तमिन्द्रैकेषां जपेयुः । गार्हपत्ये जुष्टस्तीति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । युवं तमिन्द्रापर्वता पुरोयुधेति जपन्तः । ऋ. ८-१३ [?] इति ॥

avivākye 'hani mānasagrahabhakṣaṇānantaraṃ nakṣatreṣu dṛśyamāneṣvadhvaryupramukhāḥ sarve yuvaṃ tamindraikeṣāṃ japeyuḥ | gārhapatye juṣṭastīti khaṇḍe sūtritam | yuvaṃ tamindrāparvatā puroyudheti japantaḥ | ṛ. 8-13 [?] iti ‖

original p. 530

हे इन्द्रापर्वता । इन्द्रः प्रसिद्धः । पर्वतः पर्ववान्मेघः । तदभिमानिनौ देवौ । तौ युवं युवां पुरोयुधा सङ्ग्रामे पुरतो योद्धारौ नोऽस्माकं यः शत्रुः पृतन्यात् अस्मान् हन्तुं पृतनामात्मन इच्छति तं तमिद् सर्वमपि शत्रुमपहतम् । नाशयतम् । हन्तेर्लोट्यनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यनुनासिकलोपः ॥ केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । तं तस्मिन् सर्वमपि शत्रुं हन्तुं वज्रेण साधनेन प्राप्नुतम् । ईदृक् सामर्थ्यमस्तीति दर्शयति । यद्वोऽवज्रः । लिङ्गव्यत्ययः ॥ दूरे चत्तायोत्यन्तदूरदेशे गताय ॥ चतायतेर्वा नाशकर्मणः । निष्प्रायः । आदर्शनमापन्नायेत्यर्थः । ग्रसितस्कभितेत्यादौ निपातनादिडभावः ॥ ताद्दृशं शत्रुं छन्त्सत् छन्दयति कामयते हन्तुम् । छन्देः कान्तिकर्मण इदं रूपम् । किंच गहनं दुरवगाहं स्थानमतिकठिनं हृदयं शत्रुसमीपे वेनक्षत् व्याप्नोति । नक्ष गतौ । छान्दस इकारोपजनः । इनक्षतीर्वा प्रकृत्यन्तरम् ॥ इदानीमिन्द्र एव स्तूयते । हे शूर शौर्योपेतेन्द्र अस्माकं विरोधिनः शत्रून् विश्वतो विश्वान् । सार्वविभक्तिकस्तसिल् ॥ परि परितो विश्वतो विश्वरूपायैर्दर्षीष्ट । दारयसि । किंच दर्मा शत्रूणां दारकः । दारयतेर्मेन्भ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । णिलोप उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण मनिन उदात्तत्वम् ॥ दृ भये । घटादित्वान्मितां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वम् ॥ कव पूर्वोक्तो वज्रो विश्वतः सर्वान्शत्रून् सर्वरूपायैर्वा दर्षीष्ट । दारयति । यद्वा । दर्मा शत्रूणां दारक इन्द्रो दर्षीष्ट । काष्ठ्स्नर्येन दारयति शत्रून् ॥

he indrāparvatā | indraḥ prasiddhaḥ | parvataḥ parvavānmeghaḥ | tadabhimāninau devau | tau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ puroyudhā saṅgrāme purato yoddhārau no 'smākaṃ yaḥ śatruḥ pṛtanyāt asmān hantuṃ pṛtanāmātmana icchati taṃ tamid sarvamapi śatrumapahatam | nāśayatam | hanterloṭyanudāttopadeśetyanunāsikalopaḥ ‖ kena sādhaneneti taducyate | taṃ tasmin sarvamapi śatruṃ hantuṃ vajreṇa sādhanena prāpnutam | īdṛk sāmarthyamastīti darśayati | yadvo 'vajraḥ | liṅgavyatyayaḥ ‖ dūre cattāyotyantadūradeśe gatāya ‖ catāyatervā nāśakarmaṇaḥ | niṣprāyaḥ | ādarśanamāpannāyetyarthaḥ | grasitaskabhitetyādau nipātanādiḍabhāvaḥ ‖ tāddṛśaṃ śatruṃ chantsat chandayati kāmayate hantum | chandeḥ kāntikarmaṇa idaṃ rūpam | kiṃca gahanaṃ duravagāhaṃ sthānamatikaṭhinaṃ hṛdayaṃ śatrusamīpe venakṣat vyāpnoti | nakṣa gatau | chāndasa ikāropajanaḥ | inakṣatīrvā prakṛtyantaram ‖ idānīmindra eva stūyate | he śūra śauryopetendra asmākaṃ virodhinaḥ śatrūn viśvato viśvān | sārvavibhaktikastasil ‖ pari parito viśvato viśvarūpāyairdarṣīṣṭa | dārayasi | kiṃca darmā śatrūṇāṃ dārakaḥ | dārayatermenbhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | ṇilopa udāttanivṛttisvareṇa manina udāttatvam ‖ dṛ bhaye | ghaṭāditvānmitāṃ hrasva iti hrasvatvam ‖ kava pūrvokto vajro viśvataḥ sarvānśatrūn sarvarūpāyairvā darṣīṣṭa | dārayati | yadvā | darmā śatrūṇāṃ dāraka indro darṣīṣṭa | kāṣṭhsnaryena dārayati śatrūn ‖

Sense: "O Indra and Parvata — Indra the well-known; Parvata, the parvavat cloud — the deities presiding over them: you two, purojudhā — fighting in front in battle — whichever enemy of ours (yaḥ pṛtanyāt) wishes an army against us in order to kill us — destroy (apa hatam) each and every such enemy. With what? With the thunderbolt (vajreṇa) obtain [him] to kill every enemy; so it shows that such power exists. The enemy gone very far (dūre cattāya) [cata in the sense 'destroyed', 'out of sight'], or one who wishes to kill (chantsat, from chand, 'to desire'); the difficult, impenetrable place (gahanam), the very hard heart near the enemy, [the thunderbolt] pervades (inakṣat). Now Indra alone is praised: O hero Indra, our enemies on all sides (viśvataḥ) you tear apart (dardṛṣṭa); and darmā — the tearer of enemies; or the thunderbolt, mentioned before, tears all enemies completely."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (he) indrāparvatā — O Indra and clouds (O Indra and the deity of the clouds); yuvam — you two; puroyudhā — fighting in front in battle; naḥ — our; yaḥ — which enemy; pṛtanyāt — desires an army to kill us; tam tam it — every such enemy; apa hatam — destroy; yat — which; dūre — far away; cattāya — gone (out of sight); tam — such an enemy; chantsat — desires to kill (and); gahanam — a very difficult place (the very hard-hearted enemy); inakṣat — pervades; vajreṇa — with the thunderbolt; tam tam it hatam — kill every such one; he śūra — O brave Indra; asmākam — our; viśvataḥ — all; śatrūn — enemies; pari — completely; viśvataḥ — by all means; dardṛṣṭa — you tear; darmā — the thunderbolt, destroyer of enemies [of Indra]; (śatrūn — enemies); viśvataḥ — completely; dardṛṣṭa — tears apart.

original p. 531

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra and Parvata (the cloud), you who are in front in all battles: kill all those who wish to fight us; to destroy the enemies, with the thunderbolt that pursues them however far, in whatever dense place, and kills them; O brave Indra, destroy completely our enemies by all means; and may the thunderbolt, the tearer of enemies, kill them.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Indra and Parvata, who are foremost in battles, slay every one who is arrayed against us; slay every such (adversary) with the thunderbolt — (the shaft that) bent upon his destruction pursues him, however far, or to whatever hiding-place he may have fled. You, hero, (tear) our enemies entirely to pieces; the tearer (of foes, the thunderbolt), rends them entirely asunder."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).

indrāparvatā — by this word Indra and the cloud (or the deity presiding over the cloud) are addressed. This word is found in the Ṛgveda only in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-132-6; 1-[?]-[?]; 3-[?]-[?]; and nowhere else. In explaining Ṛ.
