॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). avaḥ — pūrvādharāvarāṇām asi puradhavaś caiṣām (Pā. 5-3-39 [as read]) gives the suffix asi in the sense of "[direction]" to the word [avara]; it being a para [?], an is substituted for the stem; the form avas; by amnarūdharavarity ubhayathā chandasi (Pā. 8-2-70 [as read]) a repha [replaces the s]. mahaḥ — root maha pūjāyām; kvip ca gives the kvip suffix; genitive singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending; the genitive is in the sense of karman [i.e. object]. dādṛhi — root dṛ vidāraṇe; loṭ second person singular, sip, replaced by hi; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-73 [as read]) the vikaraṇa [śap] is luk-ed; ślau doubling of the root; ced… by the sūtra-statement the nighāta is prohibited and the final udātta by suffix-accent; in the Saṃhitā, by Vedic usage, the reduplicate is long. śrudhi — root śru śravaṇe; as before the hi suffix; śṛṇuprucchikṛ… (Pā. 6-4-102 [as read]) gives dhi; bahulaṃ chandasi [elision] of the vikaraṇa; no guṇa, as the suffix is [ṅit]; no nighāta as it is the beginning of a pāda; final udātta as before; dvyacas tasyajaḥ [as read] gives long in the Saṃhitā. śuśoca — root śuca śoke; liṭ third person singular; tiṅ → ṇal; doubling of the root; the laghūpadha guṇa because of the suffix; liti (Pā. 6-1-193 [as read]) gives the udātta to the syllable before the suffix. kṣāḥ — root kṣai jai pai kṣaye; kṣāyanti nivasanty asyām iti kṣāḥ; kvip in the sense of adhikaraṇa; ādeca upadeśe 'śiti (Pā. 6-1-45 [as read]) gives ā to the root.

original p. 562

Grammar, continued. śuṣmintamaḥ — root śuṣa śoṣaṇe; avisivi… (Uṇ. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೪೧" [?]) gives the man suffix; śuṣmo 'syāstīti śuṣmī; the suffix ini in the sense of matup; to this, in the sense of intensity, tamap is added; as it is anudātta, the vowel i has its own accent. vadhaiḥ — root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; hanasya vadhaḥ (Pā. 3-3-76 [as read]) [ap suffix and] vadha-substitute for the stem; as the accent of udātta has ceased, the suffix is udātta. īyase — root īṅ gatau; divādi; laṭ second person singular, thās; thāsaḥ se gives se; divādibhyaḥ śyan (Pā. 3-1-69 [as read]) śyan as vikaraṇa; hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34 [as read]) prohibits the nighāta; tāsyanudāttenṅit [as read] (Pā. 6-1-186 [as read]) since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta the vikaraṇa [śyan] being nit, the ādyudātta accent occurs. apratīta — root iṅ smaraṇe [as read]; kta suffix; in the vocative the āmantrita-nighāta accent. ‖ 6 ‖

Rik 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

वनोति हि सुन्वन्क्षयं परीणसः सुन्वानो हि ष्मा यजत्यव द्विषो देवानामव द्विषः । सुन्वान इत्सिषासति सहस्रा वाज्यवृतः । सुन्वानायेन्द्रो ददात्याभुवं रयिं ददात्याभुवम् ॥ ७ ॥

vanoti hi sunvankṣayaṃ parīṇasaḥ sunvāno hi ṣmā yajatyava dviṣo devānāmava dviṣaḥ | sunvāna itsiṣāsati sahasrā vājyavṛtaḥ | sunvānāyendro dadātyābhuvaṃ rayiṃ dadātyābhuvam ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

वनोति । हि । सुन्वन् । क्षयम् । परीणसः । सुन्वानः । हि । स्म । यजति । अव । द्विषः । देवानाम् । अव । द्विषः । सुन्वानः । इत् । सिषासति । सहस्रा । वाजी । अवृतः । सुन्वानाय । इन्द्रः । ददाति । आऽभुवम् । रयिम् । ददाति । आऽभुवम् ॥ ७ ॥

vanoti | hi | sunvan | kṣayam | parīṇasaḥ | sunvānaḥ | hi | sma | yajati | ava | dviṣaḥ | devānām | ava | dviṣaḥ | sunvānaḥ | it | siṣāsati | sahasrā | vājī | avṛtaḥ | sunvānāya | indraḥ | dadāti | ā 'bhuvam | rayim | dadāti | ā 'bhuvam ‖ 7 ‖

original p. 563

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 7; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "At the morning pressing, this Ṛk vanoti hi is to be inserted before the prasthita-yājyā of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; it is prescribed in the same section: 'vanoti hi sunvan kṣayaṃ parīṇaso mo ṣu vo asmad abhi tāni pauṃsyā' (Āś. [refs] [?]). O Indra, the sacrificer who presses for you gets (vanoti, wins) a dwelling [kṣaya] — a house which you may come to, [as accessible] for all classes; by your favour he obtains it. Hi is of a well-known sense. Further, the sacrificer who performs a Soma-sacrifice destroys (ava yajati) the enemies bound around him on all sides (parīṇasaḥ), the haters; and not only the enemies of the sacrifice but also the enemies of the gods. And further, the one who performs the sacrifice marked by pressing, O Indra, by your grace vājī — possessed of food — unconquered, surrounded by none [avṛtaḥ], desires (siṣāsati) to gain (san) thousands — innumerable — of riches such as cows. By what means is this obtained? — Indra gives to the sacrificer who performs the Soma-sacrifice with Indra in view ābhuvam — plentiful, all-pervading, ever-growing, very abundant — wealth in the form of cows and so on." Some grammatical remarks on siṣāsati are not transcribed.

प्रातःसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः प्रस्थितयाज्यायाः पुरस्ताद्वनोति हीत्येषा प्रक्षेपणीया । तत्रैव खण्डे सूत्रितं । वनोति हि सुन्वन्क्षयं परीणसो मो षु वो अस्मदभि तानि पौंस्या । आ. ८-१ [?] इति ॥

prātaḥsavane brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ prasthitayājyāyāḥ purastādvanoti hītyeṣā prakṣepaṇīyā | tatraiva khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | vanoti hi sunvankṣayaṃ parīṇaso mo ṣu vo asmadabhi tāni pauṃsyā | ā. 8-1 [?] iti ‖

हे इन्द्र सुन्वन् त्वामुद्दिश्याभिषवं कुर्वन्यजमानः क्षयं सर्वैर्वर्णैस्त्वया गन्तव्यं वा गृहं वनोति हि । त्वत्प्रसादात्संभजते । हि प्रसिद्धार्थः । किंच सुन्वानो हि सोमयागं कुर्वाण एव परीणसः परितो नद्धान् संबद्धान् द्विषो द्वेष्टॄन् अवयजति नाशयति । न केवलं योगद्वेषिणो देवानां द्विषोऽप्यव यजति । किंच सुन्वान इदभिषवोपलक्षितं यागं कुर्वाणो हे इन्द्र त्वत्प्रसादाद्वाजी वाजवानन्नवान् अवृतः पर्यवरणाक्रान्तः सन् सहस्रा सहस्राण्यपरिमितानि गवादिधनानि सिषासति । साधयितुं संभक्तुं वेच्छति । सनेः सनि सनीवंतर्धेति विकल्पनादिभावे जनसनखनेत्यात्वम् ॥ केनेदं लभ्यत इति तत्राह । सुन्वानायेन्द्रमुद्दिश्य सोमयागं कुर्वाणाय यजमानाय वायुमिन्द्र आभुवं समन्ताद्भवनशीलं तथाभुवं पुनर्भवनशीलमतिसमृद्धं रयिं गवादिरूपं धनं ददाति । प्रयच्छति । तस्मात्सुन्वानः सिषासतीत्यर्थः ॥

he indra sunvan tvāmuddiśyābhiṣavaṃ kurvanyajamānaḥ kṣayaṃ sarvairvarṇaistvayā gantavyaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vanoti hi | tvatprasādātsaṃbhajate | hi prasiddhārthaḥ | kiṃca sunvāno hi somayāgaṃ kurvāṇa eva parīṇasaḥ parito naddhān saṃbaddhān dviṣo dveṣṭṝn avayajati nāśayati | na kevalaṃ yogadveṣiṇo devānāṃ dviṣo 'pyava yajati | kiṃca sunvāna idabhiṣavopalakṣitaṃ yāgaṃ kurvāṇo he indra tvatprasādādvājī vājavānannavān avṛtaḥ paryavaraṇākrāntaḥ san sahasrā sahasrāṇyaparimitāni gavādidhanāni siṣāsati | sādhayituṃ saṃbhaktuṃ vecchati | saneḥ sani sanīvaṃtardheti vikalpanādibhāve janasanakhanetyātvam ‖ kenedaṃ labhyata iti tatrāha | sunvānāyendramuddiśya somayāgaṃ kurvāṇāya yajamānāya vāyumindra ābhuvaṃ samantādbhavanaśīlaṃ tathābhuvaṃ punarbhavanaśīlamatisamṛddhaṃ rayiṃ gavādirūpaṃ dhanaṃ dadāti | prayacchati | tasmātsunvānaḥ siṣāsatītyarthaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he indra — O Indra; sunvan — the sacrificer who prepares Soma-juice (for you); kṣayam — a dwelling (a house); vanoti hi — gets (by your grace); sunvānaḥ hi — the one who prepares Soma-juice; parīṇasaḥ — who are all around; dviṣaḥ — enemies; ava yajati sma — destroys (and not only these); devānām — the gods'; dviṣaḥ — enemies; ava (yajati) — destroys; sunvānāya — to the one who performs the sacrifice (in view of Indra); indraḥ — Indra; ābhuvam — abundant; rayim — wealth in cows and the like; dadāti — gives; ābhuvam — plentiful (wealth); dadāti — favours (with); tasmāt — therefore; sunvānaḥ it — the very one who performs the Soma-sacrifice; vājī — (by your favour) possessed of food; avṛtaḥ — (by others) unconquered; sahasrā — unlimited (wealth in cows and the like); siṣāsati — wishes to get.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra, one who prepares Soma-juice (for you) gets a dwelling by your favour; one who performs the Soma-sacrifice destroys the enemies around him, and the enemies of the gods also. To the one who performs the Soma-sacrifice Indra gives immense wealth in cows and the like. Therefore, O Indra, the performer of the Soma-sacrifice, by your favour possessed of food and (by others) unconquered, wishes to get unlimited wealth.

original p. 564

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Offering libations (the worshipper) obtains a (safe) asylum: offering libations, he destroys his prostrate foes: (he destroys) the enemies of the gods: abounding with food, and unsubdued (by adversaries), he hopes to attain, when offering libations, infinite (riches), for Indra grants to him who offers libations whatever there is (that he desires); he grants (him) accumulated wealth." [Print: "worshippcr" (sic); "prostrate".]

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 7).

At the morning pressing, for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest to recite before the prasthita-yājyā mantra, this Ṛk vanoti hi is to be recited as an insertion — so it is explained by the Śrauta-sūtra of Āśvalāyana, in the section called ṣaṣṭhasya, by the sūtra "vanoti hi sunvan kṣayaṃ parīṇaso mo ṣu vo asmadabhi tāni pauṃsyā" (Āś. [refs] [?]).

The meaning of this Ṛk is clear. For the one who offers Soma-juice for Indra, the Ṛṣi in this Ṛk has stated, by way of conclusion, the description of the wealth of cows, and the conquest of enemies, that Indra gives.

vanoti hi sunvan kṣayam — kṣaya means sarvair varṇaiḥ tvayā gantavyaṃ vā gṛham — "a house in which all stay for sleep [?], or the house one wishes to go to (to obtain rest)". The word, derived from the root kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ, indicates a dwelling-place. The sacrificer (or man) who prepares Soma in view of Indra and offers that Soma-juice to Indra gets a house fit to dwell in — this is the idea.

parīṇasaḥ sunvāno hi ṣmā yajati ava dviṣo devānām ava dviṣaḥ — kiṃca sunvāno somayāgaṃ kurvāṇa eva parīṇasaḥ parito naddhān saṃbaddhān dviṣo dveṣṭṝn avayajati nāśayati | na kevalaṃ yāgadveṣiṇo devānāṃ dviṣo 'py avayajati. Besides, the man who performs the Soma-sacrifice for the pleasure of Indra becomes capable of destroying the enemies around him and the enemies of the gods also.

sunvāna it siṣāsati sahasrā vājy avṛtaḥ — and the man who performs the Soma-sacrifice, by Indra's favour becomes possessed of food and free from the obstruction of enemies. Vāja means food or provisions (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೭"). Avṛtaḥ — from the root vṛñ varaṇe ("to cover") the word vṛta [is formed], meaning covered; avṛtaḥ means "one not covered, i.e. not hindered by enemies", that is "not subject to the obstructions of enemies". The word sahasra means sahasrāṇy aparimitāni — "many, countless".

original p. 565

sunvānāya indraḥ dadāti ābhuvaṃ rayiṃ dadāti — "to the man who performs the Soma-sacrifice in view of Indra, Indra gives wealth in the forms of cows, houses and food in abundance" — thus the ṛṣi praises the liberality of Indra.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). vanoti — root vana saṃbhaktau; śnu as vikaraṇa; laṭ third person singular; as it is not at the beginning of a pāda, [it is] in a nighāta position [as read]; nighāta accent does not occur, the accent of the vikaraṇa remains. sunvan — root ṣuñ abhiṣave; śatṛ substituted for laṭ; nominative singular; the suffix's initial udātta accent comes. In sunvānaḥ, śānac is substituted for laṭ; cita (Pā. 6-1-163 [as read]) gives the final udātta. parīṇasaḥ — root ṇasa kauṭilye; here used in the sense of gati [motion]; kvip by kvip ca; niṣāpaśca [as read] (Pā. 6-3-116 [as read]) gives the long in the earlier member; upasargāt samāse 'pi [as read] (Pā. 8-4-14 [as read]) gives ṇatva; by vyatyaya the ādyudātta accent comes. yajati — hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34 [as read]) gives nighāta prohibition; as śap, tip are anudātta, the accent of the root remains. dviṣaḥ — root dviṣa aprītau; kvip ca gives kvip; accusative plural. siṣāsati — root ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ gives sa for the initial ṣa; dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā [as read] (Pā. 3-1-7 [as read]) gives san in the sense of desire; sanīvantardha… (Pā. 7-2-49 [as read]) the iṭ is optional, so here it does not occur; janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ (Pā. 6-4-42 [as read]) gives ā to the root; sanyaṅoḥ gives doubling; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. sahasrā — in the neuter, śi is substituted; by śeś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70 [as read]) śi is dropped. avṛtaḥ — root vṛñ varaṇe; suffix kta; ñañ-tatpuruṣa compound; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2 [as read]) gives the earlier member its own accent. dadāti — root ḍudāñ dāne; laṭ, third person singular; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. ‖ 7 ‖

Here ends the 133rd Sūkta. Kannada closing line: "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತಮೂರನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮುಗಿದುದು". Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 134" [as read].

Sūkta 134 — ā tvā juvo (begins on printed p. 566; Anuvāka 20, first of six Sūktas)

original p. 566

ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra mūvattanālkaneya sūktavu (the one hundred and thirty-fourth Sūkta).

॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; doubtful letters [?]).

विंशेऽनुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्रा त्वा जुव इति षडृचं प्रथमं सूक्तं पारुच्छेपमात्यष्टम् [?] । त्वं नो वायविति [?] चतुष्पदाक्षरा [?] । वायव्यं त्रित्यच्छमानत्वादिदमुत्तरं च वायुदेवत्यं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । आ त्वा षड्वायव्यं त्वंत्याष्टिरिति [?] । विनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

viṃśe 'nuvāke ṣaṭ sūktāni | tatrā tvā juva iti ṣaḍṛcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktaṃ pārucchepam ātyaṣṭam [?] | tvaṃ no vāyaviti [?] catuṣpadākṣarā [?] | vāyavyaṃ trityacchamānatvād idam uttaraṃ ca vāyudevatyaṃ | atrānukramaṇikā | ā tvā ṣaḍ vāyavyaṃ tvaṃtyāṣṭir iti [?] | viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖

Kannada anuvāda (translated). With this Sūkta the twentieth Anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala begins. In this Anuvāka there are six Sūktas. Of them this Sūkta ā tvā juvaḥ is the first; it has six ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Paruccheṣa; the deity is Vāyu; the metre is Atyaṣṭi. The last ṛk, with the fourth pāda of sixteen [?] syllables tvaṃ no vāyo, is in the metre called Aṣṭi. In the Anukramaṇikā, because the word tu is used in "vāyavyaṃ tu", this Sūkta and the next Sūkta have Vāyu as their deity; and the Anukramaṇikā says "ā tvā ṣaḍ vāyavyaṃ tvaṃ tyāṣṭiḥ" [as read]. The use (viniyoga) is laiṅgika (by the sense of the text).

ಸೂಕ್ತ — Sūkta 134 [as read]. Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 20; Sūkta 134. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24 [as read, [?]]. Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 6. Ṛṣi — Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi. Devatā — Vāyu. Chandas — 1–5 Atyaṣṭi; 6 Aṣṭi [as printed: "೧-೫ ಅತ್ಯಷ್ಟಿ | ೬ ಅಷ್ಟಿ"].

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24 [as read].

आ त्वा जुवो रारहाणा अभि प्रयो वायो वहन्त्विह पूर्वपीतये सोमस्य पूर्वपीतये । ऊर्ध्वा ते अनु सूनृता मनस्तिष्ठतु जानती । नियुत्वता रथेना याहि दावने वायो मखस्य दावने ॥ १ ॥

ā tvā juvo rārahāṇā abhi prayo vāyo vahantviha pūrvapītaye somasya pūrvapītaye | ūrdhvā te anu sūnṛtā manastiṣṭhatu jānatī | niyutvatā rathenā yāhi dāvane vāyo makhasya dāvane ‖ 1 ‖

original p. 567

॥ पदपाठः ॥ The Pada prints "rarāhāṇāḥ" with short a in the first syllable, against the Saṃhitā "rārahāṇāḥ"; given as printed.

आ । त्वा । जुवः । रराहाणाः । अभि । प्रयः । वायो इति । वहन्तु । इह । पूर्वऽपीतये । सोमस्य । पूर्वऽपीतये । ऊर्ध्वा । ते । अनु । सूनृता । मनः । तिष्ठतु । जानती । नियुत्वता । रथेन । आ । याहि । दावने । वायो इति । मखस्य । दावने ॥ १ ॥

ā | tvā | juvaḥ | rarāhāṇāḥ | abhi | prayaḥ | vāyo iti | vahantu | iha | pūrva 'pītaye | somasya | pūrva 'pītaye | ūrdhvā | te | anu | sūnṛtā | manaḥ | tiṣṭhatu | jānatī | niyutvatā | rathena | ā | yāhi | dāvane | vāyo iti | makhasya | dāvane ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

हे वायो त्वा त्वां जुवो गमनशीला रराहाणाः शीघ्रगामिनो बलवन्तो वा सामर्थ्यान्नियुत्संज्ञका अश्वाः । रहि गतौ । लिटः कानच् । छान्दसोऽनुनासिकलोपः ॥ इहास्मिन्यज्ञे प्रयोऽन्नं पुरोडाशादि हविर्लक्षणमन्नमभि वहन्तु । प्रापयन्तु । किमर्थं पूर्वपीतये पूर्ववत्पानाय [?] । पुनः किमर्थं । सोमस्य पूर्वपीतये इतरदेवेभ्यः पुरा पानाय ॥ मरुद्वृधादित्वात्पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । किंच हे वायो ते तव संबन्धि मनोऽनु सूनृता प्रियसत्यात्मिका स्तुतिरूपास्मदीया वाक् तिष्ठतु । आश्रित्य सर्वदा वर्तताम् । हर्षयत्वित्यर्थः । सूनृतेति वाङ्नाम । सूनृता ब्रह्मेति तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् [?] । ऊर्ध्वोन्नता तथा जानती तव गुणान्विशेषेणागच्छन्ती [?] । सोमपानार्थं स्तुत्यर्थं च हे वायो मखस्य यज्ञस्य दावने दात्व्याय हविषे तत्स्वीकाराय । पुनः किमर्थम् । दावनेऽस्मभ्यमभिमतदानाय ॥ उभयत्र दादेः कर्मणि भावे च क्रेनोः [?] औणादिको वनिः । छान्दस उपधालोपः ॥ नियुत्वता रथेन नियुद्भिर्युक्तेन रथेना याहि । आगच्छ ॥

he vāyo tvā tvāṃ juvo gamanaśīlā rarāhāṇāḥ śīghragāmino balavanto vā sāmarthyānniyutsaṃjñakā aśvāḥ | rahi gatau | liṭaḥ kānac | chāndaso 'nunāsikalopaḥ ‖ ihāsminyajñe prayo 'nnaṃ puroḍāśādi havirlakṣaṇamannamabhi vahantu | prāpayantu | kimarthaṃ pūrvapītaye pūrvavatpānāya [?] | punaḥ kimarthaṃ | somasya pūrvapītaye itaradevebhyaḥ purā pānāya ‖ marudvṛdhāditvātpūrvapadāntodāttatvam | kiṃca he vāyo te tava saṃbandhi mano 'nu sūnṛtā priyasatyātmikā stutirūpāsmadīyā vāk tiṣṭhatu | āśritya sarvadā vartatām | harṣayatvityarthaḥ | sūnṛteti vāṅnāma | sūnṛtā brahmeti tannāmasūktatvāt [?] | ūrdhvonnatā tathā jānatī tava guṇānviśeṣeṇāgacchantī [?] | somapānārthaṃ stutyarthaṃ ca he vāyo makhasya yajñasya dāvane dātvyāya haviṣe tatsvīkārāya | punaḥ kimartham | dāvane 'smabhyamabhimatadānāya ‖ ubhayatra dādeḥ karmaṇi bhāve ca krenoḥ [?] auṇādiko vaniḥ | chāndasa upadhālopaḥ ‖ niyutvatā rathena niyudbhiryuktena rathenā yāhi | āgaccha ‖

(Sense: "O Vāyu, the juvaḥ* — swift-moving — rarāhāṇāḥ, fast-going or powerful horses named niyut [from the root rahi gatau, liṭ with kānac, the nasal elided by Vedic usage], bring to you, here at this sacrifice, the prayaḥ — food, the oblation-food of cake (puroḍāśa) and the like — for pūrvapīti, the first drinking [before the other gods] of Soma. [The accent pūrvapadāntodātta by the marudvṛdhādi rule.] Further, O Vāyu: let our speech — a praise, of a kind both dear and true (sūnṛtā) — rest ever, depending on your mind, and gladden [you]; sūnṛtā is a name of speech (vāk). Upright (ūrdhvā), knowing your qualities well, for the drinking of Soma and for praise; O Vāyu, for the giving (dāvane) of the oblation [to be given] to the sacrifice (makha) and for its acceptance; and for the giving of what we desire to us. Come with the niyut-yoked car." Grammar of dāvane: Uṇādi vani after dā [with kṛ ending?] in the sense of object or state; the penultimate elision by Vedic usage; [doubtful]).*

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he) vāyo — O Vāyu; tvā — you; juvaḥ — of swift movement and rarāhāṇāḥ — fast-going (powerful) horses; iha — in this sacrifice; prayaḥ abhi — with a view to the oblation of food; pūrvapītaye — to drink, as before (of Soma-juice); ā vahantu — may they bring; somasya — of Soma-juice; pūrvapītaye — to drink earlier [than other deities]; (vahantu — may they bring you; kiṃca — and; he vāyo — O Vāyu; ūrdhvā — excellent; jānatī — knowing [your qualities well]; sūnṛtā — dear and true (praise-) speech of ours; te manaḥ anu — according to your mind; tiṣṭhatu — may it be (gladdening your mind); makhasya — in the sacrifice; dāvane — for the one who is to receive the oblation (to be taken); dāvane — for the giver (of what we desire to us); niyutvatā — accompanied by the horses called niyut; rathena — by chariot; ā yāhi — come.

original p. 568

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, may those horses, which are of swift-moving nature and fast-going (powerful), bring you here, to our sacrifice, to receive the cake and the like and to drink the Soma-juice, as before; may our dear and true words of praise, which know well your qualities, be gladdening to your mind; come in a chariot yoked with the horses called niyut, to receive the oblation in the sacrifice and to give us what we desire.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Let your swift coursers, Vayu, bring you quickly hither, that you may be the first to drink; the first (of the gods) to drink of the Soma libation. May our upraised, discriminating, and sincere (praise) be acceptable to your mind: come with your steed-yoked car for (the libation) to be presented to you; come, Vayu, for granting (the objects of our worship)." [Print: "Let ... car" as above; "Vayu" and "grantiug" (sic) for "granting", "wqrship" (sic) for "worship".]

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).

vāyo —

अथातो मध्यस्थाना देवताः । तासां वायुः प्रथमागामी भवति । वायुः । वायुर्वातेर्वेतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मण एतेरिति स्थौलाष्ठीविः । अनर्थको वकारः ।

athāto madhyasthānā devatāḥ | tāsāṃ vāyuḥ prathamāgāmī bhavati | vāyuḥ | vāyur vāter veter vā syād gatikarmaṇa eter iti sthaulāṣṭhīviḥ | anarthako vakāraḥ |

(Ni. 10-1 [as read].) After describing the forms of Agni, of the earth, and of other deities, the author of the Nirukta, Yāska, discusses and explains in the 10th and 11th chapters the forms of the deities of the middle world (the antarikṣa). Among the deities of the antarikṣa, Vāyu has the first place (vāyuḥ prathamāgāmī bhavati). He says that this word is derived from the root vā, which gives "going" (bīsu: [as read]), or from the root vī "to go, to move about" [and] that the ṇī [as read: i] root, with the sense of motion, may be the origin; and that the letter va has no meaning, according to the opinion of Sthaulāṣṭhīvi. Yāska has cited that opinion. Special Topics continued; the page opens with the end of the sentence about Sthaulāṣṭhīvi's opinion, which Yāska also cites, and then:

original p. 569

And to show that Vāyu is a deity of the antarikṣa, he quotes —

वायवा याहि दर्शतेमे सोमा अरंकृताः । तेषां पाहि श्रुधी हवम् ॥

vāyav ā yāhi darśate me somā araṃkṛtāḥ | teṣāṃ pāhi śrudhī havam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-1 [as read].) — taking this Ṛk, in which a prayer to Vāyu is made to drink the well-prepared Soma — and then:

कमन्यं मध्यमादेवमवक्ष्यत् ।

kam anyaṃ madhyamād devam avakṣyat |

(Ni. 10-[?], as read "೧೦-೩" [?].) — "which other deity but one of the middle world would [the ṛṣi] have so addressed?", he says. In the present Ṛk, by the word vāyo, it is to be understood that the first of the deities of the antarikṣa, Vāyu, is addressed.

tvā juvaḥ ā vahantu — "may the swift-going horses bring [you]": the prayer to bring [you] with horses that move swiftly. The word juvaḥ tells the nature of the horse; derived from the root ju, in the sense of "go", it indicates swiftness of motion.

मुमुक्ष्वो [?] मनवे मानवस्यते रघुद्रुवः कृष्णसीतास ऊ जुवः । असमना अजिरासो रघुष्यदो वातजूता उप युज्यन्त आशवः ॥

mumukṣvo [?] manave mānavasyate raghudruvaḥ kṛṣṇasītāsa ū juvaḥ | asamanā ajirāso raghuṣyado vātajūtā upa yujyanta āśavaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೯೪-೪" [?].) In this Ṛk the word juvaḥ is used as an adjective of the flames of Agni, and shows the swiftness of the flames in their work of carrying [the oblation]. In combination with the word manas it means swiftness of thought.

वाचस्पतिं विश्वकर्माणमूतये मनोजुवं वाजे अद्या हुवेम । स नो विश्वानि हवनानि जोषद्विश्वशंभूरवसे साधुकर्मा ॥

vācaspatiṃ viśvakarmāṇam ūtaye manojuvaṃ vāje adyā huvema | sa no viśvāni havanāni joṣad viśvaśaṃbhūr avase sādhukarmā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೮೧-೭" [?].) In this Ṛk, the word manojuvam is a compound with manas: manaso vegena samāna-vegavantaṃ devam — "a god with speed equal to that of the mind"; everywhere the swiftness of motion is shown. So also in the Ṛk under discussion it shows the speed of the horses.

rarāhāṇāḥ — from the root rahi, in the sense of "go": raṃhatā gacchantaḥ — "going swiftly, [horses] quick to run" is an attribute of the horses; but as the nature of the horses, "running swiftly", has already been told by the epithet juvaḥ, a doubt arises that this attribute is unnecessary; hence Sāyaṇa — the sentence continues on p. 570.

original p. 570

Special Topics continued. …In this word (rarāhāṇāḥ) the commentator has given two kinds of meaning: śīghragāmino balavanto vā aśvāḥ — "swift-going or strong horses"; both meanings, śīghragāmin and balavat, are possible, he has indicated. In the present Ṛk the second meaning is the more appropriate.

prayaḥ — andhaḥ, vājaḥ and so on, in the names of food (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೯" [?]).

pūrvapītaye — this word has been repeated. The first time, pūrvavat pānāya — "to drink as in the former sacrifices"; the second time, itaradevebhyaḥ purā pānāya — "to drink before the other gods": thus the meaning is given.

ūrdhvā — ūrdhva ucchrito bhavati (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೧೫" [?]) means "high, raised up". Ordinarily we use this word to show physical height; but here, as an adjective of praise, it means "excellent".

sūnṛtā — priyasatyātmikā stutirūpāsmadīyā vāk — "our praise, both pleasant and true", Sāyaṇa explains. In explaining this same Ṛk, the meaning which Max Müller gives to this word is worthy of notice:

"Whatever the etymology of sūnṛtā may be, in our passage, which describes the morning sacrifice and the arrival of Vayu as the first of the Gods, it can hardly mean anything but dawn. ūrdhvā-sthā is an expression applied frequently to the rise of the Dawn or the morning, see iii. 55-14; i.ii. 61.-3 [sic]; viii. 45-12. In the last passage it is simply the Dawn." [Vedic Hymns, ii. p. 446.]

However the word sūnṛtā is derived, the Ṛk describes the morning pressing and also addresses Vāyu, who comes first among the deities, and so it suggests that sūnṛtā has the meaning uṣas (dawn). And the activity-words, tiṣṭhasi, tasthuḥ and so on, derived from the root sthā, in connexion with the word ūrdhva, indicate the Uṣas rising in the morning —

उषः प्रतीची भुवनानि विश्वोर्ध्वा तिष्ठस्यमृतस्य केतुः । समानमर्थं चरणीयमाना चक्रमिव नव्यस्या ववृत्स्व ॥

uṣaḥ pratīcī bhuvanāni viśvordhvā tiṣṭhasy amṛtasya ketuḥ | samānam artham caraṇīyamānā cakram iva navyasyā vavṛtsva ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-3 [as read].) — as in such Ṛks, in the present Ṛk too, the phrase ūrdhvā tiṣṭhatu indicates Uṣas. Therefore, the word sūnṛtā is a synonym for uṣas — thus [Max Müller's idea] [text continues on p. 571].

original p. 571

Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued from p. 570: …"Dawn", Max Müller's idea, which is the gist of his view, is acceptable from one point of view; but the illustration he gives, viii. 45-12, does not suit the present context as appropriately [as one might wish]. According to Sāyaṇa's explanation, the meaning is: "may our praise, which is excellent, which knows your qualities, true and pleasant, be satisfying to your mind"; and according to Max Müller's explanation: "te manaḥ jānatī sūnṛtā ūrdhvā anutiṣṭhatu — may Uṣas, knowing your nature, rise up and wait upon you". The reader may adopt whichever of the two meanings suits the context.

niyutvatā — niyuto vāyoḥ (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೨೫" [?]): niyut is the name of the horses, Vāyu's vehicle. The author of the Nirukta, taking the Ṛk —

प्र वाव्यज्जे सुप्रया बर्हिरेषामा विश्पतीव बीरिट इयाते । विशामक्तोरुषसः पूर्वहूतौ वायुः पूषा स्वस्तये नियुत्वान् ॥

pra vāvyajje suprayā barhir eṣām ā viśpatīva bīriṭa iyāte | viśām aktor uṣasaḥ pūrvahūtau vāyuḥ pūṣā svastaye niyutvān ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-3 [as read]; the first words are doubtful in several letters [?].) — shows the following derivation of niyutvān there: "niyuto 'syāśvāḥ | niyuto niyamanād vā niyojanād vā" — "it has horses called niyut; niyut from niyamana (restraining) or from niyojana (yoking)": the name niyut is well known as meaning "[horses] restrained or yoked" (Ni. 5-[?], as read "೫-೨೫" [?]). In the same way this meaning is to be taken in the present Ṛk also. Niyutvatā is an adjective of Vāyu's chariot, meaning "joined with the horses niyut".

Although the epithet niyutvān is generally more used of Vāyu, in some places it is also used of Indra and Varuṇa:

वेत्यध्वर्युः पथिभी रजिष्ठैः प्रति हव्यानि वीतये । अधा नियुत्स्व उभयस्य नः पिब शुचिं सोमं गवाशिरम् ॥

vety adhvaryuḥ pathibhī rajiṣṭhaiḥ prati havyāni vītaye | adhā niyutsva ubhayasya naḥ piba śuciṃ somaṃ gavāśiram ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-101-10 [as read, [?]]) — where it is an adjective of Vāyu [sic: "in this Ṛk of Vāyu"], and

आ वां रथो नियुत्वान्वक्षदवसेऽभि प्रयांसि सुधितानि वीतये वायो हव्यानि वीतये ।

ā vāṃ ratho niyutvān vakṣad avase 'bhi prayāṃsi sudhitāni vītaye vāyo havyāni vītaye |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-135-4 [as read].) In such Ṛks, the horses that draw the chariots belonging to both Indra and Vāyu are so described.

original p. 572

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). juvaḥ — ju is a sautra root; used in the sense of motion; kvip; nominative plural. rarāhāṇāḥ — rahi gatau; as liṭ comes, liṭaḥ kānaj vā (Pā. 3-2-106 [as read]) gives kānac for it; since the āgama is non-eternal in nature, the num augment does not occur [?]; or cita (Pā. 6-1-163 [as read]) gives the final udātta. vahantu — vaha prāpaṇe; loṭ, third person plural; since it is at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not occur; as lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the accent of the root remains. pūrvapītaye — pūrvā cāsau pītiś ca pūrvapītiḥ; puṃvat karmadhārayeti (Pā. 6-3-42 [as read]) gives puṃvadbhāva to the earlier member; marudvṛdhādīnāṃ chandasy ubhayasaṃkhyānam (Pā. 6-2-[?]) gives the earlier member the final udātta accent; dative singular. jānatī — jñā avabodhane; śatṛ for laṭ; śnā as vikaraṇa; jñājanor jā (Pā. 7-3-79 [as read]) gives jā to the root; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ (Pā. 6-4-112 [as read]) drops the ā of the vikaraṇa; in the feminine, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6 [as read]) gives ṅīp; since num is absent and ṅīp follows the śatṛ, śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173 [as read]) gives it the udātta accent. dāvane — ḍudāñ dāne; as before, the Uṇādi suffix vani in the sense of object and in the sense of state; its first vowel udātta; dative singular, by Vedic usage the penultimate elision does not occur. ‖ 1 ‖

Rik 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

मन्दन्तु त्वा मन्दिनो वायविन्दवोऽस्मत्क्राणासः सुकृता अभिद्यवो गोभिः क्राणा अभिद्यवः । यद्ध क्राणा इरध्यै दक्षं सचन्त ऊतयः । सध्रीचीना नियुतो दावने धिय उप ब्रुवत ईं धियः ॥ २ ॥

mandantu tvā mandino vāyavindavo 'smatkrāṇāsaḥ sukṛtā abhidyavo gobhiḥ krāṇā abhidyavaḥ | yaddha krāṇā iradhyai dakṣaṃ sacanta ūtayaḥ | sadhrīcīnā niyuto dāvane dhiya upa bruvata īṃ dhiyaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 573

॥ पदपाठः ॥

मन्दन्तु । त्वा । मन्दिनः । वायो इति । इन्दवः । अस्मत् । क्राणासः । सुऽकृताः । अभिऽद्यवः । गोभिः । क्राणाः । अभिऽद्यवः । यत् । ह । क्राणाः । इरध्यै । दक्षम् । सचन्ते । ऊतयः । सध्रीचीनाः । नियुतः । दावने । धियः । उप । ब्रुवते । ईम् । धियः ॥ २ ॥

mandantu | tvā | mandinaḥ | vāyo iti | indavaḥ | asmat | krāṇāsaḥ | su 'kṛtāḥ | abhi 'dyavaḥ | gobhiḥ | krāṇāḥ | abhi 'dyavaḥ | yat | ha | krāṇāḥ | iradhyai | dakṣam | sacante | ūtayaḥ | sadhrīcīnāḥ | niyutaḥ | dāvane | dhiyaḥ | upa | bruvate | īm | dhiyaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ read from the image; the small type is partly doubtful [?]. Sense: "O Vāyu, may the indus — the moisteners, the Soma-juices — of ours rejoice you (the Parasmaipada by vyatyaya). What kind of Soma-juices? Mandinaḥ — gladdeners; krāṇāsaḥ — performing their own function of joy and so on; sukṛtāḥ — well made by the pressing, the filtering through the strainer, the taking up of the cups and so on; abhidyavaḥ — shining all around; gobhiḥ krāṇāḥ — being made (poured) with gobhiḥ, i.e. speech in the form of mantras; or by those that bring [the milk] to the āhavanīya fire, being offered. [krāṇa from kṛ with śānac; the kap is elided by Vedic usage.] Further, abhidyavaḥ — going towards [you]. O Vāyu, since your niyut horses — spirited to go to our sacrificial place, capable (dakṣa) of conveying — sacante, attend you, to bring you to the offering-place [for the taking of the oblation, dāvane], with a view to the rites (dhiyaḥ); for what purpose? iradhyai — to bring, or to serve (ira gatau, with the kadhyai suffix for the infinitive); [iradhyati is a verb of service, as in the Nighaṇṭu]. What kind of horses? krāṇāḥ — carrying out their own task, the drawing of the chariot [Yāska: krāṇāḥ kurvāṇāḥ — Ni. 4-9 [?]]; ūtayaḥ — protecting, or loving; sadhrīcīnāḥ — going along with you [saha → sadhri by vibhāṣāñceḥ in the sense of kha]. And further, dhiyaḥ — priests or sacrificers, possessed of rites or of intellect, upa bruvate — come near and speak, make their desire known." Doubtful here: the grammatical details of kadhyai, sadhrīcīna.

हे वायो त्वा त्वामस्मदस्माकं संबन्धिन इन्दवः क्लेदयितारः सोमा मन्दन्तु । मादयन्तु ॥ व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदम् ॥ कीदृशाः सोमाः । मन्दिनो मादयितारः क्राणासः कुर्वाणाः स्वकार्यं हर्षादिकम् । सुकृता अभिषवदशापवित्रशोधनग्रहणादिभिः सुष्ठु कृताः । अभिद्यवोऽभितो द्योतयन्तः । गोभिर्वाग्निर्मन्त्ररूपाभिः क्राणाः क्रियमाणा हूयमानाः । यद्वा । गोभिर्गव्यैर्विराहवनीयं प्रत्याऽऽनेतृभिः क्राणा हूयमानाः ॥ करोतेः शानच् । छान्दसः कपो लुक् ॥ तथाभिद्यवोऽभिगन्तारः । हे वायो यद्यस्मात्कारणात् । हश्च [?] प्रसिद्धः । दक्षमस्माद्यागदेशं प्रति गन्तुमुत्साहवन्तं समर्थयितारमिमां त्वां नियुत एतत्संज्ञकास्त्वाश्वाः दावने दानाय हविःस्वीकारनिमित्तं धियः कर्माण्युद्दिश्य सचन्ते त्वां संगच्छन्ते यागदेशं वा । किमर्थम् । इरध्यै प्रापयितुं परिचरितुं वा । ईर गतौ । तुमर्थे कध्यैप्रत्ययः । ह्रस्वश्छान्दसः ॥ इरध्यति परिचरणकर्मा इरध्यति विधेमेति तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् ॥ कीदृशास्ताः । क्राणाः स्वव्यापारं रथवाहनादिकं कुर्वाणाः । क्राणाः कुर्वाणा इति यास्कः । नि. ४-९ [?] । ऊतयो रक्षणवत्यः प्रीतियुक्ता वा । तथा सध्रीचीनास्त्वया सहाञ्चन्तो गच्छन्त्यः । सहस्य सध्रिर्विभाषाञ्चेरिति स्वार्थे खः । व्यत्ययेनांतोदात्तः ॥ किंच धियः कर्मवन्तो बुद्धिमन्तो वा ऋत्विजो यजमाना वोप ब्रुवते । उपेत्य ब्रुवन्ति स्वाभिमतं विज्ञापयन्ति वा ॥

he vāyo tvā tvāmasmadasmākaṃ saṃbandhina indavaḥ kledayitāraḥ somā mandantu | mādayantu ‖ vyatyayena parasmaipadam ‖ kīdṛśāḥ somāḥ | mandino mādayitāraḥ krāṇāsaḥ kurvāṇāḥ svakāryaṃ harṣādikam | sukṛtā abhiṣavadaśāpavitraśodhanagrahaṇādibhiḥ suṣṭhu kṛtāḥ | abhidyavo 'bhito dyotayantaḥ | gobhirvāgnirmantrarūpābhiḥ krāṇāḥ kriyamāṇā hūyamānāḥ | yadvā | gobhirgavyairvirāhavanīyaṃ pratyā ' 'netṛbhiḥ krāṇā hūyamānāḥ ‖ karoteḥ śānac | chāndasaḥ kapo luk ‖ tathābhidyavo 'bhigantāraḥ | he vāyo yadyasmātkāraṇāt | haśca [?] prasiddhaḥ | dakṣamasmādyāgadeśaṃ prati gantumutsāhavantaṃ samarthayitāramimāṃ tvāṃ niyuta etatsaṃjñakāstvāśvāḥ dāvane dānāya haviḥsvīkāranimittaṃ dhiyaḥ karmāṇyuddiśya sacante tvāṃ saṃgacchante yāgadeśaṃ vā | kimartham | iradhyai prāpayituṃ paricarituṃ vā | īra gatau | tumarthe kadhyaipratyayaḥ | hrasvaśchāndasaḥ ‖ iradhyati paricaraṇakarmā iradhyati vidhemeti tannāmasūktatvāt ‖ kīdṛśāstāḥ | krāṇāḥ svavyāpāraṃ rathavāhanādikaṃ kurvāṇāḥ | krāṇāḥ kurvāṇā iti yāskaḥ | ni. 4-9 [?] | ūtayo rakṣaṇavatyaḥ prītiyuktā vā | tathā sadhrīcīnāstvayā sahāñcanto gacchantyaḥ | sahasya sadhrirvibhāṣāñceriti svārthe khaḥ | vyatyayenāṃtodāttaḥ ‖ kiṃca dhiyaḥ karmavanto buddhimanto vā ṛtvijo yajamānā vopa bruvate | upetya bruvanti svābhimataṃ vijñāpayanti vā ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he) vāyo — O Vāyu; yat — for which reason; dakṣam — (to our sacrificial place, to come) of a spirited one; īm — you; krāṇāḥ — (the doers of the work of drawing the chariot); ūtayaḥ — those that give protection (affectionate); sadhrīcīnāḥ — (those) going with you; niyutaḥ — the niyut (your horses); dāvane — to take the (oblation, etc.) gift; dhiyaḥ — (for the sake of the various) rites; iradhyai — to bring you (to serve you); sacante — join [you] (go with you to the sacrificial place); (kiṃca — and; dhiyaḥ — the ṛtvijs who are intellectual (the wise); upa bruvate — approaching you, speak (their own desires); tat — for that reason; — O Vāyu; tvā — you; asmat — our; mandinaḥ — gladdeners; krāṇāsaḥ — doers (of their own function of joy and so on); sukṛtāḥ — made well; abhidyavaḥ — shining; gobhiḥ — by words (in mantra-form); krāṇāḥ — called (made, poured) (and pure); abhidyavaḥ — (at all times) entering [the vessels]; indavaḥ — Soma-juices with the power of wetting; mandantu — let them gladden. Pratipadārtha: the page is a continuation of the same; the printed order of the items on pp. 573–574 is slightly different from the above, which gives the glosses in the order in which they occur in the Ṛk, with the parenthetical glosses as printed: e.g. "iradhyai — to serve (to attend on) you", "sacante — join you (to go with you to the sacrificial place)", "dhiyaḥ — the wise priests", "upa bruvate — approach you and tell their desires".

original p. 574

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, your beloved horses, the niyuts, who are capable of doing the work of drawing the chariot and fit to go with you, join you [to bring you] to the sacrificial place to receive the offerings given (the oblations and so on) and to take part in the various works of the sacrifice, and the wise priests approach and tell [you] their desires. May the Soma-juices, which gladden you, which do their work of rejoicing, which are well prepared, shining, pure, which are called with words (in the form of mantras), and which enter at all times the various vessels — may they gladden you.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "May the exhilarating drops (of the libation) exhilarate you, Vayu, being fitly prepared, doing their office, administered opportunely, rendered efficacious by (our) praises, and flowing (in due season): for which purpose, your docile and active steeds, the Niyuts, attending (your presence, and bring you to the sacrificial hall to accept the offering; to the sacrifice in which the pious (priests) represent their desires." [Print: "Vayu" without diacritics; the parenthesis "(your presence" is not closed in the print [sic]; "ritual" etc. as given.]

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).

vāyo tvā indavaḥ mandantu — "O Vāyu, may the Soma-juices pressed by us gladden you" — thus the prayer. The words mandinaḥ, krāṇāsaḥ and the like are attributes of the word indavaḥ [text continues on p. 575].

original p. 575

indavaḥ — undanaśīlāḥ sarvaṃ jagad amṛtamayena kledayitāraḥ — "that which wets the whole world with a nectar-like essence": that is, "Soma-juices that satisfy all, the gods and the rest, with an essence of the nature of nectar".

mandinaḥ — mādayitāraḥ: this shows the nature of Soma-juices that cause joy. The meaning has to be given in agreement with this attribute.

Mandī mandateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 4-[?], as read "೪-೩೮" [?]) — derived from the root mand, which has the meaning "to praise", it shows the sense "worthy of praise, and of worship". The Nirukta-author takes the Ṛk —

प्र मन्दिने पितुमदर्चता वचो यः कृष्णगर्भा निरहन्नृजिश्वना । अवस्यवो वृषणं वज्रदक्षिणं मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥

pra mandine pitumad arcatā vaco yaḥ kṛṣṇagarbhā nirahann ṛjiśvanā | avasyavo vṛṣaṇaṃ vajradakṣiṇaṃ marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-1 [as read].) — and gives the meaning of the word mandine [as above]. Durgācārya explains: mandine mandanīyāya stutyāya stutimate vā indrāya.

Matsaraḥ somo mandateḥ tṛptikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೫" [?]) — "matsara from the root mand, meaning to satisfy"; the use of the word matsara is explained at the same time. Because the root mand has both these meanings, the author of the Nirukta, in the Ṛk —

प्र वो महे मन्दमानायान्धसोऽर्चा विश्वानराय विश्वाभुवे । इन्द्रस्य यस्य सुमखं सहो महि श्रवो नृम्णं च रोदसी सपर्यतः ॥

pra vo mahe mandamānāyāndhaso 'rcā viśvānarāya viśvābhuve | indrasya yasya sumakhaṃ saho mahi śravo nṛmṇaṃ ca rodasī saparyataḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-1, as read "೧೦-೩೦-೧" [?].) — explains the word mandamānāya by synonyms: modamānāya, stūyamānāya, śabdāya mānāyeti vā — "the one who is delighted, or the one who is praised, or the one who is prayed to" (Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೧"). Besides this, in the explanation of these meanings he has included, among the names of "shining" (Ni. 2-[?]) and of "worship" [as read: arcati karma] (Ni. 3-[?]), the word mandate, which is also derived from the root mand. In the present Ṛk it means: "Soma-juices that gladden".

krāṇāsaḥ, krāṇāḥ — the word is used three times in this Ṛk. Yāska explains: "krāṇāḥ kurvāṇāḥ" (Ni. 4-[?], as read "೪-೧೯" [?]).

krāṇāsaḥ svakāryaṃ harṣādikaṃ kurvāṇāḥ — "those that produce satisfaction": this is an attribute of indavaḥ.

original p. 576

krāṇāḥ (the second) — gobhiḥ mantrarūpābhir vāgbhiḥ kriyamāṇāḥ hūyamānāḥ — "being prayed for by the Ṛks in the form of mantras": here too it is shown to be an attribute of indavaḥ.

krāṇāḥ (the third) — svavyāpāraṃ rathavāhanādikaṃ kurvāṇāḥ — "doing their own tasks, such as drawing the chariot": this is an attribute of the horses.

sadhrīcīnāḥ — tvayā sahāñcantaḥ yugapad gacchantaḥ — "going together at the same time": the inseparable connexion of the horses called niyut with Vāyu, and the unbroken companionship of the others, is well shown by this word. In the same way, the connexion between Indra and the Maruts, between the Aśvins, and between day and night is shown to be fixed companionship, by this word:

पदे इव निहिते दस्मे अन्तस्तयोरन्यद्गुह्यमाविरन्यत् । सध्रीचीना पथ्या सा विषूची महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥

pade iva nihite dasme antas tayor anyad guhyam āvir anyat | sadhrīcīnā pathyā sā viṣūcī mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?], as read "೩-೩೯-೩" [?].) Here, by the words sadhrīcīnā pathyā the "day and night" are said to be the path in the form of time which unites together. This is one kind of companionship.

उभा उ नूनं तदिदर्थयेथे वि तन्वाथे धियो वस्त्रापसेव । सध्रीचीना यातवे प्रेमजीगः सुदिनेव पृक्ष आ तंसयेथे ॥

ubhā u nūnaṃ tad idarthayethe vi tanvāthe dhiyo vastrāpaseva | sadhrīcīnā yātave prem ajīgaḥ sudineva pṛkṣa ā taṃsayethe ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-106-1 [as read].) Here the mutual relation of the Aśvins, and their going always together, is indicated.

कृणोत्स्मै वरिवो य इत्थेन्द्राय सोममुषते सुनोति । सध्रीचीनेन मनसाविवेनन्तमित्सखायं कृणुते समत्सु ॥

kṛṇotsmai varivo ya itthendrāya somam uṣate sunoti | sadhrīcīnena manasāvivenantam it sakhāyaṃ kṛṇute samatsu ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-24-6 [as read].) In this, sadhrīcīnena manasā ("with a united mind") indicates the devotion of the sacrificer: the relationship of the gods who are worshipped, with the sacrificer, that does not separate from him, from the mind fixed on Indra, loving him without interruption, without being attached to others.

iradhyai — prāpayituṃ paricarituṃ vā — derived from the root īr "to go", it shows the purpose: "to bring you [Vāyu], or to wait on you" is the meaning [text continues on p. 577].

original p. 577

Continuing: …Iradhyati, vidhema are given in the Nirukta as iradhyatiḥ paricaraṇakarmā ("iradhyati is a verb of service") — and, citing that authority, Sāyaṇa explains that the word iradhyai means service (paricaraṇa), the purport being "to serve". [In the Nirukta there is a different reading, irajyati vidhema.] Discussing the root of this word, the scholar Monier Williams, in his Dictionary, says:

"The inf ಇರಧ್ಯೈ [iradhyai] (R. VI. 134-2) is by B. R. D. (Bohtlingk & Roths, Dictionary) referred to this form, and regarded as a shortened form for ಇರಧ್ಯೈ [sic; the printed second form is different in the Kannada print and is not legible [?]]; but Sayana refer to ईर्" [i.e. īr].

That is: the opinion of that scholar is that it is from the root rādh-saṃsiddhau, whence iradhyai means "to worship" (ārādhnoti = arcati). For that he has given the support of another lexicon. Sāyaṇa explains it as derived from the root īr.

abhidyavaḥ — this word is used twice. First: sukṛtā abhidyavaḥ — "because they are purified, shining all round" — as an adjective of the word indavaḥ. Second: gobhiḥ krāṇā abhidyavaḥ — "because they are purified by mantras, they shine all round, and are powerful" — it means the Soma-juices.

Abhidyavaḥ is a technical word. It indicates either the sacrificial times, or the times connected with the Soma-juices.

प्र वो वाजा अभिद्यवो हविष्मन्तो घृताच्या । देवाञ्जिगाति सुम्नयुः ॥

pra vo vājā abhidyavo haviṣmanto ghṛtācyā | devāñ jigāti sumnayuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-27-1 [as read].) In this, he explains "abhito dyavo divasā yeṣv ity abhidyavo 'rdhamāsāś ca" and by abhidyavaḥ explains "half-months": [and]

प्र वो वाजा इत्याह मासा वै वाजा अर्धमासा अभिद्यवः ।

pra vo vājā ity āha māsā vai vājā ardhamāsā abhidyavaḥ |

(Taittirīya Saṃhitā 3-3-2-4 [as read].) — in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā "vāja" is said to be "months" and abhidyavaḥ "half-months"; the previous Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-27-1 is taken and explained. But,

विद्मा हि त्वा अभिद्यवः शिप्राः शीर्षन् हिरण्ययीः । शुभ्रा वि अञ्जत श्रिये ॥

vidmā hi tvā abhidyavaḥ śiprāḥ śīrṣan hiraṇyayīḥ | śubhrā vy añjata śriye ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2-[?], as read "೮-೨-೨೩" [?]; the first words of the quotation are doubtful [?].) In many such Ṛks, the word is meant as abhigatadīptayaḥ, "shining all around"; so in the present Ṛk too it means "shining Soma-juices".

original p. 578

gobhiḥ — mantrarūpābhir vāgbhiḥ — "by words of mantra-form". Ilā, gauḥ (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೧" [?]) and so on are among the names of vāc; the word go has other meanings besides, such as pṛthivī (earth), which were explained in other contexts. Or [it is explained as] gobhiḥ krāṇāḥ; gobhir gavyais tair āhavanīyaṃ pratyānetṛbhiḥ hūyamānāḥ — "being poured by those who bring them, the cow-products, to the āhavanīya fire": thus another meaning also is said for the present Ṛk, "the Soma-juices (indavaḥ)".

dhiyaḥ — karmavanto buddhimanto vā ṛtvijo yajamānā vā — "the priests or sacrificers, possessed of rites or of intelligence": the many meanings of the word dhī were explained before.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). mandantu — root madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 [as read]) gives Parasmaipada; idito num dhātoḥ gives the num augment; loṭ third person plural; as it is at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not occur; since the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta by tāsyanudāttenṅidvidupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam (Pā. 6-1-186 [as read]), the root's accent remains. mandinaḥ — [with the root] mentioned above, the suffix ini in the sense of tācchīlya [habit]; the first vowel of the suffix gets the udātta. indavaḥ — root undī kledane; undeḥ ic cādeḥ (Uṇ. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೩" [?]) gives the suffix un; i for the first [vowel]; nominative plural. krāṇāsaḥ — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; śānac for laṭ; bahulaṃ chandasi gives luk of the vikaraṇa; yaṇ substitution; āṅ-kuṭ- [?] (Pā. 8-4-[?]) gives ṇatva of the n; cita (Pā. 6-1-163 [as read]) gives the final udātta; since jas follows, ājjaser asuk gives the asuk augment. sukṛtāḥ — gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 [as read]) gives the gati (su) the nighāta [sic: prakṛti-svara]. iradhyai — īra gatau; when it takes the sense of the infinitive (tumarthe), tumarthe sesenasenasen… (Pā. 3-4-9 [as read]) gives the kadhyai suffix; the root has the short vowel by Vedic usage; since the suffix has the k-marker, the laghūpadha guṇa of the root does not occur; the suffix's first vowel is udātta.

original p. 579

Grammar of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 578. sacante — root ṣaca samavāye; laṭ, third person plural; as the verb is connected with yat, the nighāta accent does not occur; as the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the root's accent remains. sadhrīcīnāḥ — root añcu gatipūjanayoḥ; saha añcati — when the compound is formed, ṛtvik-dadhṛk-… (Pā. 3-2-59 [as read]) gives the suffix kvin; sahasya sadhriḥ (Pā. 6-3-95 [as read]) gives sadhri as a substitute for the preceding word; vibhāṣāñceś… (Pā. 5-4-8 [as read]) gives the suffix kha in its own sense; āyaneyīnīya… (Pā. 7-1-2 [as read]) gives īna for kha; by vyatyaya the final udātta. bruvate — root brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; adādi; laṭ, third person plural; the suffix jha → ran; ṭi's e; śap luk; ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ (Pā. 7-1-5 [as read]) gives at for the suffix; brūva īṭ [as read] — āhaś ca thāsor bhūvām … gives uvaṅ [bruva]; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. ‖ 2 ‖

Rik 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

वायुर्युङ्क्ते रोहिता वायुररुणा वायू रथे अजिरा धुरि वोळ्हवे वहिष्ठा धुरि वोळ्हवे । प्र बोधया पुरन्धिं जार आ ससतीमिव । प्र चक्षय रोदसी वासयोषसः श्रवसे वासयोषसः ॥ ३ ॥

vāyuryuṅkte rohitā vāyuraruṇā vāyū rathe ajirā dhuri voḷhave vahiṣṭhā dhuri voḷhave | pra bodhayā purandhiṃ jāra ā sasatīmiva | pra cakṣaya rodasī vāsayoṣasaḥ śravase vāsayoṣasaḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

वायुः । युङ्क्ते । रोहिता । वायुः । अरुणा । वायुः । रथे । अजिरा । धुरि । वोळ्हवे । वहिष्ठा । धुरि । वोळ्हवे । प्र । बोधय । पुरम्ऽधिम् । जारः । आ । ससतीम्ऽइव । प्र । चक्षय । रोदसी इति । वासय । उषसः । श्रवसे । वासय । उषसः ॥ ३ ॥

vāyuḥ | yuṅkte | rohitā | vāyuḥ | aruṇā | vāyuḥ | rathe | ajirā | dhuri | voḷhave | vahiṣṭhā | dhuri | voḷhave | pra | bodhaya | puram 'dhim | jāraḥ | ā | sasatīm 'iva | pra | cakṣaya | rodasī iti | vāsaya | uṣasaḥ | śravase | vāsaya | uṣasaḥ ‖ 3 ‖

original p. 580

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 3; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "This Vāyu yokes the two red (rohitā) horses in front of the chariot, at the pole, or for bearing the burden; at times he yokes two ruddy-red (aruṇā), and at times the two ajirā, moving ones, of a particular colour. Or: this is connected in both [places]. For what purpose does he yoke? — voḍhave, to bear the burden of the yoke; and further vahiṣṭhā, the two horses that bear the burden most. [The suffix iṣṭhan after vodhṛ, with elision of tṛ; the plural/dual ending ā.] When there is a great burden to bear. The repeated mention of Vāyu and of yoking is to show that he comes very quickly. Now he speaks directly: O Vāyu, purandhi — [she/he] of much intelligence, [here] by implication the sacrificer — purandhir bahudhīḥ says Yāska (Ni. 6-[?], [?]) — awaken him; come swiftly by chariot and make him aware, for the acceptance of the oblation. The illustration: as a jāra — a paramour — coming to a sleeping (sasatī) woman, a purandhi, one with a fair body, awakens her by his own signal, so you also awaken the sacrificer, who is absorbed in the rite. And for that, rodasī — heaven and earth — pra cakṣaya, make known, illuminate; and for the light, make the dawns shine (vāsaya), make it dawn; and again the same prayer: for śravas [food], that you may take the oblation-food, make the dawns shine."

अयं वायू रोहिता रोहितवर्णावश्वौ धुरि धारणप्रदेशे रथस्याग्रभागे यद्वा भारवहने युङ्क्ते । [?] नियोजयति । तथा कदाचिदरुणारुणवर्णौ धुरि युङ्क्ते । तथाजिराजिरौ गमनशीलौ वर्णविशेषयुक्तौ कदाचिद्युङ्क्ते । यद्वा । एतदुभयत्र संबध्यते । किमर्थम् । युङ्क्ते इति तदाह । वोळ्हवे धुरं वोढुं भारवहनाय । किंच वहिष्ठा वहिष्ठावतिशयेन वोढारावश्वौ ॥ वोढृशब्दादिष्ठनि तुरिष्ठमेयःसु [?] इति तृलोपः । टिकारादिकमसिद्धत्वान्नि वर्तते । द्विवचनस्याकारः ॥ धुरि वोळ्हवे महद्भारं वोढुं महति भारे वोढव्ये सति । पुनःपुनर्वायुग्रहणमश्वयोजनवचनं चातिशीघ्रमागच्छतीति ज्ञापनार्थम् । इदानीं प्रत्यक्षेणाह । हे वायो पुरन्धिं बहुप्रज्ञां सामर्थ्याद्यजमानमिति गम्यते । पुरंधिर्बहुधीरिति यास्कः । नि. ६-१३ [?] । तं प्र बोधय । रथेन शीघ्रमागत्य प्रज्ञापय हविःस्वीकारायेति भावः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । जारः पारदारिक आ ससतीमुपेत्यागमनध्यानेन [?] स्वपन्तीं पुरन्धिमिव प्रकृष्टशरीरधारिणीं योषितामिव । तां यथा स्वसंकेतेन स प्रबोधयति तद्वत्त्वमपि कर्मव्यग्रं [?] यजमानं प्रबोधय । किंच तदर्थं रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ प्र चक्षय । प्रकर्षेण प्रख्यापय । प्रकाशयेत्यर्थः । तत्र प्रकाशार्थमुषसो वासय । उषःकालानसि [?] यथावस्थापय । प्रभातं कुर्वित्यर्थः । पुनस्तदेव प्रार्थ्यते । श्रवसे श्रव इत्यन्ननाम । तव हविरूपान्नस्वीकारायोषसो वासय ॥

ayaṃ vāyū rohitā rohitavarṇāvaśvau dhuri dhāraṇapradeśe rathasyāgrabhāge yadvā bhāravahane yuṅkte | [?] niyojayati | tathā kadācidaruṇāruṇavarṇau dhuri yuṅkte | tathājirājirau gamanaśīlau varṇaviśeṣayuktau kadācidyuṅkte | yadvā | etadubhayatra saṃbadhyate | kimartham | yuṅkte iti tadāha | voḷhave dhuraṃ voḍhuṃ bhāravahanāya | kiṃca vahiṣṭhā vahiṣṭhāvatiśayena voḍhārāvaśvau ‖ voḍhṛśabdādiṣṭhani turiṣṭhameyaḥsu [?] iti tṛlopaḥ | ṭikārādikamasiddhatvānni vartate | dvivacanasyākāraḥ ‖ dhuri voḷhave mahadbhāraṃ voḍhuṃ mahati bhāre voḍhavye sati | punaḥpunarvāyugrahaṇamaśvayojanavacanaṃ cātiśīghramāgacchatīti jñāpanārtham | idānīṃ pratyakṣeṇāha | he vāyo purandhiṃ bahuprajñāṃ sāmarthyādyajamānamiti gamyate | puraṃdhirbahudhīriti yāskaḥ | ni. 6-13 [?] | taṃ pra bodhaya | rathena śīghramāgatya prajñāpaya haviḥsvīkārāyeti bhāvaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | jāraḥ pāradārika ā sasatīmupetyāgamanadhyānena [?] svapantīṃ purandhimiva prakṛṣṭaśarīradhāriṇīṃ yoṣitāmiva | tāṃ yathā svasaṃketena sa prabodhayati tadvattvamapi karmavyagraṃ [?] yajamānaṃ prabodhaya | kiṃca tadarthaṃ rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyau pra cakṣaya | prakarṣeṇa prakhyāpaya | prakāśayetyarthaḥ | tatra prakāśārthamuṣaso vāsaya | uṣaḥkālānasi [?] yathāvasthāpaya | prabhātaṃ kurvityarthaḥ | punastadeva prārthyate | śravase śrava ityannanāma | tava havirūpānnasvīkārāyoṣaso vāsaya ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. vāyuḥ — Vāyu; rohitā — two red horses; rathe — to the front part of the chariot; dhuri — to the yoke (to bear the burden); yuṅkte — yokes; kadācit — at one time; vāyuḥ — Vāyu; aruṇā — the two of ruddy colour (horses); yuṅkte — yokes; tathā — likewise; ajirā — the swift horses; voḍhave — in order to bear; — yokes; vāyuḥ — Vāyu; vahiṣṭhā — horses that are able to bear the load; dhuri voḍhave — to bear a heavy load; — yokes; (he) vāyo — O Vāyu; jāraḥ — a paramour; ā sasatīm — (awaiting the coming of a lover) one who is sleeping lightly; purandhim iva — like a woman of fair body; [ā sasatīm — owing to carelessness, deeply asleep]; purandhim — the sacrificer of much intelligence; pra bodhaya — awaken (and for that purpose).

original p. 581

Pratipadārtha concluded: rodasī — heaven and earth; pra cakṣaya — illuminate well; uṣasaḥ — the dawns; vāsaya — cause to shine (dwell); śravase — for the acceptance of the offered food; uṣasaḥ — the dawns; vāsaya — make manifest.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. Vāyu yokes his two red horses to the chariot; at times he yokes the two ruddy ones; and [at others] the swift ones, the load-bearing horses. O Vāyu, as a paramour awakens the sleeping beloved who awaits him, so awaken the wise sacrificer (him) with vigilance; light up heaven and earth; and make the dawns shine in order that you may receive the offered food.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Vayu yokes to his car his two red horses; Vayu (yokes) his purple steeds: Vayu (yokes) his two unwearied (coursers) to his car to bear their burthen; for most able are they to bear the burthen. Arouse, Vayu, the intelligent (sacrificer), as a gallant (awakens) his sleeping mistress: summon heaven and earth; light up the dawn; light up the dawn, (to receive) your sacrificial food."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).

vāyuḥ rohitā dhuri yuṅkte; aruṇā yuṅkte; ajirā yuṅkte — by sentences like these, the horses yoked to the chariot of Vāyu are described. Rohito 'gneḥ; aruṇo gāvā uṣasām [as read] — the vehicle of Agni is called rohita, the vehicles of Uṣas are called aruṇyaḥ (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೨೫" [?]): the doubt "how are these yoked to Vāyu's chariot?" arises here. But if we understand the connexion between Vāyu and Agni, and between Vāyu and Uṣas, there is no room for this doubt.

In the first Ṛk of this very Sūkta, while explaining the meaning of the word sūnṛtā, it was noted that there is one view saying that it is a synonym of uṣas. And as the word pūrvapītaye means "to drink before the other gods", and as in the Ṛk itself Uṣas is prayed to be made to shine, Vāyu has a close connexion with the deity Uṣas, and, as he appears earlier with her, this shows the similarity between the colour of the vehicle of Uṣas and the colour of the vehicle of Vāyu.

original p. 582

In the same way, at the beginning of all acts of sacrifice in the world, Agni's oblations are performed straight after the rise of Vāyu; hence at dawn, in the form of the sun, it can be said that the colour of Agni's vehicle also is equal to the colour of Vāyu's horses; [and] at the time of Vāyu's coming, it can be said that all these colours were in his horses.

ajirā — the word ajira is among the names of kṣipra ("swift") (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೯" [?]); it shows "that which moves quickly". Ordinarily this word is used as an adjective of the swift enemy, of swift horses, and of the deities that go swiftly to the sacrifice. By this adjective the going-power of Vāyu's horses is indicated. With it,

voḍhave — by this word the power of the horses to bear a burden is indicated. Thus, by the many kinds of epithets — coloured with various colours, running fast, and capable of bearing the burden — the beauty and the strength of the horses are clearly known. By the word vahiṣṭhā the extreme power is shown.

dhuri — this word is repeated. The first time, it means the place at the front of the chariot, where the yoke is fastened; the second, a heavier burden.

purandhim pra bodhaya — "awaken purandhi" is the meaning; as to purandhi [asking] "who is it, why did this name come?", [the commentator] explains with the derivation of this word. Purandhiṃ bahuprajñaṃ sāmarthyād yajamānam iti gamyate | purandhir bahudhīr iti yāskaḥ — Yāska explains this as "[one] having much intelligence" and gives the meaning of this word, "such a wise sacrificer", in the first place (anvaya), and then gives the meaning of the word as one of comparison (upamā). According to these two constructions: purandhim (iva) prakṛṣṭaśarīradhāriṇīṃ yoṣitam iva; tāṃ yathā svasaṃketena jāraḥ prabodhayati tadvat tvam api yajamānaṃ prabodhaya — "as a lover awakens, by his signal, a woman with a well-formed body, so you awaken the sacrificer": thus Vāyu's manner of rousing the sacrificer is shown.

This word purandhi indicates "abundance, plenty, ability, wealth" — [though] it suggests the meaning everywhere, since its use occurs in many places, it must be explained according to the context: this is understood from the statement of the author of the Nirukta.

ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमाः सधस्थं विश्वे अभि सन्ति देवाः । ताँ अध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टीवेभगं नासत्या पुरन्धिम् ॥

te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmāḥ sadhastham viśve abhi santi devāḥ | tāṁ adhvara uśato yakṣy agne śruṣṭīvebhagaṃ nāsatyā purandhim ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-31-[?]; as read "೨-೩೧-೪"; the second line is doubtful in several letters [?].) — in explaining the meaning of the word purandhim in this Ṛk, [text continues on p. 583]. Continuing the explanation of purandhim from p. 582: the author of the Nirukta, Yāska, says —

original p. 583

पुरन्धिर्बहुधीः । पुरन्धिर्भगः पुरःस्त्रात्र्यान्नादेक इत्येकम् । इन्द्र इत्येके परं स बहुकर्मा तैः पुरां च दारयितृतमः । वरुण इत्येके परं तं प्रज्ञया स्तौति ॥

purandhir bahudhīḥ | purandhir bhagaḥ puraḥstrātryānnādeka ity ekam | indra ity eke paraṃ sa bahukarmā taiḥ purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ | varuṇa ity eke paraṃ taṃ prajñayā stauti ‖

(Ni. 6-13 [as read, numerals doubtful [?]; the wording of the Sanskrit is doubtful in several letters [?]].) — "purandhi means one of great intelligence; one view, in the Ṛk quoted, takes bhaga as purandhi; others say it qualifies Indra, who has many deeds and is the greatest splitter of citadels (purām dārayitṛtamaḥ); others say it is Varuṇa, whom [the ṛṣi] praises for his wisdom." That is: the word purandhi means one possessing abundant intellect. But the question is who is meant by it. Some say that, in the Ṛk cited, as the word bhaga occurs before this word, it is its adjective. As dhī is among the names of karman (action), purandhi means one who has many kinds of work, or one who splits (breaks) the citadels of enemies, and some say, therefore, it is an epithet of Indra. Or, as in Ṛks such as "imā mū nu kavitamasya māyām" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-[?], as read "೭-೬೧-೩" [?]) the excellent wisdom of Varuṇa is praised, so in the present Ṛk too (the one cited by the author of the Nirukta, 2-31-4) it may be an epithet of Varuṇa describing his intelligence — thus some hold; and there are other views [of different kinds] which Yāska notes. In the matter of the performance of sacrifice, when the superiority of the offering to the gods is to be shown, or the prosperity of the oblations the sacrificer offers to the gods, this word is used — the author of the Nirukta shows in addition other examples.

आदाय श्येनो अभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सवां अयुतं च साकम् । अत्रा पुरन्धिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥

ādāya śyeno abharat somaṃ sahasraṃ savāṃ ayutaṃ ca sākam | atrā purandhir ajahād arātīr made somasya mūrā amūraḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-[?], as read "೪-೨೬-೬" [?].) For the word in this Ṛk, Durgācārya (Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೨" [?]) explains purandhiḥ bahu naḥ dhanasya dātā — "the giver of much wealth to us" — and Sāyaṇa bahukarmā ("of many works"). This word here is an epithet of Indra, the purport being "the giver".

स्वधूतो अद्रिषुतो बर्हिषि प्रियः पतिर्गवां प्रदिव इन्दुरृत्वियः । पुरन्धिवान्मनुषो यज्ञसाधनः शुचिर्धिया पवते सोम इन्द्र ते ॥

svadhūto adriṣuto barhiṣi priyaḥ patir gavāṃ pradiva induṛ ṛtviyaḥ | purandhivān manuṣo yajñasādhanaḥ śucir dhiyā pavate soma indra te ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?], as read "೯-೨೬-೪" [?].) In this Ṛk it is explained as bahukarmavān ("having many kinds of works") for the sake of the satisfaction of the gods of the man.

पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकपादजो दिवो धर्ता सिन्धुरापः समुद्रियः । विश्वे देवासः शृणवन् वचांसि मे सरस्वती सह धीभिः पुरन्ध्या ॥

pāvīravī tanyatur ekapād ajo divo dhartā sindhur āpaḥ samudriyaḥ | viśve devāsaḥ śṛṇavan vacāṃsi me sarasvatī saha dhībhiḥ purandhyā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-13 [as read].) In this, for this word the author of the Nirukta (Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೩೦" [?]) explains purandhyā stutyā prayuktāni — "[words] used with [various kinds of] praise" — i.e. "with many kinds of praise". Bahuvidhayā prajñayā (sic [?]) is the meaning of sahitā sarasvatī: "Sarasvatī, joined with much intelligence" — this is the adjective of Sarasvatī.

original p. 584

…the intelligence of many kinds; but the explanation of Durgācārya, bahudhātrī mādhyamikīyā vāk (Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೩೦" [?]), shows that Sarasvatī is a particular deity like [the mādhyamikā vāk]. In the same way —

शं नो भगः शमु नः शंसो अस्तु शं नः पुरन्धिः शमु सन्तु रायः । शं नः सत्यस्य सुयमस्य शंसः शं नो अर्यमा पुरुजातो अस्तु ॥

śaṃ no bhagaḥ śam u naḥ śaṃso astu śaṃ naḥ purandhiḥ śam u santu rāyaḥ | śaṃ naḥ satyasya suyamasya śaṃsaḥ śaṃ no aryamā purujāto astu ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-[?], as read "೨-೩೮-೩" [?].) In Ṛks such as this purandhi is understood to be a separate deity. Even Sāyaṇa did not make bhaga and the other words in this Ṛk epithets of it. And —

देवो भगः सविता रायो अंश इन्द्रो वृत्रस्य संजितो धनानाम् । ऋभुक्षा वाज उत वा पुरन्धिरवन्तु नो अमृतासस्तुरासः ॥

devo bhagaḥ savitā rāyo aṃśa indro vṛtrasya saṃjito dhanānām | ṛbhukṣā vāja uta vā purandhir avantu no amṛtāsas turāsaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?], as read "೩-೪೯-೩" [?].) — here purandhi is a synonym of Vibhvan [sic: of "Vibhu", as printed].

पुराणी देवि युवतिः पुरन्धिर्व्रतं चरसि विश्ववारे ।

purāṇī devi yuvatiḥ purandhir vrataṃ carasi viśvavāre |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-1 [as read "೩-೬೧-೧" [?]].) In such places it is an epithet of Uṣas: "one with many hymns".

In many places the word is used in respect of the wife, or in reference to women in general, giving the meaning "women who are able to get progeny — not [only] barren women — and who are stout".

अग्निः सप्तिं वाजंभरं ददात्यग्निर्वीरं श्रुत्यं कर्मनिष्ठाम् । अग्नी रोदसी वि चरत्समञ्जन्नग्निर्नारीं वीरकुक्षिं पुरन्धिम् ॥

agniḥ saptiṃ vājaṃbharaṃ dadāty agnir vīraṃ śrutyaṃ karmaniṣṭhām | agnī rodasī vi carat samañjann agnir nārīṃ vīrakukṣiṃ purandhim ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-1 [as read].) In all such Ṛks it means "a wife able to give birth"; or it may mean "a beautiful woman". As explained in the present Ṛk (I. 134-3), the word means, in many places, a woman beautiful in all limbs. The reader can note that both meanings are explained in Sāyaṇa's commentary itself.

पुरन्धिर्योषेत्याह । योषित्येव रूपं दधाति । तस्मात्स्त्री युवतिः प्रियो भावुका ॥

purandhir yoṣety āha | yoṣity eva rūpaṃ dadhāti | tasmāt strī yuvatiḥ priyo bhāvukā ‖

(Tai. Brā. 3-[?]-[?], as read "೩-೮-೧೩-೨" [?].) In this Brāhmaṇa sentence, for the word purandhi it is explained that puraṃ sarvaguṇasampūrṇaṃ śarīraṃ dhārayatīti purandhiḥ, "a woman with a beautiful body" [text continues on p. 585: "and for this same word the Taittirīya…"].

original p. 585

…and for this same word the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (2-[?]-[?], as read "೭-೩-೧೫" [?]) gives the explanation purvāsibhidhyāyate iti purandhiḥ [as read, [?]]: "one on whom men's thought is fixed" — hence, saying that this name is from the fact that "she carries a body that attracts", it has been explained that "she is a woman with an attractive body".

The scholar Max Müller has given the meaning in reference to Uṣas: "Purandhi may have meant originally door-keeper from पुर् [pur] and धि [dhi] like इषुधि [iṣudhi] and श्रेवधि [śevadhi]; whatever it meant etymologically, in our passing where she is to be woke by the wind in the morning, (cf. I. 137.2) it is again a Characteristic epithet of the dawn" (the print: "Vadic Hymus. II. P. 447" [sic for Vedic Hymns]).

On these authorities, if in the present Ṛk it is taken as a simile-word, "like a purandhi", then it means a woman, endowed with beauty; and if, in the main sentence, "purandhiṃ prabodhaya", it is construed as an object-word of the action, then it means a person of much intelligence or of many works, [i.e.] the sacrificer.

Here, Vāyu is compared to a paramour, and the sacrificer, who is the purandhi, to a prostitute (veśyāstrī) with a beautiful form. As the pleasure of the beautiful woman is the cause of the paramour's delight, so the awakening of the sacrificer, by the preparation of the oblations, is the cause of the delight of the deities, Vāyu and the others. Therefore the prayer is made: "awaken him".

sasatīm iva — this word also is an attribute of the word purandhi, and two kinds of construction are to be made for it. The first, upapatyāgamanadhyānena [?] īṣat svapantīm — "as the paramour wakes a prostitute, who, awaiting the coming of her lover, has fallen a little into sleep, so wake the sacrificer, who has gone a little to sleep owing to the completion of the rite" is the purport.

rodasī pra cakṣaya — dyāvāpṛthivyau prakarṣeṇa prakhyāpaya prakāśayety arthaḥ — "illuminate heaven and earth": in order that they be lit, "make Uṣas dwell [in them]" is the prayer.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). yuṅkte — root yujir yoge; as the root has the sense of ṇic in itself [i.e. causative sense], laṭ, third person singular; since it follows a tiṅanta [?], the nighāta accent. rohitā — root ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca; ruher aśca lo vā (Uṇ. 3-[?], as read "೩-೯೪" [?]) gives the suffix itan; the repha changes to la optionally; because the suffix conditions it, the laghūpadha guṇa; ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197 [as read]) gives the ādyudātta; since a dual follows, supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39 [as read]) gives ā for the case-ending.

original p. 586

Grammar, continued. In aruṇā also, the same: ā is the substitute. ajirā — root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ; ajira śiśira… (Uṇ. 1-[?], as read "೧-೫೩" [?]) gives the kirac suffix, finished as nipātana; by cit the final udātta; the case-ending ā as before. dhuri — sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 [as read]) gives the udātta to the seventh case-ending. voḍhave — root vaha prāpaṇe; when it takes the sense of the infinitive, tumarthe seseṇaseasen… (Pā. 3-4-9 [as read]) gives the suffix tavenḥ; hoḍhaḥ gives ḍha for ha; jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ gives dha for ta, and as it becomes ṣṭu [?], ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ gives ḍha; sahivahor odavarṇasya (Pā. 6-3-112 [as read]) gives o for the a of the root; ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ drops the earlier ḍh; since the suffix is eternal, the ādyudātta. vahiṣṭhā — root vaha, with tṛc, makes voḍhṛ; after the tṛc-ending, iṣṭhan by Vedic usage; it being para, turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu (Pā. 6-4-154 [as read]) drops the tṛ [ṭi of the tṛc]; ṣṭhatva and the like that came before are made asiddha, so they go; the ādyudātta accent; the dual ending ā, as before. bodhaya — root budha avagamane; loṭ after a ṇijanta; second person singular; as it follows a tiṅanta [i.e. it is not at the pāda beginning?], nighāta accent. purandhim — pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam gives its desired form and accent. jāraḥ — root jṛṣ vayohānau; dārajārau kartari ṇilluk ca (Pā. 3-3-[?], as read "೩-೩-೨೦-೧" [?]) gives the nipātana form. sasatīm — root saś svapne [as read: sasa svapne]; adādi; śatṛ in the sense of laṭ; in the feminine ugitaś ca gives ṅīp; śaturanumo nadyajādī (Pā. 6-1-173 [as read]) gives it the udātta accent. cakṣaya — root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; here, in the sense of "illuminating", it is abhihita; hetumati ca (Pā. 3-1-26 [as read]) gives ṇic; after the ṇijanta, loṭ; second person singular; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. ‖ 3 ‖

original p. 587

Rik 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तुभ्यमुषासः शुचयः परावति भद्रा वस्त्रा तन्वते दंसु रश्मिषु चित्रा नव्येषु रश्मिषु । तुभ्यं धेनुः सबर्दुघा विश्वा वसूनि दोहते । अजनयो मरुतो वक्षणाभ्यो दिव आ वक्षणाभ्यः ॥ ४ ॥

tubhyamuṣāsaḥ śucayaḥ parāvati bhadrā vastrā tanvate daṃsu raśmiṣu citrā navyeṣu raśmiṣu | tubhyaṃ dhenuḥ sabardughā viśvā vasūni dohate | ajanayo maruto vakṣaṇābhyo diva ā vakṣaṇābhyaḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तुभ्यम् । उषसः । शुचयः । पराऽवति । भद्रा । वस्त्रा । तन्वते । दंसु । रश्मिऽसु । चित्रा । नव्येषु । रश्मिऽषु । तुभ्यम् । धेनुः । सबःऽदुघा । विश्वा । वसूनि । दोहते । अजनयः । मरुतः । वक्षणाभ्यः । दिवः । आ । वक्षणाभ्यः ॥ ४ ॥

tubhyam | uṣasaḥ | śucayaḥ | parā 'vati | bhadrā | vastrā | tanvate | daṃsu | raśmi 'su | citrā | navyeṣu | raśmi 'ṣu | tubhyam | dhenuḥ | sabaḥ 'dughā | viśvā | vasūni | dohate | ajanayaḥ | marutaḥ | vakṣaṇābhyaḥ | divaḥ | ā | vakṣaṇābhyaḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Sense: "O Vāyu, for you (tubhyam) — for your sake — the dawns, lit by you in the way stated before, shine, pure (śucayaḥ) or bright, in the far distance (parāvati), in the sky, in the daṃsu — houses, or acts [daṃsa is a name of house; the final elision by Vedic usage]. With their rays they spread out fine, covering-fit robes (vastrā); or: for you who come, at the sacrificial houses (devayajana), for the oblation, with rays — in the blazing flames of fire — they spread lovely garments; i.e. the flames of Agni themselves spread out as garments, because at dawn the fires are kindled — so the flames are called "garments". Not merely common garments: navyeṣu — in new, praiseworthy [rays], citrā — wonderful, of many colours, they spread out (tanvate), because the rays of the dawn have many colours; and in the Agni-flame sense, the flames are of many colours by being dark, fierce etc. Further, O Vāyu, for your sacrifice the dhenu — the cow that gives joy [by nourishing] — sabardughā [sabar is a name of nectar; the milker of it, kap suffix after duh] — milks of herself all the vasūni — wealth in the form of ghee and the like [dohate: the passive yak is absent, the śap is not elided by Vedic usage]. You, O Vāyu, from the shining sky, beget (ajanayaḥ) the Maruts, your parts, who break the cloud and produce rain, for vakṣaṇābhyaḥ — for the rain-waters of flowing nature; and for vakṣaṇābhyaḥ — the rivers [vakṣaṇā is a name of rivers: vakṣaṇā rujānā, as read in the Nighaṇṭu [?]] — for their sake." The bhāṣya of Ṛk 4 concludes at the top of this page — the passage transcribed above ends at "tāsām arthāya"; the Sanskrit of both pages is one continuous passage, which I have read as above, with the splitting of lines at the page break as printed.

हे वायो तुभ्यं त्वदर्थमुषास उषसः पूर्वोक्तरीत्या त्वया प्रकाशिताः शुचयः शुद्धा दीप्ता वा परावत्यत्यन्तदूरदेशेऽन्तरिक्षे दंसु दंसेषु कर्मवत्सु [?] । यद्वा । गृहनामैतत् ॥ अन्त्यलोपश्छान्दसः ॥ गृहवदाच्छादकेषु । रश्मिषु स्वकीयेषु तैर्भद्रा भन्दनीयानि कल्याणानि वस्त्राच्छादनयोग्यानि वस्त्राणि तन्वते । विस्तारयन्ति । यद्वा । उषसो दंसु यागगृहेषु देवयजनेषु रश्मिषु होमाय प्रदीप्ताग्निज्वालावत्सु [?] आगताय तुभ्यं भद्रा वस्त्रा तन्वते । अग्निज्वाला एव वस्त्राणि विस्तारयन्तीत्यर्थः । उषःकालेऽग्नीनां प्रज्वाल्यमानत्वात्ता एव वस्त्राणीत्युपचर्यते । ननु केवलं साधारणानि वस्त्राणि नेत्याह । नव्येषु नूतनेषु स्तुत्येष्वेषु [?] । णु स्तुतौ । अचो यत् । वाङोयि प्रत्यये इत्यनादेशः । यतोनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ रश्मिषु चित्राणि नानावर्णयुक्तान्याश्चर्यभूतानि तन्वते । उषःकाले रश्मीनां नानावर्णत्वादिति भावः । अग्निद्वारेति पक्षे ज्वालानां कालीकरालीत्यादिरूपेण नानावर्णत्वाच्चित्रत्वम् ॥ किंच हे वायो तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं त्वद्यागार्थमेव धेनुर्घातादिना प्रीणयित्री गौः । जातावेकवचनम् । सबर्दुघा सबरित्यमृतनाम । तस्य दोग्ध्री । दुहः कब्बश्छेति कप् ॥ सती विश्वा वसूनि सर्वाणि धनान्याज्यादिरूपाणि दोहते स्वयमेव दुग्धे । प्रीणयतीत्यर्थः ॥ कर्मकर्तरि न दुहस्नमामिति [?] पा. ३-१-८९ [?] इति यगभावः ॥ छान्दसे शपो लुगभावः ॥ कस्तत्र विशेष इति चेत् उच्यते । हे वायो दिवो द्योतमानादन्तरिक्षान्मरुतो देवाने तन्मानकान् मेघं विशीर्य वृष्ट्युत्पादकान् त्वदंशभूतान्त्स्वीयानजनयः जनयसि उत्पादयसि । किमर्थमिति तदुच्यते । वक्षणाभ्यः प्रवहणशीलाभ्य उदभ्यः वृष्टिलक्षणाभ्यः । तथा वक्षणाभ्यः नदीनाम्नैतत् वक्षणा रुजाना इति तन्नाम्नु पाठात् । तासामर्थायेति ॥

he vāyo tubhyaṃ tvadarthamuṣāsa uṣasaḥ pūrvoktarītyā tvayā prakāśitāḥ śucayaḥ śuddhā dīptā vā parāvatyatyantadūradeśe 'ntarikṣe daṃsu daṃseṣu karmavatsu [?] | yadvā | gṛhanāmaitat ‖ antyalopaśchāndasaḥ ‖ gṛhavadācchādakeṣu | raśmiṣu svakīyeṣu tairbhadrā bhandanīyāni kalyāṇāni vastrācchādanayogyāni vastrāṇi tanvate | vistārayanti | yadvā | uṣaso daṃsu yāgagṛheṣu devayajaneṣu raśmiṣu homāya pradīptāgnijvālāvatsu [?] āgatāya tubhyaṃ bhadrā vastrā tanvate | agnijvālā eva vastrāṇi vistārayantītyarthaḥ | uṣaḥkāle 'gnīnāṃ prajvālyamānatvāttā eva vastrāṇītyupacaryate | nanu kevalaṃ sādhāraṇāni vastrāṇi netyāha | navyeṣu nūtaneṣu stutyeṣveṣu [?] | ṇu stutau | aco yat | vāṅoyi pratyaye ityanādeśaḥ | yatonāva ityādyudāttatvam ‖ raśmiṣu citrāṇi nānāvarṇayuktānyāścaryabhūtāni tanvate | uṣaḥkāle raśmīnāṃ nānāvarṇatvāditi bhāvaḥ | agnidvāreti pakṣe jvālānāṃ kālīkarālītyādirūpeṇa nānāvarṇatvāccitratvam ‖ kiṃca he vāyo tubhyaṃ tvadarthaṃ tvadyāgārthameva dhenurghātādinā prīṇayitrī gauḥ | jātāvekavacanam | sabardughā sabarityamṛtanāma | tasya dogdhrī | duhaḥ kabbaścheti kap ‖ satī viśvā vasūni sarvāṇi dhanānyājyādirūpāṇi dohate svayameva dugdhe | prīṇayatītyarthaḥ ‖ karmakartari na duhasnamāmiti [?] pā. 3-1-89 [?] iti yagabhāvaḥ ‖ chāndase śapo lugabhāvaḥ ‖ kastatra viśeṣa iti cet ucyate | he vāyo divo dyotamānādantarikṣānmaruto devāne tanmānakān meghaṃ viśīrya vṛṣṭyutpādakān tvadaṃśabhūtāntsvīyānajanayaḥ janayasi utpādayasi | kimarthamiti taducyate | vakṣaṇābhyaḥ pravahaṇaśīlābhya udabhyaḥ vṛṣṭilakṣaṇābhyaḥ | tathā vakṣaṇābhyaḥ nadīnāmnaitat vakṣaṇā rujānā iti tannāmnu pāṭhāt | tāsāmarthāyeti ‖

original p. 588

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. (he) vāyo — O Vāyu; tubhyam — for you; śucayaḥ — shining; uṣasaḥ — the dawns; parāvati — in the far-off place; daṃsu — in the houses of the doers [or in the acts]; navyeṣu — newly, praiseworthy; raśmiṣu — with the rays; bhadrā — auspicious; vastrā — garments (fit for covering); tanvate — spread out [or: parāvati — in the far-off place; śucayaḥ — shining ones; uṣasaḥ — dawns; daṃsu — in the sacrificial houses; navyeṣu — newly; raśmiṣu — in the flames of the fire kindled for the sake of the Soma (for the oblation); tubhyam (to you who come); bhadrā — auspicious; vastrā — garments, (flame-form garments); tanvate — spread out]; raśmiṣu — with the rays or the flames; citrā — of many colours, [black, fierce and so on]; tanvate — spread out; and tubhyam — for you; sabardughā — giving nectar; dhenuḥ — the cow; viśvā vasūni — all wealth (of ghee and the like); dohate — milks (by herself); divaḥ — from the shining sky; vakṣaṇābhyaḥ — for the rain-water of flowing nature; vakṣaṇābhyaḥ — and for the rivers; marutaḥ — the deities called Maruts, who split the clouds and make the rain; ā ajanayaḥ — you produce (you create).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, at dawn, for you, in the sacrificial houses, the fires kindled for you spread their flames — black, fierce and the rest [sic: the print says "Kālī, Karālī and so on, in the form of flames, are spread" (the dawns spread coloured rays)]; the cow that gives nectar (for you alone) also milks of herself the ghee and the like; and you, too, produce the Maruts, to bring rain for the rain-waters, and to give water to the rivers [from the shining sky].

original p. 589

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "For you, the brilliant dawns, (raising) from afar, spread abroad their auspicious raiment in inviting rays; in variegated and glorious rays: for you, the cow that yields ambrosia milks all kinds of treasure: you beget the Maruts, of the firmament, (for the purpose of) showering rain; (for the purpose of replenishing) the rivers." [Print: "raising" for "rising" (sic).]

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).

In this Ṛk, two kinds of meaning are given for the first half. According to the first construction, the dawns, in the antarikṣa, adorn Vāyu with rays of many colours; according to the second construction, it is described that Vāyu in the sacrificial houses is adorned with garments made of the flames of the fire.

According to the first: śucayaḥ uṣasaḥ navyeṣu raśmiṣu citrā bhadrā vastrā tanvate — "the shining dawns spread out, with their new and many-coloured rays, auspicious and covering garments"; according to the second: parāvati śucayaḥ uṣasaḥ daṃsu navyeṣu raśmiṣu citrā bhadrā vastrā tanvate — "the dawns, far away and shining, in the sacrificial houses spread out for Vāyu, with the flames of the fire — of many colours, auspicious — garments in the form of coverings": thus Sāyaṇa too has explained.

parāvati — there is no difference in the sense of this word in the two constructions. Āke, parāke and so on are found among the names of "distance" (Ni. 3-[?], as read "೩-೧೯" [?]). The author of the Nirukta, taking the Ṛk —

एतदस्या अनः शये सुसंपिष्टं विपाश्या । ससार सीं परावतः ॥

etad asyā anaḥ śaye susaṃpiṣṭaṃ vipāśyā | sasāra sīṃ parāvataḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-11 [as read]) — explains in it (Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೪೬" [?]) the sense of the word parāvataḥ. Among the deities of heaven, Uṣas is counted.

व्युर्णुवती दिवो अन्ताँ अबोध्यप स्वसारं सनुतर्युयोति । प्रमिनती मनुष्या युगानि योषा जारस्य चक्षसा वि भाति ॥

vy ūrṇuvatī divo antāṁ abodhy apa svasāraṃ sanutar yuyoti | pramināti manuṣyā yugāni yoṣā jārasya cakṣasā vi bhāti ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-11 [as read].) In Ṛks such as this, the description that she unfastens all the ends of the antarikṣa from darkness and makes [them] shine, shows the far-off path of Uṣas's movement.

सद्यश्चिद्या सद्यश्चिरिद्या [?] श्वो दीर्घं सचन्ते वरुणस्य धाम । अनवद्यास्त्रिंशतं योजनान्येकैका क्रतुं परि यन्ति सद्यः ॥

sadyaś cid yā sadyaś cirid yā [?] śvo dīrghaṃ sacante varuṇasya dhāma | anavadyās triṃśataṃ yojanāny ekaikā kratuṃ pari yanti sadyaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-8 [as read]; the first line's wording is doubtful in several letters [?].) In Ṛks such as this, the movement of Uṣas, going round thirty yojanas in a day, is described: this part is suggested in the present passage by the word parāvati. Although Uṣas is so far away, it is said that she spreads for you [Vāyu] citrā, bhadrā, vastrā; the citra-rūpa garments of the Uṣas — that is, her rays of many colours — adorn the antarikṣa Vāyu. This unique greatness of Uṣas is counted as a wonder. Therefore:

original p. 590

वाजिनीवती सूर्यस्य योषा चित्रामघा राय ईशे वसूनाम् । ऋषिष्टुता जरयन्ती मघोन्युषा उच्छति वह्निभिर्गृणाना ॥

vājinīvatī sūryasya yoṣā citrāmaghā rāya īśe vasūnām | ṛṣiṣṭutā jarayantī maghony uṣā ucchati vahnibhir gṛṇānā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-48-[?], as read "೧-೪೮-೩" [?].) In this Ṛk there is the epithet citrāmaghā: "she has wonderful riches", vicitradhanā; vicitraraśmyaiśvaryavatī [?] — "one who has the many kinds of wealth in the form of rays". As she has rays of many different colours, Uṣas has epithets such as vibhāvarī (Ṛ. 1-[?]-[?], "೧-೯೩-೪" [?]); āhanā (1-[?]-[?], "೧-೧೨೩-೪" [?]); aruṣī (3-[?]-[?], "೩-೩೯-೫" [?]); aruṇapsu (4-[?]-[?]). It is stated in the Nirukta itself that vibhāvarī and bhāsvatī are synonyms of Uṣas. Vibhāvarī means vibhāyuktā ("endowed with vibhā, brilliance"): vibhā is the mass of various lights, and a person having such a mass of radiance is meant. Aruṣī means "red"; aruṇapsu means "golden-coloured". And —

विषा वैनी भवति द्विबर्हा आविष्कृण्वाना तन्वं पुरस्तात् । ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेति साधु प्रजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ॥

viṣā vainī bhavati dvibarhā āviṣkṛṇvānā tanvaṃ purastāt | ṛtasya panthām anveti sādhu prajānatīva na diśo mināti ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?], as read "೩-೬೧-೪" [?]; the first line is doubtful [?].) In this Ṛk it is described that Uṣas, while changing her colour, and at the same time putting on new radiance, follows the path of ṛta.
