Such Uṣas, who has a colour of many kinds, in her glory she puts on Vāyu garments, and thereby spreads him out.

In the second sense, in the Agni-form too: for the Vāyu deity in the sacrificial houses also, citrā bhadrā vastrā tanvate — "of wonderful form, auspicious, [Agni] spreads the garment". Agnidvāreti pakṣe jvālānāṃ kālīkarālītyādirūpeṇa nānāvarṇatvāc citratvam — "in the case where [the dawns] come by the door of the fire, the flames are wonderful because of their many colours, such as the kālī (black) and the karālī (fierce)": the description is thus because the flames of Agni have many forms. Continuing the entry on the flames:

original p. 591

काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा । स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः ॥

kālī karālī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā | sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ ‖

(Muṇḍakopaniṣad 1-2-4 [as read].) "[The flames of the fire are:] black-coloured, terrible in form, extremely red-brown in colour, of the colour of smoke, shining, everywhere gleaming, divine": because of the colour of the flames of Agni, all such flames of every colour adorn Vāyu, as garments do; this is the purport.

bhadrā — kalyāṇāni; "that which causes auspiciousness" is the meaning. Bhadraṃ bhagena vyākhyātam | bhajanīyaṃ bhūtānām abhidravaṇīyaṃ bhavaty amayam ayatīti vā bhājanavad vā (Ni. 4-[?], as read "೪-೯" [?]). The word bhadra is used in the sense of "making fortunate" or "auspicious". Explained more fully: [it is used in the senses] that which is fit for enjoyment, that which beings eagerly desire, or that which yields pleasure; or that which is fit for a person of dignity, a vessel-like [receptacle]. The author of the Nirukta, in explaining this word, has given its sense in agreement with the context by the example of a passage from the Śruti:

सक्तुमिव तितउना पुनन्तो यत्र धीरा मनसा वाचमक्रत । अत्रा सखायः सख्यानि जानते भद्रैषां लक्ष्मीर्निहिताधि वाचि ॥

saktum iva titaunā punanto yatra dhīrā manasā vācam akrata | atrā sakhāyaḥ sakhyāni jānate bhadraiṣāṃ lakṣmīr nihitādhi vāci ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-2 [as read].) It was explained that the word bhadra here has an extensive meaning, showing prosperity, auspiciousness, happiness. Likewise in the present Ṛk, if explained in connexion with the glory of Uṣas in the antarikṣa, it is the mass of radiance that attracts all, is full of beauty, and gives happiness; if in connexion with the flames of fire, it is a mass of radiance that is auspicious and brings happiness: this is the purport.

navyeṣu — nūtaneṣu; stūyamāneṣu: "new or praiseworthy"; in the rays; for the rays of Uṣas come new at each rising, they are new. Or, the word nauti is found among the names of "worship" (arcati-karman) [Ni. 3-[?]], and since navya is derived from it, it means "worthy of praise, to be praised".

व्यूर्णोति हृदा मतिं नव्यो जायतामृतं विद्मा मे अस्य रोदसी ॥

vy ūrṇoti hṛdā matiṃ navyo jāyatām ṛtaṃ vidmā me asya rodasī ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೧೦೫-೧೫" [?]; the quotation is partly doubtful [?].)

original p. 592

In this [Ṛk] the poet prays to that Varuṇa with a sincere praise. Varuṇa, the object of the praise, is to help us: so navya is explained as "worthy of praise". Likewise in the present Ṛk too, it means the rays that are praiseworthy.

sabardughā — sabar iti amṛtanāma | tasya dogdhrī — "the cow that milks nectar" is the meaning.

धेनुं सबर्दुघां चक्रुरमृतं सबरुच्यते ।

dhenuṃ sabardughāṃ cakrur amṛtaṃ sabar ucyate |

(Bṛhaddevatā 3-[?], as read "೩-೯೫" [?].) Sabar is nectar. Since the cow was made to give milk of the nature of nectar, sabardughā is the famous mādhyamikā vāk (middle-region speech) of the form of nectar-wealth. As an example:

त्वे धेनुः सुदुघा जातवेदोऽसश्चतेव समना सबर्धुक् । त्वं नृभिर्दक्षिणावद्भिरग्ने सुमित्रेभिरिध्यसे देवयद्भिः ॥

tve dhenuḥ sudughā jātavedo 'saścateva samanā sabardhuk | tvaṃ nṛbhir dakṣiṇāvadbhir agne sumitrebhir idhyase devayadbhiḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-69-[?], as read "೧೦-೬೯-೭" [?].) In this it means the one who milks the nectar in the lightning-form Agni, [a cow] in the form of a cow, i.e. the mādhyamikā vāk. And likewise:

आ सखायः सबर्दुघां धेनुमजध्वमुप नव्यसा वचः । सृजध्वमनपस्फुराम् ॥

ā sakhāyaḥ sabardughāṃ dhenum ajadhvam upa navyasā vacaḥ | sṛjadhvam anapasphurām ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-11 [as read].) In this the author of the Nirukta explains: marutāṃ mātā pṛśnyākhyā mādhyamikā vāg dhenuḥ | marujjananahetubhūtasya payaso dogdhrīṃ dhenuṃ pṛśnim — "the mother of the Maruts, called Pṛśni, the mādhyamikā vāc, is the dhenu; the cow Pṛśni, who is the milker of the milk that is the cause of the birth of the Maruts": the mother of the Maruts, Pṛśni, is the mādhyamikā vāc, and the cow that gives nectar-milk. Not only that, but in the present Ṛk also it is said of Vāyu that marutaḥ ajanayaḥ, "you created the Maruts"; therefore here too the sabardughā dhenuḥ (the cow of nectar-milk), as cited above in the Ṛks, is the Agni-form lightning-cow, and the Pṛśni-cow, and the nectar-cow described here: it cannot be wrong to say that they are one.

By the sentence vakṣaṇābhyaḥ marutaḥ ajanayaḥ, too, the above meaning can be established. The scholar Max Müller explains that vakṣaṇābhyaḥ is connected with dhenuḥ:

"It would be better if we could refer वक्षणाभ्यः [vakṣaṇābhyaḥ] to धेनुः [dhenuḥ], the cow, the mother of the Maruts, whole Dyaus is their father. Here, however, Vayu is conceived as their father, and Dyaus as their mother." [Vedic Hymns II. p. 448.]

original p. 593

प्र ये मे बन्ध्वेषे गां वोचन्त सूरयः पृश्निं वोचन्त मातरम् ।

pra ye me bandhveṣe gāṃ vocanta sūrayaḥ pṛśniṃ vocanta mātaram |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-52-16 [as read].) — in Ṛks such as this, the dhenu in the form of Pṛśni is said to be the mother of the Maruts; and as the origin of the Maruts is stated in the present Ṛk also, it is fitting, in this scholar's [Max Müller's] opinion, to show a connexion between the word vakṣaṇābhyaḥ and the word dhenuḥ.

vakṣaṇābhyaḥ — the word is repeated. The first, pravahaṇaśīlābhya udabhyaḥ vṛṣṭilakṣaṇābhyaḥ — "for the waters that flow, in the form of rain, [fit to flow]"; the second, nadīnām aitat; tāsām arthāya — "this is a name of rivers (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೩" [?]); for their sake", the sense is "for the rivers".

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). uṣāsaḥ — long in the Saṃhitā by Vedic usage. bhadrā — root bhadi kalyāṇe sukhe ca; Uṇ. suffix rak; in the neuter plural śeś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70 [as read]) gives luk of śi; in vastrā also the Uṇ. suffix stran comes and śi is dropped. tanvate — root tanu vistāre; laṭ, third person plural; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. daṃsu — daṃsa śabde; locative plural, a para [?]; by Vedic usage the final is dropped. navyeṣu — root ṇu stutau; aco yat (Pā. 3-1-97 [as read]) gives yat; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa to the final i-vowel of the root; vānto yi pratyaye (Pā. 6-1-79 [as read]) gives av; yato nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 [as read]) gives the ādyudātta; locative plural. sabardughā — root duha prapūraṇe; when sabar is the upapada, duhaḥ kab ghaś ca (Pā. 3-2-70 [as read]) gives the suffix kap; gha for the root; since the suffix is pit, it is anudātta, so the accent of the root remains; in the compound, kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara; in the feminine, ṭāp by adantanibandhana. viśvā — śeś chandasi bahulam drops śi. dohate — root duha prapūraṇe; used in the active-passive sense [karmakartari]; karmavat karmaṇā tulyakriyaḥ (Pā. 3-1-87 [as read]) gives Ātmanepada and so on; na duhasnamām [as read] (Pā. 3-1-89 [as read]) forbids yak; the suffix in the singular, ta, with e; by Vedic usage the śap is not luk-ed; pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (Pā. 7-3-86 [as read]) gives the laghūpadha guṇa; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta.

original p. 594

Grammar, concluded. ajanayaḥ — root janī prādurbhāve; the ṇic appears, as the causal action is shown; janīvṛṣaṃ… [jñaji-] … (Pā. 6-4-[?]) gives the term mit; mitāṃ hrasvaḥ (Pā. 6-4-92 [as read]) shortens the penultimate; by Vedic usage laṅ in the sense of the present [vartamāna]; second person singular; as it is at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not occur, the ādyudātta. divaḥ — ūḍidaṃ padādi (Pā. 6-1-171 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending. ‖ 4 ‖

Rik 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तुभ्यं शुक्रासः शुचयस्तुरण्यवो मदेषूग्रा इषणन्त भुर्वण्यपामिषन्त भुर्वणि । त्वां त्सारी दसमानो भगमीट्टे तक्ष्ववीर्ये । त्वं विश्वस्माद्भुवनात्पासि धर्मणासुर्यात्पासि धर्मणा ॥ ५ ॥

tubhyaṃ śukrāsaḥ śucayasturaṇyavo madeṣūgrā iṣaṇanta bhurvaṇyapāmiṣanta bhurvaṇi | tvāṃ tsārī dasamāno bhagamīṭṭe takṣvavīrye | tvaṃ viśvasmādbhuvanātpāsi dharmaṇāsuryātpāsi dharmaṇā ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Saṃhitā and Pada read from the image; "tsārī" and "takṣvavīrye" are as printed [?].

तुभ्यम् । शुक्रासः । शुचयः । तुरण्यवः । मदेषु । उग्राः । इषणन्त । भुर्वणि । अपाम् । इषन्त । भुर्वणि । त्वाम् । त्सारी । दसमानः । भगम् । ईट्टे । तक्ष्वऽवीर्ये । त्वम् । विश्वस्मात् । भुवनात् । पासि । धर्मणा । असुर्यात् । पासि । धर्मणा ॥ ५ ॥

tubhyam | śukrāsaḥ | śucayaḥ | turaṇyavaḥ | madeṣu | ugrāḥ | iṣaṇanta | bhurvaṇi | apām | iṣanta | bhurvaṇi | tvām | tsārī | dasamānaḥ | bhagam | īṭṭe | takṣva 'vīrye | tvam | viśvasmāt | bhuvanāt | pāsi | dharmaṇā | asuryāt | pāsi | dharmaṇā ‖ 5 ‖

original p. 595

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 5; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "O Vāyu, for you the Soma-juices are śukrāsaḥ — bright, and śucayaḥ — pure; [as they come through the vessels they become exceedingly pure — what need is there to say of their purity?]. Turaṇyavaḥ — hasty [to reach you], ugrāḥ — of surging brilliance; they, in your joys (madeṣu), for the cause of your joy, in bhurvaṇi — in the rite that bears [the oblation] — go (iṣaṇanta) towards the āhavanīya or desire it [the Ātmanepada by vyatyaya]. And further they desire (iṣanta) water, in apāṃ bhurvaṇi — in the cloud (megha), since the oblation offered in the fire produces rain through the Sun; or: the sacrificers, offering for you, desire the rain of waters. Further, O Vāyu, bhagam — the worshipful you, the tsārī — one who is anxious and extremely afraid, dasamāna — wasted [by the obstructors of the sacrifice, or by the observances such as the milk-vow], the sacrificer — in takṣvavīrye — for the [driving away] of thieves who obstruct the sacrifice [?] — praises (īṭṭe, from īḍ stutau, the śap elided as in the adādi class). Since you protect from all beings (bhuvanāt), from the fear arising in the three worlds, by supporting our oblations (dharmaṇā), you protect; and further from the fear of the asurya — [the fear] connected with the Asuras — you protect specially, being endowed with the supporting and nourishing of us: since you do so, therefore I praise [you]." The reading of a phrase near "bhūtajātāt" is not clear [?].

हे वायो तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं शुक्रासो दीप्ताः शुचयः शुद्धाः । सोमस्य पात्रारोत्यन्तं शुद्धा भवन्ति । किमु वक्तव्यं तेषां शुद्धत्वे । तुरण्यवस्त्वरणयुक्तास्त्वां प्राप्तुं उग्रा उद्गूर्णतेजसः सोमा मदेषु तव मदेषु निमित्तभूतेषु भुर्वणि भरणवति योगे इषणन्त आहवनीयं प्रति गच्छन्ति इच्छन्ति वा ॥ व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । [?] ॥ किंचापां भुर्वणि मेघे इषन्त उदकमिच्छन्तीत्यपादयितुम् [?] । अग्नौ हूयमानस्याहुतेरादित्यद्वारा वृष्ट्युत्पादकत्वात् । यद्वा । यजमानास्त्वामुद्दिश्याजुह्वाना अपां वर्षणमिषन्त इच्छन्ति ॥ किंच हे वायो भगं भजनीयं त्वां त्सारी त्वरणवानत्यन्तभीतो दसमान उपक्षीणो यज्ञविघातकैः पयोव्रतादिनियमैर्वा यजमानः तक्ष्ववीर्ये तस्कराणां यज्ञविघातिनामन्यगमनाय [?] ईट्टे स्तौति ॥ ईड स्तुतौ । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । यतस्त्वं विश्वस्माद्भुवनात् सर्वस्माल्लोकात् भूतजातात् .. [?] लोकत्रयसंबन्धिनो भयाद्धर्मणास्मदीयहविषां धारणेन पासि पालयसि । किंचासुर्यादसुरसंबन्धिनो भयाद्विशेषेण पासि धर्मणास्मद्धारणेन पोषणेन वा युक्तः सन् । यत एवं करोषि अतः स्तौमीत्यर्थः ॥

he vāyo tubhyaṃ tvadarthaṃ śukrāso dīptāḥ śucayaḥ śuddhāḥ | somasya pātrārotyantaṃ śuddhā bhavanti | kimu vaktavyaṃ teṣāṃ śuddhatve | turaṇyavastvaraṇayuktāstvāṃ prāptuṃ ugrā udgūrṇatejasaḥ somā madeṣu tava madeṣu nimittabhūteṣu bhurvaṇi bharaṇavati yoge iṣaṇanta āhavanīyaṃ prati gacchanti icchanti vā ‖ vyatyayenātmanepadaṃ | [?] ‖ kiṃcāpāṃ bhurvaṇi meghe iṣanta udakamicchantītyapādayitum [?] | agnau hūyamānasyāhuterādityadvārā vṛṣṭyutpādakatvāt | yadvā | yajamānāstvāmuddiśyājuhvānā apāṃ varṣaṇamiṣanta icchanti ‖ kiṃca he vāyo bhagaṃ bhajanīyaṃ tvāṃ tsārī tvaraṇavānatyantabhīto dasamāna upakṣīṇo yajñavighātakaiḥ payovratādiniyamairvā yajamānaḥ takṣvavīrye taskarāṇāṃ yajñavighātināmanyagamanāya [?] īṭṭe stauti ‖ īḍa stutau | adāditvācchapo luk | yatastvaṃ viśvasmādbhuvanāt sarvasmāllokāt bhūtajātāt .. [?] lokatrayasaṃbandhino bhayāddharmaṇāsmadīyahaviṣāṃ dhāraṇena pāsi pālayasi | kiṃcāsuryādasurasaṃbandhino bhayādviśeṣeṇa pāsi dharmaṇāsmaddhāraṇena poṣaṇena vā yuktaḥ san | yata evaṃ karoṣi ataḥ staumītyarthaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he) vāyo — O Vāyu; tubhyam — for you; śukrāsaḥ — shining; śucayaḥ — pure; turaṇyavaḥ — (those that come to you) hasty; ugrāḥ — and fierce (Soma-juices); madeṣu — in your delights; bhurvaṇi — in the sacrifice; iṣaṇanta — go (to the āhavanīya) [or desire to go]; (kiṃca — and; apām bhurvaṇi — in the cloud; iṣanta — (the sacrificers) desire water, or (those that offer to you [and perform the sacrifice]) ask for rain [apām bhurvaṇi — rain of water]; he vāyo — O Vāyu; tvam — you; viśvasmāt bhuvanāt — from all the world (from the fear arising from the group of beings); dharmaṇā — by holding (taking up) our oblations; pāsi — you protect; and dharmaṇā — by our support; asuryāt — from fear of the Asuras; pāsi — you protect; ataḥ — therefore; bhagam — the one who is to be worshipped; tvām — you; tsārī — (extremely) fearful; dasamānaḥ — (by obstructers of the sacrifice, or by observances such as the milk-vow) wasted [the sacrificer]; takṣvavīrye — in destroying thieves; īṭṭe — praises.

original p. 596

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, the Soma-juices, bright, pure, hasty (to reach you), and capable of producing joy [intoxication], desire to be offered at the sacrifice; and they desire to be [offered] for rain in the clouds (the sacrificers who offer to you ask for the production of rain by the coming of water); you protect from fear that arises from the whole world (and from beings of the world) — [fear] which is our oblation's [havis] covering — by covering [our oblations], by protecting, and by [our] nourishment; and from fear from Asuras you protect us. Therefore the sacrificer, very fearful and weak [wasted by the obstructors, or by observances like the milk-vow], praises you in order to destroy the thieves.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "For you, the bright, pure, quick-flowing (Soma juices), potent for exhilaration, are eager for the (fire of) oblation; are eager for the cloud (showering) waters. The timid and anxious (worshipper) praises you, who are auspicious, for (driving away) thieves; for you defend (us) from all beings, (as the reward) of our righteousness: you protect us from the fear of evil spirits, (as the reward) of our righteousness."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).

This Ṛk describes the pure nature of the Soma-juices, and that they are eager to give satisfaction to Vāyu. It also describes that after drinking the Soma-juice Vāyu gains the strength to bear the world and to nourish the world and grows in power; and that the sacrificer relies upon Vāyu's protection to escape his own troubles.

In the first half, the nature of Soma-juice is told by the two epithets śukrāsaḥ and śucayaḥ. On a rough view the two words have the same meaning; but since both words are used here, there must be a subtle difference between the two.

In the Nirukta both words are stated to come from the same root. The author of the Nirukta, in explaining the Ṛk —

त्वमग्ने द्युभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिस्त्वमद्भ्यस्त्वमश्मनस्परि । त्वं वनेभ्यस्त्वमोषधीभ्यस्त्वं नृणां नृपते जायसे शुचिः ॥

tvam agne dyubhis tvam āśuśukṣaṇis tvam adbhyas tvam aśmanas pari | tvaṃ vanebhyas tvam oṣadhībhyas tvaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛpate jāyase śuciḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-1 [as read].) — in explaining the word śuciḥ there, [writes] śuciḥ śocater jvalatikarmaṇaḥ — "from the root śuc which gives the meaning 'to shine'", and first notes the physical meaning, and then the [other] meaning: ayam apītaraḥ śucir etasmād eva niṣkrītam asmāt… [as read; the rest of the quotation is not clear [?]].

original p. 597

Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued from p. 596: …kamīti nairuktāḥ [as read, [?]]. "To show moral purity (śucitva), the word śuci [is used], and the root īḍe is its origin too [?]; from it the sin is removed, as is said, [so] it is proper for this word to be used in this connexion" — such is the opinion of the author of the Nirukta (Ni. 6-1 [as read]). Again:

आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ । दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥

ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau | divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-6 [as read].) While explaining this Ṛk, he explains the derivation of the word śukra also exactly as said for the word śuci: śukraṃ śocater jvalatikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 7-[?], as read "೭-೧೧" [?]).

Sāyaṇa, in the present Ṛk, explains śukrāsaḥ as dīptāḥ and śucayaḥ as śuddhāḥ — giving to śukra the physical sense of brightness and to śuci the moral sense of purity. This difference of meaning may be intended in this passage. But the word śukra does not mean merely physical lustre; the spiritual light is also indicated by the word:

तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।

tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate |

(Kaṭha [Upaniṣad], as read "೫ ೮" [?].) In such sentences, as Śaṅkarācārya explains śukra as "pure (śubhra), clean (śuddha) — that Brahman", the word also indicates spiritual intelligence. And:

स पर्यगाच्छुक्रमकायमव्रणमस्नाविरं शुद्धमपापविद्धम् ।

sa paryagāc chukram akāyam avraṇam asnāviraṃ śuddham apāpaviddham |

(Īśa [Upaniṣad] 8.) Here, as the two words śukra and śuddha both occur, it means merely "bright". Thus, although they are derived from a single root, there are subtle differences of meaning, and so in each context the appropriate meaning is to be taken. In the present Ṛk the Soma-juice is described as giving light and shining with purity: that is the purport. In such sentences as śukraṃ jyotir ajījanat (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?], as read "೯-೮೨-೩" [?]) and ajanayat sūrye jyotir induḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?], as read "೯-೮೬-೪" [?]), the qualities of Soma, full of radiance, are described.

turaṇyavaḥ — tvaraṇayuktāḥ; "those that are in haste, who are eager to approach you" is the meaning. Ordinarily this word is used when the speed of horses' movement is shown. The author of the Nirukta, citing —

उत स्य वाजी क्षिपणिं तुरण्यति ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपिकक्ष आसनि ।

uta sya vājī kṣipaṇiṃ turaṇyati grīvāyāṃ baddho apikakṣa āsani |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-40-4 [as read].) — explains the word turaṇyati thus: "tūrṇam aśnute ity adhvānaṃ — quickly crosses the road"; here also the speed of the Soma-juice approaching Vāyu is suggested.

original p. 598

ugrāḥ — the word ugra may be explained in two ways. Udgūrṇatejasaḥ — "having manifest brilliance, or fierce (tīkṣṇa) brilliance" is the explanation. Not only does the Soma-juice have lustre of itself, it makes Indra and the other gods, who drink it, sharp-witted, as described in Ṛks such as indrasya kuṣmam irāyan [?] (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?], as read "೯-೭೧-೩" [?]); or in sentences like yo te bhīmāny āyudhā tigmāni santi dhūrvaṇe (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೬೧-೩೦" [?]) the very fearful and sharp weapons that Soma holds are mentioned, and avājuṣṭān nyabhiti karte avratān [?] (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?], as read "೯-೭೧-೯" [?]) it is described that he kills those who deviate from duties, so that this epithet is appropriate. But in the present context, as the Soma-juices are being described, the best meaning is "increasing the sharpness of Indra and the other gods".

bhurvaṇi — this word is repeated. For the first, "bharaṇavati yoge" is the meaning; for the second, "apāṃ bhurvaṇi meghe" — "in the cloud, which is a place that holds water".

This word is derived from the root bhuraṇa (dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ), "holding, nourishing", so bharaṇavati yāge means "in the sacrifice, that is the cause of food, by rain, for the world, and holds the world": the sacrifice is meant.

येना सत्या भुरण्यथो यद्वा देव भिषज्यथः । आयं वां वत्सो मतिभिर्न विन्धते हविष्मन्तं हि गच्छथः ॥

yenā satyā bhuraṇyatho yad vā deva bhiṣajyathaḥ | āyaṃ vāṃ vatso matibhir na vindhate haviṣmantaṃ hi gacchathaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?], as read "೮-೯-೬" [?]; the wording is doubtful in places [?].) In this, "bhuraṇyathaḥ — you nourish the whole world", as is described by [the words: "you two, O gods, nourish the whole world"]; so in the present place also, by the word bhurvaṇi the nature of the sacrifice, which supports the world, is described.

When the construction apāṃ bhurvaṇi is made, [the word] is in the sense of "going". Bhuraṇyuḥ, bhuraṇyati — these words, the author of the Nirukta has placed among the verbs of motion (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೯" [?]). In that motion, to show a quick moving, the name bhuraṇyu is well-known for birds (pakṣi) and others also (Ni. 3-[?], as read "೩-೨೨" [?]) — know this.

येना पावक चक्षसा भुरण्यन्तं जनाँ अनु । त्वं वरुण पश्यसि ॥

yenā pāvaka cakṣasā bhuraṇyantaṃ janāṁ anu | tvaṃ varuṇa paśyasi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-6 [as read].) For the word in the Ṛk quoted by the author of the Nirukta, Durgācārya in his commentary [says]: puṇyakṛto janān anubhuraṇyantaṃ pūrveṣāṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ mārgeṇa devayānena kṣipraṃ gacchantam anupaśyasi — "you see those of virtuous deeds, going quickly by the path of the earlier virtuous, the path to the gods": he has given only the sense of motion. If that meaning is taken in the present Ṛk too, then [Sāyaṇa's explanation]: agnau hūyamānasyāhuter ādityadvārā vṛṣṭyutpādakatvāt [text continues on p. 599].

original p. 599

Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued: …as has been explained, since the Soma-juices poured into the fire go to the Sun and become the causes of the fall of rain there, the movement of the Soma-juices is a cause for the production of clouds. Therefore apāṃ bhurvaṇi means "in the clouds" or "through the clouds, the fall of rain": Sāyaṇa explains it as the purport that the Soma-juices, joining the clouds, wish to bring about the fall of rain, or that the sacrificers, who perform the sacrifice desiring Vāyu, look for the fall of rain. As the sacrifice is directly and naturally [the sense] of this word, there is no doubt about it. But in the second construction a meaning by tradition has to be given, and to Sāyaṇa this seemed slightly strained, so he has also given a synonym-meaning [i.e. the first].

dharmaṇā — this word also is repeated. The first, asmadīyahaviṣāṃ dhāraṇena pāsi: "you protect us by taking up our oblations" — the meaning of acceptance; the second, asmaddhāraṇena poṣaṇena vā: "by holding us (protecting) and by nourishing, you protect us" — the meaning of nourishing.

bhagam — bhago bhajateḥ ("bhaga from the root bhaj"; derived from the root bhaj in the sense of worship, meaning "bhajanīya" — worshipful): it is an epithet of Vāyu. The word bhaga has in various contexts the meanings "wealth", "the deity Bhaga", and so on; all are derived from the root bhaj in the sense of "to worship".

tsārī — tvaraṇavān; atyantabhītaḥ — "extremely afraid". But since the word is derived from a root of motion, it gives the sense of one who runs away from fear. The author of the Nirukta has placed this word among the verbs of motion (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೧೯"). The usages tsaruḥ, tsarī, tsarit [as read] occur, and everywhere the sense is bhadmagati ("crooked motion"), running away by deceit.

आजकावं दुर्दृशीकं तिरो दधे मा मां पद्येन रपसा विदत्त्सरुः ।

ājakāvaṃ durdṛśīkaṃ tiro dadhe mā māṃ padyena rapasā vidat tsaruḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-1, as read "೨-೩೦-೧" [?].) — "tsaruḥ means bhadmagāmī sarpaḥ, 'the creeping snake'": the purport is only movement. In the same way in the present Ṛk also, the sense is "one who runs away from fear".

dasamānaḥ — derived from the root das, which gives the meaning "to waste (upakṣaye)". Yajñavighātakaiḥ upakṣīṇaḥ — "wasted by the obstructors of the sacrifice": Sāyaṇa explains it as "one wasted by the trouble of those who obstruct the sacrifice, or payovratādiniyamair vā — one whose body has been wasted by vow-observances such as the milk-vow", the sacrificer.

original p. 600

takṣvavīrye — tṛpuḥ, takvā and so on are in the names of "thief" (Ni. 3-[?], as read "೩-೧೯" [?]). The word takṣan, in Sāyaṇa's [explanation], is taskarāṇāṃ yajñavighātināṃ anyatra gamanāya — "for the departure to another place of the thieves who obstruct the sacrifice": "the thieves and the like who give trouble to the sacrifice run from here to a far place", is the meaning. [Sāyaṇa's] meaning, if explained as "the bearer-away of the thief", is not wrong.

मही अत्र महिना वारमृण्वथोऽरेणवस्तुज आ सद्मन्धेनवः । स्वरन्ति ता उपरताति सूर्यमा निम्रुच उषसस्तक्ववीरिव ॥

mahī atra mahinā vāram ṛṇvatho 'reṇavas tuja ā sadman dhenavaḥ | svaranti tā uparatāti sūryam ā nimruca uṣasas takvavīr iva ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-151-[?], as read "೧-೧೫೧-೩" [?]; the quotation is doubtful in several letters [?].) In this the word takvavīḥ, as Sāyaṇa himself explains it, means "one who seeks the thief" (takvā śyenaḥ, [as read: "tasya vettā gantā manuṣyaḥ" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೧೪೯-೩" [?])]); here too the same meaning can be taken, i.e. "I pray to you to drive away thieves and the like": that is the purport. Max Müller, in giving the meaning of this word, writes "The tired hunter asks luck of thee in the chase"; he takes tsārī as "hunter" and takṣvavīrye as "in the hunter's chase" [as read: "in the chase of the hunter"]; in support of his meaning he says —

"I have followed Ludwig in his Explanation त्सारी — hunter and तक्ष्ववीर्य, chase of the तक्ष्व, whatever animal it may be" — he says he has followed the explanation of the scholar Ludwig. But the commentator's meaning is more appropriate: [Vāyu is prayed] to drive away thieves, and the sacrificer prays so.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). śukrāsaḥ — root śuca śoke; khujendragra… [as read: śukrendraśuci…; rasanta…] (Uṇ. 3-[?], as read "೩-೧೪೭" [?]) — formed by nipātana with ra; as jas follows, ājjaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50 [as read]) gives the asuk augment. turaṇyavaḥ — root tvara tvarāyām; kaṇḍvādibhyo yak (Pā. 3-1-27 [as read]) gives yak in its own sense; after this the Uṇādi suffix u; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. iṣaṇanta — root iṣ gatau; vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. 3-1-85 [as read]) gives Ātmanepada; laṭ in the sense of the present by Vedic usage; jha → ata [as printed "ata"]; by Vedic usage śna — two vikaraṇas appear: śnam [and śap]; by Vedic usage the āgama does not occur. Or iṣa gatau; śnā as vikaraṇa; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ (Pā. 6-4-112 [as read]) gives lopa of the vikaraṇa's ā; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta.

original p. 601

bhurvaṇi — root bhurṇa hiṃsāyām [as read; or bhṛṇa]; the Uṇādi suffix asi [ani] for it; by Vedic usage u for the a of the root; by the suffix accent it becomes madhyodātta; supāṃ sulug (Pā. 7-1-39 [as read]) gives luk of the seventh case-ending. apām — genitive plural; ūḍidaṃ padādi (Pā. 6-1-171 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending. iṣanta — root iṣu icchāyām; by Vedic usage third person plural; the āgama and the bhāva are absent by Vedic usage; nighāta after tiṅanta. tsārī — root tsara chadmagatau; ṇini in tācchīlya [as read]; ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116 [as read]) gives vṛddhi of the penultimate; by suffix accent. dasamānaḥ — root dasu upakṣaye; śānac in the sense of laṭ; by vyatyaya the śyan does not occur; āne muk (Pā. 7-2-82 [as read]) gives muk; since lasārvadhātuka is anudātta by the sūtra tāsyanudāttenṅidvidupadeśāt…, the root's accent remains. īṭṭe — root īḍa stutau; adādi; laṭ third person singular, ta; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. 3-4-79 [as read]) gives e for ṭi; ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. 2-4-72 [as read]) gives luk of śap; kharica gives ṭa for ḍa; nighāta after a tiṅanta. pāsi — pā rakṣaṇe; laṭ second person singular; tiṅ-final, nighāta. dharmaṇā — dhṛṅ dhāraṇe; the Uṇādi suffix manin; guṇa of the final ṛ; since the suffix is nit, ādyudātta; instrumental singular. asuryāt — asura; yat in the sense of relation; yasyeti ca drops the a; tit svaritam (Pā. 6-1-185 [as read]) gives the svarita accent. ‖ 5 ‖

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

त्वं नो वायवेषामपूर्व्यः सोमानां प्रथमः पीतिमर्हसि सुतानां पीतिमर्हसि । उतो विहुत्मतीनां विशां ववर्जुषीणाम् । विश्वा इत्ते धेनवो दुह्र आशिरं घृतं दुह्रत आशिरम् ॥ ६ ॥

tvaṃ no vāyaveṣāmapūrvyaḥ somānāṃ prathamaḥ pītimarhasi sutānāṃ pītimarhasi | uto vihutmatīnāṃ viśāṃ vavarjuṣīṇām | viśvā itte dhenavo duhra āśiraṃ ghṛtaṃ duhrata āśiram ‖ 6 ‖

original p. 602

॥ पदपाठः ॥

त्वम् । नः । वायो इति । एषाम् । अपूर्व्यः । सोमानाम् । प्रथमः । पीतिम् । अर्हसि । सुतानाम् । पीतिम् । अर्हसि । उतो इति । विहुत्मतीनाम् । विशाम् । ववर्जुषीणाम् । विश्वाः । इत् । ते । धेनवः । दुह्रे । आशिरम् । घृतम् । दुह्रते । आशिरम् ॥ ६ ॥

tvam | naḥ | vāyo iti | eṣām | apūrvyaḥ | somānām | prathamaḥ | pītim | arhasi | sutānām | pītim | arhasi | uto iti | vihutmatīnām | viśām | vavarjuṣīṇām | viśvāḥ | it | te | dhenavaḥ | duhre | āśiram | ghṛtam | duhrate | āśiram ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 6; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "O Vāyu, you are apūrvya: that from which nothing is earlier is apūrva, a station; he who deserves it is apūrvya. Such, and for that very reason prathamaḥ — being before the other gods — you deserve (arhasi, you obtain) the drinking (pīti) of the somas; the drinking of the pressed (sutānām) Soma-juices you deserve — wherever there is pressing, everywhere you drink by rule: this is the meaning. Previously this was said with the idea of priority; now, to make known that at every Soma-rite your drinking occurs, it is stated separately. Not merely the drinking of Soma: uto, but also [you accept the oblation] of the vihutmatīnām — those offering specially, or invoking — and vavarjuṣīṇām — those who avoid unwanted sin — of the people (viśām), the sacrificers and priests. Or: of those sacrificers, all the cows viśvā id dhenavaḥ yield for you — they themselves milk (duhre) — milk, the āśira (mixing material); and also ghee is milked (duhrate), as material for spreading and pouring etc." Grammatical details of vavarjuṣīṇām and duhre are partly doubtful [?].

हे वायो त्वमपूर्व्यः । न विद्यते पूर्वं यस्मात् तत्स्थानमपूर्वम् । तदर्हतीत्यपूर्व्यः । तादृशः अत एव प्रथमः इतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वभूतः सन् सोमानां पीतिं पानमर्हसि । प्राप्नोषि । सुतानामभिषवकृतानां सोमानां पीतिं पानमर्हसि । यत्र यत्राभिषवोऽस्ति तत्र सर्वत्र नियमेन पिबसीत्यर्थः । पूर्वं प्राथम्याभिप्रायेण इदानीं तु सर्वत्र सोमवति योगेऽस्य पानमस्तीति ज्ञापयितुं पृथगभिधानम् । न केवलं सोमपानमात्रम् । उतो अपि तु विहुत्मतीनां विशेषेण होमवतीनामाह्वानवतीनां वा ॥ जुहोतेः संपदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । ततो मतुब्भीष [?] । ववर्जुषीणामनभिमतपापं वर्जयन्तीनां वर्जयतेर्लिटः क्वसुः जक्षद्वित् [?] । विशामृत्विग्यजमानरूपाणां प्रजानां संबन्धि हविः स्वीकरोषीति शेषः । यद्वा । तेषां यष्ट्णां विश्वा इद्धेनवः सर्वा अपि गावस्ते त्वदर्थमाशिरमाश्रयणद्रव्यं क्षीरं दुह्रे दुहन्ति स्वयमेव ॥ कर्तरि न दुहस्नमामिति यगभावः । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः । बहुलं छन्दसीति रुट् ॥ तथाशिरं घृतमुपस्तरणाभिघारणाद्याश्रयणाय [?] योग्यं करणं द्रव्यं दुह्रते ॥

he vāyo tvamapūrvyaḥ | na vidyate pūrvaṃ yasmāt tatsthānamapūrvam | tadarhatītyapūrvyaḥ | tādṛśaḥ ata eva prathamaḥ itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvabhūtaḥ san somānāṃ pītiṃ pānamarhasi | prāpnoṣi | sutānāmabhiṣavakṛtānāṃ somānāṃ pītiṃ pānamarhasi | yatra yatrābhiṣavo 'sti tatra sarvatra niyamena pibasītyarthaḥ | pūrvaṃ prāthamyābhiprāyeṇa idānīṃ tu sarvatra somavati yoge 'sya pānamastīti jñāpayituṃ pṛthagabhidhānam | na kevalaṃ somapānamātram | uto api tu vihutmatīnāṃ viśeṣeṇa homavatīnāmāhvānavatīnāṃ vā ‖ juhoteḥ saṃpadādilakṣaṇo bhāve kvip | tato matubbhīṣa [?] | vavarjuṣīṇāmanabhimatapāpaṃ varjayantīnāṃ varjayaterliṭaḥ kvasuḥ jakṣadvit [?] | viśāmṛtvigyajamānarūpāṇāṃ prajānāṃ saṃbandhi haviḥ svīkaroṣīti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | teṣāṃ yaṣṭṇāṃ viśvā iddhenavaḥ sarvā api gāvaste tvadarthamāśiramāśrayaṇadravyaṃ kṣīraṃ duhre duhanti svayameva ‖ kartari na duhasnamāmiti yagabhāvaḥ | lopasta ātmanepadeṣviti talopaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti ruṭ ‖ tathāśiraṃ ghṛtamupastaraṇābhighāraṇādyāśrayaṇāya [?] yogyaṃ karaṇaṃ dravyaṃ duhrate ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he) vāyo — O Vāyu; tvam — you; apūrvyaḥ — (in the drinking of Soma-juice) one with no one before him; (ata eva — for that very reason; prathamaḥ — (before the other deities) the first; naḥ — our; eṣām — these (placed before); somānām — of the Soma-juices (in the various vessels); pītim — the drinking; arhasi — are fit for; sutānām — of those pressed (all Soma-juices); pītim — the drinking; arhasi — are fit for; uto — and; vihutmatīnām — those who specially have soma-offerings (those having invocations of praise);

original p. 603

Pratipadārtha continued: vavarjuṣīṇām — (those who wish to give up unwanted sin) and viśām — of priests and of the sacrificers (their offerings you accept) [or: vihutmatīnām — those having special Soma-offerings; vavarjuṣīṇām — wishing to abandon unwanted sin; viśām — of the priests and the like]; viśvāḥ it dhenavaḥ — all cows; te — for you; āśiram — milk; duhre — milk (of themselves); — and; āśiram — [a substance] fit for pouring [as an abhighāraṇa]; ghṛtam — ghee; duhrate — milk.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, [in the drinking of Soma] you are the first fit one: therefore you are worthy to drink first, before the other deities, these Soma-juices of ours; at all the Soma-pressings you are the first to drink; and you accept the Soma-offerings of those priests and others who desire to give up sin; all their cows milk the milk and the ghee for you alone.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "You, Vayu, who are preceded by none, are entitled to drink first of these our libations: you are entitled to drink of the effused (juices), moreover, (of all) oblations and sin-offerings of men: for you, their cattle yield milk; (for you) they yield butter."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).

tvam apūrvyaḥ prathamaḥ somānāṃ pītim arhasi — "In drinking Soma, no one before you; you are the first of all" — this indicates an old story. That Vāyu drinks before all is said in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa in this way: Read from the image; the text of this small-type Brāhmaṇa passage is partly doubtful [?]. Sense: "The gods, for the first drinking of King Soma, could not agree, each desiring 'May I drink first, may I drink first.' Not reaching agreement they said: 'Let us run a race (āji); whoever of us wins will drink Soma first.' 'So be it.' They ran the race; of them, as they set out, Vāyu was first at the goal (mukham); then Indra; then Mitra and Varuṇa; then the Aśvins." The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa passage, concluded; read from the image, partly doubtful [?].

देवा वै सोमस्य राज्ञोऽग्रपेयेन न समपादयन्नहं प्रथमः पिबेयमहं प्रथमः पिबेयमित्येवाकामयन्त । ते संपादयन्तोऽब्रुवन्नन्तां [?] आजिमयाम । स यो न उज्जेष्यति स प्रथमः सोमस्य पास्यतीति । तथेति । स आजिमयुस्तेषामाजिं यतामभिसृष्टानां वायुर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यताथेन्द्रोऽथ मित्रावरुणावथाश्विनौ ।

devā vai somasya rājño 'grapeyena na samapādayann ahaṃ prathamaḥ pibeyam ahaṃ prathamaḥ pibeyam ity evākāmayanta | te saṃpādayanto 'bruvann [?] ājimayāma | sa yo na ujjeṣyati sa prathamaḥ somasya pāsyatīti | tatheti | sa ājimayus teṣām ājiṃ yatām abhisṛṣṭānāṃ vāyur mukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyatātha indro 'tha mitrāvaruṇāv athāśvinau |

original p. 604

सोऽवेदिन्द्रो वायुमुपैव जयेतीति तमनु पराप [?] पतत्तमाह नावभोज्जयावेति स नेत्यब्रवीदहमेवोज्जेष्यामीति तृतीयं मेऽभोज्जयावेति नेत्यब्रवीदहमेवोज्जेष्यामीति तुरीयं मेऽभोज्जयावेति तथेति तं तुरीये त्यार्जत तत्तुरीयभागीन्द्रो भवत्रिभाग्यायुः [?] ॥

so 'vedindro vāyum upaiva jayeti iti tam anu parāpa [?] patat tam āha nāvabhojjayāveti sa nety abravīd aham evojjeṣyāmīti tṛtīyaṃ me 'bhojjayāveti nety abravīd aham evojjeṣyāmīti turīyaṃ me 'bhojjayāveti tatheti taṃ turīye tyārjata tat turīyabhāgīndro bhavatribhāgyāyuḥ [?] ‖

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೧" [?].) Sense, as the Kannada explains: In the matter of who among all the gods should first drink Soma, there was first a dispute: each wanted to drink first, out of eagerness. Then all together came to an agreement: let a race be arranged, and whoever wins, to him the first drinking of Soma shall belong; all agreed. In the race Vāyu was ahead of all and took hold of the first place. Then Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and the Aśvins, one after another, joined. Seeing Vāyu win, Indra, in his eagerness to win, fell into Vāyu's side at the end. Then, addressing Vāyu: "'We two have come together; therefore let us two share in victory.' Vāyu said: 'No; I shall win alone, to get the first place.' Then Indra said: 'Give me at least the third place'; Vāyu did not agree even to that. At last, when Indra said 'Give me at least the fourth place', Vāyu agreed. Then Vāyu got the first and the third place, and Indra the fourth place." [Sic as the Kannada gives it; the Brāhmaṇa text above is doubtful in places.] In the present Ṛk, in the context of the drinking of Soma, pointing to the matter of the first place that Vāyu won, [the poet] has said "tvaṃ prathamaḥ somānāṃ pītim arhasi".

apūrvyaḥ — na vidyate pūrvaṃ yasmāt tatsthānam apūrvaṃ tad arhatīty apūrvyaḥ — "one who has none before him": it means that no one has any authority to drink Soma before Vāyu.

pūrvaṃ prāthamyābhiprāyeṇa idānīṃ tu sarvatra somavati yoge 'sya pānam astīti jñāpayituṃ pṛthag abhidhānam — "before, the drinking of Soma at the Soma-sacrifices was said of the first place; now, 'you deserve the drinking (pītim arhasi)' — the word is repeated [i.e. the repetition shows] that the first place belongs to Vāyu at all Soma-sacrifices." In the drinking of the Soma-juice there is also the acceptance of the oblations of the vihutmatīs and the vavarjuṣīs — he has to be understood as worthy of that.

vihutmatīnām — viśeṣeṇa homavatīnām; āhvānavatīnāṃ vā — "of those that specially have oblations, or those that have invocations". It is an adjective of the word viśām, in the clause viśāṃ prajānām.

original p. 605

vavarjuṣīṇām — anabhimatapāpaṃ varjayantīnām: "those who wish to remove sin, they who give up what is not desired". It is the epithet of the word viśām. By these epithets it is shown that eagerness to obtain the gods' favour, and the desire to be free of sin, as the means of obtaining purity, are the effort of the worshippers.

āśiram — āśīrāśrayaṇād vā āśrapaṇād vā (Ni. 6-[?], as read "೬-೯" [?]) — the word āśira is formed from the root śrī with the prefix ā, giving "mixing, mingling"; or from the root śrā with the prefix ā, giving the meaning "to cook finely". Three kinds of āśira — dadhyāśira, gavāśira, yavāśira — have been described before. In the present passage this word indicates the pouring of milk, mixed with Soma-juice. For this the cows are said to yield milk.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). apūrvyaḥ — pūrvam arhati pūrvyaḥ; yat in the sense of arha; ñañ-tatpuruṣa; tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ (Pā. 6-2-2 [as read]) gives the earlier member, an indeclinable, its own accent. pītim — root pā pāne; ktin in the sense of state; ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali (Pā. 6-4-66 [as read]) gives ī for the ā of the root. arhasi — root arha pūjāyām; bhvādi; laṭ second person singular; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. sutānām — root ṣuñ abhiṣave; niṣṭhā (Pā. 3-2-102 [as read]) gives kta; the suffix's accent; genitive plural. vihutmatīnām — vi a prefix; root hu dānādanayoḥ; saṃpadādibhyaḥ kvip (Pā. 3-3-108 [as read]) gives kvip in the sense of state; hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk (Pā. 6-1-71 [as read]) gives the tuk augment; when vihut asyāsti is analysed, matup; in the feminine, ugitaś ca (Pā. 4-1-6 [as read]) gives ṅīp; as both suffixes are pit, the accent of the root remains; in the prādi compound, kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara. viśām — genitive plural; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending.

original p. 606

Grammar of Ṛk 6, concluded. vavarjuṣīṇām — root vṛjī varjane; by Vedic usage liṭ comes, and for it kvasu by bhāṣāyāṃ sadavasaśruvaḥ [as read] (Pā. 3-2-107 [as read]); the root is doubled (dvirvacana); in the feminine, ṅīp by ugitaś ca; since it has the term bha, saṃprasāraṇa occurs, in the earlier member; guṇa by vyatyaya; the accent of kvasu remains; genitive plural. duhre — root duha prapūraṇe; laṭ in the karmakartṛ [reflexive-passive]; because of the sense karmavat, the Ātmanepada suffix comes; na duhasnamām (Pā. 3-1-89 [as read]) prevents yak; in the singular, the suffix ta; lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (Pā. 7-1-41 [as read]) drops the t; ṭita e; by bahulaṃ chandasi the ruṭ augment; the form duhre; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. In duhrate the suffix is plural. ‖ 6 ‖

Here ends the 134th Sūkta. Kannada closing line: "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮುಗಿದುದು".

Sūkta 135 — stīrṇaṃ barhiḥ (begins on printed p. 606; Anuvāka 20, second Sūkta)

ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತೈದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra mūvattaidaneya sūktavu (the one hundred and thirty-fifth Sūkta).

॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; doubtful letters [?]).

स्तीर्णं बर्हिरिति नवर्चं सूक्तं पारुच्छेपमात्यष्टं । पूर्वत्र कुशब्दाद्वायुदेवत्यं । आ वां रथ इत्याद्यैः पञ्चकमैन्द्रं । सप्तम्यष्टमावश्वी [?] । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । स्तीर्णं नव चतुर्थ्याद्याः पञ्चैन्द्र्योऽन्त्ये अष्टी इति । सूक्तस्य विशेषविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः । दशरात्रस्य षष्ठेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्र आद्यौ तृचौ पाकस्थयोर्वायव्यैन्द्रवायव्ययोः स्थाने विनियुक्तौ । षष्ठस्य प्रातःसवन इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । स्तीर्णं बर्हिरिति तृचौ । आ. ८-१ [?] इति ॥

stīrṇaṃ barhir iti navarcaṃ sūktaṃ pārucchepam ātyaṣṭaṃ | pūrvatra kuśabdād vāyudevatyaṃ | ā vāṃ ratha ity ādyaiḥ pañcakam aindraṃ | saptamyaṣṭamāv aśvī [?] | atrānukramaṇikā | stīrṇaṃ nava caturthyādyāḥ pañcaindryo 'ntye aṣṭī iti | sūktasya viśeṣaviniyogo laiṅgikaḥ | daśarātrasya ṣaṣṭhe 'hani prauga-śastra ādyau tṛcau pākasthayor vāyavyaindravāyavyayoḥ sthāne viniyuktau | ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavana iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | stīrṇaṃ barhir iti tṛcau | ā. 8-1 [?] iti ‖

Kannada anuvāda (translated). Anuvāda — This Sūkta stīrṇaṃ barhiḥ is the second Sūkta in the twentieth Anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. The ṛṣi is Paruccheṣa; as said before, the deity of the first three [?] ṛks is Vāyu; the five beginning with ā vāṃ rathaḥ [Ṛks 4–8] have Indra as deity; the rest are Vāyu's. The metre is Atyaṣṭi; the seventh and eighth ṛks [as read] are of the Aṣṭi metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "stīrṇaṃ nava caturthyādyāḥ pañcaindryo 'ntye aṣṭī". The special use of this Sūkta is laiṅgika. On the sixth day of the daśarātra, in the prauga-śastra, the first two tṛcas [of this Sūkta] are to be used in place of the vāyavya and aindravāyavya [mantras] of the pāka [?]; this is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrautasūtra in the section called "ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavane", by the sūtra "stīrṇaṃ barhir iti tṛcau" (Āś. [refs] [?]).

ಸೂಕ್ತ — Sūkta 135 [as read]. Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 20; Sūkta 135. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24, 25 [as read, [?]]. Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 9. Ṛṣi — Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi. Devatā — 1–3 and 9 Vāyu; 4–8 Indra [as printed]. Chandas — 1–7 Atyaṣṭi; 8, 9 Aṣṭi [as printed]. Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].

original p. 607

Rik 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स्तीर्णं बर्हिरुप नो याहि वीतये सहस्रेण नियुता नियुत्वते शतिनीभिर्नियुत्वते । तुभ्यं हि पूर्वपीतये देवा देवाय येमिरे । प्र ते सुतासो मधुमन्तो अस्थिरन्मदाय क्रत्वे अस्थिरन् ॥ १ ॥

stīrṇaṃ barhirupa no yāhi vītaye sahasreṇa niyutā niyutvate śatinībhirniyutvate | tubhyaṃ hi pūrvapītaye devā devāya yemire | pra te sutāso madhumanto asthiranmadāya kratve asthiran ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

स्तीर्णम् । बर्हिः । उप । नः । याहि । वीतये । सहस्रेण । नियुता । नियुत्वते । शतिनीभिः । नियुत्वते । तुभ्यम् । हि । पूर्वऽपीतये । देवाः । देवाय । येमिरे । प्र । ते । सुतासः । मधुऽमन्तः । अस्थिरन् । मदाय । क्रत्वे । अस्थिरन् ॥ १ ॥

stīrṇam | barhiḥ | upa | naḥ | yāhi | vītaye | sahasreṇa | niyutā | niyutvate | śatinībhiḥ | niyutvate | tubhyam | hi | pūrva 'pītaye | devāḥ | devāya | yemire | pra | te | sutāsaḥ | madhu 'mantaḥ | asthiran | madāya | kratve | asthiran ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 1; read from the image; begins p. 607, continues p. 608. Sense so far: "O Vāyu, for our sacrifice come to the strewn barhis, for the vīti — the eating of oblations. By what means? By sahasreṇa niyutā — by a thousand niyuts (the singular in the generic sense). Niyut is a name of the horses of Vāyu: niyuto vāyoḥ — as the Nirukta has it (Nai. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೫" [?]); and śatinībhiḥ — with the hundreds of niyuts: come [so]." The passage continues on p. 608. Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 135" [as read]. Bhāṣya of Ṛk 1, concluded; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

हे वायो नोऽस्मद्यज्ञार्थं स्तीर्णमास्तृतं बर्हिरभिलक्ष्य उप याहि । आगच्छ । किमर्थं । वीतये हविषां भक्षणाय । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । सहस्रेण सहस्रसंख्याकेन नियुता जातावेकवचनम् । नियुत इति वायोरश्वानां नामधेयं नियुतो वायोरिति निरुक्तत्वात् । नै. १-१५ [?] । तथा शतिनीभिः शतसंख्योपेताभिर्नियुद्भिरागच्छेति शेषः । यद्वा । सहस्रेण नियुता शतिनीभिश्च नियुद्भिर्नियुत्वते [?] तद्वते …

he vāyo no 'smadyajñārthaṃ stīrṇamāstṛtaṃ barhirabhilakṣya upa yāhi | āgaccha | kimarthaṃ | vītaye haviṣāṃ bhakṣaṇāya | kena sādhaneneti taducyate | sahasreṇa sahasrasaṃkhyākena niyutā jātāvekavacanam | niyuta iti vāyoraśvānāṃ nāmadheyaṃ niyuto vāyoriti niruktatvāt | nai. 1-15 [?] | tathā śatinībhiḥ śatasaṃkhyopetābhirniyudbhirāgaccheti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | sahasreṇa niyutā śatinībhiśca niyudbhirniyutvate [?] tadvate …

original p. 608

देवाय हविर्दीयत इति शेषः । यद्वा । तुभ्यमित्यनेन संबन्धः । उक्तसंख्याकाभिर्नियुद्भिस्तद्वते देवाय द्योतमानाय तुभ्यं । जयि च । पा. ६-१-२०३ [?] । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । पूर्वपीतये इतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वं पानाय देवा येमिरे । यमितवन्तः । यद्वा । स्तोतार ऋत्विजो देवाय तुभ्यं येमिरे । आहवनीयं प्रति सोमं नियमितवन्तः । अग्रं पिबा मधूनां सुतं वायो । ऋ. ४-४६-१ [?] इत्यादिमन्त्रान्तरप्रसिद्धयोतनार्थो हिशब्दः । किंच ते त्वदर्थं सुतासोऽभिषुता मधुमन्तो माधुर्योपेताः सोमा मदाय तव मदायास्थिरन् तिष्ठन्ति । किंच क्रत्वे कर्मणे तत्सिद्ध्यर्थमस्थिरन् । ऋत्विग्भिर्धृतास्तिष्ठन्ति । अतस्त्वं पिबेति शेषः ॥ तिष्ठतेश्छान्दसे लुजा [?] व्यत्ययेन ऋषि [?] …

devāya havirdīyata iti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | tubhyamityanena saṃbandhaḥ | uktasaṃkhyākābhirniyudbhistadvate devāya dyotamānāya tubhyaṃ | jayi ca | pā. 6-1-203 [?] | ityādyudāttatvaṃ | pūrvapītaye itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ pānāya devā yemire | yamitavantaḥ | yadvā | stotāra ṛtvijo devāya tubhyaṃ yemire | āhavanīyaṃ prati somaṃ niyamitavantaḥ | agraṃ pibā madhūnāṃ sutaṃ vāyo | ṛ. 4-46-1 [?] ityādimantrāntaraprasiddhayotanārtho hiśabdaḥ | kiṃca te tvadarthaṃ sutāso 'bhiṣutā madhumanto mādhuryopetāḥ somā madāya tava madāyāsthiran tiṣṭhanti | kiṃca kratve karmaṇe tatsiddhyarthamasthiran | ṛtvigbhirdhṛtāstiṣṭhanti | atastvaṃ pibeti śeṣaḥ ‖ tiṣṭhateśchāndase lujā [?] vyatyayena ṛṣi [?] …

Sense of this part: "[Understood:] to the god the oblation is given. Or: connect with tubhyam — to you the god who has the niyuts of the stated number, the shining god. [jayi ca (Pā. 6-1-203 [as read]) gives the ādyudātta.] Pūrvapītaye — for the drinking before the other gods the gods have restrained (yemire, held back); or: the praisers, the priests, held back the Soma for you, the god, towards the āhavanīya — as in the other mantra, agraṃ pibā madhūnāṃ sutaṃ vāyo (Ṛ. 4-46-1 [as read, [?]]), whose illustration is the purpose of the word hi. And further, for you the pressed (sutāsaḥ), honeyed (madhumantaḥ) Soma-juices asthiran: stand for your joy; and for the rite (kratu) they stand, held by the priests, for its accomplishment. So — [you] drink." The last remarks of grammar on asthiran are partly doubtful [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he) vāyo — O Vāyu; niyutvate — you who have the horses called niyut (for you, who are ready); vītaye — to receive the oblations; sahasreṇa — by a thousand; niyutā — horses (accompanied by); naḥ — our; stīrṇam — spread; barhiḥ — the darbha seat; upa yāhi — come near; niyutvate — to you who have horses niyut (who are ready to accept the oblations); śatinībhiḥ — by hundreds in number (accompanied by horses); (barhiḥ upa yāhi — come near to the darbha seat; devāḥ — the gods; devāya — to the shining; tubhyam — you; pūrvapītaye — for first drinking; yemire hi — have indeed made a rule; [or: devāḥ — the praising priests; devāya tubhyam — for you, the shining one; pūrvapītaye — for first drinking; yemire hi — have indeed offered (restrained) Soma towards the āhavanīya;] kiṃca — and; sutāsaḥ — for you pressed (and); madhumantaḥ — possessed of sweetness (these Soma-juices); te — your; madāya — for joy; pra asthiran — are ready; and kratve — for the rite of sacrifice; asthiran — are ready.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, who possess the horses called niyut — to receive the oblations, [prepared] for you — come with thousands of horses to the darbha seat we have prepared; come with hundreds of horses to the seat; all the gods have laid down that you drink first; this Soma-juice, pressed by us and endowed with sweetness, is ready to satisfy you and for the accomplishment of the sacrificial act.

original p. 609

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Approach our strewn grass, Vayu, with (your) thousand steeds, to partake of the (offered) food (prepared) for the lord of the steeds; (approach) with hundreds (to the sacrifice prepared) for the lord of the steeds: the gods hold back for you as the deity (entitled) first to drink (the libation): sweet effused juices are ready for your exhilaration: are ready for their function."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).

In this Sūkta the first three Ṛks belong to the prauga-śastra. The prauga-śastra has great importance. It is the means of [obtaining] food. In this context, one must first know the nature of the prauga-śastra with Vāyu as deity, and then how Vāyu comes to have the first drinking in the Ṛks in question, and why.

अन्नाद्यं वा एतेनावरुन्धे यत्प्रउगमन्यान्या देवता प्रउगे शस्यन्तेऽन्यदुक्थं प्रउगे क्रियते । एतद्वै यजमानस्याध्यात्मकमिवोक्थं यत्प्रउगं तस्मादेनमेतदुपेक्ष्यकमिवेत्याहुरेतेन ह्येनं होता संस्करोतीति ॥

annādyaṃ vā etenāvarundhe yat praugam anyānyā devatā prauge śasyante 'nyad ukthaṃ prauge kriyate | etad vai yajamānasyādhyātmakam ivokthaṃ yat praugaṃ tasmād enam etad upekṣyakam ivety āhur etena hy enaṃ hotā saṃskarotīti ‖

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೨" [?]; read from the image, partly doubtful [?].) By the recitation of the prauga-śastra the sacrificer gets food; for the sacrificer this śastra is [very] close to him; therefore the sacrificer must give the utmost wakefulness of attention to the pronunciation and recitation of others. By its recitation the body of the sacrificer becomes sacred, thus the general power of this mantra may be understood; then the power of the śastra of Vāyu:

वायव्यं शंसति तस्मादाहुर्वायुः प्राणः प्राणो रेतो रेतः पुरुषस्य प्रथमं संभवतः संभवतीति यद्वायव्यं शंसति प्राणमेवास्य तत्संस्करोति ।

vāyavyaṃ śaṃsati tasmād āhur vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇo reto retaḥ puruṣasya prathamaṃ saṃbhavataḥ saṃbhavatīti yad vāyavyaṃ śaṃsati prāṇam evāsya tat saṃskaroti |

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೨" [?].) Vāyu is prāṇa (breath) and prāṇa is retas (seed): before a man is born, seed is produced first. Therefore, by reciting this vāyavya triple verse, which is of the nature of prāṇa and of retas, the prāṇa of the sacrificer becomes firm.

original p. 610

Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued: But what is Vāyu's right of first drinking? There are two reasons for that. First: Agni receives the oblations before all the gods. But for that [Agni's] priority, the help of Vāyu is required: as Agni is Vāyu's offspring and has Vāyu's help, the birth of Agni itself takes place in the sacrificial house.

वायोरग्निर्जायते प्राणाद्धि बलान्मथ्यमानोऽधिजायते ।

vāyor agnir jāyate prāṇād dhi balān mathyamāno 'dhijāyate |

(Ai. Brā. [?]-[?], as read "೩-೩೫" [?].) Also:

स यदग्निः प्रवानिव दहति तदस्य वायव्यं रूपं तदस्य तेनानुसंशंसति ।

sa yad agniḥ pravān iva dahati tad asya vāyavyaṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānusaṃśaṃsati |

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೪" [?].) When Agni, kindled by flames, burns, he is in the form of Vāyu; thus Agni is identical with Vāyu. Therefore the first oblations that Agni gets also join Vāyu. Second:

अग्निः सुषमिदिति शंसति वायुर्वा अग्निः सुषमिद्वायुर्हि स्वयमात्मानं समिन्धे स्वयमिदं सर्वं यदिदं किंच वायुमेव तदन्तरिक्षलोक आयातयति ॥

agniḥ suṣamid iti śaṃsati vāyur vā agniḥ suṣamid vāyur hi svayam ātmānaṃ samindhe svayam idaṃ sarvaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca vāyum eva tad antarikṣaloka āyātayati ‖

The blazing Agni is Vāyu. Vāyu kindles himself and can [also] make the whole world blaze.

तूर्णिर्हव्यवाळिति शंसति वायुर्वै तूर्णिर्हव्यवाड्वायुर्हीदं सर्वं सद्यस्तरति यदिदं किंच वायुर्देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहति वायुमेव तदन्तरिक्षलोक आयातयति ।

tūrṇir havyavāḍ iti śaṃsati vāyur vai tūrṇir havyavāḍ vāyur hīdaṃ sarvaṃ sadyas tarati yad idaṃ kiṃca vāyur devebhyo havyaṃ vahati vāyum eva tad antarikṣaloka āyātayati |

He carries the oblations with speed. Moving through the whole universe in a moment, he distributes the oblations to all the gods.

प्रणीर्यज्ञानामिति शंसति वायुर्वै प्रणीर्यज्ञानां यदा हि प्राणित्यथ यज्ञोऽथाग्निहोत्रं वायुमेव तदन्तरिक्षलोक आयातयति ॥

praṇīr yajñānām iti śaṃsati vāyur vai praṇīr yajñānāṃ yadā hi prāṇity atha yajño 'thāgnihotraṃ vāyum eva tad antarikṣaloka āyātayati ‖

Vāyu is the giver of life to the sacrifice. The sacrifice of Vāyu is sustained by the power of the breath; therefore the Agnihotra too becomes possible. And so —

सो अध्वरा करति जातवेदा इति शंसति वायुर्वै जातवेदा वायुर्हीदं सर्वं करोति यदिदं किंच वायुमेव तदन्तरिक्षलोक आयातयति ॥

so adhvarā karati jātavedā iti śaṃsati vāyur vai jātavedā vāyur hīdaṃ sarvaṃ karoti yad idaṃ kiṃca vāyum eva tad antarikṣaloka āyātayati ‖

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೪" [?]; these Brāhmaṇa passages, in small type, are read from the image and are partly doubtful [?].) Vāyuve jātavedas (the all-knowing), "the one who has produced the whole universe", and so on: the nature of Vāyu is praised. Since Vāyu is the original cause of Agni, and since Agni is the chief helper in distributing the oblations to the gods,

original p. 611

…and since Vāyu is stated to be identical with Agni, the position of Vāyu is that it must be the first — [higher] than the right of first drinking that belongs to Agni: this point is indicated here.

devāḥ yemire — two kinds of construction are made for this. The first: "the gods fix [a rule]". As explained before, in the contest Vāyu won first; since he has the right to drink first, before all the gods, the gods themselves fixed this place for Vāyu. The second: taking the word devāḥ as "the shining priests", it is also explained that the sacrificial priests, who are the praisers, have prepared the Soma-juice towards the āhavanīya fire for your first drinking, you who are the deity of the priests.

kratve — the word kratu is found among the names of karman (action) (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೧" [?]), and among the names of prajñā (understanding) (Ni. 3-[?], as read "೩-೯" [?]). This word is used in many senses — action, wisdom, resolve, power — but in both [lists] karma and prajñā are chiefly current. In the Ṛk before us, for kratve it is explained as karmaṇe tatsiddhyartham — "for the accomplishment of the action".

asthiran — ṛtvigbhir dhṛtās tiṣṭhanti — "the Soma-juices stand held by the priests for the sake of the action": "the priests, taking the Soma-juice, stand ready to offer it for your drinking" is the meaning.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). stīrṇam — root stṛñ ācchādane; kta suffix; ṛta iddhātoḥ (Pā. 7-1-100 [as read]) gives i; hali ca (Pā. 8-2-77 [as read]) gives the long vowel; radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ pūrvasya ca daḥ (Pā. 8-2-42 [as read]) gives niṣṭhā's t the na; raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade gives ṇa; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. yāhi — root yā prāpaṇe; loṭ, second person singular; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. vītaye — root vī gatiprajanakāntyasanakhādaneṣu; for it mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ (Pā. 3-3-96 [as read]) gives ktin, udātta; dative singular. niyutā — niyut is the name of Vāyu's horses; since it is a generic indicator, the singular occurs; instrumental. śatinībhiḥ — ata iniṭhanau (Pā. 5-2-115 [as read]) gives the suffix ini in the sense of matup; since it ends in a, in the feminine ṅīp.

original p. 612

Grammar of Ṛk 1, continued. tubhyam — dative, of the yuṣmad [stem]; jayi ca (Pā. 6-1-[?], as read "೬-೧-೩೫" [?]) gives the ādyudātta. yemire — root yama uparame; liṭ third person plural; hi ca (Pā. 8-1-34 [as read]) prevents the nighāta accent; as the suffix has the c-marker [cit], cita (Pā. 6-1-163 [as read]) gives the final udātta. sutāsaḥ — root ṣuñ abhiṣave; ādi: sa [for ṣa]; in the passive, niṣṭhā gives kta; since jas follows, ājjaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50 [as read]) gives the asuk augment. asthiran — root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ [as read] luk [i.e. luṅ by Vedic usage]; vyatyayo bahulam gives ran for the suffix; sic by sicā… [for luṅ]; sthāghvor ic ca (Pā. 1-2-17 [as read]) gives kittva [of sic] and itva to the root; since a short vowel follows, hrasvād aṅgāt (Pā. 8-2-27 [as read]) drops the s of sic; the āgama of the aṅga; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. kratve — the word kratu denotes action; as the dative singular follows, by the statement jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam, guṇa and the like are optional [?]; the yaṇ-substitution. ‖ 1 ‖

Rik 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तुभ्यायं सोमः परिपूतो अद्रिभिः स्पार्हा वसानः परि कोशमर्षति शुक्रा वसानो अर्षति । तवायं भाग आयुषु सोमो देवेषु हूयते । वह वायो नियुतो याह्यस्मयुर्जुषाणो याह्यस्मयुः ॥ २ ॥

tubhyāyaṃ somaḥ paripūto adribhiḥ spārhā vasānaḥ pari kośamarṣati śukrā vasāno arṣati | tavāyaṃ bhāga āyuṣu somo deveṣu hūyate | vaha vāyo niyuto yāhyasmayurjuṣāṇo yāhyasmayuḥ ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 613

॥ पदपाठः ॥ The Pada prints "tubhya" with short final, as in the Saṃhitā "tubhyāyam"; recorded as printed.

तुभ्य । अयम् । सोमः । परिऽपूतः । अद्रिऽभिः । स्पार्हा । वसानः । परि । कोशम् । अर्षति । शुक्रा । वसानः । अर्षति । तव । अयम् । भागः । आयुषु । सोमः । देवेषु । हूयते । वह । वायो इति । नियुतः । याहि । अस्मयुः । जुषाणः । याहि । अस्मयुः ॥ २ ॥

tubhya | ayam | somaḥ | pari 'pūtaḥ | adri 'bhiḥ | spārhā | vasānaḥ | pari | kośam | arṣati | śukrā | vasānaḥ | arṣati | tava | ayam | bhāgaḥ | āyuṣu | somaḥ | deveṣu | hūyate | vaha | vāyo iti | niyutaḥ | yāhi | asmayuḥ | juṣāṇaḥ | yāhi | asmayuḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 2; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "O Vāyu, tubhya — for you (the dative case-ending elided). This Soma, offered, goes (arṣati) to the kośa — the cup (graha), the container. What kind of Soma? Adribhiḥ paripūtaḥ — purified by the pressing-stones, the instruments of pressing; or purified by the strainer of woollen fringe [daśāpavitra] and the cup. Likewise spārhā vasānaḥ — wearing desirable lustres. And further, wearing pure and bright lustres, the Soma comes to you [ṛṣī gatau; śap by vyatyaya]. O Vāyu, this Soma — your share, that which is to be shared — is offered, among men in the world [?], for you among the gods: since among all the gods the Soma is your share, therefore first to you it is offered. Further, O Vāyu: thus [approach that Soma], desirous of us (asmayuḥ). Bring the niyut horses to the offering; then go to heaven; doing so, joined with us, favouring us, or desiring us, being pleased (juṣāṇaḥ), go." Several words of the commentary here are doubtful [?].

हे वायो तुभ्य तुभ्यं त्वदर्थम् । सुपां सुलुगिति चतुर्थ्या लुक् ॥ अयं सोमो हूयमानः कोशं कोशस्थानीयं ग्रहमर्षति । गच्छति । प्राप्नोति । कीदृशः सोमः । अद्रिभिः परिपूतः । अभिषवसाधनैर्ग्रावभिरुपगतैर्जघ्नत्वेन [?] शोधितः । यद्वा । अद्रिभिरभिषुतो दशापवित्रशोधनेन ग्रहणेन वा शोधितः । तथा स्पार्हा स्पृहणीयानि तेजांसि वसानः । पिदधानः [?] । किंच शुक्रा निर्मलानि दीप्तानि वा तेजांसि वसानः सोमोऽर्षति त्वां प्राप्नोति ॥ ऋषी गतौ । व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥ हे वायो आयुषु मनुष्येषु यज्ञ्वव्यक्त्वेन [?] स्थितो भागो भजनीयः सोमस्तव त्वदर्थं देवेषु मध्ये हूयते । सर्वेषु देवेषु यतः सोमस्तव भागः अतः प्रथमं तुभ्यं हूयत इत्यर्थः । किंच हे वायो एवं तं सोममस्मयुरस्माभिस्त्वद्यार्थान् [?] मत्स्वार्थीयो [?] युः ॥ त्वं नियुतो वह । नियुत्संज्ञकानश्वानाहनाय प्रापय । ततः परं याहि दिवं प्रति गच्छ । तथा कुर्वन् अस्मयुरस्माभिर्युक्तः सन् अस्मानुनुगृह्णन् अस्मान्कामयमानो वा [?] जुषाणः प्रीयमाणो याहि । गच्छ ॥

he vāyo tubhya tubhyaṃ tvadartham | supāṃ sulugiti caturthyā luk ‖ ayaṃ somo hūyamānaḥ kośaṃ kośasthānīyaṃ grahamarṣati | gacchati | prāpnoti | kīdṛśaḥ somaḥ | adribhiḥ paripūtaḥ | abhiṣavasādhanairgrāvabhirupagatairjaghnatvena [?] śodhitaḥ | yadvā | adribhirabhiṣuto daśāpavitraśodhanena grahaṇena vā śodhitaḥ | tathā spārhā spṛhaṇīyāni tejāṃsi vasānaḥ | pidadhānaḥ [?] | kiṃca śukrā nirmalāni dīptāni vā tejāṃsi vasānaḥ somo 'rṣati tvāṃ prāpnoti ‖ ṛṣī gatau | vyatyayena śap ‖ he vāyo āyuṣu manuṣyeṣu yajñvavyaktvena [?] sthito bhāgo bhajanīyaḥ somastava tvadarthaṃ deveṣu madhye hūyate | sarveṣu deveṣu yataḥ somastava bhāgaḥ ataḥ prathamaṃ tubhyaṃ hūyata ityarthaḥ | kiṃca he vāyo evaṃ taṃ somamasmayurasmābhistvadyārthān [?] matsvārthīyo [?] yuḥ ‖ tvaṃ niyuto vaha | niyutsaṃjñakānaśvānāhanāya prāpaya | tataḥ paraṃ yāhi divaṃ prati gaccha | tathā kurvan asmayurasmābhiryuktaḥ san asmānunugṛhṇan asmānkāmayamāno vā [?] juṣāṇaḥ prīyamāṇo yāhi | gaccha ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he) vāyo — O Vāyu; tubhya — for you; adribhiḥ — by the pressing-stones (instruments of pressing); paripūtaḥ — purified; spārhā — desirable (lustres); vasānaḥ — wearing (this Soma-juice); ayam somaḥ — this Soma-juice; kośam — the large vessel that receives the Soma-juice; pari arṣati — reaches; (kiṃca — and; śukrā — pure (bright) [lustres]; vasānaḥ — wearing (the Soma-juice); arṣati — reaches (you); āyuṣu — among men (prepared for the sacrifice); bhāgaḥ — your share; ayam — this; somaḥ — Soma-juice; deveṣu — among the gods; tava — for you; hūyate — is offered; vāyo — O Vāyu; niyutaḥ — the horses called niyut; vaha — bring; asmayuḥ — desiring us; yāhi — come; juṣāṇaḥ — being pleased; asmayuḥ — [and] desiring us (favouring us); yāhi — go.

original p. 614

Pratipadārtha, concluded. …hūyate — is offered (to the homa); he vāyo — O Vāyu; asmayuḥ — joined with us (being favourable to us); tvam — you; niyutaḥ — the horses; vaha — bring (to take the Soma-juice, call them here and come); yāhi — start (afterwards towards heaven); tathā kurvan — so doing; asmayuḥ — joined to us (having a mind of favour to us); juṣāṇaḥ — pleased; yāhi — go.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, for you [everyone] has to desire this pure Soma-juice, purified by the stones (the instruments of pressing); it reaches the proper vessel (the graha); and, shining (with a colour), this Soma reaches you; the Soma-juices prepared among men for your share are offered to you, first among the deities; send the horses to carry it; go [to heaven] accepting it, and with a favourable mind towards us; go, pleased, with a favourable mind towards us.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "For you this Soma juice, purified by the stones (that bruise the plant), and clothed with enviable (splendour), flows to its (appropriate) receptacle; clothed with brilliant (splendour), this Soma is offered as they portion amongst men and amongst gods; (having received it), harness your horses, and depart well affected towards us; gratified, and well disposed towards us, depart."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).

In this Ṛk of the prauga-śastra it is shown that Soma-juice is made ready and purified, the order in which it is offered in the homa, and the prayer addressed to Vāyu to accept it.

adribhiḥ — abhiṣavasādhanaiḥ — "by the stones, the instruments with which Soma is pressed". For this instrument, two words, adri and grāvan, are in use. Although both words have the general meaning "stone", there must be a difference in their nature between the adri and the grāvan as instruments for pressing Soma, and this can be said from their epithets, or from words suggesting sound. Ordinarily, in all places Sāyaṇa explains the word adri as grāvan and the word grāvan as pāṣāṇa ("stone"); but the difference between them is not shown by such a meaning, nor are they to be taken as synonyms; it is understood from the adjectives and similes that tell the nature of those two [objects] and from the words that indicate the sound they make in pressing Soma that the two instruments are different. Babṛhāṇa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?], as read "೪-೫೯-೨" [?]); parvata (1-[?]-[?]); aśramaṇa, aśrathita, amṛtyu, anātura, ajara, amavipsnu (1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೬೪-೧೧" [?]); dhruva, kṣemakāmu (1-[?]-[?]) — all these are epithets that show the specialities of the adri. Likewise pṛthu, pṛthubudhna and the like are epithets that show the speciality of grāvan only. The grāvan is commonly compared with the bull, and the adri with the horse.

अद्रिरादृणात्येतेन । अपि वा अत्तेः स्यात् ॥

adrir ādṛṇāty etena | api vā atteḥ syāt ‖

(Ni. 4-[?], as read "೪-೪" [?].) Adri is formed either from the root dṛ, which gives the sense of "to split", or from the root ad, which gives the sense of "to eat".

This word is used in other senses also, besides "pressing the juice" or "the instrument for it". For example:

उत स्म ते परुष्ण्यामूर्णा वसत शुन्ध्यवः । उत पव्या रथानामद्रिं बिभन्त्योजसा ॥

uta sma te paruṣṇyām ūrṇā vasata śundhyavaḥ | uta pavyā rathānām adriṃ bibhanty ojasā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-52-9 [as read]; the last word of the second line is doubtful: the print has "bindanty" [?].) In this the strength of the chariots of the Maruts is described: by the strength of the wheels of that chariot, mountains are split. When it is so said, the word adri means "cloud, or mountain" — megham girim vā.

original p. 615

ब्रह्माणि मे मतयः शं सुतासः शुष्म इयर्ति प्रभृतो मे अद्रिः । आ शासते प्रति हर्यन्त्युक्थेमा हरी वहतस्ता नो अच्छ ॥

brahmāṇi me matayaḥ śaṃ sutāsaḥ śuṣma iyarti prabhṛto me adriḥ | ā śāsate prati haryanty ukthemā harī vahatas tā no accha ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೧೮೩-೪" [?]; the quotation is doubtful in places [?].) In this, in a speech between Indra and the Maruts, Indra praises the power of his own thunderbolt. Here the word adri means śatrūṇāṃ bhakṣako vajraḥ — "the thunderbolt, the devourer of enemies": that is, the thunderbolt, the weapon that destroys enemies.

बृहस्पतिर्भिनदद्रिं विदद्गाः समुस्रियाभिर्वावशन्त नरः ।

bṛhaspatir bhinad adriṃ vidad gāḥ sam usriyābhir vāvaśanta naraḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-3 [as read].) In Ṛks of this kind the word means "Asura", and:

महः स राय एषते पतिर्दन्निन इनस्य वसुनः पद आ । उप ध्रजन्तमद्रयो विधन्नित् ॥

mahaḥ sa rāya eṣate patir dann ina inasya vasunaḥ pada ā | upa dhrajantam adrayo vidhann it ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-1, as read "೧-೧೮೪-೧" [?]; the quotation is doubtful in several letters [?].)

original p. 616

Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 615: …In Ṛks of this kind, the adri means the pressing-stones; thus the word adri has many meanings, such as "mountain, cloud, Asura (atṛ [?]), devourer, paṇi" and so on. In another context the author of the Nirukta, explaining this word, —

यदिन्द्र चित्र मेहनास्ति त्वादातमद्रिवः । राधस्तन्नो विदद्वस उभयाहस्त्या भर ॥

yad indra citra mehanāsti tvādātam adrivaḥ | rādhas tan no vidadvasa ubhayāhastyā bhara ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-1, as read "೩-೬೪-೧" [?].) — taking this Ṛk, shows how the meaning of adrivaḥ, "O Indra, the possessor of the thunderbolt", is established. As the root of the word adri [or its roots] give different meanings by different derivations, the meaning has to be taken to suit each context. In the present Ṛk: abhiṣavasādhanaiḥ — "by the stones with which the Soma-juice is pressed" (purified) is the meaning.

spārhā — spṛhaṇīyāni tejāṃsi — "lustres that are to be desired": that is, lustres that attract, and so are desired.

kośam — kośaḥ kuṣṇāter vikuṣito bhavati (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೨೬" [?]) — from the root kuṣ, giving the meaning "to draw out what is inside" (antargatasya bahir niṣkarṣaṇam): a large vessel or cup that fills with Soma-juice.

āyuṣu — in general it is said to be "among men", but in many places [the word] is used in the sense "among the men who are the sacrificers": viśām atithiḥ… [as read: viśām atithiś śāru rāyave [?]] (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?], as read "೨-೨-೮" [?]); bhṛgavo viśvapsayoḥ [?] (2-[?]-[?]); uparasyāyoḥ [?] (4-[?]-[?]); cid āyave [?] (4-[?]-[?]) — in all such places, as the commentator says, the word āyus means the sacrificer; so here too it means "among men who are sacrificers". [The word āyu, being a proper-noun-like word, indicates the names of various persons, as is known from those contexts.]

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). tubhya — supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39 [as read]) gives luk of the dative. paripūtaḥ — root pūñ pavane; kta in the passive; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 [as read]) gives the gati (pari) its own accent. spārhā — spṛhāyāḥ imāni spārhāṇi; tasyedam (Pā. 4-3-120 [as read]) gives the suffix aṇ; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ gives vṛddhi of the first vowel; by ra-ending the ādyudātta; in the neuter plural, śeś chandasi bahulam drops śi.

original p. 617

Grammar, continued. vasānaḥ — root vasa ācchādane; adādi; śānac for laṭ; śap is luk; as the root is anudātta in its nature, the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta by tāsyanudāttenṅidvidupadeśāt…, and the accent of the root remains. arṣati — root ṛṣī gatau; laṭ third person singular, tip; by vyatyaya the śap [for tudādi] takes śa; because of it śa, the guṇa of the penultimate; in the tiṅanta, the nighāta accent. śukrā — root śuca śoke; Uṇ. suffix rak; in the neuter plural, śi is luk-ed. āyuṣu — root iṇ gatau; chandasīṇaḥ (Uṇ. 1-[?], as read "೧-೨" [?]) gives uṇ; ācoñciti… gives vṛddhi of the root; āy- āvādeśa; the suffix's final udātta. hūyate — root hu dānādanayoḥ; laṭ in the passive, third person; the suffix ta; e for ṭi; sārvadhātuke yak (Pā. 3-1-67 [as read]) gives yak; akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ (Pā. 7-4-25 [as read]) gives the long vowel of the root; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. vaha — root vaha prāpaṇe; used with the sense of ṇic; loṭ second person singular; as it is at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not occur; śap is anudātta and the root's accent remains. asmayuḥ — asmān ātmana icchati asmayati; supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8 [as read]) gives the suffix kyac; by Vedic usage the final is dropped; kyāc chandasi (Pā. 3-2-170 [as read]) gives u after the kya-ending; ato lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-48 [as read]) drops the a before kya; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. juṣāṇaḥ — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; śānac in the sense of laṭ; by Vedic usage the vikaraṇa is luk; āṅ-kuṭpvāj… gives ṇatva to the n of the suffix; cita (Pā. 6-1-163 [as read]) gives the final udātta. ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 618

Rik 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

आ नो नियुद्भिः शतिनीभिरध्वरं सहस्रिणीभिरुप याहि वीतये वायो हव्यानि वीतये । तवायं भाग ऋत्वियः सरश्मिः सूर्ये सचा । अध्वर्युभिर्भरमाणा अयंसत वायो शुक्रा अयंसत ॥ ३ ॥

ā no niyudbhiḥ śatinībhiradhvaraṃ sahasriṇībhirupa yāhi vītaye vāyo havyāni vītaye | tavāyaṃ bhāga ṛtviyaḥ saraśmiḥ sūrye sacā | adhvaryubhirbharamāṇā ayaṃsata vāyo śukrā ayaṃsata ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

आ । नः । नियुत्ऽभिः । शतिनीभिः । अध्वरम् । सहस्रिणीभिः । उप । याहि । वीतये । वायो इति । हव्यानि । वीतये । तव । अयम् । भागः । ऋत्वियः । सऽरश्मिः । सूर्ये । सचा । अध्वर्युऽभिः । भरमाणाः । अयंसत । वायो इति । शुक्राः । अयंसत ॥ ३ ॥

ā | naḥ | niyut 'bhiḥ | śatinībhiḥ | adhvaram | sahasriṇībhiḥ | upa | yāhi | vītaye | vāyo iti | havyāni | vītaye | tava | ayam | bhāgaḥ | ṛtviyaḥ | sa 'raśmiḥ | sūrye | sacā | adhvaryu 'bhiḥ | bharamāṇāḥ | ayaṃsata | vāyo iti | śukrāḥ | ayaṃsata ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 3; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "O Vāyu, come to our sacrifice (adhvara) with your horses, with the hundreds (śatinībhiḥ niyudbhiḥ) and thousands (sahasriṇībhiḥ), for vīti — for the satisfaction of your desire [?]; having come, for the eating of the oblations — Soma and the rest — come very quickly with hundreds and thousands of horses, for eating them. Further, this share of yours, the Soma, is ṛtviyaḥ — has come to its time, the time for giving. [Here ṛtu indicates the time of giving; ghas by Vedic usage (Pā. 5-1-106 [as read, [?]]), and siti ca (Pā. 1-4-16 [as read]); by the pada-term overriding the bha-term, in the absence of guṇa of o, yaṇ comes.] Further, the Soma, at sunrise, is saraśmiḥ — together with the rays of the Sun: of equal brightness, or accompanied by them; since at sunrise the rays arise, the time has come. And the Soma-juices, borne by the adhvaryus — the camasa-adhvaryus (the plural because they are ten) — ayaṃsata, have been made ready. O Vāyu, those Soma-juices, bright, ayaṃsata: raised extremely shining. Therefore come to consume them."

हे वायो त्वं नोऽध्वरमस्मत्संबन्धिनं यज्ञं शतिनीभिर्नियुद्भिः सहस्रिणीभिश्च ताभिस्त्वदीयैरश्वैर्नोऽस्मदध्वरमुपायाहि । उपागच्छ । किमर्थम् । वीतये त्वदभिमतकामाय [?] । आगत्य च हव्यानि वीतये सोमादिभिर्भक्षणार्थमध्वरं हव्यानि चोपलक्ष्य तेषामेव भक्षणाय शतसहस्रैरश्वैरतिशीघ्रमागच्छेत्यर्थः ॥ किंचायं तव भागो भजनीयः सोम ऋत्वियः प्राप्तकालः प्रदानावसरं प्राप्तः । ऋतुशब्देन प्रदानकालो लक्ष्यते ॥ छन्दसि घस् । पा. ५-१-१०६ [?] । सिति च । पा. १-४-१६ [?] । इति पदसंज्ञया भसंज्ञाया बाधादोर्गुणाभावे यण् ॥ किंच सोमः सूर्य उदिते सति तस्य रश्मिभिः सचा सह सरश्मिर्भवति । समानदीप्तिर्भवति । यद्वा । तैः सहितो भवति । यतः सूर्य उदिते सति रश्मिर्भवति अतः प्राप्तकाल इत्यर्थः ॥ किंच सोमा अध्वर्युभिश्चमसाध्वर्युभिः । तेषां दशत्वाद्बहुवचनं । तैर्भरमाणा भ्रियमाणा अयंसत नियता अभवन् । किंच हे वायो ते सोमाः शुक्रा अयंसत । अत्यन्तदीप्ता उद्यताः । अतस्तेषां भक्षणायागाहीत्यर्थः ॥

he vāyo tvaṃ no 'dhvaramasmatsaṃbandhinaṃ yajñaṃ śatinībhirniyudbhiḥ sahasriṇībhiśca tābhistvadīyairaśvairno 'smadadhvaramupāyāhi | upāgaccha | kimartham | vītaye tvadabhimatakāmāya [?] | āgatya ca havyāni vītaye somādibhirbhakṣaṇārthamadhvaraṃ havyāni copalakṣya teṣāmeva bhakṣaṇāya śatasahasrairaśvairatiśīghramāgacchetyarthaḥ ‖ kiṃcāyaṃ tava bhāgo bhajanīyaḥ soma ṛtviyaḥ prāptakālaḥ pradānāvasaraṃ prāptaḥ | ṛtuśabdena pradānakālo lakṣyate ‖ chandasi ghas | pā. 5-1-106 [?] | siti ca | pā. 1-4-16 [?] | iti padasaṃjñayā bhasaṃjñāyā bādhādorguṇābhāve yaṇ ‖ kiṃca somaḥ sūrya udite sati tasya raśmibhiḥ sacā saha saraśmirbhavati | samānadīptirbhavati | yadvā | taiḥ sahito bhavati | yataḥ sūrya udite sati raśmirbhavati ataḥ prāptakāla ityarthaḥ ‖ kiṃca somā adhvaryubhiścamasādhvaryubhiḥ | teṣāṃ daśatvādbahuvacanaṃ | tairbharamāṇā bhriyamāṇā ayaṃsata niyatā abhavan | kiṃca he vāyo te somāḥ śukrā ayaṃsata | atyantadīptā udyatāḥ | atasteṣāṃ bhakṣaṇāyāgāhītyarthaḥ ‖

original p. 619

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he vāyo — O Vāyu; naḥ — our; adhvaram — to the sacrifice; śatinībhiḥ — by hundreds (accompanied); sahasriṇībhiḥ — by thousands; niyudbhiḥ — with your horses (joined); vītaye — for the satisfaction of desire (and fulfilment) [iṣṭārthapūrti]; upa ā yāhi — come near (having come); havyāni — [Soma and other] oblations; vītaye — to eat (come quickly); ayam — this; tava — your; bhāgaḥ — share, the Soma-juice; ṛtviyaḥ — (for giving) has arrived at the time; kiṃca — and, the Soma-juice; sūrye sacā — when the Sun has risen (with his rays); saraśmiḥ — shining equally (and); somāḥ — Soma-juices (in the various vessels); adhvaryubhiḥ — by the camasa-adhvaryus; bharamāṇāḥ — carried; ayaṃsata — made ready; kiṃca) he vāyo — (and) O Vāyu; (te somāḥ — those Soma-juices; śukrāḥ — extremely clear; ayaṃsata — are ready.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, with hundreds and thousands of your horses come to our sacrifice for the fulfilment of your desire; come to receive the oblations, Soma and the rest; the time has come for your share to be given; after sunrise the Soma is ready, shining with the rays of the sun; borne by the camasa-adhvaryus, [the Soma-juice] (in various vessels) is ready for you; clear [juice] (flowing) is ready.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Come with hundreds and thousands of your steeds to our sacrifice to partake of (the sacrificial) food; (come), Vayu, to partake of the oblations: this is your reasonable portion, and it is radiant along with the sun; the juices borne by the priests are prepared; the pure juices, Vayu, are prepared."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).

The ṛṣi prays Vāyu to be merciful to the sacrifice with his thousands of horses — [saying] that the radiant Soma-juice is ready.

adhvaram — adhvara is the name of the sacrifice: dhvaratir hiṃsākarmā tatpratiṣedhaḥ — "as it is devoid of violence, the name adhvara is given to the sacrifice": thus the author of the Nirukta explains (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೮" [?]). The same derivation is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also:

original p. 620

तं वा एतमध्वरवन्तं तृचमन्वाह । देवान् ह वै यज्ञेन यजमानांस्तस्मा असुरा दुदूर्षां चक्रुस्ते दुधूर्षन्त इव न शेकुर्हर्वितुं ते पराबभूवुस्तस्माद्यज्ञोऽध्वरो नाम मधूर्षन्न वा [?] … परा भवति यस्यैवं विमुखोऽध्वरवन्तं तृचमन्वाह यावद्वेव सौम्येनाध्वरेणेष्ट्वा जयति तावज्जयति ॥

taṃ vā etam adhvaravantaṃ tṛcam anvāha | devān ha vai yajñena yajamānāṃs tasmā asurā dudūrṣāṃ cakruste dudhūrṣanta iva na śekur hartuṃ te parābabhūvus tasmād yajño 'dhvaro nāma madhūrṣann a vā [?] … parā bhavati yasyaivaṃ vimukho 'dhvaravantaṃ tṛcam anvāha yāvad eva saumyenādhvareṇeṣṭvā jayati tāvaj jayati ‖

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೪-೧-೪೦" [?]; this small-type passage is read from the image and is badly doubtful in several places [?].) Sense, as the Kannada gives it: Once, when the gods began to perform a sacrifice, their enemies the Asuras wished to harm them; but their wish [to harm] was not fulfilled, they failed. Therefore the sacrifice, which prevents harm, acquired the name adhvara. Knowing this secret, if one recites the tṛca that contains adhvara, the efforts of his enemy to harm him fail; whatever benefit is obtained by performing a Soma-sacrifice, the same benefit he obtains. Because of this meaning, the sacrifice has the name [adhvara]. Ordinarily this word is used independently as a synonym of yajña. Thus:

अग्ने यं यज्ञमध्वरं विश्वतः परिभूरसि । स इद्देवेषु गच्छति ॥

agne yaṃ yajñam adhvaraṃ viśvataḥ paribhūr asi | sa id deveṣu gacchati ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-4 [as read].) Here the word adhvara is an epithet of the word yajña: it is clear that it means "a sacrifice that is without violence, and prevents violence". [In the Nirukta the word adhvara is also found among the names of antarikṣa (Ni. 3-[?], as read "೩-೧೦" [?]).]

यस्य त्वमग्ने अध्वरं जुजोषो देवो मर्तस्य सुधितं रराणः ।

yasya tvam agne adhvaraṃ jujoṣo devo martasya sudhitaṃ rarāṇaḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?], as read "೪-२-೧೦" [?].) In some such Ṛks, for the word adhvara, "anusahakam annam" is explained — "unharmed food": it means food that has not been violated (ahiṃsita). In the present Ṛk it means yāga, "sacrifice"; Vāyu is prayed to come to that sacrifice to drink the Soma.

śatinībhiḥ sahasriṇībhiḥ niyudbhiḥ — "with your horses that are hundreds in number and thousands in number", so the very large number of Vāyu's horses is shown. As in sahasriṇo rathāsaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-1, as read "೨-೪೧-೧" [?]) and vahantu tvā manoyujo yuktāso navatir nava (4-[?]-[?], as read "೪-೪೮-೪, ೫" [?]) and the like, in many places the great number of the chariots and horses of Vāyu is told, so it is in the present Ṛk too.

adhvaryubhiḥ — adhvaryur adhvarayur adhvaraṃ yunakty adhvarasya netādhvaraṃ kāmayata iti vā (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೮" [?]): "he who carries out the sacrifice, or who leads the sacrifice, or who is anxious for the sacrifice", or

original p. 621

…"one who has an eye on the sacrifice (yajñe śraddhā)", hence the name adhvaryu.
