Here adhvaryu should be taken as "camasa-adhvaryus": teṣāṃ daśatvād bahuvacanam — "since there are ten of them, the plural"; "since the number of camasa-adhvaryus is ten, here there is the plural", the commentator's solution.

ते द्वो विष्यतीति स यदग्निं जुषन्ते तदेनान्नवत्यथ यद्यः सोमं बिभ्रत उपर्युपरि चरिष्यन्ति … ते द्वो विष्यतीति स यदेनान्सोमं बिभ्रते उपर्युपरि चरन्ति तदेनान्नवति तस्मादध्वर्युः समयाऽतिष्ठ्यान्नातीयादध्वर्युर्हि सोमं बिभर्ति ।

te dvo viṣyatīti sa yad agniṃ juṣante tad enān navaty atha yadyaḥ somaṃ bibhrata uparyupari cariṣyanti … te dvo viṣyatīti sa yad enān somaṃ bibhrate uparyupari caranti tad enān navati tasmād adhvaryuḥ samayātiṣṭhyān nātīyād adhvaryur hi somaṃ bibharti |

(Śa. Brā. [?]-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೩-೯-೨-೧೦" [?]; the passage is read with great doubt: only its sense is reliable [?].) Sense: while the adhvaryu carries the Soma and moves round near the vedi, the gods, eager for it, sit around; for their satisfaction the Soma-juice has to be carried by the adhvaryu — so the duties and the nature of the camasa-adhvaryus are shown. The same idea is also told in the present Ṛk: adhvaryubhiḥ bharamāṇāḥ somāḥ — "the Soma-juices carried by the adhvaryus (are ready)".

śukrāḥ — śukraṃ śocater jvalatikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 5-[?], as read "೫-೧೧" [?]) — from the root śuc, giving the sense "to shine"; an epithet describing the Soma in this context: the purified Soma, extremely radiant, shines.

ṛtviyaḥ — prāptakālaḥ pradānāvasaraṃ prāptaḥ | ṛtuśabdena pradānakālo lakṣyate — ṛtu has the meaning "time", so here ṛtviyaḥ means "the time when Soma is offered". The author of the Nirukta:

उत ग्ना व्यन्तु देवपत्नीरिन्द्राण्यग्नाय्यश्विनी राट् । आ रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु व्यन्तु देवीर्य ऋतुर्जनीनाम् ॥

uta gnā vyantu devapatnīr indrāṇy agnāyy aśvinī rāṭ | ā rodasī varuṇānī śṛṇotu vyantu devīr ya ṛtur janīnām ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46-8 [as read].) — taking this Ṛk, explains the word ṛtu as "all the time" [i.e. sakālam], indicating the context there: in those fitting times the divine wives enjoy their happiness; so in the present Ṛk also, with ṛtviyaḥ it points to the time fit for Soma to be drunk by the deity Vāyu: the time of the morning pressing. As the Soma must be offered to Vāyu before all the other deities, sūrye sacā saraśmiḥ — "by the rays of the newly risen sun", that is, "shining along with the rays of the dawn" is the meaning.

original p. 622

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). adhvaram — na vidyate dhvaraḥ hiṃsā yatra; dhvara from the root dhvṛ; ñañ-tatpuruṣa; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172 [as read]) gives the final udātta. vītaye — root vī gatyādiṣu; mantre vṛṣeṣa… (Pā. 3-3-96 [as read]) gives ktin with the udātta. ṛtviyaḥ — by the word ṛtu, by lakṣaṇā, the associated time is understood; chandasi ghas (Pā. 5-1-106 [as read]) gives the suffix ghas; āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ… (Pā. 7-1-2 [as read]) gives iya for it; siti ca (Pā. 1-4-16 [as read]) gives the pada-term because the suffix is sit; as there is no bha-term, guṇa by oro guṇaḥ does not occur, so yaṇ-substitution; the suffix's ādyudātta. sacā — root ṣaca samavāye; sa for the first letter; saṃpadādibhyaḥ kvip in the sense of state; instrumental singular; sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante — by this statement, sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. 6-1-168 [as read]) does not give the udātta to the case-ending; when it is taken as an nipāta, the ādyudātta. bharamāṇāḥ — root bhṛñ bharaṇe; in the passive [?], śānac; vyatyaya gives śap; after the sārvadhātuka the guṇa of the root's ṛ; tāsyanudāttenṅidvidupadeśāt… (Pā. 6-1-186 [as read]) — as the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the accent of the root remains. ayaṃsata — root yamu uparame; laṅ, third person plural, the suffix jha; luṅ with sic; ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ (Pā. 7-1-5 [as read]) gives at for the suffix; the m of the root becomes anusvāra by naś ca padāntasya jhali [as read] — am gets the āgama; nighāta after a tiṅanta. ‖ 3 ‖

Rik 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

आ वां रथो नियुत्वान्वक्षदवसेऽभि प्रयांसि सुधितानि वीतये वायो हव्यानि वीतये । पिबतं मध्वो अन्धसः पूर्वपेयं हि वां हितम् । वायवा चन्द्रेण राधसा गतमिन्द्रश्च राधसा गतम् ॥ ४ ॥

ā vāṃ ratho niyutvānvakṣadavase 'bhi prayāṃsi sudhitāni vītaye vāyo havyāni vītaye | pibataṃ madhvo andhasaḥ pūrvapeyaṃ hi vāṃ hitam | vāyavā candreṇa rādhasā gatamindraśca rādhasā gatam ‖ 4 ‖

original p. 623

॥ पदपाठः ॥

आ । वाम् । रथः । नियुत्वान् । वक्षत् । अवसे । अभि । प्रयांसि । सुऽधितानि । वीतये । वायो इति । हव्यानि । वीतये । पिबतम् । मध्वः । अन्धसः । पूर्वऽपेयम् । हि । वाम् । हितम् । वायो इति । आ । चन्द्रेण । राधसा । आ । गतम् । इन्द्रः । च । राधसा । आ । गतम् ॥ ४ ॥

ā | vām | rathaḥ | niyutvān | vakṣat | avase | abhi | prayāṃsi | su 'dhitāni | vītaye | vāyo iti | havyāni | vītaye | pibatam | madhvaḥ | andhasaḥ | pūrva 'peyam | hi | vām | hitam | vāyo iti | ā | candreṇa | rādhasā | ā | gatam | indraḥ | ca | rādhasā | ā | gatam ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 4; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "Having praised Vāyu alone, [the ṛṣi] now praises both Indra and Vāyu together. O Vāyu, and Indra: your chariot, which belongs to you two and has the horses called niyut, shall bring (vakṣat) you both to the place of sacrifice [vaha in leṭ, aṭ augment, sip by bahulam]. Although the niyut horses belong to Vāyu's chariot, as both deities are going together they carry Indra also. For what? avase — for coming, or for protecting. And again for what? prayāṃsi — the food (the Soma), well-placed (sudhitāni), for vīti — for the eating of them; and the havyāni — other oblations, the puroḍāśa and the like of the pressing [savanīya], for eating. [Vīti from vī with ktin; udātta by mantre vṛṣa…] Further, madhvaḥ — of the sweet andhas — the Soma: pibatam — drink the sweet Soma. Because pūrvapeyam — the drinking before the other gods — is hitam — fixed [?] for you two. [yat from pātaḥ …] Hence drink first. Or: Vāyu has the first drinking even before Indra: tvaṃ hi pūrvapā asi (Ṛ. 4-46-1 [as read, [?]]), deva vadhīhe pūrvapeyam [?] (Ṛ. 8-1-1 [as read]) and other such passages are well known; and the Brāhmaṇa on indra-turīya, [in Ai. Brā. 3-39 [?]], ... the passage devā vai somasya rājño 'grapeyena samapādayan shows that Indra drinks, with Vāyu, before other gods. And further, at the time of coming, O Vāyu and Indra, come with candreṇa rādhasā — a delightful wealth, gold, wealth of cows and so on: come with rādhas, jewels, riches." Details of the grammar of gatam are partly doubtful [?].

केवलं वायुं स्तुत्वा व्यासक्तयेन्द्रवायू स्तौति । हे वायो त्वामिन्द्रं च वां युष्मान् रथो युवयोः संबन्धी रथो नियुत्वान् नियुद्भिरश्वैरुपेतः सन् वक्षत् । देवयजनं प्रति युष्मानावहतु ॥ वहेर्लेट्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ॥ यद्यपि नियुतो वायोरेव रथस्योपेताः तथापि व्यासक्तदेवताबाहुल्यात् [?] सहैवागमनादिन्द्रार्थमपि वहन्ति । किमर्थम् । अवसे गमनाय रक्षणाय वा । पुनश्च किमर्थम् । प्रयांस्यन्नानि सोमलक्षणानि सुधितानि सुष्ठु गृहीतानि वीतये । तेषां भक्षणाय । तथा हव्यानि वीतये इतरेषां सवनीयपुरोडाशादीनां खादनाय ॥ वेतेः क्तिन् । मन्त्रे वृषेत्यादिना तस्योदात्तत्वम् ॥ किंच मध्वो मधुरस्यान्धसः सोमरूपस्य ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ मधुरं सोमं पिबतम् । यतः पूर्वपेयमितरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वपानं वां युवयोर्हितं । पात्रेरचो यदिति यत् । ऋदुपधात्वेनाकार [?] ॥ अभिमतं । अतः प्रथमं पिबतमित्यर्थः । यद्वेन्द्रादपि वायोः पूर्वपानं त्वं हि पूर्वपा असि । ऋ. ४-४६-१ [?] । देव वधीहे पूर्वपेयम् [?] । ऋ. ८-१-१ [?] । इत्यादिषु सर्वत्र प्रसिद्धम् । तथाहीन्द्रस्येतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वं वायुना सह पानं चेन्द्रतुरीयार्थवादनब्राह्मणे देवा वै सोमस्य राज्ञोऽग्रपेयेन समपादयन्नित्यत्र प्रतिपादितं । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३९ [?] ॥ किंचागमनसमये हे वायो त्वमिन्द्रश्च चन्द्रेणाह्लादकेन हिरण्येन राधसा गवादिरूपेण धनेन च सहा गतं । आगच्छतं । राधसा रत्नेन धनेन सहा गतम् ॥ गमेर्लोटि छान्दसः शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यनुनासिकलोपः ॥ लुङ् च मन्त्रे घसेति च्लेर्लुक् ॥

kevalaṃ vāyuṃ stutvā vyāsaktayendravāyū stauti | he vāyo tvāmindraṃ ca vāṃ yuṣmān ratho yuvayoḥ saṃbandhī ratho niyutvān niyudbhiraśvairupetaḥ san vakṣat | devayajanaṃ prati yuṣmānāvahatu ‖ vaherleṭyaḍāgamaḥ | sibbahulamiti sip ‖ yadyapi niyuto vāyoreva rathasyopetāḥ tathāpi vyāsaktadevatābāhulyāt [?] sahaivāgamanādindrārthamapi vahanti | kimartham | avase gamanāya rakṣaṇāya vā | punaśca kimartham | prayāṃsyannāni somalakṣaṇāni sudhitāni suṣṭhu gṛhītāni vītaye | teṣāṃ bhakṣaṇāya | tathā havyāni vītaye itareṣāṃ savanīyapuroḍāśādīnāṃ khādanāya ‖ veteḥ ktin | mantre vṛṣetyādinā tasyodāttatvam ‖ kiṃca madhvo madhurasyāndhasaḥ somarūpasya ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī ‖ madhuraṃ somaṃ pibatam | yataḥ pūrvapeyamitaradevebhyaḥ pūrvapānaṃ vāṃ yuvayorhitaṃ | pātreraco yaditi yat | ṛdupadhātvenākāra [?] ‖ abhimataṃ | ataḥ prathamaṃ pibatamityarthaḥ | yadvendrādapi vāyoḥ pūrvapānaṃ tvaṃ hi pūrvapā asi | ṛ. 4-46-1 [?] | deva vadhīhe pūrvapeyam [?] | ṛ. 8-1-1 [?] | ityādiṣu sarvatra prasiddham | tathāhīndrasyetaradevebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ vāyunā saha pānaṃ cendraturīyārthavādanabrāhmaṇe devā vai somasya rājño 'grapeyena samapādayannityatra pratipāditaṃ | ai. brā. 3-39 [?] ‖ kiṃcāgamanasamaye he vāyo tvamindraśca candreṇāhlādakena hiraṇyena rādhasā gavādirūpeṇa dhanena ca sahā gataṃ | āgacchataṃ | rādhasā ratnena dhanena sahā gatam ‖ gamerloṭi chāndasaḥ śapo luk | anudāttopadeśetyanunāsikalopaḥ ‖ luṅ ca mantre ghaseti clerluk ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he vāyo — O Vāyu; vām — both of you (you and Indra); niyutvān — accompanied by horses called niyut; rathaḥ — (your) chariot; avase — (our) protection

original p. 624

Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 4, continued: …for protection (for coming); kiṃca — and; sudhitāni — well made ready; prayāṃsi — the oblation-food in the form of Soma; vītaye — to eat; abhi — (towards our sacrificial hall) facing; ā vakṣat — may it bring, having carried; tathā — likewise; havyāni — the other oblations (such as the puroḍāśa); vītaye — to receive (may the chariot call you); pūrvapeyam — the first drinking (before the other deities); vām — for you two; hitam — desired; ataḥ — therefore; madhvaḥ — endowed with sweet juice; andhasaḥ — Soma-food; pibatam — accept and drink; ; āgamanasamaye — at the time of coming; he vāyo — O Vāyu; tvam — you; indraḥ ca — and Indra too; candreṇa — delightful (with gold, cows and the like); rādhasā — wealth (and); ā gatam — come; rādhasā — with wealth (jewels etc.); ā gatam — come.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Vāyu, may your chariot, drawn by the horses called niyut, bring you and Indra to protect us and to receive the Soma-food made ready, and may it call you to our sacrificial hall; likewise to accept the other oblations such as the puroḍāśa; for you two, the drinking [of Soma] before the other gods is desired; therefore drink this sweet Soma; and, coming, O Vāyu, you and Indra come with delightful wealth (gold, cows and the like); and come with wealth of jewels as well.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Let the chariot drawn by the Niyuts convey you both, (Indra and Vayu, to the sacrifice), for our preservation, and to partake of the consecrated viands; to partake, Vayu, of the oblations: drink of the sweet beverage; for the first draught is your (joint) due. Vayu (and Indra), come with joy-bestowing wealth; Indra (and Vayu), come with wealth."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).

Among the gods, there was a discussion as to who should have the first place in drinking Soma; finally, a contest of running was set up; in it Vāyu won and gained the first place. This is known from the story told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, "devā vai somasya rājño 'grapeyena na samapādayan" (Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೫" [?]), which has been quoted above. Therefore the first place is secure for Vāyu among all the gods.

original p. 625

अग्रं पिबा मधूनां सुतं वायो दिविष्टिषु । त्वं हि पूर्वपा असि ॥

agraṃ pibā madhūnāṃ sutaṃ vāyo diviṣṭiṣu | tvaṃ hi pūrvapā asi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-46-1 [as read].)

आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः सहस्रं ते नियुतो विश्ववार । उपो ते अन्धो मद्यमयामि यस्य देव दधिषे पूर्वपेयम् ॥

ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ sahasraṃ te niyuto viśvavāra | upo te andho madyam ayāmi yasya deva dadhiṣe pūrvapeyam ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-41-1 [as read].) In Ṛks such as these too, the same matter, that Vāyu is to have the first place, is clear; Sāyaṇa explains. Yadyapīndrād api vāyoḥ pūrvapānaṃ, tathāpīndrasyetaradevebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ vāyunā saha pānam indraturīyārthavādabrāhmaṇe pratipāditam — "although Vāyu drinks before Indra, still the drinking of Indra, with Vāyu, before the other gods is established in the Brāhmaṇa on the meaning of indraturīya": [this he says, to show that] Indra, though Vāyu should get the first place, must still be before the other gods, and that Indra made an agreement with Vāyu; Sāyaṇa points to this by the words devā vai etc. of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. As this story was explained in the Special Topics of the first Ṛk [the passage cited above], here only the matter of Indra's prayer to Vāyu, that he be given the first place along with him, is cited:

सोऽवेदिन्द्रो वायुमुपैव जयतीति तमन्वपराप्तत्तमाह नावभोज्जयावेति स नेत्यब्रवीदहमेवोज्जेष्यामीति तृतीयं मेऽभोज्जयावेति नेति हैवाब्रवीदहमेवोज्जेष्यामीति तुरीयं मेऽभोज्जयावेति तथेति तं तुरीये त्यार्जत तत्तुरीयभागीन्द्रो भवत्रिभाग्वायुः ॥

so 'ved indro vāyum upaiva jayatīti tam anvaparāptat tam āha nāvabhojjayāveti sa nety abravīd aham evojjeṣyāmīti tṛtīyaṃ me 'bhojjayāveti neti haivābravīd aham evojjeṣyāmīti turīyaṃ me 'bhojjayāveti tatheti taṃ turīye tyārjata tat turīyabhāgīndro bhavatribhāgvāyuḥ ‖

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೫" [?]; read from the image, with the doubts noted above [?].) In this contest, Indra, who knew that he would fall behind Vāyu, ran at Vāyu's speed and, reaching the goal, fell at Vāyu's side. When therefore he asked Vāyu, "We two have reached together, let us both share in the victory", Vāyu replied, "I alone won in the contest" [and refused]. Indra obtained the third share, but at last the fourth share was gained.

स एष इन्द्रतुरीयो ग्रहो गृह्यते यदैन्द्रवायवः । तदेतदृषिः पश्यन्नभ्यनूवाच नियुत्वा इन्द्रसारथिरिति । तस्माद्धैतर्हि भरताः सत्वनां वित्तं प्रयन्ति तुरीये हैव संगृहीतारो वदन्तेऽमुन्वैवानुकाशेन यदद इन्द्रः सारथिरिव भूत्वोदजयत् ॥

sa eṣa indraturīyo graho gṛhyate yad aindravāyavaḥ | tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann abhyanūvāca niyutvā indrasārathir iti | tasmād dhaitarhi bharatāḥ satvanāṃ vittaṃ prayanti turīye haiva saṃgṛhītāro vadante 'munvaivānukāśena yad ada indraḥ sārathir iva bhūtvodajayat ‖

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೫" [?]; doubtful in the second half [?].) Therefore in the aindravāya cup the fixed quarter portion belongs to Indra, and the sage saw this: for that reason he used the mantra "niyutvān indrasārathiḥ" ("Vāyu, with Indra as charioteer") [as printed]. Even now …

original p. 626

Continuing the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa passage, which this Kannada paragraph explains: …"Even now the Bharata kings, having taken the spoils, give the fourth portion to their charioteer, who is Indra's likeness [?], and so, in their own charioteer's case, give him the fourth part": thus it is said that Indra holds a secondary place in the drinking together with Vāyu.

andhasaḥ — this word is read among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೭" [?]): andha ity annanāmādhyanīyaṃ bhavati; ādhyānīyaṃ prārthanīyam — "andhas is a name for food; it is called ādhyānīya [to be thought of], prārthanīya, 'to be prayed for'": since it is [a thing] absolutely necessary, and since it is prayed for with great desire, food is given the name andhas — so he explains. In support of this derivation the author of the Nirukta (Ni. 5-[?], as read "೫-೧") takes the Ṛk —

अध्वर्यवो भरतेन्द्राय सोममामत्रेभिः सिञ्चता मद्यमन्धः । कामी हि वीरः सदमस्य पीतिं जुहोत वृष्णे तदिदेष वष्टि ॥

adhvaryavo bharatendrāya somam āmatrebhiḥ siñcatā madyam andhaḥ | kāmī hi vīraḥ sadam asya pītiṃ juhota vṛṣṇe tad id eṣa vaṣṭi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-1 [as read].) — and in that [Ṛk] explains the meaning of the word andhas in the way stated. In the present Ṛk, for the sentence prayāṃsi vītaye; andhasaḥ pibatam, prayāṃsi may be any kind of food which gives pleasure; and andhasaḥ has to be understood as food in the form of Soma: in particular, the word andhas in mantras addressed to Indra may be said everywhere to mean the food in the form of Soma.

इदं वसो सुतमन्धः पिबा सुपूर्णमुदरम् । अनाभयिन्ररिमा ते ॥

idaṃ vaso sutam andhaḥ pibā supūrṇam udaram | anābhayinn arimā te ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2-1 [as read].) In such places, the usage andhaḥ pibā is chiefly current. In all the places in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa where the word andhas is used, this Ṛk (8-2-1) is quoted, showing that the andhas offered to Indra is the Soma-juice. But in the Ṛk —

स हि द्वरो द्वरिषु वव्र ऊधनि चन्द्रबुध्नो मदवृद्धो मनीषिभिः । इन्द्रं तमह्वे स्वपस्यया धिया मंहिष्ठरातिं स हि पप्रिरन्धसः ॥

sa hi dvaro dvariṣu vavra ūdhani candrabudhno madavṛddho manīṣibhiḥ | indraṃ tam ahve svapasyayā dhiyā maṃhiṣṭharātiṃ sa hi paprir andhasaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೫೫-೩" [?]; the quotation is doubtful in places [?].) — in this Ṛk addressed to Indra the word andhas occurs, but here it is not for the drinking of Indra; it is used in many ways to be enjoyed by men; hence in such contexts it does not mean Soma. In general it means the food used by the sacrificers.

The author of the Nirukta, giving other meanings of this word, also states tamo 'ndha ucyate nāsmin dhyānaṃ bhavati (Ni. 5-[?], as read "೫-೭" [?]) — "darkness is called andha, because in it there is no [steady] vision (dhyāna)": that in darkness it is not possible to be one-pointed in mind; so the name andhas is given for darkness; and,

original p. 627

स्त्रियः सतीस्ताँ उ मे पुंस आहुः पश्यदक्षण्वान्न वि चेतदन्धः । कविर्यः पुत्रः स ईमा चिकेत यस्ता विजानात्स पितुष्पितासत् ॥

striyaḥ satīs tāṁ u me puṃsa āhuḥ paśyad akṣaṇvān na vi cetad andhaḥ | kavir yaḥ putraḥ sa īm ā ciketa yas tā vijānāt sa pituṣ pitāsat ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-16 [as read].) — taking this Ṛk, shows there the meaning "darkness" for the word andhas. In the Ṛk before us the meaning is "food in the form of Soma".

prayāṃsi — derived from the root prī with the meaning "to please"; it means "food that gives satisfaction": food in the form of milk, or in the form of puroḍāśa and the like.

candreṇa — this word is found among the names of gold (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೦" [?]). Candram iti hiraṇyanāma candater kāntikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೨" [?]): because it causes delight, gold gets the name candra. To show that the name candra is given to things having an attractive lustre, the author of the Nirukta has shown other meanings of this word:

चन्द्रमाश्चायन् द्रमति । चन्द्रो माता । चान्द्रमानमस्येति वा ।

candramāś cāyan dramati | candro mātā | cāndramānam asyeti vā |

(Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೫" [?].) "Candramas is so named as it moves while looking and moving about, or because it illuminates and measures time and so on, or because its measure shines": this name is well known for the moon. The word is derived from the root cand, which gives the meaning "to shine".

चन्दनमित्यस्य भवति ।

candanam ity asya bhavati |

— [he says that] the word candana (a word for sandal, showing coolness) is also derived from this root; and he gives another kind of derivation. According to that derivation:

चारु द्रमति चिरं द्रमति चमेर्वा पूर्वम् ।

cāru dramati ciraṃ dramati camer vā pūrvam |

— "it moves very charmingly, or it moves for a long time"; the purport may be this; or it may be derived from the root cam, which gives the sense of "drink" — and explaining thus, [he takes the Ṛk]:

नवोनवो भवति जायमानोऽह्नां केतुरुषसामेत्यग्रम् । भागं देवेभ्यो वि दधात्यायन्प्र चन्द्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः ॥

navo-navo bhavati jāyamāno 'hnāṃ ketur uṣasām etyagram | bhāgaṃ devebhyo vi dadhāty āyan pra candramās tirate dīrgham āyuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-19 [as read].) — and by the word candramāḥ in that Ṛk he says that the benefits that come from the moon are also indicated; that he is the one who distributes the portions to the gods, and gives long life to men.

original p. 628

Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued: In the Ṛk under discussion, since both the words hiraṇya and candra are used as synonyms, whatever use the world gets from the moon, the same use is obtained from gold. Gold also delights, through its lustre, as the moon does; it always brings joy to the human mind; it is also a giver of long life, in that it is a source of prosperity for sacrificing men; for the sacrifice, and for the gods, it is also a help. Candra is a synonym fitting for gold.

rādhasā — this word is repeated. The first time it is explained as gavādirūpeṇa dhanena ("with wealth in the form of cows and so on"); the second time, ratnena dhanena ("with the wealth of jewels"). Rādha is among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೧೦" [?]), in the form rādhnuvanti: because by it people accomplish their objects, or because with the help of others they settle matters and agree with each other, wealth has the name rādhaḥ well known.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). vakṣat — root vaha prāpaṇe; leṭ, third person singular, tip; iṭo 'ṭ (Pā. 3-4-106 [as read]) drops the i; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 [as read]) gives the aṭ augment; sibbahulaṃ leṭi (Pā. 3-1-34 [as read]) gives sip; hoḍhaḥ gives ḍha for ha; ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (Pā. 8-2-41 [as read]) gives ka to it, and because of it the s becomes ṣa; as it follows a tiṅanta [?], nighāta. sudhitāni — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; kta in the passive; since kta is the para [?], hi for the root in the sense of dhā; by vyatyaya, dha becomes dhi [as read]; gatir anantaraḥ gives the gati its own accent. vītaye — explained in a former mantra. pibatam — root pā pāne; loṭ second person dual; tam [as the ending] because of luk [?]; śap para; pāghrādhmā… (Pā. 7-3-78 [as read]) gives piba for the root; as it is at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not occur; as the lasārvadhātuka [is anudātta because of ādyupadeśa, tāsyanudāttenṅidvidupadeśāt…], the accent of the root remains. madhvaḥ — jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam: the genitive singular; since it is para, guṇa and the like are optional, therefore yaṇ; the genitive is in the sense of the object. pūrvapeyam — root pā pāne; aco yat (Pā. 3-1-97 [as read]) gives yat; īdyati (Pā. 6-4-65 [as read]) gives ī to the root before yat [?]; because the suffix is yat, there is guṇa; yato nāvaḥ (Pā. 6-1-213 [as read]) gives the ādyudātta.

original p. 629

Grammar, concluded. … — gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. 6-2-139 [as read]) gives the kṛt-final the accent of the earlier member [sic: kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara]. rādhasā — root rādha saṃsiddhau; Uṇ. suffix asun; since nit, the ādyudātta; instrumental singular. gatam — root gam̐lṛ gatau; loṭ, second person dual, tam; bahulaṃ chandasi gives luk of śap; anudāttopadeśa… (Pā. 6-4-37 [as read]) drops the m of the root; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. Or, by Vedic usage luṅ in the sense of the second person dual, cli — since it is para, mantre ghasa… (Pā. 2-4-80 [as read]) gives luk to it; by Vedic usage the āgama does not occur; nighāta as before. ‖ 4 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

आ वां धियो ववृत्युरध्वराँ उपेममिन्दुं मर्मृजन्त वाजिनमाशुमत्यं न वाजिनम् । तेषां पिबतमस्मयू आ नो गन्तमिहोत्या । इन्द्रवायू सुतानामद्रिभिर्युवं मदाय वाजदा युवम् ॥ ५ ॥

ā vāṃ dhiyo vavṛtyuradhvarā~ upemaminduṃ marmṛjanta vājinamāśumatyaṃ na vājinam | teṣāṃ pibatamasmayū ā no gantamihotyā | indravāyū sutānāmadribhiryuvaṃ madāya vājadā yuvam ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Saṃhitā and Pada read from the image.

ā | vām | dhiyaḥ | vavṛtyuḥ | adhvarān | upa | imam | indum | marmṛjanta | vājinam | āśum | atyam | na | vājinam | teṣām | pibatam | asmayū ityasma 'yū | ā | naḥ | gantam | iha | ūtyā | indravāyū iti | sutānām | adri 'bhiḥ | yuvam | madāya | vāja 'dā | yuvam ‖ 5 ‖

original p. 630

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 5; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "O Indra and Vāyu, the dhiyaḥ — the rites such as praise — have turned (vavṛtyuḥ), have been performed with great intensity, towards our sacrifices (adhvarān) — for you two. Further, for you the adhvaryus purify (marmṛjanta) with the woollen strainer this Soma, vājinam — going to the cups from the droṇakalaśa [?], the indu that is before [them]; the simile for the cleansing: like a swift horse, āśuṃ atyaṃ na vājinam, a fleet runner, that has strength (vājin), whom they rub clean by removing sweat and the like; so [the Soma]. Further, O Indra and Vāyu, drink the Soma-juices of those adhvaryus, purified; do the drinking; for that come here to our sacrifice with ūti — with our protection. Further, O Indra-Vāyu, desiring (asmayū) our sacrifice, drink [the juices] pressed (sutānām) by the stones — the genitive in the object-sense as before: the purpose, madāya — satisfaction, joy; since you are vājadā — givers of food. Therefore drink."

हे इन्द्रवायू वां युवां धियः कर्माणि स्तोत्रादिलक्षणान्यध्वरानुपास्मदीयान् यज्ञान् लक्ष्मीकृत्य ववृत्युः । अतिशयेन वर्तयन्ति प्रवर्तयन्ति । किंच युष्मदर्थं वाजिनं ग्रहणाय द्रोणकलशाद्ग्रहान्प्रति गमनवन्तम् [?] इमम् इन्दुं पुरतो वर्तमानं सोमं मर्मृजन्त । अध्वर्यवो दशापवित्रेण संमार्जयन्ति । मार्जने दृष्टान्तः । आशुमतिशीघ्रगामिनमत्यं न सततं गन्तारं वाजिनं वेजनवन्तमश्वमिव तं यथा स्वेदाद्यपनयनेन संमार्जयन्ति तद्वत् । किंच हे इन्द्रवायू तेषामध्वर्यूणां संबन्धिनः शोधितान् सोमान् पिबतम् । पानं कुरुतम् । तदर्थं नोऽस्माकं यज्ञं प्रतीहेदानीमूत्यास्मद्रक्षणेन सहा गतम् । आगच्छतम् । किंच हे इन्द्रवायू अस्मयू अस्मद्यज्ञमिच्छन्तौ युवं युवाम् अद्रिभिर्ग्रावभिः सुतानामभिषुतानां ॥ पूर्ववत्कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ तान् पिबतमिति शेषः । किमर्थम् । मदाय तृप्तये मोदाय वा । यतो युवं युवां वाजदा वाजस्यान्नस्य दातारौ । अतः पिबतमित्यन्वयः ॥

he indravāyū vāṃ yuvāṃ dhiyaḥ karmāṇi stotrādilakṣaṇānyadhvarānupāsmadīyān yajñān lakṣmīkṛtya vavṛtyuḥ | atiśayena vartayanti pravartayanti | kiṃca yuṣmadarthaṃ vājinaṃ grahaṇāya droṇakalaśādgrahānprati gamanavantam [?] imam induṃ purato vartamānaṃ somaṃ marmṛjanta | adhvaryavo daśāpavitreṇa saṃmārjayanti | mārjane dṛṣṭāntaḥ | āśumatiśīghragāminamatyaṃ na satataṃ gantāraṃ vājinaṃ vejanavantamaśvamiva taṃ yathā svedādyapanayanena saṃmārjayanti tadvat | kiṃca he indravāyū teṣāmadhvaryūṇāṃ saṃbandhinaḥ śodhitān somān pibatam | pānaṃ kurutam | tadarthaṃ no 'smākaṃ yajñaṃ pratīhedānīmūtyāsmadrakṣaṇena sahā gatam | āgacchatam | kiṃca he indravāyū asmayū asmadyajñamicchantau yuvaṃ yuvām adribhirgrāvabhiḥ sutānāmabhiṣutānāṃ ‖ pūrvavatkarmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī ‖ tān pibatamiti śeṣaḥ | kimartham | madāya tṛptaye modāya vā | yato yuvaṃ yuvāṃ vājadā vājasyānnasya dātārau | ataḥ pibatamityanvayaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he indra vāyū — O Indra and Vāyu; vām — to you both; dhiyaḥ — the rites in the form of praise; adhvarān upa — towards (our) sacrifices; ā vavṛtyuḥ — are performed with great intensity; vājinam — [the Soma, for you] going to the cups from the droṇakalaśa; imam indum — this Soma-juice; āśum — swiftly-going; atyam — the always-moving; vājinam na — as [grooms clean] a horse; marmṛjante — [the adhvaryus with the strainer] purify; he indra vāyū — O Indra and Vāyu; teṣām — those adhvaryus' [Soma-juices]; pibatam — drink; tadartham — for that; naḥ — our; ūtyā — with protection; iha — here; ā gatam — come; yuvam — both of you; vājadā — givers of food; ; asmayū — desirous of our sacrifice; yuvam — you both; adribhiḥ — with stones; sutānām — [of the Soma-juices] pressed; madāya — for satisfaction (joy); pibatam — drink.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra and Vāyu, your rites (in the form of praise) towards our sacrifices are performed with great intensity (have great effect); just as [grooms] wash and clean a fast-going, ever-moving swift horse for removing the sweat, the adhvaryus clean with the woollen strainer, for you, this Soma-juice that goes from the droṇakalaśa to the cups; drink it; come here, for our protection, to our sacrificial hall; and, O Indra and Vāyu, you who give food, therefore, desirous of our sacrifice, drink the Soma-juice, pressed with the stones, for your satisfaction (joy).

original p. 631

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "The pious acts (addressed) to you have given augmented (efficacy) to our sacrifices: for you, (the priests) strain this quick-dropping juice, as (the grooms rub down) a fleet, quick-running courser: drink of their (libations), and come hither, well disposed towards us, for our protection: do you both drink of the juices that have been expressed by the stones, for you are both givers of food."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).

In this Ṛk the ṛṣi describes the process of pressing the Soma-juice at the time of offering the Soma, the process of purifying it, and prays that Indra and Vāyu accept it, [saying] that it is fit for their use.

adribhiḥ sutānām; marmṛjanta — etc.: these words indicate the pressing and the purifying of the Soma-juice; that is, "it has been made ready for use in the stotra and śastra" is the purport. Sāyaṇa too, explaining this passage, says adhvaryavaḥ daśāpavitreṇa saṃmārjayanti — "the adhvaryus cleanse it with the daśāpavitra" and shows their procedure. The process of pressing and of purifying, and the implements that are used for [pressing] Soma, are described in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows:

एतान्यस्य पुरस्तादुपकल्प्यानि भवन्त्यथ सोमं राजानं क्रीणन्ति [?] … पुरस्तादुपकल्प्येऽधिषवणं चर्माधिषवणे फलके द्रोणकलशं दशापवित्रमद्रीन् पूतभृतं चाधवनीयं च स्थालीमुदञ्चनं चमसं च तद्येदेत्राजानं प्रातरभिषुण्वन्ति तदेनानि द्वेधा विग्रह्णीयाद्भ्यन्यानि सुनुयान्नाद्भ्यं दिनायान्यानि परिशिंष्यात् ॥

etāny asya purastād upakalpyāni bhavanty atha somaṃ rājānaṃ krīṇanti [?] … purastād upakalpye 'dhiṣavaṇaṃ carmādhiṣavaṇe phalake droṇakalaśaṃ daśāpavitram adrīn pūtabhṛtaṃ cādhavanīyaṃ ca sthālīm udañcanaṃ camasaṃ ca tad yed etrājānaṃ prātar abhiṣuṇvanti tad enāni dvedhā vigṛhṇīyād abhy anyāni sunuyān nādbhyaṃ dināyānyāni pariśiṃṣyāt ‖

(Ai. Brā. [?]-[?], as read "೭-೩೧" [?]; this small-type passage is read from the image and is badly doubtful throughout [?]; the sense is as the Kannada gives it.) On the first day of the rite, the adhvaryu, for pressing, must have ready all the implements needed for pressing — the pressing-board (adhiṣavaṇa), the skin, the plank, the droṇakalaśa, the strainer with ten fringes (daśāpavitra), the stones, the pūtabhṛt and ādhavanīya vessels, the dish, the ladle, the camasa — [and he arranges them for] the pressing before the morning and the others.

original p. 632

The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa passage of p. 631, explained in Kannada: …daśāpavitra, pūtabhṛt, ādhavanīya, sthālī, camasa and so on: from those the implements needed there are listed. [This is the order in which the juice is obtained; or the order may differ in the rites.]

The adhvaryu takes the skin and puts on it the Soma-plant in the form of aṃśu (stalks); first, he places the pressing-boards over them (the plank or stones) and beats them with the grāvan. Then he ties the crushed Soma-stalks with the end of the plank, together. Then he places another plank over it and, pouring on the board the water of the vasatīvarī [water] kept the previous day, in the camasa-vessel of another priest, the hotṛ, he sprinkles the crushed Soma-stalks three times, [the water] coming from the vasatīvarī. After this nigrāha procedure, he pours the water of the vasatīvarī vessel on the adri, [the stone], and then, placing the grāvan above, he spreads a little grass over it and beats once more with the grāvan to extract the juice. This act of beating is called abhiṣavaṇa. In this abhiṣava procedure there are three rounds: the first, as stated above, the adhvaryu beats eight times and completes the nigrāha rite; in the second round he beats eleven times, and in the third twelve times. After this abhiṣava rite, which comes first, [following] the procedure stated above, he performs [also] the great abhiṣava (mahābhiṣava) — for the āyā savana — and pours the juice he has obtained into the ādhavanīya vessel. After this, filtering it with a cloth called the daśāpavitra, he pours it into the pūtabhṛt vessel below. At that time the udgātṛ [or the unnetṛ] must hold this daśāpavitra cloth.

In the Ṛk before us, for the word marmṛjanta, adhvaryavo daśāpavitreṇa saṃmārjayanti is explained: "the adhvaryus cleanse with the daśāpavitra" is the matter that is shown. In the above-mentioned procedure, here the action adribhiḥ sutānām is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as follows (Tai. Saṃ. 1-4-1 [as read]):

आ ददे ग्रावास्यध्वरकृद्देवेभ्यो गम्भीरमिमम् [?] अध्वरं कृधीन्द्राय सोमꣳ सुषुतं मधुमन्तं पयस्वन्तं वृष्टिवनिम् ।

ā dade grāvāsy adhvarakṛd devebhyo gambhīram imam [?] adhvaraṃ kṛdhīndrāya somaguṃ suṣutaṃ madhumantaṃ payasvantaṃ vṛṣṭivanim |

(The middle of this quotation is garbled in the print — "kṛdhyatrena savi …" — and is doubtful [?].) "O grāvan (the upāṃśugraha-pressing-stone), who makes the sacrifice for the gods, [I take hold of] you, to press the Soma-plant; make with your sweet [?] shape the sacrifice deep, [pressing] the Soma that is sweet, rich in essence, and that brings rain, for Indra. [With this mantra the grāvan is taken.]"

original p. 633

इन्द्राय त्वा वृत्रघ्न इन्द्राय त्वा वृत्रतुर इन्द्राय त्वाभिमातिघ्न इन्द्राय त्वादित्यवत इन्द्राय त्वा विश्वदेव्यावते ॥

indrāya tvā vṛtraghna indrāya tvā vṛtratura indrāya tvābhimātighna indrāya tvādityavata indrāya tvā viśvadevyāvate ‖

"For Indra the slayer of Vṛtra [I take] you; for Indra the conqueror of Vṛtra, you; for Indra the slayer of enemies, you; for Indra accompanied by the Ādityas, you; for Indra accompanied by all the gods, you: [with this mantra, the offering is to be made for the first oblation, and the five separate offerings are indicated and the washing done]." —

श्वात्राः स्थ वृत्रतुरो राधोगूर्ता अमृतस्य पत्नीस्ता देवीर्देवत्रेमं यज्ञं धत्तोपहूताः सोमस्य पिबतोपहूतो युष्माकं सोमः पिबतु ॥

śvātrāḥ stha vṛtraturo rādhogūrtā amṛtasya patnīs tā devīr devatremaṃ yajñaṃ dhattopahūtāḥ somasya pibatopahūto yuṣmākaṃ somaḥ pibatu ‖

"O waters, full of essence, conquerors of Vṛtra, wives of the immortal [Soma], divine ones, establish this our sacrifice among the gods; invited by us, drink the Soma; may your Soma, invited by you, also drink. [With this mantra the water is to be sprinkled on the Soma-stalks.]" —

यत्ते सोम दिवि ज्योतिर्यत्पृथिव्यां यदुरावन्तरिक्षे तेनास्मै यजमानायोरु राय कृधि दात्रे वोचः ॥

yat te soma divi jyotir yat pṛthivyāṃ yad urāv antarikṣe tenāsmai yajamānāyoru rāya kṛdhi dātre vocaḥ ‖

"O Soma, with that light of yours which is in heaven, on earth, and in the wide antarikṣa, make abundant wealth for this sacrificer, and show [your] favour to the giver. [With this mantra the water is mixed with the Soma.]" —

धिषणे वीडू सती वीडयेथामूर्जं दधाथामूर्जं मे धत्तं मा वां हिꣳसिषं मा मा हिꣳसिष्टम् ।

dhiṣaṇe vīḍū satī vīḍayethām ūrjaṃ dadhāthām ūrjaṃ me dhattaṃ mā vāṃ hiṃsiṣaṃ mā mā hiṃsiṣṭam |

"O two strong dhiṣaṇās [boards], may your strength increase; take strength, and give me strength; I shall not hurt you, do not hurt me. [With this mantra the pressing-boards (abhiṣava-phalaka) are beaten.]" —

प्रागपागुदगधराक्त्वा दिश आ धावन्त्वम्ब नि ष्वर [?] ।

prāg apāg udag adharāktvā diśa ā dhāvantv amba ni ṣvara [?] |

"Let the east, the west, the north and the south, and the quarters between, rush towards you; O mother, come out swiftly. [This mantra belongs to the nigrāha procedure; the unnetṛ pours the water into the vessel of his hotṛ, and the Soma is thereby pressed.]" (These small-type Yajus mantras of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, 1-4-1 [as read], are read from the image and are doubtful in a number of letters [?]; the Kannada gloss in the print is what I have followed for the sense.)

original p. 634

यत्ते सोमादाभ्यं नाम जागृवि तस्मै ते सोम सोमाय स्वाहा ॥

yat te somādābhyaṃ nāma jāgṛvi tasmai te soma somāya svāhā ‖

[With this mantra the pratiprasthātṛ gives the Soma-stalks which he has taken, the other six, for [the second pressing] [as read: "the six Soma-stalks are taken by him"].] In this way the origin of the Soma-juice and its purification are described, and then Indra and Vāyu are prayed to come for the drinking of it. The prayer is in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā in this way:

आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः सहस्रं ते नियुतो विश्ववार । उपो ते अन्धो मद्यमयामि यस्य देव दधिषे पूर्वपेयम् । उपयामगृहीतोऽसि वायवे त्वेन्द्रवायू इमे सुताः । उप प्रयोभिरा गतमिन्दवो वामुशन्ति हि । उपयामगृहीतोऽसीन्द्रवायुभ्यां त्वैष ते योनिः सजोषाभ्यां त्वा ॥

ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ sahasraṃ te niyuto viśvavāra | upo te andho madyam ayāmi yasya deva dadhiṣe pūrvapeyam | upayāmagṛhīto 'si vāyave tvendravāyū ime sutāḥ | upa prayobhir ā gatam indavo vām uśanti hi | upayāmagṛhīto 'sīndravāyubhyāṃ tvaiṣa te yoniḥ sajoṣābhyāṃ tvā ‖

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-4-4 [as read].) "O Vāyu, who drinks pure [Soma], with a thousand of your horses give grace to us; for the drinking of the pure juice; the sweet Soma is ready for you; for the first drinking [as before], O Indra and Vāyu: come, with your food, these Soma-juices are prepared and long for you; [I take you] for Indra and Vāyu, [together] pleased; this is your place": such is the prayer to Indra and Vāyu: come, bringing wealth to us; drink this sweet and well-prepared Soma-juice, for it is prepared and ready, being clear and pure.

vājinam imaṃ vājinaṃ na — the word vājinam is repeated; the meaning of both words is the same, "moving". The first word is an attribute of indum, and gives the sense that it goes quickly [from the droṇakalaśa] to the cups [graha]; this is compared to a swift horse. The second vājinam is an attribute of atyam.

atyam — āsetrita-deśaṃ prati atanaśīlaḥ: "one who travels continuously to the desired place"; this word is used as a synonym of Agni, of Āditya, and of the horse:

अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्यो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः ।

asya śloko divīyate pṛthivyām atyo na yaṃsad yakṣabhṛd vicetāḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೧೯೦-೪" [?].) In this, atanaśīlaḥ is "Āditya" ["the one who goes constantly"]; in the present Ṛk the synonym is "horse": "the quick-going horse".

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). vavṛtyuḥ — root vṛtu vartane; in the sense of intensity, dhātor ekācaḥ halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ (Pā. 3-1-22 [as read]) gives yaṅ; the lup is elided by anyemitrakavāgi [as read]; after yaṅluganta, liṭ, third person plural; jhi → jus; the āgama yāsuṭ; ussya padāntāt (Pā. 6-1-96 [as read]) gives the single-form (pararūpa); as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta.

original p. 635

marmṛjanta — root mṛjū śuddhau; as before the yaṅ is luk-ed; after yaṅluganta, by Vedic usage laṅ; vyatyayo bahulam gives the Ātmanepada suffix; jha → ata [as printed]; guṇo yaṅluk… (Pā. 7-4-82 [as read]) gives guṇa to the reduplicate; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. asmayū — after the word asmad, in the sense of iccha, kyac; after it the suffix u; vocative dual; āmantritasya gives nighāta. gatam — root gam̐lṛ gatau; loṭ, second person dual, tam; chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 [as read]) gives the ārdhadhātuka term; the suffix is ṅit [?], so anudāttopadeśa… does not drop the m of the root [?]; anusvāra with paravarṇa; nighāta after a tiṅanta. indravāyū — as indra and vāyu are well-known deities, ānaṅ [before the earlier member] is not ordained here; devatādvandve ca (Pā. 6-2-141 [as read]) gives both members their own accent. vājadā — vājaṃ dadāti iti vājadāḥ; root ḍudāñ dāne; ato 'nupasarge kaḥ (Pā. 3-2-3 [as read]) gives the suffix ka; āto lopa iṭi ca (Pā. 6-4-64 [as read]) drops the ā of the root; supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39 [as read]) gives ā for the dual ending; āmantrita-nighāta. sutānām — root ṣuñ abhiṣave; kta in the passive; by the suffix accent, final udātta; genitive in the object-sense. ‖ 5 ‖

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

इमे वां सोमा अप्स्वा सुता इहाध्वर्युभिर्भरमाणा अयंसत वायो शुक्रा अयंसत । एते वामभ्यसृक्षत तिरः पवित्रमाशवः । युवायवोऽति रोमाण्यव्यया सोमासो अत्यव्यया ॥ ६ ॥

ime vāṃ somā apsvā sutā ihādhvaryubhirbharamāṇā ayaṃsata vāyo śukrā ayaṃsata | ete vāmabhyasṛkṣata tiraḥ pavitramāśavaḥ | yuvāyavo 'ti romāṇyavyayā somāso atyavyayā ‖ 6 ‖

original p. 636

॥ पदपाठः ॥ Pada read from the image; the third pāda is printed "yuvāyavaḥ" as one word — I have given the Pada division as युवऽवायवः, which is doubtful [?].

इमे । वाम् । सोमाः । अप्ऽसु । आ । सुताः । इह । अध्वर्युऽभिः । भरमाणाः । अयंसत । वायो इति । शुक्राः । अयंसत । एते । वाम् । अभि । असृक्षत । तिरः । पवित्रम् । आशवः । युवऽवायवः । अति । रोमाणि । अव्यया । सोमासः । अति । अव्यया ॥ ६ ॥

ime | vām | somāḥ | ap 'su | ā | sutāḥ | iha | adhvaryu 'bhiḥ | bharamāṇāḥ | ayaṃsata | vāyo iti | śukrāḥ | ayaṃsata | ete | vām | abhi | asṛkṣata | tiraḥ | pavitram | āśavaḥ | yuva 'vāyavaḥ | ati | romāṇi | avyayā | somāsaḥ | ati | avyayā ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 6; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "O Vāyu, these Soma-juices, belonging to you, and to Indra, in the rites of the priests, are pressed here, at the place of pressing, being carried (bharamāṇāḥ) — held by the adhvaryus, taken, or about to be offered — ayaṃsata: they come, they are fixed for you two. Further, these very Soma-juices, śukrāḥ — clear, shining — ayaṃsata: they are fixed. And āśavaḥ — pervading — to please you. Tiraḥ pavitram — across the crosswise strainer, the woollen strainer that hides the Soma within, they are poured (abhyasṛkṣata). Further, yuvāyavaḥ — desiring you two — the Soma-juices, avyayā: [pass through] the fine hairs (romāṇi) of the sheep-wool strainer; or avyayā = made of wool [?], [the m elided]; having passed such hairs they go out of the vessel; and again they are specially described, ati avyayā — exceedingly inexhaustible, the Soma-juices."

हे वायो वां युवयोस्तव चेन्द्रस्य च स्वभूता इमे सोमा अप्स्वप्सु [?] ऋत्विजां कर्मसु ॥ ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्त्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ इहास्मिन्नभिषवस्थाने सुता अभिषुता अध्वर्युभिर्भरमाणास्तैर्भ्रियमाणा गृहीता होतुं वा ह्रियमाणाः ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ सन्त अयंसते [?] आगच्छन्ति । युवयोर्नियता भवन्ति । किंचेत एव सोमाः शुक्राः शुभ्रा दीप्ता अयंसन्त नियता भवन्ति । किंचैते आशवो व्यापकाः सोमा वां युवां प्रीणयितुमिति शेषः । तिरः पवित्रं तिर्यग्गतं सोमान्तर्धायकं वोर्णामयं पवित्रमभ्यसृक्षत । अभिलक्ष्य सृज्यन्ते । सृष्टा भवन्ति । सृजेः कर्मणि लुङ् [?] । … किंच युवायवो युवां कामयमानाः सोमासः सोमा अव्यया अव्ययानि सूक्ष्माण्यव्यानि रोमाणि पवित्रसंबन्धीनि वारोमाणि । यद्वा । अव्यया अविमयानि [?] ॥ मकारो लुप्यते ॥ तादृशानि रोमाण्यतिक्रम्य पात्रादुद्गच्छन्तीति शेषः । पुनस्त एव विशेष्यन्ते । अत्यतिशयेनाव्यया व्ययरहिताः सोमासः सोमा अस्पृक्षतेति शेषः ॥

he vāyo vāṃ yuvayostava cendrasya ca svabhūtā ime somā apsvapsu [?] ṛtvijāṃ karmasu ‖ ūḍidamityādinā vibhaktyudāttatvam ‖ ihāsminnabhiṣavasthāne sutā abhiṣutā adhvaryubhirbharamāṇāstairbhriyamāṇā gṛhītā hotuṃ vā hriyamāṇāḥ ‖ karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ ‖ santa ayaṃsate [?] āgacchanti | yuvayorniyatā bhavanti | kiṃceta eva somāḥ śukrāḥ śubhrā dīptā ayaṃsanta niyatā bhavanti | kiṃcaite āśavo vyāpakāḥ somā vāṃ yuvāṃ prīṇayitumiti śeṣaḥ | tiraḥ pavitraṃ tiryaggataṃ somāntardhāyakaṃ vorṇāmayaṃ pavitramabhyasṛkṣata | abhilakṣya sṛjyante | sṛṣṭā bhavanti | sṛjeḥ karmaṇi luṅ [?] | … kiṃca yuvāyavo yuvāṃ kāmayamānāḥ somāsaḥ somā avyayā avyayāni sūkṣmāṇyavyāni romāṇi pavitrasaṃbandhīni vāromāṇi | yadvā | avyayā avimayāni [?] ‖ makāro lupyate ‖ tādṛśāni romāṇyatikramya pātrādudgacchantīti śeṣaḥ | punasta eva viśeṣyante | atyatiśayenāvyayā vyayarahitāḥ somāsaḥ somā aspṛkṣateti śeṣaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. he vāyo — O Vāyu; vām — for you and for Indra (to both); ime somāḥ — these Soma-juices (in the various vessels); apsu — in (our) rites; iha — here, in this place of pressing; sutāḥ — pressed; adhvaryubhiḥ — by the adhvaryus; bharamāṇāḥ — carried; ā ayaṃsata — come (fixed for you); ; te eva somāḥ — those same Soma-juices; śukrāḥ — shining; ayaṃsata — are fixed for you; ; āśavaḥ — pervading ones; ete — these Soma-juices; vām — to please you two; tiraḥ — across; pavitram — the strainer (made of wool, which has to be placed on the Soma-juice); abhi asṛkṣata — are poured (made use of); yuvāyavaḥ — desiring you; ati avyayāḥ — extremely indestructible (inexhaustible); somāsaḥ — Soma-juices; avyayā — [and] fine; romāṇi — the hairs of the wool; ati — pass over (they go out of the vessel).

original p. 637

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. O Indra and Vāyu, for you both these Soma-juices, pressed in our sacrificial rites and carried by the adhvaryus, are prepared; pure Soma-juices are prepared; these pervading juices, desiring you, have come through the sieve [pavitra] for you, and the hairs of the pavitra of the inexhaustible Soma-juices are passed, and the juices are poured [into the vessels].

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "These Soma juices, poured out in our rites, and borne by the priests, are prepared for you both: the pure juices, Vayu (and Indra), are prepared: these pervading (juices) have passed through the oblique filter for you both; the Soma juices intended for you both, pass through the woolly fleece; the inexhaustible Soma juices."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).

The nature of the Soma-juice is described: [it is] pressed with the specified rites, borne by the adhvaryus, shining with qualities such as purity, and so on.

adhvaryubhiḥ bharamāṇāḥ — hotuṃ tair hriyamāṇāḥ bhriyamāṇā vā — "taken to be offered by the adhvaryus, or held": it is an adjective of the Soma, [meaning] "carried by the adhvaryus, or taken for offering". After the pressing, the procedure to be followed by the adhvaryus in preparing the juice for offering, and the mantras to be recited at that time, are given in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as follows. It is called upāṃśugrahābhidhāna (Tai. Saṃ. 1-4-[?], as read "೧-೪-೨" [?]).

  1. वाचस्पतये पवस्व वाजिन्वृषा वृष्णो अंशुभ्यां गभस्तिपूतो देवो देवानां पवित्रमसि येषां भागोऽसि तेभ्यस्त्वा (गृह्णामि) ॥

    vācaspataye pavasva vājinn vṛṣā vṛṣṇo aṃśubhyāṃ gabhastipūto devo devānāṃ pavitram asi yeṣāṃ bhāgo 'si tebhyas tvā (gṛhṇāmi) ‖

    "O Soma, who gives food, flow for the lord of speech, [Vācaspati]: hear — the Soma-god, purified by the fingers, you are the strainer of the gods; I take you for those whose portion you are." The Kannada explains: "O Soma, the giver of food, flow [for Vācaspati], the protecting deity, by the mantra related to speech; be the strengthener for the protecting deities..." (read partly [?]).
original p. 638

Continuing mantra 1 of the upāṃśugraha series, from p. 637, as the Kannada explains it: …"become pure by the mantras. Just as before, in the forest, you were purified by the rays of the sun, so now you are purified again by the Soma-filaments hidden [within the strainer]. You are the cause of purity also for the one who drinks you, the deity among the gods; I take you for those deities to whom you are assigned and carry you to them." [In this part of the upāṃśugraha rite, the pratiprasthātṛ holds a vessel and the adhvaryu pours the juice into it. In that vessel the juice must be purified, having two portions. This procedure is to be done in order, reciting the mantra-part vācaspataye pavasva.]

  1. स्वां कृतोऽसि मधुमतीर्न इषस्कृधि विश्वेभ्यस्त्वेन्द्रियेभ्यो दिव्येभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्यः ।

    svāṃ kṛto 'si madhumatīr na iṣas kṛdhi viśvebhyas tvendriyebhyo divyebhyaḥ pārthivebhyaḥ |

    (Read from the image; the first word is doubtful [?].) "O upāṃśugraha, you have been accepted by us; make our food sweet. For all your powers — heavenly and earthly — I accept you." [With this mantra the vessel is taken and, looking at it, [the adhvaryu] pours it out in a homa [?].]

  2. मनस्त्वाष्टु ।

    manas tvāṣṭu |

    "May the mind pervade you." [With this mantra the upasthāna.]

  3. उरुं अन्तरिक्षमन्विहि ।

    uruṃ antarikṣam anvihi |

    "Go through the wide antarikṣa, favour the place of the āhavanīya." [Reciting this mantra the adhvaryu goes to the place of the āhavanīya.]

  4. स्वाहा त्वा सुभवः सूर्याय ।

    svāhā tvā subhavaḥ sūryāya |

    "Svāhā — to the Sun, easy to reach [?]." [With this mantra the juice is poured into the fire.]

  5. (स्वाहा) देवेभ्यस्त्वा मरीचिपेभ्यः ।

    (svāhā) devebhyas tvā marīcipebhyaḥ |

    [This too is the above.] It is one procedure; or another procedure is to say together "svāhā tvā subhavaḥ sūryāya devebhyas tvā marīcipebhyaḥ" and offer.

  6. एष ते योनिः प्राणाय त्वा ।

    eṣa te yoniḥ prāṇāya tvā |

    "This is your birth-place; [I take you] for the breath." [Reciting this mantra, a vine is to be put into the vessel in which the remainder is poured, the agrayaṇa vessel.]

The same procedure with slight differences is described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa in sentences like atha rājānam upāvaharati | iyaṃ vai pratiṣṭhā (Śa. Brā. [?]-[?]-[?]-[?] to [?], as read "೪-೯-೩-೨ ರಿಂದ ೩೩" [?]), which tell the duties of the adhvaryu and that he takes the prepared Soma for the offering.

śukrāḥ — śubhrāḥ dīptāḥ: "pure, shining" is the meaning.

pavitram — it is difficult to give a precise meaning for the word pavitra. Ūrṇāmayaṃ pavitraṃ somāntardhāyakam — "the strainer made of wool, which hides the Soma": that is, this strainer is made of ūrṇā (wool); [the juice] is poured on it and purified.

original p. 639

Continuing: …it is one method that the juice is purified when placed within the woollen cloth; or this person [the adhvaryu], having made [the cloth] an instrument that cleans like a sieve, pours the juice on it and purifies it — there is also this way. Probably something like that is suggested here.

The author of the Nirukta has given different meanings of this word, but to show that the purpose is the same: pavitraṃ punāteḥ (Ni. 5-[?], as read "೫-೭" [?]) — "since it purifies, it is called pavitra"; and he takes sentences such as

  1. मन्त्रः पवित्रमुच्यते ।

    mantraḥ pavitram ucyate |

    "the mantra is called pavitra": yena devāḥ pavitreṇātmānaṃ punate sadā (Sāmaveda [?]-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೩-೨-೪-೩; ೨-೮೯೩" [?]) — taking this sentence, [Yāska] shows there the meaning "mantra"; 2. raśmayaḥ pavitram ucyante — "the rays are also called pavitra"; 3. āpaḥ pavitram ucyante — "the waters are called pavitra", and

शतपवित्राः स्वधया मदन्तीर्देवीर्देवानामपि यन्ति पाथः ।

śatapavitrāḥ svadhayā madantīr devīr devānām api yanti pāthaḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?], as read "೨-೪೨-೩" [?].) — taking this Ṛk, he shows there the meaning "water". But in the present Ṛk, "to purify" is the meaning only; none of the meanings given by the author of the Nirukta — water, rays, mantra — applies. It means only an instrument of filtering. Sometimes one puts a mass of darbha-grass on the vessel and purifies the juice above it. Here, as explained as ūrṇāmayam, [the strainer] is made of a cloth of wool:

उच्छ्वञ्चस्व चन्वोर्भर सोमं पवित्र आ सृज । नि धेहि गोरधि त्वचि ॥

ucchvañcasva canvor bhara somaṃ pavitra ā sṛja | ni dhehi gor adhi tvaci ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨೮-೯" [?].) In this Ṛk, daśāpavitra ("the strainer with ten fringes") is meant. (This word has been explained in the previous Ṛk.) The daśāpavitra is just a cloth. Here, since it is said that [the juice] goes through avyayā romāṇi ati ("fine hairs"), it is understood that it is the woollen cloth that is meant; hence Sāyaṇa explained it as avi-romāṇi ("sheep-hairs"):

अव्ये वधूयुः पवते परि त्वचि श्रथ्नीते नप्तीरदितेरृतं यते । हरिरक्रान्यजतः संयतो मदो नृम्णा शिशानो महिषो न शोभते ॥

avye vadhūyuḥ pavate pari tvaci śrathnīte naptīr aditer ṛtaṃ yate | harir akrān yajataḥ saṃyato mado nṛmṇā śiśāno mahiṣo na śobhate ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?], as read "೯-೯೬-೧೩" [?]; the quotation is partly doubtful [?].) As in Ṛks like this, where avye tvaci means "in the woollen skin", so here too the word avya, in the sense of "belonging to sheep", is connected [and explained] for avyayaḥ somāsaḥ…

original p. 640

Special Topics of Ṛk 6, concluded from p. 639: …so avyayā romāṇi ati ("passing the fine hairs") must be understood as "the sound, passing through this woollen cloth": the very matter described in this Ṛk [that the Soma goes through the avya-hairs] —

प्र ते धारा अत्यण्वानि मेष्यः पुनानस्य संयतो यन्ति रंहयः । यद्गोभिरिन्दो चम्वोः समज्यस आ सुवानः सोम कलशेषु सीदसि ॥

pra te dhārā atyaṇvāni meṣyaḥ punānasya saṃyato yanti raṃhayaḥ | yad gobhir indo camvoḥ samajyasa ā suvānaḥ soma kalaśeṣu sīdasi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?], as read "೯-೧೩-೧" [?]; the quotation's wording is partly doubtful [?].) — in this, too, the order in which the Soma-juice is cleansed is described in the same way. Raṃhayaḥ dhārāḥ meṣyaḥ aṇvāni aṇūni lomāni atiyanti — "the streams, the quick flows, pass over the fine hairs of the woollen cloth": it is explained [by Sāyaṇa] as the streams, though fine, passing through the woollen strainer, [as described here].

avyayāḥ — the word avyayā is repeated; the second time it is an epithet of somāsaḥ. There it means "that which has no decay (vyaya)": "imperishable".

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). apsu — the locative plural; ūḍidaṃ padādi (Pā. 6-1-171 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending. bharamāṇāḥ — root bhṛñ bharaṇe; by vyatyaya the active suffix in the passive; śānac for laṭ; śap as vikaraṇa; guṇa of the root's ṛ; as the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the accent of the root remains. ayaṃsata — root yamu uparame; luṅ, third person plural; by nighāta after a tiṅanta. asṛkṣata — root sṛja visarge; luṅ in the passive, third person plural; ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ (Pā. 7-1-5 [as read]) gives ata [for the suffix]; sic for cli; liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu (Pā. 1-2-11 [as read]) gives the kittva of sic, so the laghūpadha guṇa of the root does not occur; therefore sṛjidṛśor jhaly am akiti (Pā. 6-1-58 [as read]) does not give the am augment; vraścabhrasja… (Pā. 8-2-36 [as read]) gives ṣa for the ja; ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si gives ka to it; because of that, the s becomes ṣa; āgama of the aṅga; nighāta after a tiṅanta. āśavaḥ — root aśū vyāptau; kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhya uṇ (Uṇ. 1-1 [as read]) gives the suffix uṇ; ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. 7-2-116 [as read]) gives vṛddhi to the penultimate of the root; by the suffix accent, the final udātta; nominative plural.

original p. 641

yuvāyavaḥ — after the word yuṣmad, supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8 [as read]) gives the suffix kyac, with doubling; since the stem is pratipādaka, yuvā [is substituted] for the base; asyaiṣā mahidṛṅkṛte [as read] gives the lengthening; kyācchandasi (Pā. 3-2-170 [as read]) gives the suffix u after the kya-ending; ato lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-48 [as read]) drops the a before kya; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. avyayā — śeś chandasi bahulam (Pā. 6-1-70 [as read]) drops śi; in avimayāni, by Vedic usage the elision of the letter occurs. ‖ 6 ‖

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अति वायो ससतो याहि शश्वतो यत्र ग्रावा वदति तत्र गच्छतं गृहमिन्द्रश्च गच्छतम् । वि सूनृता ददृशे रीयते घृतमा पूर्णया नियुता याथो अध्वरमिन्द्रश्च याथो अध्वरम् ॥ ७ ॥
