sa yadi vṛṣṭikāmaḥ syāt … mitrāvaruṇau tvā vṛṣṭyāvatām iti tad yo varṣiṣyan bhavati sa tvā vṛṣṭyāvatv iti [?] etad āhāyaṃ vai varṣiṣyan bhavati yo 'yaṃ pavate so 'yam ekaiveva pavate so 'yaṃ puruṣe praviṣṭaḥ prāṅ ca pratyaṅ ca tān imau prāṇodānau prāṇodānau vai mitrāvaruṇau tad ya eva varṣiṣyan bhavati sa tvā vṛṣṭyāvatv iti [?] tam etenaivādhvarīte [?] yadā haiva kadā ca vṛṣṭiḥ samivā [?] |

original p. 669

… तमेवैतेनैवादीते [?] यदा हैव कदा च वृष्टिः समिवैतं तमनक्त्यार्द्रामेवैतत्कृत्वा [?] आहुतिर्भूत्वा देवलोकं गच्छादिति ॥

… tam evaitenaivādīte [?] yadā haiva kadā ca vṛṣṭiḥ samivaitaṃ tam anakty ārdrām evaitat kṛtvā [?] āhutir bhūtvā devalokaṃ gacchād iti ‖

(Śa. Brā. 1-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೮-೩-೧೩" [?]; this small-type passage is read from the image and is badly doubtful in the second half [?]; the sense is as the Kannada gives.) Kannada sense: In the anuyāja-section, in the sūktavāka and the like, this part is said in praise of Mitra and Varuṇa. He who desires rain should hold the prastara [bunch of darbha] reciting "mitrāvaruṇau tvā vṛṣṭyāvatām" ("may Mitra and Varuṇa protect you with rain"). The wind in the antarikṣa is the deity of rain. When this wind moves in the antarikṣa it is one form; when it enters man it takes two forms, prāṇa and udāna. Mitra and Varuṇa are these prāṇa and udāna; therefore he who wants rain should hold the prastara with the mantra "sa tvā vṛṣṭyāvatu" — thus the matter that Mitra and Varuṇa are the causes of rain is understood.

आधारयतं पृथिवीमुत द्यां मित्रराजाना वरुणा महोभिः । वर्धयतमोषधीः पिन्वतं गा अव वृष्टिं सृजतं जीरदानू ॥

ādhārayatam pṛthivīm uta dyāṃ mitrarājānā varuṇā mahobhiḥ | vardhayatam oṣadhīḥ pinvataṃ gā ava vṛṣṭiṃ sṛjataṃ jīradānū ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?], as read "೫-೬೩-೩" [?].) Mitra and Varuṇa, by their splendid power, produce rain, and thereby support heaven and earth; they make the plants grow: so, by many such Ṛks, the quality described may be known from the present Ṛk's epithet ghṛtāsutī. Sāyaṇa quotes the sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणावहोरात्राभ्यां खलु वै पर्जन्यो वर्षति ।

ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇāv ahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣati |

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೨-೧-೭-೩" [?].) and explains the epithet ghṛtāsutī by this statement that Parjanya gives rain through Mitra and Varuṇa, who are of the nature of day and night.

enoḥ kṣatraṃ devatvaṃ na ādhṛṣe — "the power and divinity of these two, Mitra and Varuṇa, none can overcome": thus their greatness is described.

या धर्तारा रजसो रोचनस्योतादित्या दिव्या पार्थिवस्य । न वां देवा अमृता आ मिनन्ति व्रतानि मित्रावरुणा ध्रुवाणि ॥

yā dhartārā rajaso rocanasyotādityā divyā pārthivasya | na vāṃ devā amṛtā ā minanti vratāni mitrāvaruṇā dhruvāṇi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?], as read "೫-೬೯-೪" [?].) As the praise says in many places — that Mitra and Varuṇa, holding the heavens, the earth, the radiant [regions] and so on with their firm commands, cannot be opposed even by the immortal gods — that power is described here also.

original p. 670

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). jyeṣṭham — after the word praśasya in the sense of intensity the suffix iṣṭhan; jyāc ca (Pā. 5-3-61 [as read]) gives jya as the substitute for the stem; by prakṛtyaikāc (Pā. 6-4-163 [as read]) as an exception to the elision of ṭi, the stem-form remains; guṇa; since the suffix is nit, the ādyudātta. namaḥ — root ṇamu prahvatve śabde ca; Uṇ. suffix asun; since nit, the ādyudātta. matim — root mana jñāne; mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ (Pā. 3-3-96 [as read]) gives ktin the udātta. bharata — root bhṛñ bharaṇe; loṭ, second person plural, ta → tāta? [as read: tādeśa]; śap conditions the guṇa of the root's ṛ; as it follows a tiṅanta [?], nighāta. mṛḷayadbhyām — root mṛḍa sukhane; after the ṇijanta the suffix śatṛ; śap conditions the guṇa of ṇic and ay substitution; dative dual. svādiṣṭham — atiśayena svādu; atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau (Pā. 5-3-55 [as read]) gives iṣṭhan; ṭeḥ (Pā. 6-4-155 [as read]) drops u [of svādu]; the ādyudātta. samrājā — root rājṛ dīptau; the suffix kvip; as the root rāj, ending in kvip, is para [?], mo rājisamaḥ kvau (Pā. 8-3-25 [as read]) gives m for the m of sam; an exception to the anusvāra; as it is dual, supāṃ sulug… gives ā; kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara. ghṛtāsutī — ghṛtam āsūyate yābhyāṃ tau; root ṣuñ abhiṣave; ktin; in the bahuvrīhi, the earlier member keeps its accent; dual. yajñe-yajñe — nityavīpsayoḥ (Pā. 8-1-4 [as read]) gives doubling; anudāttaṃ ca (Pā. 8-1-3 [as read]) makes the pararūpa [second] wholly anudātta [?]. upastutā — root ṣṭuñ stutau; kta in the passive; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 [as read]) gives the gati (upa) its own accent; as before, ā for the dual.

original p. 671

Grammar, concluded. enoḥ — etad + os; by the paribhāṣā "a rule preceded by a saṃjñā is non-eternal", osi ca (Pā. 6-3-[?], as read "೬-೩-೧೦೩" [?]) does not give guṇa; ato guṇe (Pā. 6-1-94 [as read]) gives the pararūpa; the s becomes ruṭva, visarga. ādhṛṣe — root ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye; since it has the sense of śakya, kṛtyārthe tavaikenkeniṇtvanaḥ (Pā. 3-4-14 [as read]) gives the suffix kena; as it is kit, the laghūpadha-guṇa does not occur; kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara; since it ends in e [?], it is avyaya. devatvam — tasya bhāvas tvatalau (Pā. 5-1-119 [as read]) gives the suffix tva in the sense of state; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. nu — ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām (Pā. 6-3-133 [as read]) gives the lengthening in the Saṃhitā. ‖ 1 ‖

Rik 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अदर्शि गातुरुरवे वरीयसी पन्था ऋतस्य समयंस्त रश्मिभिश्चक्षुर्भगस्य रश्मिभिः । द्युक्षं मित्रस्य सादनमर्यम्णो वरुणस्य च । अथा दधाते बृहदुक्थ्यं वय उपस्तुत्यं बृहद्वयः ॥ २ ॥

adarśi gātururave varīyasī panthā ṛtasya samayaṃsta raśmibhiścakṣurbhagasya raśmibhiḥ | dyukṣaṃ mitrasya sādanamaryamṇo varuṇasya ca | athā dadhāte bṛhadukthyaṃ vaya upastutyaṃ bṛhadvayaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अदर्शि । गातुः । उरवे । वरीयसी । पन्थाः । ऋतस्य । सम् । अयंस्त । रश्मिऽभिः । चक्षुः । भगस्य । रश्मिऽभिः । द्युऽक्षम् । मित्रस्य । सदनम् । अर्यम्णः । वरुणस्य । च । अथ । दधाते इति । बृहत् । उक्थ्यम् । वयः । उपऽस्तुत्यम् । बृहत् । वयः ॥ २ ॥

adarśi | gātuḥ | urave | varīyasī | panthāḥ | ṛtasya | sam | ayaṃsta | raśmi 'bhiḥ | cakṣuḥ | bhagasya | raśmi 'bhiḥ | dyu 'kṣam | mitrasya | sadanam | aryamṇaḥ | varuṇasya | ca | atha | dadhāte iti | bṛhat | ukthyam | vayaḥ | upa 'stutyam | bṛhat | vayaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

original p. 672

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 2; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "Gātuḥ — the going one (Dawn, Uṣas), varīyasī — exceedingly wide, has been seen (adarśi) by all, for the urave — the wide (extensive) conjunction (yoga), for the work of going and the like. And ṛtasya — of the going [Sun, Āditya] — panthāḥ, the path in the form of the sky, raśmibhiḥ samayaṃsta — has come into conjunction with the rays, has been lit. Bhagasya — of the god of that name, who is to be worshipped by all — with his rays the cakṣuḥ — the eyes of all living beings — samayaṃsta: have come together [with light]; all became capable of seeing their own things. And of Mitra, who is the friend of all people because he causes light, the sadanam — house, the sky, dyukṣam — the dwelling place of shining things — raśmibhiḥ samayaṃsta; so too of Aryaman, the god of that name; [accent note]; and of Varuṇa, the remover of darkness, the dwelling became so. Although the Sun is one, because of difference of [attributes] separate praise is given; and although the sky which is to be lit by all three is one, still, because of the difference in the lighters it is praised threefold. After the rising there is light for the performance of rites. Therefore, because of their rising, the ukthya — praiseworthy, great, abundant vayaḥ — food in the form of oblation — they [the pair, Mitra and Varuṇa; or the Sun and Dawn] hold: dadhāte; and further they upastutyam [accept] the praise to be recited near, great, and the food." Two or three words in the last sentence are not clear [?].

गातुर्गमनशीला वरीयसी अतिशयेनोरुः उषा उरवे विस्तीर्णाय योगाय गमनादिव्यापाराय [?] अदर्शि । सर्वैर्दृष्टाभूत् । तथा ऋतस्य गमनशीलस्यादित्यस्य पन्था मार्ग आकाशलक्षणो रश्मिभिः समयंस्त । प्रकाश्येन संगतोऽभूत् । भगस्य सर्वैर्भजनीयस्यैतन्नामकस्य देवस्य रश्मिभिश्चक्षुः सर्वप्राणिनां लोचनं समयंस्त । संगतमभूत् । सर्वे स्वस्वद्रव्यदर्शनाय समर्था अभवन्नित्यर्थः । तदेन [?] सृष्टिक्रियते [?] । मित्रस्य प्रकाशककारित्वात् सर्वजनमित्रस्य सदनं गृहमन्तरिक्षं द्युक्षं दीप्तानां निवासस्थानं रश्मिभिः समयंस्त । संगतमभूत् । तथार्यम्णः एतन्नामकस्य देवस्य ॥ उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ द्युक्षं सदनं रश्मिभिः समयंस्त । किंच वरुणस्य तमोनिवारकस्यैतन्नामकस्य देवस्य सदनं तथाभूत् । यद्यपि सूर्यस्यैकत्वेऽप्युपाधिभेदेन भेदात्पृथक् स्तुतिः । तथा यद्यपि त्रिभिरपि प्रकाश्यमस्मदन्तरिक्षमेकं तथापि प्रकाशकानां भेदात् त्रिधा स्तूयते । उदयानन्तरं कर्मानुष्ठानाय प्रकाशो भवतीत्यर्थः । अथातः कारणादुदितत्वादेवोक्थ्यं स्तुत्यं बृहत् प्रभूतं वयो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं दधाते । धारयतः । किंचोपस्तुत्यमुपेत्य स्तोतव्यं [?] [...] बृहत् स्तोत्रं वयो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं च दधाते ॥

gāturgamanaśīlā varīyasī atiśayenoruḥ uṣā urave vistīrṇāya yogāya gamanādivyāpārāya [?] adarśi | sarvairdṛṣṭābhūt | tathā ṛtasya gamanaśīlasyādityasya panthā mārga ākāśalakṣaṇo raśmibhiḥ samayaṃsta | prakāśyena saṃgato 'bhūt | bhagasya sarvairbhajanīyasyaitannāmakasya devasya raśmibhiścakṣuḥ sarvaprāṇināṃ locanaṃ samayaṃsta | saṃgatamabhūt | sarve svasvadravyadarśanāya samarthā abhavannityarthaḥ | tadena [?] sṛṣṭikriyate [?] | mitrasya prakāśakakāritvāt sarvajanamitrasya sadanaṃ gṛhamantarikṣaṃ dyukṣaṃ dīptānāṃ nivāsasthānaṃ raśmibhiḥ samayaṃsta | saṃgatamabhūt | tathāryamṇaḥ etannāmakasya devasya ‖ udāttanivṛttisvareṇa vibhakterudāttatvam ‖ dyukṣaṃ sadanaṃ raśmibhiḥ samayaṃsta | kiṃca varuṇasya tamonivārakasyaitannāmakasya devasya sadanaṃ tathābhūt | yadyapi sūryasyaikatve 'pyupādhibhedena bhedātpṛthak stutiḥ | tathā yadyapi tribhirapi prakāśyamasmadantarikṣamekaṃ tathāpi prakāśakānāṃ bhedāt tridhā stūyate | udayānantaraṃ karmānuṣṭhānāya prakāśo bhavatītyarthaḥ | athātaḥ kāraṇāduditatvādevokthyaṃ stutyaṃ bṛhat prabhūtaṃ vayo havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ dadhāte | dhārayataḥ | kiṃcopastutyamupetya stotavyaṃ [?] [...] bṛhat stotraṃ vayo havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ ca dadhāte ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. varīyasī — most excellent (Uṣas, the goddess); urave — for the extensive (great) [sacrifice]; gātuḥ — as one who goes; adarśi — has been seen; ṛtasya — of the going Āditya; panthāḥ — the path (the sky, the path); raśmibhiḥ — with rays; sam ayaṃsta — has been joined (has been lighted); bhagasya — of the deity named Bhaga (Sūrya); raśmibhiḥ — with the rays; cakṣuḥ — the eyes of all living beings; samayaṃsta — meaning, become capable of seeing; mitrasya — (of Mitra who is friendly to all in giving light) of the deity Mitra (Sūrya) and; dyukṣam — the dwelling-place of shining stars and the like; sadanam — the house (the antarikṣa); samayaṃsta — became lighted; aryamṇaḥ — of Aryaman and; varuṇasya ca — of Varuṇa; sadanam — the dwelling (the antarikṣa); samayaṃsta — became possessed of light; atha — therefore (since they have risen); ukthyam — praiseworthy (excellent); bṛhat — abundant; vayaḥ — food in the form of oblation; dadhāte — (the Sun and Uṣas) accept; kiṃca — and; upastutyam — worthy of praise; bṛhat — great praise; vayaḥ — and oblation; dadhāte — both accept.

original p. 673

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. The most excellent Dawn is seen coming to the wide sacrifice; the path of the ever-moving Sun (the path of the Sun) is joined with the rays; with the rays of the deity named Bhaga (the Sun) the eyes of all [living beings] have gained the power of sight; the house of Mitra, [lord of the stars] (the sky), is lit; the sky, the dwelling of Aryaman and of Mitra (the Sun), is possessed of light; therefore both (the Sun and Dawn) accept the excellent and abundant oblation-food, and both accept the excellent praise and the oblations and so on.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "The most excellent Dawn has been seen proceeding to the comprehensive (rite): the path of the revolving (sun) has been lighted up by (his) rays: the eyes of men (have been opened) by the rays of Bhaga: the brilliant mansion of Mitra, of Aryaman, of Varuna, (has been lighted up by his rays), and therefore do you two accept the commendable and copious oblation; the praiseworthy and copious oblation."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).

As soon as Uṣas rises, the path of ṛta has been lit by the rays of Āditya: thus the Ṛk shows the close connexion between the rising of Uṣas and the path of ṛta. Here ṛta may be taken as the zodiac wheel (rāśicakra) of the antarikṣa [Zodiac]. That is:

द्वादशारं नहि तज्जराय वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य । आ पुत्रा अग्ने मिथुनासो अत्र सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च तस्थुः ॥

dvādaśāraṃ nahi taj jarāya varvarti cakraṃ pari dyām ṛtasya | ā putrā agne mithunāso atra sapta śatāni viṃśatiś ca tasthuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-11 [as read].) The wheel of ṛta, with twelve spokes, revolves in the antarikṣa; in this wheel, seven hundred and twenty sons (days and nights), in pairs, have their existence. In this description the wheel of the zodiac, which revolves, has twelve months, and also the three hundred and sixty days and nights in the year.

वेद मासो धृतव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावतः । वेदा य उपजायते ॥

veda māso dhṛtavrato dvādaśa prajāvataḥ | vedā ya upajāyate ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-8 [as read].) As described here, the three hundred and sixty days and nights are the children of the twelve months. By such examples as describe the rising of Uṣas, lighting this zodiacal wheel with her radiance, the matter described in the Ṛk under discussion becomes further clear.

original p. 674

जानात्यह्नः प्रथमस्य नाम शुक्रा कृष्णादजनिष्ट श्वितीची । ऋतस्य योषा न मिनाति धामाहरहर्निष्कृतमाचरन्ती ॥

jānāty ahnaḥ prathamasya nāma śukrā kṛṣṇād ajaniṣṭa śvitīcī | ṛtasya yoṣā na mināti dhāmāharahar niṣkṛtam ācarantī ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-9 [as read].) The Dawn-goddess, of bright form, resplendent, knows the first day's name; she is born from the black [night]; and the goddess does not transgress the path of ṛta at all, but day after day follows it, obediently.

एषा दिवो दुहिता प्रत्यदर्शि ज्योतिर्वसाना समना पुरस्तात् । ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेति साधु प्रजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ॥

eṣā divo duhitā praty adarśi jyotir vasānā samanā purastāt | ṛtasya panthām anveti sādhu prajānatīva na diśo mināti ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-124-3 [as read].) This Dawn-goddess, the daughter of heaven, adorned with a garment in the form of her own radiance, rises in the eastern quarter; and she follows the path of ṛta in the most excellent way, without missing a step.

अग्निं विश ईळते मानुषीर्या अग्निं मनुषो नहुषो वि जाताः । अग्निर्गान्धर्वीं पथ्यामृतस्याग्नेर्गव्यूतिर्घृत आ निषत्ता ॥

agniṃ viśa īḷate mānuṣīr yā agniṃ manuṣo nahuṣo vi jātāḥ | agnir gāndharvīṃ pathyām ṛtasyāgner gavyūtir ghṛta ā niṣattā ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-6 [as read].) In this, ṛtasya pathyā ("path of ṛta") is described as a path very high up in the antarikṣa, fit for the movement of the Gandharvas; and the description in the Ṛk under discussion is that Uṣas, rising on this path, makes room for the revolution of the Sun, and makes the world bright.

After the rise of Uṣas, the dwellings of Bhaga, Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa are described as lit. There is a difference of opinion whether Bhaga and Aryaman are other names of Āditya or different deities.

दक्षस्य वादिते जन्मनि व्रते राजाना मित्रावरुणा विवाससि । अतूर्तपन्थाः पुरुरथो अर्यमा सप्तहोता विषुरूपेषु जन्मसु ॥

dakṣasya vāditer janmani vrate rājānā mitrāvaruṇā vivāsasi | atūrtapanthāḥ pururatho aryamā saptahotā viṣurūpeṣu janmasu ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೬೪-೫" [?]; doubtful in the first line [?].) Quoting this Ṛk, [Yāska] explains for the word aryamā there, aryamā āditya ariṃ niyacchati — "Aryaman is Āditya, who restrains enemies" (Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೨೩" [?]); and —

तत्सु नः सविता भगो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा । शर्म यच्छन्तु सप्रथो यदीमहे ॥

tat su naḥ savitā bhago varuṇo mitro aryamā | śarma yacchantu sapratho yad īmahe ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?], as read "೮-೧೮-೩" [?].) Here Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman — all four — are said together to be sons of Aditi.

original p. 675

यो वा अर्यमणं वेद । दानकामा अस्मै प्रजा भवन्ति । यज्ञो वा अर्यमा ।

yo vā aryamaṇaṃ veda | dānakāmā asmai prajā bhavanti | yajño vā aryamā |

(Tai. Brā. 2-[?]-[?], as read "೨-೩-೫-೪" [?].) In this, Aryaman is declared to be identical with the sacrifice.

भगस्य स्वसा वरुणस्य जामिरुषः सूनृते प्रथमा जरस्व ॥

bhagasya svasā varuṇasya jāmir uṣaḥ sūnṛte prathamā jarasva ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-5 [as read].) In Ṛks such as this, Uṣas is called the sister of Bhaga. Some descriptions of this kind, which are singular, do not seem to fit with Aryaman and Bhaga as they are in other deities; this matter will be examined more closely and explained later.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). adarśi — root dṛśir prekṣaṇe; in the passive luṅ; third person singular, the suffix ta; ciṇ for ta [by] ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ; ciṇo luk (Pā. 6-4-104 [as read]) drops the word ta; since ciṇ conditions it, the guṇa of the root's ṛ; the āgama of the aṅga; as it is at the beginning of a pāda, there is no nighāta, the ādyudātta. gātuḥ — root gā gatau; kami-mani-jani… (Uṇ. 1-[?], as read "೧-೭೩" [?]) gives the suffix tu; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. varīyasī — atiśayena uru varīyasī; the suffix īyasun; it being para, priyasthirasphira… (Pā. 6-4-157 [as read]) gives var as the substitute for uru; since it is ugit, ṅīp in the feminine; since it is sit [?], the ādyudātta. ayaṃsta — root yamu uparame; luṅ, third person singular; nighāta after a tiṅanta. sadanam — root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; lyuṭ in the sense of adhikaraṇa; yuvor anākau (Pā. 7-1-1 [as read]) gives ana for yu; liti (Pā. 6-1-193 [as read]) gives the udātta to the syllable before the suffix. aryamṇaḥ — the word aryaman; the genitive singular; ālloṇyāne [as read: allopo 'naḥ (Pā. 6-4-134 [as read])] drops the a of the stem before as [in aryamṇaḥ]; as the word ends in the suffix kanin, the a is udātta; since the case-ending is anudātta and comes after, the udātta is dropped; anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (Pā. 6-1-161 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending.

original p. 676

Grammar of Ṛk 2, concluded. atha — nipātasya ca (Pā. 6-3-136 [as read]) gives the lengthening in the Saṃhitā. dadhāte — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; laṭ, third person dual; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. upastutyam — root ṣṭuñ stutau; eti-stu-śāsv-ṛ-dṛ-juṣaḥ kyap (Pā. 3-1-109 [as read]) gives the suffix kyap; hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk (Pā. 6-1-71 [as read]) gives the tuk augment to the root; since the suffix is pit, the root's accent remains; as it is a prādi-compound, kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara. ‖ 2 ‖

Rik 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ज्योतिष्मतीमदितिं धारयत्क्षितिं स्वर्वतीमा सचेते दिवेदिवे जाग्रिवांसा दिवेदिवे । ज्योतिष्मत्क्षत्रमाशाते आदित्या दानुनस्पती । मित्रस्तयोर्वरुणो यातयज्जनोऽर्यमा यातयज्जनः ॥ ३ ॥

jyotiṣmatīmaditiṃ dhārayatkṣitiṃ svarvatīmā sacete divedive jāgrivāṃsā divedive | jyotiṣmatkṣatramāśāte ādityā dānunaspatī | mitrastayorvaruṇo yātayajjano 'ryamā yātayajjanaḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ज्योतिष्मतीम् । अदितिम् । धारयत्ऽक्षितिम् । स्वःऽवतीम् । आ । सचेते इति । दिवेऽदिवे । जागृऽवांसा । दिवेऽदिवे । ज्योतिष्मत् । क्षत्रम् । आशाते इति । आदित्या । दानुनः । पती इति । मित्रः । तयोः । वरुणः । यातयत्ऽजनः । अर्यमा । यातयत्ऽजनः ॥ ३ ॥

jyotiṣmatīm | aditim | dhārayat 'kṣitim | svaḥ 'vatīm | ā | sacete iti | dive 'dive | jāgṛ 'vāṃsā | dive 'dive | jyotiṣmat | kṣatram | āśāte iti | ādityā | dānunaḥ | patī iti | mitraḥ | tayoḥ | varuṇaḥ | yātayat 'janaḥ | aryamā | yātayat 'janaḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 3; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "This sacrificer dhārayat — has established, himself made [ready] — jyotiṣmatīm — the resplendent, with the fire of the āhavanīya — aditim — the complete, indivisible — kṣitim — the earth fit for the fire's dwelling, in the form of the uttaravedi. [For the Śruti says: vitāvatī vai pṛthivī yāvatī vedir iti — 'the earth is as wide as the altar'.] Likewise svarvatīm — leading to heaven through the accomplishment of the sacrifice — such [an altar] Mitra and Varuṇa join (ā sacete); not only on this day but dive-dive — on all days. How are they? Dive-dive jāgrivāṃsā — awake every day, not lazy to go to the sacrifice. And further, having come to the altar, by accepting the resplendent ghee and the like, they obtain (āśāte) exceedingly bright kṣatram — power. [Grammar of aśnute in the Vedic laṭ [?]; śap luk by Vedic usage.] What are they? Ādityā — sons of Aditi; dānunas patī — lords of the gift (of ghee etc.), or protectors of desired gifts. [Accent notes.] Mitra and Varuṇa, both gods; and Aryaman, a single god, is yātayajjanaḥ — [leader of] the people, among them [the two], connected with them, who sets all people to their respective works; Mitra and Varuṇa are the gods of day and night, but Aryaman, by their strength, impels all beings. Further yātayajjanaḥ — he whose people carry the world, who are his messengers; or he by whom people, living beings, are pushed down into hell by the apsaras [?]; as witness of deeds he rewards beings according to their own deeds. Such Aryaman is subordinate to Mitra and Varuṇa." Parts of the last sentences are doubtful [?].

अयं यजमानो ज्योतिष्मतीमाहवनीयाग्नेस्तेजोयुक्तामदितिमदीनां सम्पूर्णलक्षणां क्षितिमग्नेर्निवासयोग्यां भूमिमुत्तरवेदिलक्षणां धारयत् । धारयति । स्वयं कृतवानित्यर्थः । वितावती वै पृथिवी यावती वेदिरिति श्रुतेः । तथा स्वर्वतीं यज्ञनिष्पत्तिद्वारा स्वर्गवतीमीदृशीं तामा सचेते । मित्रावरुणौ संगतौ भवतः । न केवलमेतस्मिन्नेवाहनि किंतु दिवेदिवे सर्वेष्वप्यहःसु । कीदृशौ तौ । दिवेदिवे प्रतिदिनं जाग्रिवांसा प्रबोधं कुर्वाणौ । यज्ञं गन्तुमनलसावित्यर्थः । किंच वेदिमागत्य ज्योतिष्मदाज्यादिस्वीकारेणातिशयेन तेजोयुक्तं क्षत्रं बलमाशाते । अश्नुवाते । प्राप्नुतः ॥ अशोतेश्छान्दसे लटि [?] इत्यनुशासनमिति वचनान्नुड्भावः [?] ॥ लटो वा छान्दसः शपो लुक् ॥ कीदृशाविति तावाह । आदित्यादिते पुत्रौ दानुनस्पती दानस्याज्यादिप्रदानस्य स्वामिनौ अभिमतदानस्य पालयितारौ वा ॥ षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेति संहितायां सत्वम् ॥ मित्रश्च वरुणश्च तावुभौ देवौ । अर्यमाप्येकस्तु देवस्तयोर्मित्रावरुणयोर्यातयज्जनः । तयोरेव संबन्धादुभयोर्मध्ये स्थितो यातयज्जनः स्वस्वव्यापारनियोजितसर्वजनः । मित्रावरुणावहोरात्रदेवौ अर्यमा तु तयोरेव सामर्थ्यात्सर्वप्राणिनः प्रेरयतीत्यर्थः । किंच यातयज्जनः । यातयन्ति लोकं यदीयाः जना प्रेष्याः स तादृशः । यद्वा । यात्यमाना नरके निपात्यमाना जनाः प्राणिनोऽप्सरोभिर्येन स तादृशः । कर्मसाक्षित्वात्स्वस्वकर्मानुरोधेन प्राणिनः सुकृते यातयतीत्यर्थः । तादृशोऽर्यमा मित्रावरुणयोर्धीनो वर्तते इति शेषः ॥

ayaṃ yajamāno jyotiṣmatīmāhavanīyāgnestejoyuktāmaditimadīnāṃ sampūrṇalakṣaṇāṃ kṣitimagnernivāsayogyāṃ bhūmimuttaravedilakṣaṇāṃ dhārayat | dhārayati | svayaṃ kṛtavānityarthaḥ | vitāvatī vai pṛthivī yāvatī vediriti śruteḥ | tathā svarvatīṃ yajñaniṣpattidvārā svargavatīmīdṛśīṃ tāmā sacete | mitrāvaruṇau saṃgatau bhavataḥ | na kevalametasminnevāhani kiṃtu divedive sarveṣvapyahaḥsu | kīdṛśau tau | divedive pratidinaṃ jāgrivāṃsā prabodhaṃ kurvāṇau | yajñaṃ gantumanalasāvityarthaḥ | kiṃca vedimāgatya jyotiṣmadājyādisvīkāreṇātiśayena tejoyuktaṃ kṣatraṃ balamāśāte | aśnuvāte | prāpnutaḥ ‖ aśoteśchāndase laṭi [?] ityanuśāsanamiti vacanānnuḍbhāvaḥ [?] ‖ laṭo vā chāndasaḥ śapo luk ‖ kīdṛśāviti tāvāha | ādityādite putrau dānunaspatī dānasyājyādipradānasya svāminau abhimatadānasya pālayitārau vā ‖ ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputreti saṃhitāyāṃ satvam ‖ mitraśca varuṇaśca tāvubhau devau | aryamāpyekastu devastayormitrāvaruṇayoryātayajjanaḥ | tayoreva saṃbandhādubhayormadhye sthito yātayajjanaḥ svasvavyāpāraniyojitasarvajanaḥ | mitrāvaruṇāvahorātradevau aryamā tu tayoreva sāmarthyātsarvaprāṇinaḥ prerayatītyarthaḥ | kiṃca yātayajjanaḥ | yātayanti lokaṃ yadīyāḥ janā preṣyāḥ sa tādṛśaḥ | yadvā | yātyamānā narake nipātyamānā janāḥ prāṇino 'psarobhiryena sa tādṛśaḥ | karmasākṣitvātsvasvakarmānurodhena prāṇinaḥ sukṛte yātayatītyarthaḥ | tādṛśo 'ryamā mitrāvaruṇayordhīno vartate iti śeṣaḥ ‖

original p. 677

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. ayam — this sacrificer; jyotiṣmatīm — (with the radiance of the āhavanīya fire) endowed with light; aditim — (having perfect marks) the undivided; kṣitim — the earth (the uttaravedi, fit for the dwelling of fire); dhārayat — has himself made ready; tathā — likewise; dive-dive — every day; jāgṛvāṃsā — awake (not lazy in coming to the sacrifice); mitrāvaruṇau — Mitra and Varuṇa; svarvatīm — (by the accomplishment of the sacrifice) that causes heaven; ata eva — therefore; svarga-yuktām — the altar joined with heaven; dive-dive — every day; ā sacete — are joined [they come, having come to the earth]; ādityā — sons of Aditi; dānunas patī — lords of the offering of ghee and the like (or protectors of desired gifts); mitraḥ varuṇaḥ — the two, Mitra and Varuṇa; jyotiṣmat — endowed with brilliance (by accepting ghee and so on); kṣatram — strength; āśāte — obtain; aryamā — Aryaman; tayoḥ — of those two, Mitra and Varuṇa, in the middle; yātayajjanaḥ — who sets all people to their respective tasks; and yātayajjanaḥ — who sends the people who do evil deeds to hell, [and sends the good to happiness].

original p. 678

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. (This sacrificer) has himself prepared the ground (the uttaravedi), radiant with the fire of the āhavanīya, and perfect in its marks; [O Mitra and Varuṇa, who are always vigilant in coming to the sacrifice], come every day to this sacrifice, which is the means of heaven; the two, sons of Aditi, lords of gifts (of ghee and the like), become radiant and powerful by accepting the ghee and so on; Aryaman (being in the middle of the two) sets all beings to their respective tasks, and sends the (evil-doing) people to hell and the like.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "(Your worshipper) has prepared ground (for the altar), free from defect, radiant (with sacrificial fire) and conferring heaven: come to it together every day, you who are vigilant; every day (at sacrifices) receive invigorated energy (by coming hither), sons of Aditi, lords of munificence: of those two, Mitra is the animator of mankind, and so is Varuna; Aryaman (likewise) is the animator of mankind."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).

jyotiṣmatīm aditiṃ kṣitiṃ dhārayat — tejoyuktāṃ saṃpūrṇalakṣaṇām uttaravedilakṣaṇāṃ bhūmiṃ yajamānaḥ svayaṃ kṛtavān: by this the Kannada shows that the sacrificer has himself prepared the earth in the form of the uttaravedi and, secondly, the greatness of the uttaravedi; all the greatness of the great altar is in the uttaravedi.

The manner of measuring and marking the earth in the form of the uttaravedi is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā; there itself its power is praised; its particular qualities are explained further in the Āraṇeya Kāṇḍa. [Here in the matter of the division of the mantras there is disagreement in the opinions of Āpastamba, Bodhāyana and others] (Tai. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೨-೩ ರಿಂದ ೫" [?]).

  1. विश्वायुरसि विश्वायुरसि [?] … वित्तायनी मे ऽसि तिक्तायनी मेऽसि [?] अवतानाः [?] नाथितमवतान्मा व्यथितम् ।

    vittāyanī me 'si tiktāyanī me 'si avatānā [?] nāthitam avatān mā vyathitam |

    (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೨-೧" [?]; the print is badly worn and I read only the beginning and end with confidence [?].) "O altar, you are the abode of my prosperity; protect me, who am afflicted, in poverty, and in time of trouble." [With this mantra the form of the altar is to be marked.]
original p. 679

शम्ययोपरिमिमीते मात्रैवास्यै युक्तेनैव युक्तमवरुन्धे । वित्तायनी मेऽसीत्याह वित्ता ह्येनानावत्क्रायनी मेऽसीत्याह तिक्तायनीनाम् [?] ऽ … नाथितमित्याह नाथितास्ह्येनानावदवतान्मा नाथितमित्याह व्यथितमित्याह व्यथितास्ह्येनानावत् ॥

śamyayopa-rimimīte mātraivāsyai yuktenaiva yuktam avarundhe | vittāyanī me 'sīty āha vittā hy enān āvat krāyanī me 'sīty āha tiktāyanī [?] … nāthitam ity āha nāthitāsy [?] enān āvad avatān mā nāthitam ity āha vyathitam ity āha vyathitāsy [?] enān āvat ‖

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-2-[?], as read "೬-೨-೨-೨" [?]; this small-type passage is read from the image and is badly doubtful in many places [?]; only its sense is reliable.) This is the measure of the altar: by the proper measure the sacrificer gets what is right for himself; he praises it as "the abode of prosperity" because it helps him through prosperity; because it helps in time of trouble and poverty, he praises it as tiktāyanī and so on.

  1. विदेरग्निर्नभो नामाग्ने अङ्गिरो योऽस्यां पृथिव्यामस्यायुषा नाम्नेहि यत्तेऽनाधृष्टं नाम यज्ञियं तेन त्वा दधे ।

    vider agnir nabho nāmāgne aṅgiro yo 'syāṃ pṛthivyām asyāyuṣā nāmnehi yat te 'nādhṛṣṭaṃ nāma yajñiyaṃ tena tvā dadhe |

    (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೧" [?].) "May Agni, of the name Nabha, know your nature; O Agni Aṅgiras, all you who are in this earth, come with the name Āyu; your name is unconquerable and fit for the sacrifice; with it I hold you." [With this mantra the earth called cātvāla is to be dug with the instrument called sphya.]

  2. अग्ने अङ्गिरो यो द्वितीयस्यां तृतीयस्यां पृथिव्यामस्यायुषा नाम्नेहि यत्तेऽनाधृष्टं नाम यज्ञियं तेन त्वा दधे ।

    agne aṅgiro yo dvitīyasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ pṛthivyām asyāyuṣā nāmnehi yat te 'nādhṛṣṭaṃ nāma yajñiyaṃ tena tvā dadhe |

    (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೧, ೩" [?].) "O Agni Aṅgiras, you who are in the second and third earths, come with the name Āyu; your name is [unconquerable and fit for the sacrifice]; I hold it." [With this mantra the digging with the sphya is repeated.]

विदेरग्निर्नभो नामाग्ने अङ्गिर इति त्रिरहर [?] ति ये एवैषु लोकेष्वग्नयस्तानेवाव रुन्धे तूष्णीं चतुर्थꣳ हरत्यनिरुक्तमेवाव रुन्धे ।

vider agnir nabho nāmāgne aṅgira iti trir [?] ati ye evaiṣu lokeṣv agnayas tān evāva rundhe tūṣṇīṃ caturthaṃ haraty aniruktam evāva rundhe |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-2-[?], as read "೬-೨-೨-೩, ೩" [?].) After digging three times, the sacrificer gets the fires of these three worlds, and by the fourth digging, silently, he gets also the unnamed (anirukta) fire.

original p. 680

  1. सिꣳहीरसि महिषीरसि ।

    siṃhīr asi mahiṣīr asi |

    (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೨" [?].) "You are a lioness; you are a she-buffalo." [According to Bodhāyana, this mantra is used for scattering the purīṣa — the earth and the powder of bricks — on the altar; according to Āpastamba, for gathering up the earth on the altar.]

सिꣳहीरसि महिषीरसीत्याह सिꣳह्येषा रूपं कृत्वोभयानन्तरापक्रम्यातिष्ठत् ।

siṃhīr asi mahiṣīr asīty āha siṃhy eṣā rūpaṃ kṛtvobhayān antarāpakramyātiṣṭhat |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-2-[?], as read "೬-೨-೨-೩" [?].) This altar, having taken the form of a lioness, stood between the two [parties] after retreating from them; therefore he calls it "siṃhī asi, mahiṣī asi".

  1. उरु प्रथस्वोरु ते यज्ञपतिः प्रथतां ध्रुवासि देवेभ्यः शुन्धस्व देवेभ्यः शुम्भस्व ।

    uru prathasvoru te yajñapatiḥ prathatāṃ dhruvāsi devebhyaḥ śundhasva devebhyaḥ śumbhasva |

    (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೩" [?].) "Spread wide; let the sacrificer too spread wide after you. You are firm; be purified for the gods, be adorned for the gods." [With these mantras are to be done the spreading of the earth, the brick-powder and the like, the sprinkling of water and the beating down.]

उरु प्रथस्वोरु ते यज्ञपतिः प्रथतामित्याह यजमानमेव प्रजया पशुभिः प्रथयति ध्रुवासीति धृत्यै देवेभ्यः शुन्धस्व देवेभ्यः शुम्भस्वेत्येवोक्षति प्र च किरति शुद्ध्यै ।

uru prathasvoru te yajñapatiḥ prathatām ity āha yajamānam eva prajayā paśubhiḥ prathayati dhruvāsīti dhṛtyai devebhyaḥ śundhasva devebhyaḥ śumbhasvety evokṣati pra ca kirati śuddhyai |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-2-[?], as read "೬-೨-೨-೩, ೪" [?].) By reciting mantras like uru prathasva, the sacrificer's cattle and offspring increase; by the mantra dhruvāsi he makes the earth firm; by śundhasva, śumbhasva, he sprinkles water and spreads the dust for purification.

  1. इन्द्रघोषस्त्वा वसुभिः पुरस्तात्पातु मनोजवास्त्वा पितृभिर्दक्षिणतः पातु प्रचेतास्त्वा रुद्रैः पश्चात्पातु विश्वकर्मा त्वादित्यैरुत्तरतः पातु ।

    indraghoṣas tvā vasubhiḥ purastāt pātu manojavās tvā pitṛbhir dakṣiṇataḥ pātu pracetās tvā rudraiḥ paścāt pātu viśvakarmā tvādityair uttarataḥ pātu |

    (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೩" [?].)
original p. 681

"May Indraghoṣa protect you in front, with the Vasus; may Manojava protect you on the south, with the Pitṛs; may Pracetas protect you behind, with the Rudras; may Viśvakarman protect you on the north, with the Ādityas." [With this mantra the prokṣaṇī water is to be sprinkled.]

इन्द्रघोषस्त्वा वसुभिः पुरस्तात्पात्वित्याह दिग्भ्य एवैनां प्रोक्षति देवाश्चोत्तरवेदिरुपावर्तेहैव विजयामहा इत्यसुरा वज्रमुद्यत्य देवानभ्यायन्त तानिन्द्रघोषो वसुभिः पुरस्तादपानुदत मनोजवाः पितृभिर्दक्षिणतः प्रचेता रुद्रैः पश्चाद्विश्वकर्मादित्यैरुत्तरतः ।

indraghoṣas tvā vasubhiḥ purastāt pātv ity āha digbhya evainām prokṣati devāś cottaravedir upāvartehaiva vijayāmahā ity asurā vajram udyatya devān abhyāyanta tān indraghoṣo vasubhiḥ purastād apānudata manojavāḥ pitṛbhir dakṣiṇataḥ pracetā rudraiḥ paścād viśvakarmādityair uttarataḥ |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-2-[?], as read "೬-೨-೨-೪, ೫" [?].) Kannada sense: "This uttaravedi has the gods as its refuge; we must bring it under our control", so thinking, the Asuras took up the thunderbolt and advanced against the gods; then Indraghoṣa, with the Vasus, in front; Manojava, with the Pitṛs, on the south; Pracetas, with the Rudras, behind; and Viśvakarman, with the Ādityas, on the north drove the Asuras off. Therefore with the mantra "indraghoṣa…" he should sprinkle the water in all directions.

यदेवमुत्तरवेदिं प्रोक्षति दिग्भ्य एव तद्यजमानो भ्रातृव्यान्प्रणुदते ।

yad evam uttaravedim prokṣati digbhya eva tad yajamāno bhrātṛvyān praṇudate |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-2-[?], as read "೬-೨-೨-೫" [?].) The sacrificer who sprinkles the altar in this way drives his enemies off from all directions.

इन्द्रो यतीन्सालावृकेभ्यः प्रायच्छत्तान्दक्षिणत उत्तरवेद्या आदधत्कृप्त्रीप्रणेनामुञ्चेषीतः तद्दक्षिणत उत्तरवेद्यै [?] नियेदेव तत्र क्रूरं तत्क्षत्रेण शमयति यं द्विष्यात्तं ध्यायेच्छुचैवैनमर्पयति ।

indro yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchat tān dakṣiṇata uttaravedyā ādadhat kṛptrīpraṇenāmuñceṣītaḥ [?] tad dakṣiṇata uttaravedyai [?] niyed eva tatra krūraṃ tat kṣatreṇa śamayati yaṃ dviṣyāt taṃ dhyāyec chucaivainam arpayati |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-2-[?], as read "೬-೨-೨-೫" [?]; read from the image, badly doubtful [?].) Kannada sense: Indra gave the ascetics (yati) to the sālāvṛka wolves; they devoured them to the south of the uttaravedi. In that [southern] part, whatever evil may be, it is destroyed. One should know only who hates [the sacrificer]; the enemy then falls into trouble.

  1. सिꣳहीरसि सपत्नसाही स्वाहा सिꣳहीरसि सुप्रजावनिः स्वाहा सिꣳहीरसि रायस्पोषवनिः स्वाहा सिꣳहीरस्यादित्यवनिः स्वाहा सिꣳहीरसि देवान्देवयते यजमानाय स्वाहा ।

    siṃhīr asi sapatnasāhī svāhā siṃhīr asi suprajāvaniḥ svāhā siṃhīr asi rāyaspoṣavaniḥ svāhā siṃhīr asy ādityavaniḥ svāhā siṃhīr asi devān devayate yajamānāya svāhā |

    (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೩, ೪" [?]; the mantra number is as read [?].) "You are a lioness, conqueror of rivals; you are a lioness, giver of good offspring; you are a lioness, giver of increase of wealth; you are a lioness, winner of the Ādityas' favour; you are a lioness, [giving] the gods to the sacrificer who desires gods: svāhā." — [the Kannada: "you conquer enemies; you give a beautiful progeny; you increase wealth; you win the favour of the Ādityas".]
original p. 682

Mantra 7 of the altar series, concluded: "…bring the gods to the sacrificer's sacrifice; may it be auspicious for you." [With this mantra five āghāras [?] are performed.] As to its greatness:

स्रोत्रवेदिरब्रवीत्स्वर्गान्मया कामान्स्यृक्ष्यध्वेति ते देवा अकामयन्तासुरान्भ्रातृव्यानभिभवेमेति तेऽजुहवुः सिꣳहीरसि सपत्नसाहीति ते ऽसुरान्भ्रातृव्यानभ्यभवन्ते ऽसुरान्भ्रातृव्यानभिभूयाकामयन्त प्रजां विन्देमहीति तेऽजुहवुः सिꣳहीरसि सुप्रजावनिः स्वाहेति ते प्रजामविन्दन्त ते प्रजां वित्त्वाकामयन्त पशून्विन्देमहीति तेऽजुहवुः सिꣳहीरसि रायस्पोषवनिः स्वाहेति ते पशूनविन्दन्त ते पशून्वित्त्वाकामयन्त प्रतिष्ठां विन्देमहीति तेऽजुहवुः सिꣳहीरस्यादित्यवनिः स्वाहेति त इमां प्रतिष्ठामविन्दन्त त इमां प्रतिष्ठां वित्त्वाकामयन्त देवता आशिष उपेयामेति तेऽजुहवुः सिꣳहीरस्यावह देवान्देवयते यजमानाय स्वाहेति ते देवता आशिष उपायन् ॥

srotravedir abravīt svargān mayā kāmān spṛkṣyadhveti te devā akāmayantāsurān bhrātṛvyān abhibhavemeti te 'juhavuḥ siṃhīr asi sapatnasāhīti te 'surān bhrātṛvyān abhyabhavan te 'surān bhrātṛvyān abhibhūyākāmayanta prajāṃ vindemahīti te 'juhavuḥ siṃhīr asi suprajāvaniḥ svāheti te prajām avindanta te prajāṃ vittvākāmayanta paśūn vindemahīti te 'juhavuḥ siṃhīr asi rāyaspoṣavaniḥ svāheti te paśūn avindanta te paśūn vittvākāmayanta pratiṣṭhāṃ vindemahīti te 'juhavuḥ siṃhīr asy ādityavaniḥ svāheti ta imāṃ pratiṣṭhām avindanta ta imāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vittvākāmayanta devatā āśiṣa upeyāmeti te 'juhavuḥ siṃhīr asy āvaha devān devayate yajamānāya svāheti te devatā āśiṣa upāyan ‖

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೨-೯-೧, ೨, ೩" [?]; read from the image, doubtful in places [?].) Kannada sense: The uttaravedi said, "Through me you will obtain all desired objects." Then the gods, wishing "may we conquer our enemies, the Asuras", made the offering with "siṃhīr asi sapatnasāhī svāhā" and became able to conquer their enemies. After conquering the Asuras, desiring offspring, they offered with "siṃhīr asi suprajāvaniḥ svāhā" and obtained sons. After obtaining offspring, desiring paśu-wealth they offered "siṃhīr asi rāyaspoṣavaniḥ svāhā" and obtained cattle. After obtaining cattle, desiring a firm footing, they offered "siṃhīr asy ādityavaniḥ svāhā" and obtained a firm footing. Then, to approach the favour of the deities, they offered "siṃhīr asy āvaha devān devayate yajamānāya svāhā" and gained the favour of the deities.

पञ्च कृत्वो व्याघारयति पञ्चाक्षरा पङ्क्तिः पाङ्क्तो यज्ञो यज्ञमेवावरुन्धे ।

pañca kṛtvo vyāghārayati pañcākṣarā paṅktiḥ pāṅkto yajño yajñam evāvarundhe |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೨-೯-೩" [?].) A foot of the paṅkti metre has five syllables; therefore he offers the āghāra five times and gets the power of the sacrifice, which has five parts.

original p. 683

अप्स्नेया व्याघारयति तस्माद्दक्षिण्यो पशवोऽङ्गानि प्र हरन्ति प्रतिष्ठित्यै ।

apsneyā vyāghārayati tasmād dakṣiṇyā paśavo 'ṅgāni pra haranti pratiṣṭhityai |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೨-೯-೩" [?]; the first word is doubtful [?].) By performing the sprinkling in a curved manner, the animals too put forth their limbs [in a curve] for their support.

  1. bhūtebhyas tvā (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೩" [?]) — "for the beings" — reciting this mantra he takes up the sruc ladle.

भूतेभ्यस्त्वेति स्रुचमुदृह्णाति ये एव देवा भूतास्तेषां तद्भागधेयं तानेव तेन प्रीणाति ।

bhūtebhyas tveti srucam udgṛhṇāti ye eva devā bhūtās teṣāṃ tad bhāgadheyaṃ tān eva tena prīṇāti |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೨-೯-೩" [?].) By reciting this mantra, as he takes up the sruc, the portion of the deities is prepared, so they are pleased.

  1. विश्वायुरसि पृथिवीं दृꣳह ध्रुवक्षिदस्यन्तरिक्षं दृꣳहाच्युतक्षिदसि दिवं दृꣳह ।

    viśvāyur asi pṛthivīṃ dṛṃha dhruvakṣid asy antarikṣaṃ dṛṃhācyutakṣid asi divaṃ dṛṃha |

    (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೩" [?].) "You are viśvāyus; make the earth firm. You are dhruvakṣit: make the antarikṣa firm. You are acyutakṣit: make the heaven firm." [With this mantra the paridhis [fire-sticks laid around] are to be arranged.]

  2. agner bhasmāsy agneḥ purīṣam asi (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೧೩-೩" [?]) — "you are Agni's ashes and Agni's dung [?]" (with this mantra the fuel-sticks and the like are to be set). Its propriety is explained by a story:

अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायाꣳसो भ्रातर आसन्ते देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहन्तः प्रामीयन्त सोऽग्निरबिभेदित्थं वाव स्य आर्तिमारिष्यतीति स निलायत सयां वनस्पतिप्रविशत् तां पूतद्रुः [?] यामोषधीषु तागं सुगन्धितेजने यां पशुषु ताम् । पेत्वस्यान्कराः [?] शृङ्गे तं देवताः प्रैषमैच्छन्तमन्वविन्दन्तम् अब्रुवन्सु [?] न आ वर्तस्व हव्यं नो वहेति सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणै यदेव गृहीतस्याहुतस्य बहिःपरिधि स्कन्दात्तन्मे भ्रातॄणां भागधेयमसदिति तस्माद्यद्गृहीतस्याहुतस्य बहिःपरिधि स्कन्दति तेषां तद्भागधेयं तानेव तेन प्रीणाति सोऽमन्यतास्यन्तो मे पूर्वे भ्रातरः प्रामेषताश्वानि [?] शातयेति स यान्यस्थान्यशातयत तत्पूतुद्रु [?] अभवद्यन्मांसमुपभृतं तद्गुग्गुलु ॥

agnes trayo jyāyāṃso bhrātara āsan te devebhyo havyaṃ vahantaḥ prāmīyanta so 'gnir abibhed itthaṃ vāva sya ārtim ārṣyatīti sa nilāyata sayāṃ vanaspatiṃ praviśat tāṃ pūtadruḥ [?] yām oṣadhīṣu tāgaṃ sugandhitejane yāṃ paśuṣu tām | petvasyānkarāḥ [?] śṛṅge taṃ devatāḥ praiṣam aicchan tam anvavindan tam abruvan su [?] na ā vartasva havyaṃ no vaheti so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai yad eva gṛhītasyāhutasya bahiḥparidhi skandāt tan me bhrātṝṇāṃ bhāgadheyam asad iti tasmād yad gṛhītasyāhutasya bahiḥparidhi skandati teṣāṃ tad bhāgadheyaṃ tān eva tena prīṇāti so 'manyatāsyanto me pūrve bhrātaraḥ prāmeṣatāśvāni [?] śātayeti sa yāny asthāny aśātayata tat pūtudru [?] abhavad yan māṃsam upabhṛtaṃ tad guggulu ‖

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೨-೯-೪, ೫" [?]; this small-type passage is read from the image and is very doubtful in many words [?]; only the outline of the story is reliable.) Outline: Agni had three elder brothers, who were carrying the oblation to the gods and died. Agni, afraid that he too would meet the same fate, hid himself; he entered the trees, the plants, the animals [and so on]; the gods searched for him and found him; they said, "Return, carry the oblation for us." He asked a boon: "Whatever falls outside the paridhi from an oblation that has been taken and offered shall be the portion of my brothers." Therefore what falls outside the paridhi is the share of those [brothers]; by it he pleases them. Of the bones, he made the pūtudru; the flesh that was gathered became guggulu [as printed].

original p. 684

The story of Agni and his brothers, concluded in the Kannada: …Agni had three elder brothers. Because they carried the oblation to the gods, they were destroyed by the burden of it. Agni, thinking "the same fate may come to me", fled far away. He spent one night in the devadāru tree, in the pūtudru tree, in the fragrant plant, in the middle of the horn of the animal [?]. Then the gods, searching for him, found him and begged him to carry the oblations for them. Agni took from them the boon "whatever of the oblations falls outside the paridhi shall go to my brothers", and afterwards he undertook the work. In the same way the brothers, being delighted with what falls outside the paridhi, were satisfied. "Since my brothers had bones [only], they were destroyed [i.e. shrunken]; therefore I shall crush all the bones", so thinking, he crushed them; in them also the pūtudru arose, and the flesh above them became guggulu.

In this way the nature and greatness of the uttaravedi are described. Therefore the epithet jyotiṣmatīm praises it. For the word jyotiṣmatīm Sāyaṇa explains āhavanīyāgnes tejoyuktām, "endowed with the splendour of the āhavanīya fire". The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa describes this altar, which has splendour, in this way: in this description, the identity of the altar and the Agni set up on the altar is shown, and its greatness praised. All the great qualities indicated by the epithets jyotiṣmatīm and aditim in the Ṛk under discussion are thus praised (Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?] to [?], as read "೧೦-೫-೪-೧ ರಿಂದ ೧೮" [?]); here the same primacy is told of the great altar and of the uttaravedi, which is part of the great altar.

अयं वाव लोको ऽग्निचित्य [?] इति तस्यापः एव परिश्रितो मनुष्या यजुष्मत्य इष्टकाः सूदोहा ओषधयश्च वनस्पतयश्च पुरीषमाहुतयः समिधोऽग्निर्लोकम्पृणा तद्वा एतत्सर्वमग्निमेवाभिसम्पद्यते तत्सर्वोऽग्निर्लोकम्पृणामेनं भूतमेतत्सर्वमभिसम्पद्यते ।

ayaṃ vāva loko 'gnicitya [?] iti tasyāpa eva pariśrito manuṣyā yajuṣmatya iṣṭakāḥ sūdohā oṣadhayaś ca vanaspatayaś ca purīṣam āhutayaḥ samidho 'gnir lokampṛṇā tad vā etat sarvam agnim evābhisampadyate tat sarvo 'gnir lokampṛṇām enaṃ bhūtam etat sarvam abhisampadyate |

(Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೫-೪-೧" [?]; read from the image, the opening words doubtful [?].) Kannada sense: This altar is the earth; the oceans that surround it are the pariśrit bricks; the yajuṣmatī bricks are men; the sūdohas are the animals; the bricks of the lokampṛṇā kind are the earthly Agni. He who knows this attains the pervasion of the world.

आन्तरिक्षꣳ ह त्वेवैष एवाग्निश्चितः । तस्य द्यावापृथिव्योरेव सन्धिः परिश्रितः परेण हान्तरिक्षं द्यावापृथिवी सन्धत्त स्माः परिश्रितो वयाꣳसि यजुष्मत्य इष्टका ऋषयः सूदोहा मरीचयः पुरीषमाहुतयः समिधो वायुर्लोकम्पृणा तद्वा एतत्सर्वं वायुमेवाभिसम्पद्यते तत्सर्वोऽग्निः ।

āntarikṣaṃ ha tv evaiṣa evāgniś citaḥ | tasya dyāvāpṛthivyor eva saṃdhiḥ pariśritaḥ pareṇa hāntarikṣaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī saṃdhatta smāḥ pariśrito vayāṃsi yajuṣmatya iṣṭakā ṛṣayaḥ sūdohā marīcayaḥ purīṣam āhutayaḥ samidho vāyur lokampṛṇā tad vā etat sarvaṃ vāyum evābhisampadyate tat sarvo 'gniḥ |

original p. 685

Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೫-೪-೨" [?]; the Sanskrit above is the beginning, and this page continues: "…the iṣṭakās are the vayāṃsi [the birds]; the yajuṣmatīs are the rays [?]; the sūdohas are rain; the purīṣa, the āhutis, the fuel; the lokampṛṇā is Vāyu." Kannada sense: This altar is the antarikṣa; the bricks that surround the altar are in the place where heaven and earth meet, with the antarikṣa; the yajuṣmatīs are the birds; the sūdohas are rain; the marīcis, the rays of the sun, [are] the purīṣas, and so on; the āhutis are the fuel; the lokampṛṇā is the all-pervading Vāyu: he who knows this principle becomes all-pervading.

द्यौर्ह त्वेवैष एवाग्निश्चितः । तस्याप एव परिश्रितो यथा ह वा इदं कोशः समुच्छ्रित एवमिमे लोका अप्स्वन्तस्तद्या इमानॄँल्लोकान् [?] परेणापस्ताः परिश्रितो देवा यजुष्मत्य इष्टका यदेवैतस्मिँल्लोके ऽन्नं तत्सूदोहा नक्षत्राणि पुरीषमाहुतयः समिध आदित्यो लोकम्पृणा तद्वा एतत्सर्वमादित्यमेवाभिसम्पद्यते तत्सर्वोऽग्निः ।

dyaur ha tv evaiṣa evāgniś citaḥ | tasyāpa eva pariśrito yathā ha vā idaṃ kośaḥ samucchrita evam ime lokā apsv antas tadyā imān lokān [?] pareṇāpas tāḥ pariśrito devā yajuṣmatya iṣṭakā yad evaitasmiṃl loke 'nnaṃ tat sūdohā nakṣatrāṇi purīṣam āhutayaḥ samidha ādityo lokampṛṇā tad vā etat sarvam ādityam evābhisampadyate tat sarvo 'gniḥ |

(Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೫-೪-೩" [?].) Kannada sense: This altar is the heaven; the pariśrits [the surrounding bricks] are the rivers (the waters). As the rivers surround the heavenly world, the pariśrits surround the altar. The yajuṣmatīs are the deities; the sūdohas are the food of the deities; the purīṣas are the stars; the lokampṛṇā is Āditya. He who knows this principle becomes pervading like Āditya.

आदित्यो ह त्वेवैष एवाग्निश्चितः । तस्य दिश एव परिश्रितास्तद्याः षष्टिश्च त्रीणि च शतानि भवन्ति षष्टिश्च ह वै त्रीणि च शतान्यादित्यस्य दिशः समन्तं परियन्ति रश्मयो यजुष्मत्य इष्टकास्ताः षष्टिश्चैव त्रीणि च शतानि भवन्ति षष्टिश्च ह वै त्रीणि च शतान्यादित्यस्य रश्मयस्तद्यैवैव्रश्चिरित्र [?] स्तद्यजुष्मतीः प्रत्यर्पयति ता रश्मीन्स्तद्दिक्षु प्रत्यर्पयत्यथ यदन्तरा दिशश्च रश्मींश्च तत्सूदोहा अथ यद्दिक्षु च रश्मिषु चान्नं तत्पुरीषं ता आहुतयस्ताः समिधोऽथ यद्दिश इति च रश्मय इति चाख्यायते तल्लोकम्पृणा तद्वा एतत्सर्वं दिश इति चैव रश्मय इति चाख्यायते तत्सर्वः ।

ādityo ha tv evaiṣa evāgniś citaḥ | tasya diśa eva pariśritās tad yāḥ ṣaṣṭiś ca trīṇi ca śatāni bhavanti ṣaṣṭiś ca ha vai trīṇi ca śatāny ādityasya diśaḥ samantaṃ pariyanti raśmayo yajuṣmatya iṣṭakās tāḥ ṣaṣṭiś caiva trīṇi ca śatāni bhavanti ṣaṣṭiś ca ha vai trīṇi ca śatāny ādityasya raśmayas tad yaivaivraścir [?] … tad yajuṣmatīḥ pratyarpayati tā raśmīn tad dikṣu pratyarpayaty atha yad antarā diśaś ca raśmīṃś ca tat sūdohā atha yad dikṣu ca raśmiṣu cānnaṃ tat purīṣaṃ tā āhutayas tāḥ samidho 'tha yad diśa iti ca raśmaya iti cākhyāyate tal lokampṛṇā tad vā etat sarvaṃ diśa iti caiva raśmaya iti cākhyāyate tat sarvaḥ |

(Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೫-೪-೪" [?]; read from the image, with several words doubtful [?].) This altar is Āditya; the pariśrits are the directions. "Three hundred and sixty" — the number of the directions and sub-directions round the Sun — is the number of the pariśrits round the altar. [In the Mahāvedi the pariśrits are [numbered] 360 [?]; with these, 30 of the gārhapatya-foot; of the dhiṣṇyas, [?] — the next two lines are cut off in the print and I do not read the figures [?].]

original p. 686

Kannada, continuing from p. 685: …the number of the pariśrits becomes together [three hundred and sixty]; each one [stands for] a day and a night, or the reflections of the days. The yajuṣmatīs are the rays of Āditya; the iṣṭakās here are according to the number of rays of Āditya. The sūdohas are the principles between the rays and the directions; the purīṣas are the foods between them; the lokampṛṇā is the all-pervading principle, the sum total of the rays and the directions. He who knows the principle of Āditya in the form of the altar becomes himself pervading.

सर्वाणि ह त्वेव भूतानि । सर्वे देवा एषोऽग्निश्चितः आपो वै सर्वे देवाः सर्वाणि भूतानि ता हैता आप एवैषोऽग्निश्चितस्तस्य नाव्या एव परिश्रितस्ताः षष्टिश्च त्रीणि च शतानि भवन्ति षष्टिश्च ह वै त्रीणि च शतान्यादित्यं नाव्याः समन्तं परियन्ति नाव्या उ एव यजुष्मत्य इष्टकास्ताः षष्टिश्चैव त्रीणि च शतानि भवन्ति षष्टिश्च ह वै त्रीणि च शतान्यादित्यं नाव्या अभिचरन्तीक्षथ [?] यदेतदन्तरा नाव्ये तत्सूदोहा अथ या अमूः षट्त्रिꣳशदिष्टका अतियन्ति यः स त्रयोदशो मास आत्मायमेव स योऽयꣳ हिरण्मयः पुरुषः ॥

sarvāṇi ha tv eva bhūtāni | sarve devā eṣo 'gniś citaḥ āpo vai sarve devāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tā haitā āpa evaiṣo 'gniś citas tasya nāvyā eva pariśritas tāḥ ṣaṣṭiś ca trīṇi ca śatāni bhavanti ṣaṣṭiś ca ha vai trīṇi ca śatāny ādityaṃ nāvyāḥ samantaṃ pariyanti nāvyā u eva yajuṣmatya iṣṭakās tāḥ ṣaṣṭiś caiva trīṇi ca śatāni bhavanti ṣaṣṭiś ca ha vai trīṇi ca śatāny ādityaṃ nāvyā abhicarantīkṣatha [?] yad etad antarā nāvye tat sūdohā atha yā amūḥ ṣaṭtriṃśad iṣṭakā atiyanti yaḥ sa trayodaśo māsa ātmāyam eva sa yo 'yaṃ hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ ‖

(Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?], [?], as read "೧೦-೫-೪-೫, ೬" [?]; read from the image; doubtful in several words [?].) Kannada sense: This altar is all beings and all gods. All beings and all deities have the water (āpas) as their source; one must understand that the altar too has the water as its source. Round the Sun, like the 360 days and nights which are flowing, there are the yajuṣmatī bricks, round the altar, which is also the Sun. In the middle of these rivers are the sūdohas. This body of the sacrificial altar is that of the golden person (hiraṇmaya puruṣa), as explained above; thus the altar is praised in various ways, and its light and greatness praised.

kṣitim — agner nivāsayogyāṃ bhūmim: "the earth fit for the dwelling of Agni" is the explanation.

तेनेमाꣳ सर्वाꣳ पृथिवीꣳ सहुविन्दत [?] … तस्मादाहुर्यावती वेदिः स्यावतीꣳ पृथिवी ।

tenemāṃ sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ sahuvindata [?] … tasmād āhur yāvatī vedi syāvatīṃ pṛthivī |

(Śa. Brā. 1-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೨-೩-೭" [?].)

चन्द्रमा एव प्रत्यक्षादित्यो यजमानस्तस्येयमेव पृथिवी वेदिः ।

candramā eva pratyakṣād ādityo yajamānas tasyeyam eva pṛthivī vediḥ |

(Śa. Brā. 11-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧೧-೮-೩-೩೯" [?].) In such sentences, as it is described that the whole earth is the sacrificial altar and the altar is [as wide as] the earth, in the Ṛk under discussion too the word used shows the identity of these two [the earth and the altar].

original p. 687

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). aditim — nañ-tatpuruṣa compound; tatpuruṣe tu (Pā. 6-2-[?], as read "೬-೨-೧೩೨" [?]) — the ñañ keeps the earlier member's accent. dhārayat — root dhṛṅ avasthāne [as read]; third person singular; by Vedic usage the āgama does not occur; in the alternative of one pada [?], in the bahuvrīhi compound, the earlier member's accent. sacete — root ṣaca samavāye; ṣa → sa at the beginning; laṭ, third person dual; nighāta after a tiṅanta. dive-dive — nityavīpsayoḥ (Pā. 8-1-4 [as read]) gives doubling in the sense of repetition; anudāttaṃ ca (Pā. 8-1-3 [as read]) makes the latter āmreḍita wholly anudātta. jāgṛvāṃsā — root jāgṛ nidrākṣaye; laṭ [as read: liṭ]; kvasuś ca (Pā. 3-2-107 [as read]) gives it kvasu; though iṭ is expected by kradīnām [?], vasv ekācā… (Pā. 2-[?]) forbids it; with the doubling, num by ugit; ātvasaṃtasya [as read: upadhāyāś ca (Pā. 8-2-[?])] gives the lengthening of the penultimate; supāṃ sulug… (Pā. 7-1-39 [as read]) gives ā for the case-ending; the accent of the suffix remains. āśāte — root aśū vyāptau; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. 3-4-6 [as read]) gives liṭ in the present sense; āthām for the third person dual; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. 3-4-79 [as read]) gives e for ṭi; with the doubling there is lengthening of the reduplicate; as per the statement āgamānuśāsanam anityam, the nuṭ augment does not occur; or in the laṭ, as the dual is para, śap is replaced by ślu by Vedic usage; nighāta after a tiṅanta. ādityā — aditer apatyaṃ pumāṃsaḥ; dityadity… (Pā. 4-1-85 [as read]) gives ṇya; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ gives vṛddhi; supāṃ sulug gives ā for the dual. dānunaḥ — root ḍudāñ dāne; dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ (Uṇ. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೨" [?]) gives nu; with the continuing nit [rule], the ādyudātta; genitive singular; as pati follows, ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra… (Pā. 8-3-53 [as read]) gives sa in the Saṃhitā for the visarga. yātayajjanaḥ — yātyamānā janā yena saḥ; in the bahuvrīhi, the earlier member keeps its accent. ‖ 3 ‖

original p. 688

Rik 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अयं मित्राय वरुणाय शंतमः सोमो भूत्ववपानेष्वाभगो देवो देवेष्वाभगः । तं देवासो जुषेरत विश्वे अद्य सजोषसः । तथा राजाना करथो यदीमह ऋतावाना यदीमहे ॥ ४ ॥

ayaṃ mitrāya varuṇāya śaṃtamaḥ somo bhūtvavapāneṣvābhago devo deveṣvābhagaḥ | taṃ devāso juṣerata viśve adya sajoṣasaḥ | tathā rājānā karatho yadīmaha ṛtāvānā yadīmahe ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अयम् । मित्राय । वरुणाय । शम्ऽतमः । सोमः । भूतु । अवऽपानेषु । आऽभगः । देवः । देवेषु । आऽभगः । तम् । देवासः । जुषेरत । विश्वे । अद्य । सऽजोषसः । तथा । राजाना । करथः । यत् । ईमहे । ऋतऽवाना । यत् । ईमहे ॥ ४ ॥

ayam | mitrāya | varuṇāya | śam 'tamaḥ | somaḥ | bhūtu | ava 'pāneṣu | ā 'bhagaḥ | devaḥ | deveṣu | ā 'bhagaḥ | tam | devāsaḥ | juṣerata | viśve | adya | sa 'joṣasaḥ | tathā | rājānā | karathaḥ | yat | īmahe | ṛta 'vānā | yat | īmahe ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 4; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "This Soma, carried by us, offered, may be śaṃtamaḥ — most agreeable, most pleasing — to Mitra and Varuṇa; bhūtu — let it be [Vedic śap luk]. In the avapānas — the cups with their mouths turned down — ā bhagaḥ — it is fully to be shared by those two. Further, devo deveṣu — shining among the gods, the followers of Mitra and Varuṇa, or among the other gods, to be shared; or among the sacrificers, praisers [deva = shining], tathā-bhagaḥ — to be shared by them all. Further, all the gods, viśve devāsaḥ, today, on this day, juṣerata — enjoy that Soma. How are they? Sajoṣasaḥ — joined in equal pleasure. And, O sovereigns, Mitra and Varuṇa, you two, do (karathaḥ) [so]; — for yad īmahe — what we ask, the gods; since we ask [īḍ gatau, divādi; the Vedic elision of the vikaraṇa]; therefore let them enjoy. Likewise, ṛtāvānā — the possessors of ṛta, truth, the sacrifice — Mitra and Varuṇa, we ask the desired fruit, or their drinking." The grammar notes are partly doubtful [?].

अयमस्माभिर्ह्रीयमाणः सोमो मित्राय वरुणाय च शंतमः प्रीयमाणः सन् सुखतमो भूतु । भवतु ॥ छान्दसः शपो लुक् । भूसुवोस्तिङीति गुणाभावः ॥ अवपानेष्वधोमुखचमसपात्रेषु विषयेषु आ सर्वतो भगो भजनीयस्ताभ्याम् । किंच देवो दीप्यमानो देवेषु मित्रावरुणानुचरेष्वितरदेवेषु वा राभगे [?] भजनीयः । यद्वा । देवेषु स्तोतृषु यजमानेषु मध्ये देवो दीप्यमानः तथाभगस्तैरेव सर्वतो भजनीयः । किंच तं सोमं विश्वे सर्वे देवासो देवा अद्यास्मिन्नहनि जुषेरते [?] सेवन्ते ॥ छान्दसो ऋषस्य रन्नादेशाभावः । बहुलं छन्दसीति रुडागमः ॥ कीदृशास्ते । सजोषसः समानप्रीतियुक्ताः । तथा राजाना राजमानौ मित्रावरुणौ युवां करथः । कुरुतम् सेनेथे [?] इत्यर्थः ॥ व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥ यद्यस्मात्कारणादीमहे यत्प्रार्थ्यमस्मद्देवान्याचामहे । ईड गतौ । दैवादिकः ॥ छान्दसो विकरणस्य लुक् ॥ तस्माज्जुषेरत । तथा ऋतावाना ऋतवन्तौ सत्यवन्तौ यज्ञवन्तौ वा मित्रावरुणावीमहे । अभिमतफलं तयोः पानं वा याचामहे ॥

ayamasmābhirhrīyamāṇaḥ somo mitrāya varuṇāya ca śaṃtamaḥ prīyamāṇaḥ san sukhatamo bhūtu | bhavatu ‖ chāndasaḥ śapo luk | bhūsuvostiṅīti guṇābhāvaḥ ‖ avapāneṣvadhomukhacamasapātreṣu viṣayeṣu ā sarvato bhago bhajanīyastābhyām | kiṃca devo dīpyamāno deveṣu mitrāvaruṇānucareṣvitaradeveṣu vā rābhage [?] bhajanīyaḥ | yadvā | deveṣu stotṛṣu yajamāneṣu madhye devo dīpyamānaḥ tathābhagastaireva sarvato bhajanīyaḥ | kiṃca taṃ somaṃ viśve sarve devāso devā adyāsminnahani juṣerate [?] sevante ‖ chāndaso ṛṣasya rannādeśābhāvaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti ruḍāgamaḥ ‖ kīdṛśāste | sajoṣasaḥ samānaprītiyuktāḥ | tathā rājānā rājamānau mitrāvaruṇau yuvāṃ karathaḥ | kurutam senethe [?] ityarthaḥ ‖ vyatyayena śap ‖ yadyasmātkāraṇādīmahe yatprārthyamasmaddevānyācāmahe | īḍa gatau | daivādikaḥ ‖ chāndaso vikaraṇasya luk ‖ tasmājjuṣerata | tathā ṛtāvānā ṛtavantau satyavantau yajñavantau vā mitrāvaruṇāvīmahe | abhimataphalaṃ tayoḥ pānaṃ vā yācāmahe ‖

original p. 689

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. ayam — this (the Soma-juice offered by us); somaḥ — Soma-juice; avapāneṣu — in the cups with their mouths turned down; ā bhagaḥ — to be fully shared; mitrāya varuṇāya — for Mitra and Varuṇa; śaṃtamaḥ — (by drinking) giving especial happiness; bhūtu — let it be; devaḥ — the shining Soma-juice; deveṣu — among the other gods (by the gods); ā bhagaḥ — [it being] received [by them] (let it be); śaṃtamaḥ bhūtu — let it be giving happiness; [or: deveṣu — among the praisers, the sacrificers; devaḥ — shining (the Soma-juice); ā bhagaḥ — to be shared by them (śaṃtamaḥ bhūtu — let it give happiness)]; ; yat — for which reason; yat — what; īmahe — we get (we wish); tat devān yācāmahe — we ask the gods for it; tat — therefore; tam — that Soma; viśve devāsaḥ — all the gods; adya — today (now); juṣerate — accept; tathā — so (as the other gods); sajoṣasaḥ — joined in equal pleasure; rājānā — shining (Mitra and Varuṇa), you two; karathaḥ — do (drink the Soma); ṛtāvānā — possessed of truth (possessing sacrifices and other rites) — you two; īmahe — we ask for the desired fruit.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. May the Soma-juice that has now been offered, in the cups turned face downward, give especial happiness to Mitra and Varuṇa who accept it; may all the gods who give us what we desire, being pleased, accept it; may Mitra and Varuṇa, possessed of truth (in the performance of the sacrifice and so on), joined in equal pleasure, grant our desired objects.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "May this Soma libation be gratifying to Mitra and Varuna, to be enjoyed by them as they drink of it, inclining downwards; a divine (beverage), fit to be enjoyed by the gods: may all the gods, well pleased, to-day accept it; therefore, royal (deities), do as we request: you, who are ever truthful, do as we request."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).

Here the order of the Soma-drinking of Mitra and Varuṇa is described.

avapāneṣu — the word avapāna has a technical use in some places; in others it simply means "a place fit for drinking". Sāyaṇa explains it as avāṅmukhacamasapātreṣu — "in cups with their mouths turned downward". Likewise:

original p. 690

ऋष्वो न कृष्णप्रो [?] वपानमा गहि पिबा सोमं वशाँ अनु । निमेघमानो मघवन्दिवेदिव ओजिष्ठं दधिषे सहः ॥

ṛṣvo na kṛṣṇapro [?] vapānam ā gahi pibā somaṃ vaśāṁ anu | nimeghamāno maghavan dive-diva ojiṣṭhaṃ dadhiṣe sahaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?], as read "೮-೪-೧೦" [?]; the first words are doubtful [?].) In this too, avanītam ["brought down"] is meant [by the word avapāna] — it shows the Soma ready for drinking in the cups, the camasa and the other vessels, and the nature of the vessel.

उष्प्वारेव [?] फर्वरेषु श्रयेथे प्रायोगेव श्वात्र्या शासुरेथः । दूकेव हि ष्मो यशसा जनेषु मापस्थातं महिषेवावपानात् ॥

uṣpvāreva [?] pharvareṣu śrayethe prāyogeva śvātryā śāsurethaḥ | dūkeva hi ṣmo yaśasā janeṣu māpa sthātaṃ mahiṣevāvapānāt ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೧೦೬-೩" [?]; the first line is doubtful in several letters [?].) In Ṛks like this, avapāna means a pond or a tank where buffaloes and the like drink. In the second of the Ṛks quoted, Sāyaṇa explains the word avapāna as pīyate 'sminn iti pānaṃ hradādi | pānam evāvapānam — "a pond and the like, where drinking [takes place]"; "the place where animals drink water is called avapāna". In the present case, we must understand the order of holding the camasa when the Soma is offered to Mitra and Varuṇa. Here the meaning is camasapātra — "the camasa vessel".

bhagaḥ — bhago bhajateḥ: from the root bhaj, which gives the meaning "to be worshipful, or fit for a share". The author of the Nirukta gives this derivation of the word (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೭" [?]). Either meaning is possible here, as an epithet of somaḥ. The word is repeated here. For the first, "worshipful"; for the second, "fit for a share".

ṛtāvānā — satyavantau yajñavantau vā mitrāvaruṇau. The word ṛta means "truth" or "sacrifice": "those who protect the truth, [or] the performers of truth, or [as in] yajño vā aryamā" (Tai. Brā. 2-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೨-೩-೫-೪" [?]) — such sentences show that the meaning is "doers of the sacrifice".

ऋतस्य गोपावधि तिष्ठथो रथं सत्यधर्माणा परमे व्योमनि । यमत्र मित्रावरुणावथो युवं तस्मै वृष्टिर्मधुमत्पिन्वते दिवः ॥

ṛtasya gopāv adhi tiṣṭhatho rathaṃ satyadharmāṇā parame vyomani | yam atra mitrāvaruṇāvatho yuvaṃ tasmai vṛṣṭir madhumat pinvate divaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?], as read "೫-೬೩-೧" [?].) In Ṛks like this, Mitra and Varuṇa are described as protectors of all the worlds, with the quality of truth, and as protectors of the sacrifices and the like; here too the same is described.

sajoṣasaḥ — samānaprītiyuktāḥ: "joined in equal pleasure": [the poet says] "you two make the Soma-drinking, with equal pleasure". The use of the order of one [cup] in which both Mitra and Varuṇa drink Soma together, at the same time and with equal pleasure, is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā in this way:

original p. 691

वरुणं देवा अब्रुवन्यज्ञꣳ संभुवा सोमꣳ राजानꣳ हनामेति सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणै मह्यं चैवैष मित्राय च सह गृह्यातै [?] इति तस्मान्मैत्रावरुणः सह गृह्यते ।

varuṇaṃ devā abruvan yajñaṃ saṃbhuvā somaṃ rājānaṃ hanāmeti so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai mahyaṃ caivaiṣa mitrāya ca saha gṛhyātai [?] iti tasmān maitrāvaruṇaḥ saha gṛhyate |

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೪-೯-೧, ೨" [?]; read from the image [?].) Kannada sense: When the gods, to kill Soma, first requested Mitra, he said, "I am everyone's friend, so I shall not agree"; and then the gods approached Varuṇa and asked the same; Varuṇa asked a boon in that connexion: "the Soma-graha must be prepared with me and with Mitra together." Accordingly, whenever the Soma-juice is pressed, the maitrāvaruṇa-graha is at one time. This, a drinking at one time and with joint pleasure, from a single vessel, is described here by the word sajoṣasaḥ.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). śaṃtamaḥ — tamap in the sense of intensity; since it is pit it is anudātta. bhūtu — root bhū sattāyām; loṭ, third person singular, tip; eruḥ (Pā. 3-4-86 [as read]) gives u for the i; bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-73 [as read]) gives luk of śap; bhūsuvos tiṅi (Pā. 7-3-88 [as read]) forbids guṇa; nighāta after a tiṅanta. avapāneṣu — root pā pāne; lyuṭ; ana for yu; since the suffix is lit [?], the udātta on the syllable before the suffix; in the prādi-compound, kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara. devāsaḥ — since jas follows, ājjaser asuk (Pā. 7-1-50 [as read]) gives the asuk augment. juṣerata — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; liṅ; third person plural, the suffix jha; by vyatyaya the ran-substitution does not occur; ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ (Pā. 7-1-5 [as read]) gives ata; by bahulaṃ chandasi the ruṭ augment; as it stands in the pada after a tiṅanta, the nighāta. sajoṣasaḥ — samānaṃ joṣo yeṣāṃ te sajoṣasaḥ; the root as above, with the suffix asun; kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara. rājānā — root rājṛ dīptau; the Uṇ. suffix kanin; dual; supāṃ sulug gives ā for the case-ending; āmantrita-nighāta.

original p. 692

Grammar of Ṛk 4, concluded. karathaḥ — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; laṭ, second person dual; since it is para, by vyatyaya [?] and bahulaṃ chandasi śap as vikaraṇa [as read]; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ (Pā. 7-3-84 [as read]) gives guṇa to the root's ṛ; nighāta after a tiṅanta. īmahe — root īḍ gatau; divādi; laṭ, first person plural, mahiṅ; ṭita e [as read: ṭeḥ e]; by bahulaṃ chandasi luk of the vikaraṇa (śyan); since the suffix is jit, ati [?], guṇa does not occur; because it is connected with yat, the nighāta does not occur; as the root is jit, the tāsyanudāttenṅit… (Pā. 6-1-186 [as read]) makes the suffix anudātta, and the root's accent remains. ṛtāvānā — chandasīvanipau (Pā. 5-2-109 [as read]) gives vanip in the sense of matup; anyeṣām api dṛśyate (Pā. 6-3-137 [as read]) gives lengthening to the earlier member; since the suffix is pit, it is anudātta; supāṃ sulug gives ā for the dual. ‖ 4 ‖

Rik 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यो मित्राय वरुणायाविधज्जनोऽनर्वाणं तं परि पातो अꣳहसो दाश्वाꣳसं मर्तमꣳहसः । तमर्यमाभि रक्षत्यृजूयन्तमनु व्रतम् । उक्थैर्य एनोः परिभूषति व्रतं स्तोमैराभूषति व्रतम् ॥ ५ ॥

yo mitrāya varuṇāyāvidhajjano 'narvāṇaṃ taṃ pari pāto am̐haso dāśvām̐saṃ martamam̐hasaḥ | tamaryamābhi rakṣatyṛjūyantamanu vratam | ukthairya enoḥ paribhūṣati vrataṃ stomairābhūṣati vratam ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यः । मित्राय । वरुणाय । अविधत् । जनः । अनर्वाणम् । तम् । परि । पातः । अꣳहसः । दाश्वाꣳसम् । मर्तम् । अꣳहसः । तम् । अर्यमा । अभि । रक्षति । ऋजुऽयन्तम् । अनु । व्रतम् । उक्थैः । यः । एनोः । परिऽभूषति । व्रतम् । स्तोमैः । आऽभूषति । व्रतम् ॥ ५ ॥

yaḥ | mitrāya | varuṇāya | avidhat | janaḥ | anarvāṇam | tam | pari | pātaḥ | am̐hasaḥ | dāśvām̐sam | martam | am̐hasaḥ | tam | aryamā | abhi | rakṣati | ṛju 'yantam | anu | vratam | ukthaiḥ | yaḥ | enoḥ | pari 'bhūṣati | vratam | stomaiḥ | ā 'bhūṣati | vratam ‖ 5 ‖

original p. 693

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 5; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?]. Sense: "Whatever person, sacrificer, serves (avidhat) Mitra and Varuṇa [the dative because of sampradāna in the rite], that person, your servant, anarvāṇam — without an enemy [arvā = enemy; bhrātṛvyo vā arvā, says the Śruti] or not alone, serving no other — protect all round (pari pātaḥ); from what? from aṃhasaḥ — sin caused by deficiency or excess. Not only the common person, but dāśvāṃsam — the one who has given oblations — martam, the mortal, from aṃhasaḥ — all sin. Not only you two, but Aryaman too, the god who regulates all, protects (abhi rakṣati) the sacrificer who behaves honestly (ṛjūyantam) towards the gods, in accordance with (anu) his rite (vratam). What is special about this man? — The sacrificer who, with ukthaiḥ, recitations, embraces the vrata — rite — of these two, Mitra and Varuṇa, and who with stomaiḥ, hymns accomplished by mantras accompanied by song, adorns your rite on all sides: so they protect him."

यो जनो यजमानो मित्राय वरुणाय च ॥ कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थी ॥ मित्रं वरुणं चाविधत् परिचरति तं जनं युष्मत्परिचारकमनर्वाणमद्वेषिणम् । भ्रातृव्यो वा अर्वेति श्रुतेः । अनल्पं वानन्यसेविनं परि पातः । परितो रक्षतां । कस्मादित्युच्यते । अꣳहसो न्यूनात्रिकैकजनितात्पापात् । न केवलं सामान्यं जनमपि तु दाश्वाꣳसं हविर्दत्त्वन्तं मर्तं मरणधर्माणमꣳहसः सर्वस्मादपि पापात् । न केवलं भवन्तावेव अपि त्वर्यमा सर्वेषां नियन्ता देव ऋजूयन्तं देवेष्वार्जवमाचरन्तं यजमानमनु व्रतं तदीयं कर्मानुलक्ष्याभि रक्षति । अभितो रक्षति । कोऽस्य जनस्य विशेष इति तत्राह । यो यजमान उक्थैः शस्त्रैरेनोरेनयोर्मित्रावरुणयोर्व्रतं कर्म परिभूषति परिगृह्णाति तथा यजमानो युष्मदीयं व्रतं कर्म स्तोमैः स्तोत्रैर्गानयुक्तमन्त्रसाध्यैराभूषति सर्वतोऽलंकरोति ॥ भूष अलंकारे । भौवादिकः ॥ तमभिरक्षन्तीत्यन्वयः ॥

yo jano yajamāno mitrāya varuṇāya ca ‖ karmaṇaḥ saṃpradānatvāccaturthī ‖ mitraṃ varuṇaṃ cāvidhat paricarati taṃ janaṃ yuṣmatparicārakamanarvāṇamadveṣiṇam | bhrātṛvyo vā arveti śruteḥ | analpaṃ vānanyasevinaṃ pari pātaḥ | parito rakṣatāṃ | kasmādityucyate | am̐haso nyūnātrikaikajanitātpāpāt | na kevalaṃ sāmānyaṃ janamapi tu dāśvām̐saṃ havirdattvantaṃ martaṃ maraṇadharmāṇamam̐hasaḥ sarvasmādapi pāpāt | na kevalaṃ bhavantāveva api tvaryamā sarveṣāṃ niyantā deva ṛjūyantaṃ deveṣvārjavamācarantaṃ yajamānamanu vrataṃ tadīyaṃ karmānulakṣyābhi rakṣati | abhito rakṣati | ko 'sya janasya viśeṣa iti tatrāha | yo yajamāna ukthaiḥ śastrairenorenayormitrāvaruṇayorvrataṃ karma paribhūṣati parigṛhṇāti tathā yajamāno yuṣmadīyaṃ vrataṃ karma stomaiḥ stotrairgānayuktamantrasādhyairābhūṣati sarvato 'laṃkaroti ‖ bhūṣa alaṃkāre | bhauvādikaḥ ‖ tamabhirakṣantītyanvayaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. yaḥ janaḥ — whichever man (sacrificer); mitrāya varuṇāya (ca) — to Mitra and Varuṇa both; avidhat — serves (waits upon); tam — that man; anarvāṇam — free of enemies (made not to have a wicked servant [?] or [?]); aṃhasaḥ — (from sin that arises from deficiency or excess); pari pātaḥ — protect completely; dāśvāṃsam — who has given oblations; martam — the mortal man; aṃhasaḥ — (from all kinds of) sin; pari pātaḥ; yaḥ — whichever sacrificer; ukthaiḥ — with the śastra-mantras; enoḥ — of these two Mitra and Varuṇa [aimed at me]; vratam — the rite; paribhūṣati — takes up; tathā — likewise; yaḥ — [whichever sacrificer]; vratam — your rite; stomaiḥ — with songs; ābhūṣati — adorns; tam — that sacrificer; ṛjūyantam — behaving straight towards the gods; aryamā — Aryaman; anu vratam — according to his rite; abhi rakṣati — protects.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. [O Mitra and Varuṇa,] making him who serves you free of enemies, you remove sin caused by deficiency and excess; you protect the mortal who has given oblations; Aryaman protects the man who behaves honestly, reciting the śastra mantras and acting in the rites of both of you and who adorns your rites with praise, in accordance with his rite; [you also protect him].

original p. 694

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Whatever individual offers adoration to Mitra and Varuna, do you preserve him entirely unharmed from sin; (preserve) from sin the mortal who presents you (with oblations): may Aryaman protect him who is sincere in his devotion, who offers worship addressed to both (Mitra and Varuna) with prayers; who offers worship with praises."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).

Mitra and Varuṇa are prayed to protect the sacrificer who serves them, by destroying his enemies and his sins.

anarvāṇam — adveṣiṇam: "make him free of enemies" is the meaning. The words arvat, arvan are included by the author of the Nirukta among the names of "horse" (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೨" [?]). But in many places this word has a variety of meanings.

यस्मै त्वं सुमायजसे स साधत्यनर्वा क्षेति दधते सुवीर्यम् । स तोतावनैनमश्नोत्यंहतिरग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥

yasmai tvaṃ sumāyajase sa sādhaty anarvā kṣeti dadhate suvīryam | sa tota vanainam aśnoty aṃhatir agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೪೩-೩" [?]; read letter by letter from the Kannada print; the second line's word-division is doubtful [?].) In this Ṛk the word arvan is a synonym of "enemy"; anarvā means "one who is not subject to an enemy" is the meaning. In the Ṛk under discussion also, Sāyaṇa upholds the meaning "enemy" for the word arvan in anarvāṇam with the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence:

अनर्वा प्रेहीत्याह भ्रातृव्यो वा अर्वा भ्रातृव्यापनुत्त्यै ॥

anarvā prehīty āha bhrātṛvyo vā arvā bhrātṛvyāpanuttyai ‖

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೩-೧-೪" [?].) — showing that arvan in the sense of bhrātṛvya, i.e. "enemy", is applicable. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?] ("೩-೩೧-೧೧" [?]) and 10-[?]-[?] ("೧೦-೩೯-೧೪" [?]) and in other such Ṛks this word is a synonym of "enemy". On the derivation of this word, the scholars Wilson and Max Müller differ. Wilson, on the Ṛk —

क्रीळं वः शर्धो मारुतमनर्वाणं रथेशुभम् । कण्वा अभि प्र गायत ॥

krīḷaṃ vaḥ śardho mārutam anarvāṇaṃ ratheśubham | kaṇvā abhi pra gāyata ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-37-1 [as read].) — when explaining the word anarvāṇam, criticises Sāyaṇa's commentary, saying thus:

original p. 695

Wilson's note, printed in English: "The phrase is anarvāṇam which the Scholiast explains bhrātṛvyarahitaṃ literally, without a brother's son, which would be a very unintelligible epithet: arvan is in its usual acceptation a horse; and being without horses would not be inapplicable to the Maruts, whose chariot is drawn by deer. bhrātṛvya may mean an enemy, but it is doubtful if arvat can admit of such an interpretation." [Rig-Veda Translation, Vol. I, p. 258.] — The scholar says that, as the vehicle of the Maruts is deer, the meaning "without horses" cannot be inappropriate here. But in opposition to this, Max Müller, when translating the same Sūkta, criticises Wilson for translating the word as "horse":

"Wilson translates anarvāṇam by without horses, though the commentator distinctly explains the word by "without an enemy". The fact is, that, in the Rig-Veda anarvā never means without horses but always without hurt or free from enemies, and the commentator is perfectly right, as sense is concerned, in rendering the world [sic] by "without an enemy or unopposed" (apratyuta)" [Sacred Books of the East, Vol. XXXII, p. 65.]

Know that although the word arvan in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā has the meaning "horse", the word anarvā always has the meaning "free of enemies". Likewise, in the Ṛk under discussion too, Mitra and Varuṇa are prayed to make the sacrificer free of enemies.

enoḥ vrataṃ ukthaiḥ paribhūṣati — it shows the fixed relation between the rite and the uktha, and by the word ukthaiḥ it is shown that "the rite acquires fullness and beauty", and that the rite thus becomes most excellent.

Uktha means a śastra in the form of mantras recited along with a stotra or after the recitation of a stotra. The stotra is to be sung by the udgātṛ; then, to assist him, the hotṛ and others — one of the Maitrāvaruṇa and others — recite the śastra. By taking one or two examples one may know the relation between the stotra and the śastra: at the morning pressing, together with the bahiṣpavamāna stotra the ājya-śastra is recited; at the midday pressing, together with the mādhyandina-pavamāna stotra, the vaiśvadeva-śastra is recited.

original p. 696

Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued from p. 695: Since, in the Ṛk before us, the praise of Mitra and Varuṇa comes in a context of praising the uktha, the greatness of the uktha, and through it the greatness of Mitra and Varuṇa, are described in the light of an old story. A story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa tells how the power of the uktha is exceedingly great, how the Asuras took shelter behind it and so became formidable to the gods, and how Indra, on being praised, came and drove them away.

ते वा असुरा मैत्रावरुणस्योक्थमभ्यपद्यन्त सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कः क्षाहं [?] चेमानितोऽसुरानोत्स्यावहा इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्वरुणस्तस्माद्वैन्द्रावरुणं मैत्रावरुणस्तृतीयसवने शंसतीन्द्रश्च हि तान्वरुणश्च नुदेताम् ।

te vā asurā maitrāvaruṇasyokthamabhyapadyanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaḥ kṣāhaṃ [?] cemān ito 'surān otsyāvahā ity ahaṃ cety abravīd varuṇas tasmād vaindrāvaruṇaṃ maitrāvaruṇas tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān varuṇaś ca nudetām |

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೦" [?]; read from the image, doubtful in the words marked [?].) Kannada sense: The Asuras entered the maitrāvaruṇa-uktha. Then Indra, seeking to drive them out by the uktha, asked, "Who will help me?" Varuṇa said that he would help. Accordingly, in the third pressing, the maitrāvaruṇa priest, an assistant of the hotṛ, [recites]

इन्द्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतम् ।

indrāvaruṇā yuvam adhvarāya no viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchatam |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೬೮-೧" [?].) — taking the Sūkta that begins with this Ṛk, and praising Indra and Varuṇa; Indra and Varuṇa then drove the Asuras off from the uktha. In the same way those Asuras, entering the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's uktha and being driven out from there, joined the acchāvāka's uktha and, being driven out from there too by Indra and Viṣṇu — such is another story of the power of the uktha.

यदाह बृहदुक्थे वयस्वते [?] इत्युक्थ्यं ग्रहं गृह्णामीत्युक्थेभ्यो ह्येनं गृह्णाति ।

yad āha bṛhaduktha vayasvate [?] ity ukthyaṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇāmīty ukthebhyo hy enaṃ gṛhṇāti |

(Śa. Brā. 4-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೪-೩-೩-೧೦" [?]; the opening is doubtful [?].) Also in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, "bṛhaduktha" is said of Indra ["him who has great ukthas, and is vigorous"], and thus the uktha — the cause of the satisfaction of Indra's valour — and through it Indra himself are praised.

उक्थ्यो भवति पशवो वा उक्थानि पशूनामवरुद्ध्यै । तस्य पञ्चदशस्तोत्राणि भवन्ति पञ्चदशशस्त्राणि ……… ॥

ukthyo bhavati paśavo vā ukthāni paśūnām avaruddhyai | tasya pañcadaśastotrāṇi bhavanti pañcadaśaśastrāṇi ……… ‖

(Ai. Brā. 4-[?], as read "೪-೧೩" [?].) The ukthya is in the form of animals; it is the means of obtaining animal-wealth. It is said in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that fifteen śastras and fifteen stotras are included in it.

As the power of the uktha was described at the time of sacrifices and other rites, so in the context of instruction in spiritual knowledge too, the greatness of the uktha, in the form of stotra and śastra, is praised.

original p. 697

उक्थं प्राणो वा उक्थं प्राणो हीदं सर्वमुत्थापयत्युद्स्माद्उक्थविद्वीरस्तिष्ठत्युक्थस्य सायुज्यꣳ सलोकतां जयति य एवं वेद ।

uktham prāṇo vā uktham prāṇo hīdaṃ sarvam utthāpayaty ud asmād uktha-vid vīras tiṣṭhaty ukthasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda |

(Bṛ. Up. 5-1-[?], as read "೫-೧-೧" [?]; read from the image, partly doubtful [?].)

उक्थं कथोपासनानन्तरम् । उक्थं शस्त्रं तद्धि प्रधानं महाव्रते क्रतौ ।

uktham kathopāsanānantaram | uktham śastraṃ tad dhi pradhānaṃ mahāvrate kratau |

(Śaṅkara's bhāṣya.) In the sacrifice called mahāvrata, the uktha is the principal śastra; the uktha is the breath (prāṇa): it lifts everything up; thus the son who knows the uktha is born well, and gains the greatness of the uktha, [attains] union with it and the same world. Explaining the greatness of the uktha, [he says] that by reciting such an uktha one performs the vrata for Mitra and Varuṇa, as the Ṛk under discussion tells.

ukthaiḥ paribhūṣati — stomair ābhūṣati — as stated, [the second half of the sentence] shows the order of procedure that performs the rite completely. Like the uktha, the stoma too has power. The nature and the various forms of the stoma are explained at length in the 138th to 150th pages of the third part of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā [as read, [?]]; here only the benefit obtained by the stoma is told.

प्रातःसवने वै गायत्रेण छन्दसा त्रिवृते स्तोमाय ज्योतिर्दधाति त्रिवृता ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पञ्चदशाय ज्योतिर्दधाति पञ्चदशेनौजसा वीर्येण सप्तदशाय ज्योतिर्दधाति सप्तदशेन प्राजापत्येन प्रजननेनैकविꣳशाय ज्योतिर्दधाति स्तोम एव तत्स्तोमाय ज्योतिर्दधात्यथो स्तोममेव स्तोममभि प्रणयति यावन्तो वै स्तोमास्तावन्तः कामास्तावन्तो लोकास्तावन्ति ज्योतीꣳष्येतावत एव स्तोमानेतावतः कामानेतावतो लोकानेतावन्ति ज्योतीꣳष्यवरुन्धे ॥

prātaḥsavane vai gāyatreṇa chandasā trivṛte stomāya jyotir dadhāti trivṛtā brahmavarcasena pañcadaśāya jyotir dadhāti pañcadaśenaujasā vīryeṇa saptadaśāya jyotir dadhāti saptadaśena prājāpatyena prajananenaikaviṃśāya jyotir dadhāti stoma eva tat stomāya jyotir dadhāty atho stomam eva stomam abhi praṇayati yāvanto vai stomās tāvantaḥ kāmās tāvanto lokās tāvanti jyotīṃṣy etāvata eva stomān etāvataḥ kāmān etāvato lokān etāvanti jyotīṃṣy avarundhe ‖

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-[?]-[?], as read "೭-೨-೨-೧" [?]; read from the image [?].) By such sentences of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā the powers of the stomas are to be understood. The sacrificer, at the morning pressing, in the place of the gāyatrī metre sets up the trivṛt-stoma with brahmavarcasa; likewise from the trivṛt, which is of the form of light, the pañcadaśa-stoma; from the pañcadaśa, full of valour, the saptadaśa-stoma; and, being connected with Prajāpati, from the saptadaśa, which is helpful to procreation, he makes the ekaviṃśa-stoma shine.
