Thus a stoma of one kind gives another kind of power and brilliance to another stoma. There are as many kinds of stoma in the stoma as there are worlds, brilliances and desired objects. And by the stoma the sacrificer obtains as many worlds, brilliances and desired objects.

original p. 698

Kannada, continuing the stoma passage of p. 697: …"the sacrificer obtains" — thus the power of the stoma is known; and as follows from the stoma-pressing, the benefit that comes is also known.

ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति सत्र्ये यजेत योऽग्निष्टोमेन यजमानोऽथ सर्वस्तोमेन यजेतेति यस्य त्रिवृतमन्तर्यन्ति प्राणाꣳस्तस्यान्तर्यन्ति प्राणेषु मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य पञ्चदशमन्तर्यन्ति वीर्यं तस्यान्तर्यन्ति वीर्ये मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य सप्तदशमन्तर्यन्ति प्रजां तस्यान्तर्यन्ति प्रजायां मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्यैकविꣳशमन्तर्यन्ति प्रतिष्ठां तस्यान्तर्यन्ति प्रतिष्ठायां मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य त्रिणवमन्तर्यन्त्यृतूꣳश्च तस्य नक्षत्रियां च विराजमन्तर्यन्त्यृतुषु मेऽस्यसन्नक्षत्रियायां च विराजीति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य त्रयस्त्रिꣳशमन्तर्यन्ति देवतास्तस्यान्तर्यन्ति देवतासु मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यो वै स्तोमानामवमं परमतां गच्छन्तं वेद परमतामेव गच्छति त्रिवृद्वै स्तोमानामवमस्त्रिवृत्परमो य एवं वेद परमतामेव गच्छति ॥

brahmavādino vadanti satrye yajeta yo 'gniṣṭomena yajamāno 'tha sarvastomena yajeteti yasya trivṛtam antaryanti prāṇāṃs tasyāntaryanti prāṇeṣu me 'syasad iti khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya pañcadaśam antaryanti vīryaṃ tasyāntaryanti vīrye me 'syasad iti khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya saptadaśam antaryanti prajāṃ tasyāntaryanti prajāyāṃ me 'syasad iti khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasyaikaviṃśam antaryanti pratiṣṭhāṃ tasyāntaryanti pratiṣṭhāyāṃ me 'syasad iti khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya triṇavam antaryanty ṛtūṃś ca tasya nakṣatriyāṃ ca virājam antaryanty ṛtuṣu me 'syasan nakṣatriyāyāṃ ca virājīti khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya trayastriṃśam antaryanti devatās tasyāntaryanti devatāsu me 'syasad iti khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yo vai stomānām avamaṃ paramatāṃ gacchantaṃ veda paramatām eva gacchati trivṛd vai stomānām avamas trivṛt paramo ya evaṃ veda paramatām eva gacchati ‖

(Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-[?]-[?], as read "೭-೧-೩-೧, ೨, ೩" [?]; read from the image, doubtful in several words [?].) Kannada sense: The brahmavādins say that those who perform the agniṣṭoma should perform the sacrifice with all the stomas, say the scholars of the Śāstra. By omitting the trivṛt-stoma, the chief breath of the sacrificer is damaged; so the sacrificer performs the sacrifice with the aim that "this sacrifice may be within my chief breath". Similarly, by omitting the pañcadaśa-stoma, strength is lost; by omitting the ekaviṃśa-stoma the firm footing is lost; by omitting the triṇava, the use of the seasons and the stars for his purpose is lost; and by omitting the trayastriṃśa-stoma, the chief deity is lost; therefore the sacrificer performs the sacrifice with the pañcadaśa for the acquisition of strength, the saptadaśa for the obtaining of progeny, the ekaviṃśa for support of life, the triṇava for the benefit of the seasons and stars, and the trayastriṃśa for the obtaining of his chief deities. The sacrificer who knows the greatness of the trivṛt-stoma, which has the first place among all the stomas, gets the first place among sacrificers; and with the agniṣṭoma joined with the trivṛt-stoma he gets splendour; with the pañcadaśa, valour; with the saptadaśa, food; with the ekaviṃśa, firm support; with the triṇava, victory; and with the trayastriṃśa, greatness.

original p. 699

स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां दृष्ट्वा धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः ॥

stomam mahad urugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhīro naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ ‖

(Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೧೧" [?].) — thus the greatness of the stoma, and the spiritual peace to be had from it, is spoken of in the Kaṭhopaniṣad.

येन च्छन्दसा स्तोष्यन्स्यात्तच्छन्द उपधावेद्येन स्तोमेन स्तोष्यमाणः स्यात्तꣳ स्तोममुपधावेत् ॥

yena chandasā stoṣyan syāt tac chanda upadhāved yena stomena stoṣyamāṇaḥ syāt taṃ stomam upadhāvet ‖

(Chāndogya Upaniṣad [?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೩-೧೦" [?]; read from the image, partly doubtful [?].) — thus even in the Chāndogya, describing the greatness of the udgītha, it is known that one must meditate, resorting to that stoma, with which the praise becomes complete in accordance with the need at hand.

In the same way, in the Ṛk before us, the stotra is of the nature of song, performed by the hotṛ and others at the time of the rite, giving exceeding benefit, and serving as an ornament of the rite. Sāyaṇa explains it as stomaiḥ stotrair gānayuktamantrasādhyaiḥ — "stomas, stotras, accomplished by mantras accompanied by song".

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). mitrāya — since the rite has the sampradāna-term, caturthī sampradāne (Pā. 2-3-13 [as read]) gives the dative. avidhat — root vidha vidhāne; by Vedic usage laṅ in the present sense; third person singular; yadvṛttānnityam (Pā. 8-1-66 [as read]) prevents the nighāta; as the āgama is udātta, the word is ādyudātta. anarvāṇam — na vidyate arvā yasya saḥ tam; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172 [as read]) gives the final udātta of the latter member. pātaḥ — root pā rakṣaṇe; loṭ, second person dual; nighāta after a tiṅanta. dāśvāṃsam — root dāśṛ dāne; dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca (Pā. 6-1-12 [as read]) — kvasu suffix is ending in nipātana; the accusative singular. martam — root mṛṅ prāṇatyāge; asi-hasi… (Uṇ. 3-[?], as read "೩-೧೧೮" [?]) gives tan; because of it the guṇa of the root's ṛ; since it is nit, the ādyudātta. rakṣati — root rakṣa pālane; laṭ, third person singular; nighāta after a tiṅanta.

original p. 700

Grammar of Ṛk 5, concluded. ṛjūyantam — ṛjūm ātmana icchati ṛjūyati; supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. 3-1-8 [as read]) gives kyac; after the kyac-ending, laṭ and for it śatṛ; the dual-ending follows, so by the ugit-rule the num augment; the accent of kyac. paribhūṣati — root bhūṣa alaṃkāre; bhvādi; laṭ, third person singular; because it is connected with yat [or yaḥ], the nighāta accent does not occur; since śap and tip are anudātta, the root's accent remains; since the udāttavat [word] tiṅ follows, tiṅ codāttavati (Pā. 8-1-71 [as read]) gives the gati (pari) the nighāta. ‖ 5 ‖

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

नमो दिवे बृहते रोदसीभ्यां मित्राय वोचं वरुणाय मीळ्हुषे सुमृळीकाय मीळ्हुषे । इन्द्रमग्निमुप स्तुहि द्युक्षमर्यमणं भगम् । ज्योग्जीवन्तः प्रजया सचेमहि सोमस्योती सचेमहि ॥ ६ ॥

namo dive bṛhate rodasībhyāṃ mitrāya vocaṃ varuṇāya mīḷhuṣe sumṛḷīkāya mīḷhuṣe | indramagnimupa stuhi dyukṣamaryamaṇaṃ bhagam | jyogjīvantaḥ prajayā sacemahi somasyotī sacemahi ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

नमः । दिवे । बृहते । रोदसीभ्याम् । मित्राय । वोचम् । वरुणाय । मीळ्हुषे । सुऽमृळीकाय । मीळ्हुषे । इन्द्रम् । अग्निम् । उप । स्तुहि । द्युक्षम् । अर्यमणम् । भगम् । ज्योक् । जीवन्तः । प्रजया । सचेमहि । सोमस्य । ऊती । सचेमहि ॥ ६ ॥

namaḥ | dive | bṛhate | rodasībhyām | mitrāya | vocam | varuṇāya | mīḷhuṣe | su 'mṛḷīkāya | mīḷhuṣe | indram | agnim | upa | stuhi | dyukṣam | aryamaṇam | bhagam | jyok | jīvantaḥ | prajayā | sacemahi | somasya | ūtī | sacemahi ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 6; read from the image; begins at the foot of p. 700.

दिवे द्योतमानाय सूर्याय नमो वोचम् । नमस्कारोपलक्षितं स्तोत्रं वोचं ब्रवीमि स्तौमीत्यर्थः । कीदृशाय तस्मै । बृहते महते [?]

dive dyotamānāya sūryāya namo vocam | namaskāropalakṣitaṃ stotraṃ vocaṃ bravīmi staumītyarthaḥ | kīdṛśāya tasmai | bṛhate mahate [?]

original p. 701

बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ स्तुत्याय । तथा रोदसीभ्यां द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां तदभिमानिदेवाभ्यां नमो वोचम् । तथा मित्राय सर्वजनहिताय अहरभिमानिदेवाय नमो वोचम् । तथा वरुणायावरकाय रात्र्यभिमानिदेवाय । तथा मीळ्हुषे अभिमतफलस्य सेक्त्रे रुद्राय । कीदृशाय तस्मै । सुमृळीकाय शोभनसुखयित्रे । पुनः स एव विशेष्यते । मीळ्हुषे सुमृळीकायेति द्वे प्रत्येकं विशेषणभूते । इदानीं यजमान ऋत्विजं स्वात्मानं वा प्रति ब्रवीति । हे होतः हे आत्मन् वा इन्द्रमग्निं द्युक्षं दीप्तिमन्तमर्यमणं भगं चोपोपेत्य बुद्ध्या प्राप्य स्तुहि । स्तुतिं कुरु । युष्मदनुग्रहाज्ज्योक् चिरकालं जीवन्तो जीवनोपेता वयं प्रजया पुत्रभृत्यादिना सचेमहि संगता भूयास्म । किंच सोमस्येन्दोरूती ऊत्या सचेमहि । कमपि स्तुत्या तत्कारिकेण रक्षणेन सहिता भूयास्मेत्यर्थः ॥

bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānamiti vibhakterudāttatvam ‖ stutyāya | tathā rodasībhyāṃ dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ tadabhimānidevābhyāṃ namo vocam | tathā mitrāya sarvajanahitāya aharabhimānidevāya namo vocam | tathā varuṇāyāvarakāya rātryabhimānidevāya | tathā mīḷhuṣe abhimataphalasya sektre rudrāya | kīdṛśāya tasmai | sumṛḷīkāya śobhanasukhayitre | punaḥ sa eva viśeṣyate | mīḷhuṣe sumṛḷīkāyeti dve pratyekaṃ viśeṣaṇabhūte | idānīṃ yajamāna ṛtvijaṃ svātmānaṃ vā prati bravīti | he hotaḥ he ātman vā indramagniṃ dyukṣaṃ dīptimantamaryamaṇaṃ bhagaṃ copopetya buddhyā prāpya stuhi | stutiṃ kuru | yuṣmadanugrahājjyok cirakālaṃ jīvanto jīvanopetā vayaṃ prajayā putrabhṛtyādinā sacemahi saṃgatā bhūyāsma | kiṃca somasyendorūtī ūtyā sacemahi | kamapi stutyā tatkārikeṇa rakṣaṇena sahitā bhūyāsmetyarthaḥ ‖

Sense: "To the shining Sun I speak namas — praise marked with reverence. To what kind of [deity]? Bṛhate — great [the accent by the upasaṃkhyāna rule]; praiseworthy. Likewise to rodasībhyām — heaven and earth, [or] to the deities presiding over them, I speak the namas; to Mitra, who is good to all people and the god presiding over the day; to Varuṇa, the covering god presiding over the night; to mīḍhuṣe — the sprinkler of the desired fruit, Rudra. What kind? Sumṛḷīkāya — the giver of good happiness. Mīḍhuṣe and sumṛḷīkāya are separate epithets. Now the sacrificer addresses the priest or himself: O hotṛ or O self, approach with understanding Indra, Agni, the brilliant (dyukṣam) Aryaman, and Bhaga, and praise them. By your grace, living long (jyok), may we be joined with offspring — sons, servants and so on. And somasya ūtī — by the protection of Soma, the moon, may we be joined: may we, through praise, be accompanied by the protection that comes from it."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. bṛhate — to the great (huge-formed) [sun]; dive — to the shining Sun; namaḥ vocam — I speak praise (I praise); — likewise; rodasībhyām — to heaven and earth; mitrāya — to Mitra (the god of the day, who is good to all); varuṇāya — to Varuṇa (the covering god, the god of the night); mīḍhuṣe — to the sprinkler of the desired fruit; sumṛḷīkāya — the giver of beautiful happiness; mīḍhuṣe — to Rudra, the granter of boons; namaḥ vocam — I speak praise [or: I praise] (O hotṛ, or O self); indram — Indra; agnim — Agni; dyukṣam — the radiant; aryamaṇam — Aryaman; bhagam — Bhaga; upa stuhi — approaching with understanding, praise; jyok — for a long time; jīvantaḥ — living; vayam — we; prajayā — with sons, servants and so on; sacemahi — may we be joined; somasya — of Soma (the moon); ūtī — by protection; sacemahi — may we be joined.

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. I praise the great, shining Sun, heaven and earth, Mitra (god of the day, good to all), Varuṇa (god of the night), and Rudra, the sprinkler of fruit and giver of good happiness; O hotṛ (or O self), approach Indra, Agni, the radiant Aryaman and Bhaga and praise them; by their grace may we, living long, be joined with sons, servants and so on, and by the protection of Soma.

original p. 702

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "I proclaim veneration to the mighty Sun, to heaven and earth, to Mitra, to the benevolent Varuna, to the conferrer of happiness, the showerer of benefits. Praise Indra, Agni, the brilliant Aryaman, and Bhaga, so that, enjoying long life, we may be blessed with progeny; we may be happy through the protecting virtues of the Soma."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).

mitrāya vocaṃ varuṇāya mīḍhuṣe sumṛḷīkāya mīḍhuṣe — repetitions of this kind are common in the compositions of the ṛṣi Paruccheṣa. On this, some may raise an objection to the style of Paruccheṣa's [composition]. The author of the Nirukta gives such an example and, showing the objection of the opponent in it, states the proper answer. Taking the Ṛk —

क्षेत्रस्य पते मधुमन्तमूर्मिं धेनुरिव पयो अस्मासु धुक्ष्व । मधुश्चुतं घृतमिव सुपूतमृतस्य नः पतयो मृळयन्तु ॥

kṣetrasya pate madhumantam ūrmiṃ dhenur iva payo asmāsu dhukṣva | madhuścutaṃ ghṛtam iva supūtam ṛtasya naḥ patayo mṛḷayantu ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?], as read "೪-೫೭-೩" [?].) he shows the objection of the opponent in this way, that "in madhumantam [and] madhuścutam there is the fault of repetition" (Ni. 10-[?], as read "೧೦-೧೪" [?]):

तदद्य क्षमान्याम्पि [?] समानाभिव्याहारं भवति तज्जामि भवतीत्येकं मधुमन्तं मधुश्चुतमिति ।

tad adya kṣamānyāmpi [?] samānābhivyāhāraṃ bhavati taj jāmi bhavatīty ekaṃ madhumantaṃ madhuścutam iti |

Read from the image; the first words are doubtful [?]; the Kannada gives: "Those who object say: the words madhuścutam and madhumantam used in one Ṛk are a fault of repetition". The reply is:

यदेव समाने पादे समानाभिव्याहारं भवति तज्जामि भवतीत्येकम् । परं हिरण्यरूपः स हिरण्यसंदृक् इति यथा ॥

yad eva samāne pāde samānābhivyāhāraṃ bhavati taj jāmi bhavatīty ekam | paraṃ "hiraṇyarūpaḥ sa hiraṇyasaṃdṛk" iti yathā ‖

But if different words are used in different pādas of one Ṛk there is no fault; the fault of repetition is possible only if they are used in the same pāda. For example:

हिरण्यरूपः स हिरण्यसंदृगपां नपात्सेदु हिरण्यवर्णः । हिरण्ययात्परि योनेर्निषद्या हिरण्यदा ददत्यन्नमस्मै ॥

hiraṇyarūpaḥ sa hiraṇyasaṃdṛg apāṃ napāt sedu hiraṇyavarṇaḥ | hiraṇyayāt pari yoner niṣadyā hiraṇyadā dadaty annam asmai ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-35-10 [as read].) In this Ṛk, since [the words] are in one pāda, [there is repetition]; so some hold that this is a fault.

original p. 703

The Nirukta's answer, continued: yathā katham ca viśeṣo jāmi bhṛtyai [?] parām — "even if [the repeated words are] in one pāda, there is no fault, since [they differ] in subtle sense": this is another opinion. For example:

योगक्षेममु त आदायाहं भूयासमुत्तम आ वो मूर्धानमक्रमीम् । अधस्पदान्म उद्वदत मण्डूका इवोदकान्मण्डूका उदकादिव ॥

yogakṣemam u ta ādāyāhaṃ bhūyāsam uttama ā vo mūrdhānam akramīm | adhas padān ma ud vadata maṇḍūkā ivodakān maṇḍūkā udakād iva ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೧೬೬-೫" [?]; the quotation is badly worn and doubtful in several letters [?].) In this, the meaning is that, because repetition shows exceeding beauty and because there is a subtle difference even in the meaning, there is no fault. The same solution can be applied to the style of Paruccheṣa. The author of the Nirukta, in quoting the very sentences of Paruccheṣa, shows that in such a repetition there is a special merit also.

अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते यथाहो दर्शनीयाहो दर्शनीया ।

abhyāse bhūyāṃsam artham manyante yathāho darśanīyāho darśanīyā |

(Ni. 10-[?], as read "೧೦-೪೩" [?].) The repetition, in the sense of habit, gives a special power to the meaning. They praise this style as "the speciality of the style of Paruccheṣa" (tat paruccheṣasya śīlam).

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed). dive — ūḍidaṃ padādi (Pā. 6-1-171 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending. bṛhate — dative singular; bṛhan mahator upasaṃkhyānam (Vārttika) gives the case-ending the udātta. vocam — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; by Vedic usage luṅ in the present sense; first person singular; ām-substitution for the singular [aṅ for cli by asti-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ (Pā. 3-1-52 [as read])]; as it is para, vaca um (Pā. 7-4-20 [as read]) gives the augment u to the root; guṇa with the following a; by Vedic usage the āgama does not occur; nighāta after a tiṅanta. mīḍhuṣe — root miha secane; dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca (Pā. 6-1-12 [as read]) — the suffix kvasu is formed by nipātana; the dative; as it is para the term bha applies; vasoḥ samprasāraṇam (Pā. 6-4-131 [as read]) gives saṃprasāraṇa; pūrvarūpa. sumṛḷīkāya — suṣṭhu mṛḷīkaṃ sukhaṃ yasyāsau sumṛḷīkaḥ; nañsubhyām (Pā. 6-2-172 [as read]) gives the final udātta of the latter member; dative singular.

original p. 704

Grammar of Ṛk 6, concluded. stuhi — root ṣṭuñ stutau; loṭ, second person singular; nighāta after a tiṅanta. jīvantaḥ — root jīva prāṇadhāraṇe; śatṛ for laṭ; nominative plural; as the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta by tāsyanudāttenṅidvidupadeśāt… (Pā. 6-1-186 [as read]), the root's accent remains. prajayā — root janī prādurbhāve; prajāyate iti prajā; upasarge ca saṃjñāyām (Pā. 3-2-99 [as read]) gives the suffix ḍa; because it is ḍit, by force the ṭi of the root is elided; kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara; instrumental singular. sacemahi — root ṣaca samavāye; liṅ, first person plural; nighāta after a tiṅanta. ūtī — ūtiyūtijūti… (Pā. 3-3-97 [as read]) — the ktin-ending, being udātta, is formed by nipātana; the instrumental singular, being para; supāṃ sulug… gives lengthening of the preceding vowel. ‖ 6 ‖

Rik 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ऊती देवानां वयमिन्द्रवन्तो मꣳसीमहि स्वयशसो मरुद्भिः । अग्निर्मित्रो वरुणः शर्म यꣳसन्तदश्याम मघवानो वयं च ॥ ७ ॥

ūtī devānāṃ vayamindravanto mam̐sīmahi svayaśaso marudbhiḥ | agnirmitro varuṇaḥ śarma yam̐santadaśyāma maghavāno vayaṃ ca ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ऊती । देवानाम् । वयम् । इन्द्रऽवन्तः । मꣳसीमहि । स्वऽयशसः । मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्निः । मित्रः । वरुणः । शर्म । यꣳसन् । तत् । अश्याम । मघऽवानः । वयम् । च ॥ ७ ॥

ūtī | devānām | vayam | indra 'vantaḥ | mam̐sīmahi | sva 'yaśasaḥ | marut 'bhiḥ | agniḥ | mitraḥ | varuṇaḥ | śarma | yam̐san | tat | aśyāma | magha 'vānaḥ | vayam | ca ‖ 7 ‖

original p. 705

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ Ṛk 7; read from the image. Sense: "We, indravantaḥ — endowed with the pleased Indra — devānām ūtī — by the satisfaction of the gods, with oblations and the like — maṃsīmahi, 'may we think' [or: 'may we know']. What kind of us? Svayaśasaḥ — of our own fame, favoured by the Maruts, who are pleased by our praise. Or: protected by the gods' protection, may we be knowers (of their greatness). And Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, the gods, yaṃsan — have given us joy — each desired boon; and we, maghavānaḥ — possessing food [from those gods], may we pervade, may we gain, that joy." (Aśyāma — liṅ of aśnoti in the benedictive; by chandasy ubhayathā it is sārvadhātuka, so s-elision.)

इन्द्रवन्तः प्रीतेनेन्द्रेण तद्वन्तो वयं देवानां देवान् ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ ऊती ऊत्या तर्पणेन हविरादिना मंसीमहि । मन्यामहे । कीदृशा वयम् । स्वयशसः स्वायत्तकीर्तयो मरुद्भिः स्तुत्वा हृष्टैर्मरुद्देवैरनुगृहीताः । यद्वा । देवानामूत्या रक्षणेन रक्षिता मंसीमहि ज्ञातारो भवेम । सामर्थ्यादेषामेव महत्त्वस्य । किंचाग्निर्मित्रवरुणा देवाः शर्म यंसन् । अस्माकं सुखं प्रायच्छन् । तं तं वरं । मघवानो वयं च त्रैदश्यान्नवन्तः संतस्तत्सुखमश्याम । व्याप्नुयाम । अश्नोतेराशिषि लिङ् च्छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकत्वात्सलोपः ॥

indravantaḥ prītenendreṇa tadvanto vayaṃ devānāṃ devān ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī ‖ ūtī ūtyā tarpaṇena havirādinā maṃsīmahi | manyāmahe | kīdṛśā vayam | svayaśasaḥ svāyattakīrtayo marudbhiḥ stutvā hṛṣṭairmaruddevairanugṛhītāḥ | yadvā | devānāmūtyā rakṣaṇena rakṣitā maṃsīmahi jñātāro bhavema | sāmarthyādeṣāmeva mahattvasya | kiṃcāgnirmitravaruṇā devāḥ śarma yaṃsan | asmākaṃ sukhaṃ prāyacchan | taṃ taṃ varaṃ | maghavāno vayaṃ ca traidaśyānnavantaḥ saṃtastatsukhamaśyāma | vyāpnuyāma | aśnoterāśiṣi liṅ cchandasyubhayatheti sārvadhātukatvātsalopaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha. indravantaḥ — endowed with Indra; svayaśasaḥ — of our own renown; marudbhiḥ — by the Maruts (pleased by our praise), [favoured]; vayam — we; devānām — the gods; ūtī — by protection (satisfaction by oblations and so on); maṃsīmahi — may we know (their greatness); or devānām — of the gods; ūtī — by the protection; maṃsīmahi — (may we) know; ; agniḥ mitraḥ varuṇaḥ — Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa; śarma — joy; yaṃsan — gave (blessed); maghavānaḥ — [from them] possessing food; vayaṃ ca — and we; tat — that joy; aśyāma — may we get (may we enjoy).

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha. May we, worthy of Indra's pleasure and the favour of the Maruts, and ourselves of renown, receive the protection of the gods; and may we, possessing food, enjoy the happiness that Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa have blessed us with.

Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed): "Worshipping Indra, and favoured by the Maruts, may we rely upon the protection of the gods; and may we affluent (through their bounty), enjoy the felicity which Agni, Mitra, and Varuna are bestowing (upon us)."

॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 7).

In this Ṛk, a kind of pride and also satisfaction are expressed: from the firm trust that "we have the favour of Indra, whom our praise has pleased, and the help of the Maruts in full", the faith that the protection of the other gods is also assured is expressed.

maṃsīmahi — jñātāro bhavema: "may we become knowers"; by experiencing their protection, "may we know their nature through it" is the meaning.

aśyāma — vyāpnuyāma: "may we pervade", i.e. "may we get fully" is the meaning.

original p. 706

Special Topics of Ṛk 7, concluded; no heading is printed — this is a closing note on the deities of the Sūkta. Although in the Sūkta before us Mitra and Varuṇa are chiefly addressed, Aryaman and Bhaga — these deities too — are prayed to along with Mitra and Varuṇa. At the end, Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa are named together. Since these deities are praised together in one Sūkta, and since some of them are put together in a single Ṛk, it is to be understood that they have a connexion in the original [nature]. On the basis of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā all these may be called Ādityas. Although the number of Ādityas is given as eight, or twelve, in the Taittirīya and other texts, in the Ṛgveda alone this number is considered more [limited]. [This matter is explained in the introduction to the first part of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā and on pp. 536–537.] On the basis of the Ṛk-Saṃhitā, the author of the Nirukta too has included under the word Āditya these six deities — Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Dakṣa, Bhaga and Aṃśa:

तथ्यं तस्मै त्रयस्य वरुणस्यार्यम्णो दक्षस्य भगस्यांशस्येति ।

tathyaṃ tasmai trayasya varuṇasyāryamṇo dakṣasya bhagasyāṃśasyeti |

(Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೧೩" [?]; the Sanskrit is badly printed in the Kannada type and I read it only in part [?].) In the Taittirīya and other texts, Mitra is connected with the Sun, and Varuṇa with the Moon, and their mutual relations are shown. Mitra, they say, created the day; Varuṇa, the night. Sometimes, according to this division, a white animal is offered to Mitra and a black animal to Varuṇa. The nature of Aryaman and Bhaga is told in subtle terms in the Ṛks preceding this Sūkta. How these deities were all born from Aditi is described in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa in this way:

अदितिः पुत्रकामा साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मौदनमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमदुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्यै धाता चार्यमा चाजायेताम् । सा द्वितीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमदुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्मै मित्रश्च वरुणश्चाजायेताम् । सा तृतीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमदुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या अꣳशश्च भगश्चाजायेताम् ।

aditiḥ putrakāmā | sādhyebhyo devebhyo brahmaudanam apacat | tasyā ucchēṣaṇam aduḥ | tat prāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyai dhātā cāryamā cājāyetām | sā dvitīyam apacat | tasyā ucchēṣaṇam aduḥ | tat prāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasmai mitraś ca varuṇaś cājāyetām | sā tṛtīyam apacat | tasyā ucchēṣaṇam aduḥ | tat prāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā aṃśaś ca bhagaś cājāyetām |

(Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1, 2 [as read: "೧-೧-೯-೧, ೨"]; read from the image; the form ucchēṣaṇam is as printed, [?].) Kannada sense: Aditi, desiring sons, cooked a brahmaudana for the Sādhya gods. They ate it and gave her the remainder. She ate that and conceived: from her Dhātṛ and Aryaman were born. The second time she cooked [again] and ate what was left; Mitra and Varuṇa were born. The third time Aṃśa and Bhaga were born.

Though they are described each in a different way in different places, since in all these deities some aspect of the Sun is seen in one way or another, the old scholars have concluded that they are all Ādityas, parts of the Sun.

original p. 707

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed). devānām — the genitive in the sense of karman. maṃsīmahi — root manu avabodhane; liṅ, first person plural; suhiṅ for mahiṅ; liṅaḥ sīyuṭ (Pā. 3-4-102 [as read]) gives the sīyuṭ augment to liṅ; yalopaḥ; since by chandasy ubhayathā (Pā. 3-4-117 [as read]) it has the ārdhadhātuka term, the s-elision does not occur; or, by the strength of the bahula statement, sip; since it is not at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta does not occur; the suffix's ādyudātta. yaṃsan — root yamu uparame; leṭ, third person plural, jhi; itaś ca lopaḥ (Pā. 3-4-97 [as read]) drops the i; jher jus [as read: jho 'ntaḥ] gives ant; sibbahulaṃ leṭi (Pā. 3-1-34 [as read]) gives sip; leṭo 'ṭāṭau (Pā. 3-4-94 [as read]) gives the aṭ augment to the suffix; as it follows a tiṅanta, nighāta. aśyāma — root aśa bhojane; āśirliṅ first person plural, mas; nityaṃ ṅiti (Pā. 7-2-81 [as read]) drops the s; yāsuṭ augment; by chandasy ubhayathā it is of the sārvadhātuka term; since it is ṅit, sārvadhātukaliṅ… [as read: liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya (Pā. 7-2-79 [as read])] gives the elision of the s; nighāta after a tiṅanta. maghavānaḥ — chandasīvanipau (Pā. 5-2-109 [as read]) gives vanip in the sense of matup; since it is pit, it is anudātta; nominative plural. ‖ 7 ‖

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥

vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃś caturo deyād vidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तकश्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये द्वितीयाष्टके प्रथमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ।

iti śrīmad-rājādhirāja-parameśvara-vaidikamārga-pravartaka-śrī-vīrabukka-bhūpāla-sāmrājya-dhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye dvitīyāṣṭake prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ |

ॐ तत्सत् ।

oṃ tat sat |

The colophon verse and the colophon are in Sanskrit, in Kannada script.) Kannada closing line (translated): "Here the First Adhyāya in the Second Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, with Sāyaṇa's commentary and the Kannada translation, is completed." (Kannada: "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಶ್ರೀ ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತವೂ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕಭಾಷಾನುವಾದಯುತವೂ ಆದ ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತೆಯ ಎರಡನೇ ಅಷ್ಟಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಮೊದಲನೆಯ ಅಧ್ಯಾಯವು ಸಮಾಪ್ತವಾದುದು".

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥

yad akṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yad bhavet | tat sarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖

शुभं भूयात् ।

śubhaṃ bhūyāt |

मङ्गलम् ।

maṅgalam |

Sense so far: "This Agni holds in his right hand — ready to give what is wished — the wealth to be given to the sacrificer, [holding it back with the left]. What kind? viśvaḥ — to be approached by all, or all-formed; vihāyāḥ — great (the word vihāyāḥ is recorded among the names of 'great': vihāyā yahva…); aratiḥ — the lord, or the delight; vasuḥ. [Grammar tail: the suffix ti from vahni, vas, ṛ…, accent on the last syllable by cidvadbhāva.] And, having taken it, śiśrathat — he loosens the held hand for the sacrificer: he gives. [Grammar: aorist of ślathayati.] The example: taraṇir na — like the Sun, the saviour: as he holds in his hand what his worshipper wants and distributes it; or the Sun, who carries all across, does not let go of the sacrificer; and śravasyayā na śiśrathat — he does not let go even for the wish for the food in the form of oblation; this Agni protects by grace; the acceptance of the oblation is a mere pretext. Now directly addressed: O Agni, among the gods you above all, for everyone who desires the oblation — Indra and the rest — [carry (ohise)] the oblation offered to each deity — puroḍāśa…"

¶ Sense. "O Indra, such as is described, hear (śrudhi; the hi becomes dhi) our invocation or praise. You, who with men — nṛbhiḥ — in whatever battles, and afterwards with the gods, the Maruts [?] — the leaders of battle, the Maruts, helpers of Indra — 'Indra with the Maruts' (Tai. Saṃ. [?], Ait. Br. [?]: 'the Maruts called him to the contest') — in all engagements, for the call to battle (bharahūti) and for the great slaying (pratūrti) of the enemies, you are dakṣāyya — of growing power; or, asked by the sacrificers, the leaders, you are able to slay foes greatly. And you who, together with the heroic Maruts, are the winner (sanitā) of heaven and of what is desired — tarutā — are the giver of food (vājam) to the sages, the priests praising you: that Indra, swift, with food (pṛkṣam) in the form of oblation, the lords (īśānāsaḥ), the priests able to seek well, serve (iradhanta); as people nourish a swift horse (atyam) with sweet fodder: 'the word atya is a name for horse', since it is read among those names." The grammar tail on tarutā, hedhibhāva, etc., is only characterized.

[Grammar: root vaś kāntau, adādi; masi with iṭ; saṃprasāraṇa by grahijyā…]. Or, 'our friend' is the connection: what Indra? sakhāyam — a very beneficent friend, or of the same renown; viśvāyum — the goer to all sacrifices; prāsaham — the great endurer of enemies; yujam — always joined, helping; again, in the food-oblations (vājeṣu) or in the sacrifices that have them, prāsaham — overcoming those who spoil the sacrifice; yujam — joined with desired fruits, or with the Maruts. And, O Indra, for our protection (ūtaye) protect (ava) our great rite (brahma). Where in particular? In whatever battles (pṛtsu, recorded among names of battle): in them no enemy harms you; whichever enemy you oppose you ward off: not any enemy harms you: by your greatness all are afraid and become obedient; no one takes up enmity, since you are without a born enemy."

¶ Sense: "O Indra, bend down thoroughly — ni ṣū nama, make bow to us — the enemy atimati ('of excessive or hostile mind') of any (kayasya cit) sacrificer devoted to you. [This root has the causative sense hidden in it.] O fierce (ugra) Indra, of mighty strength, endowed with protections or affection, by your radiant (tejiṣṭhābhiḥ) ways such as war, as by paths: as you bent down Vṛtra and the like, so bend the one who is hostile to us. Or taking with what follows: as you have yoked us to the paths of sacrifice that are full of splendour, so lead us (neṣi) by your shining protections, the fruit of the sacrifice, to the desired heaven and the like. Example: as in former times you led our fathers and the others by your protections; so now. O brave one, you are anenāḥ — known by all as sinless, since you give heaven and what is desired; or, you think us sinless. And O Indra, as the vahni — sustaining the world by giving rain and so on — you remove all the sins of pūru, i.e. man, the sacrificer (the word pūru is recorded among the names of man — pūravo jagataḥ); you protect him. Therefore, coming facing us, near, at the sacrificial place, as bearer of what is wished, you remove what is not wished and fulfil what is wished."

26. Read from the image. Ṛk 6 is addressed to Indu, i.e. Soma — the sūkta table gives "Ṛk 6 Indu". Pada: iṣa-vān, rakṣaḥ-hā, aghaśaṃsaḥ, ava-taram, kṣudram-iva.

¶ Sense: "For Indu — that is, Soma — who is of a nature to come into being, who grows each day by the increase of his phases and moistens everyone with nectar, may I be able to speak (pra voceyam) that rite or praise, to be told now; may I be able to speak it excellently, since praise is of very great (ati-mahat) worth. [Grammar: precative of vac, augment um.] For whom? The Soma-juice that, abounding in food (iṣavān) or desire, rejati — goes toward manma, the praiseworthy hymn or rite; (rejati is a verb of motion). The example of coming: havyo na — like the one to be invoked, Indra: Indra is called with 'come, Indra' and so on; like him. The same is further described: rakṣohā — the killer of the Rākṣasas who harm sacrifices — rejati — sets going, i.e. destroys, their work of killing and the like. May that Soma himself repel by the means of destruction (vadhraiḥ) the enemy who reviles us (nidaḥ), the one with an evil mind. And may the thief (aghaśaṃsaḥ, the 'proclaimer of sins' — the word aghaśaṃsa is recorded among the names of thief and of wolf), go downwards (ava sravet), to the lowest place, from his place, headlong, fall down: this fall is prayed for — as little water, that can be thrown, runs down and is lost."

Sense: "O priests, for you and for us this Indra, by his own-fame protections, when there is the avoidance (parivarga) of the ill-minded enemies, becomes prapra — eminent, able; the doubling is a metrical filler. Or: praised by us with praises that need no help from others [?], he becomes eminent in protection. Where? In the avoidance of the ill-minded, in battle; again, the same Indra, in the tearing (darīman) of the ill-minded, who intend killing — the great tearer. Thus when Indra protects well, the army (jūrṇi) of our enemies who devour us (atraiḥ) — 'jūrṇi from jū to go quickly, dru to run, or du to burn': Yāska (Ni. 6-14 [?]) — that comes to harm us, to attack us, kṣiptā — sent forth, itself is destroyed; it does not carry (na vakṣati) us — does not reach us; nor does it come again."

Sense: "O Indra, come (yāhi) before us by our path (pathā) — the path to the sacrifice, of which the Stuti has said that it is without evil (anehasā, free from sin), that is free of Rākṣasas (arakṣasā): or come toward us; how? parīṇasā — girded all round, i.e. with wealth to be given to us, of many kinds; O Indra, from afar (parāke) — from heaven — be with us; and near (īke), at our place of divine worship, partake of our oblation, or come together with us; also protect us from far (heaven and the rest) and from near (the second world); or from far, from the time not of sacrifice, coming from heaven, protect us; and near, at the time of sacrifice, at the place of worship; by what? by abhiṣṭibhiḥ — by well-performed sacrifices facing us, or by visits. What more? always, in all times — at each sacrifice, far and near — protect us with your desires, guard us well."

¶ Read from the image; the small type is partly doubtful: [?] — notably the clause on the particle na ("yady api purastād…") and "vidathāni vedanāny upeyur jñānāni". Sense: "O Indra, come near us from afar (parāvataḥ) — from heaven — return to us. The example: like this (ayam na) fire before us, or the pressed Soma that is pointed to in the present context — like him; though the particle na is generally negative, here it is taken as a particle of comparison. Or: as if from a distant place (parāvato na), though you are always present at the sacrifice, as if from far-off heaven to this sacrifice. [Case variation: āyam for amum.] Come to this place of sacrifice, to reach it. Example: like a satpati — the sacrificer, protector of the priests who are always present; [the accent of the first member is from patyāvaiśvarye]; as he comes to vidathāni — the places of knowledge/of the ceremonies; or, as Agni, the protector of existing fruits, comes to vidathāni — the sacrificial houses — so you come to the sacrificial houses; or, as the Moon, king (rājā) and lord of the stars, comes to his setting-place (astam), his own abode. And we sacrificers, possessed of food in the form of oblations, call you (havāmahe), for the pressed Soma, together with the priests (sacā — 'together', Yāska, Ni. 5-5 [?]). Example for the invocation: as sons call a father — a protector — for the vājasāti — to partake of food; so we also call you for that; and we call you, the most worthy of honour (maṃhiṣṭha), for the winning of battle, for the acceptance of oblations."

8. Read from the image; the Saṃhitā's third word prints "soma-m indra"; the first line ends "…vaṃsagaḥ"; the Pada gives tātṛṣāṇaḥ (print "ತತ್ಋಷಾಣಃ"), tuviṣṭamāya, aha viśvā-iva.

¶ Sense. At the sixth day, at the midday pressing, the ṛks before the prasthita-yājyās are the praṣepaṇīyas [?]; in this, before the Hotṛ, pibā somam indra is recited: as stated in the section ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavane: "pibā somam indra suvānam adribhir indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata" (Āś. 8-1 [?]). "O Indra, vaṃsagaḥ — of desirable going — drink the Soma. [Lengthening by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ.] What kind? suvānam — being pressed (adribhiḥ) by the pressing-stones; kośena siktam — purified by the daśāpavitra (the ten-fold strainer) that serves as a receptacle; or taken with the following avatam: as a well (avata) filled with the water suitable for it, like a well at the watering-place; as the swift bull, of desirable going (vaṃsaga), drinks it when thirsty; or the man who is very thirsty and swift going to the watering-place and drinks: so. For what purpose? For your exhilaration (madāya), for haryatāya (heroism or splendour) [root hary in the sense of going and desire], for tuviṣṭamāya — greatness, growth, for dhāyase — for that for which the exhilaration arises. Or: tuviṣṭamāya dhāyase — for much drinking. May the horses bring you, bring you facing us (ā yacchantu); example: harito na sūryam — as the horses called harit, of golden-green colour, bring the sun; as they carry him impelled toward the desired place; and ahā viśvā — all days — as the same horses carry the sun every day, so may they bring you every day to our sacrifices and the like."

12. Read from the image: ni-hitam, ni-dhim, pari-vītam, aṅgiraḥ-tamaḥ; the Saṃhitā's third word group ends "…antar aśmani".

¶ Sense. "This Indra obtained (avindat) the Soma brought from heaven (divaḥ): having it carried by the Gāyatrī in the form of a bird, brought to the earth: this is well known from the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa and others ('the Soma was in heaven; the Gāyatrī brought it'). It was guhā nihitam — placed in a hiding-place on a mountain etc., thus a treasure, without loss. The example of fetching: vor na garbham — like the young of a bird: as a hen pigeon or other bird hides its young in some inaccessible place for fear of the hunter, goes round, and finds the place again, so [Indra finds Soma], aśmani anante — in a vast rock, the mountain without measure, covered all round by creepers and thorns. In what condition? aśmani — in the stone. Though there were other places, why this one? He says: this Indra, the thunderer (vajrī), gavāṃ vrajam iva — as one finds a cow-pen hidden by the demon Paṇi in the earth with a stone over its door: conquering the demon, opening the door, and obtaining it; so, sisāsan — desiring to partake, [he found Soma]; ... And so this Indra opened (apāvṛṇot) the doors (dvāraḥ) of the waters (iṣaḥ, the water that is the cause of food) enclosed (parivṛtāḥ) by clouds all round; he made the grains and the like, desired in the fields, spread out over the earth; splitting the cloud with the thunderbolt, he gave abundance of crops by the rain: thus he did; therefore the acceptance of Soma is proper."

¶ Read from the image; the passages on kṣadmeva, the kyap-grammar on ahihatyāya and the last sentence are small and partly doubtful: [?]. Sense: "This Indra, dādhṛhāṇaḥ — firmly holding the thunderbolt in both his arms (gabhastyoḥ; gabhasti is a name of arm) — for what? for asanāya — for hurling upon the enemy — makes the sharp (tigmam) thunderbolt sharper still, saṃ śyat (root śo 'to sharpen'): as water (kṣadma — water; in the list of names of water) is made sharp by charming, to repel the enemies; again for ahihatyāya — for the slaying of Ahi, Vṛtra, or the cloud, he sharpens it a second time. O Indra, endowed fully (saṃvivyānaḥ) with strength (ojas), the armies (śavobhiḥ) and bodily strength (majmanā): as a carpenter cuts the trees of a forest to make them useful, so you cut the enemy who walks crooked [?] among us; and as with an axe one cuts a tree, so you cut our enemies."

17. Sense: "O Indra, vṛthā — without effort — you released the rivers to flow (sartave) toward the sea, splitting the cloud. The example: as you released chariots toward our sacrifice, so; and as kings and others eager for battle or food send forth chariots. And hence the flowing rivers (ūtīḥ) — those that go or protect — yoked (ayuñjata) to the common purpose water that does not diminish (akṣitam): by your grace. Artha is a kind of water [neuter]. Akṣita is recorded among the names of water and of barhis. The example: as cows, for Manu or for any person whomever, are viśvadohasaḥ — yielding all milk — so, or: the rivers, for all people, looking to the crops and so on, yield fully and flow everywhere; here the rivers are said, figuratively, to 'milk' through gratification. This is a praise of Indra alone, the giver of rain beneficial to all."

Sense: "O Indra, for you the āyavaḥ — priests, who desire wealth and have food in the form of oblation to give (āyu is recorded among the names of man) — have fashioned (atakṣiṣuḥ) this praise-speech being made; svapāḥ — skilled, doing good work, wise — as a skilful man makes a chariot well by effort, so they made it. Having done so, they have made you favourable for sumna, happiness (sumna is a name of happiness). And, O wise Indra, the priests adorn you with qualities, glorify you, swift in battles, as soldiers praise a conquering hero; or as one encourages a swift horse in battle. And we praise you for strength, for the gaining of wealth; not wealth alone but all kinds of wealth such as cows, the means of satisfaction. The example: as one praises a swift horse that always runs, for victory in battle, for the gaining of that very wealth."

¶ Sense: "O Indra, nṛto — dancing (with delight) in battle — for pūrave — [a man] — the giver of oblations, for the great Divodāsa (a king by that name) you bhinat — broke ninety (navatim) cities (puraḥ) of enemies; and, O dancer, skilful at the movement of limbs, destroyer of enemies by the throwing of hands and feet, with the thunderbolt (the weapon able to be cast) for the giver of oblations Divodāsa or another, you split … Now he speaks indirectly: for Divodāsa, atithigva — who goes to guests with worship — [Indra] fiercely (ugra), of mighty strength, in the earlier time of splitting the cities, threw down (avābharat) from the mountain, hard to reach, the demon named Śambara, who had gone up the mountain, with his own strength, head downward; he took his life. Doing what? mahaḥ — giving great riches, his cows, horses and the like, to king Divodāsa; and viśvā dhanāni — all his treasures, jewels, pearls and the like, by his strength."

¶ Sense: "This Indra protects (prāvat) in samatsu — battles — the worshipper, the Ārya, worthy of being approached by all; (samatsu is among the names of battle). And śatamūtiḥ — of hundredfold protections for his own devotees — Indra protects the sacrificer in all contests (ājiṣu) and in the great battles (svarmīḷheṣu) that sprinkle happiness [lead to heaven]; he protects by granting heaven; of heroes slain facing the enemy it is heard in the world: 'These two men pierce the orb of the sun: the ascetic joined in yoga, and the one slain facing the enemy.' (Parāśara [?]). It is told in history: on the bank of the river Aṃśumatī the black demon Kṛṣṇa, with ten thousand followers, was afflicting the (respectable people) of the (four) castes: there Indra, urged by Bṛhaspati, with the Maruts, stripped the black skin and killed him with his followers: 'the drop (drapsa) stood on the Aṃśumatī' (Ṛ. 8-96-13 [?]) etc. — to be seen later. Here it is said: this Indra, for Manu (for men), punished (śāsat) the avratān — those without vrata (rites), who hate the sacrifice; and he destroyed (arandhayat) the black skin of the demon Kṛṣṇa; and as to how: dakṣan na viśvam — he burns the whole of them, the entire host of followers; not leaving anything: he burns (oṣati) all the harming ones, whatever is left of the sinful arśasāna [the wicked], utterly."

24. Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 8, continued from p. 451:

26. Read from the image. Saṃhitā "pra vṛhaj jāta ojasā" as printed, the Pada giving jātaḥ; tuvarṇiḥ is printed "turvaṇiḥ".

¶ Sense: "Here also they relate an itihāsa: certain demons formerly, having obtained from Brahmā the boon 'let there be no death by Indra's thunderbolt', became arrogant, disregarding Indra. To kill them Indra took the wheel of the Sun's chariot and slew them. That is told here: this Indra — sūraḥ, 'the Sun', the first case for the genitive — taking the wheel (cakram) of the chariot, grown (jātaḥ) in bodily strength (ojasā), pra vṛhat — tore out. Further, aruṇaḥ — reddish, exceedingly brilliant, or moving — at prapitve, near them, comes up and muṣāyati — takes away their breath marked by speech; or he stops the sound of their blows. Or: Indra himself, standing in heaven, is praised in the form of the Sun. When sūra the sun has risen, endowed with his own splendour, he lifts the wheel-marked chariot to dispel darkness or to conquer the demons. Then, before, aruṇa — the sun's charioteer — near the demons … īśānaḥ — able to remove all darknesses or the demons — ā muṣāyati, carries off all around. Now to the context: O sage (kave, far-seeing), since you came (ajagan) from afar (parāvataḥ), from the heavenly abode, for protection (ūtaye), joined with Uśanā [or: uśanā kaviḥ — the sage Uśanas]; coming, bring all (viśvā) the means of happiness (sumnāni), wealth, and be quick (turvaṇiḥ — 'quickly sharing', Nirukta) for us; as for man (manuṣeva) — as for other priests you bring all wealth, so for us too; and not only on one day of the sacrifice but on all days (ahā viśveva): or as you give long life, so give happiness: give both.") (Doubtful readings in the small type are marked [?]; the grammar tail on muṣāyati and ajagan is characterized only.

¶ ayam) indraḥ — this Indra; sūraḥ — of the Sun; cakram — the wheel of the chariot (taking it); ojasā — by bodily strength; jātaḥ — grown; pra vṛhat — tore out against (the demons' bodies); (kiṃ ca — and); aruṇaḥ — reddish or moving; prapitve — near (them, going to them); vācam — speech or breath; muṣāyati — takes away [or:* (athavā) sūraḥ — Indra in the form of the Sun; jātaḥ — risen; ojasā — with his own splendour; cakram — the wheel (chariot); pra vṛhat — lifts up (to remove darkness); aruṇaḥ — the sun's charioteer, named Aruṇa; prapitve — near the demons (Mandeha and the rest); vācam — their voice (the sound of demons, by the wheel); muṣāyati — makes them silent; īśānaḥ — able to remove darkness (or the demons); ā muṣāyati *— destroys them entirely]; (he) kave — O sage; uśanā — joined with the sage named Uśanas; ūtaye — for our protection; parāvataḥ — from a very distant place (from the world of heaven); ajagan — came (or: yat — that you; uśanā — to Uśanas' protection; parāvataḥ — from heaven; ajagan — you came); viśvā sumnāni — all the means of happiness (taking); manuṣā iva — as (from a distant place) for a man the desired things are brought, or as for the other priests [wealth is granted]; turvaṇiḥ (bhava

Sense: "O Indra, vṛṣakarman — whose work is the showering of the desired — purāṃ dartaḥ — the splitter of the cities of demons: you, such a great one, pleased by our new (navyebhiḥ) hymns (ukthaiḥ) as now stated, protect us with protections (pāyubhiḥ) and with the happiness (śagmaiḥ) of this world and the next. And, O Indra, praised by us, the Paruccheṣas, born in the line of Divodāsa — the plural is of respect — increase (vāvṛdhīthāḥ): as dyauḥ — the shining Sun — grows by the days, so you grow by our praise."

Sūkta 131

1. The Sanskrit introduction is small and in several places unreadable to me; I give what is legible and mark [?]; the sense follows.

¶ The Kannada anuvāda of the introduction, continued from p. 466: at the midday pressing this Sūkta is made into three tṛcas (groups of three ṛks) and recited, and the stomāvāpa is done after them; the division is: the first three ṛks for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest, the next three for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the last for the Acchāvāka — as stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section caturthe 'hani, by the sūtra ṣaṣṭhe 'hani indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata (Āś. 8-11 [?], as read). On the same day, at the same pressing, the six ṛks of this Sūkta are recited one by one by the Praśāstṛ and others as preliminary to the prasthitayājyā mantras, by the sūtra indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnateti ṣaṭ in the section ṣaṣṭhasya (Āś. 8-1 [?]). In the mahāvrata, at the niṣkevalya śastra, the three ṛks beginning indrāya hi are recited as alternative anurūpa ṛks, by Śaunaka's Aitareya Āraṇyaka sūtra indraṃ yāhy upa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata (Ait. Ār. 5-1-1 [?]).

3. Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".

¶ Sense: "Heaven (dyauḥ, the shining heaven-world, or the host of gods who dwell there) and the asura (the repeller of enemies, because the dwellers there are the righteous) bows (anamnata) to Indra alone, of its own accord. [Grammar: the Vedic luṅ of nam, the ātmanepada in the intransitive sense; na duhasnunamām yag abhāvaḥ (Pā. 3-1-89 [?]); śluḥ for śap; no halādiśeṣa; loss of the nasal.] hi is for emphasis. So for Indra the great earth (mahī pṛthivī) — or all people dwelling on it — bows; the words naming the support stand for the supported, as in 'the village has come'. By what means? varīmabhiḥ — by choice praises or oblations. And when there is dyumnasātā — winning food or fame — the sacrificers, furnished with choice oblations, bow. And all the gods (viśve devāsaḥ), united in affection (sajoṣasaḥ), of one mind, formerly put Indra in front (puro dadhire) to conquer the demons: they conquered the demons through Indra. Likewise may the human pressings (mānuṣā savanāni), the morning and other pressings, be for Indra alone; and the offerings to be given by the human priests, the puroḍāśa and the rest, be for Indra, able to please him."

¶ Read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?] — notably the grammatical clause on sasahānaḥ. Sense: "O Indra, men (pūravaḥ), the sacrificers, who know your greatness and sacrifice to you alone, know (viduḥ) this heroism of yours, to be told: that you destroyed (avātiraḥ) the autumn (śāradīḥ) cities of the enemies, fortified for a year with ramparts and moats, overpowering (sasahānaḥ) them and afflicting them by seizing their wealth. And you punished (śāsaḥ) that mortal who is ayajyu — one who does not sacrifice, a spoiler of sacrifice, a Rākṣasa and the like. O lord of strength (śavasaspate), you carried off (amuṣṇāḥ) by force the great earth and these waters — the rivers and the sea — [seized by] the demons, hostile to the sacrifice, breaking their cities and recovering them: is it with sorrow? No: delighting (mandasānaḥ) you carried off these waters, the foods such as rice that benefit [men]."

14. Read from the image: the Pada's last line prints "te anyām-anyām" as one compound; Saṃhitā "cakartha kāram ebhyaḥ".

15. Sense: "O Indra, thereafter (ād it) they strew (cakiran) Soma again and again in all the pressings for your vigour (vīryasya), i.e. for your increase. [kir in the intensive with luk: the reduplicative takes ruk.] When, madeṣu, in the exhilarations produced by Soma, O showerer of desires, you protect (āvitha) the uśijaḥ — sacrificers who desire you — and since you favour us who seek your friendship, satisfying us with what is wished: for that reason you utter (cakartha kāram) for them the lion-roar in battles (pṛtanāsu): for what? pravantave — to win, since the brave seek battle. And those who dwell in your battles, near you, obtain one enjoyment after another (anyām-anyāṃ nadyam, the Vedic sense 'satisfaction, growth'); saniṣṇata — they partake; and, desiring food, wishing for food won by victory, they partake."

16. Grammar, continued.

17. Read from the image: the Pada gives uto iti, svaḥ-sātā, havīma-bhiḥ.

18. Sense: "This Indra may enjoy (juṣeta) this dawn (uṣasaḥ) of ours — the time of dawn belonging to the sūkta — i.e. may come to our sacrifice early. [hi is a filler.] And having come, bodhi — know (accept) the oblation of the one who praises (arkasya haviṣaḥ), given with the particular kinds of invocations (havīmabhiḥ); and be called by invocations at the sacrifice, the place of enjoyment of heaven or other happiness (svarsātā): called by us, he comes early and accepts the oblation. Why this? Because, O thunderer, you are aware (ciketasi), as the showerer, of desires, for the slaying of the injuring enemies (mṛdhaḥ). Therefore we say: O Indra, hear (śrudhi) my praise (manma), the praise worthy of thought, of the new — consecrated by initiation — wise vedhas, of the extraordinary newest praiser."

19. Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 6, concluded from p. 494:

20. Read from the image: the Pada gives vavṛdhānaḥ, asmayuḥ; the Saṃhitā prints "vāvṛdhāno".

¶ Sense: "O Indra, tuvijāta — taking many forms — brave, you, growing (vāvṛdhānaḥ), desiring us (asmayuḥ), strike with your thunderbolt that mortal, acting as an enemy (amitrayantam) toward us, mortal by nature. [Grammar: jahi with the substitute jā for han; the hi is not dropped by asiddhavad atrābhāt.] Which mortal? Whoever wishes us harm (aghāyati: agha is sin or pain); strike him. And hear (śṛṇuṣva), you most renowned (suśravastamaḥ). How? O Indra, by your grace may the evil intent (durmatiḥ) — the mind bent on harm — be gone (apa bhūtu); not only that of harm but all evil intent in the form of anger or abuse. The example: as a weary traveller on the road (yāmann riṣṭaṃ na) is attacked, harmed by the toil of the way, by hunger and the like, so may the evil intent that harms us go away; or, as on the path of the sacrifice you remove the obstruction in the form of violence caused by the asuras and rākṣasas."

¶ Sense: "O Indra, that well-known prayaḥ — food in the form of oblation, much kindled by contact with ghee and the like — is yours (te); pratnathā — as formerly, whenever at the time of sacrifice the oblation is yours, so now too; they always sacrifice to you alone. How is it? In which sacrifice, when the oblation is to be given, the priests make a choice kṣaya — a place, the altar; of whom? you reach (vārasi) the dwelling-place of the sacrifice (ṛta) — the truth-fruited: or ṛta is a name of water — you reach the place of water — you are a rain-giver; or you take the sacrificer to the place of the Sun (ṛta) — the heaven world. Therefore declare (vi voceḥ) such a deed. Then, because of this, all men see directly, through the Sun's rays, the rain-giving deed in the midst — between heaven and earth — in the sky; by sending to the Sun the oblation given by us, you produce rain through it: so all see it. Now he praises indirectly: that Indra is goveṣaṇaḥ — the seeker of water; also bandhukṣidbhyaḥ goveṣaṇaḥ — for the sacrificers who have become kin through offering oblations, the seeker of the well-known cows; [grammar: iṣ with the lyuṭ by bāhulaka]; or gaveṣa in the sense of searching. He is the doer in the manner stated; vide — he finds, he knows the way of obtaining water."

¶ Sense: "O Indra, this deed of yours, of the kind stated or to be stated, should be praised by all (pravācyam) quickly, as in former times (pūrvathā), so now too. What is it? That you opened (apāvṛṇoḥ) the cloud (vraja — recorded among the names of cloud — "vrajo varāha" as read) that moved in the sky for the sake of those Aṅgirases, the great ṛṣis, and produced rain; and O Indra, taking away from the Paṇis (pāyāpsya?) the herd of cows, you gave it to them and protected them; or you opened the door of the cave where the cattle stolen by the Paṇis were kept. And as you give to these ṛṣis in one manner, so conquer for us wealth or battle, and fight (yotsi) for us. And for us who press Soma, subdue (randhaya) any avrata — one who does not perform the rites, an enemy of the sacrifice; make him subject to us. Not only the non-sacrificer, but the hṛṇāyantam cit avratam — the one who, being avrata, is furious at us (cit in the sense of contempt); subdue also him who rages, and make him unable to harm again."

18. Read from the image: the Saṃhitā's third word is "janān"; the Pada gives kratu-bhiḥ, prajā-vat; "ṇ" and "ṣ" as printed.

¶ Sense: "Since the hero Indra, brave, samīkṣayat — looks well on all creatures through their kratus (knowledge or deeds): staying within all, as the inner controller, he makes them look at their objects; or he impels them by their good and bad deeds to their results; and when he so impels, the sacrificers desiring food (śravasyavaḥ), when wealth, in the form of cattle and the like, is desired (hite dhane), tarūṣanta — destroy enemies. For this reason, desiring food or the oblation for themselves or for Indra, they sacrifice (pra yakṣanta) abundantly. Moreover for that Indra alone they present āyuḥ — the food in the form of oblation, accompanied by sons and the like; when there is bādhe — the harassing of enemies; or: bādhe is a name of strength: obtaining life and food accompanied by progeny, endowed with ojas — strength — they worship Indra. And the dhītayaḥ — the active sacrificers — dadhiṣanta — hold (aspire to) okyam — a dwelling-place in Indra's neighbourhood (as in 'a cowherd settlement on the Gaṅgā' the nearness is meant): the world of Indra; the pious ones, doing works that lead to heaven, aspire to dwell in front of the gods, as if reaching them."

The upper half of Ṛk 6 is addressed to Indra and Parvata, the second half to Indra alone.

Sense: "On a non-vivākya day, after the drinking of the mānasa-grahas [?], when the stars are seen, all, with the Adhvaryu at their head, are to mutter this yuvaṃ tam indra [Ṛk]; stated in the Śrauta-sūtra, section 'gārhapatye juṣṭastīti' [?]: 'muttering yuvaṃ tam indrāparvatā purojudhā' (Āś. 8-13 [?], as read "೮-೧೩")." The reading of this small-type sūtra reference is doubtful: [?].

¶ Sense: "O Indra and Parvata — Indra the well-known; Parvata, the parvavat cloud — the deities presiding over them: you two, purojudhā — fighting in front in battle — whichever enemy of ours (yaḥ pṛtanyāt) wishes an army against us in order to kill us — destroy (apa hatam) each and every such enemy. With what? With the thunderbolt (vajreṇa) obtain [him] to kill every enemy; so it shows that such power exists. The enemy gone very far (dūre cattāya) [cata in the sense 'destroyed', 'out of sight'], or one who wishes to kill (chantsat, from chand, 'to desire'); the difficult, impenetrable place (gahanam), the very hard heart near the enemy, [the thunderbolt] pervades (inakṣat). Now Indra alone is praised: O hero Indra, our enemies on all sides (viśvataḥ) you tear apart (dardṛṣṭa); and darmā — the tearer of enemies; or the thunderbolt, mentioned before, tears all enemies completely."

Sense, with doubtful words as read: "O Indra, by the sacrifice (ṛta, i.e. force) aimed at you I purify both heaven and earth; I cleanse the two worlds of the misfortune that comes from the wicked [?]. Those wide lands that lack Indra (anindrāḥ) and are the support of the malicious, I burn up together. The lands are further described: in which the enemies, having gone about on every side, were slain — reached on all sides by us or struck by us (vlagati is a verb of motion, a Vedic root); all these, utterly (pari) crushed, lie asleep (aśeran)." Grammar: tṛhū hiṃsāyām; because of the ū-marker the iṭ is optionally forbidden; śete has the Parasmaipada by vyatyaya.

Then on vailasthānam: "The word bila means the same as garta (pit); and garta is a word for a cemetery; the word āka also means cemetery. Or: the place connected with a bila is the Nāga-world (serpent world); either of these may be meant by 'they lay there'. Or the root is bila kṣepe; ka in the sense of ghañ, with the selfsame suffix ayan; where corpses are thrown is vailasthāna, a cemetery. There, those struck by you, making the earth like a cemetery, lie everywhere; these I burn — this is the meaning." The wording of the second half is partly doubtful [?].

¶ Sense: "O adrivaḥ — devourer of enemies, or [from adri, cloud, and adarti] possessor of the cloud — O Indra: you, of the yātumatī — harming — armies; or of those armies possessing yātūni, i.e. weapons that are instruments of torment; or those that have yātus, Rākṣasas: [the genitive is in the sense of the object] of the enemies' armies, the heads (śīrṣā = śīrṣāṇi) having encompassed (abhivlagya cit) on all sides — cut off, crush them; or, cut their chariots etc. With what instrument? — with vaṭūriṇā padā: with your all-pervading foot, pervading, spread out [?]; or with the foot of the elephant, that wraps (Airāvata's foot); and not with just any foot — with the great (mahā) wrapping foot, or your own foot, or the foot of Airāvata: cut, crush." Grammar: root vaṭa veṣṭane; kharjipiñjādibhya ūrolacau (Uṇ. 4-[?] as read "೪-೯೦" [?]) gives suffix ūra; final grammar citation not legible.

21. Sense: "O Indra, Maghavan (wealthy)! Of these yātumatī armies — those having yātūni, weapons that are instruments of torment, or having Yātudhānas — destroy the strength (śardhaḥ), crush it; and, having done so, put [them] to sleep in the wretched (ārmaka) cemetery, as described above, fit for corpses, the vailasthānaka. Or: put [them] in the despised lower world, connected with a bila (hole), covered by darkness. Not in just any small place — in the mahāvailastha, the great cemetery which all must go to, or in the Nāga-world. Of what kind? — ārmaka: wretched, [fit for those who have gone to their destruction] [?]."

Sense: "O Indra, of which armies — of the kind described in the previous mantra — thrice fifty, i.e. one hundred and fifty, you destroyed by abhivlaṅgaiḥ, 'attacks' (vlaṅgati is a verb of motion), going against [them]. O Indra, that deed of yours, of the form of slaying such armies, is su manāyati — is well esteemed. And further, O Indra, even this great victory over one hundred and fifty armies [seems] to you takat — [it] is well thought of as very small." The grammatical tail is not given here.

The last grammatical lines are partly illegible to me.

¶ The bhāṣya runs on to p. 557; because the print is small and several words here are doubtful I mark the whole passage "as read, [?]". Sense so far: "The daśarātra, sixth day, in the prauga-śastra Indra …; stated in the Śrauta-sūtra, section 'ṣaṣṭhasya'. O Indra: mahaḥ — of the great cloud (genitive in the sense of the object); break the great, water-bearing cloud, the great Vṛtra [?]; and listen to us, O adrivaḥ — O possessor of the cloud. For the sky, the support of the gods, burns (śuśoca) because, there being no rain, there are no oblations and the like. Illustration: kṣā na — like the earth [kṣā = earth, the dwelling (kṣāyanti) of all], which when there is no rain burns from fear of the destruction of crops: so both worlds burn for lack of rain. [Or:] the heaven and earth burn, unable to bear the growing Asura-party that has pervaded the two worlds. Ghṛṇāt — from fear of a blazing fire, an embodied other form, as heaven and earth burned formerly in fear of blazing ones: [Here they] tell an itihāsa — formerly, when the world was covered with great darkness, the gods, having reflected, prayed to Agni; and he in the form of a trasa-man [?] …"

35. Ṛk 6, concluded; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

36. Sense: "You, certainly extremely strong, are on that account [ī-yase, from īṅ gatau, śyan by the Daivādika class] accompanied by fierce (ugra) and mighty blows, going to enemies or to clouds. Or śuṣmibhir vadhaiḥ connected: O hero, courageous, with beings [sattva]; O apratīta — one against whom Rākṣasas and others cannot advance, one attacked by enemies in battle; or, not attained by creatures of unrefined minds. Apuruṣaghnaḥ — you who do not kill men who are manly and capable of sacrifice. Trisaptaiḥ sattvaiḥ — attended by three or seven followers; so goes the construction with īyase." The printed passage is partly compressed and some words are doubtful [?].

42. Ṛk 7; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "At the morning pressing, this Ṛk vanoti hi is to be inserted before the prasthita-yājyā of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; it is prescribed in the same section: 'vanoti hi sunvan kṣayaṃ parīṇaso mo ṣu vo asmad abhi tāni pauṃsyā' (Āś. [refs] [?]). O Indra, the sacrificer who presses for you gets (vanoti, wins) a dwelling [kṣaya] — a house which you may come to, [as accessible] for all classes; by your favour he obtains it. Hi is of a well-known sense. Further, the sacrificer who performs a Soma-sacrifice destroys (ava yajati) the enemies bound around him on all sides (parīṇasaḥ), the haters; and not only the enemies of the sacrifice but also the enemies of the gods. And further, the one who performs the sacrifice marked by pressing, O Indra, by your grace vājī — possessed of food — unconquered, surrounded by none [avṛtaḥ], desires (siṣāsati) to gain (san) thousands — innumerable — of riches such as cows. By what means is this obtained? — Indra gives to the sacrificer who performs the Soma-sacrifice with Indra in view ābhuvam — plentiful, all-pervading, ever-growing, very abundant — wealth in the form of cows and so on." Some grammatical remarks on siṣāsati are not transcribed.

¶ Sense: "O Vāyu, may the indus — the moisteners, the Soma-juices — of ours rejoice you (the Parasmaipada by vyatyaya). What kind of Soma-juices? Mandinaḥ — gladdeners; krāṇāsaḥ — performing their own function of joy and so on; sukṛtāḥ — well made by the pressing, the filtering through the strainer, the taking up of the cups and so on; abhidyavaḥ — shining all around; gobhiḥ krāṇāḥ — being made (poured) with gobhiḥ, i.e. speech in the form of mantras; or by those that bring [the milk] to the āhavanīya fire, being offered. [krāṇa from kṛ with śānac; the kap is elided by Vedic usage.] Further, abhidyavaḥ — going towards [you]. O Vāyu, since your niyut horses — spirited to go to our sacrificial place, capable (dakṣa) of conveying — sacante, attend you, to bring you to the offering-place [for the taking of the oblation, dāvane], with a view to the rites (dhiyaḥ); for what purpose? iradhyai — to bring, or to serve (ira gatau, with the kadhyai suffix for the infinitive); [iradhyati is a verb of service, as in the Nighaṇṭu]. What kind of horses? krāṇāḥ — carrying out their own task, the drawing of the chariot [Yāska: krāṇāḥ kurvāṇāḥ — Ni. 4-9 [?]]; ūtayaḥ — protecting, or loving; sadhrīcīnāḥ — going along with you [saha → sadhri by vibhāṣāñceḥ in the sense of kha]. And further, dhiyaḥ — priests or sacrificers, possessed of rites or of intellect, upa bruvate — come near and speak, make their desire known." Doubtful here: the grammatical details of kadhyai, sadhrīcīna.

Pratipadārtha: the page is a continuation of the same; the printed order of the items on pp. 573–574 is slightly different from the above, which gives the glosses in the order in which they occur in the Ṛk, with the parenthetical glosses as printed: e.g. "iradhyai — to serve (to attend on) you", "sacante — join you (to go with you to the sacrificial place)", "dhiyaḥ — the wise priests", "upa bruvate — approach you and tell their desires".

17. Ṛk 3; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "This Vāyu yokes the two red (rohitā) horses in front of the chariot, at the pole, or for bearing the burden; at times he yokes two ruddy-red (aruṇā), and at times the two ajirā, moving ones, of a particular colour. Or: this is connected in both [places]. For what purpose does he yoke? — voḍhave, to bear the burden of the yoke; and further vahiṣṭhā, the two horses that bear the burden most. [The suffix iṣṭhan after vodhṛ, with elision of tṛ; the plural/dual ending ā.] When there is a great burden to bear. The repeated mention of Vāyu and of yoking is to show that he comes very quickly. Now he speaks directly: O Vāyu, purandhi — [she/he] of much intelligence, [here] by implication the sacrificer — purandhir bahudhīḥ says Yāska (Ni. 6-[?], [?]) — awaken him; come swiftly by chariot and make him aware, for the acceptance of the oblation. The illustration: as a jāra — a paramour — coming to a sleeping (sasatī) woman, a purandhi, one with a fair body, awakens her by his own signal, so you also awaken the sacrificer, who is absorbed in the rite. And for that, rodasī — heaven and earth — pra cakṣaya, make known, illuminate; and for the light, make the dawns shine (vāsaya), make it dawn; and again the same prayer: for śravas [food], that you may take the oblation-food, make the dawns shine."

22. Continuing the explanation of purandhim from p. 582: the author of the Nirukta, Yāska, says —

23. Grammar, continued.

¶ Sense: "O Vāyu, for you (tubhyam) — for your sake — the dawns, lit by you in the way stated before, shine, pure (śucayaḥ) or bright, in the far distance (parāvati), in the sky, in the daṃsu — houses, or acts [daṃsa is a name of house; the final elision by Vedic usage]. With their rays they spread out fine, covering-fit robes (vastrā); or: for you who come, at the sacrificial houses (devayajana), for the oblation, with rays — in the blazing flames of fire — they spread lovely garments; i.e. the flames of Agni themselves spread out as garments, because at dawn the fires are kindled — so the flames are called "garments". Not merely common garments: navyeṣu — in new, praiseworthy [rays], citrā — wonderful, of many colours, they spread out (tanvate), because the rays of the dawn have many colours; and in the Agni-flame sense, the flames are of many colours by being dark, fierce etc. Further, O Vāyu, for your sacrifice the dhenu — the cow that gives joy [by nourishing] — sabardughā [sabar is a name of nectar; the milker of it, kap suffix after duh] — milks of herself all the vasūni — wealth in the form of ghee and the like [dohate: the passive yak is absent, the śap is not elided by Vedic usage]. You, O Vāyu, from the shining sky, beget (ajanayaḥ) the Maruts, your parts, who break the cloud and produce rain, for vakṣaṇābhyaḥ — for the rain-waters of flowing nature; and for vakṣaṇābhyaḥ — the rivers [vakṣaṇā is a name of rivers: vakṣaṇā rujānā, as read in the Nighaṇṭu [?]] — for their sake."

¶ Sense: "O Vāyu, for you the Soma-juices are śukrāsaḥ — bright, and śucayaḥ — pure; [as they come through the vessels they become exceedingly pure — what need is there to say of their purity?]. Turaṇyavaḥ — hasty [to reach you], ugrāḥ — of surging brilliance; they, in your joys (madeṣu), for the cause of your joy, in bhurvaṇi — in the rite that bears [the oblation] — go (iṣaṇanta) towards the āhavanīya or desire it [the Ātmanepada by vyatyaya]. And further they desire (iṣanta) water, in apāṃ bhurvaṇi — in the cloud (megha), since the oblation offered in the fire produces rain through the Sun; or: the sacrificers, offering for you, desire the rain of waters. Further, O Vāyu, bhagam — the worshipful you, the tsārī — one who is anxious and extremely afraid, dasamāna — wasted [by the obstructors of the sacrifice, or by the observances such as the milk-vow], the sacrificer — in takṣvavīrye — for the [driving away] of thieves who obstruct the sacrifice [?] — praises (īṭṭe, from īḍ stutau, the śap elided as in the adādi class). Since you protect from all beings (bhuvanāt), from the fear arising in the three worlds, by supporting our oblations (dharmaṇā), you protect; and further from the fear of the asurya — [the fear] connected with the Asuras — you protect specially, being endowed with the supporting and nourishing of us: since you do so, therefore I praise [you]." The reading of a phrase near "bhūtajātāt" is not clear [?].

34. Ṛk 6; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "O Vāyu, you are apūrvya: that from which nothing is earlier is apūrva, a station; he who deserves it is apūrvya. Such, and for that very reason prathamaḥ — being before the other gods — you deserve (arhasi, you obtain) the drinking (pīti) of the somas; the drinking of the pressed (sutānām) Soma-juices you deserve — wherever there is pressing, everywhere you drink by rule: this is the meaning. Previously this was said with the idea of priority; now, to make known that at every Soma-rite your drinking occurs, it is stated separately. Not merely the drinking of Soma: uto, but also [you accept the oblation] of the vihutmatīnām — those offering specially, or invoking — and vavarjuṣīṇām — those who avoid unwanted sin — of the people (viśām), the sacrificers and priests. Or: of those sacrificers, all the cows viśvā id dhenavaḥ yield for you — they themselves milk (duhre) — milk, the āśira (mixing material); and also ghee is milked (duhrate), as material for spreading and pouring etc." Grammatical details of vavarjuṣīṇām and duhre are partly doubtful [?].

37. Read from the image; the text of this small-type Brāhmaṇa passage is partly doubtful [?]. Sense: "The gods, for the first drinking of King Soma, could not agree, each desiring 'May I drink first, may I drink first.' Not reaching agreement they said: 'Let us run a race (āji); whoever of us wins will drink Soma first.' 'So be it.' They ran the race; of them, as they set out, Vāyu was first at the goal (mukham); then Indra; then Mitra and Varuṇa; then the Aśvins."

Sūkta 135

1. Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].

3. Sense so far: "O Vāyu, for our sacrifice come to the strewn barhis, for the vīti — the eating of oblations. By what means? By sahasreṇa niyutā — by a thousand niyuts (the singular in the generic sense). Niyut is a name of the horses of Vāyu: niyuto vāyoḥ — as the Nirukta has it (Nai. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೫" [?]); and śatinībhiḥ — with the hundreds of niyuts: come [so]." The passage continues on p. 608.

[jayi ca (Pā. 6-1-203 [as read]) gives the ādyudātta.] Pūrvapītaye — for the drinking before the other gods the gods have restrained (yemire, held back); or: the praisers, the priests, held back the Soma for you, the god, towards the āhavanīya — as in the other mantra, agraṃ pibā madhūnāṃ sutaṃ vāyo (Ṛ. 4-46-1 [as read, [?]]), whose illustration is the purpose of the word hi. And further, for you the pressed (sutāsaḥ), honeyed (madhumantaḥ) Soma-juices asthiran: stand for your joy; and for the rite (kratu) they stand, held by the priests, for its accomplishment. So — [you] drink." The last remarks of grammar on asthiran are partly doubtful [?].

¶ Sense: "O Vāyu, tubhya — for you (the dative case-ending elided). This Soma, offered, goes (arṣati) to the kośa — the cup (graha), the container. What kind of Soma? Adribhiḥ paripūtaḥ — purified by the pressing-stones, the instruments of pressing; or purified by the strainer of woollen fringe [daśāpavitra] and the cup. Likewise spārhā vasānaḥ — wearing desirable lustres. And further, wearing pure and bright lustres, the Soma comes to you [ṛṣī gatau; śap by vyatyaya]. O Vāyu, this Soma — your share, that which is to be shared — is offered, among men in the world [?], for you among the gods: since among all the gods the Soma is your share, therefore first to you it is offered. Further, O Vāyu: thus [approach that Soma], desirous of us (asmayuḥ). Bring the niyut horses to the offering; then go to heaven; doing so, joined with us, favouring us, or desiring us, being pleased (juṣāṇaḥ), go." Several words of the commentary here are doubtful [?].

19. Ṛk 3; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "O Vāyu, come to our sacrifice (adhvara) with your horses, with the hundreds (śatinībhiḥ niyudbhiḥ) and thousands (sahasriṇībhiḥ), for vīti — for the satisfaction of your desire [?]; having come, for the eating of the oblations — Soma and the rest — come very quickly with hundreds and thousands of horses, for eating them. Further, this share of yours, the Soma, is ṛtviyaḥ — has come to its time, the time for giving. [Here ṛtu indicates the time of giving; ghas by Vedic usage (Pā. 5-1-106 [as read, [?]]), and siti ca (Pā. 1-4-16 [as read]); by the pada-term overriding the bha-term, in the absence of guṇa of o, yaṇ comes.] Further, the Soma, at sunrise, is saraśmiḥ — together with the rays of the Sun: of equal brightness, or accompanied by them; since at sunrise the rays arise, the time has come. And the Soma-juices, borne by the adhvaryus — the camasa-adhvaryus (the plural because they are ten) — ayaṃsata, have been made ready. O Vāyu, those Soma-juices, bright, ayaṃsata: raised extremely shining. Therefore come to consume them."

22. Ṛk 4; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "Having praised Vāyu alone, [the ṛṣi] now praises both Indra and Vāyu together. O Vāyu, and Indra: your chariot, which belongs to you two and has the horses called niyut, shall bring (vakṣat) you both to the place of sacrifice [vaha in leṭ, aṭ augment, sip by bahulam]. Although the niyut horses belong to Vāyu's chariot, as both deities are going together they carry Indra also. For what? avase — for coming, or for protecting. And again for what? prayāṃsi — the food (the Soma), well-placed (sudhitāni), for vīti — for the eating of them; and the havyāni — other oblations, the puroḍāśa and the like of the pressing [savanīya], for eating. [Vīti from vī with ktin; udātta by mantre vṛṣa…] Further, madhvaḥ — of the sweet andhas — the Soma: pibatam — drink the sweet Soma. Because pūrvapeyam — the drinking before the other gods — is hitam — fixed [?] for you two. [yat from pātaḥ …] Hence drink first. Or: Vāyu has the first drinking even before Indra: tvaṃ hi pūrvapā asi (Ṛ. 4-46-1 [as read, [?]]), deva vadhīhe pūrvapeyam [?] (Ṛ. 8-1-1 [as read]) and other such passages are well known; and the Brāhmaṇa on indra-turīya, [in Ai. Brā. 3-39 [?]], ... the passage devā vai somasya rājño 'grapeyena samapādayan shows that Indra drinks, with Vāyu, before other gods. And further, at the time of coming, O Vāyu and Indra, come with candreṇa rādhasā — a delightful wealth, gold, wealth of cows and so on: come with rādhas, jewels, riches." Details of the grammar of gatam are partly doubtful [?].

23. he vāyo — O Vāyu

24. Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 4, continued:

33. Saṃhitā and Pada read from the image.

34. Ṛk 5; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "O Indra and Vāyu, the dhiyaḥ — the rites such as praise — have turned (vavṛtyuḥ), have been performed with great intensity, towards our sacrifices (adhvarān) — for you two. Further, for you the adhvaryus purify (marmṛjanta) with the woollen strainer this Soma, vājinam — going to the cups from the droṇakalaśa [?], the indu that is before [them]; the simile for the cleansing: like a swift horse, āśuṃ atyaṃ na vājinam, a fleet runner, that has strength (vājin), whom they rub clean by removing sweat and the like; so [the Soma]. Further, O Indra and Vāyu, drink the Soma-juices of those adhvaryus, purified; do the drinking; for that come here to our sacrifice with ūti — with our protection. Further, O Indra-Vāyu, desiring (asmayū) our sacrifice, drink [the juices] pressed (sutānām) by the stones — the genitive in the object-sense as before: the purpose, madāya — satisfaction, joy; since you are vājadā — givers of food. Therefore drink."

35. he indra vāyū — O Indra and Vāyu

36. tadartham — for that

37. pibatam

38. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa passage of p. 631, explained in Kannada:

40. Ṛk 6; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

41. Sense: "O Vāyu, these Soma-juices, belonging to you, and to Indra, in the rites of the priests, are pressed here, at the place of pressing, being carried (bharamāṇāḥ) — held by the adhvaryus, taken, or about to be offered — ayaṃsata: they come, they are fixed for you two. Further, these very Soma-juices, śukrāḥ — clear, shining — ayaṃsata: they are fixed. And āśavaḥ — pervading — to please you. Tiraḥ pavitram — across the crosswise strainer, the woollen strainer that hides the Soma within, they are poured (abhyasṛkṣata). Further, yuvāyavaḥ — desiring you two — the Soma-juices, avyayā: [pass through] the fine hairs (romāṇi) of the sheep-wool strainer; or avyayā = made of wool [?], [the m elided]; having passed such hairs they go out of the vessel; and again they are specially described, ati avyayā — exceedingly inexhaustible, the Soma-juices."

42. te eva somāḥ — those same Soma-juices
