47. Bhāṣya of Ṛk 7, continued from p. 641; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

48. Sense: "To the place where the sound of the pressing-stones is heard for the pressing, go — come back to that place; go to the house — the sacrificial house; and again the place itself is described: where sūnṛtā — speech in the form of praise, of the nature of what is dear and true — vi dadṛśe is specially seen and heard; go there; and where ghṛtam — excellent ghee taken for the oblation — rīyate, flows, is carried to the āhavanīya [rīṅ sravaṇe, śyan of the divādi class]; go there; the manner of going is further described: with pūrṇayā — full, with well-nourished limbs [?] — niyutā [the generic singular], you come to our sacrifice with your horses; go straight towards it. And further, O Vāyu, you and Indra, come to our sacrifice; going together, you two go with us as well."

49. he) vāyo — O Vāyu; (tvam

52. Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read]; the English of the last Ṛk runs on from the foot of p. 642 as printed.

53. Special Topics of Ṛk 7, continued; the Kannada gloss of Ṛk 4 of the grāvan hymn, begun on p. 643:

54. Ṛk 8; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "O Indra and Vāyu, here — in this very sacrifice — aha [the particle of emphasis]: that āhuti — the thing to be offered — of the madhu (sweet, or sweet-like) you bear (vahethe, you take up), the Soma, the aśvattha [a kind of fig-tree — i.e. the Soma-plant growing on mountains and the like [?]], which the jāyavaḥ — the victors, the sacrificers — approach (upatiṣṭhanta) to buy [?]. Further, for us (asme) may those jāyavaḥ — victors, sacrifice-accomplishers — the priests, be: let them be capable; they carry out the sacrifice; or, the well-known skilful priests, the victors, be for us and for no one else. Now, "vahethe" here — what is special? He says: O Indra and Vāyu, in this sacrifice the cows, the dhenus, sākaṃ suvate — together bring forth, produce milk only for you; they become milkers [i.e. yield milk] — or the cows together bear offspring for the milkers who serve you. [suvate is of the adādi class: jottāt pāsyānudātted — by the rule that the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta, the root's accent.] Further yavaḥ — barley, generic singular, indicating grains: puroḍāśa etc. are cooked with barley and so on. And further, O Vāyu and Indra, since the cows so bear, those cows of yours do not upadasyanti — are not wasted: not become emaciated by disease and the like; and not merely not wasted — the dhenus, cows pleasing you, nāpa dasyanti — are not lost by theft and the like, [by] things to be borne away, nor destroyed." The grammatical remarks are only partly legible [?].

63. Ṛk 9; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "O Vāyu, giver of good fruit, these horses of yours that are seen before us, in the space between the two nadīs — the two roarers, heaven and earth — carry you (patayanti, make you go; or: your horses fly, go to the place of the sacrifice). Of what kind? Bāhvojasaḥ — strong in the arms; this indicates strength in all limbs. Ukṣaṇaḥ — sprinklers, i.e. young [like bulls]; mahi vrādhantaḥ — growing greatly, like bulls. [The lengthening does not occur, vā papūrvasya nigame.] And further dhanvan cit — even in the dhanvan, the empty antarikṣa where rain comes out — anāśavaḥ — not lost, not lingering in space; therefore jīrāḥ cit — very swift; or with anāśavaḥ the particle cit is conjunctive; agiraukasaḥ — those that have no gir (revilement) as their residence [?] — not detained by reviling and the like [?]. [The Vedic ālug of the instrumental.] This is clarified: sūryasyeva raśmayaḥ durniyantavaḥ — hard to hold, like the rays of the sun, which in a moment pervade the ten directions, and many; so these too. Previously it was said that they cannot be checked by voice; now by hand also: hastayor durniyantavaḥ — hard to restrain with both hands; they are swift in going to the sacrificial place." Several words of the middle are doubtful [?].

64. tvām

Sūkta 136

1. Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 26 [as read].

2. The Kannada anuvāda, concluded:

3. Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 136" [as read].

4. Ṛk 1; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "O priests, for Mitra and Varuṇa bring forth (pra bharata) jyeṣṭham — most praiseworthy, and bṛhat — great, much-grown, namaḥ — praise marked with reverence, or food in the form of oblation marked by it. Namaḥ is a name of food: [as in] nama āyuḥ in the Naighaṇṭuka lists of names. And bring matim — the thought directed to the giving of that [?]; or: bring the reverend oblation (havya). Formerly [in the foregoing Ṛks] the food was the cake to be eaten; now it is the oblation to be drunk, in the form of Soma and ghee. Of what kind are these two? Nicirābhyām — exceedingly long-lasting, eternal [as a stream]. And mṛḷayadbhyām — who by accepting the oblation themselves delighted [?] gladden the sacrificer too, and svādiṣṭham — the sweetest oblation [they eat with pleasure]. What is the special reason? Tā — those Mitra and Varuṇa, samrājā — shining well [rājate, kvip]; ghṛtāsutī — they from whom ghee is received; or from whom the ghṛta, water, the rain, is given: since the two are the deities of day and night, they give rain by day and night — as the Śruti says, ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇāv ahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣati (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-7-4 [as read, [?]]). And they yajñe-yajñe — in every sacrifice — upastutā — are praised by all the priests. [Accent notes.] Kṣatram — their strength, from anywhere, from enemy or Rākṣasa, nādhṛṣe — cannot be overcome (kena suffix in the sense of kṛtya); further, their divinity nū cid — even now — cannot be overcome; or: as before, so now; nū cit is a nipāta in the sense of 'old and new' [Ni. 3-12 [?]]. Their strength cannot be overcome by anyone — what to say of their divinity." The grammar remarks are partly doubtful [?].

5. kiṃca

6. Pratipadārtha continued:

7. Grammar, concluded.

8. Ṛk 2; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "Gātuḥ — the going one (Dawn, Uṣas), varīyasī — exceedingly wide, has been seen (adarśi) by all, for the urave — the wide (extensive) conjunction (yoga), for the work of going and the like. And ṛtasya — of the going [Sun, Āditya] — panthāḥ, the path in the form of the sky, raśmibhiḥ samayaṃsta — has come into conjunction with the rays, has been lit. Bhagasya — of the god of that name, who is to be worshipped by all — with his rays the cakṣuḥ — the eyes of all living beings — samayaṃsta: have come together [with light]; all became capable of seeing their own things. And of Mitra, who is the friend of all people because he causes light, the sadanam — house, the sky, dyukṣam — the dwelling place of shining things — raśmibhiḥ samayaṃsta; so too of Aryaman, the god of that name; [accent note]; and of Varuṇa, the remover of darkness, the dwelling became so. Although the Sun is one, because of difference of [attributes] separate praise is given; and although the sky which is to be lit by all three is one, still, because of the difference in the lighters it is praised threefold. After the rising there is light for the performance of rites. Therefore, because of their rising, the ukthya — praiseworthy, great, abundant vayaḥ — food in the form of oblation — they [the pair, Mitra and Varuṇa; or the Sun and Dawn] hold: dadhāte; and further they upastutyam [accept] the praise to be recited near, great, and the food." Two or three words in the last sentence are not clear [?].

9. samayaṃsta — meaning, become capable of seeing

10. samayaṃsta — became lighted

11. sadanam

12. kiṃca — and

13. Grammar of Ṛk 2, concluded.

14. Ṛk 3; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "This sacrificer dhārayat — has established, himself made [ready] — jyotiṣmatīm — the resplendent, with the fire of the āhavanīya — aditim — the complete, indivisible — kṣitim — the earth fit for the fire's dwelling, in the form of the uttaravedi. [For the Śruti says: vitāvatī vai pṛthivī yāvatī vedir iti — 'the earth is as wide as the altar'.] Likewise svarvatīm — leading to heaven through the accomplishment of the sacrifice — such [an altar] Mitra and Varuṇa join (ā sacete); not only on this day but dive-dive — on all days. How are they? Dive-dive jāgrivāṃsā — awake every day, not lazy to go to the sacrifice. And further, having come to the altar, by accepting the resplendent ghee and the like, they obtain (āśāte) exceedingly bright kṣatram — power. [Grammar of aśnute in the Vedic laṭ [?]; śap luk by Vedic usage.] What are they? Ādityā — sons of Aditi; dānunas patī — lords of the gift (of ghee etc.), or protectors of desired gifts. [Accent notes.] Mitra and Varuṇa, both gods; and Aryaman, a single god, is yātayajjanaḥ — [leader of] the people, among them [the two], connected with them, who sets all people to their respective works; Mitra and Varuṇa are the gods of day and night, but Aryaman, by their strength, impels all beings. Further yātayajjanaḥ — he whose people carry the world, who are his messengers; or he by whom people, living beings, are pushed down into hell by the apsaras [?]; as witness of deeds he rewards beings according to their own deeds. Such Aryaman is subordinate to Mitra and Varuṇa." Parts of the last sentences are doubtful [?].

15. ayam — this sacrificer

16. tathā — likewise

17. ata eva

18. and

19. Mantra 7 of the altar series, concluded:

20. The story of Agni and his brothers, concluded in the Kannada:

21. Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೫-೪-೨" [?]; the Sanskrit above is the beginning, and this page continues:

22. Kannada, continuing from p. 685:

23. Ṛk 4; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "This Soma, carried by us, offered, may be śaṃtamaḥ — most agreeable, most pleasing — to Mitra and Varuṇa; bhūtu — let it be [Vedic śap luk]. In the avapānas — the cups with their mouths turned down — ā bhagaḥ — it is fully to be shared by those two. Further, devo deveṣu — shining among the gods, the followers of Mitra and Varuṇa, or among the other gods, to be shared; or among the sacrificers, praisers [deva = shining], tathā-bhagaḥ — to be shared by them all. Further, all the gods, viśve devāsaḥ, today, on this day, juṣerata — enjoy that Soma. How are they? Sajoṣasaḥ — joined in equal pleasure. And, O sovereigns, Mitra and Varuṇa, you two, do (karathaḥ) [so]; — for yad īmahe — what we ask, the gods; since we ask [īḍ gatau, divādi; the Vedic elision of the vikaraṇa]; therefore let them enjoy. Likewise, ṛtāvānā — the possessors of ṛta, truth, the sacrifice — Mitra and Varuṇa, we ask the desired fruit, or their drinking." The grammar notes are partly doubtful [?].

24. śaṃtamaḥ bhūtu — let it be giving happiness

25. tat devān yācāmahe — we ask the gods for it

26. Grammar of Ṛk 4, concluded.

27. Ṛk 5; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].

¶ Sense: "Whatever person, sacrificer, serves (avidhat) Mitra and Varuṇa [the dative because of sampradāna in the rite], that person, your servant, anarvāṇam — without an enemy [arvā = enemy; bhrātṛvyo vā arvā, says the Śruti] or not alone, serving no other — protect all round (pari pātaḥ); from what? from aṃhasaḥ — sin caused by deficiency or excess. Not only the common person, but dāśvāṃsam — the one who has given oblations — martam, the mortal, from aṃhasaḥ — all sin. Not only you two, but Aryaman too, the god who regulates all, protects (abhi rakṣati) the sacrificer who behaves honestly (ṛjūyantam) towards the gods, in accordance with (anu) his rite (vratam). What is special about this man? — The sacrificer who, with ukthaiḥ, recitations, embraces the vrata — rite — of these two, Mitra and Varuṇa, and who with stomaiḥ, hymns accomplished by mantras accompanied by song, adorns your rite on all sides: so they protect him."

28. pari pātaḥ

29. tathā

30. yaḥ

33. Kannada, continuing the stoma passage of p. 697:

35. Ṛk 6; read from the image; begins at the foot of p. 700.

¶ Sense: "To the shining Sun I speak namas — praise marked with reverence. To what kind of [deity]? Bṛhate — great [the accent by the upasaṃkhyāna rule]; praiseworthy. Likewise to rodasībhyām — heaven and earth, [or] to the deities presiding over them, I speak the namas; to Mitra, who is good to all people and the god presiding over the day; to Varuṇa, the covering god presiding over the night; to mīḍhuṣe — the sprinkler of the desired fruit, Rudra. What kind? Sumṛḷīkāya — the giver of good happiness. Mīḍhuṣe and sumṛḷīkāya are separate epithets. Now the sacrificer addresses the priest or himself: O hotṛ or O self, approach with understanding Indra, Agni, the brilliant (dyukṣam) Aryaman, and Bhaga, and praise them. By your grace, living long (jyok), may we be joined with offspring — sons, servants and so on. And somasya ūtī — by the protection of Soma, the moon, may we be joined: may we, through praise, be accompanied by the protection that comes from it."

36. namaḥ vocam

37. vayam

38. Read from the image; the first words are doubtful [?]; the Kannada gives:

39. The Nirukta's answer, continued:

40. Grammar of Ṛk 6, concluded.

41. Ṛk 7; read from the image.

42. Sense: "We, indravantaḥ — endowed with the pleased Indra — devānām ūtī — by the satisfaction of the gods, with oblations and the like — maṃsīmahi, 'may we think' [or: 'may we know']. What kind of us? Svayaśasaḥ — of our own fame, favoured by the Maruts, who are pleased by our praise. Or: protected by the gods' protection, may we be knowers (of their greatness). And Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, the gods, yaṃsan — have given us joy — each desired boon; and we, maghavānaḥ — possessing food [from those gods], may we pervade, may we gain, that joy." (Aśyāma — liṅ of aśnoti in the benedictive; by chandasy ubhayathā it is sārvadhātuka, so s-elision.)
